But also know you will truly enjoy the 10-week journey. I don't normally speak for an entire class but I am fairly confident I can speak for the entire class that they enjoyed this journey, as evidenced by the standing ovation (back to back years at least) given to Professor Swamy as he concluded his last lecture. Do you wish to be intellectually challenged and feel your way of thinking of business has changed because of what you learned in a class? Then yes, I absolutely recommend this class. This is not a class just for students interested in pursuing a career in finance. You could be pursuing a career where the chances of you ever thinking about bond mathematics is under 1% and I would still highly recommend this class. Don't be fooled by the name "Fixed Income" Yes the base of the class will be on Fixed Income Investment, Treasuries, Corporate Bonds, Mortgages but Professor Swamy brings his experience and expertise to truly challenge the way you think about the geopolitical environment, the macroeconomy, the future of our country and the feds actions.

Another caveat I will add is this class tends to attract a certain type of student at Haas. Haas is already an elite community but this class just felt different still, I felt I was surrounded by the most driven and motivated students. It is very possible if you don't have a heavy quantitative background or much experience in finance that you feel you have imposter syndrome at times. Do NOT let that intimidate you from not signing up, Professor Swamy is one of the most approachable and down to earth professors I have ever had in my life. You will need to work harder possibly but I promise you it will be worth it.

Satish might be the best teacher I have ever had. This is no exaggeration. His patience is generous. His passion is contagious. He is hilarious and every class is a riot. As a former engineer, I feel that I now understand management decisions that were attributed to interest rates that made no sense to me before, and I know that my future work will benefit from this understanding no matter what I do.

This course has quickly become one of my favorites at UC Berkeley. It excels at equipping students with practical skills and knowledge in negotiation, with assignments thoughtfully designed to span a range of negotiation scenarios. The complexity of these assignments increases progressively throughout the semester, matching our growing competence and building on lecture content in a cohesive manner. For example, an early assignment involved negotiating the sale of a consumer product between two individuals, while a later assignment challenged a large group of students to represent diverse stakeholder groups in a complex negotiation that spanned a few days.

In-class activities were equally engaging. The session on "fairness," for instance, provided a fun, insightful way to immediately apply lecture concepts. Professor Solène Delencourt brings remarkable optimism and enthusiasm to the early class, making each session engaging and energizing. Her expertise and welcoming demeanor encourage active student participation, creating an enjoyable immersive experience. The "no electronics" policy was particularly refreshing, allowing students to fully engage with the material and connect with each other.

Professor Solène Delencourt genuinely cares about her students' success. It's evident in how she gladly shares stories of former students' negotiation victories. It's evident in how she incorporates in-class games with thoughtful rewards (that she thoughtfully purchased herself!). She even brought coffee and snacks to class, to help recreate real-world negotiation environments. She really goes above and beyond standard teaching practices. Her ability to balance lecture content with hands-on activities has been instrumental in helping us internalize the course material deeply. Professor Solène Delencourt consistently encourages us to attend office hours and seek support, and her dedication to the craft of negotiation is apparent in every class. I wholeheartedly recommend this course (and any course Professor Solène Delencourt teaches) to my peers— it's an invaluable experience.

sections.goodFor: Anyone remotely interested in VC, founding a startup, or understanding the Bay Area innovation ecosystem; you leave with real work samples and a strong speaker network.
sections.notFor: Students who have definitively ruled out VC and founding - one notes the class costs a lot of bid points that may be better spent elsewhere.
sections.workloadNote: Assignment-driven across 14 lectures - forming a firm, sourcing, diligence, term sheet, investment decision; one says the gaps between assignments are too short to internalize material.
sections.gradingBasis: A sequence of VC assignments (firm creation, sourcing, due diligence, term sheet/investment decision) plus case discussion.
sections.redFlags: Two mild caveats only: assignments come back-to-back with too little time to internalize, and the course bids out at a high point cost.
sections.quote: I'd say that there should be more time between assignments. Because the time window is reduced between assignments, it's harder to internalize the material fully.
comments: Yes - great course that breaks down the VC process. Very engaging course that is entertaining as well. Some of the best class speakers I've had. Great professors.
Yes def recommend

If you are interested in being a VC or being a founder, this class is super valuable. I would define it as " how to be a VC " which also helps you understand how to interact with the ecosystem. If you've already decided neither of these is for you, I would probably take other classes, especially considering how many points this class bids out for. That said, Sean and Jules are excellent and passionate teachers, and you do learn a lot. They bring in a standout guest list and keep the class engaged every week.

Absolutely! Undoubtedly the top 3 classes at Haas. They take you through every element of venture in as much detail as they can over 14 lectures. The speakers ares top notch. And it is a must take class! Sean and Jules are perfect together and I'll miss coming for the class!
Yes, definitely recommended!
The is a must take if you want to get into venture or learn about Venture. I want to become a VC because of this course and the professors
Must have class at haas
Absolutely yes! Probably the best course I've taken at Haas. Amazing professors, practical, engaging insightful Definitely. By far the most valuable class I've had at Haas!!!
Yes. I went through this course from someone who knows nothing about VC to knowing how to build a term sheet. One of the best classes I've taken so far in Haas.

Absolutely yes. This was hands down the best course I've taken at Haas and there were so many learnings and people packed into 1 semester, I want to spread it across 2 full semesters. Super insightful, super helpful and super relevant to the real world context. I like everything about this course and I would recommend you to take it simply because there's hardly any other course at Haas where you learn so much - real VCs as professors and highly relevant content. Yes - very interesting subject taught by great teachers
Highly recommended
Top classes at Haas. Do NOT miss out
Yes for sure! Definitely must take. The best class at Haas.

Yes, 100%. I would strongly recommend this course and both instructors to other students. The content is practical, the expectations are clear, and you walk away with real VC skills and work samples you can actually use.
Yes, it's very valuable for whether you're going to work in VC or a startup because it provides you all the good, bad, and the ugly about VC. It's very enlightening.
Highly recommended

Yes, I would. There are no other foundational VC courses in the program and they do bring a lot of great guest speakers that one can learn a lot from. It's also a great way to tap into the VC world and network.
Definitely recommend, top 3 courses on haas.

It was amazing, it was fun, funny, didactic, useful, broaden my perspectives about VC, and also gave me a much more concrete and applicable knowledge in what I should look for dealing with VC, whether as an investor, LP, VC, or entrepreneur.
100% yes. If you are interested in VC, don't think. Bid high and do it.
Absolutely - this is one of the best and most useful classes that I've taken at Haas if not the best.
Definitely! If anyone is remotely curious about VC, then they should take this course.
100% THIS WAS THE BEST CLASS AT HAAS

Incredible instructors who have packed an entire intro to venture capital into a 3 unit course. Yes
Highly recommend

Yes, one of the best courses I took at Haas. Anyone interested in VC or who expects to deal with VC should take this class

Strongly recommend, undoubtedly the best class I've taken at Haas.

Would recommend this course generally for anyone wanting to learn more about VC. However, I'd say that there should be more time between assignments. Because the time window is reduced between assignments, it's harder to internalize the material fully. Structure the assignment towards learning.
Yes anyone interested in vc or entrepreneurship should take this course.
Yes 100%
This is maybe THE BEST class at HAAS I have ever taken. It will be so worthwhile.

Yes, possibly the best class I have taken during my time at Haas. The quality of the content, instruction, guest speakers is fantastic. This is a great class regardless of if you want to go into the VC industry or not.

Yes definitely.

Yes! A must for the MBA student seriously considering a career in real estate.
If they are trying to recruit for real estate yes. If not, probably not

Yes I would recommend this course if you had ever thought about real estate as your possible career path, especially if you don't have any real estate experience before.
Yes, this class was very informative and helped to get a better understanding of the role that I would like to pursue upon graduation.

I am not a real estate student nor do I plan on going into real estate, but I think this was the most valuable course I've taken at Haas. It was extremely well structured and resulted in substantial learning. Abigail did an amazing job with engaging with students and making the information friendly to anyone even if they do not have a real estate background. The speakers themselves were also great at sharing about their work experience, and I really appreciated that half the class was having the speaker share a project / case study. I wish Haas would do a course like this for all industries, not just real estate!
Absolutely. The course is a great opportunity to learn about various real estate functions even (or especially) if you have no prior experience or knowledge of real estate.
I would recommend it to people who are even a little interested in real estate. Low workload but learn a lot in every class!

If you want to get a broad introduction to Real Estate, this is a great course. You're going to hear speakers come in and talk about what their jobs entail and then go through an actually project that they have worked on. There were no assignments other than a final that just wanted us to reflect on what we learned throughout the course.

100% even if you only have the slightest interest in real estate. The course is basically like a speaker series (but with more intimate conversations with guest speakers), and Abigail does a fantastic job asking our speakers the right questions to help all of the students learn about the realities of each role
Yes, if you're interested in Real Estate. This is a great (and easy) introductory class to the most common functions of interest to Haas grads.
Yes
Nice class to get an overview of the industry. If you are interested in Real Estate but you don't know where to start this class is a must

Yes, the course is great for those interested in learning the basics about Real Estate. After taking this course I had a better understanding of the career options Real Estate has to offer MBA graduates
Yes

I recommend taking this class if you are interested in real estate or not. Absolutely!

Yes absolutely, Abby is exceptionally knowledgeable about Real Estate and approachable. Both qualities were so important for most of us who knew very little about real estate and found the vastness of the subject intimidating. Because of her expert knowledge and incisive questions to the speakers, I was able to learn a tremendous amount of material in half a semester.
Yes. Abby is very relatable, and is always willing to help students build their career in real estate
Yes 100%. Abigail was one of my favorite professors during my first year at Haas.
This class was a great introduction to five functions of the real estate industry — if you are at all curious about the industry, I would highly recommend.
Highly recommend this class if you want an intro to real estate!

I would recommend this course to students looking for a survey of various real estate careers. Abby does a great job of organizing speakers and asking questions about their career and their thoughts on careers as a whole.

Absolutely. I came in knowing nothing about real estate, and left with a great baseline knowledge of real estate careers. This is essentially a speaker series for post-MBA real estate careers, so don't expect to learn techniques for closing on a home.

Yes, I would recommend this class because it is a) light lift and b) taught me a lot about a new subject Definitely. Yes - great class and learned a lot.

Yes! This was the best course I took this semester. It was a really helpful, practical intro to VC and covered a wide range of very practical topics (e.g., term sheets, valuation, etc.). The professors were great and brought in a really amazing set of guest speakers from different VCs. Classes were engaging (attendance and participation expected) and the assignments were very well designed to consolidate learnings.

It depends. If you want to break into VC or if you already work in VC, this is an extremely valuable class. For the rest, if you're just interested in VC but don't want to make a career out of it, I would not recommend this class. It gets pretty technical at times, some assignments are the very heavy lift and my general perception is that the instructors expect you to come up with extremely insightful comments, that are hard to make if you don't have previous experience in the space.

Participation is essential to this class. They keep track of participation and will cold-call people who haven't participated recently (which I did not appreciate, it felt like there were putting people on the spot too often and that the expectations were too high).
Overall, good class for people that are really into VC, not recommended otherwise.
Very valuable course, highly recommended. It is 100% VC - do not expect PE.

Highly recommend, even if you don't have experience in this industry. Instructors are well prepared for case discussions and really try to get you to think and develop points of views. Speakers are insightful and a big part of the class experience.

I would recommend this course to you only if you are really passionate about VC or are very interested to understand the world of VC. This course is definitely has a high workload and is much more discussion oriented. If you think you will learn a lot around valuation, financing, more technical skills - then you will be disappointed. There is some elements of it but it is only touched upon. Overall great course if you are new/wanting to develop a deeper understanding of the VC space.
Yes would definitely recommend to students interested in venture capital.
Yes
Yes. All 3 are fantastic and among the best I've had at Berkeley Haas.

Also, the class is very interesting if you want to be an entrepreneur because you meet several VC managing partners who explained us trends, targets and investment thesis that are very useful to raise money.

Absolutely. I'm a (hopeful) entrepreneur with a startup operator background and took this class to understand how the other-side of the investment table thinks. It delivered on that and was highly engaging every minute with some life lessons sprinkled in as well.

Would definitely recommend this course if you're interested to get a crash course and learn about venture capital. The workload was a little more than most classes, but I genuinely understood venture better through this class. The professors brought in PHENOMENAL speakers and have been personally helpful. I got a lot from the class but will caveat it doesn't necessarily prep or hone you to do a venture Associate / Sr Associate / Principal role - you'll still need to figure that out elsewhere

Recommend this class for anyone looking to get a foundational understanding of Venture Capital. The class is the best structured class I've taken at Haas given three faculty members. All three (Sean, Terry, Keval) are very knowledgeable and bring a different aspect to the course. Your venture team matters for most of the class so choose wisely. It's definitely a different vibe compared to other Haas classes (participation is 35% the final grade and case method is better in theory than in practice; also, VCs in general probably think a little too highly of themselves), but overall it was a worthwhile course. Fantastic lineup of guest speakers (Lauren Kolodny from Acrew, Byron Deeter from Bessemer, Paul Kwan from General Catalyst, to name a few), Sean/Keval/Terry have a ton of experience and great
insights/thoughts about the VC industry overall, and I did end up learning a lot about VC.
Yes - a great foundational course for a typical opaque industry in order to learn enough to be able to teach yourself more complex topics

Mixed feelings about this class- While they bring in cool speakers who are great VCs, the class itself has outdated cases from the 90s and early 2000s. Hence, it is not completely representative of today's VC market. I wish the class also focused on what it means to be a good VC- how do you ask proper diligence questions? Maybe they can bring in actual startups for us to ask live questions from the CEO
I would recommend this class if you want an intro to VC/PE. If you are already in this space, then this might not be a class for you. Either way, be prepared to do a lot of reading.

I came from a non-VC, non-financial background and I enjoyed the course. It gave me a summary of how investments and the VC world works which I think is helpful in B-school so that we can make the decisions if this is something we want to do long term or not. I also really appreciated all the guest speakers the instructors chose and brought in as they came from diverse backgrounds and provided very good context and supplement to class instruction. Overall, I would recommend this class.

Yes, I would absolutely recommend as this class is very informational and fun. Almost everyone, no matter you want to become a VC or not, should probably take this course because you will apply the knowledge from this class
somewhere in your career and investment.

Yes, useful class if you aren't familiar with VC and if you want to learn more. Workload isn't too crazy for a 3-unit class. Absolutely! Gives a great insight and understanding on how VC evaluate opportunities and make the deal flow work from start to end. Any one focusing on entrepreneurship or VC should take this class.
For an overview kinda course, it suffices. But you don't learn a lot more, especially on the valuation side. Very good guest speakers though

Yes

If you are at all interested in working in the VC industry, then I would recommend it as you will make important contacts and introductions in the industry. I would recommend this course. It took a few lectures to get into it, but the lectures, discussions, and guest speakers were very informative. The course is lighter on theory but the discussion and speakers are rich (both in bank account and educational value). It is a good way to bring together learnings from other classes and enjoy yourself while you learn.

Yes. The course is really good for anyone who is interested in learning about the VC field. The course covers all the aspects of the VC business. The combination of relevant cases and relevant speakers makes the whole experience really great. I highly recommend this course.

Yes I would. This class is a comprehensive intro to VC and has extremely well prepared content and guest speakers. It teaches you not only the basic stuff such as term sheet and valuation, but also give you an overall picture about the entire VC industry and help you understand the dynamics. Instructors often hold partner's meeting in class to discuss about the pros and cons of a deal and your argument about it. Some of the guest speakers are very helpful as well - they are from different background and worked in different stages of VC firms.

This was a nice class to take and get deeper into the VC and startup ecosystem. It was not necessarily what I expected, but I enjoyed the class and I think it gave me a more realistic view of the industry and it's challenges. It was not a class that boasted that everyone should be in VC/PE, and did talk frankly about challenges in the industry and what the future could hold. I would recommend it if you don't have internship or work experience in VC.
This was a great class and gave me a good overview of what VC world would be like

Yes, I would recommend this course - more for students whoa re interested in VC not PE. We did not spend alot of time on PE business model and strategy. This is a great balance of theoretical and practical course for students who are exploring a career in VC.

Highly recommend for anyone interested in either a career in VC or entrepreneurship or investing. This class has resulted in substantial learning to peak inside into the world of venture capitalists. A great class to take after the entrepreneurship class.
Yes

I would recommend this course to a fellow student if Sean and Keval take a larger role in future iterations. I would highly recommend this course to fellow Berkeley students, including those not interested in entrepreneurship or venture capital. I believe this course substantially improved my understanding of the industry and I have a greater appreciation for the opportunities in Berkeley and the entire Bay Area. This is easily a top 2 course I have taken at Haas so far.

You get as much out of this class as you put into it. If you put little into it, you'll get a basic overview of the business of venture capital (spoiler alert: it's still a lot of luck and n-of-1 wins); if you put a lot into it, I think you can develop a great network starting with the professors and learn an interesting baseline that will help you start a career in venture (or better understand some of the questions VCS ask if you're thinking about entrepreneurship). If you're trying to deeply understand VC/ what VCs are looking for, you probably won't get all the way there with this course, but it's a good introduction if you're exploring/ just getting started.
Heartily recommend this course. One of the best courses at Haas.

Yes. The class has an amazing amount of breadth and is good at presenting what it's like to pursue a career in VC. The industry itself can be very ambiguous, so don't expect any black and white solutions or career paths, but it's very thought provoking.
Yes, but students need to be prepared to spend more time research and network after the class to learn more about the actual VC business

Yes,very valuable insight which you would never be able to just teach yourself. However there were many confusing points in the class due to lack of clarity from the professor. I would ABSOLUTELY recommend this class to a fellow student. It is a lot of work, relative to other MBA classes, and Sean's teaching style is intense and may not be for everyone. Sean is additionally one of the best and most engaging lecturers I have had at Haas.
Emphatically, yes

Very valuable class that teaches you a lot about venture capital. The assignments are hard and not necessarily tied to in class work so that is frustrating. But this is the most engaging high energy night class I've taken at Haas. Cold calling and lots of participation required.
Yes, only if they want to enter VC or raise funds from a VC.
Yes, this class was extremely worthwhile. If you want to learn about venture capital this class is a must. One of the best classes offered in the entire MBA program.

One of the big value adds to this class is the amount of guess lecturers and speakers - this made lectures dynamic and their insights provided alternative viewpoints and approaches.

I would definitely recommend this course to any aspiring Venture Capitalist / Entrepreneur as it teaches you the A-Z of Venture Capital. The guest speakers are incredible and the frameworks Sean teaches are invaluable - especially with regards to Term Sheets and Valuation!

Yes! Even if you aren't interested in a career in VC, the frameworks for evaluating investment opportunities are extensible. Would wholeheartedly recommend this instructor and course to anyone interested in VC. Definitely yes, if you are interested in VC, starting a startup or generally learn a lot about the VC and innovation ecosystem.
Yes, I highly recommend this class! It was my first elective, but the best class so far. It is very applicable to my day-to- day work.

YES
Simply the best class at Haas.

EW295B provides a strong overview of how venture capital works, though you will need some prior knowledge of venture capital to truly get the most of out the class. Highly recommend for those who want to pursue Entrepreneurship in particular, as it is useful primer for seeing fundraising from the other side of the table. Yes

I would definitely recommend this class. I leave having a much more foundational understanding of the VC industry that I did coming in. Absolutely, this is the course to come to Haas MBA for. Exposure, knowledge and experience.

Such an amazing class! I can't believe how good this was. You should definitely take it regardless of your experience in VC (I have 4 years of direct experience and loved it as much as my friend that has no prior experience) if you are interested in the industry.

If you're looking to get into VC, this is definitely the course to do it. If you're in VC and want to learn more or get more external expertise, I would. Yes — I'm leaving with a solid understanding of VC and have a new roster of folks that I might be able to approach when I start something.
Strongly recommend! One of the best course in Haas.
Yes, for someone who comes from a purely operating background this was a great preview into the workings of the VC world
Best class I have taken at Haas. The outside speakers alone are worth the class but Sean and team are engaging and their polish made me excited to attend lecture.

yes, I think this is a good, starting class for those who want to learn VC from the scratch

Awesome class

Yes, this was one of my favorite courses at Haas so far. I had no background in VC and learned a ton. Expectations are high (one case per class, occasional cold calling), but for me it was worth it. definitly. after taking the course one will be prepared to work in VC industry
YES, I will tell people from Denmark coming next year to take this course

This class is great. Sean is very passionate, well connected in the industry, and for many people, this is one of their favorite classes at Haas.

Yes 100% recommend. Courseload was a bit much, but the learnings were soooo valuable. Highly recommend for anyone interested in VC

Yes! First- 3 unit classes are the worst value and, in my experience, almost never worth the time and cost. I would absolutely recommend this course. It is likely the best class that I have taken while at Haas and the professor is fantastic.
Yes
Yes. 100%. Sean is an amazing teach and I would highly recommend everyone who is curious about VC/PE to take this class.

Yes, i think if you want to explore a career in VC or want to start your company, this is probably the class a must take class. Yes - great class if you interested in VC or startups! It was a great overview of the industry with awesome speakers. Yes - I thought this was one of the better taught classes. I think I learned a lot. I thought the professors did a great job overall.

Absolutely -whether you're interested in VC or not, it is incredibly insightful and useful to understand the VC landscape given our affiliation with the tech industry and silicon valley in general. Learnings bleed outside of class and you will be better for it.

Yes, for sure. This is a very valuable class to take at Haas, regardless of whether your long term job plans are in VC or not. You get an excellent idea of the landscape and practical experience that you can take to other roles as well. Additionally, Sean and his teaching team are wonderful!
Yes, he did a great job teaching the class, and I felt engaged throughout
Sean is an amazing professor. Who is very very charismatic and makes a 6pm class extraordinary.

You really learn a ton and have even more fun!!!
Yes! Best professor at Haas.
2000% This is the best class that I've taken in years. All of it was applicable to the career I want to pursue and I think it would be helpful to entrepreneurs and the like as well.
Yes - take this course instead of New Venture Finance! I learned a lot more and felt like class time was used much more effectively.

Corporate Financial Reporting Provides a deeper understanding into why the company and its CEO/CFO might have wanted to present certain numbers as they did and what users of that financial information (e.g. investors) have to watch out / blind-spots (including how certain numbers could be distorted/misrepresented). Every week the class explores certain topics in financial reporting (e.g. how ARR is recognized/reported) as well as the decision making that went behind it.

Comparisons with other finance/accounting courses at Haas: While Introduction to Finance or Financial Accounting courses cover the basics, and Corporate Finance covers what metrics company looks at to manage themselves internally, Corporate Financial Reporting takes an in-depth look at how a company prepares and presents their financial statements for outsiders and what investors/viewers have to watch out for.

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting CFO-level financial decision-making - profitability, financing decisions, valuation. Pivots into finance, consultants, GMs. Many say it should be core. Pick a good team.
sections.notFor: Students with no finance background and only passive interest. Several felt behind in a cohort full of banking backgrounds; one says don't take it unless ready for 5+ hrs/week staying afloat.
sections.workloadNote: One graded case per week worked in groups, ~5+ hours each; readings are light. Heavy but repeatedly described as never busy work, with concepts revisited every few classes.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly group cases graded pass/fail on effort (called flexible), plus a final students expect to be conceptual, not calculation-based.
sections.redFlags: Two criticize the case format: you self-teach the case (often with AI), then re-walk it in class, adding little if you already know finance. Several say non-finance students find it frustrating.
sections.quote: Be warned that this class is a LOT of work: we had one case a week (to be worked on in groups) and each case took ~5+ hours.

Gustavo is a great and kind instructor, but my recommendation depends on your background / discipline. If you have a finance background or can commit to attending office hours/ limiting your AI use, this is a great and practical class. The following class, Gustavo does go over the case and concepts in depth which is helpful but can feel frustrating if you relied on AI to help you do the case and didn't really internalize the concepts. Grading of cases is based on effort which is great and the final seems like its going to be more conceptual questions rather than any actual calculations which is a huge relief. A Haas must-take class for everyone. This really should be called Strategic Finance as it is mainly a case-based class discussing the strategic implications of CFO decisions. I would absolutely recommend this course to a fellow student. As someone who has no experience with accounting, Sunil communicated all concepts clearly and in a straightforward manner, while also encouraging us to understand the real world applications of this content.

I'd highly recommend Professor Dutta to other students. He is so approachable, friendly, and engaging. He makes accounting interesting and fun (which I didn't know could be true) and made this my favorite Fall A class. I've taken accounting before, and learned a little bit more from this class in terms of the intuition. If you have taken accounting before and are considering waiving it, I think that could be a good idea too because the more advanced material is only in the last couple of lectures.
Definitely! He made a sort of dry subject very engaging and interesting through examples, personal stories, why it matters, etc.
Yes, great instructor that keeps a sometimes dry subject very entertaining.

All students who does not have any financial backgrounds are easy to catch up with the class.
Yes - would recommend to those with no Accounting background. This course may not be useful to someone who has intermediate to advanced working knowledge of Accounting.
Yes, if they have limited accounting experience. Else, it may be too basic.

Despite the fact that this is a required core course, I do think that learning the foundational accounting concepts are helpful, particularly as a mechanism to assess companies outside of an industry you are familiar with or one that you are interested in.

Yes -- I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. Everyone has to learn accounting, and Sunil is a great teacher. He truly cares about whether or not we understand the material, and he tries to make it fun. He also makes a lot of time for our questions (of which we had many).
Yes! Easy class, super nice professor.

I absolutely loved Sunil!! Such a kind, welcoming, and genuine demeanor that made attending class at 9 am in our first term a pleasure. I wish Sunil taught all our classes:) made the content interesting with wonderful real-world examples and I think our entire cohort developed a soft spot for him! Couldn't recommend his class and teaching style more. You really do learn a lot about the applications of accounting to the real world, especially to the tech industry:) Yes I will! Although I was working in a bank before but it is always good to refresh the knowledge and US regulation by taking his class. Student presentations are also inspiring and informative!
I would recommend this course highly for someone with no accounting background (like myself). I would recommend Professor Dutta very highly.

Yes, It's a great foundation for Finance and Sunil is a great instructor in teaching general and basic concepts. Yes, I would recommend. It was great a course to learn accounting for the first time. It can be fast paced, but the structured learning will help you each step of the way.
Absolutely - accounting is the language of business and is extremely applicable to any field post Haas. Yes - if they don't have any background in accounting/finance
Yes, he makes accounting fun.
Yes, this course is great for learning the fundamentals of accounting and connecting the dots for what firms need to care about in regards to accounting.
Yes - basic introduction to accounting that has substantial helped me understand how the financial of firms work and able to applied them to real world scenarios!
Yes!
YES - you will learn and have fun.
Yes. Sunil is lovely and informative, and you will learn the basics of accounting, which is useful no matter what role you seek.
Yes! I can't think of a better accounting professor, honestly.
Yes. The instructor is clear and helpful. The material is relevant.
Yes!

Yes! Any class with Sunil is sure to be worth your while, he is so passionate about the topics and the students' actual learning. He loves to hear examples from students' experiences and takes the time to fully explain any topic. I would recommend this course - Sunil is a great professor that made a seemingly pedantic subject engaging and interesting. The homework and quizzes we had throughout the semester were worth completing -- not super long and helped us better understand the material.
Yes, you will learn and understand accounting while having fun!

I would absolutely recommend Sunil! He is an incredible professor, I felt lucky to have him. He made a topic that is traditionally seen as boring both relatable and interesting. I feel like I learned a lot about the topic that I can take forward in my life. He clearly connected lecture, homework, and quizzes so that the material built and expectations were clear. More than that, he is a kind person who clearly cares about his students.
Yes, great and fun class
Yes
Yes. It's a great way to go over fundamental accounting concepts. The class feels fun and engaging. The professor ties the academic content to relevant real-world examples.
Yes! Sunil does an excellent job of highlighting accounting fundamentals to those with limited background, while reinforcing the concepts through applied real world business cases.
Yes, definitely recommend.
Yes highly
Not really... I have heard such good things about Omri (the other ACCY teacher) and his class seems to be really engaging. I'd say that Sunil is fine but that you really want to hope for Omri.
YES!! Sunil is the best, always making sure we understand the subject, making accounting interesting
Absolutely
Yes. Sunil makes the class interesting and is very clear in his explanations.
Yes, I just recommended the class to a few students planning to take it in Fall
Yes. This is a great course to better understand what it is like to work in VC, and to really build out your startup and VC network.

Yes! If you are at all interested in both doing good for the world with business/startups and venture capital investing, this is the class for you. I took this class after Impact Startup Launchpad and it was so useful to see the startup landscape from the investors' point of view. It really made things click, and I feel more prepared to go into technology entrepreneurship as a founder myself. The course was very welcoming to my non-MBA background (I'm a Ph.D.

student in EECS) and think it benefits a lot from a diverse student cohort. The work load was all fairly manageable outside of my daytime work schedule. I really liked working with my team and feel we gelled together. I highly recommend taking this class.
I got a lot of hand-on experiences. Even if I am an international, this class really broadens my network and skills, so highly recommended it!

Absolutely. One of the most practical classes that resembles real life deal sourcing and venture investing. I spent three years in venture investing, and this class is pretty much what you do in real life. I wish it was a little more fast paced, but great timing for people who have not experience in the industry.

Yes, this has been my greatest learning experience at Haas so far. While it is of course recommended for those interested in impact investing, there is also a great opportunity here for students pursuing other fields to gain insight into how the sector functions. I am hard-pressed to think of another course or learning experience which better exemplifies Haas values than this one.

I would recommend this course to those who would like to learn more about impact investing and gain hands-on experience. Perhaps the biggest advantage is growing your network with the teachers, assigned mentor, and

professionals you connect with over the course of the semester. I wish the instruction at the beginning of the course had been at a slower pace and reinforced to promote deeper learned. Jeep and Adair are incredible assets to this course, and are extremely well informed and helpful. They really balance each other out well.

Yes definitely, you will be able to experience the entire lifecycle from sourcing a startup that suits your investment thesis to pitching it out to a very experienced investment committee. I would say it is an unprecedented opportunity. Yes, amazing and kind industry professionals that make this a hands on learning experience and class.

I would highly recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. This course was the best preparation for a VC career as I gained experience sourcing, diligencing, and analyzing start-ups for investment. We had VC advisors for each group, and networked with investors to source and review the start-ups. It's amazing practical experience, and will be invaluable for me to have this experience as I interview for future VC roles.

This course is excellent as long as you have a strong team who is engaged. I took this in my 3rd year of the EWMBA program, and I felt like it was a great way to put what I've learned at Haas to the test in terms of evaluating companies and determining their financial viability, etc. It's an amazing way to grow your network (through founder and fund conversations), and to learn more about a given impact space. I am walking away from this course not only with knowledge of what it's like to be a venture partner at a fund, but also much deeper knowledge about the startup space and how to evaluate companies. It also gives you great practice in presenting and pitching, which you don't always get in Haas classes. Highly recommend as long as you're willing to put in the time and the effort!

Yes! Best Value for not too much time AI course! Super helpful 3 weeks of lectures that basically cover all of New Venture Finance. Cool opportunity to learn about the VC and startup world. Try to join class with team interested in similar topics to get onto 1 team. Less work than it sounds like, mostly calls with startups that are always interesting. Yes, this is an awesome opportunity to practice being an impact VC and get real-world experience and connections that will benefit you if you choose to go into the industry. Even if you are not interested in working in impact investing, you get to explore a particular sector in-depth and strengthen your analysis, presentation, and decision-making skills. I would recommend this class to other Haas students! It was great to get practice impact investing

Absolutely -- I learned more in this class than my VC internships considering I was able to conduct all of the due- diligence calls myself which you rarely get to do at a firm. I felt like there was no unnecessary education -- everything was super relevant to a career in VC.
Yes. Really exciting and interesting, but you get as much as you put in, so be wary of how much time you can dedicate to the work.

Yes, this class has been exactly what I've come to Haas for - a practical understanding of how VC investments are made and negotiated. I only wish this class was longer and allowed us to invest in more companies over a longer period of time.
Yes

YES. Jeep and Adair are amazing instructors. They provide the right level of guidance and weekly support. Your team is selected by the professors and GSI (which can be a tossup), but the hands-on experience you get is invaluable. Where else do you get the chance to learn about Cap Tables, Term Sheets, Valuations and then reach out to 50 different startups and get to learn how to conduct due-diligence conversations and identify 'red flags v. green flags'! Yes! Great class, learned a ton, instructors treat you like actual VC partners and provide great feedback
Yes, it was one of the best classes I took at Haas. I was able to reach out to and talk to CEO's from companies/startups I would like to create in the future.

Yes, absolutely - there won't be another class like it that is experiential in a VC context. It's a great way to get your feet wet and see if you enjoy this space as well if you're considering it as a career path.

I am conflicted about this course. It was very difficult for me, but I think that is because of my learning style. The instructors are great, well-organized, and passionate. The almost pure group work was difficult for me though. Yes. They are both experienced professionals who can guide students to have a better understanding in VC-startup ecosystem.

Yes - I would highly recommend it. Recall that this course is quite intensive in terms of workload and also sometimes the ability to source deals. However, that said this course is a perfect primer to understand the VC world. Totally recommended. Build a strong relationship with them, as they teach you about VC while connecting you to the right people.

This class was my favorite capstone class mostly due to the hand-on experience and the opportunity to be a in the shoes of a VC investor. The class was a little under my radar during the bidding process, and I hope more people get the word out for future Haas students. I especially like how the professors went to lengths to create teams based on interests and industry experience. I've taken other classes where the material was interesting, but it was applied to a sector that had little to do with my professional career. The whole experience was first rate.

I would if they are interested in the VC space as well as Impact Investing, this course was great practice into the real thing. Be prepared to treat is like a part time internship with some typical work frustrations (from a team and "client" perspective). Overall though, a great change from typical lecture and case study courses.

If you're interested in impact investing, especially climate VC, this course is a must. Adair and Jeep are legends in the field and will give you the platform to build experience and a portfolio of work for yourself.

This class is one of the most worthwhile classes at Haas to get a better understanding of impact and venture investing. HIF equips you with great mentors and companies to connect with and provides great support along the way.

sections.goodFor: Anyone curious about VC or impact investing, beginner or experienced - you effectively do an associate's job for a semester and build a founder/Haas network; one landed an internship from it.
sections.notFor: Students who can't commit real time, or who want a lecture-structured class - it is mostly independent learning and your experience depends on a randomly assigned team.
sections.workloadNote: Short structured crash course in new venture finance up front, then roughly three months of real VC work - founder calls, sourcing, due diligence - largely independent and team-driven.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; work is team due diligence on real startups plus a brief front-end frameworks module. Grading itself is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: Two students flag that a good part of the experience depends on your randomly assigned group, and stress the real time commitment and heavy independent learning. No other complaints in 23 comments.
sections.quote: Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice.
comments: Absolutely! I keep telling everyone this is my MBA capstone, because it brings together everything I've learned in the MBA. I feel like I've actually gotten VC experience and have built up a pretty cool network of Haasies and founders Yes!
Absolutely. If you are even slightly curious about investing and impact investing, this class is great for intro as well as for experienced professionals.
Yes. Really knowledgeable professor.

Yes with the caveat it does depend on the team you get placed with, which is selected for you. This course is great because it gives real exposure and practice to startups, business models and funding. I got so much more out of this than a lecture and appreciate the hands on learning

Absolutely, take this class if you want to get a real experience of what it is like to be a venture capitalist. yes, 1000%. super practical crash course in new venture finance followed by a real application of VC investing for 3 months. one of the best semesters I've had at Haas.
YES - one of the best applied innovation classes I've taken! I took this and IBD and got great takeaways from both - the more real life application we can do in the classroom the better!
Yes, if you are a beginner in this space.

For anyone interested in VC, social impact, or impact investing, this is a must-take class! It's a lot of independent learning but I've learned more in this semester than I have in most other classes. If you're on the fence, take it! Absolutely. I took this class because I was curious about impact VC. I got that and so much more out of this class. I really owe my future career aspirations to this class.

Highly recommend. This was one of the most impactful courses to truly understanding the work of a VC investor. I learned a lot &, more importantly, had the chance to put my learnings into practice with numerous calls with startups Great class and one of the best I've taken at Haas.

YES, as long as you're committed to spending a solid time on it. Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice. Jeep and Adair are inspiring, knowledgeable and extremely accessible. One of my favorite classes!

I really learned a lot from this course - this course really teaches you how to be VC. I talked with many inspiring founders and learned a ton about the industry. There is a lot of work especially team work but the more time you spend the more rewarding it is.
Absolutely - best class I've taken.
Yes
If you are interested in how the VC due diligence process works from either the founder or the VC persepective, this course is awesome!

I would absolutely recommend this course! This was my favorite class at Haas. I learned a lot about impact investing. Take this if you're curious what impact investing is like. You do the job for a few months and can see if it's for you. This experience also helped me land an internship in the space.
Yes., Great course to take if you are interested in learning more about how venture capital works and being able to see it happen in action.
Yes,I've recommended the class to everyone who asked for what class to take in Spring

Absolutely. This class was very informative and took us through the journey of a what an associate working VC might do over the course of their company search. I liked that there was a brief structured portion of the class where we learned about frameworks and other basic industry knowledge, and that we had plenty of time for application in the real world.
This is the best course at Haas! You get to be an actual VC! Take this course even if you don't want to do VC, its just really good experience!!!

sections.goodFor: Students with no prior venture experience who want a real VC rep - sourcing deals, meeting founders, running diligence, pitching. Noted as flexible/remote-friendly for EWMBA after the first few weeks.
sections.notFor: People who already worked in venture (one says take a different Applied Innovation class), anyone not genuinely interested (it becomes a lot of work), and those expecting a real impact focus.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified but repeatedly called a heavy lift; about half the course is lab time. Load is elastic - meet minimum assignment requirements, or sink endless hours into sourcing and diligence.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; minimum assignment requirements plus sourcing, due diligence and pitch deliverables
sections.redFlags: 2 students say the 'Impact' name is a misnomer - the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses on market-rate returns. Workload is team-dependent, and the $75k check size makes sourcing hard.
sections.quote: Will add that the "Impact" naming is a bit of a misnomer -- from day 1, the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses heavily on market-rate returns.
comments: Yes
Absolutely. I wish I was able to take it sooner (it bid out when I was a first year). One of the most practical classes I took at Haas.
Yes. I believe anyone interested in venture capital and financing young companies with high potential should take this course.
yes! so fun getting our hands dirty with sourcing and due diligence. I realize there's still a lot of quant concepts I don't fully understand, but perhaps that is the reality of the industry.

Yes -- both Jeep and Adair were phenomenal instructors, and I found the overall course to be worthwhile, especially if you are aspiring to be in VC or otherwise just exploring it as a potential pathway. You really do get to act as a VC for the course of the semester, so it's a great opportunity to see how you like it and build some experience. The workload can be what you make of it -- if you/your team want to go all in, you could spend endless time sourcing and screening deals, diligencing, etc; you can fulfill minimum assignment requirements with a lot less work, though, if you don't feel passionate about investing a ton of time.

Will add that the "Impact" naming is a bit of a misnomer -- from day 1, the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses heavily on market-rate returns. Be warned if you are primarily taking this for the "Impact" spin, and know that it's really just traditional VC with a hint of impact framing.

This is a great class if you want to experience being a VC with lower stakes than in the real world. It is a heavy lift class and you need to be prepared to spend a lot of time sourcing deals, meeting founders and doing due diligence on the companies. Your experience will be very team dependent so how much work you do also depends on how engaged your team is. The professors are phenomenal and are always very willing to help students throughout.
Yes would recommend
100%!! Really great class. Honestly just wish I took it earlier as it would have helped me a lot!!
Yes I do. There is no better way to connect with start-ups, than saying that we can invest in them. Also, helps understand what a good start up is.
Yes, great way to get your hands dirty and practice sourcing and evaluation.
Yes I'd recommend this class, you are thrown into the deep end but you learn how to be a VC in a very hands on way, so it's worth it

Yes! if you are interested in learning about what it is like to be a VC but also want to focus on impact investing, this is the course to take! you will learn so much about another world of VC but also, it was really neat to learn about all the differnt companies in the different sectors where impact is needed.

Yes, I would recommend as long as they are interested in VC and/or impact investing. It gives real life hands-on experience on sourcing, performing due diligence and pitching. However if you are not very interested, it will be a lot of work and you won't enjoy.

Yes I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is interested in early-stage technology or VC investing. Anyone who is dissuaded by the "impact" framing of the class should speak to a past student who will surely emphasize the practical learning from the class and the very professionally applicable nature of the content. If you're interested in the real VC experience, it's the class that you must take. Although the workload may be higher than in other classes, the hands-on experience as a VC and learning is truly something that you want to get out of your MBA program.
Strongly recommend - very good opportunity to think and evaluate as a VC
Yes, this is the most practical and fun course I've taken at Haas. Very much recommend for quality of instruction, for anyone interested in impact investing or VC

If you have never done anything in venture before, then I 100% recommend this class. It's exactly what you would get from a venture internship, and Adair and Jeep provide a safe space to explore and learn. They are open, direct, and honest. I greatly appreciated their feedback. If you have been in venture before, then I don't think you need to take this class. I would invest your time learning something new in another Applied Innovation class.

Adair is a seasoned educator. You can tell that she is passionate about teaching and she really tries to decrease the amount of busy work in class. Jeep is a great investor. She's got incredible stories about what she has invested in and really encourages individuals to find their own passions / areas of investment. Both professors give up a lot of time to help students enter the vc space and riff off of each other. This is the first VC class I've taken at Haas where it's not a "bro" culture dominated space. Would highly recommend if you're interested in VC and/or talking to entrepreneurs. I would definitely recommend the Haas Impact Fund for those who are looking for hands on VC experience. It's a really fun class because you are actively sourcing real deals, so you meet with founders and do due diligence with real financials and materials from early stage companies. For EWMBA students - you have to get to campus by 4pm for a few weeks in the beginning of the semester, but then the rest of the semester you don't need to go to campus because you're coordinating remotely with your team. So it's actually quite flexible which can be especially good for EWMBA students. Lastly, Jeep and Adair are fantastic professors - getting to learn from them is a privilege. Really cool course but be prepared to dedicate the time and effort. The 75k check size is a bit of a challenge so be prepared to build and use your networks to access deals and improve your sourcing funnel. Adair and Jeep are amazing and it's worth taking the course just to work with them. But I can't emphasize this enough - the course requires time and there aren't any shortcuts at the end of the day so make sure you know what you're signing up for. Absolutely! Great way to learn what it takes to be a VC and guided by supportive, sharp advisors who bring experience from the field.

I would recommend this experiential learning course to anyone who is interesting in gaining quick learning and hands- on experience in VC. The impact part of the course is also meaningful, but it does not take away from the VC-learning aspect of the course. You have to plan on having a lot of time to do out of class work. This is a time intensive projec- based course; similar in the vein of time commitment to clean tech to market etc. Make sure your schedule allows you the time you need to do the work; as long as this is well set up for you, the course and instructors will deliver an awesome learning experience.
I would definitely recommend Haas Impact Fund to a fellow student. The class's hands-on-experience and material created a learning experience unique in the program. I really enjoyed this class.

I'd recommend this course to the students who are prepping to get into VC. It's a great class to network with VCs and founders. I've learned a lot from professors, mentors, founders, and investors. There is a lot of self-study involved as well, since half of the course is lab time.
Take this class if you want to work on investing for a potential move into the field (or to learn about being an angel).

sections.goodFor: Current or aspiring managers wanting a concrete 1:1 coaching framework, better questioning skills, and lots of live practice — applicable to personal life too.
sections.notFor: Only caveat raised is format: full-day Sunday sessions are long. No substantive content criticism appeared in any comment.
sections.workloadNote: Manageable, compressed into two Sunday sessions. Class time is dominated by small-group coaching practice and feedback reps rather than lecture; 'the more you put into it, the more you'll get out.'
sections.gradingBasis: In-class coaching practice and participation; grading not discussed.
sections.quote: The class can be long on a sunday but workload is manageable, and the more you put into it, the more you'll get out of it.
comments: This class is good at honing in on coaching vs therapy. It's good for anyone who wants to ultimately lead an organization and work on their interpersonal skills. The class can be long on a sunday but workload is manageable, and the more you put into it, the more you'll get out of it.

Highly recommend this class. It was one of the most practical, applicable courses I've taken at Haas. And, while I usually struggle with the length of Sunday classes, the amount of small group engagement and practice made the class length make sense to me
I definitely recommend. This is one of my favorite course by far. I have learned so much not only about coaching but also my life in just two Sundays.
Yes, must take. Some of the few very useful classes for your personal and professional life.
Yes because 1:1 coaching is important for managers
Would HIGHLY recommend this course and these instructors. one of my favorite Haas classes! So useful and will leverage these frameworks for the rest of my career. (and personal life!)

Yes, I would recommend to anyone who want to develop skills in coaching. The hands on practice was very effective. Great course for people who love to help unleash the potential in others! Helps you think about what it means to be a coach and how to be coached better as well.

This was a great course to learn how to coach without imposing your views on others and engaging empathetically and focusing on the outcome for your coach-ee. There is tons of practice to get good at the skill with enough flexibility for you to practice out your own style. Ultimately I would recommend this class to anyone looking to learn how to ask better questions and bring a meaningful impact to those you work and connect with.
Yes, it's very helpful to grow as a leader to understand coaching. The framework used was highly effective and something ill use the rest of my career

I would definitely recommend this course if you want to practice coaching. I thought I knew what being a good coach looked like before and I realized it was much harder than expected, so now I feel a lot more prepared to be a coach Yes
Yes, think coaching is a very important skill to learn and understand
Yes

Yes. This is not a too intense course but a great course to learn about coaching. It's easier said than done would recommend! very engaging and interesting class and learned a lot. really good way to practice coaching and get a full understanding of what it is. Left with a solid foundation of how to be a good coach and to practice it in reality.
Absolutely. I think the frameworks learned can easily be applied to situations in office or work personal relationships really easy. Love the toolkits I was able to learn over the two day class.
Yes

Absolutely! I really felt that a complex topic as becoming a coach was really well addressed from a theoretical level all the way to practicing, getting feedback, and getting in the reps. I felt how I improved and put into practice the things we learnt in just 2 days!
Yes! This was actually a really helpful class. I walked away with tools and frameworks I can apply with my team at work to be a better manager. This was well worth it!
Yes, thought the class structure was great.
Well designed and worth of enrollment. I think it would be very helpful to my future career

rows.title: Designing Futures: Technology & Society
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2021 Fall;2023 Spring;2024 Spring;2025 Spring;2026 Spring

comments: Thought provoking and enjoyable class. Amazing guest speakers. Sometimes unclear instruction on homework, but in those cases I felt it allowed more freedom of choice.
Yes - this is a fun class to flex your creativity and learn new design thinking methodologies.

I really liked this class and loved working with Sandeep, Joe, and Joanne — they are amazing / inspiring people. I think the class could be improved with more active / engaging in-class activities and discussion.
Absolutely. It was a fantastic way of doing design thinking in perhaps even more of a structured way. Would definitely recommend, it helps to have that background in advance though.

Yes!! This course was creative and interesting. It forces b-school students to think about solving problems in a different way. I love their methodology and teaching style. All three also made themselves readily available and were effective brainstorming partners. This has been one of my favorite courses at Haas. I think we're really lucky to have it offered!! 100% yes. Just a weird and wacky class for the nerds and creatives among us. Super fun and immersive. And the professors are amazing.

I found this class to be a wonderful way to learn and practice design thinking frameworks. It was also a lot of fun and a great way to push myself to think creatively. Definitely a unique course at Haas and a great complement to more traditional business courses.
Yes! This course really helped me think outside the box. I used to consider myself not creatively inclined, but this course really helped me develop that skill and use it in realistic situations.

Yes! This has been the best class I have taken at Haas. While there are lots of assignments, they are all really fun to do and have helped me learn so much. This class has really changed how I move through the world!
Yes - it's definitely out there, and probably not super applicable to a lot of immediate post-MBA jobs, but a great supplemental class to understand design and innovation.

This class is hands-on and different. Lots of design thinking. Wish it wasn't so strictly centered around climate change as I didn't know it would be before signing up. Knowledgable and kind professors though who have worked on great things at IDEO and have a lot of cool connections.

Yes. This class is a low lift and you get to learn a little bit more about a topic that may be interesting to you. I wouldn't think of it as a class, but more as an exercise on futuring - really suspending disbelief and waving a magic want for what a potential future could be. That's a very different skill than incremental design and is a welcome counterpoint to everything else that's taught in product/business design schools.

I'm glad I took the course, as it exposed me to some interesting ways of thinking about the future and being creative. I wish that I had more time outside of class to engage more with the readings, homework and thinking through the learnings - it felt somewhat rushed and forced in parts even though the workload is very manageable.

This was a great class to really hone your creative thinking skills and envision what the future might look like, as well as the signals that currently exist that might help make that future a concrete reality. The professors are all subject matter experts, and brought in a variety of speakers to discuss themes in innovation and futurism. Great class!

If you haven't taken a Design Thinking course before, I would take this course. I enjoyed the creativity I got to use. I would say that I'm not sure if I learned any tangible skills. More so I was able to be creative and think of fun and cool future ideas.

I would recommend for a lighter lift class that's centered around creativity, coming up with wacky ideas, and developing them within frameworks. You will be constricted by the theme for the particular semester, which changed each year. For example, this semester's theme was climate change so each group created a product idea by the end of the semester that addressed climate change in some way. It may not be the best idea to take this class of the theme is not something you have a strong interest in.

Yes. This is a really fun, worth-while course. Especially for students who want to develop their creativity and perhaps direct it towards brainstorming / ideating solutions. The worlds of sci-fi and business continuously influence one another. This course is a great introduction to that kind of cyclical, inspiring thinking.

Look, going in you have to know this is a strange class. Requirements and assignment criteria are sort of moving targets, and there's really no right answers at all. On the other hand, it's not just BS. So it's in this space between tangible and intangible, and you have to want to consciously opt-in to this experience where you aren't really sure where you'll be at the end. If you enjoy thinking about a nebulous future and trying to hone down your view of the future more, then this class is for you! It doesn't fall into too much of the Design Thinking greatest hits and the main value is in the relationships I built with other classmates, as well as with the professor team. This class isn't for everyone, but it's not a ton of work (the weekly assignments are usually somewhat light), and it may change how you see the world a bit.
Yes
I would strongly recommend this course to anyone interested in exploring how to think about the future and how to explore what business opportunities might exist in the future.

I'm torn here. I really like all of the instructors and how much passion they put into the class and their overall responsiveness. However, I did not feel like I learned anything that I could truly integrate into my career in the way that I hoped. It wasn't super practical and I feel like it will be difficult to explain in different contexts beyond innovation and design. Probably my least favorite course I took this semester, which is unfortunate.

Yes. If you're really not into thinking about far off hard-to-imagine things, and you want to only discuss something that exists in front of you, don't take it. But I genuinely think for all different kinds of disciplines and careers it's a useful and fun exercise to try to compile signals and extrapolate way out into the future, and it's really hard to do that often without something like this class and a pretty regimented process to do so. I found it really useful to take some of my own ideas I'm tinkering around in my own time/career and just push them further.

It was ok! Lots of homework assignments but they were fun. The instructors were lovely people. It was a nice deep dive into design, though probably hard to take the learnings out into the real world. For me, it felt like a fun and creative brain break every week.
Great course that provides a unique opportunity to 'think differently' during the semester. Highly worthwhile. sure. Its a good design course.

This was one of my favorite classes!!! Really interesting content and empowered me to think in a different way. The professors have perfected this course over time––perfect balance between workload and engaging content.

Absolutely! This course is a must. Designing futures is one of the best courses I've taken at Haas and I'm really proud of the work we've done in labs. The course is very useful for those envisioning careers in creativity–unlocked fields like entrepreneurship, venture capital, sustainability, social impact, healthcare, etc. There are unique ways to learn to disrupt the status quo and learn through divergent futures.

I would definitely recommend this course to anyone who wants to learn a different way of creative thinking that's still very applicable to the business world. The facilitators were amazing and created a very thoughtful and fun class environment.

Absolutely. This class is creative and fun and gives you a different perspective from which to base your strategic thinking. It reminded me that business can be fun and wacky but at the same time have serious consequences if we're not able to recognize our agency and influence over the future. It?s a must class for anyone that sees themselves as a leader who?s business decisions can have a significant impact on the future of society. Therefore all of us should take it.
Yes, I learned in class and teachers have a good heart & genuinely care. Interesting and thoughtprovoking, and useful tools to apply for post MBA life.
I would strongly recommend this course – it made me think in a different way in comparison to my other Haas courses. I really truly enjoyed the class and our final presenation
Yes! 100%. Not completely sure if I'll use it in my career. But it was really fun to think about the future. The framework is also helpful to think about signal and future scenarios.

Yes – it is a helpful structure and framework to look at the future with different tools and lenses. It's also fun to work in a group to come up with different scenarios of what the future could look like.
Yes! Highly recommend it!

Taking this class is like a breath of fresh air in Haas. It makes us connect to our creative selves and have fun with it! Material is not very applicable but it is a course for those who want to get connected to our creative part! Yes! Good class with fun environment for learning Design Thinking methodology.

Yes – I think a 7 week course made a lot of sense and I almost wished each of our classes had a bit more engagement and group exercises as a way to help implement some of the material we learned. Maybe small or short exercises? But overall just to get a taste of design thinking I thought it was very helpful

Yes, this class helps you think about ideas in a way that is different than most other Haas classes. It is fun and very useful to think about topics in a future-looking and intentional design perspective.
Highly recommend this class. It is an engaging creative exercise and it is interesting to see where your team can wonder about the future, and where others wonder about as well.

Def take it to bond with your classmates for one last time. The most creative class I've taken at Haas and chill. Workload is slightly more than 1-credit with sth due every week (although it's just p/f)
Totally!!

I definitely recommend this class! It is a good space to think outside of the box, leave your comfort zone and think about the implications of current technologies or trends. It is a class that encourages you to be creative, take risks and link your future scenarios with current signals so that they are based on facts and potential changes but not solely on imagination. The professors are great, come from very cool backgrounds and make everyone feel heard!

Yes. This course was a great opportunity for me to flex the creative side of my brain. I do not consider myself a creative person, so developing frameworks and thought process about the future really helped me lean in to that aspect. I'm grateful that the instructors made the course welcoming and approachable to all. Working in a group and thinking about the future was a highlight as I got to learn from my classmates perspectives
Yes. Good if you're looking for a class that's a relatively light workload and to challenge your thinking to be more boundless. But class takeaways are more of the intangibles.
Yes, it is a great course that helps you think outside the box.

Yes - highly recommend! This was my favorite elective at Haas. It gave me the opportunity to scratch a creative itch that I felt was missing from the Haas curriculum. The professors and so knowledgeable and have many interesting perspectives/experiences to share and its clear that they have put a lot of time and effort to refine this course based on previous years' feedback. I think they've nailed it!
Yes, they are great

Of course I will recommend this class, probably top 3 classes I took at Haas. The opportunity to have 3 professors in such a small class is incredible, also all of them are actively working in amazing stuff, so they are close to what innovation and the future looks. This is an opportunity to go deep into the future, use a proper framework, and come up with a story that is actually not that far from reality.

I would recommend Designing the Future. I thought it was going to be a bit too "fluffy" but I found that it was actually quite useful. The ability to develop and apply frameworks to think about different visions of the future seems quite useful, and I'm sure I'll use it. Joe, Joanne, and Sandeep are enthusiastic and they have made interesting careers in part by using the skills that they teach, so it's clear that they are "practicing what they preach" so to speak. On the whole it's a fun class with a reasonable workload that I'd sign up for again.

Yes! This class feels like a fantastic departure from the Haas bubble. It challenges you to think in completely different ways and flex different muscles than the ones we rely on for so much of the MBA. It creates space for writing, creativity, innovation, and strategic thinking in ways that will absolutely be helpful post-grad regardless of industry. strongly recommend this class
I loved the course!! It was refreshing and great to be able to discuss the future in a structured way. Really glad I took it and all three Professors were super knowlegeable and helpful
Yes! Loved it. So fun and the perfect class to take as a 2nd year

Yes. The instructors and this course are by far the best at Haas. There is a humanness to the material and the teachings that cannot be replicated in other classes. Truly 10/10 and again, my only critique is that I wish it were longer.
I would 100% recommend this class. It is so fun, not a lot of work. You will enjoy every class. Just make sure to pick a good team. Stay Weird.

Yes, I would recommend it to anyone looking to develop their long-term outlook and strategic thinking. Given that they have actual experience, they're able to share how their teachings apply to real-world cases and keep the class relevant.

sections.goodFor: Students who want creative, abstract, design-thinking work that is unlike other MBA classes - useful for startup/VC thinking and long-horizon strategy.
sections.notFor: Students who want technical or immediately applicable hard skills; one calls it 'effectively creative writing' and one found the team project a difficult waste of time.

Yes! I think it's a fun class and provides an alternate perspective on strategy formation from the traditional "gather the data, make a hypothesis, drive to it." It's also a great class to reflect on big problems that you may not think about in depth otherwise.

I would absolutely recommend this course. It is somewhat fast in this one-unit iteration, but the instructors are good people and thoughtful guiders of discussion. It could easily have devolved into something ungrounded and nebulous, and it's a credit to both the instructors and the rest of the class that it did not.

I highly recommend this class! It was very provocative, fun and different compared to other classes I've taken at Haas.
