10/10 amazing class! The most engaging and estimulating I had during my MBA. 2 hours of my week where I forgot about the existence my cell phone.

Absolutely! This class and it's instructors really let you broaden your horizon and think beyond your immediate priorities and interests. It's also a super fun and playful way to learn design thinking tools.

This will feel like a different kind of class than the typical MBA class but in the best way. The teachers are seasoned professionals from the design world and show how knowing how to think about the future is a critical skill personally and professionally.
Yes! This is a great class to practice creative thinking and learn about strategizing for an unknown future in a constructive way.

Best class I had at Haas. Finally was challenged to think. yes!!

Take this class and actually put some time and effort into the work.
Yes!! This is one of the best and most powerful courses I've taken at haas. In a moment of rapid change, it's one of the few classes that teaches a structure for how to think about the future.
I would! Great conversations. I looked forward to this class every week. With all this uncertainty, this class teaches to accept and think three steps ahead

I ABSOLUTELY recommend. If you're looking for a class that helps you think where "disruption" comes from and non- linear frameworks to understand the world, this is your class. Also expect to give "life" to your own rabbit holes and dystopian/utopian futures - which was really fun:)

Yes! They were all exposed to IDEO at a point in their careers and provides best in class design thinking methods I loved this class!! Was one of my favorites at Haas, really stretched my thinking, and was well executed class. I really appreciate that this class helps shift my way of thinking and prompts more outside the box ways of seeing the world and thinking about trends and futures. I think this is a very applicable class for strategic business thinking, but beyond that a really fun way explore the edge of the latest trends and shifts shaping our world today. Really excellent teaching team, great structure, tight syllabus, high ROI, fun creative class.

Yes! This course is way different thana most of the courses in Haas. This a course that takes you out of the comfort zone, it challenge your traditional structure of thinking and take your imigination to places you won't imagine The frameworks learned during the course were in stark contrast to the standard business education, and were incredibly generative for thinking about the future of tech, work, and life given changes we see in every facet of life due to AI and more. The workload was manageable and made sense for the duration and credit for the class. I only wish this could have been a bit longer of a course (~10 weeks) so that we could dig deeper into the scenarios and learn to internalize the frameworks more.

Yeah definitely! You need to be someone who's willing to embrace their more creative / unstructured thinking side to enjoy this class. That exercise in and of itself has me thinking more critically about the world around me, and I think the skills I built in this class will be valuable in my future career endeavors.

DEFINITELY. 100% my favorite course. It massaged my brain in a way that other Haas classes have not. I loved how much creativity and collaboration came out of it. Plus, the teaching team gives INCREDIBLE feedback.

Absolutely! Definitely take this class if you care about where the future of things are headed (you should). Honestly think this should be part of the core curriculum. It's also a lot of fun and wonky and nice balance to some of the more technical and traditional hard-skill MBA classes. And yet it's still a hard-skill, just an overlooked one. Take it, take it!

Interested course that made you think about the preferred world you want to live in. Required group efforts for almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, but fun if you enjoy brainstorming and unique presentations as a way to think outside the box.
YES! This has been my favourite class at Haas, and has genuinely impacted the way I view the world. I'll be looking for signals and reading op-eds from the future for years to come.

Yes! Yes!! Very unique course that gives you an opportunity to practice thinking about the future in a structured way. I loved coming to class every week and it was genuinely fun to work on our final project, as you get to focus on a topic that interests you

Yes because it allows for the tip of the iceberg to be encountered around social issues, but be prepared and wary for the class to be extremely capitalistic without much data/room for counterarguments. When issues and questioning of the status quo came up, many times, the instructors didn't have the answers or relied on conceptual concepts. Math or data isn't used much in this class to back up arguments rather than descriptive statistics. This class allows someone to be creative around solving social issues, but at its underlying core, the course doesn't answer the crucial answer in its entirety of how do you solve or combat social issues. The course feels that it helps one brainstorm bandaid business oriented solutions without exploring issues at its core and how to truly combat it. Moreover, the course makes a lot of excuses for the pitfalls of capitalism and expects it to be passed off. For example, when discussing compensation structures and how they're centered around the course's impact triangle concept, it became dicey with no solutions offered. One thing to point out is that readings really push the capitalist perspective to social issues rather than diverse issues, particularly in overworking workers and labor by stretching them thin for value. Burnout is accepted and normalized. Another example would be each business leader that came in already operated with mindsets that they're doing their best without much emphasis on how they're solving the underlying root causes of each problem. All in all, the course allows for a student to be challenged and explore different models out there and it's good to address the overlaying present issues, but not great at addressing underlying issues and deriving a model from there. Case studies, videos, and resources are great!

sections.goodFor: Graduating seniors and grad students, first-gen/low-income students, and international students new to the US financial system; anyone with no personal finance background.
sections.notFor: International students who don't plan to stay in the US (content is US-specific). One student found the videos and lectures hard to stay engaged with; another wanted more relevant assignments.
sections.workloadNote: Repeatedly called simple, easy and manageable — 'a really easy course.' Weekly lectures plus assigned videos; assignments are applied (open accounts, budget, review credit).
sections.gradingBasis: Not explicitly detailed; assignments and video-based coursework are referenced. Several students describe it as low-pressure.
sections.redFlags: Minor and non-recurring: 2 students found the video/lecture format hard to pay attention to, 1 wanted better assignments, 1 flagged some weeks as excessively jargon-heavy.

Definitely take this class. The community is awesome, and getting three units of credit to work on your own startup, with real time and resources to build momentum, is a pretty rare opportunity. The class also gives you credits for Lovable, AWS, Claude Pro, and other tools, which makes a real difference when you're building.

Compared to programs like Lean Launch Pad, which lean heavily on customer interviews alone with a tight weekly cadence of identical deliverables for every team, this is much more flexible. You'll still do customer discovery, but you'll also have the structure to leverage the newest AI tools and actually ship in parallel. Different startups can be at different stages — you can pivot, break up with your team and join a new one, start over, and run customer discovery and building in parallel. This structure also reflects how products are actually getting built today. Software is so much cheaper to ship now, so customer discovery and building can happen in parallel, not in the old waterfall sequence of research-then-build. The class mirrors how real startups operate, which makes the experience much more applicable to the real world. Progress is defined in terms of what's actually moving the needle for your team's specific venture, not busywork deliverables. It feels like a real incubator, not a academic checklist.

How the class is structured: you're making real progress every week. Class sessions usually open with an hour topic overview from the professors, followed by a guest speaker, and then dedicated mentoring time where you can get advice from the week's in person mentors and collaborate with teammates and other peers on whatever challenges you're working through. The mentor program is a real highlight. There's a deep roster of mentors brought in from a wide range of backgrounds and industries, and you have choice in who you work with. Combined with the peer collaboration in class, the community feels built in and there to support everyone.

Set your expectations going in: if you're looking for a tightly structured curriculum with a lot of rigorous frameworks, this may not be that. But if you come in thinking of it as a great incubator community led by Omri (who's an exceptional teacher and infuses life lessons alongside entrepreneurship lesson) you'll get a ton out of it. He's beloved for good reason. One signal of how inspiring this community is: about 20 of the 27 teams from this cohort are continuing their ventures past the end of the class. That speaks for itself. Heads up that it's a lot of work, plan for it to take meaningful time and energy. But if you're game for that, you'll learn a ton.

Even if you're not sure entrepreneurship is your long-term path, this class is still worth taking. With AI, the lines between PM, engineer, designer, and user researcher are collapsing, we may not even have separate roles for much longer, just "builders." This class is one of the best opportunities at Haas to practice being an "AI builder", wearing all those hats at once. You'll do real customer research, real building, and real iteration alongside teammates with different perspectives, with your ideas challenged by real customers. The broader skills: flexible thinking, customer empathy, the ability to pivot and learn from your learnings, humility, the willingness to try different creative approaches, are applicable far beyond entrepreneurship. I'd recommend this for anyone with curiosity about AI, entrepreneurship, product, or even just what it's like to spend a semester working with a team on a creative project. I highly recommend taking this class because it gives you the opportunity to actually build a product and learn through practice. However, I suggest that students come in with a validated idea (for example, already having done 20–30 customer interviews); otherwise, you may end up spending half of the course on customer discovery, while teams that start with a concrete idea can use the time to build and iterate on their product. I would even recommend taking Lean Launchpad, which focuses heavily on customer discovery, before this class so that you can get the most benefit from the experience.

rows.title: Strategically Managing Healthcare Policy - Washington Campus

comments: Healthcare policy was one of my favorite, if not most favorite, course I've taken at Haas. The learnings and insights from key opinion leaders in Washington and Haas faculty were unparalleled. Absolutely take this course if you're in healthcare or policy, ideally in-person.
yes best class so far

The complexity of the healthcare system in the United States is something that is often overlooked, but it is crucial for your career and for you personally. It's also important to be educated on the topic to contribute to a better future for US policy.

Yes. I would to all medical providers. I have not learned these materials in medical school, my training, and my long career. The present healthcare system is not economically sustainable. We need more impactful changes and innovations to pull us out of our mess.

Kim is awesome, no doubt about any of the courses that she has given and had heard from fellow students was true picture. She has broader knowledge about health care and healthcare policies or pharmacy or you name it she will teach you so many ways to look at the problem. I feel confident that I can take what I learned into my work.

I would absolutely recommend this course for anyone who wants to know "how the sausage is made" with regards to how policies are instigated, influenced and interpreted by many different political entities in Washington DC.

Absolutely!!!! Yes! If there's only one course you do in Haas, please make it this one. One of my favorite classes I've taken thus far. For how much Berkeley touts itself as rich with entrepreneurship resources, I've been generally quite disappointed with the offerings -- ESPECIALLY for those who are called to make an actual positive impact through business (and not just market that they do) and/or who are not interested in building VC funded businesses that must scale exponentially. For the 2nd half of every class, Gloria + Kris brought in CEOs and Founders of amazing companies like Burt's Bees, SunRun, Forum Mobility, Sesame Workshop, Guild Education, just to name a few...

Gloria and Kris' strengths both lie in their experience, compassion, and perfect mix of expertise/intelligence and humility. Unlike most of my classes, especially Core, this class felt directly applicable and relevant to me as an experienced entrepreneur. I started another business during this class (one I thought I might have to wait until I retired to do)!

Also, as a woman of color, I also personally found myself feeling so so comfortable and inspired in class in ways that I never felt throughout any of my Core + Elective classes to date. It makes a difference to see oneself at least a little in the faculty.
Yes! I really like the connection of content-->case-->speakers of the case!
Yes - guest speakers and professors are really inspiring!

This is one of the BEST courses I have taken at Haas! This should be a core class at Haas - this is such an important, much needed class for MBAs. Speakers in this class inspired me and reassured me in our abilities to create change in this world

I would absolutely recommend this course to any Haas student interested in making an impact. The quality and caliber of this class is hard to overstate. Every week we would have phenomenal speakers come to class - often the CEOs of major social impact organizations - come to speak with us and share their experiences and insights. We would be given cases, and then the protagonists of those cases would somehow miraculously show up in our class to be speak to us. It was amazing. The class was always full - no one ever wanted to miss it. It was so good that we even had many alumni auditors who came back to school just sit in and listen.
yes strongly

Any MBA (or other grad student) interested in social impact?whether working in mission-driven org/role or starting their own social enterprise?should take this class! This class is the ideal mix of case method and traditional frameworks tailored to social impact topics AND amazing guest speakers from all types of orgs and topical issue areas. You'll learn both theoretical frameworks and quite concrete concepts like what type of legal structure to choose for an org, pros and cons of various funding and revenue models, and how to think about impact measurement and evaluation. This was also the first semester this class was taught, so I can only imagine it getting better as the instructors implement feedback?which they truly value and ask for at the end of each class meeting.

I will highly recommend this course to anyone interested in social impact. Kristin and Gloria were both amazing instructors, and bought a wealth of knowledge and expertise in social impact and I eel like my perspective has broadened so much after this class. The rich diversity of speakers that were part of each class were also top-notch. Literally having speakers who were the protagonist for each case study was mind blowing.

I would 1000% recommend this course to anyone who wants to make an impact through their careers. As an EWMBA student in my 3rd and last year, this has been the most inspiring and best value class I have taken. This is saying a lot considering that I am generally a staunch believer that no 3 unit class is worth its value -- this class has proved to be the 1 exception so far. The class is set up so that each session has 1 case discussion, some class discussion, and then a guest speaker -- who usually the case was based on! The opportunity to do a class study and then speak directly to leaders within the companies and hear everyones inspiring journeys was a unique experience I haven't gotten from any other course so far. It was very well-structured around the impact triangle, and learning different frameworks to create an optimal business model for social impact. On top of that, the instructors Gloria and Kris are incredibly experienced as social entrepreneurs, and really care about teaching this course effectively. They even took the effort to remember everyone's names -- not something I've seen in other classes. I'm glad I decided to take this class (1st time it was offered) and again would fully recommend it!!

This is one of the best classes I had at Haas. Gloria and Kristin are so inspiring, and they put so much heart into this class. Speakers are amazing, cases are amazing, and learnings are amazing. This class is the most transformative class you will find in Haas! The professors are highly motivated and really driven to making not just the class experience great, but also be a great network outside of class. Most worth it 3 credit course!
YES!!!! Take this course - it is amazing!

The class format was such that each guest speaker spent about half their time taking questions from the class, and it's not a huge class, so it made for very intimate and engaging conversations. A huge takeaway from this class for me was what it takes to be a leader that cares about and delivers on social impact. If that's not you.... why are you even at Haas?
Yes, this course gave me interesting perspective about social impact not only in non-profit space but also in for profit landscape. Many applicable framework and amazing guest speakers.

The course is designed super intentionally and it is entirely case- based, with discussion of real companies operating within the social impact space each week, plus awesome guest speakers relevant to each case every single week. The group project is a bit more time-intensive than other classes with similar credits - I feel it is closer to an AI project than a "normal" group project, but it is fine overall. Absolutely! Kris and Gloria care so deeply about the structure of the curriculum, the AMAZING speakers they bring in and bring in weekly course concepts to life, and sharing both the funder and social entrepreneur sides of the ecosystem. I highly recommend this class for anyone remotely interested in how they can integrate social impact into their career or personal lives. Don't miss this class!

I would highly recommend this course to any student interested in social impact. Yes, I highly recommend this class for anyone interested in the intersection of social impact and business. The intention, care, and rigor that the syllabus is put together with is unparalleled. Gloria and Kris are incredible and care so deeply about their students and motivating social impact work. I loved the " ask Gloria and Kris " sessions sprinkled throughout the course which felt like fireside chats - they both have such deep and diverse social entrepreneurship experience and general life experience to share that it's such a treat to hear and learn from them. Yes! great calss for anyone trying to work in the social impact space and learn more about the trade-offs and frameworks in the space.

Yes because it allows for the tip of the iceberg to be encountered around social issues, but be prepared and wary for the class to be extremely capitalistic without much data/room for counterarguments. When issues and questioning of the status quo came up, many times, the instructors didn't have the answers or relied on conceptual concepts. Math or data isn't used much in this class to back up arguments rather than descriptive statistics. This class allows someone to be creative around solving social issues, but at its underlying core, the course doesn't answer the crucial answer in its entirety of how do you solve or combat social issues. The course feels that it helps one brainstorm bandaid business oriented solutions without exploring issues at its core and how to truly combat it. Moreover, the course makes a lot of excuses for the pitfalls of capitalism and expects it to be passed off. For example, when discussing compensation structures and how they're centered around the course's impact triangle concept, it became dicey with no solutions offered. One thing to point out is that readings really push the capitalist perspective to social issues rather than diverse issues, particularly in overworking workers and labor by stretching them thin for value. Burnout is accepted and normalized. Another example would be each business leader that came in already operated with mindsets that they're doing their best without much emphasis on how they're solving the underlying root causes of each problem. All in all, the course allows for a student to be challenged and explore different models out there and it's good to address the overlaying present issues, but not great at addressing underlying issues and deriving a model from there. Case studies, videos, and resources are great!

If you are interested in private equity, this is your course at Haas. The teaching style is vastly different than the mind- numbing academic approach of other classes. It's real-world with tons of guest speakers and a very direct feedback approach from instructors. Not for everyone, and for that reason it is a solid class--the instructors do not try to please every student but rather try to be honest, realistic and realistic. In short, the feel of the class reflects the feel of the private equity world. Recommended.

I would recommend this course to anyone new to the PE or M&A space as it provides a great overall picture of how the industry works and how value is created. I would not recommend this course for those that already have prior experience in these roles or functions.

This is a must-take class! Many concepts and frameworks can be applied to industries other than PE&LBO, e.g. startup, VC, small to large corporations how to operate a business in the right way, and what are important to create value. Yes, there are some important frameworks we learn about PE and deal making

Yes, for whose who already in this industry, this is a booster; for those who want to be into, this is a good starter Absolutely incredible class!! Stellar instructors that have revolutionized an industry and are considered legends! Learning from this teaching team has been a privilege and Haas need to make all classes like this one. Absolutely recommend!! Top 2 of the classes I have taken at Haas.
Yes, This is a very good course and for me personally will use what I have learnt so far.

I would HIGHLY recommend this class for anyone interested in learning more about private equity. This was one of the most well-worth classes I've taken at Haas. You get the opportunity to be taught by the best and brightest in the PE industry. The guest speakers were amazing, and were directly involved in the case studies that we learned in class. Can't recommend this class enough. Take it.

Absolutely, the experiential nature of the class, working on the leading cases, world-class speakers, you name it. Class requires being present & putting in your best effort to get the best out of the class.
Yes its one of the best - just wish it was in person.
I would recommend this course to future students.

Yes, I think this course was one of the courses I will take away for years after graduation. It is a ton of work and I cannot stress how important it is to find a strong reliable team going in, but the more work you put in, the more you get out of it (guaranteed)!
No. The professor does not add any valuable insights to the material. He does however bury his students in absurd amounts of work beyond any other 2 credit course I've taken at haas
I would recommend taking a 1 unit course on this subject. I would not recommend wasting 2 unit, primarily because the material is repetitive.

I am on the fence about this class. If you don't already have a finance background, you won't learn a lot of finance skills in this class. Similar, like me, if you have somewhat of a finance background, you also won't go into too much depth to cover buyouts. Could be interesting as there are a lot of guest speakers who work in different facets of LBOs (i.e., operators, mid-market investors), high-level strategy content, but I would only loosely categorize this class as a finance offering. Typical homework was strategy write-up and we had a couple of class projects that were more focused on presentation building.

1000% I would recommend this class to anyone. The learnings especially on value creation and leadership at portfolio companies are invaluable. You rarely get insights from professionals of the caliber of the guess speakers in a very intimate set up. I was also impressed by the high level of engagement Peter and Sam were able to get from all students even though the class was on Zoom. The GSI also does an amazing job in keeping the class interactive and engaging. All around an A-Class Team of instructors delivering A-Class learning experience.

Highly recommended, definitely worth 1 credit.
Yes, absolutely

I would 100% recommend this class and Sam as an instructor. He is real world professional who brings great examples to class!
yes.
100% - excellent professor

Yes for sure! Yes definitely
Yes! its a good intro to LBO and very interesting insight in the industry as well!
Yes. Great intro to the LBO Frameworks. Sad this is professor Sam's last year teaching this course.
It's a good course for people interested in Private Equity.

I would highly recommend Sam because he is very organized and makes a complex industry simple. Highly recommend taking this class as it will provide valuable learning for anyone pivoting in to finance field. I would recommend if they are looking to get into a finance field.
Yes
Definitely! Top 3 finance class so far. Didn't felt bored at all

providing a good introduction of PE and LBO.

The highest ROI class I've taken at Haas. Highly recommended!
