Absolutely yes! I have learned an incredible amount of things about audience-specific pitching that I didn?t even know existed. I think every single student should take this class because it gives you the necessary tools to be able to communicate effectively in the world, regardless of your expertise or goals.
I would recommend this course to a fellow student that is interested in getting more practice in public speaking and learning practical skills to increase their presentation skills.
Yes - Has great content and effective teaching methodology + Creates an inclusive classroom
He is a master in his class, if you want to see a fundamental change in yourself, attend this class. I am very sure you'll leave with something more than you ever imagined.
Good class to take. Blends storytelling and a more business approach to public speaking.
Definitely recommend!!! Professor is skilled in teaching and provides practical steps and guidance on how to be a better communicator
This is a great course and opportunity to practice and sharpen your communication in a supportive environment, with innovative tools and approach. Highly recommended.
Of course.
The course is very practical.
100000% no one should leave Haas without taking this course
Yes it's amazing to see how much my peers and I progressed after just 2 days of class
yes
Yes, absolute recommend! Really useful and love all the real-life scenarios
Absolutely
Yes I would recommend this course. Very good practice and applicable to all professional fields.

Yes, I would recommend, but just make sure that you are always on time to Adam?s classes, and understand that his grading philosophy may be unusual, as he graded most students? first assignment very low, even before the first class, to showcase where we?re starting from and how much we will earn. Also, the class is very structured, so just something to keep aware of. But he is an expert in the field, and a very thoughtful person who wants us all to succeed. And gives excellent feedback.

Yes, it's the best soft skill class taught in Haas, very practical, unlike other course like leadcomm, it is more applicable to real work environment. For example, it taught you to use a very simple ladder framework, but it's so powerful that you can apply in all kinds of scenarios, ranging from hosting meeting, maintaining friendships, to pitch in startup competitions.
Yes, I would recommend. This is a good class that helps your become a better speaker and communicator.
Helps you communicate at different levels and effectively. I learned the importance of breathing and pacing my speech, in addition to use great hooks to grab people's attention.
I also learned the importance of brining in your ask early on in the pitch.
Overall recommend the course
Favorite class so far, not only it taught me how to manage effective communication with relevant tools, but also helped me understand better Why we communicate.
Yes; useful class to take if you are actively working on a pitch
Yes
Great course, especially if you have some specific pitch you want to work on
If you need practical structured ways to improve presentations, this class will give you what you want in an environment that sets you up for success.
YES, because it is a great way to mentally begin the journey of becoming a better presenter and honing that skill Yes
Strongly recommend, the best mba class so far
Highly recommend, class was pleasantly uncomfortable and a lot of fun.
Absolutely recommend it. One of the best courses to put your 1 credit towards. Course leaves you with practices, tools and frameworks to ace any presentation or conversation.

Yes 100% - especially if you are an international student. Adam values all voices in the class equally and helps you become a better presenter when speaking in english. If you want to work on your pronunciation, avoid filler words, practice speaking without memorising your script- this is the class for you

100%. Copying in my previous response: This was one of the best classes I've taken at Haas. Adam's gift is breaking down the nerve wracking art of giving a solid pitch — it's uncanny. I'm leaving feeling 5x more confident in my public speaking and extemporaneous abilities.

One of the top classes at Haas! Applicable to any field, super interactive and engaging, and frameworks that will benefit me for life. We can all improve how we communicate, and even though the class is focused on refining a "pitch", the tools included can be applied to any situation where you're speaking - from public impromptu presentations to 1:1 conversations. The class itself was full of interactive activities and stories from the professor. The day flew by. I'd highly recommend this course to anyone at Haas. Even better if you can take it in person! Highly recommend this course, even if students think they communicate well already. This class stretches you to learn by putting you out of your comfort zone and making you practice the concepts in real-time.

Adam was also great at keeping the flow of the class going, knowing that the class is 2 full days (9-5pm). He incorporated different modalities (big group and small group work, individual work, video assignments and asynchronous work). I was energized throughout the day and felt like the time flew by. The concepts were also very clear and easy to grasp but also apply to real-world situations immediately. This class is great value considering its 1 credit but the learning is very applicable and something I see myself using long term.
Yes, definitely. It's awesome.
Yes! Such a great, interactive class that provides you with skills that will directly help you in your professional life and beyond. The frameworks that you learn are so valuable
Yes!

I've taken a variety of 1 credit leadership or communications courses at Haas and this one was the most impactful. We had so much time to practice our pitches, get feedback and refine. Adam provided useful frameworks that I will be using in my presentations going forward.
Absolutely if you want to learn how to present effectively! My interviewing and pitching skills increased by over 500% from this instructor. Must take!

sections.goodFor: Students with a specific pitch they care about, and anyone anxious about public speaking who wants a safe space plus storytelling frameworks.
sections.notFor: Students without a specific pitch (learnings stay limited), those wanting small-group coaching (try Storytelling for Leadership), and anyone impatient with workshop-style exercises.
sections.workloadNote: Two full Saturday 9-5 weekend sessions; work is preparing and iterating a personal pitch plus in-class exercises. Little outside-class load described.
sections.gradingBasis: Personal pitch development/iteration and class assignments tied to lecture concepts; not detailed further.
sections.redFlags: 4 of 21: fluffy workshop exercises and reviewing YouTube videos not worth two full Saturdays, class too large for real individual coaching, and one says the instructor did not start sessions on time.
sections.quote: I would recommend this course to anyone who has a specific pitch they want to practice. If you don't have anything specific, your learnings will be limited.
comments: Yes you should absolutely take this class. Don't worry - it's a safe space even if you're scared of public speaking like me. You will learn so much and it will be very empowering. Adam is a really inspiring person to meet too. Yes, I would. Despite the fact that it's a weekend class, I feel like I got a lot of value out of being in this course. Adam made the class fun and interactive, and I think he focuses clearly on the takeaways he wants you to leave class with which I greatly appreciated.
Yes
Yes! Nice to get a different perspective on a very relevant topic - frameworks are easy to absorb and very applicable for life

I highly recommend this class to anyone who has struggled with public speaking and in particular short pitches or storytelling. It is one of my favorite classes at Haas and well worth the weekend spent.
Yes, learning from Adam and his strong professional background is an amazing opportunity to improve in public speaking and delivering impactful and engaging messages

Adam is an expert communicator and facilitator. His command of storytelling techniques and ability to coach others is perfect for this course: he has crafted an experience that is interactive, insightful, and dynamic. Working on a personal pitch that was important to us make the topics personal and tangible, and the iterating on our and others'pitches revealed many opportunities for improvement in our individual journeys. Class assignments were also well suited for practicing concepts covered in lecture. The frameworks introduced were highly applicable and relevant, and I appreciated how he incorporated the feedback and suggestions given after day 1 into day 2 in order to address the needs students raised.Each class session, I was surprised at how the 8 hours passed by quickly. Overall, a wonderful experience and the highest value weekend class I have taken at Berkeley as an FTMBA student. Highly recommended. I would recommend this course to anyone who has a specific pitch they want to practice. If you don't have anything specific, your learnings will be limited.
Yes

Yes, for anybody looking to get some framework and thought process behind how to effectively communicate in front of an audience, then this is your course. It's not life changing, but a sufficiently good value add
Absolutely! I loved spending my weekend days with Adam and learning from his diverse experience.

I recommend this class most if you have something you need to pitch that you are passionate about. I chose the wrong pitch topic initially and although I could have changed it, I never did and I think you get more out of the class if you have something you're really excited about.
Adam is great, and has a ton of interesting experience.
Sure.
Yes. Great opportunity to feel more comfortable with public speaking
Yes

Not really. The course and instructor reviews set my expectations high and this course failed most of them. While very accomplished and well meaning, the instructor needs to upgrade how workshoppy this course can be and reduce several of the fluffy bits.
Not worth my time as an MBA student and for two full Saturdays, I don't think I learnt enough
content/material/techniques worthy of the time. Lecture style was bearable but the physical exercises and reviewing youtube video did not respect the time and money I invest in an MBA.

Finally, as someone teaching at Berkeley, being paid by Berkeley students, listing Berkeley in their teaching experience -- it was quite cocky to not start the class at Berkeley time especially when it's a 9-5 pm weekend class?! Not very audience-focused behavior from the instructor at all.
One of the most practical courses at Haas. High impact 2 day course
Yes. Great value for the time invested in this course
Not recommended. If you expect smaller group presentation coaching or feedback from the lecturer, there are other courses with smaller class size like storytelling for leadership.
Yes, highlight recommend for anyone working on an idea
Yes, I think this is a very practical and effective class to enhance your communication style

Absolutely, Molly was an amazing professor who brought such deep insight and expertise to the class, and was truly invested in making the class a positive, meaningful learning experience. This was a very interesting class, definitely relevant for anyone considering the startup world!

I wholeheartedly recommend Molly Turner! She has amazing experience working with startups and deftly translated this experience into well organized course content. Loved this class and really enjoyed Molly's teaching style. Yes, if you want to have an understanding of the importance of policy considerations for any small company, this is the class to take. Be ready to create a very thorough policy plan over the course of the class.

Molly is amazing. She is a true industry leader and her stories are both interesting and contain a lot of valuable and applicable information. While policy is neither my background nor is it the type of work I want to do moving forward, this was a great way to dip my toes in the water. The class is very focused on startups (as is in the name) so make sure that is what you want to research/work on in the future.
Yes. Its a good mix of policy and business
Highly recommend for anyone interested in working on the policy side of a startup, or for potential founders who will engage in thorny regulatory landscapes such as technology or cannabis.
Yes! This class is really valuable for not only learning more about policy strategy, but applying this strategy to real- world startups!

GREAT class. Molly brings a TON of relevant experience and knowledge. She organized the course very purposefully and each class resulted in substantial learning. She is very well connected in the startup policy space, and brought in really great speakers. Heads up that there was a lot of work due in the class, but Molly understood that and says she will tweak for the next time.

YES! There's no other person I would recommend on this particular topic. She is truly a subject-matter expert. Yes! This is a great class for anyone focused on tech, startups or entrepreneurship. It's great real world experience intro the policy sphere and every class is the most interesting podcast you can find. It's great to start thinking about how to incorporate policy work into any future role.

Absolutely - great instruction in an uncommon topic & thoughtful feedback from an experienced, successful practitioner. This is a course you couldn't get at another business school. The course required more work than the average Haas course, but each assignment resulted in clear learning & didn't feel like we were just spinning our wheels.

Yes! Take as many courses with Molly as you can. You will learn so much from her and from the wonderful guest speakers she brings in! Leaving this course I feel like I have a good grasp on what it takes to navigate policy challenges at any size startup and build a policy team!

I would recommend this course if it undergoes a few design changes. The course is excellent in that Molly is a policy expert and provides a depth of expertise and personal experiences from her time at Airbnb. However, assignments were due weekly, which was more of a commitment than I was expecting. I would recommend this course if the number of assignments are cut in half.
Yes, great course and unique subject area - hard to find similar courses elsewhere.

Absolutely! Learning in a hands on way with Molly and all of the policy experts she brought in from Lyft, Airbnb and other cool startups as well as gov't officials doing cool things like figuring out how to regulate micro mobility in Oakland/SF was extremely worthwhile. Very much recommend!

Molly is an excellent communicator and super well connected and informed on this topic (because she lives it). I appreciate her candid style and friendly approach and think Haasies should 100% take advantage of this course if they plan to build a startup in a regulated space.

I would absolutely recommend this class to anyone interested in startup policy or entrepreneurship in highly regulated areas. There is a good reason this is taught in the business school and not in Goldman, and that is the business interconnectedness of policy. It is not about what policy should be for the best possible society, but about what actions startups can, should, and do take to turn regulatory challenges into advantages. It's different than any other Haas class I have taken, and I find that outstanding. If you are trying to get the most diverse experience you can at Haas, this is a great course for it. It is a lot of work, but you get to choose your own
adventure/topic/company, so its in your hands to make it a labor of love.
Big time. Every Haas student should have a dose of this. Even if not necessarily interested only in early stage companies.
Yes. IF you want to work in a startup, this class is a must.

YES! Molly is an incredible instructor who brings her wealth of startup and policy experience to inform the course curriculum and learnings. I learned the mechanics of how to craft policy strategy for a startup, and enjoyed the final: pitching my strategy to a VC and head of policy who work in the same field as my selected strategy. Overall one of the best classes I've taken during my 2–year master's program at Berkeley.

Yes, it is one of the best classes I have had in my entire academic career. I am an LLM student, and this class has added much important knowledge for my future. I highly recommend it! Hopefully, this same class will be at Berkeley Law in the future!
GREAT course – really interesting and strongly recommend. You?ll learn far more than any normal lecture based class.

I HIGHLY recommend this class for anyone interested in working at a startup – especially in a strategy or go–to–market function, even if you don't intend to enter a highly regulated industry. The course work is very practical and applied rather than theoretical. I've already leveraged the frameworks and systematic methodology from this class multiple times in recruiting interviews. The workload is slightly on the heavier side for a 2–unit elective, but if you focus your project on a startup in an industry you care about, it can help you get a job. Molly is also THE expert on this topic. She brings not only a wealth of expertise but also deep enthusiasm and an a rockstar network of guest speakers.

Molly is an experienced professional that has a lot of value she can bring to the classroom. I highly recommend taking her class. It is a bit more work than other 2 credits class, but the work is worthwhile and results in a meaningful learning experience.

I found this class to be incredibly valuable. During my time at Haas, I have focused on many entrepreneurship experiences and I never heard about the policy implications of a startup until I took this class. I learned highly specialized learning that I am now aware of for when I am at my own startup. It is a lot of work so be prepared to work hard, and make sure you find a partner for the class project.

I highly recommend this course to anyone interested in business. It provides a thorough understanding of the regulatory and legal aspects that are crucial to business operations. Unlike other courses that primarily focus on the commercial aspects, this course gives valuable insights into the legal challenges that startups, especially disruptive ones, may face when they operate in gray areas of the law. It's essential knowledge for anyone involved in or planning to start a business.
definitely. You choose a startup and develop a policy for it, and meet amazing people in the industry.

Absolutely, I'd recommend the course. Between the content, guests, Mollys insights, and the project that the course culminates in, this class is one of the best at Haas. It was a treat to have a small class but this should definitely be available for a larger group

Yes, I'd recommend this to any student interested in policy or venture-backed start-ups. I think it is an rare, incredible class structure that blends business and policy. So many companies need this - just look at OpenAI, TikTok, etc. etc. This class is very unlike every other class I have taken at Berkeley. Molly has tons of very valuable experience (eg. she pitched her job as policy strategist to Airbnb at the time and has been an advisor for Uber and many other 'greg-area, high potential' startups). After this class I feel like I have a nice playbook of how to navigate policy strategy that will come in handy at foreseen, and unforeseen times. The smaller nature of the class makes it very interactive and a great learning opportunity
Yes, the course is wonderful, interesting, and practical for anyone interested in working at or founding a start-up.

sections.goodFor: Aspiring startup policy leads, founders in regulated industries, and anyone at the public-policy/business intersection; pairs well with Tech and the City.
sections.notFor: Students who cannot absorb group-driven work (your group matters a lot) or who want a lighter 2-credit class; one says it is really only for founders in regulated industries.
sections.workloadNote: Assignments compound across the semester and are mostly group-based; one student says the load feels like an easy 3-credit class rather than a 2-credit one. Weekly guest speakers.
sections.gradingBasis: Primarily compounding group project assignments on a startup you choose; instructor gives lots of feedback and holds high standards.
sections.redFlags: Workload exceeds the 2-credit billing (1-2 comments) and coursework is group-driven so your team determines your experience; instructor described as intense with high standards.
sections.quote: The workload feels more like an easy 3-credit class vs. a 2- credit class, and classwork is primarily group-project oriented so your group matters a lot.
comments: Yes, Molly brings a really interesting perspective into the classroom and is incredibly knowledgeable. Even as someone interested in the food space, I learned so much from Molly's anecdotes from her work experience and from the guest speakers who came. The assignments were really valuable, and it was wonderful that they compounded throughout the semester. This was a fun class! Just the right amount of work and class time!

She did an incredible job of offering practical guidance and the format of the class was super engaging. The assignments were long enough to feel worthwhile, but not so long that I was overburdened. The class had the right amount of flexibility and I appreciated Molly's tough hard questions.

Yes, if you're interested in policy for startups. Molly is incredibly knowledgeable about the space, gives lots of feedback, and brings in great guest speakers. I feel like I have a much stronger understanding about what it takes to think of creative solutions for policy problems with startups. The workload feels more like an easy 3-credit class vs. a 2- credit class, and classwork is primarily group-project oriented so your group matters a lot. If you're ok with that, I'd definitely recommend.
Yes, I would recommend.
Highly highly recommended, as she's one of the best people who can teach this course, and also has the experience to back it up
everybody should understand that we live in a world where a small group of people make decisions for us. this class considers those people in the business sense so yes you should take the class

Molly is one of the best instructors at Haas. She is intense and has high standards, but you will learn a lot if you are willing to put in the time. She has very unique experience from leading policy at Airbnb and many other experiences consulting with startups, but she also has a great network and is humble enough to know when to bring in guest speakers who have better expertise in a certain area than her.

One thing I like about this class is that it has the vibe of some of the more applied courses where you're working on a real company, but you also don't have to manage a consulting relationship that's not necessary to the learning here. You just pick a startup you want to work on.

Such a great complement to her other course, Tech and the City that did not feel duplicative. This course works great for aspiring policy leads at startups but also for anyone who wants to work at a startup that is in a regulated industry. I would recommend this class to the student who want to dig deep into some selected policy area. It requires the business understanding and also regulatory landscape. And jump from that, we build the policy recommendation and execution strategiesz
yes, for those who are interested in the intersection of public policy and business, this course is one of the rare you can find here at Cal
Yes, it is very hands on and Molly is very engaged
I would 100% recommend this instructor and course. Molly is exceptional and this course follows in the footsteps of Tech & the City's greatness.
I would recommend this course only to startup founders who are working in a regulated industry.

Definitely - I was able to learn about an angle of business that isn't explored in traditional Haas classes. I really enjoyed the guests Molly brings - they are extremely relevant and thoughtful and again offer a perspective of business that is underexplored in Haas

sections.goodFor: Students in design, engineering, marketing or business who want hands-on market research and user-need discovery by actually talking to people outside school.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting structure and guidance, or who doesn't want their experience hostage to teammates - with no individual assignments some members coast. Pick a project you care about or you get little.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (8 comments). Team-based customer discovery built around the business model canvas; no individual assignments, only recurring progress presentations, so pace is set by your team.
sections.gradingBasis: Team progress presentations only - students note there are no individual assignments.
sections.redFlags: Little structure/guidance and everything rides on team dynamics (2 of 8); no individual assignments so teammates can slack; one says the weekend Startup Disco course teaches the same skill set.
sections.quote: There are no individual assignments, just presentations to update on progress, so some team members tend to slack and this can be quite frustrating and discouraging.
comments: Yes! If you are interested in anything design, engineering, marketing, business, etc... This class is essential to understanding market research and user needs. However, it is key to chose a project that interests you.

Ofcourse! This was a great experience overall. I would prefer a bit more structure and guidance. Your experience solely depends on your team dynamic and you pretty much have to do everything on your own. There are no individual assignments, just presentations to update on progress, so some team members tend to slack and this can be quite frustrating and discouraging. As long as you are willing to give it your all, you will have a good experience. The entire class spins around the business model canvas, so if that is something you are interested in, go for it. If not, take the weekend starup dsico. I took both and startup disco pretty much teaches you all the necessary skill sets. Yes, good experience talking to people outside of school and haven't had any interaction with
Yes- both were great. It has been the best course I've taken so far.
Yes, because it is a course where you learn through experience.
I would but I would make sure to tell the students to be intentional with the project selections; it should mean something to them and really make them curious.
I would recommend this to other students because doing customer discovery and understanding user need is the most important part of any business. Regardless of what role you work.
Yes I would recommend very unique and in depth perspectives

Yes, in this class you can learn the basic structure of the business model and let you know how an early-stage startup needs to approach when they are trying to find their customers' needs. But you need to be familiar with the resources and choose an ideal topic, or you may not gain the result you want. Besides, the whole process is to some degree iterative.

rows.title: An Introduction to Code for MBAs

comments: Yes. This is not a class for you to learn to code. However, if you want to learn some fundamentals about the coding process, the engineering community, and important technical concepts (API, Agile, and etc.), this is the right class. Joe is super practical and interesting, and you will learn a lot from him.
I highly recommend this introductory course. Joe is a great professor and the course load is great.

100% would recommend. Sad to see that this course is not offered to classmates in the upcoming fall. I lucked out. Joe has a clear understanding of the topics necessary for MBAs to do well during tech interviews. We need more courses like this.

YES! Joe is an excellent instructor and he gets it. He understands how to distill an intimidating topic for novices in a way that is approachable, digestible, and creates a base for continued growth. This course resulted in substantial learning for me in a way where I will now feel confident in talking with programmers and engineers. Unless you plan on retiring next year, you'll need a baseline understanding of coding. This is the class for you.
Absolutely! Great class with lots of learning.

This was the only 6-9 class where I didn't play in the background and actually listened to. Joe is a great teacher and the contents of each class were extremely relevant for those who want to pursue a PM career and have zero technical background. Highly recommend this course.

I would highly recommend Joe Wadcan's Intro to Code course. If you need a boost of confidence in your ability to talk fluently and competently about tech subjects with developers, this is exactly what you're looking for.
Yes! Joe is amazing, practical, and understanding. Would highly recommend this class - wish I had taken it before my internship in tech!
Yes - great course to get an introduction to technical subject matter and great for working in PM or really in any capacity with developers/engineers.

Good introductory course on coding concepts, definitely not foundational coding though. At the end of the day, it helps me better understand certain technical news or articles on tech industry and players.

This is one of the classes you have to take before you leave Haas. It's more useful in the modern world than most of your core classes, it's not a huge lift, it leaves you will real knowledge and skill and a form of literacy that you cannot afford not to have. Joe's amazing, and makes the material extremely accessible.

Absolutely! Joe is a Haasie as well and everything was exceptionally well planned and accessible to all students. He saw a need in terms of content and I feel significantly more prepared to work in a tech setting later in my career. There is a reason why this course fills up quickly during class bidding!
If you don't know anything about programming, SQL, Python, it is a great class. I highly recommend complementing it with online, in practice courses because it is very theoretical in many topics.
Absolutely. It's a great way to get an introduction to a developer's world and language, extremely useful for those who will be working with developers/investing in their tools.

If you know some tech but feel like you are missing some real-world knowledge/skills/processes in the tech space, this is the class for you. Joe does a phenomenal job explaining tech concepts for a non-technical audience. If you are looking for a class where you learn how to program, this is not the course for that. We learned a little bit of code but that's not really the point of the class and we only learned a little bit of code. This course is great if you have wondered before about Github best practices (or want to know what Github is), have wondered how the internet works, have wondered what developers care about, and want to know software development best practices and methodologies. Also, I have wondered for a long time what APIs are - this class answered that for me. Highly recommend for those hoping to better understand the software development world without becoming a developer themselves.

Yes - I entered into it with zero knowledge about coding or tech. It has helped me understand some of the basics behind what it is that tech companies and developers do. I feel more comfortable having intelligent conversations with tech people after taking this class. I am also working on my own startup, and understanding APIs, languages, and how PMs operate has already been super helpful.
Yes, of course!!! 100% recommend
If you are looking to understand technical aspects better, then this is useful. I think some of the lessons should be rearranged in order but there is definitely value.

Yes. If you've ever watched Silicon Valley and laughed awkwardly while not totally getting the joke, this class may be for you. I have spent my career working on the non-technical side of startups and though I found this class did not teach me anything earth-shattering, it helped answer the questions that I'm too embarrassed to ask at work because I think I should know the answers by now. It covers a broad range of topics and terms that are just useful to know if you want to navigate the tech scene, and Joe is a really great professor who makes the topics feel approachable (even over Zoom).
100000% would recommend this course. It needs to be part of core! If you don't know anything about how
technology works you'll be at such a disadvantage when trying to engage in meaningful change at companies (which increasingly revolves around software).
Definitely great for anyone without a coding background looking to understand that world a bit better
Absolutely would recommend this course to fellow students. It honestly should be part of core-curriculum given where the world is moving. Joe is wonderful!

Yes - This was a good basic class. If you are looking for the fundamentals on technology, then this is the class for you. I'd recommend this class and instructor to beginners who have no experience in working with developers or in tech. For those who have some experience in working with developers, this may still beneficial, but this class is mostly tailored to non-tech beginners. Nonetheless, great contents if you are prepping for tech interviews.

Yes, highly worthwhile class and highly recommended!!! Got to learn a little bit of everything, dive into many technical areas, and build my technical vocabulary. Class sessions fly by due to the diverse course content and hands on coding activities. Joe is also a great, enthusiastic, and approachable professor - would definitely be interested in taking a class with him again!

This is an extremely valuable class if you're planning on working in tech (or starting a company) and you don't have a software developer background. It's not just learning about coding / computer science (in fact, that's a very small part of the class), it's more learning about the tech and developer ecosystem, the tools they use, and how companies develop code along with trends in this space for tech companies. Extremely valuable for product managers (or to-be product managers) that don't have that tech background.

Yes! Really practical course with clear takeaways for technology industry. I am new to a very enterprise-tech focused VC role and it's been great to get the foundations from this course in a digestible way.

I would definitely recommend this course! Joe is a fantastic instructor. He was by far one of the most engaging instructors I had over Zoom, and I'm sure it's even more engaging in person. It's obvious he also cares about his students and he tries to make himself available for any questions. My hesitation w/ enrolling prior to this class was "Couldn't I learn this for free online?" And of course the answer to that is yes. However, with my limited programming knowledge, it probably would've taken HOURS to gain a thorough understanding of the tech landscape instead of spiraling down rabbit holes w/ the abundance of resources out there for learning coding. Joe does a really good job at putting together a course structure that gives you a basic but thorough understanding of tech-related terminology and tools. While you won't dive deep into any particular skill (don't expect to walk away learning how to code or to do SQL at an advanced or even intermediate level), I still highly recommend this course to anyone who wants to better understand how to work in the tech industry.
Yes, if you have zero exposure to the world of investment/entrepreneurship

It is a bit of an intense week. A roughly 48 hour deep dive as an entrepreneur and then another roughly 48 deep dive as a VC. The style of the class is to sort of throw you in to the deep end and let you figure it out. It can get a little intense, but it works. I learned a ton about both worlds and their connection.

Definitely recommend it to students looking for 1) connection with fellow MBA students from different parts of the world 2) condensed introduction to entrepreneurship and VC and their connection, and 3) experimental learning by building business model as entrepreneur and building investment thesis as VC partner. However, if you already have experience with entrepreneurship and/or VC or have taken some classes with either subject, this may not be the right level of class for you. [Only for remote learning] Since a lot of students are taking this remotely from different time zones, you have classmates that are taking this class 3am in the morning. Prepare for different energy
level/availability/etc. when doing group project after class.

I would recommend the instructor and course if the student was newer to entrepreneurship and the Bay Area, the topic is definitely well covered. While I thought the course itself was valuable, I found the group assignments via Zoom and all constricted to a week very difficult. It was hard for me to coordinate with my team in different time zones and often times we were tasked to submit assignments on very short turnaround. I understand it's only a week long course and so it's not possible to have much depth in the assignments but I would almost prefer less assignments spread out over time. In addition, some students apparently were not going to receive grades or credits for the course and I feel that definitely makes the incentives less aligned for group project work.

If you could split this course into two different courses, I might take the first one with Sara (entrepreneur-side), but I would definitely not take the one with David (VC-side). The entrepreneur-side portion of the class was much more "real-life impact" as you got to work and talk with actual founders of companies, and fit those discussions into well- defined and taught aspects of entrepreneurship management. The VC-side was nearly impossible to follow, as David's approach to teaching material was entirely disjointed and followed logical progression, leaving most students without any kind of substantial learning. The guest speakers, as wonderful as they were, began to just start feeling like time- fillers, as the discussion with them were often unguided and rehashed comments made by other speakers. Their contributions would be much more impactful if they were tied to specific parts of the teaching and had their discussion based around that module. All in all, not a good course for Haas to be showing externally to the GNAM world.
It is a good overview of the entrepreneurship and VC ecosystem in Silicon Valley, but the class did not move the needle much for me.
Great course. Be prepared to work very hard. But it is only one week so you can do it.
Yes, totally. I learnt a lot
Yes yes and yes! They are amazing!

Yes, amazing course. You get to meet so many incredible people from around the world and get a deep insight into the silicon valley ecosystem. Very different course from the others and highly recommended
I hope it will have more company visits rather than staying in classroom

Dr. Vivek Rao and Dr. David Charon are a great team. They gave us good exposure to both the entrepreneurial and VC sides of the ecosystem in the Bay Area through interactive classes, meaningful panel discussions, and role plays. Having students from prominent B-schools around the world enriched the whole experience.

I would highly recommend this course for anyone interested in a crash course in VC and entrepreneurship. If you already have understanding and knowledge of both sides, the first two sessions may not deliver new information. That said, the other parts of the course will still give value - panels and small speaker sessions, pitching (as both a VC and startup), working in new and small teams, company visit. The professors work as a friendly and dynamic duo and keep things lively in what can be quite an intense week!

I would highly recommend this course, you will not only learn things within the classroom, also you will also meet new ppl from other top B schools, life is all about knowing new person, and team up with them, especially those who are better or same excellent as you.

I thought this course would be more about the Bay Area and Silicon Valley entrepreneurship scene but it was more of an introductory course for entrepreneurship and VC more generally. I was hoping for more company visits. It was largely geared towards the students from other institutions that were there as part of GNAM.

I already recommend to my cohort and will continue to support this course. If I do well, such as raising capital successfully to form a fund, I am more than happy to come back to share my journey next year.
Yes, was a great course to understand their basics of Entrepreneurship and Venture Capital. It was also amazing to meet and network with people from all across the globe.

I would recommend to those who wants to have an overview of the entrepreneurship and venture capital. I HIGHLY recommend this course. It offers something for everyone regardless of where they are in their MBA journey. Yes, David has a unique perspective on the subject matter and communicates his perspective effectively. Yes, absolutely worth. You would get a perspective from both entrepreneurship and investor with the hands on projects.

This class was a great opportunity to bond with a group of international MBA Students if you don't have the opportunity to undergo another international experience while at Haas. The class was very hands on- numerous guest speaks including both VC's and entrepreneurs, site visits to start-ups, tours of Bakar and Berkeley SkyDeck which was a unique experience unlike any other Haas class.
Yes! Thank you!
yes. made great connections and good sharing from industry experts which was exactly what I expected from of this short course.

sections.goodFor: Students who want a fast immersion in how Bay Area VC and startups actually work, and who want to network with entrepreneurial students from beyond Haas.
sections.notFor: Not addressed - none of the 6 commenters raised a reason to avoid it.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (6 comments) and no workload detail given; described as a crash course/immersion into the Bay Area VC and startup ecosystem.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.quote: For those looking to expand their network with entrepreneurial-minded students beyond Haas, this is the perfect crash course/immersion.
comments: I strongly recommnd this class for eveyone who is interested in the eco system in the bayarea.
Great class! The class gives a great perspective on investing and entrepreneurship.
Yes, great representation of Berkeley haas mba and entrepreneurship and VC courses having taken both

Yes, I would highly recommend both David Charron and Sean as instructors. David's nurturing yet direct style fosters a supportive environment that encourages open dialogue and practical entrepreneurial skills. Sean's effectiveness and focused " money " mentality provide valuable insights into venture capital, enriching the learning experience. Together, they offer a well-rounded perspective on entrepreneurship and VC, preparing students very well for future ventures and careers.

I would recommend instructor and course to a fellow student. This is a great opportunity to learn how bay area VC and start up works, and meet people from different part of the world, and hear their perspective
For those looking to expand their network with entrepreneurial-minded students beyond Haas, this is the perfect crash course/immersion.
Yes
Yes! Valuable for any leaders hoping to create or evaluate social impact initiatives.

Yes, 100% especially to students from the Goldman School of Public POlicy due to the social impact theme. Yes. Yes Yes. Very intuitive. I came in with no social impact marketing background and now, I am confidence to share that I am prepared to narrate and curate a compelling story.

I'm a FTMBA student and would HIGHLY recommend this course to anyone interested in social impact issues, even if marketing isn't your primary area of interest (it wasn't for me). Even though the course focuses on social impact marketing in a corporate context, our discussion also touched on the nonprofit and government sectors, with classmates from the public policy and part-time programs offering valuable perspectives. I thought the speakers were excellent and came from a variety of different backgrounds that I found fascinating. Courtney was also an incredibly engaging speaker, which is all the more impressive considering that this class met on two Sundays.

I would highly recommend this course. I didn't have much expectations when I signed up, but I was pleasantly surprised by the volume of interesting content and the caliber of the guest speakers who bring in some very valuable real-world experience.

Yes. I'm an MPA student who has worked in arts nonprofits. I am taking a lot back to think about how to market our work better. I'd love for Courtney to teach a class at GSPP that could cover both social cause marketing and nonprofit marketing along with its logistics and ways to leverage impact.
Yes definitely. It is quite chill class, and you can listen from 6 guest speakers.
Yes!!
Yes! It's very specific and certainly useful if one is interested in the field of CSR and communication

Yes. I think it is super relevant. My opinion might be biased as I am personally interested in this topic. Unequivocally. I am not a marketer. I'm barely taking marketing classes here at Haas. This class leans corporate CSR, more than nonprofit impact space; still, there are speakers from a wide range of industries that bring a valuable diversity of perspective. This class was a relatively low lift as far as preparation and assignments - Courtney focuses on in-class discussion. The discussions were meaningful- digging into ethics, morality, business values. The course is well organized, landing on different "tensions" in marketing campaigns.
I highly highly highly recommend. I'm a 2Y ft student and this is my favorite class that I've taken.
Yes. This class is so great. Time goes by so quickly for an all day class. Brings in many different perspectives and so thoughtful.
Highly recommend, especially for those interesting in sales and marketing.

I would recommend this class if you are a marketer interested in the social impact side of brand marketing. This class is about how for-profit companies use social impact in their marketing; not how to create social impact through marketing. Courtney has a breadth of knowledge and close connections with marketers in the Bay. It is also a great space to meet FT&EWMBA students/MBA alums who are working in marketing.
Class can be a bit high level at times. People working directly in marketing have the most to gain, since it's a good place for those with deeper knowledge to workshop direct issues.
Absolutely. Great for people interested in purpose driven marketing

I recommend this course for anybody who is in the social impact space or just thinking about where to start with marketing their product. This is a 1-unit course that is super hands on, you get to hear from marketing professionals and engage with them in a meaningful way to learn first hand about a super dynamic and fast moving field. With the final project you get to apply knowledge and learn through the feedback and hands-on practice.
Yes. Very important class.

This was an interesting marketing course, but if you're looking for marketing fundamentals that teach you how to make an effective marketing plan, you won't get that. This is a course that could be supplemental to those who have a good grasp of marketing. It could be an interesting course for exposure to new industries.

I highly recommend this class! Courtney incorporates lots of real-life campaigns and clients to make learning more interesting and exciting. If you are interested in marketing OR social impact, this class will be invaluable. However, I suggest having some basic concepts of marketing as you are expected to apply them to the case that you work on. For someone already familiar with the topic or in nonprofit, I would recommend it if the course is altered to include an opportunity for students to workshop/reflect on a social impact marketing topic they are facing or have faced at work. For others, I would recommend the class because Courtney has great connections so the guest speakers were all insightful, and his additional comments would be great for someone unfamiliar with social impact marketing. I would highly recommend Courtney and course to any student, regardless of their marketing background, who has an interest in the intersection of social impact, business, and marketing. I entered the class with limited marketing experience, yet I found it to be incredibly valuable.

From a consumer standpoint, the course has taught me how to critically evaluate whether a company is truly making the impact they claim. From a business perspective, I now have a solid framework for creating impactful campaigns and business solutions, and for bringing those ideas to life with a focus on social impact.

This course provides both theoretical knowledge and practical application, making it an excellent choice for students who want to deepen their understanding of socially conscious marketing. I wholeheartedly recommend it!

Yes. This class teaches not only marketing but also living a meaningful life depends on how deep you want to go. Absolutely! Courtney is a great professor and I believe any student regardless of past experience or emphasis can learn something from this course.
Yes! Courtney is awesome. He really genuinely cares about the work and that comes through in his lectures, energy and passion!

rows.title: Designing Futures: Technology & Society
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2021 Fall;2023 Spring;2024 Spring;2025 Spring;2026 Spring

comments: Thought provoking and enjoyable class. Amazing guest speakers. Sometimes unclear instruction on homework, but in those cases I felt it allowed more freedom of choice.

Yes! This has been the best class I have taken at Haas. While there are lots of assignments, they are all really fun to do and have helped me learn so much. This class has really changed how I move through the world!
Yes! This course really helped me think outside the box. I used to consider myself not creatively inclined, but this course really helped me develop that skill and use it in realistic situations.

I really liked this class and loved working with Sandeep, Joe, and Joanne — they are amazing / inspiring people. I think the class could be improved with more active / engaging in-class activities and discussion.
Yes - this is a fun class to flex your creativity and learn new design thinking methodologies.
100% yes. Just a weird and wacky class for the nerds and creatives among us. Super fun and immersive. And the professors are amazing.
Absolutely. It was a fantastic way of doing design thinking in perhaps even more of a structured way. Would definitely recommend, it helps to have that background in advance though.

Yes!! This course was creative and interesting. It forces b-school students to think about solving problems in a different way. I love their methodology and teaching style. All three also made themselves readily available and were effective brainstorming partners. This has been one of my favorite courses at Haas. I think we're really lucky to have it offered!! I found this class to be a wonderful way to learn and practice design thinking frameworks. It was also a lot of fun and a great way to push myself to think creatively. Definitely a unique course at Haas and a great complement to more traditional business courses.

This was a great class to really hone your creative thinking skills and envision what the future might look like, as well as the signals that currently exist that might help make that future a concrete reality. The professors are all subject matter experts, and brought in a variety of speakers to discuss themes in innovation and futurism. Great class!

I would recommend for a lighter lift class that's centered around creativity, coming up with wacky ideas, and developing them within frameworks. You will be constricted by the theme for the particular semester, which changed each year. For example, this semester's theme was climate change so each group created a product idea by the end of the semester that addressed climate change in some way. It may not be the best idea to take this class of the theme is not something you have a strong interest in.

Yes. This is a really fun, worth-while course. Especially for students who want to develop their creativity and perhaps direct it towards brainstorming / ideating solutions. The worlds of sci-fi and business continuously influence one another. This course is a great introduction to that kind of cyclical, inspiring thinking.
Yes

Look, going in you have to know this is a strange class. Requirements and assignment criteria are sort of moving targets, and there's really no right answers at all. On the other hand, it's not just BS. So it's in this space between tangible and intangible, and you have to want to consciously opt-in to this experience where you aren't really sure where you'll be at the end. If you enjoy thinking about a nebulous future and trying to hone down your view of the future more, then this class is for you! It doesn't fall into too much of the Design Thinking greatest hits and the main value is in the relationships I built with other classmates, as well as with the professor team. This class isn't for everyone, but it's not a ton of work (the weekly assignments are usually somewhat light), and it may change how you see the world a bit.

If you haven't taken a Design Thinking course before, I would take this course. I enjoyed the creativity I got to use. I would say that I'm not sure if I learned any tangible skills. More so I was able to be creative and think of fun and cool future ideas.

Great course that provides a unique opportunity to 'think differently' during the semester. Highly worthwhile. Yes. This class is a low lift and you get to learn a little bit more about a topic that may be interesting to you. I wouldn't think of it as a class, but more as an exercise on futuring - really suspending disbelief and waving a magic want for what a potential future could be. That's a very different skill than incremental design and is a welcome counterpoint to everything else that's taught in product/business design schools.

Yes. If you're really not into thinking about far off hard-to-imagine things, and you want to only discuss something that exists in front of you, don't take it. But I genuinely think for all different kinds of disciplines and careers it's a useful and fun exercise to try to compile signals and extrapolate way out into the future, and it's really hard to do that often without something like this class and a pretty regimented process to do so. I found it really useful to take some of my own ideas I'm tinkering around in my own time/career and just push them further.

It was ok! Lots of homework assignments but they were fun. The instructors were lovely people. It was a nice deep dive into design, though probably hard to take the learnings out into the real world. For me, it felt like a fun and creative brain break every week.
I would strongly recommend this course to anyone interested in exploring how to think about the future and how to explore what business opportunities might exist in the future.

I'm torn here. I really like all of the instructors and how much passion they put into the class and their overall responsiveness. However, I did not feel like I learned anything that I could truly integrate into my career in the way that I hoped. It wasn't super practical and I feel like it will be difficult to explain in different contexts beyond innovation and design. Probably my least favorite course I took this semester, which is unfortunate.
Yes - it's definitely out there, and probably not super applicable to a lot of immediate post-MBA jobs, but a great supplemental class to understand design and innovation.

I'm glad I took the course, as it exposed me to some interesting ways of thinking about the future and being creative. I wish that I had more time outside of class to engage more with the readings, homework and thinking through the learnings - it felt somewhat rushed and forced in parts even though the workload is very manageable.

This class is hands-on and different. Lots of design thinking. Wish it wasn't so strictly centered around climate change as I didn't know it would be before signing up. Knowledgable and kind professors though who have worked on great things at IDEO and have a lot of cool connections.
sure. Its a good design course.

This was one of my favorite classes!!! Really interesting content and empowered me to think in a different way. The professors have perfected this course over time––perfect balance between workload and engaging content.

Absolutely! This course is a must. Designing futures is one of the best courses I've taken at Haas and I'm really proud of the work we've done in labs. The course is very useful for those envisioning careers in creativity–unlocked fields like entrepreneurship, venture capital, sustainability, social impact, healthcare, etc. There are unique ways to learn to disrupt the status quo and learn through divergent futures.

I would definitely recommend this course to anyone who wants to learn a different way of creative thinking that's still very applicable to the business world. The facilitators were amazing and created a very thoughtful and fun class environment.

Absolutely. This class is creative and fun and gives you a different perspective from which to base your strategic thinking. It reminded me that business can be fun and wacky but at the same time have serious consequences if we're not able to recognize our agency and influence over the future. It?s a must class for anyone that sees themselves as a leader who?s business decisions can have a significant impact on the future of society. Therefore all of us should take it.
Yes, I learned in class and teachers have a good heart & genuinely care. Interesting and thoughtprovoking, and useful tools to apply for post MBA life.
I would strongly recommend this course – it made me think in a different way in comparison to my other Haas courses. I really truly enjoyed the class and our final presenation
Yes! 100%. Not completely sure if I'll use it in my career. But it was really fun to think about the future. The framework is also helpful to think about signal and future scenarios.

Yes – it is a helpful structure and framework to look at the future with different tools and lenses. It's also fun to work in a group to come up with different scenarios of what the future could look like.
Yes! Highly recommend it!

Taking this class is like a breath of fresh air in Haas. It makes us connect to our creative selves and have fun with it! Material is not very applicable but it is a course for those who want to get connected to our creative part! Yes! Good class with fun environment for learning Design Thinking methodology.

Yes – I think a 7 week course made a lot of sense and I almost wished each of our classes had a bit more engagement and group exercises as a way to help implement some of the material we learned. Maybe small or short exercises? But overall just to get a taste of design thinking I thought it was very helpful

Yes, this class helps you think about ideas in a way that is different than most other Haas classes. It is fun and very useful to think about topics in a future-looking and intentional design perspective.
Highly recommend this class. It is an engaging creative exercise and it is interesting to see where your team can wonder about the future, and where others wonder about as well.

Def take it to bond with your classmates for one last time. The most creative class I've taken at Haas and chill. Workload is slightly more than 1-credit with sth due every week (although it's just p/f)
Totally!!

I definitely recommend this class! It is a good space to think outside of the box, leave your comfort zone and think about the implications of current technologies or trends. It is a class that encourages you to be creative, take risks and link your future scenarios with current signals so that they are based on facts and potential changes but not solely on imagination. The professors are great, come from very cool backgrounds and make everyone feel heard!

Yes. This course was a great opportunity for me to flex the creative side of my brain. I do not consider myself a creative person, so developing frameworks and thought process about the future really helped me lean in to that aspect. I'm grateful that the instructors made the course welcoming and approachable to all. Working in a group and thinking about the future was a highlight as I got to learn from my classmates perspectives
Yes. Good if you're looking for a class that's a relatively light workload and to challenge your thinking to be more boundless. But class takeaways are more of the intangibles.
Yes, it is a great course that helps you think outside the box.

Yes - highly recommend! This was my favorite elective at Haas. It gave me the opportunity to scratch a creative itch that I felt was missing from the Haas curriculum. The professors and so knowledgeable and have many interesting perspectives/experiences to share and its clear that they have put a lot of time and effort to refine this course based on previous years' feedback. I think they've nailed it!
Yes, they are great

Of course I will recommend this class, probably top 3 classes I took at Haas. The opportunity to have 3 professors in such a small class is incredible, also all of them are actively working in amazing stuff, so they are close to what innovation and the future looks. This is an opportunity to go deep into the future, use a proper framework, and come up with a story that is actually not that far from reality.

I would recommend Designing the Future. I thought it was going to be a bit too "fluffy" but I found that it was actually quite useful. The ability to develop and apply frameworks to think about different visions of the future seems quite useful, and I'm sure I'll use it. Joe, Joanne, and Sandeep are enthusiastic and they have made interesting careers in part by using the skills that they teach, so it's clear that they are "practicing what they preach" so to speak. On the whole it's a fun class with a reasonable workload that I'd sign up for again.

Yes! This class feels like a fantastic departure from the Haas bubble. It challenges you to think in completely different ways and flex different muscles than the ones we rely on for so much of the MBA. It creates space for writing, creativity, innovation, and strategic thinking in ways that will absolutely be helpful post-grad regardless of industry. strongly recommend this class
I loved the course!! It was refreshing and great to be able to discuss the future in a structured way. Really glad I took it and all three Professors were super knowlegeable and helpful
Yes! Loved it. So fun and the perfect class to take as a 2nd year

Yes. The instructors and this course are by far the best at Haas. There is a humanness to the material and the teachings that cannot be replicated in other classes. I have admittedly been disengaged and disinterested in the majority of courses at Haas, but this is one that had my attention and interest from start to finish. Truly 10/10 and again, my only critique is that I wish it were longer.
I would 100% recommend this class. It is so fun, not a lot of work. You will enjoy every class. Just make sure to pick a good team. Stay Weird.

Yes, I would recommend it to anyone looking to develop their long-term outlook and strategic thinking. The instructors are all practitioners of their discipline, which is a great change of pace compared to the MBAs-turned- executive coaches-turned-business school lecturers. Given that they have actual experience, they're able to share how their teachings apply to real-world cases and keep the class relevant.

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting a break from analytical MBA classes — futures thinking, design thinking tools, creative scenario building; useful for startup/VC-bound students.
sections.notFor: Students wanting technical or immediately tactical skills — one calls it 'effectively creative writing.' Groups are assigned, and one student found the team project a waste of time.
sections.workloadNote: Low-lift, 'chill workload' 1-unit course; ~2 hours/week of class. Readings plus a team scenario project; the one-unit format makes it feel fast.
sections.gradingBasis: Group scenario work and class discussion; grading not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Only one dissent: a student found parts a waste of time and had a difficult experience with the assigned team project. Groups cannot be chosen.
sections.quote: It's a fun, lightweight course - effectively creative writing. If you're looking for something off the beaten path and very soft-skill, this is it.
comments: Yes, it is a short course for you to explore future scenarios of an industry you might be interested on. It includes a framework for analyzing future scenarios that help structure thoughts and discussions.

Yes! I think it's a fun class and provides an alternate perspective on strategy formation from the traditional "gather the data, make a hypothesis, drive to it." It's also a great class to reflect on big problems that you may not think about in depth otherwise.

I would absolutely recommend this course. It is somewhat fast in this one-unit iteration, but the instructors are good people and thoughtful guiders of discussion. It could easily have devolved into something ungrounded and nebulous, and it's a credit to both the instructors and the rest of the class that it did not.

I highly recommend this class! It was very provocative, fun and different compared to other classes I've taken at Haas. Come with an open mind and willingness to challenge your beliefs and work in groups that you won't be able to choose. I am sure I will use the reflections from this class a lot in my professional life.
10/10 amazing class! The most engaging and estimulating I had during my MBA. 2 hours of my week where I forgot about the existence my cell phone.

Absolutely! This class and it's instructors really let you broaden your horizon and think beyond your immediate priorities and interests. It's also a super fun and playful way to learn design thinking tools.

This will feel like a different kind of class than the typical MBA class but in the best way. The teachers are seasoned professionals from the design world and show how knowing how to think about the future is a critical skill personally and professionally.
Yes! This is a great class to practice creative thinking and learn about strategizing for an unknown future in a constructive way.

Best class I had at Haas. Finally was challenged to think. Reflecting on the future, starting from real life signals, and critically evaluating their likelihood and implications was rewarding and definitelly builds useful skills. Also, the team work it required was really useful, it's not like you can divide work, it impliead discussing abstract issues and reaching concensus was challenging. Professors were motivating, engaging, brought interesting examples, created a warm and welcoming enviroment. Must take class! Very different to anything else
Strongly recommended; helps build mental diagrams about how to prepare and build the future of business and society.
Mixed; this is a laid-back course that is nice to take with friends. Generally low-lift, but I felt like it was (at points) a waste of time and difficult experience with the team project.
Absolutely! It's a really interesting class that has unexpected learnings and experiences. Really cool readings and the classes are just perfectly social and reflective.
yes!!
Yes I would highly recommend these instructors and this course!

Yes I would definitely recommend this class. This class, although not super technical serves as a moment in your business school career to think differently. An environment and opportunity to let your mind wander off of profitability and into the unknown. A skill and exercise that I believe will enhance anyone's tool kit as they continue progress as a life long learner.
It is a fun course! Chill workload, good discussions and good professors. I definitely recommend it if you want to have more abstract discussion

Yes, I would recommend. Very different to other classes we have, stimulates other kind of thinking. And it is very cool. Probably the most fun I've had in a class at Haas! Imagining scenarios and discussing them was the highlight, but there are also a lot of learnings and guidance on how to apply these to real world scenarios

Definitely! Was one of the most engaging classes that I have taken during my MBA journey. Professors were amazing, and really effective at teaching us what design thinking is, in a structured and grounded way (it was just a "think about a crazy future class". I learned so much about how to think about the future, which is specifically relevant as I am planning to work in the startup / VC space which is all built on futures.
Yes, It's a different class from all of the business classes that I have taken at Haas and definitely a nice change to get you thinking outside the box.
Extremely recommended. Super informative, different and fun class of the MBA.
It's a fun, lightweight course- effectively creative writing. If you're looking for something off the beaten path and very soft-skill, this is it.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy or systems change who are open to ambiguity and want signals/scenarios/storytelling tools beyond standard MBA frameworks.
sections.notFor: Students who want traditional structure, hard quantitative skills or clean answers. Several say take it when you are not maxed on units, since the assignments need thinking time.
sections.workloadNote: Group effort on almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, building to a self-chosen final project and presentation. Workload called manageable for the credits and explicitly not busy work.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - assignments, group work and final presentations are described, but grading is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: None recurring. Two students wish the course ran longer (~10 weeks) so they could go deeper into scenarios and internalize the frameworks.
sections.quote: Required group efforts for almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, but fun if you enjoy brainstorming and unique presentations as a way to think outside the box.
comments: Yes. This is such a unique and fun class at Haas. A critique I have had of some of the other classes I have taken is that it can often feel like you're being given busy work. Everything in this class felt intentional and helped us get to where we needed to go, even if it didn't feel like that in the moment. Take this class and actually put some time and effort into the work.
Yes!! This is one of the best and most powerful courses I've taken at haas. In a moment of rapid change, it's one of the few classes that teaches a structure for how to think about the future.
I would! Great conversations. I looked forward to this class every week. With all this uncertainty, this class teaches to accept and think three steps ahead

Yes. I would recommend this course to students who want a more creative, expansive class that still connects back to strategy, technology, business, and society. The course is strongest if you are open to ambiguity and interested in thinking beyond traditional MBA frameworks. It pushes you to use signals, scenarios, and storytelling to explore how the future might unfold, which felt different from most Haas classes in a good way. I would especially recommend it for students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy, or systems change.

I ABSOLUTELY recommend. If you're looking for a class that helps you think where "disruption" comes from and non- linear frameworks to understand the world, this is your class. Also recommend to do it when you're not maxxed in units so you have time to think about the assignments and dive into the frameworks. Also expect to give "life" to your own rabbit holes and dystopian/utopian futures - which was really fun:)

Yes! They were all exposed to IDEO at a point in their careers and provides best in class design thinking methods I loved this class!! Was one of my favorites at Haas, really stretched my thinking, and was well executed class. I really appreciate that this class helps shift my way of thinking and prompts more outside the box ways of seeing the world and thinking about trends and futures. I think this is a very applicable class for strategic business thinking, but beyond that a really fun way explore the edge of the latest trends and shifts shaping our world today. Really excellent teaching team, great structure, tight syllabus, high ROI, fun creative class.

Yes! This course is way different thana most of the courses in Haas. This a course that takes you out of the comfort zone, it challenge your traditional structure of thinking and take your imigination to places you won't imagine The frameworks learned during the course were in stark contrast to the standard business education, and were incredibly generative for thinking about the future of tech, work, and life given changes we see in every facet of life due to AI and more. The workload was manageable and made sense for the duration and credit for the class. I only wish this could have been a bit longer of a course (~10 weeks) so that we could dig deeper into the scenarios and learn to internalize the frameworks more.

Yeah definitely! You need to be someone who's willing to embrace their more creative / unstructured thinking side to enjoy this class. For me, it was an awesome opportunity to get outside of my comfort zone and explore information and sources that I'm not usually accustomed to, and try to spend more time just thinking about signals and how they develop / where they're headed. That exercise in and of itself has me thinking more critically about the world around me, and I think the skills I built in this class will be valuable in my future career endeavors.

sections.goodFor: Juniors/seniors and grad students about to earn income; first-gen and low-income students; internationals staying in the US; anyone with zero finance background.

Everyone should take this class at some point in their life! Even for people who don't want to start a company, the class teaches you an extremely helpful methodology for any project or innovation. 100% recommended! But be ready to work a lot!

Yes, very interesting learning experience!
