Yes, absolutely! Lean launchpad is a great course to get the true startup feel. Resulting in amazing experience and substantial learnings.

Do yourself a favor and take this class. This class is a MUST if you plan to go down the entrepreneurship route. It's a lot of work but the leanings are 10x. You will come out very satisfied at the end of the class. Also, it's the only class at Haas where you have 3 instructors for entire class and mentors assigned to each group. Both the instructors and mentors have lots of experience working in the start-up ecosystem.
I also highly recommend this class even if you don't plan to do entrepreneurship. Lean methodologies learned in this class can be applied to any idea or project at big corporations

I would 100000% recommend this course to anyone who wants to know what it takes to build a startup from scratch. Whether you go work at a startup or consulting, this course will give you lessons that you can apply in your career across the board including talking to customers, learning through iterating and understanding what it takes to achieve product–market fit. I 10x more recommend this course to folks who want to stay in the tech ecosystem either as an operator or an investor.

The Lean Launch Pad... is something that will define your semester. You must go into it fully committed and passionate about the core driving force of your idea, but not the idea itself. Because you are going to put in more effort into this course than anything else in Haas, and your idea WILL be different at the end of it all. Without passion, you are going to dread each week, struggling to source and complete 10 interviews. With passion, you will be desperate (in a good way) to hear that next piece of feedback or advice from your potential customers. So, go into this experience fully prepared to lock in and commit with your team to make the most out of this limited and extremely valuable time you have to explore an idea.

I regret to say that I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this particular class, due to a number of pertinent reasons. My primary concern stems from the problematic methodology used in team formation. It appears that the course creators did not fully appreciate the constraints, such as limited commitment or time availability, that MBA students often face. These issues can significantly impede the effective engagement in a demanding course such as this.

Despite the fact that you may be fortunate enough to secure a team of committed individuals, another issue arises – the lack of education on how to effectively collaborate. The course consistently challenges students to work together on a weekly basis, yet it fails to provide the necessary tools and techniques to accomplish this successfully. As a consequence, the individual chosen to lead the team, whether on a rotating basis or as a permanent role, is subjected to an unfair additional burden. The workload can quickly become overwhelming.

Another pivotal issue lies in the insufficient direction provided to the teams. This is particularly alarming given the diverse backgrounds of the participants. I speak from experience when I say that even large consulting firms and seasoned management require guidance in structuring team operations. Unfortunately, this course does not offer such assistance.

Problem–solving and synthesizing valuable insights from interviews are integral parts of any project, yet the course fails to adequately guide students in these areas. While these skills can indeed be taught, and there are knowledgeable individuals, including peers, who could offer help, the teaching staff and the class structure largely overlook this necessity. Instead, a great deal of time is suboptimally spent requiring students to provide feedback on each other's presentations.

In reality, only a fraction of the comments made prove to be useful. As the course advances, these critiques often become an afterthought. The truth is, no one understands your project as well as you do. Unless the person providing feedback is a seasoned expert in your business domain, their contributions may be limited.

I question the course's strategy of forcing students to comment on unrelated topics. Instead, why not encourage us to leverage our networks, which is a fundamental aspect of the MBA experience? Sharing our networks could yield far more valuable insights and facilitate more meaningful interactions among students.

Despite its shortcomings, I believe this course has potential. However, it leaves much to be desired in terms of effectiveness. The lessons I gleaned from this experience could have been delivered in a more condensed format, such as a weekend class. Additionally, the underwhelming outcomes produced by my classmates only further underline my concerns.

In conclusion, while the course could potentially be a valuable learning experience, it requires significant improvements in areas such as team formation, collaborative skills training, problem–solving guidance, and effective use of class time and resources. Until these issues are addressed, I find it difficult to recommend this class.

I would but I would highly encourage the teaching staff to make it clear to students that this model isn't necessarily compatible with deep tech. The commercialization process is different and you should be encouraged to think about what kinds of industries this model works well in. While some lessons are universal, the class is miles easier when focused on particular kinds of solutions. Otherwise, hardware/deeptech startups run around looking for PMF for way too long.
Yes.
This is definitely the heaviest course load of any class at Haas but also the most worthwhile of any I've taken or expect to take. Super thankful to have gone through this experience

I would recommend the class, but only to people who have SAAS or other software/service ideas. The class is not well- suited for climate tech or hardware in general, or maybe the instructors are just not used to it.

If you are interested in entrepreneurship, this is THE course to take. It has completely transformed the way I think about starting a business. I started the course thinking that I have the best idea in the world, but as the team interacted with users and instructors, and used the canvas to look at the idea from various angles, I had a good reality check. At the end, I felt, thank god I didn't start building this immediately and iterate it on a high fidelity MVP! While I didn't come out of this with a business, it has equipped me with the key toolset to quickly strip down an idea and understand what needs to be explored in order and where to move the business. It was a TON of work, but I highly recommend it!

I would recommend this course if you are looking to start a business or have a business idea in the bag and do not have any business background. This course will set you off in a practical way and help you understand if your idea is viable or not through your learnings. Expect lots of hours of learning outside classroom through interviews. The AI platform made idea generation seamless and give more room to learning and helping think in the right direction.

Your biggest strengths in this class is your team. Make sure you are on a team that are collectively as enthusiastic as you are about the course and your idea. You will be working a lot with your team, make sure you have a diverse team with different skill sets and experience. This will enrich your experience.

Overall it's a practical heavy class and deserves giving your best if you are really interested in entrepreneurship. This course was not what I expected. It is not so much teaching you how to launch a start-up, as teaching you how to properly learn about a market. There are many, many interviews which you have to do - so consider whether the course is worth it for you or not. If you're just trying to learn about start-ups and the process, then this probably isn't it. If you're dedicated to an idea that you really want to pursue, then this course is more helpful

If you truly want to experience the uncertainty, ambiguity, and struggles of starting something, then this course is definitely for you. Keep in mind that your idea at the end of the class will likely be different from the one you start with. Therefore, the focus of the class is more on learning throughout the process, developing leadership and teamwork skills, and working under pressure.
It highly depends on the student's goals and motivations. It is only a useful class for people serious about exploring entrepreneurship.
I would highly recommend - even if it doesn't lead to a great idea, it will teach you many important skills you'll need as a business professional

I would 100% recommend this course to future students, especially those who are interested in entrepreneurship. The learning from this class makes most of the other courses I've taken feel like a walk in the park. The experience is so hands-on: startup team dynamics, talking to customers, refining business model, and more.

I would, however, recommend that people sign up in their second year instead of first for two reasons: (1) A lot of what you do and knowledge applied in this class come from other fundamental subjects: finance, marketing, operations, and soft skills. I think you can get more out of this class if you do this class after you've gotten more exposure to different subjects. (2) Many people are doing both internship recruiting the second semester of first year. This makes the class pretty stressful sometimes and harder to get the most out of it. You'd be doing yourself a favor by taking this class in your final semester (assuming you have a return offer from summer internship or some plan secured by then).

I would recommend this if you are interesting from learning from and meeting with incredibly accomplished people, but keep in mind that this really is /a lot/ of work outside of class and you need to love your team and have some interest in your ideas.

Overall, I remain unconvinced of whether the Lean Launchpad model is the best way to start actually establishing a real, revenue earning business. If you are a student who doesn't have a business idea, or has no idea where to start on their entrepreneurship journey, this class may be what you need to launch you.
yes this course is awesome.
Absolutely

This is an awesome course, despite the instructors. The course design absolutely nailed it - it motivates every one of the 40 people in class to put 15-20 hours a week, every week. It ensured that everyone learned by doing and practicing, and everyone was engaged in lectures, office hours, presentations etc. Over the years, the course has really perfected these aspects and if you want to be an entrepreneur, you'll definitely learn a lot!

That said, some things could make this course even better. Like more up to date lectures and much less obsession with the course tool, Glidr. The instructors, especially the lead instructor Jim, could've really stepped up. I feel mixed about this. It is a phenomenal opportunity to explore the startup world BUT it was very presentation heavy with limited guidance. I think the workload wasn't even the issue - I would do all the work and still appreciate doing something more than listening to presentations and giving presentations.
I would but would be very clear that this is not a course meant to build your business. This is an academic exercise. If you actually want to build a business, you don't need to take this course.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this to others, with the caveat that it requires a significant amount of work. My goals were to make entrepreneurship less intimidating and to practice execution over perfection. This course fulfilled both of these requirements for me! Yes absolutely. Absolutely take it if you want to be an entrepreneur or at least want to test the hypothesis of whether you want to be an entrepreneur. It will confirm or disconfirm that hypothesis. But a spot in this class is incredibly valuable -- take it seriously and make the most of your experience.

Yes I will receommend the course. However, please note that doing this course along with recruitment is really challenging. Please do proper due-deligence to form your teams- you want a team with whom you can have fun. Yes! It has been my favorite class I have taken at Berkeley so far.
Yes, but seriously its 20 hours. you may not have a good team and it will be very hard. But it was worth it. One of the hardest but most rewarding courses you can take.

This class is so practical than any other classes I have taken. It's more engaging but very difficult. I would surely recommend to someone who want get into entrepreneurship. This class provides all you need to build a startup and I feel so confident building a startup any time soon
Get out of the building! Best class to learn how to actually make change. I've never felt more challenged, but I've learned a life long lesson.

comments: YES! this should be a required workshop

Highly reckoned this course for people who want to understand the science behind climate change and what it means for business leaders. About 75% of the course is focused on the science aspect versus the business aspect, but gives a strong foundation and understanding to a very complex and relevant topic. Drew is an awesome, knowledgeable and passionate professor and he made a Sunday class really enjoyable!
yes!

Yes, great brief course with a lot of approachable science and exposure to the issues of climate change. Definitely worth 1 unit if you don?t have the capacity to take the 3 unit course. Drew?s lectures are very engaging and fun! Really enjoyed this class! It was the perfect intro to climate change and how businesses really should be thinking about it. I feel like my eyes were opened to so many pieces of climate change that get distorted by greenwashing and politics, and feel much more equipped to have these discussions with peers moving forward.
Yes! Very digestible and straightforward to understand. Professor demystified a lot of hard climate change topics and made the entire experience very engaging.
Yes, I highly recommend this course and this professor. One of my favorite electives at Haas!

Drew is extremely knowledgeable about this topic, and it was a pleasure to learn from him. He answered questions very well, is a dynamic, fun, and engaging speaker, and was clear about the points he was trying to cmmunicate. I learned a lot from the course, despite it only be 1 unit long. I thought the 1 unit course was a perfect balance of cost and value of learning for me - I would highly recommend it.

Since it was the first time this class was offered, I anticipate there will be some tailoring of the content based on feedback received. The course ended up focusing a lot more on science, and only left about 3 hours for the business applications, but I think with the course feedback, that shold hopefully shift next time this is offered. Overall, I would recommend the class for everyone to at least understand the basics and fundamentals of climate change and the actions that will have the most impact to solving the problem.
Totally, should be a must

Yes definitely recommend the 1 unit climate change essentials for business leaders. With the passing of SB 253 & SB 261 plus the growing supply chain transparency pressures pushed by the Amazon and Microsofts of the world, ESG reporting is becoming a reality for more and more companies. Reporting the Scope 1-3 is becoming a new norm as part of the transition to the green economy, knowing about it and its significance on the global temperature is impactful. Learning about the fundamentals including Keeling curve is a must learn for any business leader that is leaning green. sections.gradingBasis: unclear - no student mentions grading; the work centers on a client project, generating insights and presenting them.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (3): your experience depends heavily on project draw and team buy-in - some projects are far harder, and teammates who are not bought in make it hard work. Team leads carry noticeably more.
sections.quote: I would recommend the course. It's a great process to go through and understand. But caveat, if people are not bought into the project, it can be hard work.
comments: This was the most meaningful course of my first year. I absolutely loved being able to test and learn design thinking and consulting in such a growth-minded and fun environment. You will truly get as much out of this course as you put into it. The course's mantra of "trust the process, do the work", is something that I can't wait to apply for the rest of my life!
Yes
Yes, especially if you want a (relatively) chill Applied Innovation class that keeps you local
Yes - hugely applicable, great frameworks, repeatable process
Yes
Yes, absolutely! Both Haas and Ischool/ MIMS students should learn this method, how to work in diverse teams, the power of feedback, and would enhance their product design and management skills.
Great for someone that is looking to gain experience in engaging with clients

Great course. Highly practical. Good learning experience if you want to know how to present or interact to clients. It is not a direct consulting class, but if u have 0 prior experience this will give a good introduction. More a framework class to understand design thinking.

I would recommend the course. It's a great process to go through and understand. But caveat, if people are not bought into the project, it can be hard work. I'd encourage team buy in from the beginning

I would recommend this course as it helps get some relevant experience in design thinking and client work. However, some projects are more difficult than others, so it may require far more work. Be prepared to invest energy into this, especially if you are one of the team leads.

This is a great course for any students exploring the consulting or design thinking spaces. It will give you plenty of practical experience and provide a boost to your resume when applying to jobs. This course does require a substantial amount of work outside the classroom, but it's worth it in the end!
Yes, helpful for navigating team and client dynamics.

Yes, it was great because you learn a ton about how to generate insights and communicate them, storytelling is a big part of this course and you get to practice it in real-time. It was also a great bonding experience with our team.

sections.goodFor: Students who want real client/consulting reps, design-thinking practice, and comfort with ambiguity; useful signal for consulting internships and leadership growth.
sections.notFor: Anyone who can't accept that the outcome rides on a randomly assigned team and client, or who wants structured skill instruction - it is learning by doing, not curriculum.
sections.workloadNote: Semester-long real-client consulting project with an internal team; called a fair amount of hands-on work. Evening sessions are short lectures plus team work time.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; work centers on team client deliverables and a final client-facing output. Grading itself is not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Outcome hinges on your assigned team/client (3 mentions; one carried a lot of dead weight). 1: class time wildly inefficient, no instructor/TA help. one student reported the team-lead role was unexpectedly draining.
sections.quote: Ultimately, your experience is far, far, far too at the mercy of who you get grouped up with on your team.
comments: The frameworks and thought process that I learned from this class were something I immediately started applying at my job, and I'm sure I will continue using them. It forces you to think in unconventional ways, to explore alternatives and to validate ideas. Working so closely with a team for a semester is also one of the best experiences I've had at Haas. I would definitely recommend the course.
I got a lot out of this course. I had fun, I learned a lot.

8 times out of 10, I would absolutely NOT recommend this course to a fellow student, unless they indicated to me that they would benefit from going through the type of consulting project that this course offers. Ultimately, your experience is far, far, far too at the mercy of who you get grouped up with on your team. While I had some great team members, I'm exhausted from carrying a LOT of dead weight.
Yes
Yes. This course is helpful in case you're looking for an internship and/or looking to work with a client without fear of failure

Haas@Work is a signature course at Haas for a reason and brings human-centered design and innovation principles into practice with real clients. The class combines consulting, product management, AI, strategy, and client work together in a hands on class. Even though it meets in the evenings, I found every class to be valuable time to work with my team and learn consulting and innovation skills that apply in any job context. I loved this class and highly recommend it, although it is a fair amount of hands on work with the internal team and client!

I highly recommend this course to anyone looking to work in the consulting industry. It involves real client needs and helps solve their actual pain points. The entire process closely reflects what real consulting work is actually like. Yes, absolutely; it was very hands on and helped me develop tools for dealing with ambiguous problems and helped in understanding how to " trust the process "
I probably wouldn't recommend the course. With the rise of AI tools today, I feel like part of the course's value proposition has become less compelling

Yes, this class is great if you're looking for hands-on client experience, experience with design thinking methodology, or growth in leadership (internal or client-facing). The experience can be mixed based on the client project you are assigned to, however. It's also less about structured learning and skill sets and more about learning through doing and getting comfortable with navigating ambiguous, complex problem spaces.

Yes, I would recommend both the course and professor. I appreciated the open creative space that was created for us to work in, the lectures were relevant and helpful, but short enough to leave time for group work. I enjoyed working on a real project with real clients and appreciate the structure of this course for making that possible.
No. The class time felt wildly inefficient and I didn't feel like the instructors or TAs stepped in to help or push us along when needed

Would absolutely recommend! Great overview of the topic and awesome discussion
I would definitely recommend this class to a fellow student. No matter what your background, you will find this class to be engaging. The speakers were all great, and broke up the class sessions.

I recommend Professor Macpherson and Health Care in the 21st Century with enthusiasm. This course was insightful, fun to attend, and resulted in substantial learning. I wish I can attend more like this!

Absolutely would recommend Kim 1000%. She's able to masterfully parse through the disjointed information that is endemic to the healthcare sector, and makes it manageable to understand. Anyone that is remotely "healthcare curious" needs to speak with her and take her courses.

Kim is great! Super approachable and ready to help students out as much as possible. There are moments where her knowledge of healthcare is so deep that it can get kind of confusing, but if you have questions she's more than happy to explain. The course ebbs and flows in terms of how much work it is, going from very light to really aggressive around the midterm / some of the cases.
Yes, especially if you have no healthcare background
Absolutely! She has a wealth of knowledge to share and extremely kind and engaging.
go for it! great way to get an overview of the healthcare system

100% - Kim is one of the best instructors at Haas. As a non healthcare student, I was interested in just learning and gaining broad exposure to healthcare, which I think I did from this class. The class does tend to have both Dualies and tons of second year students who do not have healthcare backgrounds, so it tends to have a wide range of experiences. I personally enjoyed the course, but I know it got very granular and detailed at times (hard to follow sometimes). Loved some of the guest speakers and Kim's lectures were very fascinating.
Yes. Great overview of healtcare as an industry - i found it very useful as someone without any background in healthcare who will be going into consulting.

Yes! This class is a great business introduction to the US healthcare system. It might be overwhelming content-wise if you don't have a healthcare background or are not from the US, but all the information is extremely practical and interesting.
I would definitely recommend this instructor. She is well-versed and does a great job of opening up and curating discussions.

Yes. Amazing survey class. Extremely engaging and sparked lots of curiosity in the space, even for non-duallies. I would recommend this course as a great introduction to the complexities of the US healthcare system. Kim is super knowledgeable about this area and great at simplifying complex issues.

I would recommend this course to any student interested in learning more about healthcare, whether you're experienced or new to the industry. Healthcare will continue to play an important role in our lives and this is a great way to dive in.

I would 100% recommend Kim and this class to anyone at all interested in healthcare. She is an incredible lecturer and brain trust in the field of health and the class very well balanced depth and breadth, covering all key healthcare sectors, tied together by key themes, while also providing enough granularity on any given topic.

I would definitely recommend this course. As someone without much healthcare experience, it was an incredible survey of the healthcare industry (payers, providers, device/software innovation, pharma, etc.). I think it was also very useful for students with a stronger healthcare background. Kim is extremely engaging, knowledgable, and well connected. I thoroughly enjoyed the class.

Yes absolutely. Regardless of if you have a healthcare background, this course is an amazing intro to wide range of topics in the healthcare industry ranging from providers, payers, pharma/biotech, med devices, health tech, etc. Kim is super knowledgeable and helpful and stays up to date on the latest information in healthcare.

I recommend taking this class for a high-level overview of how healthcare works in America. Kim is a great professor, she truly cares about her students. The final project is enjoyable and really allows you to think through solutions for healthcare in the US.
I would recommend the course and instructor to anyone interested in US healthcare - Kim is extremely knowledgeable in the space and the guest speakers are renowned in their field.

Yes and yes; the course is useful for understanding how the US healthcare system works and who are the relevant parties involved (motivations, history, etc.). Kim is very knowledgeable and kind and always willing to help students learn and/or connect to folks in industry.

I think this course should be made mandatory to anyone remotely interested in Healthcare. Kim is a legend and staple with deep knowledge and ability to marry policy, business, and theory of healthcare with practice.
a course about US healthcare system, not international perspective and you won't have practical conclusions from being in class or reading the slides

Yes. Great content knowledge if you're curious about or interested in healthcare, especially in the US. Class is less interactive than it could be though, so this is probably a better class to just sit back and take in information. Kim does maker herself accessible to questions or challenging ideas.
Really appreciated this class as an expert deep dive into the healthcare industry!

I recommend this class for anyone who wants to understand the current issues in the health care system. Absolutely recommend -- amazing professor and excellent resource for students interested in the healthcare sector. I would absolutely recommend Kim's courses to any student. It may feel challenging at times but everything that is taught is practical and useful knowledge.
I would recommend this to another student who is interested in learning more about healthcare.
absolutely, this is one of the few courses at haas which i felt i learnt alot from
It is really good to understand landscape or big picture about healthcare in the US, so I would strongly recommend to people who are interested in healthcare!
Yes, it is helpful to future career and day to day life.
100% take this course if you're interested in healthcare. You will learn so much! Something for everyone to engage with (e.g., policy, social determinants, health delivery, tech & innovation, pharma)
I loved this class!!

As a second year MBA student without a background in healthcare, I found this course really interesting. I definitely learned a ton about the healthcare industry. The workload is a bit peaky. Yes! Kim is amazing. A must take if you want to learn and know more about healthcare.
Yes, I would recommend this course to anyone interested in healthcare. Kim is an amazing wealth of knowledge for so many different aspects of the health ecosystem.

This is a really great course - a very interesting overview to the health sector and brilliantly taught! Yes, this course is very worthwhile for anyone interested in the healthcare industry-- career wise or even as a patient/consumer.
Yes. This course gives a great overview of US Healthcare and students bring a variety of healthcare experiences that enhanced my learnings.

Kim is a great teacher, who makes every lecture worthwhile. Her presentation style keeps you attentive through the whole lecture and she is always available for questions and chats outside of class. If you can, definitely take a class with her.

Yes - I would highly recommend this class for anyone who is remotely interested in healthcare. It's such a broad- ranging and complex industry and Kim does a nice job of putting together an engaging syllabus to cover each topic. One of the best classes and teacher in Haas. If you don't know anything about healthcare, as I did, its.even better. You get a very good picture about the main topics in healthcare and how it works in the US.

Yes - this course and Kim were immensely helpful for getting to know the healthcare industry in detail! Yes, because it will give you a nice foundation on how to look at the healthcare industry.
Definitely, Kim is a great intro to the Dualie program and the course lays a good foundation
Yes, the scope of the class is broad and insightful.
Amazing class! Kim knows so much from the industry and gives a great overview. Tons of awesome speakers and fun having a cross listed class.
Yes I would recommend. Engaging instruction, learned a lot, reasonable workload
I would recommend this course to people who are not familiar with the US healthcare system.
This is a great crash course if you're interested in healthcare, and I highly recommend it. The courseload is moderate and consists of three written cases and one final project.
Yes I would reccomend to anyone interested in healthcare

Absolutely! Even if you are not interested in a career in healthcare, this is one of the most engaging courses at Haas. Kim is incredible at facilitating discussion and making you think in new ways. You cover every aspect of healthcare in the US and some global context as well.
Yes - anyone who is interested in HC (or lives in the US) should take this course

Would definitely recommend this class for anyone remotely interested in the healthcare industry and also for anyone looking to take an extra elective taught by a fantastic professor/lecturer. Kim is a phenomenal presenter who is extremely well-networked with people in the healthcare and healthtech industry; the guest speakers are a huge highlight of the course. As someone who is not an MPH/MBA student and has previously never worked in anything related to healthcare, I still did fairly well in the course and was able to keep up. It's not a heavy lift of a class-- good use of time and an engaging class experience!
Totally. It is a great way to get an introduction to the healthcare system in the US, how it works, its evolution, its current state and what opportunities can be found to improve it.
One of the best classes I took in my 1st year fall.
If you are interested in working the industry, this is a must. Kim is very experienced, brings amazing speakers and makes you wanna go to class.

Kim is one of the best professors at Haas. This course was one of my top 3 classes also. The content is industry specific, but you learn a lot, about the US healthcare system, international perspectives, the business side of health. Classes are fun and insightful as Kim is a very engaging speaker, super knowledgable, well connected and up to date on industry news and trends.
Kim is wonderful! Unshakeable. Offers a wonderful lineup of influential, relevant guest speakers.

Yes. 100%. See my previous response. Every student should be required to take a class with Kim before graduation. I learned so much about the healthcare system in the US in just a few short months, and I feel like I can now carry a meaningful conversation about the problems facing US healthcare, as well as the potential solutions. If you're interested in healthcare at all, then I highly recommend this class.

sections.goodFor: Anyone interested in any corner of US healthcare (digital health, pharma, services) - Macpherson's network and guest speakers are repeatedly cited, including for internships.
sections.notFor: Students wanting frameworks and structured instruction - after the first few weeks it runs as a speaker series; the merely curious with no healthcare background may struggle to keep up.
sections.workloadNote: Bimodal: three case assignments described as 'a TON of work' plus a heavy final project, sprinkled through the semester; outside those the course is not much work.
sections.gradingBasis: Three case write-ups plus a final project; students call the assignments fair.
sections.redFlags: Two to three say Kim largely stops teaching after the first few weeks and it becomes a speaker series with limited practical frameworks and little discussion time; the three cases are very heavy.
sections.quote: Outside of the first few weeks of the course though Kim doesn't really teach the class, it functions more like a speaker series.
comments: For those interested in understanding the US healthcare landscape this is a class someone should strongly consider taking.

This course gave a great overview of the complexities of the healthcare system in an engaging and digestible way for students who range in level of past experience in healthcare. I'd recommend the class as it is well-organized and fair in terms of assignments. Kim's passion and enthusiasm for the subject comes across in her lecturing style. She is up- to-date in what's going on in the healthcare world which lends itself well to the material/curriculum that she updates every year. She is also well-connected to people in industry and brings in stellar guest lecturers. Although cases require a significant amount of time, there are only a few sprinkled out through the semester and stimulating to think about and apply learnings from class. If interested in any aspects of American healthcare (digital health, pharma, healthcare services, etc.), I'd recommend taking the class.

This class brings in amazing speakers from healthcare companies shaping the industry. Kim's connections go hard and you can get a lot out of them. Outside of the first few weeks of the course though Kim doesn't really teach the class, it functions more like a speaker series. As awesome as the speakers were I was hoping for a bit more practical instruction and frameworks. The three cases you have to complete are a TON of work. But they are very interesting and relevant and I learned a lot from them that I've taken into networking sessions. Outside of the three cases and final project which are all a heavy lift, the course is not a lot of work.
Yes, I thought it was good - tons of very good speakers, but not a lot of time to engage and discuss as a class. Kim is very good.

Yes, with the qualifier that this is a very different class structure than most MBA classes and can be harder in that sense. Kim is incredibly smart, well-informed in the space, and well-connected, which can help you get an internship over the summer if that is what you are looking for
Absolutely! If you have any interest in Healthcare at all this is an amazing class to take!
Yes! one of the must-take course here at Haas

sections.goodFor: Students interested in people, management, human capital, HR, or data broadly; several non-quantitative students said it unexpectedly became their favorite class. Commenters also flag the AI/ML, algorithmic-bias, and experiment-design content as relevant well beyond HR.
sections.workloadNote: One commenter noted the learning was substantial relative to the amount of work required, implying a manageable load.
sections.quote: Absolutely. This class was highly informative with a strong professor leading the course. The amount of learning was substantial for the amount of work needed to be put into the class.
comments: Yes, yes, yes! Absolutely love how engaging Professor G is. The class covers the most interesting topics I've had during my entire Haas career. Unexpectedly my favorite class at Haas. Must take if you are at all interested in human capital/people/management.

Absolutely. This class was highly informative with a strong professor leading the course. The amount of learning was substantial for the amount of work needed to be put into the class. Very intellectually engaging.

Yes and yes; the course is really fascinating and with data becoming ubiquitous, it is useful to understand how it will be used for good/evil (even if unintentionally). Furthermore, the course made me appreciate how data is a precious resource for recruiting/retaining talent and it is imperative to understand how that will be used. And Doug is very nice and knowledgeable and really wants his students to learn so the course is fun and engaging.

Definitely - I did not have high expectations for this class as someone that does not identify as a quantitative or data driven person but it ended up being my favorite class of the semester. The content was digestible, relevant, and helpful for future applications in data and people strategy decision making.

I would recommend Douglas to any student who is interested in People Analytics, people in any form, or data in any form. Yes. He does a lot of interesting research that he references throughout class. He is very passionate about the subject matter.
Absolutely. Even for students who aren't interested in HR specifically, the learnings about AI and ML were very relevant to the future of work and society.

Yes, loved this class! Topics of the course were extremely interesting and relevant to our current society, talking about algorithms and algorithmic bias, how to design HR systems with diversity/equity/inclusion lens. Professor incorporated a balance of academic studies, concepts, and class activities which all contributed to the learning. He was also very receptive to discussion and incorporating a lot of people's voices in the discussion.
Yes, for anyone interested in how people interact in an increasingly digital world and how analytics will take on a bigger role in the future.
yes

Professor Douglas is excellent with making the learning relevant. He spends extra timing making sure he has the latest examples and cases. He also includes a variety of ways to engage-- between lecture, discussion, team activities and experiments in class. Most importantly, he is the one and one professor I've had at Haas who has done extensive work in learning about social identities, system issues and connecting it to the learning in the most relevant way. I was consistently amazed with how thoughtful he was -- a simple example is acknowledging gender identity and how to include a variety of identities when running experiments. I think Professor Douglas should teach a micro-class or be observed by other Professors on how to incorporate Diversity, Inclusion and Equity into coursework.

Yes. This class was not only relevant to people analytics, but all types of experiments you could think to do. It sparked an interest in a topic I had not originally thought I'd pursue and I think everyone should give it a try! Absolutely. He is the best professor at Haas.

Yes. This course reflects on the usage of Data Science in an area that doesn't get enough spotlight. Impact of Analytics on people. This is a very important area and i think this course helps throw light on this often overlooked area of Data Science.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this course. It's an excellent introduction for anyone who is curious about real estate but doesn't yet have a deep understanding of how the industry works in the U.S. Most people initially think of real estate only in terms of development or residential brokerage. This course opens your eyes to the much broader set of career paths available — including commercial acquisitions, asset management, affordable housing, and real estate investment, among others.

Hearing directly from experienced professionals provides a realistic picture of the work involved, the types of skills that matter, and the lifestyle and compensation considerations in each area. By the end of the course, you'll have a clear, high-level view of where you might fit within the real estate ecosystem, whether you're considering it as a full-time career or a future side investment.
