Yes, would recommend. Very comprehensive and relevant to the social sector. Combines important curriculum, with a very experienced instructor and interdisciplinary class. Diverse content, that is well delivered and extremely applicable. nA

Social Impact Metrics is a topic that is not very straightforward. There is no correct way that social impact data should be collected, processed, and shared. So this class explains that clearly and provides case studies on theories of change, but ultimately it feels difficult to come out of the class having a new sense of expertise. Even though the course label "metrics" would convey some sort of learned skill to manipulate and understand data, this could be viewed more as a survey course about how social impact metrics are very hazy.

I really appreciated the chance to dive into social impact metrics, and appreciated the warmth and ideas of Colin and my fellow classmates, but it's definitely a heavy workload, and I often wanted to have clearer takeaways to class sessions.

Yes, Colin is a clear and engaging lecturer. Class discussions were interesting, inclusive, and thought-provoking. The workload was reasonable and assignments did a good job of linking theory to application. Sometimes the course felt disorganized but it was an overall positive experience.
Medium - the case discussions were interesting and I really enjoyed the topic, but I found many of the organizational aspects frustrating
YES! Such a fun class, and it was great learning from students from non-MBA programs. Highly recommend. Great way to learn more than the basics that you'd cover in a typical MBA program.
Yes, and yes! 100%.

Unfortunately, I would not recommend this course. It was generally a drag. The content was repetitive and narrowly focused on impact metrics within development and non-profits. This class seemed more fitting for a policy school rather than the business school.

Yes I would recommend this class- it's a great introduction to the concept of impact measurement and navigating different methods of measurement balanced against the cost of doing the evaluation. We cover many industries and countries in our discussions and the professor is really supportive of our learning and engagement.

Colin is very knowledgable on the subject, passionate about social impact, a great discussion facilitator, and especially great at helping students think critically (a student might answer a question bluntly and then he'd have a conversational approach to helping them expand). I found myself thinking very critically; moreso than other courses. He runs an enjoyable class and is enthusiastic about the subject.
Yes, definitely.

I would totally recommend this course. The content is very comprehensive and the professor is quite engaging. The assignments are hard but very worthwhile and make us learn and think through. I had no background in social impact metrics even if I had worked with social impact for quite a long time. To me, this was a great course but you can enjoy the most if you have some extra 2 hours to work on pre-readings per week.

This was one of my favorite courses at Haas. Out of all the classes I have taken, this one pushed me to think the most critically, and to really dive deep in asking "why." The class was well-facilitated, I felt like I learned a great deal from the content, the professor, and my classmates, and I overall came out of this class feeling like a more informed business leader and person moving forward.

While the level of preparation for this class is high given the weekly cases, the main benefit is the ability to learn from Colin who will cement both your interest and skepticism in the industry and who will convince you of the value of the field. This class made me want to become a social impact leader and keep Colin in my network to succeed in future roles.
Yes. I would like to recommend to my fellow friends so they know that this course allows them to think holistically about the social impact
Yes! Passionate, knowledgeable, encouraging, thoughtful professor!
Yes! Amazing course for anyone who wants to work in a social impact organisation
Yes I would recommend this. I had no idea at all about Social Impact and this has been a good introduction to it. I am very satisfied with the course.

I would take this class if you're curious about what social impact is, how metrics can be leveraged in social impact, if you want to learn from Colin, who has had a wealth of experience in global health and consulting - he is one of the kindest professors at Haas. This class gives you the tools to critically think about and evaluate social impact organizations - there are also interesting case studies from around the world (e.g., Uganda, South Korea)

sections.goodFor: Students headed into nonprofit, social sector or impact investing work, or anyone who has to measure hard-to-quantify outcomes; also good from a public health angle.
sections.notFor: Students not going into social impact say relevance drops off; the all-case, participation-required format can get boring, and the course largely endorses metrics rather than critiquing them.
sections.workloadNote: Weekly cases and readings; students specifically say assignments are fair with no busy work and that they reinforce the class concepts. Hours not stated.
sections.gradingBasis: Case discussion with participation required, weekly readings, and assignments students call fair with no busy work.
sections.redFlags: Two of 15 say relevance falls off sharply if you're not entering the social sector; one found the all-case format boring at times; one wanted a more critical take on the limits of metrics.
sections.quote: At times, it can be a little boring because it's all case-based with discussions in class and participation is necessary.
comments: I would recommend this course as Colin is an effective lecturer engaging students in thought-provoking discussions. He applies theory to the real-world and walks through specific case studies that enable critical learning. Yes, if they are interested in a career in social impact. I think it's less relevant to me than I was expecting but I still found the learnings and frameworks for critiquing study design interesting.
Yes absolutely!

Yes, absolutely. I'd highly recommend this course — especially for anyone interested in working in the social sector or tackling problems where good measurement really matters. Social Impact Metrics gives you practical tools you can apply immediately, and Colin's teaching style makes even the tougher analytical concepts feel clear, engaging, and surprisingly fun.
Colin is very engaging, approachable, and passionate! He was effective at facilitating case discussions in a way that didn't just feel like a regurgitation of case facts.

Colin is an incredible professor. Super knowledgeable about the subject and the class is structured in a way that really facilitates learning. Assignments are fair, there's no busy work, and I felt the assignments helped me gain a better understanding of the concepts discussed in class. I thought the cases were very informative and interesting as well! Would recommend.
definitely!! great guy all around, funny and very knowledgeable on the subject

I would recommend this class for someone who is definitely going to go into non-profit or social impact work. I sometimes felt like it lost the forest for the trees: is non-profit work really the place to make the most impact or do we need to figure out how to change private companies to shift more in this direction as well? I felt that the class could have been a little more critical of using metrics rather than fully endorsing them as an always excellent tool. I would absolutely recommend this course to anyone interested in social impact! Professor Boyle has amazing insights and course content is extremely applicable and helpful for any social impact professional.
Colin Boyle is a wonderful professor! I really enjoyed this course and consider it a must-take if you're interested in the social sector.

Great class if you're interested in social impact, especially if you're interested in data and metrics. Colin is a extremely knowledgeable and has a great personality. He really cares about the information and the class is structured well. At times, it can be a little boring because it's all case-based with discussions in class and participation is necessary. Yes, this can help you understand a less traditional way of thinking to help us be better, more rounded out leaders in the future

Yes, Colin was a true facilitator of insightful conversation for each week's case, challenging students to dig deeper to question why certain social impact decisions were made by organizations and how to best evaluate outcomes from a data-driven perspective. The class provided a very unbiased perspective and allowed people like me (who have little social impact experience) to better understand the complexities of investing and decision-making within the industry. I would recommend this class if you are interested in social impact work -- it gives a good foundation for how to think about measuring impact and what the limitations and opportunities are for different metrics or study designs I would recommend this course to peers, because it gives a strong foundation in critical thinking about impact, evaluation, and the intersection of the two. Colin crafted an insightful, engaging, and valuable course that raised important considerations for both the theory and practice of impact evaluation. The class readings were helpful in diving into the topic we discussed and lecture & discussion of underlying assumptions was great for uncovering the why evaluation happens and how to get the most out of the process. I thought the course was well structured and that Colin does a great job facilitating discussion to support student learning.
yes

Yes for professor Boyle I would give him the highest of recommendation. For the class I think it is great for everyone who is interested in working with some sort of measurement, even if not Social Impact. A lot of the ideas can transfer to other fields where outcomes can be difficult to measure.
Yes, it is useful for real-world decision making. This is one of the best class I've taken so far.

This course is a great complement to other Haas classes in that it helps evaluate the effectiveness of initiatives not focused on profit. It's a great lens to be able to use in your career and personal life.
I would. I think it is a unique and valuable opportunity to explore a new area, particularly coming from a public health perspective.

Definitely recommend it to students looking for 1) connection with fellow MBA students from different parts of the world 2) condensed introduction to entrepreneurship and VC and their connection, and 3) experimental learning by building business model as entrepreneur and building investment thesis as VC partner. However, if you already have experience with entrepreneurship and/or VC or have taken some classes with either subject, this may not be the right level of class for you. [Only for remote learning] Since a lot of students are taking this remotely from different time zones, you have classmates that are taking this class 3am in the morning. Prepare for different energy
level/availability/etc. when doing group project after class.

If you could split this course into two different courses, I might take the first one with Sara (entrepreneur-side), but I would definitely not take the one with David (VC-side). The entrepreneur-side portion of the class was much more "real-life impact" as you got to work and talk with actual founders of companies, and fit those discussions into well- defined and taught aspects of entrepreneurship management. The VC-side was nearly impossible to follow, as David's approach to teaching material was entirely disjointed and followed logical progression, leaving most students without any kind of substantial learning. The guest speakers, as wonderful as they were, began to just start feeling like time- fillers, as the discussion with them were often unguided and rehashed comments made by other speakers. Their contributions would be much more impactful if they were tied to specific parts of the teaching and had their discussion based around that module. All in all, not a good course for Haas to be showing externally to the GNAM world.

It is a bit of an intense week. A roughly 48 hour deep dive as an entrepreneur and then another roughly 48 deep dive as a VC. The style of the class is to sort of throw you in to the deep end and let you figure it out. It can get a little intense, but it works. I learned a ton about both worlds and their connection.

I would recommend the instructor and course if the student was newer to entrepreneurship and the Bay Area, the topic is definitely well covered. While I thought the course itself was valuable, I found the group assignments via Zoom and all constricted to a week very difficult. It was hard for me to coordinate with my team in different time zones and often times we were tasked to submit assignments on very short turnaround. I understand it's only a week long course and so it's not possible to have much depth in the assignments but I would almost prefer less assignments spread out over time. In addition, some students apparently were not going to receive grades or credits for the course and I feel that definitely makes the incentives less aligned for group project work.
Yes, if you have zero exposure to the world of investment/entrepreneurship
Great course. Be prepared to work very hard. But it is only one week so you can do it.
It is a good overview of the entrepreneurship and VC ecosystem in Silicon Valley, but the class did not move the needle much for me.
Yes, totally. I learnt a lot
Yes yes and yes! They are amazing!

Yes, amazing course. You get to meet so many incredible people from around the world and get a deep insight into the silicon valley ecosystem. Very different course from the others and highly recommended
I hope it will have more company visits rather than staying in classroom

Dr. Vivek Rao and Dr. David Charon are a great team. They gave us good exposure to both the entrepreneurial and VC sides of the ecosystem in the Bay Area through interactive classes, meaningful panel discussions, and role plays. Having students from prominent B-schools around the world enriched the whole experience.

I would highly recommend this course for anyone interested in a crash course in VC and entrepreneurship. If you already have understanding and knowledge of both sides, the first two sessions may not deliver new information. That said, the other parts of the course will still give value - panels and small speaker sessions, pitching (as both a VC and startup), working in new and small teams, company visit. The professors work as a friendly and dynamic duo and keep things lively in what can be quite an intense week!

I would highly recommend this course, you will not only learn things within the classroom, also you will also meet new ppl from other top B schools, life is all about knowing new person, and team up with them, especially those who are better or same excellent as you.

I thought this course would be more about the Bay Area and Silicon Valley entrepreneurship scene but it was more of an introductory course for entrepreneurship and VC more generally. I was hoping for more company visits. It was largely geared towards the students from other institutions that were there as part of GNAM.

sections.goodFor: Students new to entrepreneurship and venture capital who want a hands-on crash course, and anyone who values networking with international MBA students from other schools; the guest panels, pitching from both founder and VC sides, and site visits get consistent praise.
sections.notFor: Students who already have entrepreneurship or VC experience say it will not move the needle, and some expected more Bay Area company visits than the mostly classroom format delivered. One remote-year student also warned about coordinating group work across time zones.
sections.workloadNote: A compressed one-week intensive that students call intense, with back-to-back entrepreneur and VC deep dives and group assignments on very short turnarounds.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (3 comments): too introductory for anyone with prior entrepreneurship or VC exposure. Recurring (2 comments): fewer company visits than the course title suggests.
sections.quote: Yes, amazing course. You get to meet so many incredible people from around the world and get a deep insight into the silicon valley ecosystem.
comments: I already recommend to my cohort and will continue to support this course. If I do well, such as raising capital successfully to form a fund, I am more than happy to come back to share my journey next year.
Yes, was a great course to understand their basics of Entrepreneurship and Venture Capital. It was also amazing to meet and network with people from all across the globe.

I would recommend to those who wants to have an overview of the entrepreneurship and venture capital. I HIGHLY recommend this course. It offers something for everyone regardless of where they are in their MBA journey. Yes, David has a unique perspective on the subject matter and communicates his perspective effectively. Yes, absolutely worth. You would get a perspective from both entrepreneurship and investor with the hands on projects.

This class was a great opportunity to bond with a group of international MBA Students if you don't have the opportunity to undergo another international experience while at Haas. The class was very hands on- numerous guest speaks including both VC's and entrepreneurs, site visits to start-ups, tours of Bakar and Berkeley SkyDeck which was a unique experience unlike any other Haas class.
Yes! Thank you!
yes. made great connections and good sharing from industry experts which was exactly what I expected from of this short course.

rows.title: Sales Force Management and Channel Strategy

sections.goodFor: Anyone going into sales, go-to-market, channel/partner strategy or biz dev - especially at-scale selling rather than startup scrappiness. Praised by tech and engineering backgrounds.
sections.notFor: Students who already worked in sales or channel-partner teams; one says most of the course will feel basic, though the strategy/leadership angle may still add value.
sections.workloadNote: Coursework requires solid PowerPoint skills (though not necessarily presenting); assignments called thought-provoking and practical. Guest speakers and cases feature heavily. Hours not stated.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - PowerPoint-based assignments and cases are mentioned, but no exams or grading breakdown are discussed.
sections.redFlags: Little recurring criticism. One says those with prior sales/channel experience will find it basic; one found a guest speaker's delivery unexciting; Azhar's dry humor takes a class or two to get used to.
sections.quote: If you have prior experience working in sales/channel partner teams or experience closely collaborating with these teams then you may find most of the course basic for you.
comments: This class is invaluable for those who work directly with a sales team or who plan to manage/create one in the future. The coursework requires a solid understanding of creating PowerPoint presentations (though not necessarily presenting them). I would highly recommend this class, even if it is solely to understand the incentivization and structuring of a sales team.
Yes, fantastic class

I would highly recommend this course and professor to my fellow students. I had no prior knowledge of sales teams and channels, yet came away with a great understanding of how their success is paramount to a company's operations.
Some of the guest speakers that I consider paramount to our learning:
-Abde Tambawalla
-Joshua Sivaslian
-Yamini Rangan
I thought that Chris Jones' presentation was not very exciting, but I really appreciated his case, as well as his POV. It is very interesting to learn about his perspective as a VAR.

Many Haas classes teach scrappy startup sales, but companies at scale operate way differently. This class is essential for anyone wanting to work on the "revenue side" of a company (where everyone should want to work...) This course has been an amazing learning experience for me. Coming from technology background, I had very limited exposure to sales. The course helped me understand the principles and strategies that the sales and marketing teams employ in planning go to market strategies.
Yes
Absolutely Yes
This class is essential for anyone aiming to develop expertise in sales and channel strategy.

It covers several foundational marketing concepts that every business or marketing student should understand. Fantastic class - take it. Really different perspective on go to market than any other class at haas. Take it with Wasim - dry sense of humor make take a class or two to get used to but he is the GOAT for a reason... you learn about how to set up a sales motion and what types of sales teams work for different kinds of products and markets. Strong focus on channels and especially how to work with partners which is somewhat unique and not that common to have a specific class on. Prof is just a good person to learn from, period.

Prof Azhar is amazing; super knowledgable and a great instructor. This course broadly covers salesforce management and channel strategy and you get an overview of the key challenges and dynamics. The course had some really great speakers; learnt a lot from them and you get to interact on a personal level.

If you have prior experience working in sales/channel partner teams or experience closely collaborating with these teams then you may find most of the course basic for you. However, you can still learn to sharpen your strategic and leadership skills in those domains.

This has been one of the best courses I have taken at Haas. It provides a deep dive into channel strategy and the principles required to design, manage, and scale successful go-to-market organizations. Coming from an engineering background, the course opened an entirely new world for me and fundamentally shifted how I think about business development, pivots, and growth strategy.

The assignments were thought provoking and reinforced the concepts in a practical, engaging way. Professor Azhar is extremely approachable, fosters rich class discussion, and drives down to the crux of the concept. The guest speakers were outstanding — experienced, relevant, and deeply current. They covered a wide range of topics, from GTM design to sales force management, and offered insights that were both inspirational and aspirational.

I would highly recommend this course to anyone interested in strategy, channels, or business development. Extremely recommended if you would like to understand more about the sales channel or sales structure.

rows.title: Startup Sales
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2022 Spring;2022 Fall;2023 Spring;2023 Fall;2024 Spring;2024 Fall;2025 Spring;2025 Fall;2026 Spring

comments: Absolutely, one of my favorite course. Provided practicable approaches to navigating sales as a startup.

Yes. If you are considering becoming a sales for startups or a founder one day, this class is for you. No previous sales experience is required. Joe will have a thorough dive into the sale functions, techniques, compensation, and common practice in this class. It is one of the most useful classes I took at Haas.

Yes, Joe gives a comprehensive and hands on view of what sales function looks like in different stages of startup. Super solid learning in startup and what sales is all about. NOT focused on sales techniques or soft skills.
Yes, for students that want to start a business or you just want to know more about sales. One caveat is that this course does focus more on sales for small companies not for big companies
Yes Joe is a superstar and his connection and knowledge in the industry is super valuable

Would definitely recommend this class not only for students interested in the sales function but really for ANY founder or anyone considering starting a company. The Founder / CEO is the primary sales person for the first part of the journey (and longer than you'd think). In addition to a lot of good content on how to build a sales team, we also covered topics broadly relevant to startups, including pricing.
I would recommed startups sales to anyone interested in B2B sales or startups in genereal

This course is very helpful for individuals who are interested in starting or working at an early stage startup. It's still useful for people who don't fit into those two buckets, but more from a high-level "what is sales" angle. Would recommend!
Highly recommended

Yes. Joe just gets it. He knows how to teach what the students need to know. This is a very high value course, meaning that I got a ton out of it for the amount of time I put in. It is not a high-lift course, but do the assignments and the readings because they are all valuable and the opposite of busy work. If you're not going to do the assignments, don't take the class. Joe is very organized, tells good anecdotes that ground the topic in reality, and does a good job engaging the class when appropriate. Everything I learned was applicable to my job post-Haas, which is a testament to the real-world applications of Joe's teaching.

This is one of the better courses I've taken at Haas, despite the fact that I'm neither going into sales nor startups. Very low/reasonable lift in terms of coursework, and a great exploration of sales fundamentals with a ton of very nitty-gritty (in a good way) start-up facts/advice/info. Joe is a really effective, thoughtful, clear professor with plenty of start-up and sales experience to draw real-life examples from. Readings are short and to the point. Lectures are very useful. I would strongly recommend this class.

I would recommend this course to another student, but with the caveat to read the course description closely. This course will not 'teach' you how to become an effective salesperson, rather it will teach you about the function of sales and how it fits into a larger oganization. If that's what you're looking for, it'll be a great course. If you want to learn persuasion techniques and how to 'close a deal', you're better taking negotiations.

Absolutely. It is highly insightful and practical. Great for people who are interested in entrepreneurship, sales, business development or growth. Likely to be one of my favourite classes in Berkeley.
Great class! Joe is a very enthusiastic and knowledgable person, giving many insights and thoughts. I also like the assignments design a lot, both practical and helpful.
Would recommend to students interested in sales execution and sales management without prior experience. Useful for entrepreneurs.
Highly recommend to students who would like to know what real startup sales is. Models coupled with real-world examples and simulations make this class extremely effective.

This is really the only sales class that is offered at Haas. I think that sales should be part of our core curriculum. What percentage of graduates are ever going to utilize a concept from micro-economics? Probably not very many! What percentage of us will engage with or manage sales? Probably a lot! None of the material is particularly complex or advanced, but learning the general jargon and overall material will put you a step ahead of your peers when you begin your post-Haas career!
yes!
Highly recommended -- would want every student to take this alse class
Absolutely, one of the most valuable classes I took while at Haas
Best course to understand revenue generation. Highly recommend

This should be one of your top 5 courses at Haas. If you are doing a startup, or want to work at one, it is required reading. The good news is that Joe is wildly entertaining, a great teacher, stays up to date, has real experience, and a great teacher.

I would recommend this course-Joe organizes it very well and the material covers a lot of sales information that I had no prior exposure to. Probably a little easy if you have a lot of sales experience, but good for career pivoters. Absolutely recommend. Great teacher, great energy, more practical knowledge.
This is one of the best classes I have taken at Haas. If you are interested in entrepreneurship, tech, startups, or sales, this class is invaluable. One of the most practically helpful classes.
Yes, everyone needs to know sales

This class was very enjoyable. Joe is such an engaging professor and I looked forward to coming to class every session. The course material is very relevant to those who are interested in tech sales and those who want to or are starting their own companies.
Yes! A great class with a good mix of interesting readings (you'll probably find new substacks and/or twitters to subscribe to) and Joe's knowledge of the start up space is great.
Yes
Yes, I really loved this class and I think anyone interested in sales should take it
yes, great overview
Yes! He rocks!!

If you're interested in learning more about the sales function, or even have worked in sales-adjacent roles and want to know more about their incentives, organizational structure, different types of (unexpected) sales roles, and how you can better work with a sales team (or join a sales team) in the future, then this is a great class to take. Additionally, if you're starting your own company (or joining an early stage startup), Joe does a great job explaining how the sales function changes (and should change) as a company goes through its various phases. Overall very valuable class, and fills a gap in the MBA curriculum as one of the only sales-related classes available at Haas.

Yes! But I would be clear that this class is is very much oriented around specific mechanics of startup sales. It is not theoretical or general business development, but goes deeply into terms, how sales teams are structured, etc. Absolutely-if you are interested in tech and startups, it is key to learn the material in this class. Joe is also a Haasie, so he also provides an exceptionally positive classroom experience.
Definitely I would recommend! It is very light class full of content!
I had no idea how big were a sales team and how difficult/important it is to develop it very well since the beginning - This class supported me very well on that!

Loved this course - gives you a crash course in startup sales and growth. Joe is an engaging and helpful instructor! Yes! Great class if want to start a business, or learn more about sales. Somewhat slow moving at times, but a low lift and Joe is the best

Yes. It's the only sales class at Haas, and I think it's essential to have at least a basic knowledge. If you come from a sales role, the course it's probably basic, but if not, it's beneficial. If you want to be an entrepreneur, it's also handy. You learn how to formulate, test, and pivot ideas from a sales perspective.
Yes, I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student; however, I would caution them about course quizzes and work assignments.
Yes - definitely if student is involved in a new venture or startup

Joe is passionate about teaching the subject. I would only recommend this course if you are interested in exploring sales in a B2B and startup context. However, many things covered in class are a little basic and I'm not sure if you need a two-hour lecture to learn them.

Yes, on a value for time basis this is one of the more useful classes at Haas. Joe is conscious of making sure the material is real-world applicable while not overloading students. While nothing in the course was mind-blowing, I certainly feel like I am more equipped to structure and lead a sales organization after taking this class

I thought this course was interesting and had a relatively light load compared to other classes. I think it didn't really lead to a substantial amount of learning but that may be also due to the fact that I am not actively interested in the start-up space. The assignments were interesting and I think I have a new perspective on sales and start ups which might be helpful in the future.

100% - one of my favorite classes so far. My advice to future students is to not be turned off by the word " sales " in this course title, like I was at first. This class isn't just about how to be a salesperson – it has much broader applications and can be useful for anyone in almost any post-MBA role.
Yes. For folks that have no background in sales, this class is good

For anyone interested in entrepreneurship this class is fantastic. Sales is key to any business especially when starting out. The material is on point, the speakers are helpful, and Joe is a great teacher. This class is the definition of great bang for your buck.
This course was so refreshing! It was so applicable to the world of Software / Tech / Saas in a way that no other class at Haas has been.
Joe was extremely organized, all of his examples were up-to-date, his guest speakers were engaging, and the assignments resulted in actual learnings.

If you've worked in sales or were sales adjacent in a SAAS company previously, much of what will be taught will be review. But otherwise, I'd recommend it to everyone. Lots of valuable nuggets of startup advice as well.

Absolutely. This course has been one of the best I've taken at Haas. As someone who wants to be a product manager who understands go to market and possibly one day wants to found a company, everything taught in this course is valuable.
Yes! If you are interested in startups, this is a great course

I definitely recommend this course if you have a serious interest in startups and/or sales. It provides the nuts and bolts of what's required to generate revenue in a new to late stage startup. If this is not a serious interest of yours, you may be bored as it definitely gets in the weeds. But if startups are your thing, you will learn really valuable information. Startup Sales is a great class which is super focused on practical application. It provides a great intro to startup sales (particularly B2B SaaS). Also, Joe is a great professor and makes class fun and engaging. The work load is also very manageable.

Joe has a ton of practical experience as an operator and a sales professional. He brings that to class every day and turns it into a high-efficiency learning experience. In many ways, this course and Joe's other course are some of the highest efficiency classes I have had, in terms of learning/time spent. Joe is additionally funny, engaging, and insightful. He's easily one of the best instructors I have had at Haas so far.
If you are interested in starting a company or exploring sales roles, you should check out this class!

I would recommend this course if you ever think you'll be working at a startup in a sales role or not. Sales is the engine of any early stage company, so having an appreciation for the function and thinking about things like sales structure, compensation, and growth strategy is critically important.

Yes! Joe is very personable and cares about the learning of his students. He is very approachable and willing to spend more/less time on material we are more interested in. I think this class is enjoyable and not too much work, but not necessarily a "must take."

Yes, it provides a very systematic approach to learning startup sales and how to scale the sales organization as the business grows. Sales is one of the biggest functions and it's helpful to learn how the function works and think about how it relates to my future job (or even consider working in the sales organization). Plus Joe is amazing! He really has the hands-on experience to share the most practical and useful knowledge.
Anyone interested in building and running a startup should take this class!

This class is great if you are interested in start-ups, growing a business or sales. It is not a class that will teach you how to be a sales person. Rather it teaches you a lot about start-ups and things to consider when establishing your first sales organization.
great prof with practical lessons and excellent energy

Joe is a great professor with a ton of expertise and broad knowledge. I'm not as interested in the SaaS/ tech world, so the topics were not as relevant or interesting to me. I wish I had known that before taking the class.
Interesting class if you want to learn about sales

Hell yes I will. Professor Wadcan's track record and experience speaks for itself, and he is not an academic hack preaching to students. He is a seasoned professional in the world of startups, someone who has lived through the fire, and not just some PhD who is lecturing to students without any life experience. Startup Sales is my favorite class at Haas and most valuable, and it has everything to do with Professor Wadcan sharing his valuable insights with the student body. He is someone we can respect because of his experience.

Yes, this is a great practical class if you are interested in startups or sales. I had no experience with sales prior to this course and I learned a lot that I think will prepare me well for life at a startup or even at a larger company that is involved with sales. Joe is energetic and has lots of great real world experience. He also brings in many speakers who have founded their own companies and offer a great perspective. The course is heavily SaaS focused (as Joe says at the beginning) so if you are not interested in tech than maybe it won't be for you as much.
Yes - this course focusses heavily on SaaS sales. Its learnings carry over into all sales and provide useful information to any business manager.

comments: YES - Fantastic subject matter. Focuses on the psychology (backed with clear experiments and research) that go into consumer decision making. I walked away with clear and specific tools to use when developing ad campaigns, marketing materials, or even just any sort of product that will be used by another human being. She also gave us simple heuristics to go off of to manage rapid A/B tests, things like how to determine a good sample size or when a result is significant.

Yes, this is the only Haas course that goes deep into consumer behaviour. If you're new to Marketing and consumer growth for your startup/big companies, I definitely recommend this course. Especially, if you want to design Marketing ads for your product and learn what ticks your customers, this is the course to take.

Yes, Consumer insights with Professor Evers is one of the more interesting classes I have taken at Haas, and really brings home a lot of theories related to marketing and decision-making in a B2C context, which is helpful in today's world. Definitely in my top 5 favorite classes at Haas.

You don't get into the nitty gritty of laws, it's more about the application of them to business.
Yes. The topic is very beneficial to business students in general

Yes, I would definitely recommend it. I think the learnings from this class will definitely be useful to my future career. It has also opened my eyes to a deeper understanding of how business operates. I think legal learning should be
incorporated to all business curriculum.

I would recommend this class to others because it taught me a lot and I think it is important information for future business leaders. The final paper is a bit long, but overall it wasn't too much work and it was very interesting to learn from someone who is a corporate executive.

This was possibly my favorite class at Haas. Steve has created such a good list of topics to cover and has a fantastic roster of guest lecturers to take the message home. Steve himself is such an impressive guy with a storied career and a bright mind. I can't think of a single Haas student that wouldn't benefit from this class. There is a bit of workload involved in terms of a presentation and a paper but it is more than worth it. I am shocked this isn't a 50+ person class in Chou. It is more than worthy.

No, I would not. Steve is kind, but not the best professor and I did not take a lot of value from this course. His lectures are brutal to sit through and a third of the class are just listening to class presentations. Take a different legal class if you are interested in the topic.

I highly recommend this course. Steve discusses topics that will be relevant to folks trying to start a business or work for a large corporation. The workload is relatively light during the semester; however, there is a 5,000 word paper due at the end of the class (10+ pages).

I would absolutely recommend this course to any Haas student that is interested in learning about the role legal will play in their future business career - hint: it will impact everything! I think the biggest take-away was the role legal can play as a strategic partner to a business enterprise as opposed to an adversary (which was my biased opinion coming in).
Yes! Steve is great and brings a super interesting perspective given his role at American Airlines and his

vast/impressive network (which he brings in as guest speakers in about 1/3 of the classes). He assigns a lot of reading but it's not required, there was 1 group project and 1 final paper for the whole class, so it's relatively low lift too. Also good exposure to the legal side of business, especially if you're in startups/entrepreneurship.

Absolutely yes! This course is a must at Haas - with an opportunity to engage and network with one of our most successful Haasies. I highly recommend this course. You'll both learn so much from the legal environment and engage with an executive with years of experience leading a major Fortune 500 and driving private equity deals.
Yes
Yes, Steve is great! It's a light lift class and I found the real world applications to Steve's work very interesting. Yes definitely would recommend this course.
Worthwhile class if you are interested in law & business and do not want to take a course at the law school. Very low lift so also a good option to add to an already packed schedule.

Yes, would definitely recommend the course - it provides a great understanding of important legal topics which are relevant to any corporate or start-up business role. The course is highly practical and provides a helpful framework of the various topics to consider where law and business intersect.

Yes - I would recommend this class to all MBAs who want to directly learn from an experienced and accomplished executive at a high profile company on a topic that all business students should at least be familiar with.

rows.title: Systems Thinking
rows.disagree: High rating, but comment tone is mixed or negative

comments: I really recommend this course!I think the homelessness subject was fascinating and made the whole course! It is a relatable, important topic, and it forces students to think about a real-life problem that we should all be cognizant of (if we are not already).

I would absolutely recommend this instructor (both Andrew and Sara) to a fellow student as well as this class. This class breaks down highly theoretical concepts to something more tangible and usable. This provided invaluable inputs to thinking about my positioning in the system and also what systems change might look like which I think every leader should be made aware of. If this was offered as a 10-week course I would definitely take it!
It is a good introduction class to understand the applied system thinking process
I would definitely recommend this course to anyone looking to learn a new process and way of framing problems that gets us out of linear thinking models.
Highly recommend this class. Once you start thinking in systems, you can't stop!
Yes! Its a great 1 unit class that gives a new way of thinking.
Yes! Pretty good course and introduction to a new field altogether!

Yes, this was a really important class I recommend every Haas student to take to think more critically and holistically about the systems that we all find ourselves in at work and personal and social lives
I would absolutely recommend both instructors and this course to a fellow student.
Its design thinking, but for systems. Read the books, if you like the book you'll like the class

This class is a great way to understand a problem differently. Usually, when attacking a problem, there is a period in which you download what you know. The systems map technique lets you understand how it fits together and influences output and outcome.
Yes I would!

Systems thinking is such a critical concept to explore, challenge yourself with, and understand. You will struggle in this course, but it's a good think to help you understand that problems aren't always easy, and every action has a reaction. I would, although I was expecting a slightly more rigorous coursework and depth of content.

Absolutely worth taking this class as the theory and practice ties into the world outside of business in our personal lives and definitely our day jobs. This class load is very manageable yet extremely impactful. Both Sara and Andrew are great teachers and guides in learning systems thinking and making it very easy to understand and apply.
Yes! If you are interested in understanding how systems work together.
I'd recommend to any one who is interested in how they can use systems thinking to solve problems.
Yes - systems thinking is such an important skill to have, although I wish the instructors took the technology angle as the main focus as opposed to the homelessness problem.
I would recommend to other students who need to apply a systems thinking approach in their daily professional activities

Good class. The sessions are very practical, the homework and readings really build the foundations for what you apply in class. It's a good balance of design and innovation and quite practical. It is also fairly easy, and you'll get out of the class what you put in to it. Put forth a good effort, and you'll learn. trust the process.
Yes a good course to add to your repertoire of tools to analyse situations. Dr Beckman is a heavy weight in the field of Systems Thinking
Absolutely, it has real world value and applicability.

Yes, this is an important way of thinking that is not taught in other classes at Haas (and other programs, too) Yes! Engaging, interactive class with tasks in teams. Professors are wonderful. Systems thinking has been super useful and applicable both professionally and personally.
Yes. I fall in love in this subject after my first class.

Absolutely! Both instructors did an excellent job of leading the class through practicing each concept we learned as well as highlighting where in our work we can benefit from a systems thinking approach.
Yes - I think this was a valuable class that tied together concepts from many classes. This might be an interesting concept to include in other strategy-esque core classes.
Yes! This course has helped me approach problems from a different angle and think through solutions holistically. I enjoyed interacting with the material in class, which made learning it easier.
Yes, especially for breaking down a high-level problem into smaller sub-parts

Yes, I would, with some modifications to the format to be more collaborative and interactive, instead of broken into small, self-organized feedback sessions. The systems way of thinking is really helpful and interesting, and I developed a fresh way to deal with old problems.

Yes, a useful way to think and an easy/generally enjoyable 1-credit class. As with most 1-credit classes, it could be about 25% shorter. Focuses primarily on thinking through social problems, so that should be at least interesting to you (although the tools are applicable to business as well, just not what the class focuses on).
YES! Great, engaging instructor who enjoys the course. Thank you for creating this amazing course. Really added a unique perspective to my worldview.

I highly recommend this course. The way professors present the concept with their own experience is unique and helpful. The tool itself is very useful to think in a different way about complex problems. I loved it!
yes
Yes, I can recommend this course to widen your perspective of creating and delivering changes
Yes

Would recommend this as a helpful 1-unit class. The examples used were not always directly tied to work examples, but are broad enough that you can extract insights accordingly to apply in your own life or work.

Yes. Great class that's really helpful in teaching you the tool to analyze any systems in a way that will holistic allow you to identify all possible root causes prior to getting to a conclusion of what changes are needed.
depends - i think it was an interesting perspective on how to think about and break down problems, but I don't feel inclined to use this methodology in real-life or work examples
Totally!

I'd definitely recommend this class to anyone who is interested in broad, complicated issues and how to begin attacking them. Andrew and Sara are fantastic professors and really care about helping you understand the systemic issues important to you.
yes! very interesting and fun course -- expanded my thinking on many important social issues

Yes - I thought this class was thought provoking enough to warrant 1 unit/two Sundays. There are interesting frameworks to use and I really enjoyed how they drew connections to other course takeaways and concepts (like bullwhip effect from operations).
Definitely. Loved that we got the option to pick our own system to analyze so this can help you outside of this class as well.
Yes!

I would recommend because it's helpful for overall strategy and approaching difficult problems. There is a fair amount of time dedicated to homelessness, but the instructors did a good job trying to apply it to business problems too. I enjoyed the course overall and would recommend.

I would recommend it for someone in nonprofit already working on navigating and improving a system. The entire second session focuses on the homeless crisis. Both sessions were mostly group discussion and I wish there had been more lecture time and examples of systems.
Yes! Great course and very helpful in thinking more expansively regarding different issues.
More time with groups with similar interests!

I would recommend this course. I think the content is very useful and is well taught. I think a lot of the content can be learned by reading the textbook, but the application to homelessness and our own systems problem was helpful. 10000%! This is an excellent class to think from a macro- systems perspective and is highly applicable and important across industries and functions. Particularly useful for those entering into social impact careers.

Unless you are interested in social impact or something related to non-profit issues, I don't recommend this class. The concept itself is helpful, and instructors are well prepared and paasionte, but not sure if I should spend 2 full days of the weekend.
yes!

Good course on system thinking - would've liked to hear more about the change management component and apply more to a business setting. Heavy emphasis on social problems and felt like 50% of the class was on homelessness rather than other types of system as a whole.

sections.goodFor: Product management-track students and anyone tackling complex, multi-stakeholder problems; workshop-style class with mapping tools and in-class application.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a low-key 1-unit class that ends when class ends; one student says it stays theoretical and just proves 'systems are complicated' without giving tools to solve them.

sections.redFlags: Workload heavy for 1 credit with a final assignment after sessions end (3 students); one says exercises are theoretical and give no problem-solving tools; several dislike the two-Sunday compressed format.

comments: Yes! They are great.
Yes; Helpful for any industry or problem solving role in a career. Organizing thinking is a skill and the frameworks presented will help me in future roles.
Yes. This is a very handy course

Yes I'd definitely recommend both Andrew and Sara! They were great facilitators and I loved how creative and different this class was - definitely not what I'd expect in a business school curriculum. I wish the class were a 7 week course not over 2 sundays, but overall I liked the class!

I would recommend this class-- The concepts are relevant and extremely applicable to all areas of work and industry. The instructors were well-prepared and thorough and it was highly worthwhile material. I would be prepared for a fair amount of work.

This class is a lot of work, perhaps too much for a one unit course! Be prepared to spend significant time on the assignments outside of class and after it's done for the final assignment. If you're looking for something lowkey that ends when the course ends, take something else.
Yes! Andrew is very genuine in his approach to teaching and methodical in his explanation

No - it doesn't equip us with tools to solve challenges. A lot of it was theoretical and the discussion could have short. It felt like we spent two days to boil down to something students intuitively understand - that systems are complicated and there are many factors. I don't think assignments / exercises supported learning and just drew out or repeated that fact

Yes! I thought this course was very valuable for understanding how to reform and improve systems and processes across sectors. If anything, I wish the class involved more frequent, shorter sessions so that we could fully grasp each concept, practice it and then layer on a new skill.

Yes - while this class is a good amount of work, it is applicable and relevant to a lot of problems in our lives. I hope to use my learnings and takeaways in new ways that push me to grow as an individual and leader

Wonderful course which allows you to implement systems thinking to real life problems. Love the structure of the course along with the classroom-workshop like approach. Perfect mix of lecture, group discussions and in person application of theory for a weekend class. 100% recommend.

No doubts! If you want to understand how to recognize and approach complex problems, this class is a must. Valuable tools and reflections to understand that not all the problems can be solved with a linear approach.

I would recommend this course. It is very interesting to break down issues and understand stakeholders, inputs, outputs, and relationships surrounding a problem. However, the Sunday format can be hard if you don't like working on Sundays.
This course is a super interesting way to analyze complex systems and learn new ways of mapping! The course load is a bit heavy for a 1 credit class so be sure to plan your schedule accordingly.
Yes. I recommend this course to anyone thinking of going into Product Management or interested in finding solutions to complex problems
I think I would recommend
Good course if you're looking for how to approach thinking about complex issues in a new way. Interesting applications and appropriate workload for a 1-unit course.

For any student who's looking to understand and solve complex problems, I think this can be a really useful class and I would recommend. I feel like this co-teaching tandem also brings the range of expertise needed for the class to function.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in policy, systems change or untangling complex 'thorny' problems who want applied, non-linear problem-structuring skills.
sections.notFor: Anyone weighing workload against credits - the load is widely seen as too high for 1 unit; one self-funded student calls the quality disappointing.

comments: Yes! While this class content is conceptually dense (like learning a new language) it provides a great structure to take complex, often thorny problems, to clarify them and ensure that fixes will actually work.
Yes! Course provided good insights
Systems Thinking is critical to address the polycrisis facing society.
yes. It challenges you to not think problems linearly.

Learnt a lot from this course - thought it was very applied which I appreciated. We spent a lot of time in class internalizing the material through exercises as opposed to just lecturing. A good amount of work for a 1 unit so keep that in mind. Overall was an effective valuable class and I came out of it with tangible skills - would recommend! No, the work load is too high for a 1 unit class. There was too much reading and too many assignments outside of class. Class time often felt wasted and the learning seemed to be pushed outside of class time instead of happening inside the classroom.
Reduce the workload before class, it was a big ask for busy students for a 1 unit class
No, as someone who is paying for this MBA with their own money, I felt disappointed in the quality of this course. Students who have sponsorship may feel more tolerant of a free 1 credit easy class.
Definitely. Solid Yes. Loved the course
I would recommend because of the topic. But would advise other classes for the workload versus credit
Yes. Definitely recommend! System thinking is essential knowledge and the instructors did an amazing job at teaching us!

Interesting topic and good facilitators. Too much work for a 1-credit course (hopefully they amend this for next year). Thankfully they incorporated AI into the assignments, but I assume most people didn't have time to meaningfully engage with most of the material.
I absolutely recommend this course, especially for students interested in policy making and system change!

rows.title: Strategy and Leadership for Social Impact

comments: If you are new to strategy and the nonprofit sector, and enjoy very academic / case-based discussions, I would say this class is for you. If you're hoping to develop specific skills to use in the near future, you may find this class too theoretical.
yes - they lead with genuine empathy for their students and are experts in the field of social impact. not too much of a heavy lift course, perfect amount of work for a 2 unit classs
Yes, definitely. Is a very good overview of the social sector with many examples and deep conversations

Yes, to those interested in entering the social sector (which includes pretty much anything that's not for-profit, *and* for-profits with a strong social mission). I thought this class was a very useful overview of the distinct challenges of the sector and covered a lot of material, from domestic to international and from education to financial independence to health and more. I even learned some useful things about the for-profit sector as contrasted with the social sector. And Ben and Colin are great people to know.

If you're interested in social impact, then yes. The class is heavy in cases and discussions so be prepared for that Yes, this is a great class. I like the casestudy format and the structured discussions. It was also an interesting class I was always looking forward to.

This is the perfect course for anyone interested in figuring out exactly where in the social sector they want to work or contribute. It's a general course that covers a wide range of topics. Ben and Colin bring in guest lecturers that are truly incredible social sector leaders, and do a great job of outlining key trends, tensions, challenges, and themes that arise in this sector. Ben and Colin are excellent professors that really care about the material and their students, and make sincere efforts to stay in touch with the class. Even if you're only interested in being a board member or volunteer, I'd still highly recommend this course.
Yes; both very thoughtful and kind. Deeply knowledgeable about the space; link theory to practice often

This is an excellent course to take if you are interested in social impact as a personal interest and/or career focus. We read several interesting cases and heard from a number of stakeholders at foundations/non profits - this was truly an eye opening course. Thank you Ben & Colin!

If you want to learn solid skills on how to be an effective social sector leader, this is the class. Take it! Would definitely recommend. Colin was a great instructor with a wealth of background knowledge. I found the class engaging every week and the discussions something to be looked forward to. Especially for those looking for an intro to social impact, this class was a great primer. Even for those who have somewhat of a social impact background, the cases and conversation with Colin really added a lot to my thoughts about the topics.
YES! Absolutely! A must class for students who are interested in learning about the public, private, and social sectors and how they intersect and differ.

Absolutely. 10/10. This class does an amazing job of outlining social sector leadership while also fortifying general leadership principles. Colin is an outstanding instructor and I would recommend any of his classes to anyone remotely interested!
Colin's an amazing instructor, brings super insightful case studies to the classroom, and designs assignments that require students to think critically and learn from.

I would absolutely recommend this course! Colin is a great professor with lots of experience in and knowledge of the social sector. He covers a wide range of relevant topics, picks good cases, and is full of dad jokes. One of my favorite professors at Haas. I definitely know that I'll be applying what I learned in this class as I look towards a career in social impact (though I think the learnings from this course are applicable to a wider ranger of careers). Yes! Colin is great – an overall good guy who cares a lot about social impact and equipping future leaders (us) to make a difference in our careers post–haas

Yes! Great professor who was BCG global health partner and has nonprofit board experience. Professor is very kind, open, welcoming, facilitates great discussions. Course is eye opening to the challenges of the nonprofit leardership world. You do need to read the weekly cases (that can be a bit long) to participate in class discussion, but the students are all passionate on the course topic and discuss well. Also have a few analytical papers to write.
Yes, totally! This class is helpful for whoever is interested in social impact. You do not need a lot of background.
Absolutely
Yes, Colin's class on social impact strategy is a refreshing break from the Haas core. Take it and learn a lot about the social sector.
Yes! fun class to go deeper into the non-profit world

Probably not. Colin is pretty pessimistic about the nonprofit sector and wasn't very inspiring and likes to point out and joke about what is wrong with nonprofits. I would have preferred to hear from leaders who believe. Students sit on their computers in class and don't participate. The class was under-enrolled and there are better places to learn strategy, impact and social impact and to be surrounded by students. Lectures are pretty long and guest lectures aren't the best in Haas. You can probably get all the learnings from Nonprofit Boards in half the time and half the work.

This is a great course for future nonprofit leaders and anyone interested in learning about the social impact sector. Colin is a dynamic and kind professor with an incredible amount of knowledge to share with students.
Yes, without a doubt
Yes - Colin is a great professor. I learned a lot!
Yes, I will
Yes - would recommend! Come ready to discuss and delve into the details. You should do the readings to get the most out of the class.

If you're interested in Social Impact, you have to take this course. Colin is a fantastic prof and you'll a ton from him. Practical assignments which help you go deeper into the nonprofit/social impact space. 10/10

Yes!!!!
I really loved this course.

Colin's teaching style is very effective - fast-paced but sharp with both depth, real-talk into pitfalls, an incentive / spark to think from different perspectives and clarifying vague/abstract paradoxes.

comments: Yes, helps deepen thinking about strategic concepts specific to technology firms. I would add however that this is a quintessential "you get out of it what you put in" class, meaning attending lectures alone contributes less of a percentage of the class's learning than it would for some other classes, if that makes sense.

This course is good if you are interested in a basic view into network effects and competitive advantages through application as opposed to theory. The content is interesting, although I would have preferred more stimulating and insightful conversations. It does have a strong focus on telcoms & chips, with a cursory touch on software. Yes I would. Jon is a great instructor, very well-prepared and knowledgable
Yes recommend.
Of course. No matter in which role/funcion, understand the strategy behind the marketing will help help to develop new ideas!
Yes - recommend the course fully.
If you work in any software or technology field and want to learn strategies to apply at work, then this class fits the bill. Jon's material is fresh and relevant.
Yes because he was engaged in his students
Yes, it was definitely a worhwhile class to take.
Yes! Prof Metzler is great--he cares about the content and cares about his students. The class is a good overview of different technologies, such as telco, chip manufacturing, etc.

Yes, I would. It was a fun course to attend and I think it helps to simply explore different businesses and models in the tech world. It is a step-up from the core strategy course and what I was expecting out of core strategy. I loved the cases and Jon brought a couple additive guest speakers. This is also a fun class to participate in and Jon encourages participation in a nice way (not assaulting cold calls).

Depends on what you're looking for. This is a good survey class about tech strategy in different verticals and industries within tech. If you had previous exposure - you might not learn as much. Jon cares a lot about the students and there is a lot you can learn from him regardless.

As the class was on zoom and at night, I'd recommend reading books about telecom/tech rather than take the class. There were a lot of readings/assignments and I'm not sure how much I retained. Aside from that, you get out what you put in, so if you're excited about debating Nokia's OS decision / downfall or gaming console strategies, this may be a great class for you.
Yes! This course is incredibly well thought out. I cannot over emphasize the care and thought that Jon has put into the construction of each lesson.

100% yes! Easily top 3 of Haas classes I've taken. Jon is the most prepared, thoughtful, and genuinely caring teacher I've had at Haas, and he takes great pride in this class. He also loves hearing about students'experiences, and gracefully weaves student perspectives into the course. If you're going into tech, at all interested in tech, or just want another strategy course, you have to take this class. Don't be dissuaded by some of the denser subject matter (such as the Telecom stuff) because it's actually really interesting and all inter-related, and essential to giving you a deeper understanding of the tech world and how it operates. Amazing class!

Much of what we covered is putting descriptions to issues we are already familiar with or learned through the core. Professor is friendly, helpful, and invested in his students--so if you are particularly excited about the space, he's a great person to get to know!

I would really recommend the course. Great applied strategy class focused on the tech and telecom industries. Yes! Jon is by far one of the best professors I've had. I wish he had taught core strategy for FTMBA.
I would absolutely recommend Jon/the course. If you are interested in tech/telco, this is a must-take class at Haas. yes
YES. Especially if you are new to tech or taking a tech job or loved core strategy take this class with Jon. Yes, its a 'low lyft' but fun class.
Yes - its a good class
yes
Yes
Yes, manageable workload, interesting cases, good discussion

Yes, this is a great course for students interested in the tech space and want to deep-dive on strategy in this industry. Yes. Interesting subject matter, really cool speakers. Jon really cares, and it shows.
I would - has foundational concepts in tech - i.e. all Haas students should know Anti-fragile, though it should focus more on application

If you are interested in dedicating time to exploring tech companies and tech topics, this is a great course. However, I don't think the strategic learning (e.g., theory, frameworks) was strong in this class.
Absolutely - Jon is one of my favorite professors at Haas. Brilliant, kind, empathic, humble, and caring - Jon exemplifies the defining principles & teaches a very interesting class.
Yes if interested in tech/strategy! Highly engaging content.

Jon is super knowledgable and well-connected in the industry. The guest speakers he brings in are great, and he is always open to help his students. Jon also orders food for the class when there is a guest speaker, and the "props" are much valued too.
Yes, but perhaps with a lighter semester load since the workload was on the higher side.
Yes. If you're interested in tech, it's a must take course for strategy.

Yes, recommend for those who could use tech strategy and enjoy reading about journeys of successful organizations. Jon is great with students, encourages participation in a way that students feel like speaking up. Great guest lectures. I enjoyed this course. There is an individual memo, group memo and a final paper and presentation. For 2 units, i think the presentation was overkill and didnt add much.
Yes

I hadn't actually planned to take this class originally but am very happy that I gave it a chance! The professor is very prepared and a welcome repreive personality-wise after some other "i know everything/my classroom-my rules" personality professors who can get kind of draining after a semester. Would definitely recommend as one of the better "strategy" courses at Haas!!

Yes. If you don't have any tech background and current are not involved in tech industry, this is a great class for you to enter this world and under each segment better. Cases are new and really relative to current market.
Yes, if you are interested in network effects, telecom, and technology, and how they are intertwined.
Yes
Yes. To develop understanding of current companies, events and strategies
No I would not, not enough new learnings.
Yes! this is a very useful class and and Jon is a caring professor who is invested into creating a great learning experience
If you are new to network topics, this is a good beginner class. It is a relatively low workload and easy to follow along. However, a bit slow paced, and similar to the strategy core class.
Yes
YES 100%!! The content is SO relevant and interesting! We touched on so many relevant/current aspects of

technology+. Very wholistic approach, both history and present. We somehow managed to get breadth and depth. Also really enjoyed the guest speakers, great diverse group. Also, Jon is an incredible professor -- knows his stuff, thoughtful, kind, challenges us, brings pizza, and has great guest speakers!

Yes, I absolutely recommend this class and Professor Metzler! He is incredibly smart and knowledgable about the space so I learned a ton over the course of the semester. If you are going into Big Tech or want to have a stronger understanding of how networks function, this is a great course to take. Professor Metzler also LOVES to teach and interact with students, so it's a fun and inclusive learning environment.

Yes if someone is interested in going into industries with networked economies. Helpful for those looking for careers in media, utilities, or SAAS in particular. Otherwise, it felt like a lot of rehashing of strategy core curriculum. This class is a must-take if you are somewhat related to the tech industry. Professor Meltzer is able to take current events in a thoughtful and analytical light while keeping a consistent through-line in learnings of modern tech strategy. Workload is just about right and thoughtfully considered.

I would recommend Jon and this course (S4NE) to any business student, especially those interested than strategy. This was the the only course I've found at Haas that really built on core strategy, and I think it was executed in a much more applicable and exciting way.
100% recommendation. It's a prefect class to know the trends in tech world.

Yes! Highly knowledgeable instructor helping us explore critical topics at the frontier of tech. Tons of interesting cases to review with a professor who is personally invested in all of his students.
Hell yes.
For sure recommended to better understand TMT. A great mix of teaching, discussions, presentations, cases and guest speakers.

The classic strategy answer- "it depends". This class is an extension of the core strategy class and covers topics that are relevant to specific industries and functions, with a heavy focus on tech. It started with hardware business topics that were less engaging for me. Where I benefitted the most was in applying frameworks for platform businesses and build/buy/partner decisions, and applying frameworks in the final strategy project.

This course provides a strong foundation in understanding network effects, platform strategy, and standards, which are highly relevant in today's digital and AI-driven economy. The frameworks are clear and widely applicable, and the case discussions (e.g., Spotify, Qualcomm) help translate theory into real-world strategic thinking.

Jon Metzler is an engaging and thoughtful instructor who encourages participation and creates a collaborative classroom environment. His teaching style emphasizes intuition and critical thinking, rather than rote memorization, which makes the learning experience both practical and intellectually stimulating.

That said, some of the course content can feel slightly dated. Students who are particularly interested in cutting-edge AI or the latest Big Tech developments may need to supplement with current events on their own.
Overall, I would highly recommend this course to students interested in technology strategy, platforms, or digital business models, especially those looking to build a strong conceptual foundation.
This is THE strategy class for our modern age. If you want to understand the business landscape of 2026 and beyond, take this class.
Strongly recommend — this is one of the most engaging and well-executed courses, and Jon Metzler is exceptional across teaching, facilitation, and course design.

He makes a technically complex and sometimes niche subject area accessible without diluting its rigor. Despite being fully online, the class is highly engaging, with thoughtful cold calls, structured discussions, and excellent guest speakers that elevate the learning experience. The course is especially great at helping you connect the dots across the evolution of networks — where we started, where we are today, and where things are going — so you leave with a clear, practical mental model rather than isolated concepts.

One of the most valuable aspects is how inclusive the environment is: whether you come in with deep industry experience or very limited exposure, you will be able to contribute and learn meaningfully. As someone without a technical background, I initially felt intimidated, but the course design and facilitation quickly made it approachable and rewarding.

Workload is very manageable (especially as an EMBA). High ROI given the quality of discussion and insight. Overall, S4NE with Jon Metzler is a standout course and a highlight of my Haas experience — I would recommend it to anyone, especially those looking to better understand how networks shape modern business and technology.

MBA236L is a great introductory and one of very few private equity course at Haas. If you are not from a finance background, this course will build you a foundational understanding of the industry and the different investment strategies that the players employ. The instructors are seasoned professionals in the industry and are very passionate about their work and teachings. The cases that we go over every week are very interesting, yet is not too heavy on the workload. Overall, a very well-rounded, informative class for novices in finance.

One thing to note is that, No, this course will not get you a job in private equity right out of school - many students seemed to be mistaking this. Unless you go to work for a mom-and-pop shop type of tiny fund that no one's ever heard of, the road to private equity is pretty well structured/laid out in today's world. You do investment banking for 2- 3 years and then lateral as a deal/finance role or you go work in consulting at MBB and lateral into an operational role. So do not come into this class expecting you could learn enough skills or list this class on your resume and find a job in private equity right out of school. With the right set of expectations, MBA236L is a very helpful and engaging learning experience.
