Absolutely, this is a must-take class in the MBA program. Even if you're not focused on finance or don't come from a financial background, you'll learn how to create value by sticking to core business fundamentals, thinking creatively, and being extremely disciplined in execution. The workload is heavy, but it's more than worth it for the quality of learning and practical insight you gain.

Highly recommended! This class will challenge and push you. Not only do you gain great knowledge about PE and LBO, but you become a more confident and well rounded business person. This is the type of MBA class I was looking for.

Yes, I would recommend both professors to fellow students. They have a rapid fire and sharp angle in engaging the class that it closes the gap that can be felt especially via a zoom class. Their insight into the industry is a goldmine that they both share with the class.

I would recommend this course if you are looking for a boot-camp style crash course on PE. This class and the professors will challenge you to defend your stance on every case. It's a lot of work but in the end you will have learned a lot about PE and potential career opportunities.
Yes, I would because it is very interactive and at least give me a taste of what is PE LBO.
Yes, more than theory of investment, the real life challenges associated with investment thesis are clearly taught. Goes to show that there are lot more than excel calculations when making a deal
Yes I would

Yes I would. This class was super valuable for anyone who is interested in Private Equity, or finance generally. Also, many of the learnings and takeaways are applicable to the corporate world and entrepreneurship. Great class! Yes I would. The workload is significant with a lot of reading, but both professors have a lot of experience to share. The strategy, insights and anecdotes form working on deals is invaluable. This narrative isn't available in online modeling classes or other finance mba classes. The subject matter is very specific but high value for anyone looking to work in the field.

I'd definitely recommend this course to anyone interested in PE or adjacent industries; the content and perspectives are fantastic. That said, people should be aware that the workload is heavier than you'd expect for a 2-unit class, and in my experience it was actually more work than some of the toughest 3-unit courses.
Yeees! Very valuable and no other class at haas similar

It's hard to give a simple recommendation. On one hand, the course prepares you extremely well and you truly learn a lot. But you have to be the type of student who doesn't mind spending a significant amount of time on cases — even when it might be more efficient to focus on the core concepts rather than spending twenty minutes or more on a single case while another still waits. There are definitely more efficient ways to teach the material, and given how much there is to absorb in an MBA program, it may make more sense to focus on the highest-value concepts and dive deep, rather than working through two cases when one of them doesn't add much.
I would recommend the course if you're aiming for IB or PE and have the time to dedicate to it. It's tougher for part- time MBA students who are balancing work, life, and other classes.

The professor himself is legendary. A major part of the appeal is simply the chance to learn from him. Just don't expect hands-on work with detailed models. I would suggest that he provide the underlying models and walk the class through them — that would create a real playbook for how to approach the analysis and allow us to experiment with the assumptions.

One more important point: the slides and materials he prepares for each class are fantastic. He clearly cares about what you learn, and the quality of the content reflects that. He consistently brings in great speakers as well. It will be a sad day when he retires.
I would definitely recommend this course to other students. You will be challenged and will grow more than you expect.

If you're not seriously considering a PE career, then my answer is no. It didn't really give me practical LBO modeling skills, and I felt that the learning I got didn't justify the amount of time and energy it required.

rows.title: Deep Tech Innovation & Entrepreneurship
rows.disagree: High rating, but comment tone is mixed or negative

sections.goodFor: Students exploring deep tech, consulting-style work with real startups, or how VCs think; cross-listed with MEng and Law, so the network expands a lot.
sections.notFor: Anyone needing a predictable workload - it is intense and volatile - or who cannot absorb the risk of a weak team or a poor startup assignment.
sections.workloadNote: Volatile and at times heavy load with real work outside class, on a live early-stage startup; includes pitch days with alums and industry experts. Thin evidence - only 5 comments.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; team work with a real early-stage startup plus pitch days are the described deliverables.
sections.redFlags: Two of five flag load and luck: a volatile, at times heavy workload, and an experience highly dependent on your team dynamics and assigned startup. Small sample, treat as directional.
sections.quote: Experience is highly dependent on your team dynamics and startup assignment
comments: yes. if you are looking for insight on what consulting is like, or what deep tech is, this is the class for you. its very intense and it does require you to work outside of the class. but it is rewarding -- this class is also with MEng and Law so your network expands like crazy. there are also pitch days where you meet alums and industry experts. so you meet a lot of people and learn a lot!

Excellent Entrepreneurship course in both Deep Tech and pure Tech. I learned a lot from Costumer Discovery, Interviews skills, Product-Market fit in Deep Tech, Go-To-Market strategies, Pricing Models, Competitive Strategy,..etc dealing with Early Stage REAL Startups.
Yes - Prof. Rappaport and the teaching cohort are great resources, and each lecture was valuable for anyone interested in starting their own business or getting a look into how VCs think and operate.

I would recommend this course to a student with the stipulation that they may expect a volatile and at times heavy workload. With this in mind, you will certainly learn many fascinating and useful skills about patent defense, market entry, and technical products.
Experience is highly dependent on your team dynamics and startup assignment

sections.goodFor: Students committed to deep tech commercialization who want a client project and real network access - the ~3 networking nights draw VCs, serial entrepreneurs and operators of unusually high quality.
sections.notFor: MBAs wanting consulting or entrepreneurship practice - one says other Haas experiential courses do it better. You carry teams of masters students with 0-2 years of experience, across an age gap.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (5 comments), contested: two say workload is 3x the unit count - interviews, weekly assignments, deliverables, several presentation rounds; one calls the class reasonably laidback.
sections.gradingBasis: weekly assignments, project deliverables, and mid-term, alumni-night and final demo-day presentations
sections.redFlags: 2 students: business students hard-carry teams of young masters students as pseudo-coaches, and workload far exceeds the unit count. Experience swings on client and teammate engagement and assigned industry.
sections.quote: The workload is much higher than you think, because the teams are usually Masters students who are fresh out of undergrad with <2 years of work experience
comments: Not if you're a business student, unless you are making a hard pivot and are seriously in need of a hands-on client project on your resume, and you're willing to put in the time and unpaid labour for it. It's a good project to talk about during interviews, but that can easily be achieved through other Haas Experiential Learning courses or an in-semester internship. The workload is much higher than you think, because the teams are usually Masters students who are fresh out of undergrad with <2 years of work experience (often 0 or 1 year), so it's much more work than you'd think to coordinate with them and work with them to get the material up to a standard that you're willing to present and put your name on. The projects are usually a business question at its core (market entry, commercialisation, pricing, etc) and most groups this year had max 1 business school student, so as a business student you'll be hard-carrying most of the analysis and being a pseudo-coach for the rest of your team trying to grapple with business content that they might be learning for the first time.

Also be aware that there is usually an age gap, so if you're above the median age for business school students, be prepared to have sufficient patience to work with other students in the 22 to 25 year old range.

One advantage of this course is that the networking nights are truly impressive. Lots of VCs, serial entrepreneurs, and folks from all backgrounds (e.g. ex-military, someone who used to work at a large insurer and now is a GTM specialist for healthtech startups). The quality of contacts here is higher than the average business school networking event, so it does have value if you're interested in continuing in the deep tech space. Networking nights happen ~3 times per term (mid-term presentation, alumni night, and final demo day, though along the way you sometimes get connected with one-time "mentors" that you can speak to about your project too).

The course is a great opportunity to leaarn about the path to commercializing frontier "deep tech" innovations (frontier technologies). Profs Rappaport and Bowman are great and have experience, especially on the patent and regulation side of things. The course is a great opportunity to connect with industry professionals and experts that may open up future opportunities. That said, be ready for an extremely heavy workload. The class easily takes 3x the time suggested by the unit count and requires managing interviews, project deliverables, weekly assignments, and several rounds of presentations. The experience is also heavily team-dependent and teams are formed based on interest and past experience (plus availability)

I think this course has a lot to offer. It gives you exposure and experience to working at an early stage startup. Prof Rappaport and the GSIs offer a reasonably laidback class, and I think any complaints of the course are probably centered on their teams or startups. I enjoyed the course and would recommend it whole heartedly.

From a business student perspective, if you are eager to support early stage startups in whatever challenge they might have, this class is for you. If you are interested in practicing consulting skills or entrepreneurship, there are probaly better options out there.

Startups come in various development stages and industries, so you should come prepared to work in industries you did not want/expect to work with and with founders with differing levels of engagement.

If you want to work on the commercialization of deep tech with real clients, this is a very good class. However, be prepared for a heavy workload. Also, as you might expect, the experience can vary significantly depending on the client and your teammates.

Yes, definitely recommend it. Feels like an extension of Leadership communication class. Sharif is a great instructor and you will learn a lot about your presentation techniques and a lot of personal things about your classmates I tend to be very hard in course reviews. This course is the best if you need to improve your communication skills. This was an incredibly valuable class, and I feel strongly that my Haas experience would not have been complete without it. This class doesn't just teach you how to tell more compelling, authentic stories but also encourages you to be more open and vulnerable, to reflect on the moments and relationships that have shaped your life, and to think holistically about your purpose and position in the world. I'm so thankful to Sharif for taking us on this journey and am excited to put these learnings into action in the rest of my time at Haas and in my post-Haas career.

Shariff is an extraordinary professor and coach. He'll get the best of you and your stories through his authentic feedback. In the few hours this course lasts, if you are open to improving and willing to stretch yourself, you'll become a completely different speaker and storyteller.
YES!!!! Do it!!!! You will not regret it

100% I would absolutely recommend Sharif. He knows his stuff, he's highly agile (tailors his coaching) and he brings such positive energy to the classroom. This is definitely one of the best classes I took at Haas and hands-down the best REMOTE class I've taken during the pandemic.
Yes. Take this course. You invest in analytics, finance, marketing, etc. in business school but this course will allow you to be the manager you want to be. This should be in the core!
Definitely recommend! Substantial learning that you can apply immediately! It also helped me to think in a new way about defining moments of my life, so I am grateful for this!

Definitely take this class- it is important to tell stories but more important to see the value in your classmates and learn from each of them while you have the chance. This class will grow you outside of your comfort zone and will remind you why Haas is so special!

Absolutely. I believe this course is a must for Haas students. We learn so much about theory; I believe it is equally important to learn how to present that information in a memorable way. This course provides an opportunity to learn how to do just that.

Yes! I went into this course not sure about it (and wanting to just take a "soft skills class"), but it has blown me away. One of my favorite classes at Haas so far! I think there are really tangible lessons that will be useful in any career. YES, totally worth it. He genuinely cares and you get to meet your classmates better.
Yes, this was one of the best leadership development courses at Haas. This is a must take course!!!!
This a too US-focused way of telling stories, just bear that in mind

I would 100% recommend this class. It is one of the best classes I have taken at Haas. I took this class virtually and although it would have been better in person, I feel like I was able to connect with my fellow classmates and learn so much about them. Sharif is a gifted storyteller and a great coach. I feel like I learned so much about storytelling and story creation through this course and these lessons will be so valuable throughout my career.
Fantastic class! Sharif and Arina are excellent coaches and you really level up your storytelling abilities. Also a great way to hear interesting stories and get to know your classmates better

This is an excellent course that I recommend to any Haasie. Storytelling is an invaluable skill and this class does an excellent job teaching it and coaching you through it. You will also get the benefit of hearing many amazing stories from your classmates in the process. Overall, definitely would recommend.
Yes - would recommend. Excellent chance to work on your story telling and get to know you classmates better. YES, one of my favorite classes at Haas. Also a great way to get to know classmates.
Yes! Storytelling is such an important leadership quality.
Definitely!
yes, highly recommend this class for anyone to explore who they are and who they want to me. it's a public speaking class and it's also a lot of introspection.
Yes, great course! You'll learn a lot and read "Lead with a Story" which is a great book!

Yes. Sharif's and Arina's energy and degree to which they cares about us is remarkable and inspiring. It made me really lean into the course and be vulnerable, which led to me gaining a lot from the course.

Highly recommend this course - Arina and Shariff go above and beyond to provide personalized storytelling feedback and care a lot about each students development. Despite the virutal nature, I learned a lot
Yes. If you are a beginner in story-telling and being vulnerable, this class will result in significant learning and self- awareness

I would not recommend this course unless a student feels they really need public speaking improvement. I felt that this course really was just a recap of LeadComm and not very differentiated or distinguished. We really just covered the same concepts and principles of good basic public speaking. I was hoping that this course would be more focused on actual business communication instead of personal stories and was a bit disappointed
Yes. Best class at Haas. Will make you grow as a person and as a leader.

Yes, great way to get to know your classmates, do personal reflection as you look to become a leader of an organization, and work on your delivery. The stories are very personal so it's hard to think about when you would actually tell them, but the skills and confidence you build through the class are worthwhile and can be applied to the workplace or your social life!
Would highly recommend this course to anyone interested in finding stories from their lives and working on public speaking!

I would recommend for a fellow student more as know yourself perspective than anything else. It helped me dig in myself and remember what I believe in. Hence, to inspire others in the process. It is a must for business school, when sometimes you forget about yourself.
Yes, because storytelling is extremely important in today's world!
Yes. This is one of the best classes I have taken at Haas!

Absolutely recommend, a must-take class! It's a great opportunity to craft and hone your storytelling skills. The course did a great job stretching my comfort zone and I was able to try new things and learn a totally new style of storytelling that has improved how engaging my stories can be. Sharif was amazing at recognizing value and strengths, then coaching improvement areas, while encouraging me to stretch myself to grow as a storyteller.
I think any public speaking is good - so would recommend this as further practice
Yes, but take the semester long course
No - did not think the online nature of the class was helpful. Nor the stories we practice were transferable to my professional life. Its was like leadcomm with less time to implement the learnings.

Not sure. This is a great course if you want some help with public speaking and specifically how to deliver a story in a compelling way. It is less interesting if you want to learn more about the structure and the building of a good story. Yes, I would recommend but would not expect it to change your world in terms of being able to give good speeches, but mainly take some nuggets to remember as you go forward in your career and practicing is always good.
This class seems like a continuation of Leadership Communication. If a student wants more of that, I would say yes. Otherwise, no.
Yes if you want to improve your storytelling capability not your presentation skills
Yes
Yes. Super applicable skills.
YES. learn how to captivate an audience.

I've taken a lot of the soft-skill / speaking / human connection courses at Haas, and this one really shines and stands out. Sharif is such a gentle person and I feel like the class was perhaps worth it just to spend the time with him. He is amazing at giving direct, honest feedback about how to become better storytellers and public speakers and caters things to each individual person and meets them where they are. He doesn't make people feel uncomfortable but helps push people outside their comfort zones. 100% recommend if you want to work on your storytelling abilities, this class is really one where "you get out what you put in" and how much you challenge yourself.

This course will make you uncomfortable if you aren't already an incredible public speaker, but that's the point and at no point was the discomfort such that I felt unsafe. This course is a beautiful blend of tactical advice, bite-sized iterations, and learning from seeing how others approach story-telling. Sharif did a great job of creating a safe space for us to learn and grow. If you want to take the next level up of Lead Comm, this is a great class to get that. The class teaches a vivid, theatric method to deliver stories. It is efficient in teaching verbal varieties, gestures, etc. Take it if this appeals to you.
Yes, absolutely! This was such a valuable class that went much deeper into the mechanics of storytelling than did LeadComm.
No. I dont think it was really applicable to the types of presentations i will have to take in the future

I would recommend Storytelling with Arina and Sharif (the non-weekend sessions). I recommend for people who would like a stage to practice storytelling. This stage was very important to my growth and I appreciate that a lot. If that's valuable to you, you should take this class.

Highly recommend this class, it will take you to another level in your storytelling. I appreciate how targeting this kind of storytelling is and relatable it is to the business world. Sharif and Arina make an incredible pair. One of my favorite classes at Haas.
Yes - very helpful class

Yes I would recommend that others take this course. For me, it was one of those courses that made me uncomfortable. I didn't look forward to class and agonized over having to deliver my next speech. But that's what I needed, and I really believe that I was able to make lasting improvements in the short timeframe of this course. It's worth all of the discomfort.
Definitely recommend this class, especially if you like the LeadCom.

I would not recommend this course and instructor. I'm not completely sure why this course bids out so often. The course is very similar to Leadership Communications. The professors seem to take the course a bit too seriously. The weekly reflections felt a lot like busy work. Lastly, it wasn't clear when we would use these stories and apply them in the business world.

I would recommend this course and the instructors to someone who is seeking more practice in either public speaking or structuring their speeches. This class helped not only gain constructive feedback regarding presence during speeches but also informational tools to structure a speech and utilize the audience for engagement.
This class will encourage you to stretch. Take it if you are really committed to improving your performance as a storyteller.

This is a must take soft skills class. It's what Leading Communications should've been. You learn valuable and practical speech skills from this storytelling class. I was taking this class while doing interviews, and I saw immediate difference when I applied skills to day-to-day interactions.

A highly engaging class that will provide a safe space for you to improve your storytelling. I would recommend to anyone who wants to improve their speaking ability. Feedback and exercises are tailored to you and your areas of improvement. You will also learn more about your classmates and connect with them through stories.
Yes, you will take away valuable skills as a public speaker/storyteller. Not many other classes will offer something like this

Yes, but know that in this course you will spend a lot of time providing feedback for others. There is nothing wrong with this, but if you really want to grow in your presentation/storytelling abilities, you will need to keep working on them in your own time.
I would definitely recommend this instructor. He was great. I felt like he genuinely wanted to work with us and help us improve. He pushed us to stretch ourselves outside of our comfort zones.
I would, this has been a top ten class during my time at Haas.
I would not take this if it were a remote class; good in person classs.

Yes, would highly recommend this class taught by Sharif. He was very organized and effectively pushed students to improve. The videos, readings, and workload was also enjoyable. I would have liked this course to be 2 credits versus 1 if possible to allow for more time to deliver more speeches and improve over time. Overall, highly recommend. yes i would this was a great experential laerning exercise, even if it was on zoom. i imagine it could be even more powerful irl!
Yes. Sharif is fantastic. I would actively seek to take other courses he is teaching.

sections.goodFor: Students who want to level up public speaking and storytelling beyond LeadComm and are willing to be vulnerable and stretch outside their comfort zone; Sharif's personalized, direct coaching is the standout, and many also valued getting to know classmates through their stories.
sections.notFor: Those who felt LeadComm covered enough, or who want business-presentation content rather than personal storytelling; a recurring minority found it a repeat of LeadComm with stories that don't transfer to professional settings, and some said it loses a lot over Zoom.
sections.workloadNote: Weekly speeches and reflections are manageable, but sessions are emotionally demanding and require being fully engaged for three hours at a time.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (6+ comments): substantial overlap with Leadership Communications; a handful (3-4) found the personal stories not transferable to business use, and a few said the remote format undercut the class.
sections.quote: This is a must take soft skills class. It's what Leading Communications should've been.
comments: Yes, this was a really fun class and unique from any class I've taken at Haas except for Lead Comms. I'm not 100% sure how much I'll apply what I learned, but it was a rewarding class.

Yes, I would recommend this course. If you want to improve public speaking skills, this is the right class to do it. And since the class size was small, the coaching felt personalized. It is similar to Leadership Communication class. Yes! This class made me so much more confident with public speaking in the short amount of time that we have. It's similar to lead comm in terms of tasks (weekly speeches and reflections), but I felt I was able to take away a lot more practical knowledge of how to be a better storyteller and communicator.

This just an extension of Lead Comms. Take it if you enjoyed that and want an opportunity to practice storytelling for a purpose more. Definitely not a bad way to acquire a credit. Just know that you'll need to be mentally and emotionally present for 3hrs at a time.

This course definitely teaches you a lot about the nuances of storytelling. However, this is a very emotionally draining course; be expected to be physically exhausted at the end of course sessions due to being engaged 100% of the time.

rows.title: International Business Development for MBAs, IP course

comments: The instructors played a very limited role in the overall experience, but Judy and Whitney were overall great people to meet. I would not recommend the course to fellow students - there are a lot of uncertainties that are left up to chance: location, company, and team. Unfortunately I think there are better uses of your time to work on things with people who are aligned on goals and learnings other than IBD

Whitney is awesome, and I highly recommend learning from her in any capacity available. IBD as a course is hit or miss. There are many variables that are left to chance, and sometimes it works out and other times it falls flat. Students should be very aware of what they are giving up: potentially learning a hard skill, missing Haas Boats (bigger FOMO than anticipated) and sometimes you don't grow as much as you would think. Nonetheless, it's a unique opportunity and one you won't get in any other class
Yes
100% best course so far.
Definitely. She has a ton of experience and is very passionate about what she does and why is it important for students to learn the skills taught
Yes. Please do the course and thank me after. Very insightful project
Yes, I'd obviously recommend.
I would recommend the instructor.
I would not recommend this course due to it being a miss in terms of in-country experience.

I would - but it's a toss up. You may get lucky with your team and client, you may not. If you don't have a consultant on your team, the work becomes infinitely harder. I am glad I took the class but I can tell my peer group is about 50/50 on whether they regret it or not.
I'd definitely recommend IBD as your applied innovation class. The course is challenging but rewarding and will give you the opportunity to gain some hands on experiential learning.
Absolutely, I already have recommended many of the first years
Absolutely. I got more out of it than I will probably get out of any other project at Haas. It was fun and practical experience.

sections.goodFor: Students exploring or entering hedge funds and investing; works for novices and for those with intensive investing backgrounds alike; useful for company-evaluation skills.
sections.notFor: Students who want to improve personal trading skills, or who need options/foundational trading grounding first - one says the course lacks a bridge from the Asset Management course.
sections.workloadNote: 3-credit course with near-weekly group presentations and trade-idea prep, plus meaningful out-of-class group meeting time; one student calls it 'not a super heavy lift', another 'a lot of work'.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly group presentations and trade/stock pitches; guest lectures. Grade weights not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Bloomberg terminal access badly limited (1, emphatic). One calls the format amateurish: inefficient bCourses use, pointless Bloomberg training, lectures not recorded, presentation feedback never implemented.
sections.quote: There are presentations every week for the most part but its not a super heavy lift.
comments: Yes, this class is interesting if you want to enter or explore the hedge fund world. The industry speakers were really interesting to learn from and hear how different firms are approaching their investment strategies. There are presentations every week for the most part but its not a super heavy lift.
Yes, the line up of great speakers and trade ideas from other students were fantastic
Yes.
Yes, if the student wants to make their own hedge fund or join a fund. I would not recommend to a student who wants to improve their trading skills.

I would recommend this course but understand that it's a 3-credit course that requires significant time outside of the classroom, meeting with groups and preparing presentations every week. Professors were great!
Yes, if you wanna know more about Hedge Funds, it's a fantastic class. Both profs, are very welcoming and very well connected.
100%. One of the best classes at Berkeley, knowledgeable instructors from both sides of the investment universe (allocator vs investor), easily reached outside of course, clear takeaways/work product
Yes I would. This class is helpful and can let students get first hand information from some hedge fund managers and learn from their cases. That's super cool to get to know some high level managers

Absolutely. If you don't know anything about hedge fund strategies, this is precisely the course for you. Joel and David are awesome instructors who truly want to help students learn about the industry and what hedge fund PMs do on a daily basis.
highly recommend
Yes

Wish there were a more foundational course/ a few classes to bridge this class with the Asset Management course taught by Sam. It would be incredibly helpful to have introductory lectures from Joel and David focused on trading options before diving into more complex topics later in the term. This would also better support students without a hedge fund background in getting more out of the guest lectures and advanced material.

The course is a great way to learn about hedge funds. It's perfect for both those who have no experience or knowledge of the topic, as well as students would have intensive investing backgrounds. The course is tailored in a way that students of all varying backgrounds would get value.
Highly recommend every student to take this course. A lot of work but very worthwhile I think I've significantly improved my ability to evaluate companies and understand hedge funds much better

I really like this class but there are some challenges. The Bloomberg terminal access is a huge problem. I dont know why Berkeley can't just pay for the mobile anywhere access or get more terminals. My undergrad was 1/10th the size and we had 5x many more terminals available. I also think that the knowledge in this class is so deep that it can't fit in one course so I challenge the instructors to think about how to make the course lifelong whether it be by creating public websites, a new textbook, or even some alumni group where future information will be shared.
Yes - I would highly recommend it as it's one of the most interesting and practical class I've taken at Haas yes

I would recommend the course; it's interesting and practical, and gives a good overview of what most hedge funds do. However, its format needs improvement; it felt somewhat amateurish. Inefficient use of bCourses, a pointless Bloomberg training, detailed feedback on presentations that are never implemented, lectures aren't recorded, and other details that, while not crucial, frustrate a student who pays thousands of dollars for top-quality education. If you can overlook these factors, you'll enjoy a course that teaches you all the basics you need to know about hedge funds. Great guest speakers too, probably the highlight of the course.

Yes, if somebody would like to get more knowledge and technical pitch development this lass definently worth it. I highly recommend if you are in finance industry and would like to build professional career in this industry this course you can take.
Yes

sections.goodFor: Students who want to go deep on public markets/investing, learn Bloomberg, and meet practitioners; one of the few deep-finance offerings at Haas.
sections.notFor: Students with only cursory finance interest or no background - one says without more numerical exercises the learning stays high-level and hard to grasp.
sections.workloadNote: Near-weekly team stock/strategy pitches plus a final project designing your own hedge fund strategy; several call it lighter than it looks because work splits across the team.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly student pitch presentations and a final hedge fund strategy project; guest speaker sessions.
sections.redFlags: One student says the course is too high-level and lacks practical numerical exercises to understand strategy mechanics; another warns you cannot wing the weekly presentations.
sections.quote: for those without that background, the course can be challenging to fully grasp. Without more practical, numerical exercises... the learning is more high-level than hands-on.
comments: I would recommend. Very worthwhile.
Yes, by far if you are self-driven and have an engaged team. The course is as good as you and your team make it. I think that having a sub-par team could make this course far worse.

I strongly recommend that any student at Haas interested in finance and seeking to better understand financial risk, upside, and how to express it take this class. The weekly student pitches and guest speakers are a great modality to learn these things in an academically vulnerable yet rigorous environment.

Yes I would if they were interested in going deep on finance and investing. If they only had a cursory interest I may not, but I think that is a good thing because I think this is one of the fewer offerings for people who are looking at going deep on a finance topic

ABSOLUTELY - but also be aware of the work involved! Weekly presentations that you actually need to thoroughly understand!! Cannot just wing this class - but that is also what helped me learn a lot!! I also loved Joel and David. Funny, engaging professors and trying to really help you learn and grow. Helpful to learn how to use bloomberg as well. Overall, great class!
Yes, this class was great. I think anyone even remotely curious about finance should take this class.

Yes, I would recommend this course for students who have prior exposure to or a strong interest in the hedge fund space. It offers a broad view of the industry and the guest speakers from different funds are excellent. However, for those without that background, the course can be challenging to fully grasp. Without more practical, numerical exercises, it's difficult to develop a deep understanding of the rationale and mechanics behind certain investment strategies. As it stands, the learning is more high-level than hands-on.

If you are interested in hedge funds or wealth management, this is an incredibly immersive class that dives deep into different hedge fund strategies and connects these strategies to actual practitioners in the field. I felt that the guest speakers who were brought into the class were more impressive than the respective speakers in other classes. I highly recommend this course, especially for anyone that doesn't know anything about hedge funds. Great mix of general introduction, solid guest speakers, and a final project that makes you create a hedge fund strategy of your own.

It's a great group of people that have really similar interests but media is so wide that we all come in with different areas of expertise. Roy somehow knows about nearly all of these areas and also brings wonderful guests to help supplement our discussion. Truly highly recommend!
Yes, highly recommend if interested in media & entertainment
Absolutely. Everything in this course was relevant and there was no wasted time. The interactions with other students is well managed asynchronously, and it is thoughtful and valuable.

I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to understand the breadth of the media industry and hear from media entrepreneurs from a broad array of media genres. This is not a heavy lift class to any extent and very much can be described as "you get out of it what you put into it." Roy's a solid professor and certainly someone I would want to know post-Haas. But he also makes it clear from the beginning that the value of the class will come from the class interviews with folks in media, the readings, and your media project analyzing the decision of a leader in the media industry.
Yes.

Yes! This is the perfect 1-unit class for anyone who is interested in media and the day-to-day developments within it. It was comprehensive, thought-provoking, discussion-based, and fun to learn about. Above all that though, Roy is the best. He personally took time out of his day to advise me on career/industry experience when I was having a tough time navigating the internship offer acceptance process and torn between two paths and how to navigate them in a way that wouldn't hurt my chances at either company. He gave me such calm, collected, useful, and positive advice. I see him as a mentor and know I can count on him for future guidance.
100% - Roy is fantastic and cares about his students. He is deeply knowledgeable about the space and is well connected in the industry. Class is very fun!
Yes, this is a great class for people who are interested and wants to learn about media industry.

Yes absolutely, Roy is the bomb. Minimal workload and tons of learning from a true practitioner who seems to know everything about the media landscape. Also super current on cutting edge industry developments. As someone less knowledgeable about Media, I learned a ton and still felt engaged in the class discussions, though it can feel a bit niche at times since other classmates have very strong passions for media and may take the discussion in various directions.
Yes - interesting class based on current conditions - always exciting things to talk about in class.

If you love media, you'll love this class! Not too many course options to talk about the business of and its implications at Haas, so this is super valuable even if you're not angling for a role in the business after graduation. Yes! Excellent class to understand the media industry and his real world experience has shaped how I see all of media and how I might pursue a career in media later.
Maybe, if you're looking for an easy class. Or if you're really interested in new media and closely follow the industry on your own. Otherwise you won't get a lot out of the lectures
Yes - this has been one of my favorite classes at Berkeley so far. The course is dynamic and engaging and the professor is knowledgeable and kind.

I was happy to spend time attending this class. Roy and fellow students always leave you with something to look into further. If you're not into media/entertainment then you may not enjoy these 2 hours, but if you are its worth it. Also the project one of the few times that I enjoyed fulfilling an academic requirement. It was less "work" and more "personal exploration"
I would ABSOLUTELY recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. I have learned SO MUCH in this class about the media industry. I am very happy I was able to take this course.

Yes, this is the kind of survey class that I think all MBAs should take because it's information that is valuable no matter what your career aspirations are. Media touches us every day, so we should all be aware of how it works, how it's changing, and how we can best participate.

Yes! Great class, great professor, and you can put in as much work as you would like. Don't expect it to be a "how to make it in the entertainment industry" course and you'll be happy. If you're interested in media as a career or as a consumer, you'll enjoy this.
Yes! Gives a solid understanding of the media industry.

Absolutely would recommend this course. It's a very low lift, work-wise, but the return on effort is high. Roy brings in incredible speakers, leads compelling discussions, and offers unique real-world insights into the media business based on the experiences of his career. There's no reason not to take this class.
Absolutely! Any student interested in pursuing a career in media must take this class.
Yes
Yes
Absolutely - even though the class is light on content, I learned a lot and constantly apply the'scarcity'framework to other industries

Yes, I would recommend it overall, since it's the only real media class at Haas. That said, students should go into this class knowing it is, at best, a very very perfunctory survey of the media landscape, and will be of limited use in preparing for a career in media.
Yes to those interested in the media industry, both professionally or casually!

If you are interested in all aspects of media then Roy is a great resource and I would highly recommend taking the class. You can focus on what you want and don't have to put much energy into topics you don't want to.
Yes, would recommend

Roy is an exceptional instructor who really cares about the students. He brought in true industry giants from many disciplines within the media industry and the learnings were tremendous. Great class with low effort. Would definitely recommend.
Definitely! If you have any curiosity around Media, the class is extremely valuable and thought provoking.

Yes! Roy is great at fostering discussions and has an up-to-date vision of the media industry, which I really appreciated. Really low lift chill class for introduction to media. Great guest speakers that opened my eyes.

Absolutely. If anything about the media world is interesting to you this is a must take. Roy takes us on a journey to understand the different players in the industry and the structure and then brings that to life with an amazing selection of guest speakers. As a bonus, Roy is deeply caring and he's just a great man to have in your corner.

It's a good survey class and interesting if you're curious about media, but not a deep dive, so you get as much as you put into it (ask Roy questions and definitely chat offline to get more out of the class)
Absoutely!!! STRONG STRONG recommend for anyone thinking of getting into a media space or anything adjacent to it!

1. If you are interested in a career in the Media industry, you should definitely take this class. Not only does this tell you a lot about the different industries, Roy helps you view them in multiple perspectives, which was a new experience for me (also helpful for interviews)
2. If you are just interested in Media industry, it is also fun

3. To be honest, this is a very low-lift 1 unit class. If you are looking for a fun 1 unit class before graduation, this is it If you have even a fleeting interest in media, you need to take this course. The entire course is class discussion, covering multiple segments of the media industry.
Highly recommend this course, especially if you need an intro into Impact investing. Justina & Rebekkah were amazing. You will need to follow-up with another course if you want to get more in-depth.
yes

It is clear that both Rebekah and Justina know ALOT about the subject. That said, there were challenges and gaps in course delivery as well as information shared. This might improve over time or it might not.

Yes! This is a great learning experience especially for those who might be remotely interested in the Impact Investing space. The instructors bring a lot of positive and genuine energy to class. Yes. Overall this class gives a good overview of this impact investing landscape and facilitates networking opportunities with industry leaders who come as guest speakers. Yes. Easy one-unit class that introduces the student to the space with minimal out of class work.
Yes - especially if you're interested in the climate space.

This class is a really informative introduction to the career paths, challenges, and continued work to do in impact investing. The group project was a great opportunity to connect with others interested in similar topics and delve into some problem solving.

I absolutely recommend this course to all Haas students. I think it's definitely worth seeing (without the high time commitment of a heavier unit course) if Impact Investing is something that he or she could be interested in. It's something I didn't think I would be coming into Haas but realized during my journey it is very much something I want to be a part of my future career.

I would absolutely recommend this course if you have any interest whatsoever in impact investing, or if social and environmental impact are generally important to you. yes. this class is a great introduction to the space. extremely worthwhile

Absolutely. This is one of the more productive weekend classes. Targeted material and very relevant to industry trends I would have loved to incorporate the recommendations provided during our presentation into our paper. Other than that, everything else was fantastic!
Yes, good course to begin learning about sustainable and impact investing, as well as to get a baseline level of knowledge even if you're going into a slightly adjacent field.

Even though it's a Sunday class, there are plenty of breaks, and I appreciated the opportunities to connect with students from all over!

I would recommend this course! I was able to do a deep dive into an impact topic I cared about and got to learn about the space. Yes I would recommend it for a fellow student who wants to gain knowledge about sustainable investment

I would recommend this class to a fellow student, but I would appreciate if there was less verbiage on slides. Would absolutely recommend this course to anyone in the impact sector -- wonderful speakers, Justina and Rebekah are incredibly generous with their time, and so much to learn!
Yes, I would recommend this as a crash course to get familiar with the impact investing landscape and to make connections with industry professionals.

I would recommend this course as an intro to impact investing and even just financing companies in general. I would recommend students completely new to this space try to get a base understanding of the space before stepping into the first class. Yes, if you want an introduction to the Impact space - this is a great course to take
I'd recommend the course if you are interested in new perspectives in the investing /asset management industry - the group project was highly unstructured and that created challenges for many groups

yes. course was a great introduction to impact investing. I thought the class used the time effectively and efficiently over 2 Sundays. Guest speakers were very knowledgeable and group project was pragmatically doable
Yes
Not someone with my background. Someone who wants to focus on investing, yes.
The nine to 5 straight was butal

Yes, absolutely. The instructors are very knowledgeable and bring deep, real-world experience to the class. 100% recommend. Super helpful professors who are eager to discuss career as much as class content. Can't

Yes, I learned a lot about impact investing, challenges, and the diversity within it. It was very useful information packed into just 1 credit.

Maybe, the lecture format was slightly disengaging, more structure and concrete subject coverage would have helped me come along better in lectures (I.e. Identify key subjects ahead of driving into them)
Great opportunity to get to know about impact investing market who want to explore this market

Yes, I'd recommend this course and both instructors for anyone interested in social impact investing. Instructors really know their stuff and have great networks that allows them to bring knowledgeable speakers. They also are

I definitely would recommend this course and instructor to fellow students. It's a great way to understand how financial action in certain areas can tangibly create impact.

Yes, for someone that doesn't have any experience with impact investment or a similar field, this class is a great introduction. The guest speakers are all very interesting and super insightful too.

Yes! This was a great, low-lift course to build a solid foundational understanding of what impact investing is, the different vehicles for impact investing, and important players in the space. Yes I would, I believe these professors are grounded in the field and the class reflects this, particularly the way they integrate the specialists and speakers.
Yes highly recommend. Great well rounded course
yes
Absolutely - I wish I could take it again or wish it was even longer.

Yes, I would recommend both this course and instructor to a fellow student. The speakers that were brought in were great. Yes. It is a good overview for someone with an interest but little to no experience in the impact investing space as long as they manage their expectations and know that we can't go too deep into the subject matter over two Sundays. yes!
absolutely - an excellent primer to introduce students to the world of sustainable finance

Yes but you have to understand this class is about investing landscape not in terms of startups / companies out there in the space, but different investment vehicles that are affecting change via catalyzing flow of investment dollars into impact areas.
Absolutely

Yes

Yes!!!! This class was very instructive systems thinking is a great tool very useful for problem solving and consulting! I would absolutely recommend this course and instructor. It was interactive and engaging and gave me practical tools that I can take forward into my post-Haas career.

Yes! The class was extremely interesting and could be relevant to anyone.
Absolutely worthwhile, you learn really new and interesting ways to think about difficult problems

This class gave us tools to dive deep into the systems behind complex topics (like the Facebook Files and homelessness in the Bay), and it taught me a new way of thinking that I hadn't experienced before. Sara and Andrew are also a perfect pair to teach this class; both of them were very knowledgeable and brought their extensive experiences to the table.

I really recommend this course!I think the homelessness subject was fascinating and made the whole course! It is a relatable, important topic, and it forces students to think about a real-life problem that we should all be cognizant of (if we are not already).

I would absolutely recommend this instructor (both Andrew and Sara) to a fellow student as well as this class. Yes! Pretty good course and introduction to a new field altogether!

Yes, this was a really important class I recommend every Haas student to take to think more critically and holistically about the systems that we all find ourselves in at work and personal and social lives
I would absolutely recommend both instructors and this course to a fellow student.
Its design thinking, but for systems. Read the books, if you like the book you'll like the class

Yes I would!

Absolutely worth taking this class as the theory and practice ties into the world outside of business in our personal lives and definitely our day jobs. Yes! If you are interested in understanding how systems work together.

Yes a good course to add to your repertoire of tools to analyse situations. Dr Beckman is a heavy weight in the field of Systems Thinking

Yes, this is an important way of thinking that is not taught in other classes at Haas (and other programs, too) Yes! Engaging, interactive class with tasks in teams. Professors are wonderful. Systems thinking has been super useful and applicable both professionally and personally.

YES! Great, engaging instructor who enjoys the course. Thank you for creating this amazing course. Really added a unique perspective to my worldview.

Yes!

yes!

Professor Pearce is a former C-level executive and it shows. He has a deep expertise of the material, and the way he answers questions is both inspiring and full of learning.
Bill's amazing. Bill will teach you the things you won't learn anywhere else. And theyre all such useful stuff for work - please, just take the course

This class is fantastic! Bill used great examples, there are great learnings, and it is all really applicable to the future wherever your journey takes you next. Essentially, it's a comprehensive deep dive into core career learnings to prepare us for the future

Yes, if you're really interested in learning about innovation and pursuing a career. Bill is awesome! The three credit nature of this class becomes very repetitive if you don't want to go into innovation.
Yes - particularly if interested in corporate innovation in tech and CPG. I thought there would be a little more diversity in topics, but understand the limitations.

This was one of the most useful classes at Haas, especially if you work for a large company. Bill is an engaging lecturer who has a clear structure / scaffold for course concepts, and peppers his lectures with real-life scenarios. I appreciated the mixture of assignments throughout the semester, which gave me an opportunity to test my understanding at various points, and clarify concepts before the final project. I have a much better "toolkit" with which to approach my work, and in deciding which ideas to champion.
Yes, great way to think about innovation, especially if you interact with an innovation cell at a company.
Yes!
I would recommend the professor but this course doesn't feel worth the money. I wish it were a 2unit class with less content.
Bill knows his stuff. Take this course instead of power and politics. It's soft skills, but fun.

sections.quote: Highly recommend it, mostly because of Bill. He is a legend at Haas, a professor that's been in the trenches.
comments: Highly recommend it, mostly because of Bill. He is a legend at Haas, a professor that's been in the trenches. Yes, I highly recommend this class! Bill is my favorite professor at Haas and has great stories, teachings, examples, and content. Really valuable class with practical application and great takeaways.

Very much so. And honestly, I'd recommend it for students interested in people, HR, operations, or general leadership. I think it doubles not only as a marketing and product class but also as a class on how organization design can empower or inhibit innovation
Yes, because Bill always has good insights.
Without a doubt. For anyone taking the non startup route, this is a must take course at Haas.

This is a must-take course. Professor is extremely experienced and well positioned to teach this course. He has navigated so many scenarios that are covered in this class. If you are interested in climbing the ladder in corporate, this is important to ensure you join the right company.

Yes, highly recommend this class. Bill is one of the best professor's I had at Haas. He has a lovely personality, knows the material like the back of his hand, has rich industry experience and loves helping students. The course is up to date with what's going on in the world and Bill is always happy and available to help students in and outside the classroom. Highly recommend Bill and his corporate launchpad class.
Yes, I would recomend. The content is relevant for every organization and made me reflect on how corporations fail or succeed in today's innovative world.

This is a great course! It teaches you a lot of things from working with startups to market discovery as well as exposes you to a lot of ideas in the climate tech space. Definitely one of the heavier lifts in terms of workload but was rewarding!

I would recommend this course to students if they want to understand the reality of startup market research. The course is quite scrappy and the research and conclusions are never developed in absolute confidence, but one of my key learning from the course is that it really is like that outside of the course too. Teams learn and grow and never stop learning and growing.

I'm not a Haas student, but I recommend C2M if you're interested in the cleantech space and have at least 5 hours/week to spend on this class for 15 weeks. You get how much you invest in the class. It was particularly rewarding to work with PhDs and grad students pursuing other fields of study, and a nice intro to network with folks in the space. Would absolutely recommend this course if you're interested in climate tech or deep tech / hard tech start-ups in general. The course was especially helpful for non-Haas students, as it included lots of business frameworks, practice building slides and presentations, working with clients, etc.

I would recommend this course to a fellow student if they are looking for a broad overview into connecting research/technology with business development. While the course content itself is not challenging, the workload and time commitment does become extensive especially as you approach the end of the semester. You will be able to learn a lot of new business concepts and understand what can make or break a technology, which as a someone from a research background don't necessarily get exposure to normally. The class structure can sometimes make it difficult to see how all the pieces fit together, but process ultimately gets the students to where they need to be. The class is very much designed to be "you get what you put into it".

I would but only if they're willing to put in the time. Overall, it was a lot of work with some assignments that felt silly or unnecessary but I do think I got a lot out of it as someone who has never worked in the hard sciences. If you're interested in commercialization work at all, this class is necessary.
Yes! Incredibly value learning opportunity. In addition to learning about startups, it also felt like a great presentation/public speaking skill buillder
I would recommend it cautiously, for several reasons.
1) The workload is heavy.
2) Lectures and class deliverables feel somewhat disconnected from the actual market research you end up doing, but the actual work is very interesting.

3) The climate tech curriculum is interesting, and could have more promise if the guest speakers come with a prepared presentation — I feel I got more value out of the guest lectures that had presentations this semester.
4) Rehearsals for summit and feedback from instructors during in-class working session is quite helpful.
Yes! I would definitely recommend this course to students. It was a lot of work but I learned so much about my start up and market and generally the process of climate tech commercialization.

It is a good class and a great way to learn more about a industry that you're interested in. I recommend being really thorough with the startup selection (before class starts), as that can make or break your experience (I got the one I wanted and really liked it). It is also a lot of work, be prepared to email (and cold email) many, many people that you're interested in talking to.

If you're interested in clean tech / climate tech, you must take this course for the learning, the network you build, and the credibility it gives you in the climate tech community (yes, really). Provides great hands-on introduction to a wide range of skill sets -- market research, techno-economic analysis, storytelling for business, customer research. It requires a ton of work, which you won't want to (or really be able to) put off until the end of the semester, but you'll have learned a lot by the end of it. Delivering this material in a compelling fashion as a classroom experience is a tall order for the instructors given the sheer breadth pf the course -- and the tension with the need to dive deep in your individual startup -- but the faculty puts a ton of effort into making it work and brings the very relevant experience and network to bear to do so.
Yes. Definitely recommended. Think of this class as Lean Launchpad 2.0 on steroids focusing on deep-tech and climate sectors. The most rigorous Applied Innovation class I have ever taken

It's a lot of work for little return. You must be *really really* into climate tech to enjoy this class. One nice thing about this class is the multi-disciplinary team you get to work on with PhD's, Law students, and Public Policy folks and you get to view problems from multiple angles.

Yes I will particularly because of the overall experience and impact. particularly for technical students I believe is a great opportunity to get to understand how startups work and even how exactly it may mean working in a founder of a a startup and the dynamics of the real world experience. I would however be very specific on the demands of the course and notify them of the extra requirements of time they may have to devote to the course in the beginning of the semester

Working alongside a real-world startup to understand their technology and find where it fits in the larger market was great, but the course did not really set you up for success. Class time was spent more on high-level theories and frameworks than actionable advice or insights, the group project dynamic of the deliverables made it more stressful and contentious than it needed to be, and at the end of the day I'm confident I would have learned more and worked less if I'd just done an internship at a climatetech start-up instead.

I'd highly recommend this course to students who are interested in or want to learn more about climate tech. The alumni and startup network, together with the industry expert guest speakers are valuable resources that brought this class to a next level. To me, this is more of a "program" than a "course", in the sense that there are amazing networking opportunities with guest speakers each class and happy hours to connect with past alumni. C2M is also a high profile program in the climate tech space and adds credentials to your experience if you want to work in the space in the future.
es, I would recommend it. For students with a technical background, it provides an excellent opportunity to explore potential business avenues.

I would recommend this class. I learned a lot about the business world that I would never have gotten a chance to engage with in other classes. I really appreciate how many people we got connected to and how many resources I was offered while taking this class. I am also extremely grateful for all the instructor's time and effort put into organizing multiple guest speakers, the MetLife Coaches, the Summit, etc... I have never taken a class with this much dedication put behind it. It is very energizing to see that much passion and energy behind a graduate class, not many classes in other departments are like this. This class was a great opportunity to put myself outside of my comfort zone and develop additional communication, analytical, and presentation skills. I have never spoken to a room that big before so the summit was a really knew and exciting experience. I also very much appreciate Berkeley offering a class with a values driven goal, if this was a class about a generic tech start up as opposed to a climate tech related one, I would not have been as engaged. The overall emphasis on supporting companies that are finding solutions to serious climate issues makes this class very motivating and the experience very rewarding. I am sure the skills I developed in this class will prove useful in the future. I found most assignments to be valuable and instructive, although I felt that some deadlines were arbitrary and unhelpful. The multiple business model canvas assignments did not really help our team. The assignment we struggled with the most was the TEA by far. I hade never made one before and I think we weren't properly prepared in this class to build a satisfactory TEA so I felt very unfulfilled by this assignment. To be clear, I think it is a great thing to learn how to do and excellent material for the class, but I would have appreciated more time spent on how to develop one and possibly multiple checkins and feedback sessions on this assignment as well. Without a complete TEA I felt that the some of the subsequent economic modeling we did on promising markets was inaccurate. The example TEAs provided were very helpful.

sections.goodFor: Students new to cleantech/deep tech who want consulting-style experiential work, startup exposure, networking and presentation/storytelling practice.
sections.notFor: Anyone time-constrained or already experienced in startups/product launch (too basic); one calls it administrative and 'fluffy', geared to the summit rather than to useful startup input.
sections.workloadNote: Called one of the heaviest at Haas; stakeholder interviews, entrepreneur meetings and assignments all happen outside the 3-hour weekly session, which several call long/redundant.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; team deliverables and the final C2M Summit presentation are the visible outputs.
sections.redFlags: Opaque startup matching (one gave 96/100 points to a choice and missed it); no control over teammates; long redundant lectures; outcome hinges on team and assigned startup; non-MBA teammates less available.
sections.quote: the workload is probably one of the heaviest among all classes I've taken as a third year MBA student... you don't get to choose your teammate
comments: Yes, if you're interested in climate technology. In particular, building out a network in climate/energy and/or thinking through how tech can scale are the core strengths of the class. The guest speakers and networking opportunities in this class are fantastic. And the teaching team does a good job introducing how to interview stakeholders, how to approach techno-economic analysis, and preparing you to present. However, while I have some frameworks to think about how tech scales (TEA, Competitive Analysis, TAM), these concepts are introduced then left up to us to really apply them in-depth. Because of this (as well as all the stakeholder interviews we have to do), the class can feel like a lot of work.

Yes! This is a great course for anyone, even someone with no experience in clean tech. It'll give you exposure and there's tons of investment that the course makes in you as a professional regardless of your industry vertical Yes, depending on what you are looking to get out of it and how much time you have. This is a great class for consulting experiential learning, plus startup and deep tech real-world experience -- both of which are great things. If you're looking for a safe environment that's flexible in terms of workload and has team members to lean on, this class is a great fit. If you're looking to learn lots by doing, want to learn quickly, and want to learn broadly, then an in- semester internship is likely more effective from a time-effort perspective -- but this is a much larger commitment than a class.
Yes I would

Yes. These instructors are really helpful not only delivering the program but also navigating related issues and problems

Do not recommend. This course is highly overrated. It is not well structured to result in substantial learning or to set you up for success. (1) This is an AI class, but it has only one instructor and GSI (for the context, another AI course Haas@Work has several instructors working with your team, guiding you, giving instant feedback etc). At the end of the day, you will be only watching Vince's videos and then trying to do something superficial with your team. (2) In terms of course load, you will also spread yourself thin since you need to report to your project sponsors and to the instructor, oftentimes doing double amount of not correlated work. (3) The course was changed to no add/drop, so if you end up with a team/project you don't like, there is no way out. On the positive side, Vince's pre-recorded videos are good and the curated list of reading is also very useful. Final advice, talk to people who took the class before making the decision.
I recommend this course as a strong foundation for those wanting to pursue a PM career

I would recommend this course to a fellow student, and for a more unique reason. I took this course to peek behind the curtain of Product Management, as that was the career I aspired to when I arrived on campus. By taking this course, I discovered that a career in Product was not for me, which is a very valuable insight. For the most part, MBA grads will not be headed straight into Product roles at Google, Apple, Facebook, etc (most likely will be Amazon). Everyone wants the prestige of working in Product for one of those companies, but not everyone wants to engage in the day to day mechanics of being in Product. This class gave me that insight, and I am grateful for the experience. Also, you'll feel more like a consultant during this course... the sponsor has a vision, and our team felt that we were more or less validating that vision using the frameworks in class. We had no interaction with marketing, engineering, sales, etc.

Product management is a fairly light lift AI course where you work with a client on a software product (usually). The quality of the clients varies, and in turn the quality of the learning, but it's a good class.

Personally, through the course I realized that I do not want to do product management, but was still worth while to learn about the framework that product managers use.
