I would recommend this course to anyone interested in learning about real estate and sustainability! There is a ton to learn about how real estate leverages new technologies to build sustainable developments.
Always take Nancy's class, she is the best in the game, you really want to go to her office hours too if you have time.

Yes. If you want a good overview of commercial real estate, this is the class to think. Prof Nancy Wallace is a giant in the field, and it is a privilege to hear her view and experiences. Prof Ed MacFarlane is also a wonderful resource to learn from, given his rich experience as an industry practitioner.
Yes, it would be good for an overview of development design and finance. If you have experience to have taken other development course it may be repetitive.
I would recommend taking a class with Nancy but I would not recommend taking a class with Ed.

Nancy does a great job teaching real estate courses and I wish she taught the entire class rather than split it 50/50. She is great at connecting the actual world of real estate with theory and cares about the students learning.
Definitely. While class content was interesting and worthwhile, Nancy as a professor would be the main motivator in recommending this class to others.
Yes I would. Nancy is a wealth of knowledge and inspires passion for innovative investment solutions to tackle social and environmental challenges.

I would highly recommend it. However some points for improvement– More about real estate investment vehicles, strategies and case examples. I would have also appreciated a little time every class dedicated to talk about current events or discuss a historical event related to the topic of discussion for that class.
Yes
Yes, but for MREDD there was a lot of crossover with previous classes, so the most relevant section for MREDD folks was Nancy's section.

Nancy Wallace is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. Her wealth of industry knowledge and experience made the class exciting, and her teaching style made the tricky course material easy to understand. The workload is just right, and I've learned a lot from the class. Coursework includes a very reasonable midterm to test your financial analysis knowledge to prepare you for a real–life current real estate development scenario in the second part of the course. You will not come across any outdated business school cases here. Weekly guest lecturers bring a very interesting and unique perspective to help students develop a well–rounded understanding of the subject matter. 10/10!
Absolutely, Nancy is wonderful and a really great teacher.
Neutral

Yes, this is a great course for any student that is not familiar with real estate to get first–hand experience. Absolutely. It was an incredible learning opportunity and forced me to think collaboratively and creatively. I am a CED student and the class was a great opportunity to work with other programs' students and share our perspectives.
yes if interested in real estate, it will be a great to get an overall sense
Yes - Nancy is extremely knowledgable and passionate about real estate development, there is no one in the world that would be more qualified to teach this class.
Keep doing what your are doing. the content is great!

The instructors are great! Super knowledgable and enthusiastic and keyed in. However, the class is very much you get what you put in. So if you're not genuinely interested and self motivated, you'll get very little from it as it's a low lift from the assignments point of view. Also you can get away with skipping a lot of the lectures. However if you're interested and curious and try out some new things, it's a great environment where you can get a lot of mentorship. And learn a lot from guest speakers who gave often frustratingly dense lectures. Very self guided learning, overall! Not as it currently is. In order to actually learn about real estate, you would need to teach yourself or go to office hours. Lectures are scattered and unhelpful.
yeah

Yes, however maybe not to an MRED student with a finance background. Lots of the materials covered are already covered in the MRED program, and some of the content was a repeat of what was covered in my undergrad real estate finance classes.

I recommend this course. Ed and Nancy have incredible industry knowledge and passion for the topic. The course is well designed to take you from a real estate novice to knowing just enough to be dangerous. Most of the guest speakers for this class are fascinating and relevant. The assignments are hefty but you work in a group so the workload is reasonable. However, the catch with this class is that you only get the most out of it if you invest time in working through the pro formas in the homework so I would recommend making time for that if you take this class. Yeah, and Nancy honestly is a delight. The sort of professor who inspires you to be like them.

This was a really worthwhile course - the instructors and guest speakers were so informative and gave very engaging real world examples of the challenges and opportunities in real estate development. The hands-on project was also really engaging. This course is a lot of work - so I wouldn't necessarily recommend for someone without a deep interest in real estate, or someone not wanting to pursue a career in real estate.
Absolutely. Exceptional overview of both commercial real estate development, asset analysis, and sustainability considerations in the real estate industry.
Yes, of course. I think it's a great survey of real estate, we have great speakers, the quality of the content is excellent and both Nancy and Ed do a great job and are very accessible and supportive

Good intro class to real estate investment, but need the student to take some initiatives to dig into the material. Nancy is very kind and make you feel very engaged and comfortable in class. She has a ton of experience in real estate! I definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in real estate.

sections.goodFor: Students serious about commercial real estate or project development (business, engineering or architecture side), especially those already working in RE who can self-direct.
sections.notFor: Anyone hoping to learn personal real estate investing, or with no RE vocabulary — you'll be lost early. Sustainability content is thinner than the title suggests. Not great for EWMBA peer-sharing.
sections.workloadNote: Hours not stated, but the final project is a large sustained lift with a pro forma model and progress reports; students say guidance on how to build it is only high level.
sections.gradingBasis: 'Almost half the grade is based on the final project,' plus student presentations/progress reports and in-class exercises.
sections.redFlags: Guest speakers eat ~half of nearly every class, crowding out teaching (4+); assignments posted 2-3 days before due, students chased the teaching team (2); pro forma guidance too high-level (3).
sections.quote: 90 minutes of almost every class was scattershot guest speakers talking about their various developments across the country that didn't add much to my learning.
comments: Highly recommend this course to those who look to learn fundamental and systematic real estate investment and development
Nancy has a lot to teach, but i think half of the time was spent on guest speakers which ate up the time to learn some really practical skills in real estate investment/finance

I would recommend this to folks who are serious or seriously curious about going into commercial real estate, but not for anybody else. I came in thinking this would be a nice foundation for future personal real estate investments, giving me the ability to evaluate the profitability of, say, buying a house or a small set of apartments. I also was hoping for in depth evaluation of the state of the real estate industry in the climate transition and where / how it needed to move faster. Unfortunately, neither of these were the case. We quickly dove into jargon and nuances of commercial real estate, which was good for the half of the class who had taken real estate classes already, but which made it difficult for me to engage. I do think the lineup of speakers were quite cool (e.g., the developers of Hudson Yards in NYC), but again, very focused on larger scale commercial real estate.

There's a slight disconnect among real estate classes. We learn how to build a proforma multiple times. There should be a foundational pro forma building course, giving other courses more time to go deeper into their specific real estate topic.

"Highly recommended! If you're a student interested in project development — whether from the business side or the engineering/architecture side — this class is extremely valuable. It equips you with the tools to plan, execute, and finance a project effectively."

Yes. It is definitely tailored for students already working in real estate or pursuing jobs in real estate, but it was well taught and the guest lecturers and panels were all incredibly additive to the course experience.
This class is worth what you put into it. I found immense value in the guest speakers, and as a gateway to the real estate industry.

I recommend taking this class for anybody interested in commercial real estate development. Professor Wallace is a great professor and has her pulse on the market, able to convey difficult concepts simply. Ed McFarlane supplements Nancy's lectures well, as an Architect he adds a practical element to classes and between the both of them can answer any question you may have. Each class starts with guest speakers, who are industry practitioners. This alone is great exposure and worth attending the class. What you get out of this class is very reliant on what you put in. As someone working in Real Estate, I can firmly say I learned some new things and got some great ideas.

Yes I would recommend this course to fellow students as think the insights from professionals were great to have in class and the exercises in the class helped develop real estate analysis skills I didn't have before.
Yes, good class to learn how real estate development numbers work
Would definitely recommend for anybody interested in real estate finance and how to view it from a sustainability lense!
Yes, I would, if the person was interested in pursuing a career in real estate. The material can be a bit overwhelming if a students does not know about the fundamentals of real estate investments.

This is good class to take if you are interested in learning more about real estate - the professors are both experts in this field - and are willing to look towards the future of where it should be going. However, the first few weeks will feel like getting thrown into the deep end - but it's actually quite manageable! I'd recommend. Real estate is something you should have given a bit of thought before graduating from business school (it is the biggest asset class in the US after all).

I loved Nancy Wallace as a knowledgeable professional but I would not recommend this course. I had hoped to get more practical financial skills in this course, but felt that ultimately very little teaching happened. 90 minutes of almost every class was scattershot guest speakers talking about their various developments across the country that didn't add much to my learning. And the other 90 min was often student presentations advancing towards the final project...but that left little time to do any real teaching/skill-building.

Also the course felt disorganized. The curriculum felt haphazard with topics not often progressing logically from one to the next, and assignments (and their accompanying details) wouldn't be created on BCourses until often 2-3 days before they were due. We would often have to remind the teaching team to post assignments (things that were vaguely labeled in the Syllabus like "Progress Report 2") and to give us details about what to submit, and then scramble to get those materials together on time. This is especially surprising in a 30-person course with two Readers that could have been supporting.

I would recommend as a very introductory class for real estate. It goes through most of the topics, but if someone wants something more technical or specific about the financials, this is not the class. Overall, speakers were great. Would liked to have more concrete learnings about applying sustainable features into real estate.

Yes. This class is a must for whoever used to, wants, or is about to work in the Real Estate industry. Professors are super professional and knowledgeable in this area. This class provides a hands on experience in Real Estate and cover almost every aspect of the industry from financial pro-forma to sustainability. If you don't have any finance or real estate background like me, this class might be a bit challenging but still manageable.

I would recommend this class as a great intro to real estate development and understanding the high level levers that could be utilized. Covers key topics and familiarizes you with different projects and companies within the ecosystem. I would recommend this course if you are interested in the built environment. That said, if you are only casually interested then this may be too technical/heavy on the finance side of things. The course has some heavy hitters as guest speakers who have implemented projects all over the country.

I would recommend this course for students who already have a good understanding of real estate or who are willing to put in extra time and effort outside of class to get up to speed on the concepts and fundamentals. Instructors were not the most organized and often were delayed in communicating expectations for class assignments. Half of the lecture time for almost each class was reserved for guest speakers, which was sometimes useful and interesting but not always. Almost half the grade is based on the final project and there is very little guidance on how to actually work through the pro forma model, complete the research, etc. (guidance is very high level).
I would recommend this course to students who want to dive deeper into the financial side of sustainable

development. This introductory course would require someone to have heard certain terminology from real estate to make this course more worthwhile. Other than terminology, coming from an engineering background, I was able to share sustainable strategies and was able to correlate how efficiency affects financial results.

I wouldn't recommend this to an EWMBA student. I didn't enjoy the low opportunity to share experiences and knowledge that other students had. This course is great prep for some one seeking a career in commercial real estate. However, as a someone with no background in real estate this course lacks breadth. I still don't understand how to develop a commercial real estate project. I get a few concepts like pro-forma and pitching projects to LPs.

sections.goodFor: Anyone interested in real estate development/investment or sustainability in the built environment, or wanting GP/LP incentives, pro formas, industry lingo and strong networking access.
sections.notFor: Students without finance or modeling experience - one warns it can be VERY difficult with lingo and concepts coming fast. One says do not pay for it, audit instead.
sections.workloadNote: Experiential 3-unit course: pro forma modeling through case studies plus a final team project, with a heavy guest-speaker roster. One warns there is a lot to absorb very quickly.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - case studies and a final team project are described, but no exams or grading breakdown are mentioned.
sections.redFlags: One student says most of the class is listening to guest lectures with the two professors hardly lecturing themselves, and would audit rather than pay. Pace and modeling demands are heavy for finance novices.
sections.quote: This is definitely a 3 unit and requires a lot of time and effort. Make sure you have a good, collaborative, communicative group because you will need to lean on them a lot
comments: I would highly recommend this instructor and course, especially for students interested in real estate. Regardless of whether you have a prior background in the field, the instructor is very supportive and makes a strong effort to help students understand the material. The course includes a project based on real-world scenarios, which provides a valuable and comprehensive experience of the real estate process. It allows students to engage with the challenges, opportunities, and complexities of real estate development in a meaningful way. Overall, it is a very rewarding and insightful course.
Yes, highly recommend this course. This course helps student to understand the real estate principle a lot if you are interested.

Whether you're interested in a career in real estate or just want to understand what defines a good real estate investment, you should take MBA280. This is a foundational course for anyone curious about the built environment. Nancy Wallace and Ed McFarlan are Berkeley's best and are complemented by an excellent roster of guest speakers. This is an experiential course so students should come prepared to work hard because they'll only get as much out of the class as they're willing to put in.
Yes, if they are interested in GP/LP real estate side of the business. it is very useful to understand the incentives for the built environment.
Yes, for the connections and networking opportunities the class affords.

Terrific course, the professors (especially Professor Wallace) add so much insight and context atop the great guest speakers. If you're interested in sustainability in the built environment and/or real estate development I highly recommend this class
Yes, if you're interested in real estate. this is one that should be taken.
Yes I would. The professors and guest speakers were wonderful and really deepened my understanding of the real estate industry.

I would not recommend paying for this class. If you are able to audit it, that would be much better. Most of the class is listening to guest lectures and the two professors hardly do any lectures themselves.

Yes, I would recommend this class if you are interested in a career in real estate. It provides a solid introduction to pro formas and financial modeling, taught by two stellar professors who are genuinely passionate about teaching and eager to help students learn. They emphasize gaining hands-on development experience while incorporating

sustainability principles. I learned a lot despite having very little pro forma experience when I entered the class, and my knowledge of pro formas grew significantly during the course through practice with case studies and the final team project (the Professors provided a lot of support). Both professors are very approachable and make themselves available. office hours, responding promptly over email. They are thoughtful in bringing a stellar lineup of industry guests, developers, investors, and other professionals, who share their experiences. This greatly enhances the classroom experience and offers a valuable opportunity to connect with industry leaders. You will leave with useful tools, industry terminology, and connections, as both professors are well-connected and encourage students to reach out to speakers and contacts. This was my favorite class during Haas, and I only regret not being able to take more classes with Professors Wallace and Ed.

I definitely recommend this course to folks, especially if you are looking to develop or hone your real estate skills. If you don't have muc h modeling experience or finance background, this course could be VERY difficult for you. There is A LOT to absorb very quickly, including industry lingo but also concepts. This is definitely a 3 unit and requires a lot of time and effort. Make sure you have a good, collaborative, communicative group because you will need to lean on them a lot with the case studies and projects. I'm not kidding. But it is worth it and you will feel prepared to talk shop about real estate after this class. I took away a lot, even if I don't plan to go into a real estate job after my MBA.

rows.title: From Query to Insights: Analytics with SQL & AI Assistants
rows.ghostNote: Two-Sunday intensive on getting from a business question to an answer with SQL plus AI assistants. The nearest prior is strong: the same instructor's SQL Programming course rates 6.27 across eight terms.

rows.title: AI Workflow Automation for Business Leaders
rows.ghostNote: New two-Sunday intensive on automating business workflows with AI tools. No course history under any name; the instructor's career record is the only signal.

rows.title: Technology Speaker Series
rows.ghostNote: One-unit, six-week technology speaker series: guest practitioners across the tech industry. Same instructor also runs the two AI Sunday intensives this term.

comments: I would definitely recommend this course if you want to learn more about real estate finance to get into the commercial real estate industry or even if you are looking at making some passive investments in things like real estate syndication / real estate private equity, etc. I also feel like this course gave a lot of insight as to why there are certain lending practices and financial systems in place in the United States, which is helpful for seeing how financial structures and incentives are set up.
Highly recommend - if you want to get a working knowledge of the financial aspects of the real estate market and asset class.

Tim knows this subject in and out. You?ll get a wonderful survey of the policy history that created our current system (lots of trial and error ending in financial crises). Then you?ll get a boot camp on doing the work within our modern system. The outside speakers are top notch as well. While Tim is great, you should recognize that this is a technical class focused on a fairly niche topic, so make sure it?s the right subject matter for you.
Yes

I highly recommend Professor McQuade and RE Finance to anyone interested in RE or finance generally. Tim does an incredible job of discussing how RE is the backbone of the US economy, the history of our RE system, and teaching technical financial skills necessary for a career in RE.

The course was well designed and had a wide variety of topics covered that could give a better idea of RE finance and Securitization to the student. Also, it gave an opportunity to students who wanted to delve deeper. The professor is one of the best the school has. Probably top 3. Extremely knowledgeable and extremely helpful and approachable. I chose this class mainly for the professor as I knew he would deliver and would be there to explain things and break things down in understandable bits. Absolutely and 100% recommend.

Yes, highly recommend--Tim's content is fresh, interesting, and trumps other professor's formats. One of my best instructors at Haas. He clearly cares a lot about the course and his students and is fair with
adjustments/accommodations.
Yes! Tim is extremely knowledgeable on the course's subject matter, and does a great job of making complex topics accessible.
I would if the student is looking to work in the real estate industry.

If you want to have a career in real estate or something real estate-adjacent (like management consulting focusing in real estate), this is a must-take course. Tim is knowledgeable, and the course is very thorough. If you want to learn a little bit about real estate but not for a career, this course could be too heavy.
Yes

If you are interested in real estate and particularly the credit markets, this is a must take. This is not necessarily a course for someone casually interested in the subject. For those in finance or real estate, I think this is one of the best courses to take at Haas.
Yes I would and I have! I learned more about finance in this course than I did in core finance.
Yes! Tim is an excellent instructor and genuinely cares about his students. He quickly responds outside of class hours and is excellent to work with.

I would recommend this course to a fellow student. I would preface by saying this is not the class to take if you just want an introduction to the qualitative side of Real Estate Investing, it's a blend of finance and real estate. It is absolutely a must take for anyone interested in pursuing a career in real estate. However, I think if you are generally interested in Real Estate investing or just want to strengthen your finance knowledge (through Real Estate concepts), this is a great class to take at all.
Yes, he was very engaging and classes were very educational
I recommend this instructor in general. This class is very specific to Real Estate Finance, if you are not interested in this completely the class might not be for you.

This is a fantastic course that anyone should take if they want to learn more about real estate finance and how it works in our world today. The topics are complex but Tim does a great job making them more straightforward. Setting the course aside, Tim an amazing instructor with a world of knowledge and you should take any of his classes if you get the chance!
I recommend this course to anyone interested in real estate finance and investment. Will have an overall
understanding and technical finance calculation of all the financing approaches from various types of property and securities.
Tim is nice and would love to discuss any questions no matter class-related or not.

Tim is on of the best professors I?ve had in 3 years at Haas and one of the best courses. He is incredibly knowledgeable and has a great, meticulous way of explaining complex concepts in real estate financing anyone can understand. He is very thorough and engaging in his way of teaching that can easily keep you focused for 3 full hours. Highly recommend to anyone who is interested in real estate finance!

Yes. Prof McQuade's ability to break down complex and difficult finance concepts simply and clearly is unsurpassed in any of the quantitative class I've taken at Haas. His ability to answer questions and liven up a 3 hr night class with real- world examples and his own research also makes the course material come to life.

I would recommend the professor, however, caution to the difficulty of the structure based on complexity and homework. That said, I give large credit to Tim, he?s been more accessible and thorough in his explanation than the majority of professors I?ve had at Berkeley which is a huge credit to him. I hope to stay in touch and appreciate everything he brings to the classroom.

Yes, but depends on the fellow student. I would not recommend this course for someone who is not from a STEM background and has low will to face challenges. If I knew the person could handle it, I would definitely recommend. Maybe auditing is a good option for people that don't understand finance, that allows the student to immerse themselves in the content without the weight of the tests.
Yes, it definitely adds to the academic experience of the MRED+D program because there's a gap in finance-related subjects.

I would absolutely recommend this professor. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject and a very energetic professor. Just be aware that this course is much less about home buying/residential mortgages and more about the industry from Wall Street's point of view.

yes. this is a course that will introduce you to all the foundation needed to understand real estate finance. Even though it is foundation, it is still relatively intense for people who don't have a finance background. there will be a learning curve, but i still enjoyed what I got out so far. I think the work load can be reduced a lit. maybe one exam and a presentation. maybe an extra small homework sets
Yes, Tim is a great guy and honestly a better teacher of course I wish the midterm was a little easier but I really enjoyed learning from him
Definitely recommend this course for anyone looking to understand how financing works in Real Estate (not just residential but also in commerical and mega projects).
Very interesting set of case studies discussed that help contextualize in-class mathematical learning to real world application

Yes, this course provides a very robust overview of real estate finance. The instructor is very knowledgeable and not only provides articulate explanations of concepts, but also dives into excel during class and includes real world applications and cases within the course. I highly recommend taking this course from McQuade if you are considering any career in real estate.
I would, this course was very helpful in teaching a subject I knew little about and the knowledge I gained was helpful for when I met with industry professionals.
Yes - it covers a range of important topics even if you do not want to go into real estate
Yes, he's a very energetic and interesting professor. Relevant course, but it is tough.
I recommend Tim for sure. He is incredibly knowledgable, fair, and approachable.

100% recommend to all MRED students, really helps fill out the financial foundation from the first MRED term. I'm so glad this course was recommended to me, at first I thought it would be too high level or dry for me, but the coverage of green financing, new areas of research and new potential financial structures for climate and insurance modeling were all really informative. The project was great, and the knowledge from the course helped me even during the same semester in other classes I was taking. A++
Yes, I would definitely recommend Tim and this class, because it has been very great and has taught me a lot regarding the applicability of real estate finance in the world.

I highly recommend this course for students who want to delve deeper into the real estate world and/or pursue a career there. I do not recommend it for those who are shopping for RE classes or want 3 easy units. It is a very specific and demanding course in terms of completely new things you can learn, compared to other RE or finance courses. Tim, the guest speakers, and the diversity of the class (FTMBA, EWMBA, MREDD) are unique and valuable. It is a challenging and sometimes technical course, but definitely one from which I learned the most.
I would recommend this class to every student who wants to go into real estate. Especially real estate finance. It gives you the fundamentals concepts of real estate finance

I would not recommend this course to students who are looking for an introduction to real estate finance / who are just dipping their feet into the subject. The material is fairly dense and technical, not easily accessible for beginners or even those who come with a basic knowledge of finance.
Yes, strongly recommend. This course is very analytical, so you need to be good at math.
Yes, very relevant to real estate as an industry.
I would absolutely recommend this course to other students; you learn a lot about real estate financing vehicles. Yes - very interesting and broad learning!
Yes. Tim is a effective communicator and able to explain the content in a timely and effective manner

I would not recommend this course unless you are certain that you are interested in real estate and love using Excel to estimate cash flows. This course is HIGHLY technical and I struggled to grasp many of the concepts due to the sheer volume and complexity of the material. Professor McQuade is extremely intelligent but I don't think he's aware of how many students are completely lost during the lecture.
I would recommend it if you have experience in real estate and are invested in the topic. Otherwise, I don't think this was an introductory course.

This course is accurately advertised - it is purely real estate finance and securitization. If that's what you're looking for then Tim is a good instructor and an authority on the topic. The workload was reasonable and the homework
assignments/projects/cases were applicable and supported actually learning the material. It wasn't the highest impact 3 unit elective I have taken; but yes, overall I do recommend the course.

Absolutely! This class was great for individuals looking to understand how capital generally works and how it is utilized for real estate investments. I've taken my share of real estate courses and still found this course, materials and guest speakers to be incredibly valuable. I strongly suggest this course to anyone looking to understand such a key part of economics.
Tim is very passionate about the subject and you can tell he knows his stuff about real estate finance. His class is great if you want to pursue a career in real estate development.

However, I would not recommend the course if you do not plan to pursue a career or you have a passive interest in real estate, as the subject matter can get very technical. I wish there were opportunities for Tim to break up the lecture style to have more cases and real-life applicaitons to the concepts taught. I would also suggest Tim slows down his lectures and allows for more questions to be asked.

No. I think the content is valuable but the style of delivery made the class pointless for me and I had to self-teach outside of the lectures. I could have taken an online course for this instead of spending my Tuesday nights in class If interested in real estate finance and securitization I would definitely recommend this course as it gives a very good overview of the dynamics of the market
Would recommend for sure.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in real estate or bond math who want to evaluate deals and structures; good access to McQuade for people trying to break into the space.
sections.notFor: Split: one says too advanced without base finance/RE knowledge, another says the pace is slow if you have finance background. Very specific subject with limited use outside finance.
sections.workloadNote: One student calls the workload moderate. Expect Excel time working through cash flows; sessions run history, bond math, REITs, PE and mortgage-backed securities, plus guest lecturers.
sections.gradingBasis: a midterm that several found difficult (described as difficult every year)
sections.redFlags: Students disagree sharply on the prerequisite level - one found it too advanced without background, another found it slow with background. Midterm noted as difficult by 1.
sections.quote: If you took intro to finance or have a finance background at all, nothing in this class should be overly difficult or technical, and the pace may actually be a little slow if you do.
comments: Yes. He is very engaged.
Yes I would!

This is a great class and Tim is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about this class, which makes lectures and class enjoyable. There are also a good number of guest lecturers that do a great job of translating what you learn in this class to application. If you are interested in real estate or even just want to learn more about it, this is a great class that covers a wide range of topics and isn't too quantitatively intense.

yes, especially for those who do not come from a finance background and wants to deep dive into the world of real estate finance. this course will help you understand an evaluate financial deals and structures used in the market Yes
Yes, if you are interested in this topic, this is a great course!
I would only recommed it to someone who has base financial and real estate knowledge or else it is way too advanced and hard to keep up with
Yes. Professor McQuade is a great lecturer and knows the material throroughly.
Yes, I believe Tim is has good insight into the topics and also brought in great speakers. The midterm was difficult but it seemed like it is every year.
yes, it may not be as applicable for your job if you don't pursuing a career in finance, but its good to understand the general secondary market for mortgages
Yes, good professor and teaches at an appropriate pace. The class is very specific though

Great instructor, really knows his stuff and keeps the class engaging. If you took intro to finance or have a finance background at all, nothing in this class should be overly difficult or technical, and the pace may actually be a little slow if you do. Prof. McQuade is also very approachable, great person to connect with if you're trying to work in the space. Workload is moderate.

I highly recommend this course. Professor McQuade starts the course by providing a succinct history to explain our modern real estate finance system. The sessions go from there, as he dives into bond math, REITs, and private equity, culminating into mortgage backed securities.
I am someone with extensive experience in commercial real estate, and I can say that this is one of the classes that defines why I came to business school at Haas.
Yes, I would recommend Tim's course as it was very well structured and provided a overview in great detail about the real estate financing opportunities in the US.

Yes I would recomend it for students interested in general bond math and the real estate market. It is one of the more technical courses I've taken, so be prepared to spend some time in excel understanding a cash flow

Yes, really awesome course to learn about entrepreneurship in a low-lift manner. It was fun, engaging, and impressive how much we were able to do in just 48 hours. Highly recommend to students with any inkling of startup and product ideation!
Yes. Great team building and bonding experience. Challenging platform to dive into research and push yourself to be creative and efficient

I would recommend those who want to understand the basics of entrepreneurship to take this class. While I'm not sure if our idea will live on beyond the course of the class, I feel like I walked away with a much better idea of how I would approach launching a new venture.

Yes, I would recommend if you have no knowledge of startup discovery method or how to think of an idea and evolve it into something more tangible on paper. But if you have had start up experience, I would not recommend since you will not be learning anything new.
Yes, definitely.

This course was extremely useful for reinforcing practical concepts introduced in Data & Decisions and complex methods taught in Big Data & Better Decisions. Professor Yang presented the information and intuition behind different methods very clearly, while addressing questions in class respectfully and with confidence. This course was a useful primer for or opportunity to practice essential data analytics skills! I appreciated Luyi's preparation and manner a lot. The Data Mining course needed more hands-on, in-class practice on R and/or Python for people without programming experience, who aer the folks that the class was supposedly aimed at. To find the time, you can "prune" the number of topics, digressions, and long explanations of the simpler concepts. I personally feel I would have learned and retained much more had the number of topics been less, and guided practice been increased. Did we really need all three classifiers, Logistic Regression, k-NN, AND Classification Tree? Better would have been to pick one or two and practice it in class. It was too much to navigate coding on our own, in homework groups. Groups without members with coding experience must have been seriously out of luck.

The fact that this may not be offered in the coming year is disappointing (understandably that the professor is taking time to re-energize which is also much needed to continue her work). Would love to see someone else pick this up or be hired to continue offering this class.

Yes. The people in the class make it amazing. Learned so much from my peers and had more rich, candid, and real conversations here than in any other Haas class. Especially if you've never interacted with DEI before, it will be a huge value add and space for introspection and knowing yourself better. There are tangible ways you can commit to being a better and more inclusive leader.

Yes. If you're interested in learning how to be a more dynamic, empathetic, and inclusive leader, Kellie is the professor and EFL is the class for you. Kellie and EFL challenge you to grow in ways no other course even considers.

Yes! 100%. This course is critical for anyone who is looking for a DEI-focused class. Some aspects may be introductory, but you can learn a lot from your classmates and also continue to build your DEI competency. I wish this class was part of core for Fall A/B or Spring A/B.

I would recommend this class. Its the broadest DEI course at Haas as of this writing in fall 2021. Its good for an AI, its good for personal learning. Just be prepared to be vulnerable and don't be scared.

Yes. If you're reading this at a time when Kellie decides to teach an MBA course again, take this class. You gain a lot of great resources to inform a business case for DEI. You get to interact with your classmates in deeper conversations than in most courses here at Haas. Kellie is one of the few profs here that I feel who actually proactively and explicitly demonstrates care for not only the class content, but also the well-being and education of students in her class. Would absolutely recommend, especially to those who are less familiar with DEI and equity fluent leadership. There is so much to learn in the space and the coursework lends itself to facilitating a wonderful and committed community to learn alongside.

I wish this was a required course for all of Haas. It is such a unique gift to be able to reflect, learn, and act in one class. It requires bravery to be willing to share and acknowledge your own shortcomings, but I truly think anyone who takes this class comes out the other end as a better leader. Kellie has an immense amount of experience and brought great guest speakers that really enhanced the course.
Absolutely. I wish everyone would take this course, or some version of it, as a requirement for Haas graduation. It is what we're all about.
Everyone will gain value from this class. If nothing else, you'll get to know people on a deeper level than you may ever will at Haas. Even your best friends.

Absolutely. In a world that is becoming more diverse, as leaders we need the tools to navigate and empathize with our teams and colleagues. When faced with individuals who are different, it's imperative to learn how to find the commonalities but also appreciate the differences, and how to utilize them in the workplace.

I recommend this course to anyone who is interested in Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, regardless of where they are on their learning journey. Professor Kellie makes it clear that we are student always when it comes to DEI topics, and she is great at building the psychological safety needed for everyone to feel comfortable sharing their lived experiences. Many of the topics presented in lecture are not necessarily brand new to the students, but we did a lot of deep dive into new ways and angles to view the issues.

Don't leave Haas without taking this class! A leader is a leader of people first. If you can't lead people, you aren't a true leader. This course teaches you how to lead people that are different from you and helps you to learn how to become a better leader after leading Haas! Again, don't let preconception of what this course may be bias you from actually developing the types of skills you need to be an effective leader.

Equity fluent leadership is EXTREMELY important for all Haas/Berkeley alumni. I think it should be a required class for all undergrad and graduate programs. It is a class where you participate in discussions every week and the content can be deep or heavy, but I think in order for us to be leaders and to make positive change in the world this content is crucial. Lastly, Kellie is extremely impressive. She has great experiences to share from a strategic and tactical perspective, extremely impressive speakers she brings in and every class was a joy to attend. Highly recommend for MBA students!

Becoming more aware of equity fluent leadership will make you a more effective leader, full stop. How to create a psychologically safe environment where everyone can participate at their fullest is hugely beneficial skill. Kellie is an expert in this space and is able to provide broad learnings AND specific tactics to give students a clear understanding of the impact of Equity Fluent Leadership and how to lead people effectively.

yes! i think everyone should learn to be an equity fluent leader and Kellie does a great job of teaching it. I would highly recommend Kellie and EFL to other students. I would recommend this class to anyone. Kellie is a fantastic and empathetic teacher and leader - you won't want to miss learning from her. And the consulting project you do in this class is very high-level - I consulted with the Chief Diversity Officer at Yelp.
I highly recommend professor McElhaney; she is phenomenal in designing a course, focusing on meaningful

YES YES YES. Take this class. Awesome class discussions, epic companies submitting projects for the consulting piece, all around fabulous. Also, I was a little concerned it was going to be some "woke warriors" dominating the class but it was way more grounded, genuine discussion, debate, and personal learning.
Would fully recommend this to anyone who is remotely interested in DEIB.

I think every student at Berkeley should take this course! Equity-Fluent Leadership skills and knowledge are needed now more than ever before. I also think the Center for Equity, Gender, & Leadership's work should be more prioritized at Haas.

Absolutely, I wholeheartedly recommend this instructor and course to any fellow student interested in gaining a deep understanding of ESG principles and their practical applications in the business world. Professor Giessler is not only highly knowledgeable in the field of ESG but also incredibly passionate about the topic of ESG. Her enthusiasm is infectious and motivates students to engage actively in learning. 10 / 10 would recommend!!!

I would definitely recommend this course if you are at all interested in corporate sustainability, human rights, and governance best practices. It provides a thorough overview of these legal frameworks and brings in relevant cases. The class also has a reasonable workload and fits well into a busy schedule.

If you are remotely interested in ESG, this is an incredibly helpful course to understand all facets of it and how to apply it to your unique profession. Jo is an expert in her field and provides a wealth of knowledge from her experiences and research. We cover all facets of ESG, but stay hunkered to the business case behind it. The class is incredibly relevant, as we stay up to date with the latest news and policy developments. Jo provides actionable steps for us as
professionals to step up and make a change in our organizations. 100% would recommend!
YES! This is a very important for every Haas student and critical knowledge for the future of business!

Jo is a subject-matter expert in this field and pulls from her career experience addressing these issues in the real world. The topics can be complex (the space is changing quickly and has a complex history); she did a great job of teaching the content and clearly articulating key points, backgrounds, frustrating contradictions in rules, and giving appropriate context, all while bringing in current events (really loved that!). It was so great to have a practitioner's perspective for this course! She also had very helpful charts to explain theory, which we will be able to use in our careers moving forward and helpful discussions about change management (a key part of ESG!).
Yes, it is good for people who still learn about ESG and want to be exposed with a real life cases.

I hesitate to recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. I think of the student is interested in entering the ESG space, specifically for a company that interacts directly with the E or S of ESG heavily, I think it's a natural fit. However, for other roles in traditional tech or finance, I am not sure there is as much room to take full advantage. To reach a broader audience, I think a key question that should be better answered in the course (though it was indirectly at many times) is how to demystify ESG and make the business case. I think to outsiders or foreigners to ESG, I am not confident that the way the course material was presented would sway them to think differently. However, that is not to say that any of the course elements are missing to make that argument - just the organization and presentation.

sections.goodFor: Students who want a stage to practice storytelling and public speaking with personalized coaching in a small class; repeatedly recommended for people who liked Leadership Communications and want to go deeper, or beginners seeking confidence and self-awareness.
sections.notFor: Students expecting business-presentation training; several said it is essentially a LeadComm recap built on personal stories, and a couple found the reflections busy work and the applicability to workplace presentations unclear.
sections.workloadNote: Weekly speeches and written reflections; the load is more emotional than technical, with students describing 3-hour sessions that demand full presence and are draining.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (4+ comments): heavy overlap with Leadership Communications; a few questioned how the personal-story format transfers to business settings; sessions are emotionally taxing.
sections.quote: Highly recommend this class, it will take you to another level in your storytelling.
comments: This course definitely teaches you a lot about the nuances of storytelling. However, this is a very emotionally draining course; be expected to be physically exhausted at the end of course sessions due to being engaged 100% of the time. Yes, 100%! One of the best classes at Haas. If anyone wants to have some experience with entrepreneurship, this is a great class. The teaching team is also fantastic!

Amazing course with ridiculous workload, but you get what you put in- maybe even a billion dollar business, and grow as much either way. Form a team with people who are really dedicated and go out there to figure if there's a viable business to be made. You get tons of mentorship from 5+ startup veterans. No punches pull, no hand holding. It can feel a bit like Shark Tank if all the Sharks want is for you to grow as an entrepreneur and be successful. (I had a good experience in this regard but think it would be de-motivating to be working with a lame team/idea.) Make sure you join a team with people you work well with, and a project you're passionate about, because it is quite tough otherwise.
absolutely not, this course dragged down my semester so hard and was an emotional drain. I had to continue to participate well after any tangible learning was done

sections.goodFor: Anyone serious about startups - including engineers - who wants customer-discovery reps, a real hunt for product-market fit, and access to world-class mentors, VCs and industry leaders.
sections.notFor: Students who can't commit far beyond class hours, or who expect to build a product - one warns you're only testing ideas on a soundboard and will be confused often.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy and well beyond scheduled class hours: weekly office hours, 10 customer discovery interviews per week, mentor meetings, team prep sessions and a weekly presentation.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - weekly presentations and customer-discovery progress structure the course, but grading is never described.

The program ends up saving a lot of time as a founder since you don't waste time aimlessly building.

Yes, I would recommend this course, this is one of the courses which taught me a lot of things in a fast paced manner, the amount of work I got done in any course is not even comparable to anything else which I have taken

This course challenges you to get out of the classroom and talk to real people. Rather than just discussing theories and frameworks on paper, we apply them every week. It is inspiring to hear about other teams' progress, as well as the experiences of the instructors and mentors. YES! It is a lot of work, but if startups is something that interests you, I would definitely recommend you try it out! If I was to give any other students advice: you aren't building anything here just testing ideas out on a soundboard, you're going to be confused often which means you're doing it right, and have some fun with it.

Bill is one of Haas's most important assets and I would highly recommend taking at least one of his courses. I also loved the 10-week marketing strategy simulation/competition.
