sections.gradingBasis: Weekly team presentations on customer discovery progress; grading not otherwise discussed.
sections.quote: the course demands a significant time commitment well beyond scheduled class hours, including weekly office hours, 10 customer discovery interviews per week, mentor meetings
comments: If you're serious about entrepreneurship and not sure where to get started, LLP is a great class. It could help steer you in the right direction. The number one takeaway for me was customer feedback, the class is about finding PMF and real customers, which you have to do by talking to potential customers. The program ends up saving a lot of time as a founder since you don't waste time aimlessly building.

Yes, I would recommend this course, this is one of the courses which taught me a lot of things in a fast paced manner, the amount of work I got done in any course is not even comparable to anything else which I have taken

This course challenges you to get out of the classroom and talk to real people. Rather than just discussing theories and frameworks on paper, we apply them every week. It is inspiring to hear about other teams' progress, as well as the experiences of the instructors and mentors. Even if you don't have a specific startup idea, the process provides learnings that are beneficial in any professional setting.

YES! It is a lot of work, but if startups is something that interests you, I would definitely recommend you try it out! I would highly recommend this course for any engineer looking to understand the secret keys to entrepreneurship. In addition to knowing the steps to bring you design idea to a real product, you will gain invaluable connections to business leaders, VC's, and other students.
Yes. He is generally open to criticism that leads to better class outcomes and helpful if approached. I enjoyed the dry humour in the class.
I would recommend this course because it's not about learning from theory but learning from failures and successes in real life.

The greatest strength of this course is the access it provides to world-class mentors and industry leaders. The opportunity to learn directly from their experience and receive personalized guidance is priceless and not something easily replicated in a traditional classroom setting. That said, the course demands a significant time commitment well beyond scheduled class hours, including weekly office hours, 10 customer discovery interviews per week, mentor meetings, team preparation sessions, and a weekly presentation. For students who can make that investment, the return is exceptional.

Yes 100%. This course is probably one of the best I have taken at Haas. The sheer wealth of knowledge I gained from videos, from mentorship, and the people I got connected to were fantastic. It's a lot of work but it's appropriately advertised/marketed as such and I've really enjoyed my time in the class. If I was to give any other students advice: you aren't building anything here just testing ideas out on a soundboard, you're going to be confused often which means you're doing it right, and have some fun with it.

sections.goodFor: Students who want a structured, low-risk place to develop a venture idea with a team; commenters valued the roadmap for entrepreneurship and the instructor's real founding experience.
sections.quote: Gives a great roadmap for entrepreneurship and is a safe place to experiment with ideas.
comments: Yep, It was a great experience to get to work on a venture idea with a great team, helpful resources and support. I really enjoyed working with Aaron - he has tenacity and real founding experience.
Yes. Gives a great roadmap for entrepreneurship and is a safe place to experiment with ideas.
Yes
Yes, probably my favorite class this spring semester.

Absolutely. Very interesting material and Molly is a fantastically knowledgeable and engaging lecturer. The class is more rigid in it's direction and discussion than other classes I have had at Haas, but this isn't necessarily bad. This was the best course I have taken at Haas by far, I would recommend it to anyone who is interested in tech, VC, cities, or people.

I'd absolutely recommend this class! Molly is a fantastic teacher, who does an excellent job mixing theoretical urban policy learnings at the beginning of the class with practical applications through guest speakers in the second half. The workload is heavily front-loaded to the beginning, but overall it's a light lift. This class has a lot of hype, but it's worth it. I appreciated my discussions with the classroom and learned a lot from those in the classroom as well as the 14+ speakers! It's mainly discussion based, so helpful to come prepared to speak.

Absolutely, if you're interested in the intersection of tech, VC-backed start-ups and public policy. Molly is a great professor with practical experience. This class is not for people who casually interested in the tech industry and plan to work in big tech, but don't have an interest in urban issues and city/local governance.

I would absolutely recommend this class to every person who wants to think about the social impact of their work, whether it is urban, in technology, both, or neither. The discussions are thorough and profound, and the readings provide much-needed context that students are often lacking.

Yes I would recommend the instructor and the course to another student, I think this was some of the most fascinating discussions I've had at Haas so far and I don't think I would have thought much about this ecosystem on a critical level if it had not been for this class.

Absolutely - this was a fantastic class. We spend so much of business school focusing on the business questions, but this class offered a wider perspective that brought together a mixture of different disciplines. I felt like I was actually thinking again.

The guest speakers were well curated and informative. If you have any interest in urban technology, take this course! Yes. She is an invaluable resource to Haas. DO NOT LOSE HER. Molly taught us to think about the "why" and is one of the finest teachers I have ever had.

Yes, this class was a great way to challenge some of the tech and VC optimism to think about how we start ups can actually make the world a better place. Molly is a great instructor and has an amazing network of guest speakers to invite.
Amazing class, if you're interested in tech you'll learn a lot about startups, VC, government, and policy. Will make you think and learn a lot.

Yes, I would highly recommend this course to anyone going into startups, VC or big tech. I think it challenges you to think critically and consider the community impacts of emerging technologies and business models. You will also learn about the role of government and non-profits in working on solutions with the private sector. It's a lot of reading and class discussion, but Molly is great at facilitating.

Yes, but know what you're getting into. The first third of the class is effectively an urban planning/history class where there's a lot of dense reading and more academic discussions. Things got a bit more interesting in the second two thirds, where Molly brings in guest speakers from a number of different fields (VC, startups, government, journalists). Hearing from these experts was a highlight. I think this class would be best as a smaller discussion-based class. Unfortunately we had ~75 people, which made participating really challenging and feel unwieldy. Overall the topics are really interesting, but it felt a little more like listening to a podcast than actively engaging. I have a few high-level take-aways after taking the class, but no tangible skills. I didn't expect that, but again, something to keep in mind when considering what you're looking for in a class.

The class is good for anyone who wants to understand the connections of technology, cities, and government. Yes, it's very different from other classes. If they plan on founding a tech-based start-up, I'd consider this class essential.

Yes, especially if you are interested in tech as an industry and/or startups and venture capital (with a tech focus). Yes. Especially if they are interested in Tech either from the founder, government or VC perspective.
For students interested in urban tech and policy this class is great. Or if you are planning to pursue a career in tech, I would recommend this class.
Yes, very insightful course
Yes would recommend but if you don't like podcasts than maybe not.
Yes if you want a case based class around talking through urban problems and figuring out the question to ask, less if you just want to listen to solutions.
yes yes yes
Great class. Take it. Nuff said.
Yes
Yes, she is extremely knowledgeable and personable. Great connection as we go out into the world.
Yes! Take this class!! Molly's an excellent instructor and this class is wonderful. Particularly if you are interested in tech, government, or VC

Yes - if you have any interest in urban-related tech companies or tech generally, this course gives helpful context on what types of careers exist and what their impact may be. Even if you aren't interested in a tech career, the class is well organized and entertaining, with great speakers throughout.
I would recommend this to any student looking to break into VC or entrepreneurship to better understand real life challenges and opportunities in this ecosystem.

Maybe, if you are interested in Tech and want to make connections then this is a good class for you. But if you want to explore topics organically and have stimulating conversations then I would suggest taking a different class. I would recommend this class but i wouldn't prioritize it over P&P. It's unique but i think getting the readings from a classmate is more or less akin to my learnings from the class. I don't know how much class discussions contributed to my learning, but I actually really enjoyed the readings.

I would not recommend this course if the section size is over 30 people. There is a great opportunity here for discussion and engaged learning; with too many people, that opportunity disappears. Molly can force some good discussion, but tends to take too much time with the guests, leaving very little time for student interaction. Yes

I would recommend this class if you are planning to found a startup or even if you are just working in the Tech industry. This course really makes you think about all the players on the chess board in the intersection of tech and policy. It is a discussion-heavy class that relies on every single student to contribute, it's not a class where you can sit back and listen to someone lecture for 1.5 hours.
absolutely would recommend - much different from any other class I've taken at Haas and resulted in significant learning

100%. This is the best class that I have taken at Haas. Molly is an expert. She is kind and encouraging, while also challenging students to develop their own opinions and perspectives. I so valued the way she often asked follow up questions to force students to clarify their point of view. The guests she brought in were engaging, and represented a breadth of stakeholders in the startup and urban ecosystem. It was extremely valuable to have this breadth of representation - one I have not seen in any other class.
Best class at haas

This is a good and interesting class. Very front loaded when it comes to work and intensity. But it gets better towards the end. The teaching style can feel intimidating and pressured to talk especially with the grading style
Yes, i liked the speakers and hearing my classmates speak.
Yes, Molly is very well-prepared and this is a good course for getting up to date on urban tech.

This course skillfully connected sustainability, food, and business, emphasizing the critical intersection of sustainable practices in food systems and their implications for the business world. It provided valuable opportunities to explore how innovative solutions can address global challenges in these areas, while also expanding my understanding of the field's vast potential. The instructor offered excellent insights and connections, fostering both knowledge and professional growth. This course is a must for anyone passionate about creating impactful, sustainable change through food and business strategies.
Yes, I recommend it. You can experience new experiences that you can't do in other existing classes.

Yes! both Miyoko and Brittany are one of the nicest instructors I've had on campus and they're deeply understanding with the role of being a student is. They not only provide opportunities outside of this class for jobs/internships, but they're great people and wish the best for everyone. I think this class is great for people interested in food systems (injustice, animal welfare, sustainability, shelf life, etc.) and also just basic business skills of being a consultant/entrepreneur. I've learned many valuable lessons in just the project itself and I love the instructors a lot. Great environment!

I really enjoyed this course because it was able to highlight all sectors in food systems in a digestible manner. The guest speakers were always inspiring to hear and motivate me to learn more about food systems and the plant-based community. I think this class is inspiring in getting to recognize knowledge about plant-centric diets that is never showcased in other courses at Berkeley.

This class was so unique and informative. It was such a treat to be in a college-level course that actually discussed the importance and intersectionality of moving towards a plant-based world. I loved the dynamic and varied intro to the business world and consulting that it provided, without compromising any values. Both Brittany and Miyoko were incredible, so knowledgeable and willing to help in any way possible.
Yes, this is the best course ever. Everyone should take it.
Both instructors are extremely helpful and are exceptional and passionate for this class!

Yes definitely. Since in addition to being a class, it also acts as an internship opportunity to work with companies, it is different than any other course I've taken at Berkeley. It was a wonderful learning and working experience and taught me so much.

sections.goodFor: Students new to food systems or plant-based business who want topic exposure, strong guest speakers, potlucks, and connections into food companies and institutions.
sections.notFor: MBAs expecting business-skill building: mixed undergrad/grad teams mean MBAs report teaching teammates market sizing and client professionalism. Also skip if you have food systems background.
sections.workloadNote: Many small assignments described as busy work on top of a semester-long external client project; classes largely on Zoom with guest speakers and in-person potlucks. 3 credits.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; many small assignments plus a team deliverable for an external client (market sizing, competitor research, pitch deck).
sections.redFlags: One-sided advocacy - 'vegan propaganda' framing (3 of 17); many small busy-work assignments pitched at undergrad level (4); MBAs report PM-ing undergrad teammates on real client work; Zoom sessions disengaging.
sections.quote: be prepared for the class to feel a bit like vegan propaganda at times - if youre aware and open to that, I think it's a great class and highly recommend.
comments: This class is helpful if you are new to food systems and the plant-based world and it is a good learning experience about everything involved in animal agriculture processes and the negative impacts socially, environmentally, ethically ets. Lots of good guest speakers but signing up to ask a question before we heard them speak is not best, since we don't know exactly what they will talk about and usually the questions are already answered. The in-person potluck days are fun - I really enjoyed trying plant-based dishes from others. I would say as an MBA this was a LOT of little assignments that were a lot of busy work, in addition to project with an external client, so the class seems a little more geared towards undergraduates than graduate-level students, so I think less little required assignments should be required for this to be a 3-credit course with an experiential learning component.
Yes, engaging, so interesting, found my niche

Working with a client in a team setting is a great learning experience, which I would highly recommend. You get more out of this class if you're into food systems, obviously, but prior experience isn't super necessary at all. I would 100% recommend this course to a fellow student because of Miyoko and Brittanys' passion towards the topic. It is an excellent place to build teamwork strengths as you get to work with many different classmates and have so many opportunities to share ideas with each other. This class is also an excellent place to gain more connections if you intend to work in the food business because of the group projects that connect you to relavent food businesses and institutions and all the guest speakers as well.

Interesting class for students who have never taken a food systems or plant-based class in the past, but you won't gain too much additional information if you came in with prior knowledge. The speakers and semester-long partnerships are interesting, but do note that having Zoom discussions isn't the most engaging and you'll be working with undergraduates who may depend on your MBA knowledge to ensure project success.
The professors, Brittany and Miyoko, are extremely knowledgeable and great people to know. If you plan to work in food systems in the future, they can absolutely help to support!
I definitely would recommend this class to other people. Its super important and cool.

I do wish it was slightly less one sided and they talked about case studies of sustainable meat production, or at least discussed how that fits into a sustainable food system, because at times it felt too heavy on that "veganism woohoo!!!" type of education.
Yes, since it is very informative, ran by passionate instructors, and gives people great opportunities to hear from many different experts in the world of plant-based foods.

No, absolutely not. Do NOT take this class. I was warned by past 2nd years and did not listen. Because this is an applied innovation class where we work with clients to solve a problem, I thought that more of the focus of the class would be on how to actually solve those problems and gain important business skills such as: understanding market landscape and market size, how to do research for startup businesses or nonprofits, skill building on being professional when working with clients (which is something I felt my team really needed), designing a go-to-market strategy, etc. Instead, this class was mostly about why animal agriculture is bad and plant-centric diets are important, and taught us very very little about how to do the actual work we are supposed to do for our clients.

Because the teams are made up of a mix of undergrads and people from different graduate programs, I was the only MBA student on our team. We were working with a startup and asked to do market sizing, competitor landscape research, profitability analysis, create a pitch deck for funders, etc. No one on my team had any idea to do this, except me who had a very baseline idea. Instead of learning this in the class, I was responsible for TEACHING my team how to do it. I was also the only one with experience working with clients, and felt I had to teach my team how to be professional and responsive. It felt like herding cats, and a big part of the workload for me was effectively being a PM trying to wrangle undergrads. It was horrible.

I wish the course had focused more on actually building our business skills and teaching less experienced folks how to be professional, given it's a Haas class, and less focused on why it's important to be plant-centric. That's valuable info and it's good to have a few lectures on that, but not the whole class.

Yes for sure. If students were interested in plant-based movement or the food system in general this class gives a really good overview/mix of topics related to both of the field mentioned. There are graduate/MBA students that I didn't know this class combined.
Yes, but more for undergrad then MBA
Yes definitely, if you are passionate about challenging the societal norm and exploring food systems! But it would be better if in person.

This is an interesting applied innovation course, not a ton of outside work and cool guest speakers. I have changed my perspective on plant based eating quite a lot as a result of this class. A lot of the material is super interesting. Overall though, be prepared for the class to feel a bit like vegan propaganda at times - if youre aware and open to that, I think it's a great class and highly recommend.

Yes very much so. I have learned about foundations and habits that I will aspire to keep for the rest of my life surrounding my food choices. I think it's extremely important to learn about our food system and to inspire to make a change in the world.

Taking this class really depends on what you want to learn. I personally thought it would integrate business management and food systems a little more but that's my fault for not reading the description clearly. If someone wants to learn more about food systems and health impacts, they should definitely take it. It's also a good way to learn about food in general and since there aren't many of those classes at Berkeley, this would be a good one to take. yes
Yes, it was useful
I'd definitely recommend the instructor. Not sure about this course specifically. I like any opportunity to practice presenting. But also I think I wanted a bit more emphasis on AI tools.

Yes, I would recommend this class to those who want to get practice presenting and getting feedback to improve. The AI aspect wasn't very present but I appreciated being introduced to Gamma and benefited taking the class because of it.
I would recommend this course and instructor if you want a stress free enviroment to practice your presentation skills. Having two 8 hour classes to just practice is very nice and beneficial.

Yes, I think it's overall a helpful course, especially for someone who may not feel too comfortable with public speaking This is a good presentations class where you learn a lot about presenting better. If you're looking for more of an AI or efficiency focus, it falls short! Hence, my guess (strictly a guess only) is that the content might also overlap with other communications courses such Leadership Communications.
Yes sure as presentations are critical in business world
Instructor yes, course maybe not. I would have liked to spend more time with AI tools in the course. However, the human centered part took a bigger chunk of the course - I would say about 65%.

sections.goodFor: Anyone nervous about public speaking who wants safe, repeated practice with good feedback; called light lift, high reward and one of the few touchy-feely classes at Haas.
sections.notFor: Students expecting AI content - one says explicitly that the class focuses on personal human presentations, not AI, despite the title.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (9 mostly one-line comments). Described as a very light lift; class time goes to presentation practice, improv and instructor feedback. No assignments or hours described.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - presentations and instructor feedback are mentioned, but grading is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: One student notes the class is about human presentation skills rather than AI despite the course title. Thin evidence overall (9 short comments).
sections.quote: Yes, but this class focuses on personal human presentations not AI.
comments: Yes it was a great course
Yes! Overall very fun class. Even if you don't like public speaking, it's great practice.
Yes, but this class focuses on personal human presentations not AI.
Yes
Yes

Yes. Take this class. If you are nervous about public speaking, still take it -- so many people in the class were, and that's what made this class amazing (we all learned together in a safe space and were vulnerable with each other). Very light lift, high reward class, and one of the few touchy, feely classes at Haas.
Yes
Yes, amazing presenter, great teacher and gives good feedback on presentations! The course was well structured and worth my time
Yes! It's engaging, makes you speak publicly, pushes you outside your comfort zone, you learn improv etx

sections.goodFor: Students testing a VC or growth-equity career in climate who want real sourcing, diligence and check-writing experience, and who will commit fully alongside their team.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting structure, clear guidance or a low-effort group class; also flagged as risky if you need slower pacing or rewatchable material.
sections.workloadNote: Substantial and self-directed: less class time, more team time sourcing deals, emailing GPs and doing diligence - 'it felt like a job instead of a class.' Office hours carry much of the learning.
sections.gradingBasis: Team deal sourcing, thesis development and pitching, culminating in a real investment; explicit grading not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Little structure or clear guidance - you figure it out yourself (3); outcome depends heavily on teammates; one reports a chronic failure to turn mics on so recordings are unusable, plus fast pacing.
sections.quote: At times it felt like a job instead of a class which can be good or bad depending on what you're looking for.
comments: Yes, especially for those who are interested in Venture capital and Climate solutions. It is a way to practise how to source out deals and due diligence. I took this course to learn more about Climate solution and do something totally different from Finance and I find the class to be interesting.
Yes would recommend - great course well delivered and good guest speakers.

Yes definitely recommend – very practical hands on experience. Lot of learning by doing. There is also a dose of luck and networking involved in how smooth the class feels. A great place to learn more about growth stage climate investing and go through a proxy of sourcing and working through a deal thesis. Definitely go to office hours, a lot of the learning happens there

Will caution that it is not a small amount of work and the experience is highly dependent on your team/commitment, like all of these group classes. You get out of it what you put in but unfortunately you also get out of it what your teammates put in. (To that end, if you want an easy class where you don't have to try too much, please take a non- group class as this one is really hard for 1-2 people to carry and many of the folks taking this class care to try it on for a career and take it seriously)
Yes I would, it is a great way to get an idea of the job of a VC in a very impactful way.

Yes, I highly recommend this class - it's so unique! It lets you live as a climate growth equity investor for a few months without having to sign your life away to a firm. The learnings can be applied to many contexts within the climate space - i.e. VC/growth equity investing, project finance, private debt, founders, etc.
DEFINITELY! Great class to test out if you'd like VC
I would 100% recommend this course to a fellow student who wants to learn about climate and. VC through

application. The instructors do a great job of creating groups with diverse skillsets and while lots of work, the course leaves you with real world experience in pitching and sourcing deals. Matt and Todd are also wonderful people! One note is that much of the course is untraditional, less class time and more time spent in teams sourcing deals, emailing GPs, and more. At times it felt like a job instead of a class which can be good or bad depending on what you're looking for.
Yes! Great way to get a taste of a true berkeley experience/plug into SF VC community/try something new.

Take this class if you are interested in climate and new technologies. It is definitely a VC class but 90% of what you learn is related to climate investment more so than VC in general. The course also lets you learn about other clean investment vehicles without diving too deep into actual deal valuation etc.

If you have a learning disability I'd be wary of taking this class, they go through the material very quickly without a lot of time to engage with it. Additionally, they have a chronic issue of forgetting to put the mics on so you can't go back and watch the materials.
Yes, I would recommend both of them! They will help you understand the material and make time for you if you need it!

This course involves sourcing, picking, and winning a real live deal and giving them an actual check. You get out what you put in, so its highly valuable as a VC and climate practicum. All the teams find something cool, so make sure you can commit to putting your best foot forward!
It's been one of the most valuable courses I've taken at Haas. Requires a lot of work without clear guidance/ figuring it out by yourself (but that's work).
If you're interesting in VC/ Growth equity space, this class will give you the opportunity to actually do the work. Don't expect structure or a clear pathway.

Absolutely -- 100% the best university course I have ever taken and a life experience I will carry with me for the rest of my career. Its an incredible opportunity for students to participate in this class

sections.goodFor: Students needing an easy 3-credit toward a sustainability certificate, or wanting an accessible intro to emissions accounting, climate risk and corporate disclosures plus speaker access.
sections.notFor: Anyone chasing 'bang for your buck' in skills — content is thin for the credits, not business-school-focused, and at least one student says the material needs updating.
sections.workloadNote: Light — explicitly called an 'EASY 3-credit class.' Much of class time goes to guest speakers, and sessions often wrap up early; one student says the core content could fit in half the sessions.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: In a small sample (8): guest speakers used as filler and classes wrapped early (2), content stretched thin across too many sessions (1), material needs updating (1). Several recommend the instructor, not the course.
sections.quote: If you're looking for an EASY 3-credit class to fulfill your degree requirements... then this is it. But if you're looking for the most 'bang for your buck'... then this is NOT it.
comments: Professor Omar Romero-Hernandez is an absolute gem of a human - so genuinely nice and funny, which made the class enjoyable. If you're looking for an EASY 3-credit class to fulfill your degree requirements (i.e. sustainability certificate), then this is it. But if you're looking for the most "bang for your buck" (gaining valuable knowledge and skills)... then this is NOT it. While some of the topics in the curriculum were interesting/helpful (emissions accounting, implementation of sustainability initiatives at companies, etc.) but it could have been covered in half as many classes. The rest was filled with guest speakers (some more interesting than others) and wrapping up class early.
I would definitely recommend the instructor, he is great. I am not sure if I would recommend the course.
Course is very interesting because you have a wide ranging of guest speakers and one is able to contextualize the week's material.
If content updated, yes!
Yes, I would recommend this instructor. He's exceedingly personable and understanding.
Yes

Yes, but it's not a business school-focused class. I think it's a helpful intro to climate risk and disclosures, and Professor Omar is wonderful, but the introduction to various awesome guest speakers is what makes the class worthwhile. I would recommend this class to anyone interested in ssutainability! The course is what you make of it.

sections.goodFor: Anyone interested in startups, VC or early-stage investing - and students who are merely curious; several call it the class you cannot leave Haas without taking.
sections.notFor: One student notes the cases skew heavily to B2B software with little B2C or non-software coverage; otherwise no commenter identifies who should avoid it.
sections.workloadNote: Repeatedly called relatively low lift for the return; case discussions with scheduled and surprise guest speakers, plus assignments students call worthwhile. Hours not stated.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; assignments and case discussion are mentioned but no weightings.
sections.redFlags: One of 21 notes heavy B2B software focus and wants more B2C/non-software examples; no other complaints recur.
sections.quote: Great course, brings in excellent and impressive speakers. Relatively light lift. The course focuses a lot on B2B software.
comments: Take it even if you are not sure wheather or not you are going to be an entrepreneur in the future

I would absolutely recommend this course. It was clear from the beginning that the professors were incredibly intentional in designing a truly exceptional learning experience. Every aspect - from the thoughtfully selected case discussions to the frameworks and material - felt directly relevant and applicable to real-world entrepreneurship. The guest speakers (both the scheduled ones and the surprise guest speakers!) brought invaluable insights, making the classroom even more exciting. This course not only deepened my understanding of entrepreneurial strategy and decision-making but also left me feeling genuinely inspired to apply the lessons beyond the classroom.
Yes! This class was amazing! The professors are fantastic, the assignments are worthwhile, and it's a relatively low lift with maximum return on your time.
Yes, this class help me understand entrepreneurship and VC at a baseline level that will help me further into my journey
I've recommended this course to everyone who will listen. This is the best class I've taken at Haas.
Yes, this is my favorite class and the professors are both so knowledgeable. a must-take class for anyone. Keep Jules on staff!!!

I would strongly recommend the Entrepreneurship course with Jules and Sharat. It feels like what I expected a business school course to be: fascinating cases, great instructors, and extraordinary guests to bring the cases to life. If you came to Haas to get into entrepreneurship or early-stage investing, you cannot leave without taking this class with these two.

Yes absolutely. The course was immensely valuable. The instructors' experiences, speakers, and case studies gave me a great appreciation for the different ways for entrepreneurs to create and capture value. I feel like I will reference these teachings in a few years when I begin my own venture.
Yes - great Applied Innovation course for those interested in entrepreneurship
Absolutely take this class! I think this course should be a core course for anyone in business school!

I'd definitely recommend this course — it's fun, engaging, and packed with interesting cases. The class discussions were always lively, the guest speakers were a great addition, and Jules'perspective from the VC world made the experience even more insightful
EXCELLENT COURSE.
I would recommend both
If you are an entrepreneur or are curious about it you must take this class. Amazing professors and guest speakers. This class is a must if you plan to be a founder
Yes! If you ever want to start a company or work at a startup.
One of the best courses at Haas, anyone remotely interested in startups, VC, or in general being a self-starter would benefit greatly from this class

Yes yes absolutely yes. If unsure, register first, join the first class, then decide. You would not regret it! I am already recommending 1yrs to take this course next year — many of us 2nd years are on an unofficial marketing campaign to get this class filled because it's added so much value to my MBA experience. This is by-far my favorite course because of the variety of hands-on skills one can build.
Yes! The best class so far
If you are interested at all in startups or VC, take this course. They bring in amazing speakers and cases are relevant for any future entrepreneur.

Great course, brings in excellent and impressive speakers. Relatively light lift. The course focuses a lot on B2B software. It makes sense but I would've liked to see some examples of more B2C & non-software related topics.
Yes - omg if you want to learn about practical entrepreneurship skills and mindset its so helpful!

sections.goodFor: Aspiring founders and investors who want direct access to Frederic Kerrest's Okta 0-to-IPO experience, his network, and stage-spanning guest speakers.
sections.notFor: Students wanting broad foundational entrepreneurship - one argues the course narrows to 'an AI wrapper that can raise VC funding'; cases are stale and overlap the core.

Definitely take this class. The community is awesome, and getting three units of credit to work on your own startup, with real time and resources to build momentum, is a pretty rare opportunity. The class also gives you credits for Lovable, AWS, Claude Pro, and other tools, which makes a real difference when you're building.

Compared to programs like Lean Launch Pad, which lean heavily on customer interviews alone with a tight weekly cadence of identical deliverables for every team, this is much more flexible. You'll still do customer discovery, but you'll also have the structure to leverage the newest AI tools and actually ship in parallel. Different startups can be at different stages — you can pivot, break up with your team and join a new one, start over, and run customer discovery and building in parallel. This structure also reflects how products are actually getting built today. Software is so much cheaper to ship now, so customer discovery and building can happen in parallel, not in the old waterfall sequence of research-then-build. The class mirrors how real startups operate, which makes the experience much more applicable to the real world. Progress is defined in terms of what's actually moving the needle for your team's specific venture, not busywork deliverables. It feels like a real incubator, not a academic checklist.

How the class is structured: you're making real progress every week. Class sessions usually open with an hour topic overview from the professors, followed by a guest speaker, and then dedicated mentoring time where you can get advice from the week's in person mentors and collaborate with teammates and other peers on whatever challenges you're working through. The mentor program is a real highlight. There's a deep roster of mentors brought in from a wide range of backgrounds and industries, and you have choice in who you work with. Combined with the peer collaboration in class, the community feels built in and there to support everyone.

Set your expectations going in: if you're looking for a tightly structured curriculum with a lot of rigorous frameworks, this may not be that. But if you come in thinking of it as a great incubator community led by Omri (who's an exceptional teacher and infuses life lessons alongside entrepreneurship lesson) you'll get a ton out of it. He's beloved for good reason. One signal of how inspiring this community is: about 20 of the 27 teams from this cohort are continuing their ventures past the end of the class. That speaks for itself. Heads up that it's a lot of work, plan for it to take meaningful time and energy. But if you're game for that, you'll learn a ton.

Even if you're not sure entrepreneurship is your long-term path, this class is still worth taking. With AI, the lines between PM, engineer, designer, and user researcher are collapsing, we may not even have separate roles for much longer, just "builders." This class is one of the best opportunities at Haas to practice being an "AI builder", wearing all those hats at once. You'll do real customer research, real building, and real iteration alongside teammates with different perspectives, with your ideas challenged by real customers. The broader skills: flexible thinking, customer empathy, the ability to pivot and learn from your learnings, humility, the willingness to try different creative approaches, are applicable far beyond entrepreneurship. I'd recommend this for anyone with curiosity about AI, entrepreneurship, product, or even just what it's like to spend a semester working with a team on a creative project. I highly recommend taking this class because it gives you the opportunity to actually build a product and learn through practice. However, I suggest that students come in with a validated idea (for example, already having done 20–30 customer interviews); otherwise, you may end up spending half of the course on customer discovery, while teams that start with a concrete idea can use the time to build and iterate on their product. I would even recommend taking Lean Launchpad, which focuses heavily on customer discovery, before this class so that you can get the most benefit from the experience.

Unlike many professors, you can tell that Tim has a deep level of hands-on expertise in negotiations. The course is remarkably engaging, practical, and useful. Each class and exercise is designed a different negotiation scenario you might encounter: salary negotiations, negotiating in a group setting, acting a mediator, negotiating over email, etc. Tim delivers useful frameworks and strategies for approaching each situation that can be easily understood and immediately deployed. You learn practical skills like how to ask meaningful questions to uncover the other party's underlying interests or defuse someone who's a combative negotiator. The most valuable class I took at Haas — I wish I had taken it sooner.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in social change, social impact or nonprofit consulting who want an inspiring instructor, a strong practitioner network, and frameworks not taught elsewhere at Haas.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a light 2-unit class, or who is not interested in consulting deliverables - one student says the syllabus should be upfront that assignments are consulting-skills heavy.
sections.workloadNote: More work than students expect for a 2-unit class; assignments are time-intensive consulting simulations (pick an org, diagnose an issue, build a deck, present as if to a client). First-time offering.
sections.gradingBasis: Consulting-style assignments: pick an organization, identify an issue, build a deck, present as if to a client; plus discussion.
sections.redFlags: First offering: 2-3 say structure was unclear week to week ('building the ship as it was floating') and workload exceeds a 2-unit class; assignments are consulting decks, irrelevant to one non-consulting student.
sections.quote: it seemed like Steve was building the ship as it was floating and so it was unclear to me and other students what to expect on a week to week basis
comments: Yes; the course was one of the best/if not the best course that I have taken at Haas. This was precisely because Steve was the instructor, not based on the course curriculum. The way he engaged the students and iterated his course design was truly remarkable. I could clearly see the dedication that he has provided in every lecture. The positive energy that he brought was truly contagious. Berkeley was lucky to have Steve teach the course for MBA students. Easily one of the best classes I've taken during my time here. The learning in this class is so broadly applicable (life, work, school, etc.) and the way that the course is taught, it will stick with you more than for other classes. Steve is an extremely charismatic, passionate, and caring individual - this came through in how he led the course and interacted with students. The time you invest in this class has an exceptional return. Even if you don't have an interest in going into social impact, you will have many takeaways from this class.
Yes

1000% - one of the most interesting courses I took at Haas. It is more work thank you think it will be but it's worthwhile and really close to what you'd do in the professional world. I almost think part of this class should either replace or be combined with the core biz comm class for FTMBA.
Yes, but if the class structure improves.

Steve is well-versed in social change work and community building. He provided tangible examples of the concepts covered in class and has built a community of practitioners who served as guest speakers and added a great deal of context to the material. Steve is empathetic and brings hopes to these topics of social change that can feel heavy and difficult to change. The case studies and frameworks he introduced were helpful in breaking down complex problems and provided deep insights into how to change hearts and minds. As far as the course as a whole, it seemed like Steve was building the ship as it was floating and so it was unclear to me and other students what to expect on a week to week basis or how the full picture fit together. I think this primarily due to the fact that it was his time teaching, but with time and having had this first experience I have hope that the course will improve. That said, I would recommend the course to other students. It was a great way to overview the history of social movements (though mostly from a US context) and think through our personal theories of change. Expect to do a bit more work than you might think (though expectations may be more clear with future iterations of the class and more teaching experience from Steve), but you will learn a lot and be among students with similar values.

YES. Steve is superb: extremely experienced, personable, and organized. This is one of my favorite classes at Haas, and I can't believe I got to take it. Steve treats students like professional peers, which means that learning happens at a higher level than many classes. Be prepared that it is a lot of work (though hopefully Steve will take feedback to improve that in later semesters), but the work is relevant and valuable. Take this class, get to know Steve and his phenomenal and inspiring network, and have a great time with the other awesome people this class attracts. Yes, absolutley! This should be a core class
YES 100% if you want to think about things in a new way and be truly inspired, that is.

Overall, I expected this course to be more focused on social change and less consulting skills heavy. If I were planning to be a consultant, particularly in the social impact space, I would have found this course immensely valuable. As it is, the assignments were a lot of work, and seemed to simulate consulting projects -- pick an organization, identify an issue, build a deck, and present in class as if to the client. Because I'm not planning to be a consultant of any kind, I didn't find these assignments to be as relevant to me. Therefore, I wish the assignments had been a bit more diversified, or that the syllabus had been more up front that the course is geared towards consultant skills. Absolutely take this class. Learning from Steve was the highlight of my semester, and I am so thankful I will have him in my network for life. This course will push you to think differently, and the assignment themselves are great learning opportunities. If you are a little curious in social change, take this course.

One of the BEST classes I have taken at Haas. Steve truly cares about all the students, the content is phenomenal, and there is a lot of interesting concepts that aren't taught in other classes. At times, it can be a lot of work, but he does it in the best interest of the students. He is open to feedback and really makes sure students are learning and growing. I think you should absolutely take this class if you are interested in social impact - Steve is giving with his network and provides helpful critiques that felt similar to what I have received in the real world. If you are interested in nonprofit consulting in particular I think this class could be helpful.

Steve is very knowledgeable about social change and is committed to his students. I learned a lot about inspiring, leading, and strategy from the lens of large scale social change. Steve is funny, self-aware, asks for feedback, and actually takes it into account in order to improve the course. He cares a lot about outcome and brings a wide range of guest speakers. This is my favorite class that I've taken and you will learn a lot despite it only being a 2 unit course. I would! As someone who has worked in social impact for a decade, I was surprised that most of the content we learned about was new to me! Steve is incredibly passionate, joyous, knowledgeable, and caring. He really wants everyone to succeed and become better people. Great professor and interesting class!

Steve is super inspiring and an optimist. He takes this work seriously and wants you to too. It's not a skate-by class, but it's more interesting and fulfilling if you put effort into the discussions and assignments. Expect to produce consulting-style recommendations for scaling a movement. These were time-intensive but really valuable assignments. 100% recommend taking this class. Steve Naga-Mai is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Very passionate about Social Change, and someone who brought 110% of himself to the classroom. You will learn a ton about how large scale social change happens. You will also learn of a very compelling model to live by--he is a great leader, communicator, and person. If you take the class and life of social change (to some capacity) seriously, this class can really have an impact on you.

rows.title: The Business of Energy Transition
rows.ghostNote: New full-term course on the business of the energy transition: markets, policy and infrastructure investment. The instructor's prior record is thin (two observations) but her earlier climate course was liked more than it was valued (worth 5.47 vs effectiveness 6.19).

comments: I really recommend this class. It's stressful and time-consuming with this weekly deadline to get 8 interviews (or as much as we can). But apart from that it's a very unique experience, interactive and a chance to have this learning on how to get out of the building. This class completed all my learning objectives and radically changed the way I would start any entrepreneurial journey now.
Yes i would, the instructors and the course are very well designed and will give you real world experience when doing customer discovery and building a business model for the startups

I would definitely recommend both instructors! I learned a lot from this class and believe there's a wide variety of projects to cater to your interests and still focus on customer discovery. I would also highly suggest speaking with the inventor/mentor about their availability/expectations when choosing your semester-long project.

Yes I will recommend but, also highlight that this course is intensive in term of hours spent. Sometimes it may take up to 10-11 hours per week. On average, due to smaller team of just 2- we had to spend more time to get things done. It became overwhelmed. Would be great to have more people to join the class.

I would definitely recommend this course and these awesome instructors. The class is extremely engaging, and the course itself makes you exposed to the methods needed to speak to people in industries. If you have any social anxiety about speaking to people and cold calling and emailing, this class will fix that through exposure and make you much more confident in yourself and your speaking abilities. It really teaches you the methods needed to learn about cool people, industries, and the problems in those industries. Highly highly recommend taking this course, but make sure you have a good trustworthy team because the time spent interviewing is quite a lot, so you need a good team to spread out work!
I would definitely recommend this course. I was able to gain a lot of experience and knowledge both from within and outside the class.
I would

The highlight of this course is to work with students outside of Haas and explore industries outside of software through rapid learning and interviews. I have not taken a course like this before and applying the Lean Startup methodology was a valuable experience in the context of a future startup.
Yes. It pushes you out of your comfort zone and the teachings are valuable

I would recommend, I learned so much from this class, this knowledge and the connections I have made are invaluable. Great course for learning how to do customer discovery interviews - will force you to push yourself to find and speak with people
It requires A LOT of effort for just a 2 credit course
Yes.

(1) The world needs more people who can translate scientific inventions into market! I haven't taken a science class since high school, and 12 years later, I was speaking to CXOs at synthetic biology companies. You can do it! It was very disappointing to see EVERY HAAS STUDENT except two drop the class. This is a Haas course, mind you. We're at the best research institution in the world! Why aren't everyone trying to learn more about cutting-edge patented technologies?

(2) Any Lean Business Canvas courses - I highly recommend. You learn so much about how to find and talk to people. Even the most introverted humans that don't want to talk to anyone at all would benefit from this class, just by becoming used to finding and talking to people and learning from them.
Yes I will recommend. This course helps us to understand customer discovery and market research in a very practical way.

sections.goodFor: Students who want hands-on lean-startup and customer-discovery practice, including anyone nervous about cold outreach, since the class forces you out of the building and builds real interviewing confidence, networking, and cross-campus teamwork.
sections.notFor: Anyone without weekly time to run interviews all semester; one commenter also objected to a required roughly $100 software fee for course content they felt should be free on bCourses.
