sections.redFlags: Recurring (5+ comments): the interview quota makes the time commitment disproportionate to 2 credits. One-off complaints: a required ~$100 software purchase for class content, and small teams being stretched thin.
sections.quote: Yes. It pushes you out of your comfort zone and the teachings are valuable
comments: Yes great learning experience and very interactive

I would recommend the course for experience in customer discovery. However, I would inform them they must pay $100 for software to access the class content and videos. I think this model is unfair. I see the value in paying for Innovations Within for the business canvas features, however, I believe the presentations and videos to prepare for class should be published on Bcourses.

I would recommend to a fellow student given it is an excellent introduction to the lean process, however it is very customer discovery interview heavy and perhaps this took away from some of the learning given how much time it required outside of class.
Yes- 10/10. probably the only Haas class you need to take as a non-MBA student.
Yes. Mostly because it is practical. I learnt a lot. Being an introvert, it was challenging in a good way to go out and talk to people. I also got to meet new people and make new friends
Yes as long as you have time during the semester to do the interviews
Course is great for networking opportunities as it forces you to be out there and find connections for interviews.
Yes, absolutely! Lean launchpad is a great course to get the true startup feel. Resulting in amazing experience and substantial learnings.

Yes, but only if the student was serious about the topic. I found lean launchpad to be one of the most enriching experiences of my academic career. It carries a true sense of importance, and the people you're working with are fantastic.

The best class I've taken at Haas. LLP is an intense and very effective crash course to learn entrepreneurship. It's an incredibly hands on experience that does not feel at all like a traditional class. The teaching team is also incredibly knowledgeable.

I would highly recommend this class to students who are interested in entrepreneurship because it is invaluable. It is the most well-resourced class that I have ever taken in my life. There are a plethora of professors and mentors provided to each team which helps them navigate the customer discovery process.
Absolutely! Take this class even if you have an inkling of an interest in developing an idea. Hands down one of the most humbling, challenging yet rewarding classes I have taken at Haas.
Definitely yes! Best class of Haas by far.
I would recommend this course, if you have the time and energy to do a TON of work.

Yes, very interesting learning experience! Its a ton of work (could be spending 10-20hrs/week outside class) but learn a lot about yourself, working in stressful situations, working with different teammate personalities, how to approach a complex problem or unknown problem, etc. Overall a fun experience and you wont regret taking the class.

I would recommend these instructors and this course to fellow students, with two thumbs up for the instructors. I do think there could be efficiency gains in learning by dropping some of the Osterwalder stuff and by slightly reducing the interview requirements around the time for building MVPs. This class required a ton of work and resulted in a ton of learning, but the work to learning output was not always maximally efficient. Overall I think the class has been the best learning experience I've had at Haas. It's fantastic for aspiring entrepreneurs and Product Managers alike, but could still be improved with only slight changes.

Everyone should take this class at some point in their life! Even for people who don't want to start a company, the class teaches you an extremely helpful methodology for any project or innovation. 100% recommended! But be ready to work a lot!
Yes, if you are willing to spend many hours on this class and are okay with learning the course concepts on your own time.
No, if you are the type of person that likes to have a set syllabus, and grading expectations for the course as no grading criteria has ever been discussed during the course.

This is a really hand on and very rigorous entrepreneurship class. I cannot think of a better group of instructors and format for delivering the content of this class. Kudos to the teaching team for all their support!

I would recommend taking this course, as long as you have a strong team. Your team doesn't have to be best friends; however, you all need to have similar goals and commitments to the project. Lean Launchpad was applied learning at its finest. I personally think that I learned more about start-ups skills by taking this course than I would've had I interned at a start-up while in school. I'll be taking a number of this course's lessons with me past-Haas. Do yourself a favor and take this class. This class is a MUST if you plan to go down the entrepreneurship route. It's a lot of work but the leanings are 10x. You will come out very satisfied at the end of the class. Also, it's the only class at Haas where you have 3 instructors for entire class and mentors assigned to each group. Both the instructors and mentors have lots of experience working in the start-up ecosystem.
I also highly recommend this class even if you don't plan to do entrepreneurship. Lean methodologies learned in this class can be applied to any idea or project at big corporations

I would 100000% recommend this course to anyone who wants to know what it takes to build a startup from scratch. Whether you go work at a startup or consulting, this course will give you lessons that you can apply in your career across the board including talking to customers, learning through iterating and understanding what it takes to achieve product–market fit. I 10x more recommend this course to folks who want to stay in the tech ecosystem either as an operator or an investor.

The Lean Launch Pad... is something that will define your semester. You must go into it fully committed and passionate about the core driving force of your idea, but not the idea itself. Because you are going to put in more effort into this course than anything else in Haas, and your idea WILL be different at the end of it all. Without passion, you are going to dread each week, struggling to source and complete 10 interviews. With passion, you will be desperate (in a good way) to hear that next piece of feedback or advice from your potential customers. So, go into this experience fully prepared to lock in and commit with your team to make the most out of this limited and extremely valuable time you have to explore an idea.

I regret to say that I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this particular class, due to a number of pertinent reasons. My primary concern stems from the problematic methodology used in team formation. It appears that the course creators did not fully appreciate the constraints, such as limited commitment or time availability, that MBA students often face. These issues can significantly impede the effective engagement in a demanding course such as this.

Despite the fact that you may be fortunate enough to secure a team of committed individuals, another issue arises – the lack of education on how to effectively collaborate. The course consistently challenges students to work together on a weekly basis, yet it fails to provide the necessary tools and techniques to accomplish this successfully. As a consequence, the individual chosen to lead the team, whether on a rotating basis or as a permanent role, is subjected to an unfair additional burden. The workload can quickly become overwhelming.

Another pivotal issue lies in the insufficient direction provided to the teams. This is particularly alarming given the diverse backgrounds of the participants. I speak from experience when I say that even large consulting firms and seasoned management require guidance in structuring team operations. Unfortunately, this course does not offer such assistance.

Problem–solving and synthesizing valuable insights from interviews are integral parts of any project, yet the course fails to adequately guide students in these areas. While these skills can indeed be taught, and there are knowledgeable individuals, including peers, who could offer help, the teaching staff and the class structure largely overlook this necessity. Instead, a great deal of time is suboptimally spent requiring students to provide feedback on each other's presentations.

In reality, only a fraction of the comments made prove to be useful. As the course advances, these critiques often become an afterthought. The truth is, no one understands your project as well as you do. Unless the person providing feedback is a seasoned expert in your business domain, their contributions may be limited.

I question the course's strategy of forcing students to comment on unrelated topics. Instead, why not encourage us to leverage our networks, which is a fundamental aspect of the MBA experience? Sharing our networks could yield far more valuable insights and facilitate more meaningful interactions among students.

Despite its shortcomings, I believe this course has potential. However, it leaves much to be desired in terms of effectiveness. The lessons I gleaned from this experience could have been delivered in a more condensed format, such as a weekend class. Additionally, the underwhelming outcomes produced by my classmates only further underline my concerns.

In conclusion, while the course could potentially be a valuable learning experience, it requires significant improvements in areas such as team formation, collaborative skills training, problem–solving guidance, and effective use of class time and resources. Until these issues are addressed, I find it difficult to recommend this class.

I would but I would highly encourage the teaching staff to make it clear to students that this model isn't necessarily compatible with deep tech. The commercialization process is different and you should be encouraged to think about what kinds of industries this model works well in. While some lessons are universal, the class is miles easier when focused on particular kinds of solutions. Otherwise, hardware/deeptech startups run around looking for PMF for way too long.
Yes.
This is definitely the heaviest course load of any class at Haas but also the most worthwhile of any I've taken or expect to take. Super thankful to have gone through this experience

I would recommend the class, but only to people who have SAAS or other software/service ideas. The class is not well- suited for climate tech or hardware in general, or maybe the instructors are just not used to it.

If you are interested in entrepreneurship, this is THE course to take. It has completely transformed the way I think about starting a business. I started the course thinking that I have the best idea in the world, but as the team interacted with users and instructors, and used the canvas to look at the idea from various angles, I had a good reality check. At the end, I felt, thank god I didn't start building this immediately and iterate it on a high fidelity MVP! While I didn't come out of this with a business, it has equipped me with the key toolset to quickly strip down an idea and understand what needs to be explored in order and where to move the business. It was a TON of work, but I highly recommend it!

I would recommend this course if you are looking to start a business or have a business idea in the bag and do not have any business background. This course will set you off in a practical way and help you understand if your idea is viable or not through your learnings. Expect lots of hours of learning outside classroom through interviews. The AI platform made idea generation seamless and give more room to learning and helping think in the right direction.

Your biggest strengths in this class is your team. Make sure you are on a team that are collectively as enthusiastic as you are about the course and your idea. You will be working a lot with your team, make sure you have a diverse team with different skill sets and experience. This will enrich your experience.

Overall it's a practical heavy class and deserves giving your best if you are really interested in entrepreneurship. This course was not what I expected. It is not so much teaching you how to launch a start-up, as teaching you how to properly learn about a market. There are many, many interviews which you have to do - so consider whether the course is worth it for you or not. If you're just trying to learn about start-ups and the process, then this probably isn't it. If you're dedicated to an idea that you really want to pursue, then this course is more helpful

If you truly want to experience the uncertainty, ambiguity, and struggles of starting something, then this course is definitely for you. Keep in mind that your idea at the end of the class will likely be different from the one you start with. Therefore, the focus of the class is more on learning throughout the process, developing leadership and teamwork skills, and working under pressure.
It highly depends on the student's goals and motivations. It is only a useful class for people serious about exploring entrepreneurship.
I would highly recommend - even if it doesn't lead to a great idea, it will teach you many important skills you'll need as a business professional

I would 100% recommend this course to future students, especially those who are interested in entrepreneurship. The learning from this class makes most of the other courses I've taken feel like a walk in the park. The experience is so hands-on: startup team dynamics, talking to customers, refining business model, and more.

I would, however, recommend that people sign up in their second year instead of first for two reasons: (1) A lot of what you do and knowledge applied in this class come from other fundamental subjects: finance, marketing, operations, and soft skills. I think you can get more out of this class if you do this class after you've gotten more exposure to different subjects. (2) Many people are doing both internship recruiting the second semester of first year. This makes the class pretty stressful sometimes and harder to get the most out of it. You'd be doing yourself a favor by taking this class in your final semester (assuming you have a return offer from summer internship or some plan secured by then).

sections.goodFor: Students seriously considering founding a company, ideally with an idea their whole team believes in and access to real customers. Great interview fodder - people ask about the 100+ interviews.
sections.notFor: Anyone lukewarm about their idea or team, recruiting heavily, or hoping to actually build a revenue business - two call it an academic exercise, and it doesn't teach the quant side of startups.
sections.workloadNote: Multiple students independently report 15-20 hours a week, every week, sustained across the term: 100+ customer interviews, weekly presentations, plus ad-hoc requests. Brutal alongside recruiting.
sections.gradingBasis: weekly team presentations and customer-interview progress tracked in the course tool Glidr
sections.redFlags: Instructors are the weak point (3): 'awesome course, despite the instructors', lectures not up to date, obsession with the Glidr tool, presentation-heavy with limited guidance. Bad team or lukewarm idea = huge drag (4).
sections.quote: This is an awesome course, despite the instructors. The course design absolutely nailed it - it motivates every one of the 40 people in class to put 15-20 hours a week, every week.
comments: I would recommend this course! it helped me figure out whether or not entrepreneurship is for me, taught me how to have hard conversations and pushed me beyond my limits.

I would recommend this if you are interesting from learning from and meeting with incredibly accomplished people, but keep in mind that this really is /a lot/ of work outside of class and you need to love your team and have some interest in your ideas.

Overall, I remain unconvinced of whether the Lean Launchpad model is the best way to start actually establishing a real, revenue earning business. If you are a student who doesn't have a business idea, or has no idea where to start on their entrepreneurship journey, this class may be what you need to launch you.
yes this course is awesome.
Absolutely

This is an awesome course, despite the instructors. The course design absolutely nailed it - it motivates every one of the 40 people in class to put 15-20 hours a week, every week. It ensured that everyone learned by doing and practicing, and everyone was engaged in lectures, office hours, presentations etc. Over the years, the course has really perfected these aspects and if you want to be an entrepreneur, you'll definitely learn a lot!

That said, some things could make this course even better. Like more up to date lectures and much less obsession with the course tool, Glidr. The instructors, especially the lead instructor Jim, could've really stepped up. I feel mixed about this. It is a phenomenal opportunity to explore the startup world BUT it was very presentation heavy with limited guidance. I think the workload wasn't even the issue - I would do all the work and still appreciate doing something more than listening to presentations and giving presentations.
I would but would be very clear that this is not a course meant to build your business. This is an academic exercise. If you actually want to build a business, you don't need to take this course.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this to others, with the caveat that it requires a significant amount of work. However, for those who are ready to put in the effort, it can be incredibly valuable, especially for anyone looking to learn about entrepreneurship. As someone coming from a different country, this has definitely been the best experience so far!
Yes, it's a great class for developing grit and character.
yah

Absolutely! This was hands down the best class I've taken at Haas. It pushed us to talk to real users, test our assumptions, and make meaningful progress every single week. I only wish we had more time to build, by the time we gained confidence in our direction, the quarter was almost over. Highly recommend for anyone serious about entrepreneurship.

yes, i would only recommend it for students who are seriously thinking of starting a company due to the time commitment. But if you fall into this group this is invaluable and you will feel ready to do it once complete. I would absolutley recommend this class to others. This is what I have talked most about in interviews even when its a small one liner on my CV, companies and people pick it out and want to learn more about your 100+ customer interviews

I would recommend this class to someone who has an idea that they realistically think they can bring to the market. I will also advise that you try solving a problem where you have access to the customers you will be helping. That will make the class much more straightforward. If you have a good idea that you would like to make real, this is a good place to start. If you are applying just to be in the class or entering with an idea that all 5 members of your team are not 100% on board with, the class will be very challenging.
ABSOLUTELY. This is probably the most meaningful class I have taken at Berkeley. If you want to start a business of any sort, this is the class for you.
Yes, it is such a unique course. I highly recommend everyone experiences it.

If you have an idea you're excited about, and a team you work well with, this is a great course. If you're only lukewarm about your idea, change that quickly because it can be a huge drag. I was in the lucky camp, and this course is now a launching pad for me to actually start businesses with classmates. My goals were to make entrepreneurship less intimidating and to practice execution over perfection. This course fulfilled both of these requirements for me! Yes absolutely. The course is basically simulating the early stages of entrepreneurial experience and having such a course gives students a real picture of potential real-world challenges when they start their own venture. Class workload is 20 hours a week. Not very useful for the quant part of understanding a startup. Good for problem discovery

Absolutely take it if you want to be an entrepreneur or at least want to test the hypothesis of whether you want to be an entrepreneur. It will confirm or disconfirm that hypothesis. This will be the most demanding course you take at Haas -- do not take it unless you are absolutely committed. But a spot in this class is incredibly valuable -- take it seriously and make the most of your experience.

Yes I will receommend the course. However, please note that doing this course along with recruitment is really challenging. It is easily more that 10 hours a week and on top of that their can be ad-hoc request. Not each class will be worth it. Please do proper due-deligence to form your teams- you want a team with whom you can have fun. Yes! It has been my favorite class I have taken at Berkeley so far.
Yes, but seriously its 20 hours. you may not have a good team and it will be very hard. But it was worth it. One of the hardest but most rewarding courses you can take.

This class is so practical than any other classes I have taken. It's more engaging but very difficult. I would surely recommend to someone who want get into entrepreneurship. This class provides all you need to build a startup and I feel so confident building a startup any time soon
Get out of the building! Best class to learn how to actually make change. I've never felt more challenged, but I've learned a life long lesson.

Maybe...it was an interesting course on climate and held a lot of potential, but I felt that it was a bit unorganized, perhaps because this was the first time it was offered so the kinks just need to be worked out. Kate Gordon is amazing professor but I was not impressed with Libby Schaaf, but the class was worth taking just for Kate alone.
Yes - interesting content! Could improve structure of assignments and discussions.
Incredible gathering of all the students interested in the space. I learned a lot from other students & a ton from the speakers

I would recommend if you are interested in California's green initiatives. I feel like the class is very California focused. I would recommend both lecturers but not this class until there was a major overhaul to the curriculum to be broadly applicable to those interested in facilitating a more rapid climate transition.
Yes, but with caveats. Not a class to "learn" from climate change. It is more a class to discuss current/past sustainability efforts

I would recommend this course with reservations. If you are looking for a course where you can have interesting discussion with your classmates about select aspects of policy, infrastructure, and finance as they relate to climate, I would recommend this course. If you are looking for a course that has a comprehensive throughline that teaches you about how to leverage policy to affect climate change, this class might not be for you.
100%. It serves as a fantastic survey of how climate, politics, and finance intersect and is taught by one of Berkeley's biggest climate experts, Kate Gordon, and a great speaker in Libby Schaff.

This class is great for understanding how public and private actors approach climate. Guest speakers are great and the professors know a ton and have a lot of great experiences to share. Assumes intermediate level understanding of climate so do not recommend to "newbies."

The course felt way too specific to California and the intricacies of various California laws. While the content was really interesting and so were the guest speakers it often felt like the things that we were learning just wouldn't be relevant overtime as we expand our careers beyond California. I would have loved more time spent on public and private partnerships.

This was a great class to take from experts in the field of enacting sustainability measures. I'd recommend this for folks who have a background in sustainability and want to learn about how policy measures can make a difference in solving for climate change.
I will recommend the course and the professors. The course mostly focuses in California but professors bring a great set of speakers and multiple lessons learned from their past work experience

This is a good class to learn more about politics of financing infrastructure projects in California. Most of the classes were focused on specific state policies and how them impact the development of projects (both promoting or stifling them).

I would definitely recommend this course. I learned a ton about areas I didn't realize were so interesting – how local governments finance climate resilience projects, how climate lobbying works, and so much about the state of California's approach to infrastructure, air quality, and more. I took it at the same time as Business Models for Social Impact, and there were some cool parallels to be drawn. Kate Gordon is a POWERHOUSE. Recommend!
Yes!

I would highly recommend this course. I think it is fantastic if you are new to the climate space or well informed. I also appreciated the focus on multilevel actions - from global policies to municipal action.

Yes, thank you so much for teaching this class. I think it brought together all types of students who were interested in the climate space and gave us an opportunity to talk about the non-science aspects of climate change. I really enjoyed the readings, and Kate was such an engaging professor and an amazing person to know in the climate space.
I do not recommend, the course was chaotic and too focused on California

Yes of course. All the climate fellow should take this course and this is valuable resource for them best understanding.. Yes, I've recommended the class to lots of 1st year students who are interested in climate or just curious to learn about it. This is my first climate class, and I feel so rewarding and thinking about masking a impact in my career This class is a worthwhile foray into climate action because--unlike many sustainability focused courses at Berkeley-- the policy focus imbues it with a sense of pragmatism. Taught by real practitioners, it was a worthwhile elective. Easy lift and great guest speakers if it fits in your schedule. Not very applicable learnings though.
Yes definitely! You will learn about the capital stacks, policy initiatives and international/local implications about climate mitigation/adaptation from two great teachers.

Highly recommend. Kate Gordon provides a insightful and incisive overview of the broad policy and finance landscape; insights into specific frameworks, approaches, and policy/finance tools; and concrete examples of what has
worked/not worked in real life, and Libby Schaaf sheds light on what this means at the local level
Yes! Great class with great professors
Yes! A great overview of climate topics

sections.goodFor: Students who care about climate policy and systems change and want a broad primer plus access to an exceptional slate of guest speakers and the Berkeley climate community.
sections.notFor: Anyone drawn by the 'Finance & Infrastructure' in the title — not emphasized. Students who've taken several climate classes find it repetitive; law school climate classes give more per credit.
sections.workloadNote: 'Very reasonable workload,' though one notes you must spend extra energy speaking up in class. Format is guest speakers plus discussion; assignments were criticized as unclear.
sections.gradingBasis: Class discussion/participation and assignments; several note assignments lacked clarity. Weights not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Title oversells finance/infrastructure (2); lacks focus and sequence, 'bites off too much' (3); assignments unclear (2); Libby less prepared than Kate (1); 1 says real insight comes from classmates, not profs.
sections.quote: Fantastic guest speakers. Very reasonable workload. Just super broad topic lacking a clear focus, sequence, and takeaway... Climate, infra, politics, and finance is sort of everything
comments: Absolutely worthwhile class to link together material that isnt otherwise inherently connected and through this class and the guest speakers we found a way to make remarkably intuitive connections to understand the ultimate goal of how to behave in a climate adapting world.

If you really care about climate policy, yes. Not so much if you're attracted to the "Finance and Infrastructure" parts of the title, which are not emphasized. Interesting class to get a feel for what a Public Policy degree feels like. Very theoretical, and fun class discussions. The real insights come from all the climate-interested people enrolled in the class rather than the profs themselves.

Maybe - if you have deep knowledge of the space and want to go deeper, but you have to be able to really make the experience into what you need it to be because it's a little all over the place as currently designed.

Yes, I would recommend this course to individuals interested in understanding the relevance of climate change and systems change. We dive into hairy problems and have an open dialogue where many viewpoints are welcomed. Great speakers who are experts in their fields.
YES - this class provides a holistic understanding of the challenges and solutions around climate change.

The course is more suitable for students who have much experience in climate and are planning to pursue a career in this path. Sutdents who just want to learn sth in Climate may find the course a bit dry...

I would absolutely recommend this class, especially as a person who had very little knowledge about approaching climate change from a policy and organizational lens. This class takes a broad approach which is great for people who are seeking to broaden their aperture in the climate space.

I would recommend this course to another student. It is a really engaging class grounded in real-world examples. Both professors are very engaged and willing to meet with students to gain a deeper understanding of course content. This course provides a high level overview of many different climate topics and Isa good primer for the space. What you get out of the course is what you put in to it, and it could be just that you got to hear from a lot of really cool people about really cool stuff, or that you took personal initiative to deep dive into one area of the course and came away with a really good understanding of that topic.

This is a good class for getting a foundation in climate infrastructure and considerations. The topics covered in class were helpful for understanding the landscape of government interventions and financing instruments. Kate was a more engaging and prepared lecturer than Libby, but Libby often had an interesting perspective given her role as former Mayor Oakland. The two were a good balance, but a few improvements to the class like clearer assignments would have improved the overall course experience.
most phenomenal course I took at Haas. Be prepared to work a little, and spend extra energy speaking up in class as this is more challenging than typical MBA courses.

Totally recommend - for people who want to learn about climate, it's a great place to hear about the most topical discussions going on at the global, federal and state level. For students with more experience in climate, it's a relatively laid-back class where you can come, have good conversations, hear from and meet amazing speakers and connect with the broader Berkeley climate community.

Yes, I would. Great professors with cool experiences. Fantastic guest speakers. Very reasonable workload. Just super broad topic lacking a clear focus, sequence, and takeaway... Climate, infra, politics, and finance is sort of everything... bites off too much.

I would definitely recommend this course! Kate and Libby bring in an extraordinary slate of speakers and have great experience to share with students. If you're interested in the subject matter, I think it's a must-take.

Yes. It's a good politics and sustainability course. However, I think I'd take a law school climate class over this if I had already taken several climate classes (my case), as some of the information from this class was repetitive from other classes. If you haven't taken many climate classes, you definitely would take this if you're interested in the political side. Note that it focused a lot on CA and the US, but good to have the basis/ model and know how to expand that out to other regions or countries. The law school climate classes just give you a better marginal benefit per credit hour than this class with less duplicative information if you've already taken many business school climate classes. Yes - interesting to see policy and business views come together.

Yes — this course is one of the few that truly connects climate policy, financing, and infrastructure in a way that feels both practical and immediately relevant to real-world challenges. Kate Gordon and Libby Schaaf create an engaging environment that blends policy insight with lived experience, making the class valuable for anyone interested in the intersection of climate and decision-making.
Yes, if you are willing to spend many hours on this class and are okay with learning the course concepts on your own time.
No, if you are the type of person that likes to have a set syllabus, and grading expectations for the course as no grading criteria has ever been discussed during the course.

This is a really hand on and very rigorous entrepreneurship class. I cannot think of a better group of instructors and format for delivering the content of this class. Kudos to the teaching team for all their support!

Everyone should take this class at some point in their life! Even for people who don't want to start a company, the class teaches you an extremely helpful methodology for any project or innovation. 100% recommended! But be ready to work a lot!

I would recommend these instructors and this course to fellow students, with two thumbs up for the instructors. I do think there could be efficiency gains in learning by dropping some of the Osterwalder stuff and by slightly reducing the interview requirements around the time for building MVPs. This class required a ton of work and resulted in a ton of learning, but the work to learning output was not always maximally efficient. Overall I think the class has been the best learning experience I've had at Haas. It's fantastic for aspiring entrepreneurs and Product Managers alike, but could still be improved with only slight changes.

Yes, very interesting learning experience! Its a ton of work (could be spending 10-20hrs/week outside class) but learn a lot about yourself, working in stressful situations, working with different teammate personalities, how to approach a complex problem or unknown problem, etc. Overall a fun experience and you wont regret taking the class.

I would highly recommend this class to students who are interested in entrepreneurship because it is invaluable. It is the most well-resourced class that I have ever taken in my life. There are a plethora of professors and mentors provided to each team which helps them navigate the customer discovery process.
I would recommend this course, if you have the time and energy to do a TON of work.
Absolutely! Take this class even if you have an inkling of an interest in developing an idea. Hands down one of the most humbling, challenging yet rewarding classes I have taken at Haas.

The best class I've taken at Haas. LLP is an intense and very effective crash course to learn entrepreneurship. It's an incredibly hands on experience that does not feel at all like a traditional class. The teaching team is also incredibly knowledgeable.

I would recommend taking this course, as long as you have a strong team. Your team doesn't have to be best friends; however, you all need to have similar goals and commitments to the project. Lean Launchpad was applied learning at its finest. I personally think that I learned more about start-ups skills by taking this course than I would've had I interned at a start-up while in school. I'll be taking a number of this course's lessons with me past-Haas. Yes, but only if the student was serious about the topic. I found lean launchpad to be one of the most enriching experiences of my academic career. It carries a true sense of importance, and the people you're working with are fantastic.
Definitely yes! Best class of Haas by far.
Yes, absolutely! Lean launchpad is a great course to get the true startup feel. Resulting in amazing experience and substantial learnings.

Do yourself a favor and take this class. This class is a MUST if you plan to go down the entrepreneurship route. It's a lot of work but the leanings are 10x. You will come out very satisfied at the end of the class. Also, it's the only class at Haas where you have 3 instructors for entire class and mentors assigned to each group. Both the instructors and mentors have lots of experience working in the start-up ecosystem.
I also highly recommend this class even if you don't plan to do entrepreneurship. Lean methodologies learned in this class can be applied to any idea or project at big corporations

I would 100000% recommend this course to anyone who wants to know what it takes to build a startup from scratch. Whether you go work at a startup or consulting, this course will give you lessons that you can apply in your career across the board including talking to customers, learning through iterating and understanding what it takes to achieve product–market fit. I 10x more recommend this course to folks who want to stay in the tech ecosystem either as an operator or an investor.

The Lean Launch Pad... is something that will define your semester. You must go into it fully committed and passionate about the core driving force of your idea, but not the idea itself. Because you are going to put in more effort into this course than anything else in Haas, and your idea WILL be different at the end of it all. Without passion, you are going to dread each week, struggling to source and complete 10 interviews. With passion, you will be desperate (in a good way) to hear that next piece of feedback or advice from your potential customers. So, go into this experience fully prepared to lock in and commit with your team to make the most out of this limited and extremely valuable time you have to explore an idea.

I regret to say that I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this particular class, due to a number of pertinent reasons. My primary concern stems from the problematic methodology used in team formation. It appears that the course creators did not fully appreciate the constraints, such as limited commitment or time availability, that MBA students often face. These issues can significantly impede the effective engagement in a demanding course such as this.

Despite the fact that you may be fortunate enough to secure a team of committed individuals, another issue arises – the lack of education on how to effectively collaborate. The course consistently challenges students to work together on a weekly basis, yet it fails to provide the necessary tools and techniques to accomplish this successfully. As a consequence, the individual chosen to lead the team, whether on a rotating basis or as a permanent role, is subjected to an unfair additional burden. The workload can quickly become overwhelming.

Another pivotal issue lies in the insufficient direction provided to the teams. This is particularly alarming given the diverse backgrounds of the participants. I speak from experience when I say that even large consulting firms and seasoned management require guidance in structuring team operations. Unfortunately, this course does not offer such assistance.

Problem–solving and synthesizing valuable insights from interviews are integral parts of any project, yet the course fails to adequately guide students in these areas. While these skills can indeed be taught, and there are knowledgeable individuals, including peers, who could offer help, the teaching staff and the class structure largely overlook this necessity. Instead, a great deal of time is suboptimally spent requiring students to provide feedback on each other's presentations.

In reality, only a fraction of the comments made prove to be useful. As the course advances, these critiques often become an afterthought. The truth is, no one understands your project as well as you do. Unless the person providing feedback is a seasoned expert in your business domain, their contributions may be limited.

I question the course's strategy of forcing students to comment on unrelated topics. Instead, why not encourage us to leverage our networks, which is a fundamental aspect of the MBA experience? Sharing our networks could yield far more valuable insights and facilitate more meaningful interactions among students.

Despite its shortcomings, I believe this course has potential. However, it leaves much to be desired in terms of effectiveness. The lessons I gleaned from this experience could have been delivered in a more condensed format, such as a weekend class. Additionally, the underwhelming outcomes produced by my classmates only further underline my concerns.

In conclusion, while the course could potentially be a valuable learning experience, it requires significant improvements in areas such as team formation, collaborative skills training, problem–solving guidance, and effective use of class time and resources. Until these issues are addressed, I find it difficult to recommend this class.

I would but I would highly encourage the teaching staff to make it clear to students that this model isn't necessarily compatible with deep tech. The commercialization process is different and you should be encouraged to think about what kinds of industries this model works well in. While some lessons are universal, the class is miles easier when focused on particular kinds of solutions. Otherwise, hardware/deeptech startups run around looking for PMF for way too long.
Yes.
This is definitely the heaviest course load of any class at Haas but also the most worthwhile of any I've taken or expect to take. Super thankful to have gone through this experience

I would recommend the class, but only to people who have SAAS or other software/service ideas. The class is not well- suited for climate tech or hardware in general, or maybe the instructors are just not used to it.

If you are interested in entrepreneurship, this is THE course to take. It has completely transformed the way I think about starting a business. I started the course thinking that I have the best idea in the world, but as the team interacted with users and instructors, and used the canvas to look at the idea from various angles, I had a good reality check. At the end, I felt, thank god I didn't start building this immediately and iterate it on a high fidelity MVP! While I didn't come out of this with a business, it has equipped me with the key toolset to quickly strip down an idea and understand what needs to be explored in order and where to move the business. It was a TON of work, but I highly recommend it!

I would recommend this course if you are looking to start a business or have a business idea in the bag and do not have any business background. This course will set you off in a practical way and help you understand if your idea is viable or not through your learnings. Expect lots of hours of learning outside classroom through interviews. The AI platform made idea generation seamless and give more room to learning and helping think in the right direction.

Your biggest strengths in this class is your team. Make sure you are on a team that are collectively as enthusiastic as you are about the course and your idea. You will be working a lot with your team, make sure you have a diverse team with different skill sets and experience. This will enrich your experience.

Overall it's a practical heavy class and deserves giving your best if you are really interested in entrepreneurship. This course was not what I expected. It is not so much teaching you how to launch a start-up, as teaching you how to properly learn about a market. There are many, many interviews which you have to do - so consider whether the course is worth it for you or not. If you're just trying to learn about start-ups and the process, then this probably isn't it. If you're dedicated to an idea that you really want to pursue, then this course is more helpful

If you truly want to experience the uncertainty, ambiguity, and struggles of starting something, then this course is definitely for you. Keep in mind that your idea at the end of the class will likely be different from the one you start with. Therefore, the focus of the class is more on learning throughout the process, developing leadership and teamwork skills, and working under pressure.
It highly depends on the student's goals and motivations. It is only a useful class for people serious about exploring entrepreneurship.
I would highly recommend - even if it doesn't lead to a great idea, it will teach you many important skills you'll need as a business professional

I would 100% recommend this course to future students, especially those who are interested in entrepreneurship. The learning from this class makes most of the other courses I've taken feel like a walk in the park. The experience is so hands-on: startup team dynamics, talking to customers, refining business model, and more.

I would, however, recommend that people sign up in their second year instead of first for two reasons: (1) A lot of what you do and knowledge applied in this class come from other fundamental subjects: finance, marketing, operations, and soft skills. I think you can get more out of this class if you do this class after you've gotten more exposure to different subjects. (2) Many people are doing both internship recruiting the second semester of first year. This makes the class pretty stressful sometimes and harder to get the most out of it. You'd be doing yourself a favor by taking this class in your final semester (assuming you have a return offer from summer internship or some plan secured by then).

sections.goodFor: Students seriously considering founding a company who have an idea they care about, a team they trust and access to real customers; the 100+ interviews are a strong interview story.
sections.notFor: Anyone recruiting simultaneously, lukewarm on their idea, or on a team that isn't fully bought in - it is the most demanding class at Haas and becomes a huge drag if any of those fail.
sections.workloadNote: A sustained weekly grind, not front- or back-loaded: 15-20 hrs/week of customer discovery (100+ interviews) plus weekly presentations and ad-hoc requests. Brutal alongside recruiting.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly team presentations and customer-discovery progress tracked in the course tool Glidr; team-based throughout. No exams mentioned.
sections.redFlags: Recurring: instructors (esp. lead Jim) underdeliver vs. the course design (2-3 mentions); presentation-heavy with limited guidance; dated lectures and obsession with the Glidr tool; 1 calls it academic.
sections.quote: This is an awesome course, despite the instructors. The course design absolutely nailed it - it motivates every one of the 40 people in class to put 15-20 hours a week, every week.
comments: I would recommend this course! it helped me figure out whether or not entrepreneurship is for me, taught me how to have hard conversations and pushed me beyond my limits.

I would recommend this if you are interesting from learning from and meeting with incredibly accomplished people, but keep in mind that this really is /a lot/ of work outside of class and you need to love your team and have some interest in your ideas.

Overall, I remain unconvinced of whether the Lean Launchpad model is the best way to start actually establishing a real, revenue earning business. If you are a student who doesn't have a business idea, or has no idea where to start on their entrepreneurship journey, this class may be what you need to launch you.
yes this course is awesome.
Absolutely

This is an awesome course, despite the instructors. The course design absolutely nailed it - it motivates every one of the 40 people in class to put 15-20 hours a week, every week. It ensured that everyone learned by doing and practicing, and everyone was engaged in lectures, office hours, presentations etc. Over the years, the course has really perfected these aspects and if you want to be an entrepreneur, you'll definitely learn a lot!

That said, some things could make this course even better. Like more up to date lectures and much less obsession with the course tool, Glidr. The instructors, especially the lead instructor Jim, could've really stepped up. I feel mixed about this. It is a phenomenal opportunity to explore the startup world BUT it was very presentation heavy with limited guidance. I think the workload wasn't even the issue - I would do all the work and still appreciate doing something more than listening to presentations and giving presentations.
I would but would be very clear that this is not a course meant to build your business. This is an academic exercise. If you actually want to build a business, you don't need to take this course.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this to others, with the caveat that it requires a significant amount of work. However, for those who are ready to put in the effort, it can be incredibly valuable, especially for anyone looking to learn about entrepreneurship. As someone coming from a different country, this has definitely been the best experience so far!
Yes, it's a great class for developing grit and character.
yah

Absolutely! This was hands down the best class I've taken at Haas. It pushed us to talk to real users, test our assumptions, and make meaningful progress every single week. I only wish we had more time to build, by the time we gained confidence in our direction, the quarter was almost over. Highly recommend for anyone serious about entrepreneurship.

yes, i would only recommend it for students who are seriously thinking of starting a company due to the time commitment. But if you fall into this group this is invaluable and you will feel ready to do it once complete. I would absolutley recommend this class to others. This is what I have talked most about in interviews even when its a small one liner on my CV, companies and people pick it out and want to learn more about your 100+ customer interviews

I would recommend this class to someone who has an idea that they realistically think they can bring to the market. I will also advise that you try solving a problem where you have access to the customers you will be helping. That will make the class much more straightforward. If you have a good idea that you would like to make real, this is a good place to start. If you are applying just to be in the class or entering with an idea that all 5 members of your team are not 100% on board with, the class will be very challenging.
ABSOLUTELY. This is probably the most meaningful class I have taken at Berkeley. If you want to start a business of any sort, this is the class for you.
Yes, it is such a unique course. I highly recommend everyone experiences it.

If you have an idea you're excited about, and a team you work well with, this is a great course. If you're only lukewarm about your idea, change that quickly because it can be a huge drag. I was in the lucky camp, and this course is now a launching pad for me to actually start businesses with classmates. My goals were to make entrepreneurship less intimidating and to practice execution over perfection. This course fulfilled both of these requirements for me! Yes absolutely. The course is basically simulating the early stages of entrepreneurial experience and having such a course gives students a real picture of potential real-world challenges when they start their own venture. Class workload is 20 hours a week. Not very useful for the quant part of understanding a startup. Good for problem discovery

Absolutely take it if you want to be an entrepreneur or at least want to test the hypothesis of whether you want to be an entrepreneur. It will confirm or disconfirm that hypothesis. This will be the most demanding course you take at Haas -- do not take it unless you are absolutely committed. But a spot in this class is incredibly valuable -- take it seriously and make the most of your experience.

Yes I will receommend the course. However, please note that doing this course along with recruitment is really challenging. It is easily more that 10 hours a week and on top of that their can be ad-hoc request. Not each class will be worth it. Please do proper due-deligence to form your teams- you want a team with whom you can have fun. Yes! It has been my favorite class I have taken at Berkeley so far.
Yes, but seriously its 20 hours. you may not have a good team and it will be very hard. But it was worth it. One of the hardest but most rewarding courses you can take.

This class is so practical than any other classes I have taken. It's more engaging but very difficult. I would surely recommend to someone who want get into entrepreneurship. This class provides all you need to build a startup and I feel so confident building a startup any time soon
Get out of the building! Best class to learn how to actually make change. I've never felt more challenged, but I've learned a life long lesson.

rows.title: Climate Change Essentials for Business Leaders

comments: It's a low lift course, and it's quite informative for a 2 Sunday commitment.
Yes! It is an excellent introduction towards understanding how climate change works and why. It is on the cientific side, so it just only the step one towards being involved in sustainability
Yes, very informative. Must take!

Absolutely would recommend these professors and course! It was like a crash course on climate change issues and solutions. Everyone should be educated on this topic and they were amazing/the best people to do it!

Yes - I thought it was a good high-level overview of climate change for people who plan to work in some aspect of the business world. It was focused on how companies/corporations engage with sustainability targets, but with the first half of the class giving a great deep-dive into climate science. If you have already studied environmental science or climate change extensively, I wouldn't recommend it (too basic) but is good for someone without much experience in this field.

Yes - professor was clearly passionate about the topic and did a great job explaining the basics of climate change science and teaching us to think critically about businesses' claims around their own climate impact and commitments (e.g., net zero emissions, greenwashing)
I'd definitely recommend if you are interested in learning more about how severe the situation is and listen about the situation from a geologist (not 100% business focused!)
Amazing immersion! Great class for both newbies and those already familiar with climate topics.

Absolutely! One of the best (and relevant) courses I have taken at Haas. The instructors are extremely knowledgable, bring a science-based approach to the course and make the learning experience extremely interesting and engaging. Yes with some caveats. I think it gives an adequate primer on climate change that we as Haas students can take to the corporate world to explain why global warming and climate change really are threats. Course also does well to explain some of the pitfalls or green washing. I think the 1 unit is more than enough and I'm glad I didn't take the 3 unit version of this class.

I would 100% recommend this course if you have any interest in climate change and would like a crash course. For me, it was helpful and reinforced my desire to continue climate courses and try to incorporate this into my future career. This very focused on climate change and not necessarily its application to business.
Yes

Would definitely recommend this course for a high level overview on climate change and business if students are interested but don't want to commit to 3 units. Appreciated that other students in the course engaged in discussion made it more rich too. It's very high level but informative class

Instructors are passionate about climate change and that is well transferred to students during class. I consider myself well aware about climate change and have decent technical depth in understanding processes, but I still learned a lot from this class.
Should be a core course for all Haas MBA program!

This class is heavy on the science and very light on the business side. It's a good course if you don't know much about the climate and want to learn more, but will feel a bit dull and repetitive if you already have a decent understanding of climate change. That said, it's a very light workload -- no pre-reading and only one assignment -- so works great with busy schedules! I thought Omar was an engaging lecturer but Isaacs was a bit dry.
Yes, good class to take if climate sustainability matters to you but you're not trying to only take climate classes. I think is a must for understanding the basics of climate change.
Yes, really well taught and done in a very practical sense. There was no fat on the bone in this class, almost all of the time spent was useful
Yes - informative and a very balanced 1 credit class

Yes!!! Everyone should make sure to take a class with Roy throughout their time at Haas. Not only is he a great teacher, but learning about Unions & other forms of organizing has changed my entire perspective on the workforce and the economy and the relative distribution of power within it. Highly recommend!

Highly recommend - this was an incredibly interesting course on a subject that is going to become more timely in business and Roy gave us different perspectives to walk away with and a lot more confidence and information to be able to critically think about the considerations of organized labor

100% - great class, minimal effort, lots of learning, lots of engagement in the topic given it's emerging and new. Yep! SUPER low lift and doesn't overlap with anything we've taken at Haas, so it's worth it for the different perspective. Can't emphasize enough low of a lift it was. Also, Roy is just a really cool guy
Yep - for anyone interested in the learning about the future of human labor in an AI-future.
Yes. Super interesting and relevant topic for us as we prepare to reenter the workforce in a management role. And, this topic directly relates to the "S" in ESG.
Yes!! A highly engaging, relevant, and progressive course.
This is a great class if you're interested in unions! It also pulled together a great group of students!

This is my favorite class I've taken at Haas so far! He was wonderful at creating a safe, inclusive environment - especially important for a course diving into a topic with a lot of nuance and discussion required, like labor organizing. I also really really appreciate how he seems to understand (more than most other professors at Haas) that the most utility of a class comes from being able to learn and discuss the aspects of the subject that are relevant to our working lives, not from doing theoretical work that may or may not apply to our real-life experiences. (In other words, I appreciated that the assigned work was not excessive, and the work we did have was directly useful for better understanding unions in our working lives after school).
YES! The first labor union class at a business school and definitely an eye-opener

Highly recommend! One of the more timely and useful classes I?ve taken at Haas, learned a lot and feel much more informed about current events in labor organizing and how I might approach working with labor organizations. Heck yes. Take this class. At its core it's a class about power dynamics. It's not pro- or anti-union, it's more about creating a place to understand various ways labor might organize and how to think about this from the perspective of employee/worker, business management/leaders, and the organization itself. Very cool, very relevant, and awesome discussions.

Yes! This was probably the most interesting class I?ve taken at Haas. The class discussions were so interesting and Roy bring in great guest speakers. Not too much work (though the readings are great), but tons of learning.
Yes! I learned a lot and this will be an important topic in the future.
Yes
Yes! Such a unique subject and the way Roy teaches it makes it an incredibly valuable and eye-opening experience

sections.goodFor: Future managers who will deal with labor, and anyone interested in organizing, social change, or critiques of corporate power - even skeptics.
sections.notFor: Students who already have union or labor-organizing experience - one found the content obvious and the class a 'long and winding walk through unions'.
sections.workloadNote: Repeatedly called low-lift with little outside coursework; class is discussion-driven with a capstone organizing project run with the whole class as one group.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; class discussion and a whole-class capstone organizing project.
sections.redFlags: One student says it is only an intro to unions and does not teach management-union interaction; experience depends heavily on who else is in the discussion-based class.
sections.quote: Your experience will largely depend on the makeup of your class, as it's highly discussion based and also involves a group project where the entire class is one group.
comments: Yes! its a fun course and pretty low lift!
Yes absolutely. This is one of the best classes I've taken at Haas. Roy is a gem!

This class was not at all what I thought it would be. It was kind of a long and winding walk through unions rather than teaching me how management and unions can better interact. Maybe some of it felt obvious to me because I have prior experience with unions, but I don't think any of the content was especially interesting. I'm not sure this class would be useful unless you're looking for an intro to unions.

Definitely would recommend. This class is so different from the other Haas courses but so necessary. Very few of us know the dynamics of labor organizing, yet it is one of the most powerful countervailing forces we have against corporate power and capitalism's shortcomings. Yes, one of the best professor I've had in my grad school experience ( I am not a JD or LLM student). if you have any questions about IPOs, this course will likely answer them, and if not, Pro. Kennedy certainly will be able to. I highly recommend the IPO Essentials course to anyone interested in learning about the initial public offering (IPO) process. This course is designed for individuals with varying levels of experience, making it an ideal choice for both beginners and professionals in the field.

For those who are new to IPOs, the course provides a comprehensive overview of the essentials, including the steps involved in preparing for an IPO, the legal and regulatory requirements, and the different roles involved in the process. By the end of the course, you will have a solid understanding of what it takes to successfully launch an IPO and be equipped with the knowledge needed to start working on IPO projects with confidence.

If you already have experience with IPOs, the course is still highly valuable as it provides a deeper understanding of the US capital market and encourages critical thinking about it. The course also offers the opportunity to compare and contrast the differences between international capital markets, helping you identify new opportunities and strategies to implement in your work.

Power and politics was arguably the most valuable course I took at Haas. It taught me a lot about myself, and more importantly, how others perceive me. It has helped me form a strategy around how to present myself and carry myself in different contexts to maximize my "strengths" and minimize my "weaknesses".
I would not recommend this course if taught by Brandi. However, if it is offered by Cameron Anderson I would recommend taking it.

sections.goodFor: Commenters say virtually every MBA should take it: practical, science-backed frameworks for navigating power, influence, networks, and office politics in any career, with self-reflection many found genuinely enlightening. The flipped-classroom, experiential format and Brandi's energy drew repeated praise.
sections.notFor: One commenter would only recommend the course if taught by a different professor; otherwise no one warned students off.
sections.workloadNote: Described as just right and not overly burdensome; not too hard, but built around activities and self-reflection.
sections.quote: Power and politics was arguably the most valuable course I took at Haas. It taught me a lot about myself, and more importantly, how others perceive me.
comments: Yes. Love the diversity and having a woman instructor.

Yes! She brings passion to the room and creates a good conversation in a topic that's not easy to explain Yes, Brandi reinforces teachings in this flipped classroom model to focus on experiential learning. She navigates classroom discussions well.
I would definitely recommend this class, there is so much practical application and the material is relevant to any profession or field. Genuinely one of the best courses I've taken.
I definitely recommend this course. It provides the science and psychology behind power and politics in organizations. These are useful topics for any MBA to understand.
I would recommend this course if you are interested in learning about VC/PE, though I would not recommend this course if you are interested in learning how to get into VC/PE.
For an overview kinda course, it suffices. But you don't learn a lot more, especially on the valuation side. Very good guest speakers though
Absolutely! Gives a great insight and understanding on how VC evaluate opportunities and make the deal flow work from start to end. Any one focusing on entrepreneurship or VC should take this class.
Yes

Yes. The course is really good for anyone who is interested in learning about the VC field. The course covers all the aspects of the VC business. The combination of relevant cases and relevant speakers makes the whole experience really great. I highly recommend this course.

I would recommend this course. It took a few lectures to get into it, but the lectures, discussions, and guest speakers were very informative. The course is lighter on theory but the discussion and speakers are rich (both in bank account and educational value). It is a good way to bring together learnings from other classes and enjoy yourself while you learn.

Yes, useful class if you aren't familiar with VC and if you want to learn more. Workload isn't too crazy for a 3-unit class. I learned a lot since I have no prior experience in the VC industry. However, I believe it could have been a 2 unit course rather than a 3 unit course, and it could have been more concise. If you are at all interested in working in the VC industry, then I would recommend it as you will make important contacts and introductions in the industry. This was a nice class to take and get deeper into the VC and startup ecosystem. It was not necessarily what I expected, but I enjoyed the class and I think it gave me a more realistic view of the industry and it's challenges. It was not a class that boasted that everyone should be in VC/PE, and did talk frankly about challenges in the industry and what the future could hold. I would recommend it if you don't have internship or work experience in VC.
This was a great class and gave me a good overview of what VC world would be like

Highly recommend for anyone interested in either a career in VC or entrepreneurship or investing. This class has resulted in substantial learning to peak inside into the world of venture capitalists. A great class to take after the entrepreneurship class.

Yes, I would recommend this course - more for students whoa re interested in VC not PE. We did not spend alot of time on PE business model and strategy. This is a great balance of theoretical and practical course for students who are exploring a career in VC.
Yes

I would recommend this course to a fellow student if Sean and Keval take a larger role in future iterations. I would highly recommend this course to fellow Berkeley students, including those not interested in entrepreneurship or venture capital. I believe this course substantially improved my understanding of the industry and I have a greater appreciation for the opportunities in Berkeley and the entire Bay Area. This is easily a top 2 course I have taken at Haas so far.

You get as much out of this class as you put into it. If you put little into it, you'll get a basic overview of the business of venture capital (spoiler alert: it's still a lot of luck and n-of-1 wins); if you put a lot into it, I think you can develop a great network starting with the professors and learn an interesting baseline that will help you start a career in venture (or better understand some of the questions VCS ask if you're thinking about entrepreneurship). If you're trying to deeply understand VC/ what VCs are looking for, you probably won't get all the way there with this course, but it's a good introduction if you're exploring/ just getting started.
Heartily recommend this course. One of the best courses at Haas.

Yes. The class has an amazing amount of breadth and is good at presenting what it's like to pursue a career in VC. The industry itself can be very ambiguous, so don't expect any black and white solutions or career paths, but it's very thought provoking.
Yes, but students need to be prepared to spend more time research and network after the class to learn more about the actual VC business

Yes,very valuable insight which you would never be able to just teach yourself. However there were many confusing points in the class due to lack of clarity from the professor. If you dont have investing background you will need to spend some extra time familiarizing yourself with terminology or being careful with the problem sets.
Yes - great class and learned a lot.

I would only recommend it to people who have worked in VC before - it seems like the entire class had already worked in VC, and the playing field was not level at all. There was no basic intro to the concept of PE and VC, and many of my peers felt lost in class.

Yes! This was the best course I took this semester. It was a really helpful, practical intro to VC and covered a wide range of very practical topics (e.g., term sheets, valuation, etc.). The professors were great and brought in a really amazing set of guest speakers from different VCs. Classes were engaging (attendance and participation expected) and the assignments were very well designed to consolidate learnings.

It depends. If you want to break into VC or if you already work in VC, this is an extremely valuable class. For the rest, if you're just interested in VC but don't want to make a career out of it, I would not recommend this class. It gets pretty technical at times, some assignments are the very heavy lift and my general perception is that the instructors expect you to come up with extremely insightful comments, that are hard to make if you don't have previous experience in the space.

Participation is essential to this class. They keep track of participation and will cold-call people who haven't participated recently (which I did not appreciate, it felt like there were putting people on the spot too often and that the expectations were too high).
Overall, good class for people that are really into VC, not recommended otherwise.

Highly recommend, even if you don't have experience in this industry. Instructors are well prepared for case discussions and really try to get you to think and develop points of views. Speakers are insightful and a big part of the class experience.
Very valuable course, highly recommended. It is 100% VC - do not expect PE.

I would recommend this course to you only if you are really passionate about VC or are very interested to understand the world of VC. This course is definitely has a high workload and is much more discussion oriented. If you think you will learn a lot around valuation, financing, more technical skills - then you will be disappointed. There is some elements of it but it is only touched upon. Overall great course if you are new/wanting to develop a deeper understanding of the VC space.
Yes would definitely recommend to students interested in venture capital.
Yes
Yes. All 3 are fantastic and among the best I've had at Berkeley Haas.

Yes, especially if you want to pursue a career in VC. About Private Equity, understood as LBO, the class has nothing. Also, the class is very interesting if you want to be an entrepreneur because you meet several VC managing partners who explained us trends, targets and investment thesis that are very useful to raise money.

Absolutely. I'm a (hopeful) entrepreneur with a startup operator background and took this class to understand how the other-side of the investment table thinks. It delivered on that and was highly engaging every minute with some life lessons sprinkled in as well.

Would definitely recommend this course if you're interested to get a crash course and learn about venture capital. The workload was a little more than most classes, but I genuinely understood venture better through this class. The professors brought in PHENOMENAL speakers and have been personally helpful. I got a lot from the class but will caveat it doesn't necessarily prep or hone you to do a venture Associate / Sr Associate / Principal role - you'll still need to figure that out elsewhere

It's definitely a different vibe compared to other Haas classes (participation is 35% the final grade and case method is better in theory than in practice; also, VCs in general probably think a little too highly of themselves), but overall it was a worthwhile course. Fantastic lineup of guest speakers (Lauren Kolodny from Acrew, Byron Deeter from Bessemer, Paul Kwan from General Catalyst, to name a few), Sean/Keval/Terry have a ton of experience and great
insights/thoughts about the VC industry overall, and I did end up learning a lot about VC.

Recommend this class for anyone looking to get a foundational understanding of Venture Capital. The class is the best structured class I've taken at Haas given three faculty members. All three (Sean, Terry, Keval) are very knowledgeable and bring a different aspect to the course. Your venture team matters for most of the class so choose wisely. I would recommend this class if you want an intro to VC/PE. If you are already in this space, then this might not be a class for you. Either way, be prepared to do a lot of reading.

Mixed feelings about this class- While they bring in cool speakers who are great VCs, the class itself has outdated cases from the 90s and early 2000s. Hence, it is not completely representative of today's VC market. I wish the class also focused on what it means to be a good VC- how do you ask proper diligence questions? Maybe they can bring in actual startups for us to ask live questions from the CEO
Yes - a great foundational course for a typical opaque industry in order to learn enough to be able to teach yourself more complex topics

Yes, I would absolutely recommend as this class is very informational and fun. Almost everyone, no matter you want to become a VC or not, should probably take this course because you will apply the knowledge from this class
somewhere in your career and investment.

Yes I would. This class is a comprehensive intro to VC and has extremely well prepared content and guest speakers. It teaches you not only the basic stuff such as term sheet and valuation, but also give you an overall picture about the entire VC industry and help you understand the dynamics. Instructors often hold partner's meeting in class to discuss about the pros and cons of a deal and your argument about it. Some of the guest speakers are very helpful as well - they are from different background and worked in different stages of VC firms.

I came from a non-VC, non-financial background and I enjoyed the course. It gave me a summary of how investments and the VC world works which I think is helpful in B-school so that we can make the decisions if this is something we want to do long term or not. I also really appreciated all the guest speakers the instructors chose and brought in as they came from diverse backgrounds and provided very good context and supplement to class instruction. Overall, I would recommend this class.

sections.goodFor: Repeatedly called one of the best classes at Haas for anyone targeting VC or planning to raise from VCs as a founder; the guest speaker lineup (managing partners across stages and sectors) is cited as worth the class by itself. Works for true beginners and experienced VC folks alike, per multiple commenters.
sections.notFor: Despite the title there is essentially no private equity or LBO content, so skip it if PE is your goal. Several students without a finance or VC background felt lost when lectures jumped into calculations, and those wanting deep technical valuation training or casual observers unwilling to carry the heavy, participation-driven load were disappointed.
sections.workloadNote: Heavier than a typical MBA elective: a case per class, substantial reading, and assignments several called hard, though most felt the work translated directly into learning.
sections.gradingBasis: Participation weighs heavily (one student cites 35% of the final grade), with case discussions, cold calling, problem sets, and a venture team component.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (5+ comments): no PE content despite the course name; recurring (4+ comments): assumes VC/finance background and newcomers can feel lost; a few (3): cold-calling and participation pressure felt excessive; isolated: outdated cases from the 90s/2000s, assignments disconnected from class.
sections.quote: Yes, this class was extremely worthwhile. If you want to learn about venture capital this class is a must. One of the best classes offered in the entire MBA program.
comments: I would ABSOLUTELY recommend this class to a fellow student. It is a lot of work, relative to other MBA classes, and Sean's teaching style is intense and may not be for everyone. I recommend this class to anyone interested in VC and even those who have already worked in VC. This class goes deep enough into the details to be practically useful to those going into VC. Sean is additionally one of the best and most engaging lecturers I have had at Haas.
Emphatically, yes

Very valuable class that teaches you a lot about venture capital. The assignments are hard and not necessarily tied to in class work so that is frustrating. But this is the most engaging high energy night class I've taken at Haas. Cold calling and lots of participation required.
Yes, only if they want to enter VC or raise funds from a VC.
