Yes, this class was extremely worthwhile. If you want to learn about venture capital this class is a must. One of the best classes offered in the entire MBA program.

Absolutely! This class was really insightful for someone not coming from a VC background. The cases, lectures, and assignments were well structured and lead to meaningful learning. Sean/Keval et al are also fantastic professors to teach this. They bring decades of expertise and insights which adds value to this class. One of the big value adds to this class is the amount of guess lecturers and speakers - this made lectures dynamic and their insights provided alternative viewpoints and approaches.

I would definitely recommend this course to any aspiring Venture Capitalist / Entrepreneur as it teaches you the A-Z of Venture Capital. The guest speakers are incredible and the frameworks Sean teaches are invaluable - especially with regards to Term Sheets and Valuation!

Yes! Even if you aren't interested in a career in VC, the frameworks for evaluating investment opportunities are extensible. Workload is a little on the heavier side but all the assignments resulted in substantial learning No, if you don't have sufficient VCPE background. Sometimes, I found it hard to keep up with the pace of the lecture as lecturers dive right into calculations without providing basic foundations.

Would wholeheartedly recommend this instructor and course to anyone interested in VC. This class resulted in tangible learning outcomes that would not have been possible without taking the course, and the exposure to guest speakers, internship announcements, and related opportunities is unparalleled across Haas' course offerings. Definitely yes, if you are interested in VC, starting a startup or generally learn a lot about the VC and innovation ecosystem.
Yes, I highly recommend this class! It was my first elective, but the best class so far. It is very applicable to my day-to- day work.
With instructors' hands-on experience and extensive connections in the industry, the course is very engaging and can result in significant learning.
YES
Simply the best class at Haas.

EW295B provides a strong overview of how venture capital works, though you will need some prior knowledge of venture capital to truly get the most of out the class. The course moves quickly and covers a lot of content, and is filled with a a number of insights and speakers from across the industry. Highly recommend for those who want to pursue Entrepreneurship in particular, as it is useful primer for seeing fundraising from the other side of the table. Yes

I would definitely recommend this class. I leave having a much more foundational understanding of the VC industry that I did coming in. However, we do cover some very specific, though relevant, details of VC and a baseline knowledge of the industry would have helped. The beginning of the class felt just like so much content to understand and absorb rather than expanding on knowledge I already possessed.
Absolutely, this is the course to come to Haas MBA for. Exposure, knowledge and experience.

Such an amazing class! I can't believe how good this was. You should definitely take it regardless of your experience in VC (I have 4 years of direct experience and loved it as much as my friend that has no prior experience) if you are interested in the industry.

If you're looking to get into VC, this is definitely the course to do it. If you're in VC and want to learn more or get more external expertise, I would. New to VC myself, I learned a TON here, especially because of the guest speakers bringing in a macro and varied VC perspective. Sean and Keval are knowledgeable SMEs and enthusiastic about the topic. It is a good bit of work, but value adding.
Yes — I'm leaving with a solid understanding of VC and have a new roster of folks that I might be able to approach when I start something.
Strongly recommend! One of the best course in Haas.
Yes, for someone who comes from a purely operating background this was a great preview into the workings of the VC world
Best class I have taken at Haas. The outside speakers alone are worth the class but Sean and team are engaging and their polish made me excited to attend lecture.
Yes! I learned a lot in the class and this is one of the best classes at Haas.
Yes, if you're interested in venture capital, this is the class for you.
Yes I would, I consistently enjoyed going to class. Expect that this class is wide and not deep, but I did feel like I got a lot out of the class
yes, I think this is a good, starting class for those who want to learn VC from the scratch

Yes, this was a top 3 Haas course for me. Sean and Keval are so enthusiastic about VCPE and every class is buzzing with energy. Sean really cares about his students and wants them to learn and grow in their careers. The guest speakers come from a wide breadth of backgrounds (varying types of investment stages and industries, and plenty of female speakers) and allows students to connect with those working in the industry. I'd retake this class again in a heartbeat.

This is a fairly advanced course so you should only take it if you want to go into VC or be an entrepreneur who will work with VC's. Everything in the class is about how be a successful VC, run a VC firm, and make good investments. There is nothing on private equity or other areas of finance in general. So it's the perfect class for any wanna-be VC's and entrepreneurs.
Awesome class
Yes, course was a great way to learn and understand VC through course work and weekly guest speakers.

Yes, this was one of my favorite courses at Haas so far. I had no background in VC and learned a ton. Expectations are high (one case per class, occasional cold calling), but for me it was worth it. Sean is really engaged and clearly loves teaching. There are also a ton of great high-level guest speakers.

rows.title: Strategy and Leadership for Social Impact

comments: Yes; both very thoughtful and kind. Deeply knowledgeable about the space; link theory to practice often

If you are new to strategy and the nonprofit sector, and enjoy very academic / case-based discussions, I would say this class is for you. If you're hoping to develop specific skills to use in the near future, you may find this class too theoretical.
Yes, definitely. Is a very good overview of the social sector with many examples and deep conversations
yes - they lead with genuine empathy for their students and are experts in the field of social impact. not too much of a heavy lift course, perfect amount of work for a 2 unit classs

Yes, to those interested in entering the social sector (which includes pretty much anything that's not for-profit, *and* for-profits with a strong social mission). I thought this class was a very useful overview of the distinct challenges of the sector and covered a lot of material, from domestic to international and from education to financial independence to health and more. I even learned some useful things about the for-profit sector as contrasted with the social sector. And Ben and Colin are great people to know.

If you're interested in social impact, then yes. The class is heavy in cases and discussions so be prepared for that Yes, this is a great class. I like the casestudy format and the structured discussions. It was also an interesting class I was always looking forward to.

This is an excellent course to take if you are interested in social impact as a personal interest and/or career focus. We read several interesting cases and heard from a number of stakeholders at foundations/non profits - this was truly an eye opening course. Thank you Ben & Colin!

This is the perfect course for anyone interested in figuring out exactly where in the social sector they want to work or contribute. It's a general course that covers a wide range of topics. Ben and Colin bring in guest lecturers that are truly incredible social sector leaders, and do a great job of outlining key trends, tensions, challenges, and themes that arise in this sector. Ben and Colin are excellent professors that really care about the material and their students, and make sincere efforts to stay in touch with the class. Even if you're only interested in being a board member or volunteer, I'd still highly recommend this course.

Yes. Vinnie is a funny, engaging speaker with deep knowledge of these topics. He also brought renowned and interesting guest speakers. I like how he facilitated discussion between the students and kept us involved and laughing throughout the course. It's basically just lecture, group project/paper, and a final paper.

Yes, he is passionate and energetic. He explains concepts through real life examples which makes it more visible and easier to understand. One can see he is an expert in the matter and his previous experience really adds to the course content.
Yes- absolutely. Vinnie is a really engaging lecturer and facilitates lively discussions.
Yes, absolutely recommend this course
Its a must-take if you're interested in international business outside of the traditional realms of market strategy Yes,

I would definitely recommend both this course and instructor. Vinod knows what's going on in the world and packages the course material and discussion to relevant issues that will affect us as business leaders. Very relevant material that every Haas student should take.
Great mix of business and strategy cases

Yes- If you are interested hon political and non-market considerations for business. Vinnie is very thoughtful in how he leads discussions, and also invited some great guest lecturers for some of the classes. I learned a lot and it was a different kind of thinking than many MBA classes.

Yes - Vinnie has seen a lot and has plenty of knowledge of what happens in the political economy. The class is useful for thinking beyond market strategies but some content is a little dry and textbook-centric. End of term paper is significant amount of writing so be ready for a undergrad style written paper for your final.
Absolutely!
Yes, the course is interesting and provide opportunities to apply what you learn in class to real life examples. Absolutely. Great class. Learned a lot.
Speakers truly elevate the class and the coursework challenges you to develop and articulate real investment strategies.

Obviously, Hedge Funds strategies is as high finance as high finance goes. If you are transitioning to a buy-side or investing career post MBA, the course provides very useful tools to enable you excel in the role. If your post MBA role is in Asset Management, Portfolio Management, or Hedge Funds, definitely look into taking this class.

Yes, I have little finance background but wanted to learn about hedge funds and this was a great way to do it. I'm really glad I took the course. I did not take Asset Management prior and my only real finance experience was Core Finance - I was totally fine although having a good team with more financial background really helped.
Yes, if you are curious to dive in more to financial services, learn in depth about different hedge fund strategies, and hear from industry experts in the space.

Yes, definitely recommend. It is a lot of work, but Haas does not do justice teaching actual technical material to MBA students. This is one of the few classes that actually covers material that is not focused around the soft skills. Yes, its a great course to learn about Hedge Funds through lectures/amazing guest speakers/projects, the various hedge fund strategies, building investment pitches, and creating your own hedge fund strategy

Yes, even if you are not interested in a career in finance, Hedge Fund strategies goes beyond finance - into realms of data science, trading (in general), arbitrage, and general markets. The speakers were excellent.
Yes
Yes! It's a great way to learn about how hedge funds function and to get deep into the markets. Really cool way to fulfill the AI requirement, too!
Yes - helpful to understand the essentials of HFs and building practice pitching
Yes - I think it's a really interesting and unique class. I liked the hands-on approach to learning (all the presentations), and it really helped me learn a ton.
Yes. The class is great for people with all experience levels of investing. I had 0 experience and I came away understanding a bunch of different hedge fund strategies

Yes. I think it's an excellent class to learn about investment management, even if you don't have any experience in finance. The course reviews the investment theories at an introductory level and asks students to put the knowledge into practice by building and presenting investment pitches. However, it's important to highlight the course load. It's a lot of work. Most of the week, you have a pitch to build and present, which implies a good amount of effort. I will strongly recommend this course to anyone who has any kind of interest in investment.
Personally if I knew this course existed, I wold have signed up for Haas MBA 5-6 years ago just for this course. This is an amazing course, and deserves a lot fo credit.
I wish I could get more out of the course by spending more time on the projects and presentations, but some other courses took a lot fo time, that limited the amount of time I could spend here.
If you are curious about what hedge funds actually do and what kinds of strategies are prevalent, this class is the perfect place to learn that and get connected with the industry experts.
Absolutely. If you are interested in asset management; this is a very useful course to take.
Yes, very interesting topic with professors that care about your learning.
this is a good course you'll learn a lot. workload can be a little heavy though
Yes. I came in with little investing and Hedge Fund knowledge and now I feel I learned a lot.
I feel prepared to speak to this subject matter in the future.

I would recommend this course to a fellow student, especially if they want to challenge themselves in the area of investment strategies. This class is relevant for anyone in the finance space - even people who just manage their own portfolio. It is not just for people interested in Hedge Funds.
Yes

Absolutely stellar academic experience. By far the best in Haas and Law school. The hands on approach, where you actually learn different aspects of trading and finance, the world class speakers that are stars in the hedge funds world and the guidance by the professors makes it by far the best class. If one likes trading or finance in general then its a no brainer. Also, we built an amazing relationship with the class due to the unique delivery and knowledge of the class. Yes, this is the best applied innovation course at Haas and Sam/Bill are a phenomenal team with extensive experience that increases learnings and is fun along the way.
Yes, even if you're not that interested in working at a hedge fund. The class was interesting, and not that much work (for an AI at least). I genuinely looked forward to attending this class

I would recommend this class for anyone who wants to learn about what real hedge fund managers do and how they practice their profession. I would also recommend this class for anyone who wants to take a more sophisticated approach to their own investments, or translate their own ideas about what is happening in the world into tangible trade ideas.

Yes. This is one of the most engaging class. Sam and Bill are very knowledgable and always open for discussion Yes this is an excellent course to dive deep into hedge funds and a finance topic. I feel like Haas MBA lacks in–depth finance courses and needs more courses like this one.

I definitely would recommend this instructor and course to our fellow student. We get to meet different students from different program. I learn a lot from pitches and guest speaker. It is a very fun and interesting class.

Absolutely. Mr. Olesky and Mr. Rindfuss are a fantastic duo and I can't believe they will be splitting up. They complemented each other so well and their experience, knowledge, and care for students was very much appreciated. If you are interested in hedge funds, no matter your level of prior knowledge of finance, investing or hedge funds, this course will give you exposure to the mechanics of hedge funds, and professional hedge fund managers who can speak to their real world experiences.

Yes. Excellent course with lots of learning. I thought I learned a lot from both a fundamentals and a practical perspective. It's a fair amount of work, but you'll learn a lot. I recommend this as the AI course of selection if you're interested in finance (if you're not interested in finance, it might be a little dry). Yes absolutely! Great content!
I feel this is the best MBA course at Haas.

I highly recommend this course to people interested in learning more about asset management. As a person who doesn't have a strong finance background, I sometimes struggled with the technical part or industry jargon. Still, I learned much about different hedge fund strategies and put the concepts into practical trading presentations. Sam, Bill, and the speakers they invited are fantastic – they all have extensive experience in the space and are willing to share their expertise.
Definitely! One of the best classes that I have taken at Haas

Yes, if you're interested in investing strategies and hedge funds! Joel and Sam are super knowledgeable, and have great industry contacts. The speakers are smart, humble, and good to connect with if you're interested in the industry. 10000% will recommend to all other Haas students - no question.
100% definitely! already done that

Highly recommend if considering a career in finance or consulting. Relatively low-lift compared to other AI classes. However, your experience is very dependent on your group so it's important to form a good group early and let the instructors know who your group is.
Yes - super useful to understand the different strategies that are available.

I would definitely suggest for people interested or curious about finance. This could be a great experience to execute strategies, get together with folks interested in finance and learn from guest speakers
I would recommend this class if you want to learn about hedge funds.
I think there's too much of a focus on the presentations and as a result, you spend too much time listening to other groups present. Otherwise great class

Yes - if you want to learn about hedge funds this is a great way to get an overview of all. For people in finance, it will give you a broad overview of a variety of hedge funds that you may or may not know about.
Yes - it was a very challenging and insightful learning experience. The class got very technical at times, so I would recommend it more strongly to those that have a background in finance.

This engaging course emphasizes real-world application over theory, encouraging active participation and idea generation. It's perfect for those eager to apply what they learn directly to practical scenarios.
Yes! A must for all students interested in investment management!

I would highly recommend this course to anyone looking to learn about varying investment strategies and connect with professionals implementing such strategies. The course isn't very technical in teaching the actual execution of the strategies, but it is perfect for those interested in hedge funds but don't know where to start.
Yes, but highly dependent on the client you are matched with, how reasonable they are with scope creep (or
shrinkage), as well as the mentor you have for your project. It took much longer than expected to nail down scope and get to work on our deliverable, and that discrepancy led to a lot of stress.

Interesting AI course. This was my third AI course total so I feel I have a good position to judge them from. This one was the most real world since we were out working with real companies. It was also by far the most work intensive in terms of the time the projects demanded. The other AI courses were three credits, this one was only 2 credits. So for that reason I cannot strongly recommend it compared to the others. If the course was increased to 3cr and included some lecture type sessions that supplemented the Impact investing weekend 1cr course, then I would highly
recommend it.

I would recommend this course if you want to go into an impact investing or ESG role so that you can get hand-on client experience. There is very little class content, so this is really just a 12 week mini-internship with a real company. Good course overall with a variety of topics. It is crucial to choose your project wisely and define the scope as this will have a high impact on your experience.

It's a project-based class so it really depends on what project you end up with and what client you work with. There is a lot of client expectation management involved and definitely feels more like a consulting project rather than an investment project. The course organization is a little messy in the beginning because the 3 instructors were also new in teaching it, but hopefully it'll get better next year.

Take this class if you want to get to know the awesome faculty better (Amon, Liz, Etter) and work on a concrete project for an external party. Similar to any AI class, your experience in the practicum will largely depend on who your client is and the nature of the project. The course will give you hands on experience with a real-life, real-time problem faced by an impact investor. Your experience here will be incredibly helpful if you want to go into impact consulting or impact investing.
Totally worth it! Dive deep into an impact project and learn as you go. Your mentor is important to help you bridge your knowledge gaps and they are very committed to help through working sessions.
Yes! The projects were super interesting and my project helped me getting a lot closer to my summer internship since I was very interested in this field.
Do not expect a lot of structure though. It's all about working with an interesting client on an interesting project and figuring it out with your group.

Yes, this was one of the most practical courses I've ever had. It was a well structured consulting project where I could get true hands on experience in a field I am looking to work in after work (impact investing). I'd recommend this as a must do class for anyone who wants to work at the intersection of impact and finance. Amon, Liz, and Steve bring their real world knowledge, experience, and networks into the classroom to help us have impactful projects, learn new things, and help position us for jobs and internships after school.

I would not recommend this course unless changes are made to ensure that projects are within the scope of what can reasonably be asked of students taking a 2 unit course over the length of one semester, and the faculty take a more active role in managing the clients' expectations.

Overall, yes. I thought the professors did an excellent job finding quality speakers and trying to be supportive as teams managed the client relationships. The projects were well-sourced and generally interesting. It is "project work" class -- there's very little aside from that. So if you're not wanting to deal with team dynamics and a client, and are looking for more instruction, then I'd reconsider.

Yes, I would recommend this course to another student interested in social impact VC. This is a hands-on course. Impact Investing Practicum is a good opportunity to gain hands on experience with an impact investing firm within the context of a Haas class. With the volatility and time commitment of in-semester internships, it's a good way to guarantee that you'll get this experience. Ultimately, you get out what you put in, and the projects vary substantially, but it's a great opportunity. There are some kinks to work out on the organizational side, but those should hopefully be fixed going forward.
Would recommend for students interested in impact investing bc of the practical experience.
Decent class – it's a bit too much like a consulting project. More of a focus on vc or growth investing would be nice
This course is worthwhile only if you want a very independent consulting project for an impact fund, without learning anything from instructors about the industry as a whole.
Yes but is very dependent on the project

No. If student wants to learn about impact investing this is not the class to do so. I dont think the professors took into account that students came from varying experiences and some have limited background in impact investing. It is very disappointing that professors just threw the students into the client work without any assistance. This course also heavily dependent on getting good team members that can equitable do the work but it is not the case for some team!

No – we did not feel supported and empowered by peer advisors to do effective work on the project. One of the professors communicated to our team in a patronizing and condescending way. Many of the clients had
interesting work and this class does have potential, but it was not met.
Would definitely recommend this course if you're interested in VC because it's great hands–on experience with a real fund!
Yes great on the job experience – pick your client well. access to impact investors

I would not recommend to get any class from Stephen Etter, if you would like to be respected as an individual and not be treated as 5th grade students. Liz Rockett on the other hand is a kind person and overall, I am thankful that Impact Investing Practicum class exists. It gives students a unique opportunity to work with real world projects with noteworthy funds.

This is a great class if you want to not only learn about impact investing, but get involved with a client on a real project where you can make a contribution. I had heard complaints about the course in previous versions, but I think the instructors really took those to heart and reformatted the source a bit and I thought it was great. It was a good combination of self-paced learning, real life projects, and instruction.
Its a great class to get hands on experience working with impact investing funds. The course brings a lot of great impact investors and funds students can connect with.

I would! This class is great hands on experience into Impact Investing. Treat it like a part-time internship (set agreed timelines and stick to them, communicate with the client like a true consultant) during the semester if you really want to get the most out of it.

This class is a mixed bag. There may be very inconsistent experiences. It is very heavy group work for your client project which can be valuable as a resume builder. If you don't have an impact investing or climate and sustainability background you will have to invest in supplementary learning because the client project topics are much deeper in scope than the 3-4 classes the cover high level topics.

Additionally you don't get to select your team and that significantly impacted the experience given that different members will have different levels of expertise, skills, and motivation (i.e. first year vs. second years vs. non-Haas students). There are no checks and balances if work is being distributed equally and if the client scope is still in alignment. Recommend that you flag any issues with team or client early to professors.

A great course to get your hands dirty if you're interested in impact investing. Highly recommend taking a prep course for this e.g., Impact Investing Landscape, PE/VC class to get a better understanding of the types of work, players, asks, etc. This is best for a 2nd year spring.
Yes, definitely, the project gave me an opportunity to work an impact investing firm
I would recommend it as a great opportunity for learning outside of the classroom. Great for anyone with an interest in impact investing.

I would recommend this to students looking for a project centric class that helps you learn about investing and wants to start a network in the investing field. If you are like me and were not looking to get into investing but wanted to learn more about it (specifically impact or climate investing) this is a good but not great fit. The class really lends itself well to people who want to test the hypothesis of working in impact investing, and consequently there is very little theory. There are other classes like corporate finance (strong recommend) or PE or Fixed income (strong recommend) or LBOs for people who want to feel they have a strong fundamental understanding and large knowledge base about investing.

The projects in this class are useful work for the client, but it isn't day to day work. You will not be able to say you have experience working as an investor exactly or have confidence that you could do investing, but you will through work learn what it is like to work in the industry.

I would recommend this class to students who want to work with specific funds. It is hard for me to take the project I have done and apply it to my future work given its so specific for the fund itself.
Absolutely, yes.

Yes, for anyone looking to enter the impact investing space, the set of clients Liz / Etta was able to bring onboard is really impressive. We learnt a lot working directly with the client on their project. That said, the class is somewhat unstructured (like many AI classes) and requires a fair amount of team coordination and discipline.

I definitely recommend this course because you get real world experience in the field. The professors have a wealth of industry experience that they openly share and they are very excited to help students navigate the field. Yes, absolutely. This is such a great way to get experience working with real clients. In semester internships can be difficult to get without having any background in impact investing, so to have the opportunity to work directly with funds as a part of class (and with the support of industry vets aka professors) is tremendously valuable. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to gain experience in impact investing. It is great exposure and a great opportunity to learn more about different impact investors and get experience and build a network in an impact investing firm.

The instructors are still figuring out how to structure course and class time, and so that could be improved. But if you get a good client project, then it's very worth it. You get out what you put in.
Yes I would - it was a great learning experience and I have a lot of course material that I can now link back to things I see and hear about in the real world.

sections.goodFor: Students pivoting into climate/impact VC who want a real project, investor connections and interview material - one landed an in-semester internship through their client.
sections.notFor: Students wanting a structured intro to impact investing or classroom teaching - learning is peer-to-peer and self-driven, and a vague client can leave you with an unfocused project.
sections.workloadNote: Almost all work is the self-driven client project; one says it can be a lot for 2 units if scope is not set with the client. Classes are sometimes cancelled for project work time.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the client project deliverable dominates, with peer-to-peer sharing of other teams' projects.
sections.redFlags: Experience hinges on the assigned client and group (5+); one reports classes often cancelled at the last minute for 'project work time' with little deep learning from the professors.
sections.quote: what you get out of it really depends on the client and project you get. If you get a client who doesn't really know what they want... the project may end up being very unfocused
comments: Absolutely - specially if you're interested in getting real life experience more about impact and climate investing and/or working with it.

I learned a lot with this course, but I think part of it was because of the client we were assigned to. Potentially this is a class that the more you give the more you get, and part of it depends on the clients engagement and organization to support the project.

Amazing opportunity to connect with the impact and climate investing space - we got to know a lot of the clients and part of them (not only ours) joined the final happy hour and we were able to network more.
Yes, this was a fantastic class for anyone that wants hands-on experience in impact investing

Yes if you're interested in hands-on experience in impact investing. Like most experiential classes, your group and project idea will have a big impact on your actual experience, but I found the ROI on project time very high and would have invested more time in this class if I could do it over. Both instructors are very willing to share their expertise and time with you, the lectures themselves are very informative, and I highly recommend this class.
Yes
Definitely would recommend the course! I thought this was a great experience working with a client and learning real world applications of what we learn in the classroom.
Yes, especially for future investors! It's fun and meaningful to work with real VCs/investors.
Yes if you already have experience in this industry. If you are new it is how much you put into this class.

I would recommend this course with the caveat that what you get out of it really depends on the client and project you get. If you get a client who doesn't really know what they want or how to utilize your skills, the project may end up being very unfocused, and you may not learn as much as your peers. A lot of our project felt self-driven, and we kind of lost the benefit of working with someone who works in the industry- we didn't really get to know what he does on a day-to-day basis. That said it was useful to speak to my experience in interviews and gave us credibility to have conversations with some really influential people in the industry.

Yes! Your experience will be somewhat colored by the client youre paired with but regardless, the class is an incredible value add. You'll also have a lot of opportunities to learn from your classmates' projects.

This class is entirely based on your client project, with little to no lecture or deep learning coming from the professors. In fact, class is often cancelled (at the last minute) to give us more "project work time." Honestly, I was hoping to learn more about impact investing from the professors who are such seasoned professionals in this space, but they seem to believe that it's only worthwhile to learn by doing through our client projects, which are highly variable depending on the assigned client and topic.

This was a fantastic class! We had the chance to work with real-world clients and could select them during the first week. I really appreciated how dedicated Etter and Liz were to our growth and supporting us throughout the process. Coming in with no understanding of impact investing (or investing, in general), I felt like it helped to provide me with a deeper understanding and real-world skills.

If you want to work in VC, TAKE THIS CLASS! As someone who is looking to pivot into Climate VC, this may have been the single most impactful class I took in my first year at Haas. Landing a first role in venture is hard, but this class gives you the practical experience to make it easier. The connections with your client are also very helpful, and mine led to an in-semester internship with a fund my client connected me with.
I would recommend this class as it does a great job of tying in the real world into Haas. It was also extremely interesting to see all the other projects other teams were covering.

Good class, very hands-on, but like any applied innovation, the workload and overall class experience depends heavily on the group and client you are assigned. I feel like the class can end up being a lot of work for only 2 units if you don't set a clear scope with your client or get a hard to tackle problem. A lot of the class is self-driven and learning is meant to be peer-to-peer, so this might not be the best class if you are looking for an introductory overview of the impact investing space.
Absolutely, fantastic instructors that bring deep industry knowledge and a great network
Yes fun class and engaging

I would definitely recommend this course if you are interested in climate investing. The projects themselves vary, but Liz and Etter are great resources if you are willing to engage with the class and put in the time.
Yes I would especially if you have never thought about impact investing (applications, capital structures etc.)

rows.title: Climate Change and Business Strategy
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2021 Fall;2022 Spring;2022 Fall;2023 Spring;2023 Fall;2024 Fall;2025 Fall

comments: Absolutely! I've already recommended this class to several classmates for next year. I think it's a critical course for anyone who cares about the climate. In fact I think this would be a great core class for first years, as I believe all Haas students should graduate with a foundational understanding of climate and the role business can play in climate solutions.

Yes. I think this class has a lot of potential, but fell short in its first iteration. I felt like the "business strategy" aspect of the course was really missing. Perhaps this will come naturally when the case studies are completed (he was writing case studies for this class so the last few weeks there were no readings, just speakers). I'm grateful we kicked off the class with getting into the science of climate change, but I don't think we ever really dove into what businesses can and should do to tackle climate change.

I enjoyed this class. I'd say it leans more "climate change" than "business strategy," but the three papers assigned provide a lot of flexibility for students to do a deep dive into the business implications for an industry of their choosing. I got a lot out of this course.

I would recommend this class for folks who are particularly interested in Climate Change and want a fairly easy workload. The first third (science portion) was quite helpful and provided great information. However, the business- focused discussion was a bit...unstructured. I imagine this course will improve quite a bit when held in person (versus on Zoom), however, as engagement and interaction will likely be higher.

Yes - I am leaving this class with a much more holistic view of how a company's actions directly impact the climate through carbon emissions. I am also leaving with a much more detailed and nuanced view of the ecosystem of

innovation in climate as well as how existing companies should consider addressing these challenges. Climate change is such a huge, real and immediately pressing problem for the world and I think the understanding that is developed through this course should be a requirement for anyone graduating with an MBA.

There are a few research papers which required work, but I got a lot out of the research and time that I put into writing them and I got to choose an industry and a company that was interesting to me.

I would strongly recommend this course. It gives great insight into the scale and scope of climate change and how it affects business. Even if that does not interest you for your career, the class is vry interesting and the professor is very engaging.

I was really pleased to hear about science and sit on a lecture during the first weeks of this class. I really enjoyed it, as it was my only class at Haas with a classic teaching setting, learning every minute about the science of the earth. Drew has incredible knowledge on diverse topics (from science to strategy and innovation), which contributes
immensely to the discussions!
Yes, Drew offers an interesting window into this field.

Yes! This was a great course that presents a good baseline in climate science and some interesting approaches for what businesses can do about it. It was capped off with some great guest speakers in the last half of the class! Yes! I feel the class is good and has a lot of potential to be even better (given that this was the first time it was taught and the content is still evolving). Drew is very knowledgeable and a great teacher!

Yes - if you want a crash course in climate science and a lens through which to view how businesses can have a direct and indirect impact, this is an extremely thorough way to do so. Drew is extremely passionate, organized and clear. He is extremely invested in both the climate as well as furthering the learnings of his students, and this shows with the thoughtful discussions he encourages and the carefully crafted syllabus and content and ucrates.
It is an excellent class, recommended for everyone. Even if you're not planning to pursue
climatetech/energy/sustainability full-time, this class is extremely good as it teaches you the science and impacts of climate change in every aspect of business.
Yes! Expert in the field you taught the concepts in a way that was interesting, fun, and inspiring
This course is fundamental for the world we live in now, a must-take.
This class is a MUST for everyone going through the MBA. Major life & business decisions will be questioned in this class, and it is extremely effective at fusing science with business.
Yes - every student should know the basics of climate change

The first part of the class that covers the science behind climate change was extremely engaging and worthwhile. It made me realize that I didn't have as much of a grasp on the subject as I thought. Unfortunately the class went down hill for me from there, although I'm still glad that I took it overall. The guest speakers towards the end were interesting but the middle of the course felt not well planned out.
Yes. I enjoyed learning about the science behind climate change and learning from the perspective of businesses to address climate change.
if this course were better developed and planned then yes i would recommend this to a fellow student. however, the class is much more focused on climate science than business strategy applications.
Yes! Great course, great guest speakers, the course will continue to improve over time. Professors Isaacs is a wealth of knowledge.

Climate change is one of the major challenges of our generation and this course provides an excellent introduction into the science of climate and how businesses can take action. This is still a new course and that comes through in the refinement of the homework assignments and lecture material. Prof Isaacs brings in some top notch guest lecturers for the last third of the class.

I think this class will be great in a year or two after it ungoes some more tweaking. I wish we focused more on business strategy. Heavy emphasis on climate science on the beginning which is important but it felt like we were missing the translation to applicable business strategy.
Yes

No, overall I think needs some work and should not be a three credit course. However, it depends on what you are looking for. If you are looking for a course that will explain the basics of climate change and you don't have a technical background in the subject, this is a digestible course that will certainly inform you on he subject. However, the second part on business strategy lacked structure and centered around group discussions or guest speakers. This content would be better covered by going through examples and deep dives on how companies are addressing climate
change through case studies, however we only had two out of five studies since they were still being written. Yes, very much needed part of Haas studies

Take this course! A mix of environmental science and practical business application makes an interesting and relevant course. Professor Isaacs brings invaluable knowledge and enthusiasm that makes the class worthwhile.
Great class for those who long for a dose of science in their MBA experience. Some form of this class needs to be added to the core curriculum.

Yes! Great course great instructor. The subject matter is easily digestible and is about a great topic. Issacs presents a daunting subject with ease and allows for open discussion over a range of climate topics
Awesome course! Engaging lectures and important material.
Yes! One of the best classes I've ever taken.
Absolutely.
Yes absolutely, this class made me refocus my interests towards sustainability at Haas! Climate change is a global issues for all industries, this should be a core class
Yes, I would recommend. The professor has great story telling skills and will convert a layman to a climate expert by the end of the course!

I would definitely recommend this course and Drew. I think it can be described as "Climate Change 101", since it is essential to set a strong base knowledge about the science behind Climate Change. Drew is really knowledgeable and passionate about the topic and explains that science exceptionally.

This course should be part of the core curriculum, and would be particularly useful for students who would not necessarily think of taking a climate change class in the first place! I really hope that Haas will take that step in making this compulsory for all students, given how urgent climate change is and how important it is for Haas too. However, I would have found the class more valuable if it had been a 6-week class instead of 15 weeks, as it felt repetitive after the first few sessions.

I would absolutely recommend this course! Professor Isaacs is clearly passionate about climate change and is excited to share his extensive knowledge with students. The course is well-organized in terms of structure and lectures. There are a decent amount of writing assignments, but I learned a ton, and I now feel very confident in my ability to dive deep on climate-related business topics.
This needs to be a core course, with some modifications.
How can MBA graduates from HAAS not go through this course?

Yes, but with caution -- this is a 101 level course with more climate change focus than business strategy Maybe. It resulted in a ton of learning, and the science portion was awesome. However, the course was disorganized after the science portion ended, and I feel like I never really got to understand good business strategies to address climate change. There was a ton of work outside of the class with substantial amounts of writing, which was never brought up, and just felt like busywork.
I do think professor Isaacs is AMAZING though. He's an outstanding lecturer who clearly knows his stuff, and cares immensely about his students.
Overall, as an intro course to climate change it is very good, but be mindful of the work.
Yes! Absolutely recommend this course, Drew is a fantastic instructor
This should class should be part of the core program for FT MBAs. Don't graduate without taking a Climate Change class like this one!
Yes, this is a great intro class on the science around climate change which is fundamental if you want to work in the sustainability space. 100% worth your time.
Yes. Super impactful content and Professor Isaac is both very knowledgeable in this subject and very engaged with students.
I would recommend this course because it is relatively low lift and the topic is interesting, but it's important to know that the depth of climate knowledge you will gain is also high level.

This is the best course I have taken at Haas. Andrew's biggest strength is his ability to share the most complex scientific ideas in the most simple way, catered to students with non-scientific business backgrounds. He is abreast with the latest happening in the climate change space and his effort in putting that information forward in class for us is obvious. He is well-connected in the climate space and gives the students access to knowledgeable speakers. He has shaped the class very thoughtfully starting with the basics, ultimately making us think hard about the climate policy of the businesses we pursue after MBA. He leaves you with the superpower to convince anyone on this planet of the reality of climate change and calling out the bogus solutions in place.

This class is essential for learning the basic language of climate. Even if you are not pursuing a career in a directly related field, this is an excellent class to "level set" understanding of the current state of the climate change problem. I learned a tremendous amount and the class was one that I looked forward to each week.
This course should be taught as a core class.

This is a good introductory course to climate change and its effects on businesses. But it is very introductory so if you already know something about the topic, it will feel repetitive. And the workload is not trivial.

If you have 0 knowledge of climate change, this class is for you. If you have any curiosity or general competency in climate change, don't take this class. Unfortunately, the class is not about business strategy. There are no sections on supply chain innovation or other particular part of business resilience or risk. Further, there's no class time spent on how to put together a climate strategy for your company. The speakers that come in are mostly white males and some are completely irrelevant to climate change. I don't know why this is a Haas class.

If you've worked with climate tech or in the geosciences, much of this class will be redundant information. The class is a fantastic introduction to understanding climate science, but it is extremely light on the business tools and strategy that you might want in your career. Want to know if carbon credits are bad and why? This class has you covered. Want to understand CA's Low carbon fuel standard and it's impact on business costs or the IRA? The class will disappoint. The class does have some guest speakers that are worth slogging through the rest of the class. The instructor is a scientist and can be condescending on topics where he likely knows less than his students; it isn't a dealbreaker but you should be warned. If you want to work in any climate-adjacent field, this class is likely worthwhile, but temper expectations a bit.

Yes, this should be a required course for everyone attending any business school. Climate change is the most pressing issue of our time and is directly relevant to businesses and business decisions related to risk, opportunities, and social resiliency.

It's great to learn about the science of climate change but the business strategy component falls short - if you are looking for actionable takeaways rather than only the science, there might be better courses

If you know nothing about climate change, this is a great survey course on climate science. If you already know a lot of the science, you might find the class content slightly lacking. That being said, Drew is an engaging lecturer so if nothing else it's a fun time.
To understand the science behind climate change, carbon credits, etc - I'd definitely recommend it. If you are trying to learn the business strategy part of it, then this class is not for you.

Yes- this class should be a requirement for anyone working in climate tech or anyone that wants to take on climate change. A fundamental understanding of the cause, effects, and levers at play is absolutely necessary to make proper change. Sadly, there are many initiatives underway that clearly do not rest on a sound foundation of the problem at hand and therefore are failing to make meaningful impacts. This class gives students the ability to spot balls from strikes.
Yes, I think this class should be a core class
The first few sessions on science were really strong and great to have learnt. The sessions on business strategy were less helpful, but overall, I'm really glad I took this course!
Yes - a lot of learning about the most important topic business should face in our lifetime.
Yes definitely. This course resulted in substantial learning and I feel much more able to have intelligent climate conversations.

I'd recommend the first 5-6 weeks ("the science"); the last 5-6 weeks ("business strategy") were a miss. Consider auditing the first classes instead of taking the course, although it's fairly low lift and also contributes to Sust'y certificate, so may be worth it for you:)

100%! If you are interested in climate, understanding the science behind it is essential. Andrew makes it look so simple and really gets you thinking about solutions that have the most vs the least impact.

Everyone needs to take a version of a climate change and business strategy course at Haas. It impacts every area of business and to leave Haas without understanding the basics of climate change, how it impacts your role, and what your company can do to transition would be a crime. Drew Isaacs does a great job of breaking these concepts down and challenging preconceived notions. You will never be the same after this course.

While this course is a good dive into the science of climate change, it was severely lacking when it came to business solutions. I know that this is partly because there aren't many good solutions right now, but I wished that there was more of a focus on what is working and/or what could work, no matter the scale. Overall, the tone of the class was too fatalistic and academic. This was the course that I was most curious about this semester, but I was disappointed by the lack of solutions and the same rhetoric each week. If the course content stays the same, the course needs to just be called "Climate Change" and only worth 1 or 2 units max.
I would definitely encourage students to take this class. It is very useful to understand climate change and its drivers and what we can do as individuals and professionals to tackle it.

Yes. If you do not have a science background and want a crash course in the fundamentals of climate change, you should totally take this course. This course equipped me with the knowledge to have thoughtful conversations on climate change, mitigation strategies, and emerging technologies. I'll definitely take this experience with me in my career.

I would recommend Drew because he is a passionate, engaging, knowledgeable, and friendly speaker on climate change. However, the course "Climate Change & Business Strategy" was mostly focused on climate change and under–delivered on business strategy, so depending on your interests, you may wish to take a different course.

Yes? Drew is a legend. Wonderful professor, caring, thoughtful. Really great guest speakers. A lot of writing but thats preferred over group assignments and tests. Drews assignments allowed us to go deep into the readings. Overall really fantastic class? def. a highlight at Haas and such an important subject. As future business leaders we need to understand climate change.

This is a "high effort, high reward" class that is perfect for any aspiring sustainability or climate leader. Everyone should have this knowledge, but if you're more casually interested in the content then take a good look at the syllabus before signing up, as the workload last year was substantial (weekly 1–page single spaced reflection on readings, plus three 2000–word research papers).

Yes! I found out about this course from a fellow student, which is why I wanted to take it. I'm an MPH student as well so this class is not well–known among my cohort, but I'm very glad I was in the know and took it. I learned so much and it was a fun environment.

Take this class if you want to learn about climate change, why it's important, and what's being done right now to address it. Also a great place to learn where there are shortcomings in addressing climate change and connecting with others who want to make a change in the business community to address these shortfalls. Yes, excellent course to understand climate change and the professor is great at explaining

Yes, totally! If you are curious about climate change and its impact on any sector, this is a very good course, I would absolutely recommend this class to everyone! I feel like where we are right now is 1998, right before the internet. Climate solutions are about to explode (they already have been to some extent!) and the space needs people from all backgrounds to be educated about the biggest problems, misconceptions, and opportunities. I learned SO much and I thought I was already quite educated in this space. I will not stop talking about my learnings from this class to anyone who will listen – it will change your life, just take it! And PS – Drew is amazing, the workload is so manageable, and the people are all really great too:)

Yes! Climate change is more relevant than ever as company's begin to grapple with real–world impacts on ESG strategies and investor expectations. This class provides an invaluable baseline to speak intelligently on both the climate science and the business impacts derived from climate change.

Yes, I would recommend this course to every MBA student. Climate Change is going to affect how many businesses operate (either from a viability point of view, compliance, regulation, etc). I thought the course and instructors gave a solid overview of the science behind Climate Change and then spent a lot of the focus area on how this would affect various aspects of business as well as what opportunities there are in this growing industry. For someone like me with little professional experience in this area, it was eye opening and useful to learn about.

I would absolutely recommend Drew to fellow students. Drew brings a lot of energy to the classroom. He does a good job of simultaneously keeping things light but serious all at the same time. I think that's incredibly important when talking about climate because it keeps people engaged even when the information is somewhat upsetting.

This course NEEDS to become core. Haas doesn't have a cohesive, fundamental understanding of the levers which need to be pulled to address climate change. While there are some things that could be tweaked to make it a more cohesive core course, this class is a must-take.
This class is a great introduction to climate science and definitely deepened my understanding of the topic. Definitely! This is the most valuable course I have taken at Berkeley Haas so far.
I would recommend it to those who wish to delve into climate change and sustainability. It is informative and must to know as a professional

Yes - this is a great course for deepening your understanding of climate change and how it impacts the business landscape. Though it felt repetitive at times, its an important reminder of the severity and inspires personal and professional action.

The class is efficient, discussing many topics which are relevant to business, such as greenwashing, carbon offset, and renewable energy. These topics are an indispensable part of the ESG of a company, especially a big or international company.

If you're already familiar with climate change, this class isn't for you. There isn't new information or insight on what climate change business strategies look like, just a bunch of facts and figures about how climate change is impacting the world. If you don't know about climate change, this class also isn't for you. The workload is heavy and includes weekly written assignments, 3 research papers, and case studies that require independent research.
Absolutely, highly recommended to better understand all the nuances of climate change science and technologies and methods being used for mitigation.

I absolutely would. Andrew Isaacs is definitely one of the most knowledgeable climate scientists I've met and being able to gain knowledge first-hand from him was awesome! His enthusiasm, energy, sense of humor and style of teaching were great!

Yes, I highly recommend the course if you are to go into climate. It really touches on the fundamentals of climate change. It goes beyond, the earth is getting warmer and so we must do something about it but to the depth of why things are happening and the key levers that are necessary to fight it.

Yes, I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. Andrew Isaacs's course is invaluable for anyone who wants to become a better engineer, role model, or advocate for environmental sustainability. It provides a comprehensive understanding of climate change and equips students with the tools to address its challenges effectively. The course not only enhances technical and business knowledge but also inspires students to make a positive impact on society by fostering innovation and awareness.
100% - one of the best classes I've taken at Haas. Should be part of the core moving forward, it's incredibly important material from a career and life perspective.
Yes! incredible course with a really useful explanation of climate basics and a fantastic lecturer

sections.goodFor: Students wanting foundations in climate change and how companies are acting on it - including where companies mislead people about their actions.
sections.notFor: Students not broadly interested in climate topics - classes can drag when a given session's topic is outside your interest. Thin evidence (4 comments).
sections.workloadNote: Not discussed - only 4 comments, three of them one line. One notes class sessions can feel long when the day's topic does not interest you.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.quote: The classes can feel long if the topic is not one you're interested in but overall the course encapsulates a lot over the semester.
comments: Yes
Yes, I would recommend as it provides a very detailed picture about the climate change and how companies are trying to take actions and/or mislead people
yes

Climate change is foundational for all future business leaders and for any students that would like to learn foundations, this is a great course to take. The classes can feel long if the topic is not one you're interested in but overall the course encapsulates a lot over the semester.

Yes I will recommend but, also highlight that this course is intensive in term of hours spent. Sometimes it may take up to 10-11 hours per week. On average, due to smaller team of just 2- we had to spend more time to get things done. It became overwhelmed. Would be great to have more people to join the class.

I really recommend this class. It's stressful and time-consuming with this weekly deadline to get 8 interviews (or as much as we can). But apart from that it's a very unique experience, interactive and a chance to have this learning on how to get out of the building. This class completed all my learning objectives and radically changed the way I would start any entrepreneurial journey now.

I would definitely recommend both instructors! I learned a lot from this class and believe there's a wide variety of projects to cater to your interests and still focus on customer discovery. I would also highly suggest speaking with the inventor/mentor about their availability/expectations when choosing your semester-long project.
Yes i would, the instructors and the course are very well designed and will give you real world experience when doing customer discovery and building a business model for the startups

I would definitely recommend this course and these awesome instructors. The class is extremely engaging, and the course itself makes you exposed to the methods needed to speak to people in industries. If you have any social anxiety about speaking to people and cold calling and emailing, this class will fix that through exposure and make you much more confident in yourself and your speaking abilities. It really teaches you the methods needed to learn about cool people, industries, and the problems in those industries. Highly highly recommend taking this course, but make sure you have a good trustworthy team because the time spent interviewing is quite a lot, so you need a good team to spread out work!
I would definitely recommend this course. I was able to gain a lot of experience and knowledge both from within and outside the class.
I would

The highlight of this course is to work with students outside of Haas and explore industries outside of software through rapid learning and interviews. I have not taken a course like this before and applying the Lean Startup methodology was a valuable experience in the context of a future startup.
Yes. It pushes you out of your comfort zone and the teachings are valuable

I would recommend, I learned so much from this class, this knowledge and the connections I have made are invaluable. Great course for learning how to do customer discovery interviews - will force you to push yourself to find and speak with people
It requires A LOT of effort for just a 2 credit course
Yes.

(1) The world needs more people who can translate scientific inventions into market! I haven't taken a science class since high school, and 12 years later, I was speaking to CXOs at synthetic biology companies. You can do it! It was very disappointing to see EVERY HAAS STUDENT except two drop the class. This is a Haas course, mind you. We're at the best research institution in the world! Why aren't everyone trying to learn more about cutting-edge patented technologies?

(2) Any Lean Business Canvas courses - I highly recommend. You learn so much about how to find and talk to people. Even the most introverted humans that don't want to talk to anyone at all would benefit from this class, just by becoming used to finding and talking to people and learning from them.
Yes I will recommend. This course helps us to understand customer discovery and market research in a very practical way.
Yes! I think it allowed me to exercise my muscles in business and reaching out to people just to ask questions. I think it's really unique and a great learning opportunity.
If you would like to learn the whole process of finding customer segments for technological seeds, this course would be super helpful.
But if you like to be focused on more theories or frameworks to find customers of startups, this might not be your course.

This is like any other 'lean' class - it's goal and learnings come from customer discovery via interviews. As such, it's a lot of work and your experience will be almost solely dependent on your teammates.
Would recommend
YES! Especially, if the student has an engineering or science background, because it is different from other technical courses.

This is a very valuable class to take. It will force you to get out of your comfort zone and talk to the industry. You will also learn how to be resilient and gritty. Trust me, lots of emails and linkedins will be sent and a very small percentage of them will respond. Overall this is a critical class if you ever want to create a start up
Yes great learning experience and very interactive

I would recommend the course for experience in customer discovery. However, I would inform them they must pay $100 for software to access the class content and videos. I think this model is unfair. I see the value in paying for Innovations Within for the business canvas features, however, I believe the presentations and videos to prepare for class should be published on Bcourses.

I would recommend to a fellow student given it is an excellent introduction to the lean process, however it is very customer discovery interview heavy and perhaps this took away from some of the learning given how much time it required outside of class.
Yes- 10/10. probably the only Haas class you need to take as a non-MBA student.
Yes. Mostly because it is practical. I learnt a lot. Being an introvert, it was challenging in a good way to go out and talk to people. I also got to meet new people and make new friends
Yes as long as you have time during the semester to do the interviews
Course is great for networking opportunities as it forces you to be out there and find connections for interviews.

sections.goodFor: Students in any function (design, engineering, marketing, business) who want hands-on customer discovery and user-need research through real conversations outside school.
sections.notFor: Students who want structure, guidance and individual accountability; one says Startup Disco teaches the same skill set in a weekend.
sections.workloadNote: Team customer-discovery project structured entirely around the business model canvas; no individual assignments, only progress presentations, so effort depends on your team and project choice.
sections.gradingBasis: Progress presentations only - no individual assignments, which one student says lets teammates slack without consequence.
sections.redFlags: More structure and guidance wanted (2); no individual assignments means teammates can slack (1); value hinges on choosing a project you actually care about (3 say so).
sections.quote: Your experience solely depends on your team dynamic and you pretty much have to do everything on your own.
comments: Yes! If you are interested in anything design, engineering, marketing, business, etc... This class is essential to understanding market research and user needs. However, it is key to chose a project that interests you.

Ofcourse! This was a great experience overall. I would prefer a bit more structure and guidance. Your experience solely depends on your team dynamic and you pretty much have to do everything on your own. There are no individual assignments, just presentations to update on progress, so some team members tend to slack and this can be quite frustrating and discouraging. As long as you are willing to give it your all, you will have a good experience. The entire class spins around the business model canvas, so if that is something you are interested in, go for it. If not, take the weekend starup dsico. I took both and startup disco pretty much teaches you all the necessary skill sets. Yes, good experience talking to people outside of school and haven't had any interaction with
Yes- both were great. It has been the best course I've taken so far.
Yes, because it is a course where you learn through experience.
I would but I would make sure to tell the students to be intentional with the project selections; it should mean something to them and really make them curious.
I would recommend this to other students because doing customer discovery and understanding user need is the most important part of any business. Regardless of what role you work.
Yes I would recommend very unique and in depth perspectives

Yes, in this class you can learn the basic structure of the business model and let you know how an early-stage startup needs to approach when they are trying to find their customers' needs. But you need to be familiar with the resources and choose an ideal topic, or you may not gain the result you want. Besides, the whole process is to some degree iterative.

Yes - this was one of my most amazing classes I've taken at Haas. I think that it provides such a depth of personal and interpersonal learning outside of any class. This is not a business class but more so a life class. I think that I learned more about being a leader and being a strong human than any other class at Haas. This class does require you to take it very seriously to get the most benefit out of it plus honoring the effort your fellow students put into it. I would not take this class if you are not committed to showing up. I would take this class if you are looking to learn more about how you can connect more deeply with other people.

I highly highly highly recommend this course. I think it should be mandatory. The amount of connection built among the group in such a short time is incredible, I've struggled with connection and belonging my whole life and this course created a safe place to feel "buoyed" and held by others. This is such an emotionally driven course and some precaution should be taken as there are likely things under the surface that will come up. This course is really counter- culture and goes against the social conditioning we've had our whole lives. We talk about deeply personal things, we focus on deep listening and ensuring everyone feels heard. I can't think of a better example of what Haas stands for than this course, because this is the course that most exemplifies "confidence without attitude". Before taking it, I was interested to get someone else's feedback and shocked to learn that "they couldn't recommend it" because of some things that came up in their course. I feel sad knowing that valuable lessons were not taken away from that experience, because I know Erica would have done her best to encourage connection instead of disconnection. I can't recommend this course enough, it really was a powerful experience. The downside is that it's a lot of effort, these things take a lot of work. The homework is challenging and reflective and you will feel tired throughout the days of the workshop. But it is so worth it.

Yes - this course requires significant energy, but the material is very interesting and fulfilling. I would recommend this course for anyone who wants to have a positive impact on their team (and anyone around them, really), and wants to learn how to advocate for themselves and resolve conflicts for the long-term with mutual understanding and appreciation.

I learned a lot from group practicing where I would never have had the opportunity to practice otherwise. But there're just too many assignments -- before, during, and after classes. Sometimes, I feel overwhelmed by the mental energy put in this class, especially the 2nd week where we had day-long classes for 3 days.

I would highly recommend this instructor and course because to be quite frank, I feel now that I have the tools to improve the relationships I have and to form strong connections with the people I have yet to meet! Erica really allows you to explore and examine the factors that have shaped your identity, and she provides data-driven research related to the emotions that we feel. It's a wonderful class to take, and I truly have learned so many things that I'll keep with me for the rest of my life.

I would 100% recommend this class. This class can really change how to interact with families, friends, and colleagues. I would recommend this course, but I think it could be slightly better in person. Zoom gives way to not paying attention.
Wonderful course and instructor, Erica is great!
Came into this class dealing with some past trauma and some recent trauma, thought this course was just about communication, that's it.

But this course ended up being a powerful experience in which I was granted the rare opportunity to interact with strangers and classmates in a highly structured setting, and also ask tough questions of others. Ended up learning a great deal about myself!
Yes and I am sure the course will be even more engaging in person in Amsterdam than virtually
We didn't get to go to the netherlands this year, but I thought this was an interesting and fast way to get exposure to the design thinking process.

Yes! Take this class if you are looking into developing a faster framework to view insights and business problems and have an iterative process on hand at your next job or internship. It helped me think as a future business leader how to approach problems in a multi-disciplinary approach and it could be seen in what other groups presented, from CPG to experiential in-store experiences, and technology solutions, a lot of these aspects could be implemented to push the "healthy-eating habits" that the brief asked. Lots of room to get creative!
Yes, this is an effective course to learn and apply Design Thinking principles with an optimal workload. There were no unnecessary exercises or assignments.

Rajiv and Sam were great instructors. It is a shame that this class was virtual because I feel like you miss out a lot on the excitement of the subject matter by being tied to a screen. Obviously no ones fault and the entire teaching team did their best to bring the subject to life. Definitely recommend this as an in person experience.
Yes the class resulted in learnings

I would highly recommend it. The learning is substantial, but also depends upon your team a little bit. I was fortunate to have a good time which really put in the time and used the resources. You can apply the skills learnt from this course to any kind of work, but it has huge application for entrepreneurship and consulting.

I would only recommend taking this course if you can do it in person. It is difficult to get what you want out of work like this when you're distributing it via all-day virtual sessions a month apart.

Great instructors. Course is super valuable if someone wants to learn and experience design thinking first hand. I would have preferred in person Netherlands though, because there is lot of collaboration work and the experience of seeing/feeling problems we are trying to solve in real is super critical. I do not recommend this course if it is online only version, otherwise definitely worth taking this class.

I would, but really wish that we were able to experience this in NL, especially since it should make up such a large portion of the course fees. Or, have the opportunity to visit THNK in the future when the pandemic is over! Yes, the virtual experience was pretty good and I would imagine the experience would have been great if it was in Netherlands Experiencing the problem and culture first hand in Netherlands would have made it the perfect class. Yes, but only if it's in-person.

Absolutely, this has been one of the most impactful classes I've taken at Haas. It crystallized so many learnings for me, and was a great applied innovation course for anyone interested in the design thinking framework. I loved the focused, time-intensive structure of the program to maximize engagement.
Yes, it is a fun and challenging class which pushed me out of my comfort zone and allowed me to experience a culture I never have before.

I would recommend this course but would high suggest some major improvements. The ad-hoc free flow style is not ideal for MBA students. Days and events should be clear and not ambiguous at all. The thinking and activities to get you outside your comfort zone are good and welcomed.
Yes! Resulted in a great learning experience that was hands on and challenged our way of thinking

I would recommend this class to other students who are not only interested in designing innovative solutions but also who work in established company. Some of the concepts could also apply to problems in established company. Of course, spending time in Amsterdam was super fun!
100%. The most immersive and I think most fun/beneficial course I?ve taken at Haas.

Yes, absolutely. It's been extremely valuable for me to have one short intense study immersive experience, and I wish there was at least one option open to all Haas students every semester. It has been so enriching for me to be outside of a familiar environment and to stretch myself in a way I haven't for a while.

Yes. I honestly think that Haas needs to eliminate the other required design courses (the 2 day required design course for part time program and we innovate) and replace those courses with a version of this. This was so much more helpful and practical. I thought the other courses were a waste of time that I did not learn anything in. As a result of those courses I was very skeptical of this course, but it turned out to be amazing.
Maybe. Depends on how passionate you are about design thinking and what the prompt is. I had a great experience, but am not sure every bschool person will.
Yes i would?it?s an awesome immersive experience!
Yes
Yes, great way to learn and apply design thinking skills with a practical prompt.
