I would recommend this class to anyone looking to experience a different culture, teaching methodology, and learn more about how to apply design thinking. I enjoyed the challenge of working for the third party client and the process of the intro to the final presentation was well worth the journey. This class allowed me to get out of my standard day to day ways of approaching problems, and learn toolsets I can take back to my job. Amsterdam was also a beautiful city and made the experience well worth it.

Yes. The unique opportunity to learn about a new culture while also learning about a new design thinking/systems design framework - something inherent in this course - is amazing. I also really loved the challenge this year - it was right on point with my intersection of interests and the role I think business should play in social impact. Yes. This class truly makes you learn about design thinking and how to innovate with the method.
Yes! This class is so much fun, especially in a new country. It?s also a great opportunity to network with people not in the full time MBA program.
100% recommend to students who are interested in design thinking or try to learn things in a way that is more room for creativity and innovation

Yes! This course was a great learning experience in design thinking and allowed you to delve into the process without interruption for a week. If you've already done a lot of this work in the past it might not be anything revolutionary, but it's still deeply useful/fun/insight-provoking to have protected time to engage in this type of process and to share the experience with fellow students. Your team definitely makes a difference (for me, in a very positive way!) so just be aware of that when going into the course.
I highly recommend Sam for teaching experiential learning classes. The content, assignments, and classroom flow works really well.
Take this class if you want a thorough crash course in what Design Thinking is! ITS SO FUN AND EYE OPENING!! Would recommend spending both the weekend before and after to enjoy the city.

Absolutely! However, it really is meant for someone open to engaging with new creative ways of problem solving and the right attitude in processing the content so it may not be for everyone depending on their expectations and openness to a very different format for learning. I think it could be valuable for everyone to experience but it is also greatly dependent on their willingness to get messy in the process.

Sam's ability to bridge theoretical knowledge with real-world applications transformed the learning experience, making it not only relevant but immediately applicable for all participants. His teaching style was highly engaging, providing invaluable coaching and a suite of practical frameworks that participants could directly apply to their professional contexts.

I HIGHLY recommend this class to anyone who wants to know more about design thinking. I'd say it is a even amazing experience to do this in Amsterdam. You don't get many opportunities to have a class with experimental projects with real clients in a foreign country with your classmates and some more from other programs at Haas otherwise you might not. I took IBD as well and I love both but I want to say this one is more well organized and you do go home with takeaways without while IBD has some unpredictable factors - random assignment of project, country, team members, clients, workload, and your experiences really depends. (although I enjoyed my IBD) Fair workload, a tons of learning, unforgettable experiences, but 2 units, take it!

Yes! Best class taken in Haas, also will recommend FT student to take, since it's a good chance to meet EW friend here. Yes I would recommend. It's important to get out of the confines of Berkeley and California and experience a different culture and different business climate. Anchor on that first and the content second.
Really good course on design sprint, highly recommend
Sure
Yes! To students looking to explore PM or PMM.
Yes! He is a fun instructor, figuring out his voice in lectures. As he iterates, I'm sure he will get more comfortable teaching!
The THNK faculty was wonderful too and he did a great job collaborating with them during the week to provide us a fun environment!
Yes absolutely. One of the best courses I've taken at Haas

The course is quite expensive, costing $7,000 in fees, not including the additional expenses for travel, accommodation, and other costs in Amsterdam. In total, it adds up to almost $10,000 for a 5-day course. I'm unsure if it's worth the investment. Perhaps it would make more sense to have the THNK instructors come to the Bay area in the US, which could potentially be more cost-effective. While the course content is helpful, I believe it should be more affordable for students in terms of the overall cost.
Go for it. This experiential learning has so much to offer that you can apply on your day to day job.
Yes I would!!

Absolutely recommend it if you're looking to learn Design Thinking, along with an experential learning of working on a real corporate challenge. Also Amsterdam is beautiful - It was great to be in this compressed zone with fellow students and be immersed in the challenge and come up with solutions. The course is very active with very little in the way of lectures - it's mostly learn by doing which I really loved. 100% recommend!

Would highly recommend this course. I feel that anyone, regardless of background or experience level, can take away so much from the class and learn about how to think more creatively and design solutions. Out of the Haas classes I've taken, this one has expanded my mind the most.

I would absolutely recommend this class and Sam as an instructor! I've actually been incredibly interested about this class since even before I applied to Haas, and so I've had high excitement for it - and it's gone above and beyond what I would've expected. In this class you really are encouraged to stretch yourself, your mindset and perspectives, and your ways of thinking and innovating in a safe, friendly space, with an amazing group of instructors and peers. Everything in this class is immediately applicable in the real world as well, and though as a design sprint it's a lot of things that you go through during the week, the team does an incredible job of helping you to process and absorb all of the learnings. I'm actually shocked at how much we were able to learn and achieve in this short time frame, and it's a sentiment shared by everyone in this class that I've spoken with. Sam did an excellent job facilitating us and our learnings - we all always felt comfortable under his instruction, and that we were heard and understood and listened to. I really appreciate how he took us through the course and his leadership style; he'd coach and guide us through, and create innovative ways for us to gain all of these incredible learnings. So yes in summary, I would totally recommend Design Sprint for Corporate Innovation and absolutely recommend Sam Ha as a Professor:)

sections.goodFor: Students who want hands-on design-thinking and innovation tools, a consultant-for-a-week experience, and an international/cultural break from normal Haas classes.
sections.notFor: Introverts who find high-intensity workshops overstimulating (1 explicit), and anyone who needs structure or expects a polished final idea out of one week.
sections.workloadNote: One-week immersive sprint in Amsterdam run with the THNK school: build and test a prototype for a real client in a week. Scrappy and workshop-style with very little structure.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the work is the week-long team prototype and client problem. No exams mentioned.
sections.redFlags: Caveats rather than defects: deliberately low structure and fail-fast pacing, and one notes it can be overstimulating for introverts. Set expectations that a one-week output won't be brilliant.
sections.quote: It's scrappy and workshoppy and expect very little structure and a way of trying things and failing fast.
comments: Yes. Great course with real experience
Yes. THNK particularly. Rod and Alyssa are very well experienced and it felt eased to do the practices under their guidance in class.

Yes. If you are looking for an opportunity to learn design thinking, improve your knowledge of it and explore different tools, this is the right class for you. I loved that we built and tested a prototype all in one week.
I highly recommend applying for this hands-on course. The class is very diverse. Content is will structured and applicable.
100% recommend this course! It was a great way to get out of the usual day-to-day of Haas. It exposed me to new ideas, new places, and new people - basically, what Haas is all about.
Yes! It was fun, professional and organized - a good balance from real world experiences, educational and also experience a foreign culture!
Absolutely give this course a try if you are looking for inspiration to lead change through innovation. The frameworks are super helpful to implement in any function.

I would definitely recommend this class! The THNK school is amazing and I loved our topic and how it was related to sustainability and consumer products. The THNK school provided us with experiences and tools to explore many new concepts and ideas. This class also got me super excited about exploring entrepreneurship (although not directly related to it), so happy with my decision to take the class!
Yes - it was a great course. One of my favorite experiences of my time at Haas.

It's a decent class to take to get a new perspective on how to innovate and have design thinking to problem solving. It's scrappy and workshoppy and expect very little structure and a way of trying things and failing fast. Worthwhile. The class is highly engaging and can be overstimulating for some introverts, but a great introduction on innovation. Safe and fun environment to pilot innovation concepts.
Along with Embodied Leadership is the course that I've got out the most during Haas.
High value course. Don't miss. Tons of frameworks and insights to be learned in a practical way. An opportunity to experience being a consultant for a week and apply all the learnings.
I would highly recommend this course. It's a great real world application of innovation principles.
Absolutely recommend this course! Sam is a fantastic instructor and the THNK team is great. Highly interactive project-based course.

This is a valuable course if you're interested in real innovation techniques and tools. You need to adjust your expectations that your final product idea will be the best idea you've ever had — impossible in one week — but if you're in it for the process then this is a great way to learn and do in real time for a real client and real problem. The instructor Sam has great innovation industry experience and has curated this class so intentionally and in a way that will help MBA students to think differently about what the true value of design-thinking and consulting services should be.

sections.goodFor: Students who want an intense, hands-on design-thinking and idea-generation experience abroad, and who like being pushed out of their comfort zone with real city/AI stakeholders.
sections.notFor: People wanting a directly transferable skill - one says design thinking doesn't suit every org or role. Leadership games can frustrate, and the immersive format brings real highs and lows.
sections.workloadNote: Week-long immersive sprint in Amsterdam, not weekly hours; full days of THNK-run discovery-to-prototyping work, leadership games and daily reflections. Constant time pressure reported.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; daily reflections and team sprint deliverables are the visible work
sections.redFlags: 1 student reports favoritism and says teams with consultants had an advantage; 1 says exercises need more fluidity; several note constant time pressure and frustrating leadership games.
sections.quote: On the downsides be prepare to play a lot of leadership games (that sometimes can feel frustrated), constantly feel like you don't have enough time
comments: Yes, good immersive experience on real-world project
If you want o see your ideas come to fruition in small and fast paced manner, while enjoying those small wins, this class is a perfect blend of theories and practice.
Yes!! Sam was an excellent instructor

Yes, this course is very experiential and impactful but if please bring your full self without distractions as this can make a real difference in your mental models. While everyday being in Amsterdam may look fun, use the daily reflections properly to carry forward the learnings long term.

The class teaches a fascinating way to focus on the idea generation and user need. Often, we are focused soley on creating solutions at work from a problem statement. It's rare to spend a bulk of the time actually going through the motions of asking questions, thinking about user needs, and coming to form ideas rather than trying to nail a problem. Yes absolutely! Sam makes learning fun! He shared innovation concepts through understandable and memorable exercises that I'll be able to use in my daily work moving forward!
I would recommend this course for someone with prior consulting experience as a lot of teams had consultants and it put them at an advantage. There is also favoritism so be mindful of that.

Yes, I would wholeheartedly recommend this course. It was an awesome way to push me out of my comfort zone and force me to focus on listening to needs and ideating rather than jumping to solutions which is something I love to do. I got to hands on vibe code which is valuable and fun. I also was forced to constantly think about more roles on teams and how to step back and let other ideas shine. I love the week long immersive course format, there is so much excitement and so much to learn when that's all that occupies your mind. It was also such a valuable way to understand other cultures through the lens of innovation and business. I don't know when I will have the opportunity to do something like this again. On the downsides be prepare to play a lot of leadership games (that sometimes can feel frustrated), constantly feel like you don't have enough time, and expect the highs and lows of an immersive experience like this one. Overall this class pushed me most out of my comfort zone of any class at Haas and really shakes up the traditional format for classes which is so fun.
I would definitely recommend the course. The ability to learn about leadership and innovation in practice in a new environment is very unique

Yes! Great week in Amsterdam. The THNK school is sort of like an IDEO, where you get to work on a case study and go through the full discovery to prototyping process. The stakeholders (in our case, the city of Amsterdam and AI professionals) were great! And the THNK staff (shout out to Edna who coordinated our great lunches) were super accommodating and personable. Fun design sprint, and useful whether you are a novice or familiar.
Yes
Yes; this was a fun, fast-paced course that was really focused on applied learning and different than any other classes I've taken at Haas.
Yes

Yes I would recommend Sam, I wish he taught some other courses because he brings a lot of fun and practical application to the course, which is sometimes lacking in other courses. You will gets hands on in his class and he will push you to improve and experiment in an enjoyable way.

Here you learned design thinking process, this is cool process but it's not suitable for every role and org. So to consider that before applying if you're truly want something practical it might not for you. But if you want a fun experience in Amsterdam this course can give you exactly that.
Yes. This is a very fun and educational experience. Being hands on in a meaningful project is all business graduates need to grow and work with a diverse group of people.
Yes, I would recommend Sam! He was a wonderful instructor.
Course would be better if there's increased fluidity to the exercises
Yes absolutely

Yes, I would. Well structured and thoughtful course. Kim's knowledge and accessibility during this course were incredible. This was a well-thought-out course. I love that we had access to real-world case and company experts during this course. We focus on historical cases a lot at Haas. This was a welcome change to assess the company's current problem and access the company stakeholders to fill knowledge gaps.
Yes, She is very intriguing to listen to and you can tell she has a particular love for this subject. I love the energy she brings to this class even though it is an 8-hour class.
I would recommend this class to anyone - deep dive on relevant topics with amazing speakers!
Yes, I would. I think that there's a lot of important concepts about the biotech industry that I didn't even know about prior to the course.
Yes. Great one-credit course with guest speakers talking about the latest trends in biotech and pharma.
Yes.

Great class, the guest speakers are AMAZING. I recommend doing the readings as there is just limited time for class discussions on all of it. We touched on so many topics within the healthcare space and I felt every student had something to provide and something special to take away.
Most certainly I would recommend to anyone with interest in pharma.
Yes would recommend to anyone interested in the industry

I highly highly highly recommend this course. I think it should be mandatory. The amount of connection built among the group in such a short time is incredible, I've struggled with connection and belonging my whole life and this course created a safe place to feel "buoyed" and held by others. This is such an emotionally driven course and some precaution should be taken as there are likely things under the surface that will come up. This course is really counter- culture and goes against the social conditioning we've had our whole lives. We talk about deeply personal things, we focus on deep listening and ensuring everyone feels heard. I can't think of a better example of what Haas stands for than this course, because this is the course that most exemplifies "confidence without attitude". Before taking it, I was interested to get someone else's feedback and shocked to learn that "they couldn't recommend it" because of some things that came up in their course. I feel sad knowing that valuable lessons were not taken away from that experience, because I know Erica would have done her best to encourage connection instead of disconnection. I can't recommend this course enough, it really was a powerful experience. The downside is that it's a lot of effort, these things take a lot of work. The homework is challenging and reflective and you will feel tired throughout the days of the workshop. But it is so worth it.

On a personal note, I consider it unprofessional to appeal to students' emotions right before a course evaluation. Attempting to influence students' feelings immediately before an assessment is a clear intent to skew evaluations. I do not recommend this course for three reasons:

The course does not encourage shared learning among students but rather promotes a unidirectional knowledge transfer from the professor to the class. I believe that part of the MBA experience should involve learning from both peers and professors, with the instructor acting as a mediator of conversation.

The tools introduced in this course unnecessarily complicate mathematical concepts to justify a quantitative framework. Moreover, there is no empirical evidence demonstrating the superiority of this framework over alternative approaches. For instance, when the course claimed that hyper-targeting is a better tool than A/B testing, no substantive evidence was provided to support this assertion. Instead, it appears to be an unnecessary complication designed to justify the course's existence or the need for a marketing department.

Finally, there is a significant disconnect between my professional experience and the content learned in class. I have rarely encountered metrics like BDI and CDI in my professional work. It would have been more beneficial to learn practical skills such as conducting customer insights surveys. The application of two-factor analysis seems highly subject to interpretation and yields few tangible actions. Furthermore, the course never addressed customer journey mapping or explored different communication channels and their respective strategies.

I would recommend this class if you are highly interested in a low lift entrepreneurship class where most of the value will come from meeting with your team and figuring out how to pitch to VCs at the end of the semester.

If you're interested in trying out Entrepreneurship and are focused on traditional startup fields like emerging tech or B2B Saas, it's probably a decent class. If you're focusing on a less traditional startup, including social enterprises, this class is not the best.

This class was really disappointing. It did not seem that Kurt was invested in the course or as invested as we expected him to be. He clearly knows a lot, but the teaching was not very practical after Darwin day. It did not help us learn how to interview customers, develop a product etc. It was only useful to think of an idea. From there we were on our own. I would not recommend.
First, I don't know how is this a low-lift class.. (maybe as an MBA Applied Innovation class?).

- It wasn't for me as it had weekly assignments (not worth a lot 2 points but if you are a good student you will be spending 1-3 hours every week for readings and the one pager for 9 weeks straight) and then the team assignment comes in while you are required to submit these weekly assignments..eventually the writing moved from article like to q&a without much impact on my score.. so make it simple

Second, the current structure of the class assignment doesn't make it easy for the team to work in collaboration until week 10 or 11.. and you don't know what other teams are working on until demo day..

Finally, the morning class starts at 8 AM but could finish way early 9 or 10 AM (post team formation) with the rest of time to be for team work. So the evening class makes a better option as it will be finishing early.

I would recommend the course for anyone with a strong idea who wants leadership experience working with a team and delivering a pitch presentation to real VCs. It is also a great opportunity to meet students in other masters programs at Berkeley. However, I would clarify that the lecture content is trivial and there is not much structure to the project work. You get out of this class what you put into it.

No. I would only recommend this class for individuals who have an idea that they are passionate about, and who are looking to work on that idea throughout the class. The class is very high-level, and doesn't have enough content to support the 14-week course length. Kurt can be a helpful advisor, but struggles to connect with students (especially women and people of color).
I would recommend this course. I thought it was a good intro to the entrepreneurship process and I learned a lot by going through the process.

This was extremely student paced/ led, which sort of makes sense when you think of a class titled "Entrepreneurship". However, we had little frameworks in place to succeed. You have to do a ton of readings and write a 1 page paper each week in addition to developing your concept; these felt like busy work. I had substantial learning from this, but the important caveat is your group makes/ breaks this class. Be sure to calibrate expectations upfront and be careful choosing your members.
Definitely would recommend this course! Whether you have a business idea or you just want to know more about the entrepreneurship process, this class will give you a deep dive.
No. I found this class boring. The lecture portion was just an anemic summary of standard entrepreneurial topics. I didn't learn very much and this isn't worth 3 units.

Absolutely! Even if you think entrepreneurship is not for you, I highly recommend taking this course as an eye opener and if for just the experience and pushing you outside of your comfort zone. This is probably the best course I've taken thus far at Haas
Yes, super helpful if you want to start your own company.
Would highly recommend even if you aren't planning to build a start-up currently
Absolutely it was so engaging

Hell yes. For one, every veteran must take a course with Professor Beyer because he will have your back and is a strong advocate for our community. Moreover, this class was an eye-opening experience for me as a military and finance professional. I was skeptical about the MBA until I found immense value in staying put at Berkeley and in the Bay Area because of Professor Beyer and my learnings in the Entrepreneurship class. I unequivocally recommend this class to my peers.
Yes!
Yes- especially if your pitch ends up being chosen. Even if not, it's a safe environment to see how you would function in a start-up environment.

I would strongly encourage this class. I feel prepared with a basic understanding of how a founder goes from identifying an opportunity through raising an initial round. I fundamentally have a different idea of what it means to be a founder/co-founder and feel much more confident in my ability to start a winning company. Also, I think this is a lighter lift than similar courses at Haas such as Lean Launch Pad.
Yes. A fun course, especially if you seriously want to build a business.
Yes definitely, great course for someone wanting to start their entrepreneurial journey, or for someone who wants to work for startups or for someone who wants to work in VC/PE.
Yes definitely a must course to take

Its a good introductory course but I wish we spent more time actually building things like financial models in class. I would only recommend it early on in your academic career - its not as valuable when you're about to graduate and you bring other people in the class down with your lack of motivation.
I would definitely recommend this course and the instructors to other students!
Yes
Yes, super knowledgeable and well prepared and answer any and all questions.

Yes. Great at the real-world application. You learn so much and it's fun, every single class was enjoyable. Yes - great class whether you see entrepreneurship in your future or not. Excellent content for what it takes to build a business.

Absolutely. You might think that the best way to start a business is to go start a business and not take a class on starting a business. You will learn so much from this class which are mistakes you want to avoid and things you need to do well. Kurt is a super star professor and has many valuable insights from his time as an Entrepreneur and is an excellent resource through out the course.

Yes, especially if they want to understand how to be an entrepreneur as well as understand the world of selling. yes! It helps anyone who has an idea to materialize achieve it step by step. The most amazing part is you probably find your partner in the class!
yes if you ever wondered if you had what it takes to create a start up, this class if for you. The next step is then figuring out if you want to

I would 100% recommend other students to take this course - You will not find a better way to simulate the process of starting a company. Kurt has extensive experience and through interesting guest speakers + the group project you will be much more knowledgeable about the entire ecosystem
Ye

Yes, good high-level intro to Entrepreneurship! A bit high workload for the actual learnings in the course. I already recommended it to some engineering friend because engineer we do not know a lot about business and having the point of view of founder it great teaching
Yes! I highly recommend both instructors and the course to fellow students.
This class is an excellent capstone for the entire mba experience
YES, great class. A must for Haasies. Do not miss this class by Dr Kurt Beyer and Shiva Somasundaram!
Yes, it's really the best flight sim for anyone interested in being an entrepreneur.

Interesting course, especially if you want to see if your business idea is ready for prime time or not. While a lot of VC work does take place online nowadays, the course being fully remote was challenging in my opinion. If i had my time again, I would have taken it in person.

I think this is a worthwhile class for people who have a startup idea that they would like a framework for pressure testing. That being said, if you do not get your project picked in Darwin day your overall motivation and gain from the course might go down. Overall fun, interesting, and has a lot of potential to add value to your startup idea. Yes
Yes recommend
Absolutely - great industry knowledge of startups and VC. Learning from people who didn't just study this but do it in their everyday lives. Learnings are fantastic.

I would not recommend this class online. The collaborations during the class felt quite forced, it was hard to connect to other students and frankly connect with the professors and guest speakers. Generally, it felt like a huge lost opportunity since a huge part of entrepreneurship is networking.
If someone was committed to starting a company, potentially for the feedback.

I would recommend this class to students with start-ups who want to grow their start-ups further, students with exceptional ideas, or students who want to work on others' start-up ideas. The best part of the class is getting to work on developing the start-up ideas, which is about half of the class.

This is a good class if you have an idea and want to vet it, or are interested in going through the motions on someone else's business. There are not rigid decks or financial models provided that are useful/universal. The lectures are okay; better if you have not taken many business classes as they cover basic business principles (blue ocean, demand space, pricing models, etc.).
Also, do not recommend this class online. I think the format really killed this session unfortunately.

Absolutely not. I hated this class. Part of it was because I think the online format is very terrible. Kurt tries to engage everyone by asking questions, but it just does not work. Also, in a class like this, I think it's critical to be able to meet your classmates, which naturally cannot happen. Another reason I disliked this class was that it was too theoretical. I liked the theory in the beginning, as it was helpful to learn a structured way to come up with an idea (thinking of macro trends and a blue ocean, etc.), but overall it was just too much. Moreover, if you're not familiar with the format - in the class you ultimately work on a business idea with a team. I think there wasn't enough time to work on it thoughtfully, and there was very limited guidance from the instructors. It just ended up being a super frustrating group project with it often feeling like nobody had any direction or motivation except the person who's idea was picked. Additionally, the speakers listed in the old syllabus are really cool, and were one of the reasons I took the class. Even with the online format, the speakers for the class were nowhere near that caliber. Also there are too many time- consuming assignments that add no value. The class is a hard pass, especially in an online format.

Yes. I think ti's very valuable. One of the better online classes. I think the format does work relatively well for online format. Certain components would be better in person like meeting our classmates and talking in person, but as stated in the class, the new reality is that in a post-COVID world, everything is online.

Only if it is improved--the virtual one needs a lot of improvement. This was the first time they tried it virtually, so hoping they will take feedback and make it better if they offer it again. There needs to a better structure to keep folks engaged, and facilitate them to exchange ideas and build connections both within and across groups. They should also bring in more guest speakers/entrepreneurs--this was advertised as a big advantage of being virtual and did not live up to my expectation.

I personally did not enjoy the class - it felt too long in terms of class length and was hard to stay engaged. Also, the content was relatively light but lectures were very lengthy. All in all, I would not recommend the course as it felt like a drag.

For anyone looking to have a good understanding of how to build your company or starting their entrepreneurial journey should absolutely take this course! It will open up a lot of opportunities if you are truly passionate about your idea! Prof. Kurt and Shiva are both perfect combo for this class and walk you through all the frameworks in a conversational format.
Yes. Can learn a lot in class but you have to ask the questions. Be prepared to follow up with pointed references as well since you may get a generic response.

Kurt is successful and entrepreneur and can be a great mentor in your entrepreneurial journey. The biggest advantage is to have Kurt by your side. I would highly recommend individuals to have certain ideas in mind about their startup before signing up for this class.
Yep, It was a great experience to get to work on a venture idea with a great team, helpful resources and support. I really enjoyed working with Aaron - he has tenacity and real founding experience.
Yes. Gives a great roadmap for entrepreneurship and is a safe place to experiment with ideas.
Yes
Yes, probably my favorite class this spring semester.
I think this course is very practical and can personally participate in the works of startup, so I highly recommend it. No

Great class to take if you want to experience what a startup accelerator feels like. But know that that comes with less structure and it will challenge you to be a presenter and " sell " your idea. You will also do a LOT of work if you end up being selected as a founder (because your idea got picked as 1 of 10 among 50 or so pitches). You know your product best so you will have to really pull through the weight to do customer discovery interviews and provide real leadership to your team who just joins you mid class. Your group can be make or break for your experience in the class. This class had a lot of potential and failed to deliver to my expectations. Some of it was likely due to the unforeseen circumstances surrounding Kurt's health, but Dave and Shiva never seemed to recover their footing over the remaining 10 weeks, even with Kurt's template. It was hard to believe that this is a course that has been taught for many years, and that both instructors have been involved in previous iterations.

I found the level of disorganization in this course extremely disconcerting. Dave and Shiva seemed to talk regularly but not align. When asked about the difference in their responses, they said it was a learning opportunity for us to learn and evaluate different frameworks, which I would have found more believable if they had shared this upfront. The timing of this course was also off, with a lot of material crammed into half of the course. It would have been far more useful to do Darwin Day in week 2 (like the weekend version with Sharat, which has much more glowing feedback), and then spend the rest of the course working on our projects and evaluating different business models, while having lectures that mimicked the stage of our projects.

As a lecturer, Shiva clearly knows his material, but he always seems to defer to the other instructor in the room, until he's by himself. Dave was very encouraging and also facilitated some great class discussion. I think either of them might have been good as standalone instructors, but the combination just didn't work well.
In its current form, I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.
No
why not? definitely.

This course is great if you a) want to consider entrepreneurship and b) are willing to experience it live, even if that's with someone else's idea. Only 1/4 people's ideas are used for the lab part of this class, so if you sign up realize you'll be experiencing startup stuff with a team, and that team may not be using your particular idea.

Absolutely, I would highly recommend this course and the instructors to fellow students. The class is exceptionally well-structured, with a perfect balance of practical application and theoretical insights. Kurt is an outstanding professor who excels at fostering meaningful discussions and creating a collaborative learning environment. Shiva is incredibly approachable, and his content-rich sessions offer valuable knowledge that's directly applicable to real-world entrepreneurial challenges. Together, the instructors make this class both engaging and impactful. If you're looking to develop your entrepreneurial mindset and skills, this course is a must!

I recommend this course for those who are willing to start their first company and have ambitions for a unicorn! I would not recommend this course. This course will not provide any resources or instruction on developing your ideas or creating a startup that you cannot already find for free on Y-Combinator's "Startup School" videos. This course also provides limited opportunities to develop or gain feedback on your own personal business ideas or new startups (limited feedback is only available to <20% of students). There are more than 70 students present for each lecture, which means there's limited opportunities for meaningful conversations or personal engagement. You will not receive personal feedback on the homework assignments or any feedback on the group projects. Overall, this course will probably not help advance your learning and growth as a student and potential entrepreneur more than any other free resources available online. This is not the Berkeley Entrepreneurship resource you are looking for - skip it and find something else.
Yes
Yes, as it gives you a well-rounded scan of the silicon valley entrepreneurship landscape and exposure to key industry players.

sections.goodFor: Students new to entrepreneurship or VC who want a layered framework for building a business plan and a real pitch to VCs from firms like Lightspeed and a16z.
sections.notFor: Anyone attached to their own idea — team formation is forced and better ideas get dropped for popular ones. Also poor for those needing organized logistics or responsive teaching staff.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy and back-loaded: weekly essays/write-ups that several call busy work, plus a semester-long team venture project that intensifies at the end.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly written assignments, attendance sign-in, and team deliverables ending in a VC pitch; final deliverable expectations called unclear.
sections.redFlags: Quality drops sharply after week 3-4 and after 'Darwin Day' (3); weekly essays are busy work (2); GSI rigid and wrongly marked attendance (1); substitute instructor weeks taught little (1); TA/prof slow to respond (2).
sections.quote: The structure appeared to unintentionally encourage groupthink and popularity-driven decisions, often at the expense of better ideas.
comments: Absolutely!

YES!! This course is one of my favorites so far. You get practical experience to test the entrepreneurship journey along with solid advice, clear examples, and team support. It is a lot of work if you are truly passionate about your chosen project so do be aware of that. Especially if you are new to the VC/entrepreneurship space, I HIGHLY recommend taking this course. I learned so much that I can now directly apply as a possible entraphsip or really any new project. Both professors are so willing to help and also honest with their feedback which I so appreciate!
Great experience in taking that first step into becoming a founder. This class is a safe environment to test your VC's ideas, again VC ideas!

Yes, I would highly recommend this course to any MBA student, or those considering entrepreneurship. Its extremely hands on, so only take it if you are ready to engage and put the work in, especially at the end of the semester. The learnings are invaluable and whether or not you have an idea or business you want to work on now, this will help you learn how to think about problem spaces, validate ideas and progress through bringing a product/service to life. If you do have an idea or business now, this will be an opportunity for guided strategic development.

The course began on a strong note, with the first 3 – 4 weeks offering well-structured and valuable content. However, the quality and coherence of the course declined significantly afterward. The structure appeared to unintentionally encourage groupthink and popularity-driven decisions, often at the expense of better ideas. Strong projects were sometimes overlooked, while weaker or duplicate ideas advanced. While the professors aim to stay neutral in team formation and idea selection, some degree of intervention — especially when multiple teams are proposing near- identical or clearly underdeveloped concepts — might improve the overall experience and outcomes.

A more flexible team formation process would also be beneficial. Forcing students to join groups they may not be genuinely interested in, rather than allowing them to pursue topics they are passionate about, can limit engagement and stifle creativity.

Also I really want to emphasize how the GSI was unnecessarily strict and annoying about random things when they themselves were so disorganized. Many students, including myself, found the GSI to be overly rigid and

unapproachable. For instance, I was incorrectly marked absent from a session I clearly attended and signed in for. When I raised the issue, the GSI dismissed it without considering a correction. This kind of inflexibility and lack of responsiveness undermines trust and adds unnecessary frustration to the student experience. Given that most graduate students are working professionals, a more respectful and collaborative approach would have been more appropriate.

If you have not done anything in entrepreneurship before I think it is helpful framework. The final deliverables lacked clarity on what was expected and the fact that the class was a simulation goes against the seeming expectation for you to actually build a company. It is hard to tell if the expectation is an educational endeavor or for you to actually build a company which makes assignments difficult.

I would 100% recommend this course. It's fantastic from a learning perspective, I loved how the course was structured layer by layer to build up a business plan. I've already taken an entrepreneurship course, but this landed in a much bigger way.
I would say you get out what you put in. And your team is so important to making this an enjoyable process, so keep this in mind.

100% recommend it. The EWMBA version has more interesting students, and the teaching staff are both legends too. If you want to learn how to synthesize an and take it all the way to pitching it to VCs from Lightspeed, a16z, etc, this is the class for you.
Only if they have an idea that they are passionate about and want to launch.
Hands down I would certainly recommend this class to other students interested in exploring the world of entrepreneurship or VC.

I would, but this course is pretty disorganized and has a lot of busy work. They need to get rid of the weekly assignment/write ups because I didn't get much value from those. Instead, have check points related to our main project to keep teams on track. Also, it was really hard to reach the TA and professor, slow replies, and not always getting quality time

Definitely recommend. Even if you don't see yourself as an entrepreneur, this course can be helpful in understanding the start-up ecosystem and gaining knowledge about funding, business model, strategy etc.
I absolutely would. This should be a required course and is full of invaluable lessons for all.
yes, I would definitely recommend the class to someone interested in learning about startups and wanting to get a holistic view on the process of startups.
I would not because I could have learned so much more by having devoted class time to learn by doing rather than listening to lectures.
yes

No. The class was helpful the first few weeks when we were all working towards our own ideas and pitch. The class took a nosedive once Professor Beyer had to step out and Shiva stepped in. We didn't learn anything during the weeks Shiva instructed. The class workload is too heavy (essays every week) and wasn't helpful. This class would be more effective if each student continued working on their ideas throughout the semester.

There is a 35% chance I would only recommend this class to my fellow students. For most of them, it would be a no. Maybe this is because I had a sub-par experience with my team after Darwin Day, but after speaking with many of my fellow classmates, there was a lack of interest in the class across the board after Darin Day. The motivation to come to this class went down substantially for me and many of my classmates after Darin Day, but we all still came and felt unmotivated through the end of the semester.

sections.goodFor: Students who want Lean Startup framing for validating a new venture, or who value hearing directly from a few successful entrepreneur guests.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting step-by-step guidance on starting a venture - one of two commenters attended every class and says lectures rambled and taught nothing beyond blue ocean strategy.
sections.workloadNote: Only 2 comments - evidence is very thin. Students pitch a startup idea, then work in teams on the ideas selected by vote/professor; one says no instruction accompanies that work.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; student startup pitches and team work on selected ideas.
sections.redFlags: 1 of 2 commenters reports rambling lectures unrelated to assignments, no instruction to support the team startup work, and calls it a waste of credits and money.
sections.quote: I have attended all classes and walked away learning nothing but the definition of blue ocean strategy. Waste of credits and money.
comments: I would not recommend this course unless you are looking to hear from a couple of successful entrepreneurs. Majority of class does not teach anything, its more of rambling on topics unrelated to assignments or how to actually step by step start your own venture. Only one class "blue ocean strategy" is explained, and I could have googled it. We did not learn anything unfortunately. You create your own startup one day-which may or may not be chosen. You then are told to work with peers on the selected group ideas the professors pick or are based on student votes, and are not taught anything to help you with these startups. I have attended all classes and walked away learning nothing but the definition of blue ocean strategy. Waste of credits and money.
Yes, the focus on the "Lean Startup" methodology makes this course essential for anyone serious about validating a new venture.

sections.goodFor: Aspiring entrepreneurs, including people arriving without an idea; several cite a comprehensive framework from concept through go-to-market and fundraising. Take it in person.
sections.notFor: Students unwilling to work hard if their startup isn't picked, or who can't tolerate uneven teammates - one reports classmates checked out of group work because only their own idea mattered.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (7 comments). Team-based work on selected startup ideas - everyone pitches a company idea - plus customer surveys, where one student reports conflicting guidance (200 responses vs 30).
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - a pitched company idea and team project work are described, but grading is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: One alleges opaque project selection, an unqualified TA teaching half the course (incorrect pricing lecture), and end 'VCs' largely from Beyer's own fund. Another says a co-lecturer was rude to female founders.
sections.quote: you should only take this course if you have intention in working hard independent of your startup getting picked
comments: I would definitely recommend Dr. Beyer to students who want to learn about entrepreneurship. I would additionally say that you should only take this course if you have intention in working hard independent of your startup getting picked. I'm a student who came in to learn about entrepreneurship, not because I had a pre-existing idea, and I left with a lot of learnings. But it was disheartening working with people who were checked out on group work, because they only were interested in themselves.

I think the course was well-designed overall. If Shiva continues to co-lecture, he needs to come better prepared to the sessions. Also, please do not bring back Niki; she was rude to all female founders.

I would certainly recommend this course to wanna be entrepreneurs as it provides a comprehensive framework to think of your business all the way from conceptualizing your idea, to going to market, raising funds and sustaining it. Quite a few of Kurt's students from this course have gone on to become successful entrepreneurs which in my opinion is a testimony to effectiveness and impact of this course on your entrepreneurial journeys.
I would 100% recommend this course if you are even remotely interested in becoming an entrepreneur. This was one of the most fun classes at haas.
YES!!! Take it in person, though. Wait to take the class until you feel like you have an entrepreneurship idea that you're really excited about, since everyone must pitch a company idea.
Yes, absolutely. I loved the class learnings.

I came away from this class not trusting Kurt Beyer or his TA, Shiven, who teaches literally half the course. From the unclear way in which projects were chosen ("We did it all by voting -- except for the last few, which we chose.") to letting someone HIGHY unqualified teach half the course (Shiven -- who gave a straight up incorrect lecture on pricing.) to Shiven saying that we needed 200 survey responses and then Kurt implying sometime later that we needed 30 to him saying that there would be a bunch of VCs at the end and it was all either people who weren't VCs or were part of his own fund, I don't trust this guy. He's self-serving. If you want to stroke someone's ego and hope that you get chosen for a project and want him as a VC even though he doesn't seem trustworthy, take the course. Otherwise, steer away.

rows.title: International Business Development for MBAs, IP course

comments: Will definitely recommend this course to any student.It's once a life experience you don't want miss out! YES!!!!!! This course is a MUST. It was the highlight of my academic experience at Haas. Such an incredible opportunity to apply the concepts of the core curriculum to the real world and travel abroad....do not miss the opportunity!!!! Yes, the is by far the best applied innovation course that I have taken at Haas. The travel portion of the class was incredible.
Absolutely, the lessons one learns in this class are very valuable based on their practical application and influence thery have on critical thinking skills.
Absolutely
Highly recommend. IBD is the best course I've taken at Haas.
Yes!
I already recommended this class to my classmates. This was one of the most rewarding class I've had in my first year. And since it's only available during your first year, so don't miss it!
This was the best course I took at Haas - could not recommend more!

sections.goodFor: Students who want international consulting experience and travel, and who can tolerate not knowing their country, team or client at sign-up. Several call it their favorite Haas experience.
sections.notFor: Anyone unwilling to work extra hours or take assignment uncertainty. Team leads do far more work with little recognition, and projects that aren't go-to-market fit the curriculum poorly.
sections.workloadNote: Not weekly-quantified but heavy: spring coursework, 80+ hours per week during the two-week in-country stint, plus assignments carried into the following fall for the last credit.
sections.gradingBasis: team client deliverables, a blog post and a final presentation; students say length guidelines were not enforced consistently
sections.redFlags: Credit-to-work mismatch is the loudest complaint (2 say it should be 4 credits given fall assignments); assignment instructions confusing, changing and unevenly enforced (2); class time not relevant to all projects (2).
sections.quote: Project, team, and country dependent. Super MBA experience and would recommend doing it. Team leads should expect to do a lot more work with little recognition.
comments: Absolutely. Amazing opportunity to get consulting experience while traveling the world.
This is a truly transformative experience. A lot of work, a lot of hard work!! But you get to learn so much, experience so much, and explore so much! I highly recommend this course????
I would. This was a GREAT course!!

This course, as many people know, carries a lot of uncertainty. When you sign up for the course, you have no knowledge about what experience you are doing to get (country, team, client), so it is definitely a risk. But that said, I think the whole experience was worth it once you are able to go to your country, experience a new culture, and meet your client in person.

There were a few issues with this course throughout the semester that I hope are addressed: 1. The class time was not always relevant to all projects and it seemed not the best use of time for all teams. I think sharing a variety of resources that might or might not be applicable to projects would be rather, rather than providing only one framework or way to do things and assume that all teams can use this in their project. 2. Especially at the end, guidelines provided for some assignments were not followed by all teams. For example, we were told to keep the blog post at certain length, or the final presentation at 3 slides and these guidelines seemed almost "optional" and not really enforced by all teams, creating an unfair advantage for those teams who did follow the guidelines. 3. This class should be 4 credits if they still make us do assignments in the fall semester. I think it is ridiculous that we only get 2 credits in the spring for the amount of work we put in, including traveling in country and working 80+ hours for two weeks while in- country. All other applied innovation classes that have client-facing work are 3 credits. The fact that we also need to do a presentation in the fall to get the final 1 credit out of the 3 does not make sense at all, and this should be 1 credit IN ADDITION to the 3 credits we should already be earning for all our work from January to May. I hope this changes for future classes.
Yes if they are willing to work extra hours
Project, team, and country dependent. Super MBA experience and would recommend doing it. Team leads should
expect to do a lot more work with little recognition.

It's a great course with plenty of opportunity. Well-organized but not all projects are Go To Market strategy, and that is all the course focuses on. Instructors are very helpful, but instructions for assignments are confusing and change constantly
Yes, this was my all time favorite experience at Haas. The in country travel was a once in a lifetime experience, and I made lifelong friendships with my teammates.
Yes for the travel and consulting case experience!! Bang for your buck

comments: Yes.

Yes. This is a great class that is far more relevant and useful then the filler "design thinking" classes with which this is sometimes unfairly grouped. This class is far better. The guests are great, the class is engaging, and it's a good Saturday class without a manageable work load.
Yes, excellent professor, really enjoyed the course. Very applicable for the real world.
Well done!!!
Yes, it encourages thinking beyond the traditional business strategy process.
Yes. You'll learn something new, especially if you're looking to go into strategy consulting. And In tech this form of thinking is quite useful as well!

Without question. In fact, I have already recommended this class to several of my friends here at Haas. All too often I'll take a class that's like "Meh:-\", or "that was okay:-)" but this class was a cut above most in that FEELS expensive. It feels like I'm taking a class at a world class business school, and I walk away from each session empowered knowing I'm building a skills that will be well worn tools in my tool belt. This class was an absolute joy and I learned so much from it.
Yes definitely!

Yes. You should take this class if you're interested in the potential long-term impacts to society, businesses, etc. Yes, if you are in a role where you can drive substantial change than I believe this is an important class. It can help you think broadly about the future.
Absolutely. I learned a lot and had a lot of fun while doing it

I would recommend taking at least one Barry Schwartz class. I'm taking this class and a Goodson class (M&A) at the same time and it's a great balance - and opposite point of view. Barry is a pioneer in choice research and has influenced a number of the most influential I/O Psyche, OB, etc. researchers in the world. He brought in a stellar series of teachers to pitch their research (Adam Grant, Angela Duckworth, Amy Wrzesniewski, etc).

My background is that I achieved greater success by the age of 30 than I thought I would achieve in my entire career; which left me with a pretty big hole in my wellbeing because I'm asking "what next. Is this it? Just more promotions, more money? I don't want 3 houses, I want to be happy". If you're there now, or if you think you will feel that in the future, take a Barry class and ask tough questions. He has a way of pointing you in the direction of wellbeing. For example, I know at least 1 student who switched jobs because their life was in direct contradiction to what he was learning in this class. 10 weeks later he's at a new company and much happier. On the other hand, 50% of students didn't show up to the last class. That is to say: with Barry, you get what you put in.

The class structure is that grades were based on 6 essays. Essays re-enforce learnings but otherwise Barry's lax style of "read what you find interesting" makes the workload whatever you make it. I read all of the readings for the first 8 weeks and it did take a substantial amount of time, however could have gotten away with a lot less (and in turn, gotten far less out of the class). Those who rank the course low on workload likely didn't actually do the readings: which, I suppose, to each their own if you want to waste $7,000 on an easy A... but take this class because you're soul searching and enjoy struggling with implementing the topics with your classmates.

10/10. Must-take course. This course will fundamentally change the way you think about the workplace and your own career. Barry critically evaluates the very foundation of how work is structured, how we incentivize and evaluate employees, what it takes to establish happiness at work, how to lead with practical wisdom, how we should "job craft" to turn our work into Callings vs Careers, and beyond. Barry is incredibly intelligent, with an impressive body of work and an even-more-impressive community of guest lecturers to call on, including Angela Duckworth, Adam Grant, and beyond. Take this course!! And prepare to change your mind about what matters and work and what's in your control to change.

I highly recommend this class for students that care about innovation broadly whether in startups or broadly! yes! great learnings and more unique than a lot of courses

rows.f26Day: These courses exist for the benefit of the rest of campus, or for populations other than our MBAs - not included on our schedule or in bidding.  However, MBA students may take these courses; they count toward your required MBA units for graduation when taken for letter grade. Please add/drop via CalCentral per campus deadlines and request information from the Instructors. These courses are not managed by the FTMBA Office.

comments: Yes, this course was a great introduction to the plant-based and cell-cultured landscape. Working with companies directly was an interesting experience.
I would say yes but there is a lot of work that felt busy work

I think this course is really dependent on your client and team, but if placed on a strong client and team + student is self motivated, this course is very rewarding because it provides real world experience.

I was excited to learn about the food industry, but found that I could have benefitted from starting with a more traditional classroom approach (lectures, cases) as opposed to jumping directly into client work - I was able to learn deeply about my client and their work, but didn?t get a more holistic view of the plant-based space. Having a mix of students across UC Berkeley programs provided a valuable variety of insights, but can make coordinating

responsibilities (across different schedules, priorities, skill sets, etc.) difficult. It would be helpful to establish a team lead and other team member roles and responsibilities early on. Ultimately I think this is a great opportunity for undergrads, but not very revolutionary for MBAs. That said, the workload is manageable, the instructors are really kind, and you have the chance work with cool companies.
Absolutely

I would recommend this if you are interested in food/agriculture and/or environmental sustainability. For MBA students, it's a good experience to work with and possibly lead some undergrad students from different disciplines. This course provides a very unique opportunity to gain hands-on experiences in collaborating with driven individuals who wish to leverage on the emerging enthusiasm in sustainable foods.

Yes, I absolutely would. This is a great opportunity to dive into the plant-centered food system and understand where the industry is going. The class builds both hard and soft skills, provides excellent networking opportunities, and sets up the potential for jobs/internships in the future... all of this while getting units!
Yes! Got practical knowledge and insight into a new interesting field.

I would! I loved this class and learned a ton. I would HIGHLY recommend this class to all of my friends and I truly enjoyed it. This class helped me gain real life consulting experience while working in an emerging and impactful industry.
Yes, if interested in food systems. Not useful for those not.

Yes, content is highly interesting and professors and peers are amazing

The consulting projects give students great experience working with clients with many different backgrounds. The projects are all very different and there is an opportunity to gain skills in marketing, operations, finance, project management, and event planning.

I DO NOT recommend this class to a graduate student. Your assignments are very elementary level and class time feels like it's a waste as it's remote and no one is engaged. I took this class with the hope of getting a deeper knowledge of the plant based food space and don't feel like I learned very much. Your "challenge" project is a toss up based on your client but a lot of them are marketing or social media related.
I would not - especially as an MBA student the learning is minimal and the client/team placement is so variable, you have no control over it. Not a worthwhile class.

This course skillfully connected sustainability, food, and business, emphasizing the critical intersection of sustainable practices in food systems and their implications for the business world. It provided valuable opportunities to explore how innovative solutions can address global challenges in these areas, while also expanding my understanding of the field's vast potential. The instructor offered excellent insights and connections, fostering both knowledge and professional growth. This course is a must for anyone passionate about creating impactful, sustainable change through food and business strategies.
Yes, I recommend it. You can experience new experiences that you can't do in other existing classes.

Yes! both Miyoko and Brittany are one of the nicest instructors I've had on campus and they're deeply understanding with the role of being a student is. They not only provide opportunities outside of this class for jobs/internships, but they're great people and wish the best for everyone. I think this class is great for people interested in food systems (injustice, animal welfare, sustainability, shelf life, etc.) and also just basic business skills of being a consultant/entrepreneur. I've learned many valuable lessons in just the project itself and I love the instructors a lot. Great environment!

I really enjoyed this course because it was able to highlight all sectors in food systems in a digestible manner. The guest speakers were always inspiring to hear and motivate me to learn more about food systems and the plant-based community. I think this class is inspiring in getting to recognize knowledge about plant-centric diets that is never showcased in other courses at Berkeley.

This class was so unique and informative. It was such a treat to be in a college-level course that actually discussed the importance and intersectionality of moving towards a plant-based world. I loved the dynamic and varied intro to the business world and consulting that it provided, without compromising any values. Both Brittany and Miyoko were incredible, so knowledgeable and willing to help in any way possible.
Yes, this is the best course ever. Everyone should take it.
Both instructors are extremely helpful and are exceptional and passionate for this class!

Yes definitely. Since in addition to being a class, it also acts as an internship opportunity to work with companies, it is different than any other course I've taken at Berkeley. It was a wonderful learning and working experience and taught me so much.

The in-person potluck days are fun - I really enjoyed trying plant-based dishes from others. I would say as an MBA this was a LOT of little assignments that were a lot of busy work, in addition to project with an external client, so the class seems a little more geared towards undergraduates than graduate-level students, so I think less little required assignments should be required for this to be a 3-credit course with an experiential learning component.
Yes, engaging, so interesting, found my niche

I definitely would recommend this class to other people. Its super important and cool.

I do wish it was slightly less one sided and they talked about case studies of sustainable meat production, or at least discussed how that fits into a sustainable food system, because at times it felt too heavy on that "veganism woohoo!!!" type of education.
Yes, since it is very informative, ran by passionate instructors, and gives people great opportunities to hear from many different experts in the world of plant-based foods.

No, absolutely not. Do NOT take this class. I was warned by past 2nd years and did not listen. Because this is an applied innovation class where we work with clients to solve a problem, I thought that more of the focus of the class would be on how to actually solve those problems and gain important business skills such as: understanding market landscape and market size, how to do research for startup businesses or nonprofits, skill building on being professional when working with clients (which is something I felt my team really needed), designing a go-to-market strategy, etc. Instead, this class was mostly about why animal agriculture is bad and plant-centric diets are important, and taught us very very little about how to do the actual work we are supposed to do for our clients.

Because the teams are made up of a mix of undergrads and people from different graduate programs, I was the only MBA student on our team. We were working with a startup and asked to do market sizing, competitor landscape research, profitability analysis, create a pitch deck for funders, etc. No one on my team had any idea to do this, except me who had a very baseline idea. Instead of learning this in the class, I was responsible for TEACHING my team how to do it. I was also the only one with experience working with clients, and felt I had to teach my team how to be professional and responsive. It felt like herding cats, and a big part of the workload for me was effectively being a PM trying to wrangle undergrads. It was horrible.

I wish the course had focused more on actually building our business skills and teaching less experienced folks how to be professional, given it's a Haas class, and less focused on why it's important to be plant-centric. That's valuable info and it's good to have a few lectures on that, but not the whole class.

Yes for sure. If students were interested in plant-based movement or the food system in general this class gives a really good overview/mix of topics related to both of the field mentioned. There are graduate/MBA students that I didn't know this class combined.

Overall though, be prepared for the class to feel a bit like vegan propaganda at times - if youre aware and open to that, I think it's a great class and highly recommend.

rows.title: Responsible Supply Chains & Operations in Action
rows.disagree: Modest rating, but comments are uniformly enthusiastic

sections.goodFor: Anyone interested in supply chain generally (not just sustainability), tech/CPG supply chain careers, and Sustainable Business certificate students; strong guest speakers.
sections.notFor: Students not focused on supply chain - two say the credit hours are better spent elsewhere; anyone wanting implementation tools or technical supply chain (try engineering).
sections.workloadNote: Weekly readings before class plus cases and simulations; front-loaded - 'pretty light after the first few weeks.' Manageable final project applying the concepts.
sections.gradingBasis: Participation weighted ~40% with cold calls on the readings, plus cases and a final project.
sections.redFlags: Two say the sustainability-only lens limits it and it doesn't give tools to actually implement responsible supply chains; two say non-supply-chain students should take something else.
sections.quote: Readings every week before class and you might get cold calls, participation heavy 40% so be ready to voice out your ideas
comments: I would only recommend this class, as it stands now, if you really want to focus on sustainability. If you are looking to learn about supply chains, you'd probably be better off taking an elective in one of the engineering departments. Amy is great and brings in very senior, knowledgeable guests, but I think a lot of the takeaways that aren't sustainability specific do relate more to concerns you might have 10 years down the line in a role, not in your first few years post- MBA.
yes, if you have any interest in learning about supply chains this is a beneficial class

Yes, absolutely — as the world moves towards strengthening sustainability initiatives across the world, supply chains are an area where environmental impacts can be extremely severe at scale, and this makes a great class to be more knowledgeable in how to apply real world solutions for future Haas MBAs.

I would recommend this course to other students. As it stands, this is the only supply chain class held at Haas and it was very well designed for a both a deep dive into core operations topics and more nuanced discussion about the realities of creating tangible products and value for businesses and communities. The guest speakers were varied in professional background and perspective and brought great context to the theory we had discussed in class. Assignments were manageable and like a value add.

If you aren't focusing your post-MBA career on supply chains, take another class for sure, as you'll gain more from other classes that have similar credit hours/ time in class. If you are focusing on supply chains, this is solely focused on responsible/ sustainable supply chains, and even within this subset of supply chain work doesn't necessarily give you the tools to implement them in your own firm. I'd take this class again if I were interested in this topic, needed to fill up credit hour requirements, or wanted a low-credit-hour class. But otherwise, I'd look elsewhere for your electives. Yes, for sure.

I would recommend this class to students who are not only interested in sustainable/responsible supply chains, but supply chains in general. comments: I really enjoyed this class and would recommend it to fellow students. This class was great, and the perfect compliment to Haas's current sustainability offerings. The readings/cases were interesting and every class brought in a guest speaker to expand on their personal area of expertise. Be prepared to participate in class discussions, but other than that there was really just one main assignment that you build on throughout the course. The workload was very manageable, especially compared to level of learning achieved. Yes! Sanchita's extensive work and research in the topic really elevated the class beyond an academic discussion. The guest speakers she brought in were meaningful and extremely relevant players in the area - especially if you have any interest in apparel manufacturing, which is her focus. We also had some MPAs which added some great variety and context to the Haas ecosystem and hopefully continues - so added bonus if you have any interest in policy and international governance topics.
Yes! Sanchita is deeply passionate about teaching, the topic, and works very hard to make sure that all voices are heard. If you're interested in the supply chains this is a great intro class.
