Robert is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable, and cares so much about his students and the class. He is wonderful to learn from. I am so grateful to have taken this class. It was one of the best I've taken!

Yes, must take. Skip other spring break plans for this class. The course is interdisciplinary and critically examines how economies, societies, and people can be better in different elements than the American way. Loved reading and preparing for the immersion week knowing that it would translate to fruitful and engaging conversations during the week. Even yet, it has provided me with a refreshed perspective that we (as a society) can change as long as we are intentional and focused on our priorities.

Yes, but be aware that the week in Copenhagen is very heavy towards environmental sustainability, not necessarily sustainable capitalism in general, so those who are not interested in this may have a bit of a learning curve to keep up. I enjoyed hearing about these topics, but would've loved to see more entrepreneurship and early stage innovation mixed in as well.

This was a 60 person class with masters of climate solutions students along with full time and part time students. Definitely recommend! This class served as a sort of capstone for me across several other classes. It brought together learnings from classes in economics, systems change, labor organizing, policy, capitalism and growth, etc etc. I really enjoyed the comparative analysis format of US vs Nordics to develop my knowledge of both systems. You will worry when bidding that you'll be bummed to be in class over spring break. Do not fear! It is a wonderful experience and you get to immerse yourself in the city with MBA friends between / after the sessions. I found this super worthwhile overall. Very high ROI on learning vs overall HW.
Yes would recommend, seeing real life application of school theory was very insightful

sections.goodFor: Students who need the AI Certificate credit and want theoretical grounding in AI fundamentals and future-of-work research; Toby Stuart's sessions are singled out as excellent.
sections.notFor: Anyone expecting hands-on AI/LLM use or practical business AI strategy - there is none; also too foundational for AI-experienced students, and there is overlap with the intro coding class.
sections.workloadNote: Identical comment set to the other MBA296-2 section. Half-semester, four professors; pre-class questions (often opened late), in-class quizzes, low-value assignments.
sections.gradingBasis: In-class printed quizzes, pre-class questions, assignments; quizzes called poorly prepared (typos, faulty structure, too few printouts).
sections.redFlags: Recurring (8+ of 17): first offering was 'a hot mess' - four professors with no handoffs, misaligned start date, unmaintained bCourses, no GSI, poorly prepared quizzes, theory-only with no hands-on AI despite the title.
sections.quote: There were 4 professors who each taught a few weeks of class separately... they never seemed to actually talk to each other or have a handover when switching to then next professor
comments: This class had a few interesting lectures but overall was a pretty chaotic overview of AI and the future of work. The technical foundations and future of work sessions were interesting but the class is very dependent on the professors and how many sessions you have with each of them. Hopefully it will continue to improve as the AI Certificate improves over the semesters.
Course is poorly designed. I dont feel i have learned anything. Very theoretical, not hands-on. Until the PO designs a better course, wouldnt take it.

No. This class was billed as a strategic class for non-technical people to learn more about how to leverage AI in workflows, and we didn't once use AI/an LLM of our choosing in class. I expected to become more more AI-literate as a result of this class, and I am coming away from it having no new skills other than knowing a few hypotheses of how AI may (or may not) impact the labor market.

The way it was this year, not really. I'm sure the fact that it was the first time this course was offered played a role but it was a complete mess. Start date was misaligned between students and professors (we all showed up to the first class, professor didn't show up and then emailed us saying the class actually started a week later), quizzes covered topics that were a bit irrelevant in my opinion and were very poorly prepared (typos, faulty structure, not enough print outs for everyone, etc), assignments didn't add much value, and content overall was too theoretical and not very practical. Hopefully all of this (and other problems we had) improve drastically for next year.

While the topic is important, the course needs A LOT of work. Having four different instructors for the course was a recipe for administrative disaster. I think this course will improve next year, so I would still take it, but I want to note that it may be too foundational for AI experts. Toby Stuart who hopefully remains one of the lecturers for the course is a great industry leader and makes you think.
I would not recommend, better off taking an LLM course. I am not sure what they were trying to do making us take this course.

Yes. This class should be a core class, right after Data and Decisions. It is crucial for today's market that every MBA students masterizes these concepts and is able to "talk AI" and understand the technology in a proper way Interesting course to get exposure to the nuts and bolts of AI and how it will affect workplaces and society from several different perceptives.
Yes, The course is useful and brings clarity about AI in the business world

I would recommend this class because I still got unique insights into what's happening in the space and readings I would not go looking for own my own, but not all the professors were equally good (Toby Stuart was great; Jonathan Kolstad was good; and Anastasia Fedyk was not as great; we haven't had the fourth professor at the time of this submission so can't speak to them) but the learning experience fluctuated a lot depending on who was teaching. If Toby is teaching his own class on this subject, I would probably just take that.

No, but I think this class can only get better (hopefully it will). Some general comments about how to improve the class (it didn't feel appropriate to write it down only for one faculty): stop relying on the "this is the first time we teach the class so things will go wrong" and actively try to prevent that from happening (Question the status quo, anyone?); if you ask us to answer the pre class questions before 11 pm, make sure to open them with enough time to answer (most of the times I would try to answer them on Saturday (closed), Sunday 11am (closed), Sunday 5pm (still closed), and then by 9pm it was open but it closed at 11pm), and several times they didn't even open the questions so you would be checking all the time until finally giving up; communicate with other faculty on a regular basis (e.g., it happened twice that the printed quizzes were not enough for the students); and in general, the class should be called AI foundations and not Business AI foundations, as there was little to no connection to the business side (eg., it explained how AI works when translating words into 0s and 1s, then doing some calculations for the error, distance, etc when it could have been explained much simpler and why this is relevant); if the class will continue to have this technical focus, then there is plenty of overlap with the Intro to coding class
It was ok- I hope they update it to be reflective of the feedback in terms of balancing how much time was spent on the content the students found most interesting
If you need the AI certificate sure. I'd like to see an iteration of this class with less professors. 4 in one half semester was way too much.

I think this course could be good but this year was not well coordinated and prepare given it was the first edition. Also, is important it is taught from a business/ corporate lenses, not so focus on research and academia but rather what kind of problems, challenges and decisions we are gonna have to face in the corporate world (even if we don't have a technical role) and what do we need to make them efficiently. I would think of the course as a guide for a student who is put in charge of defining the AI strategy of a company, what kind of tools they implement and how these are integrated, what factors to take into account, how do you train employees, what workflows should be redefined, etc. I would recommend this class because I learned a lot about how businesses are currently thinking about AI and what AI strategy should look like.

This course will give you a strong and broad understanding of AI fundamentals from the theory perspective, which is great. There is little content on its application, though, nor really content on policy/ how to handle it/ etc. There is also no hands-on learning with AI. So if you take this class, be well aware that what you get out is theory and understanding (which is a helpful thing, no doubt), not practical application.

Hopefully, from an organization perspective, this class will improve because it was a hot mess this semester. There were 4 professors who each taught a few weeks of class separately. This was great from a knowledge and perspective breadth POV. However, they never seemed to actually talk to each other or have a handover when switching to then next professor, which made the class disjointed as they didn't seem to know what was covered, where we were at, when quizes where, if past deck material was actually posted, etc.. Furthermore, they didn't seem to manage or update bCourses regularly, causing confusion, and there was no real GSI in tow to help keep up with this either. First year course with a number of different professors so it tended to be disaggregated. Solid material and deep dive into AI.

sections.goodFor: Mostly only students who need it for the AI Certificate, where it is required; a couple say individual instructors (Toby Stuart, Abhishek Nagaraj) were worth hearing.
sections.notFor: Anyone expecting practical business applications of AI - students say that is essentially absent; non-technical students, for whom success 'seemed out of reach.'
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified. Rotating lectures from four instructors (Zsolt, Thomas Lee, Abhishek, Toby Stuart) plus quizzes; students describe it as disjointed rather than heavy.
sections.gradingBasis: Quizzes students say test slide memorization or material not covered in class; attendance appears not to count.
sections.redFlags: Most comments: 4 rotating instructors, disjointed, no clear objectives; title a misnomer as business application is absent; too technical for non-technical students yet shallow for technical ones; unfair quizzes.
sections.quote: The name "Business AI Foundations" is a misnomer. We never really got into the practical business applications of AI in any meaningful way.
comments: As it stands right now, I cannot. I hope this becomes the class it should be (and a part of core), but clearly it was hastily put together and expectations the faculty had for the class were very different than what we had as students. If we want a technical AI class, we can go to a different school - we are here for a business class and this was not it. Additionally, the first two quizzes were mostly on concepts that were not even discussed (at least in detail) in class. No, not at all. And this is the only class at Haas where I'd say that.

The name "Business AI Foundations" is a misnomer. We never really got into the practical business applications of AI in any meaningful way. The course covered AI at a surface level from a technical perspective, but I didn't leave with any greater practical knowledge of how to actually use it. I think I got more value messing around on my computer during lectures than I did from the lectures themselves. Three of the four instructors I'd be interested in taking again, just in different classes.

So I'm left wondering what the point was. If this had been called just "AI Foundations," it was too surface level to earn the title. The business portion felt almost entirely absent. And the fact that it's required for the AI Certificate and costs a real chunk of points makes that worse, not better. The curriculum needs to change and the instructor team needs to be managed pretty dramatically before this is worth taking. Knowing what I know now, I wouldn't take it.

You have to take this for the certificate but if you don't need the certificate, you can probably get a similar amount of value out of just talking to other students, keeping up with the news, and taking Data Mining

Yes, this is an important class. Four instructors in such a short period was not idea. But in the future, one or two professors would be idea. Overall, this is an important class and i encourage everyone to take it to understand the AI impact and landscape in business.
Not as it currently stands - I recognize that the administration is revising the course to be more pertinent to stuent desires and to what the market is asking for, however.
The course give insights into the world of AI in bits and pieces, but it failed to bring it together, particularly difficult to see its business alignment.

This course has potential, but it's disappointing in its current form. The course spent a lot of time on technical topics that were too complex for non-technical people to understand, and not complex enough to add value for technical people. The rotating professors seemed cool in theory but made the class feel disjointed. If the curriculum was overhauled and focused more on practical business applications of AI and problems that businesses are encountering, it would be much more worth it.

If this course were more refined, I would recommend it - but in its current state, I would not. There is a lot of potential, and I believe the professors could be excellent, but the class needs stronger continuity across instructors, content, and the evolution of each lecture, as well as clearer connections to real-world business applications. The learning objectives were often unclear, and the quizzes did not meaningfully reinforce learning... they felt more like memorization of lecture slides than true understanding. As a result, I'm leaving the course unsure of what I actually learned. Given how rapidly AI is evolving, this is an incredibly important moment to offer a course like this at Haas, and it feels like the class didn't fully harness that opportunity.
For a Business AI Foundations class: Zsolt - Lean Yes, Thomas - No, Abhishek - Strong Yes, Toby - Maybe
no, but honestly this class is new, and I'm trying to give it the benefit of the doubt.
- You can't have this many professors in a course, especially because it doesn't seem like they had a lot of communication on how the class w as going
- What is the purpose of this class? That needs to be more clearly outlined
- Maybe include takeaways in each class so we can understand what we're supposed to take from all of this.

Interesting content, but definitely they are still figuring the structure out. I think with time it will be a really good class. Yes, I'd recommend it but it needs improvement. The overall course felt a bit disorganized.
Yes

All of the instructors were great except for Thomas Lee. He clearly knows a lot on the topic but struggles to communicate key concepts. He often reverts to highly pedantic and confrontational lines of questioning with students. This course needs some work. While the technical aspects of AI are interesting and important foundational knowledge, this course was too technical without linking that knowledge to business decisions. The quizzes were very difficult even if you did attend classes, while class attendance did not seem to be valued at all in the grading scheme. For people without a technical background, being successful in this class seemed out of reach. The last two classes were by far the best.
No. No one should take this class.

If Toby Stuart is teaching it yes. He was great. Really thought provoking and worthwhile discussion. Otherwise maybe not. Parts of the class were super technical and other parts just felt random? Feel like we need things to be more hands on and less theoretical

No, this class lacks practical applications of AI, and AI in business. This note is cross-professor and about the design and content of the class. Unfortunately, the added value from the class is currently very limited.
I don't know that I would take the course again in its current format. It felt very disjointed across professors and did not quite meet my learning goals for the course.

I'd recommend this course and professor for anyone interested in FinTech, Crypto, or Blockchain. This course has tons of information, and is very up-to-date as it weaves in events that are currently happening in the rapidly changing FinTech field. This course did a good job explaining the concepts and applications of crypto/blockchain. Professor Parlour is extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the field and manages time and interesting discussions very well.

I think the course overview needs to be laid out more clearly. My hope was this class would focus more on the legacy payment ecosystem and less on crypto. I think we went down a lot of rabbit holes associated with crypto which is an area I am not particularly interested in. That may honestly be my fault for not looking into course more, but just what I would have preferred.

I would absolutely recommend this course. All the readings included in the class were interesting and up to date with current fintech news. This class was a great overview of fintech generally, with a deep dive into crypto. I found this to be helpful for anyone looking to work in fintech or better understand financial systems. If you are not interested in crypto I would not recommend, as it was the main focus for the second half of the class.

100%! I came with close to zero knowledge, and while I can't say I'm Elon Musk or a professional bitcoin miner (neither of which was a course objective), I can now speak more intelligently about FinTech, crypto, DeFi and many other topics covered in class. It's not a QUANT class, there were a few exercises, but don't expect this to be a traditional finance course.

This class is a great introduction to financial technology, payment systems, blockchain and crypto currency. Christine Parlour is passionate about the space and it is really great to hear her insights along with class discussion. One thing I loved about this class was it was approachable as someone without a FinTech background, and helped broaden my knowledge and familiarity with the subject.

100%! One of the best classes I took at Haas and is definetly incredibly unique in the sense that it links case readings with C-level guest speakers that can discuss in detail marketing strategies employed around the world
Yes!

Very helpful course, even for non-MBA students, feeling lucky to enroll this course and learned marketing from many perspectives, culture difference and corresponding strategies are so interesting and attractive, learned many experiences here.
Definitely. The mix about cases, guest speakers, and lecture is what you expect from an MBA class

Highly recommend this class to anyone interested in learning more about Marketing. Katherine brought extensive international experience to this class (none of the other Haas courses have this level of a global perspective) and invited outstanding marketing leaders as guest speakers to the classroom. She truly dedicated herself to this course, and my peers would agree that she absolutely did a fantastic job.

One of my favorite classes at Haas. Thanks to Katherine, I ended up applying for full-time roles in product marketing - she is an inspiring, sharp, and engaging lecturer. One of the few classes at Haas that allows you to think about business leadership in a global context.
Hell yes. Because she's authentic and has real-world experience.

Absolutely. This was a rare Haas class that looked at international cases both US companies looking abroad and foreign companies in different markets. It attracted a diverse group of students who had a lot to offer from their work and life experiences. I took this class to step into a more international mindset which is hard to find in many of the other Haas classes and this class definitely met that need. It was also a class on culture and people management beyond just the marketing perspective.
Absolutely, Professor Ray used her network of executives to teach us and brought her industry knowledge to the table in each class. Also, loved how engaging the class was with group work.

Yes! Katherine brings her and her students' international experiences into the classroom, which doesn't happen often enough at Haas, and it's as much as an international strategy class as it is an international marketing class. I would definitely recommend this course to anyone that is interested in marketing and management of international brands. This class went beyond marketing into general management, organizational and corporate strategy, and more. Katherine is a new professor and could make some improvements to her teaching style but she brings a really unique perspective as a very seasoned international professional and leveraged her industry connections to bring in amazing guest speakers.

Yes, take this class - Katherine is amazing - a true professional and a breath of fresh air at Haas. Her cross cultural knowledge and real world stories made this class amazing. She also brought is by far the best and most high quality guest speakers of any class I've taken at Haas.
Yes!

Highly recommend taking a course with Katherine! This was her first class at Haas and she was a total natural. Her incredible background brings real connections in the classroom - speakers from Google, Chanel, etc. Wow! You will not be disappointed.
This class made me want to go into international marketing and strategy as a career choice. Deeply impressed with how the class became more and more useful with each passing day

I would absolutely recommend this course to a fellow student. First, this course by far had the most interesting / impressive "outside" speakers. In addition to that, Professor Ray is an incredible resource, teacher and lecturer. Each class was extremely interesting and worthwhile.
Yes, one of the best courses I have taken at Haas. Much osmotic learning to be had, lots of hidden areas to learn and superb guest speakers who can speak to theory tangibly

Absolutely! By far the best Haas course I have taken. The quality of content and speakers were leaps and bounds better than any other course I have taken. I rarely write comments for these evaluations, and she deserves a big Kudos for facing teaching for the first time head on and succeeding. Please continue teaching and please teach the core class. YES!!
yes

Yes, really good class where you can learn a lot. I have very little interest in marketing and almost zero interest in fashion/beauty (where a lot of Katherine's experience is), but I still really enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Yes! Katherine has a wealth of marketing experience at global brands like Nike and Louis Vuitton and I learned a lot in this class. One thing to note is the focus of the course is B2C so don't expect a lot of B2B marketing insights. Yes!

I would recommend this class to anyone interested in marketing, and professional development in a global setting. The class is in a very nice and attractive setting, with a great mix of lecture, guest speakers and discussions. Yes, especially for students who do not have a lot of experience in global businesses
Yes, important topic and meaningful cases. But, again would recommend deeper analysis of cases and more time to address challenges/questions that students may face in the real world.

I think so, I think it could be improved slightly but I learned a lot, and the guest speakers gave great perspective Definitely. This course is a very high-level view of marketing, primarily for large international brands. The professor has a TON of useful, relevant experience that really adds to the material.
For those who are interested in guess speakers with global experience, this is the class for you
Would recommend

Low lift class and interesting to learn from an industry professional. However, would want to see that Katherine?s implemented some of the feedback around creating more structure of the lecture material and case discussions before I recommended to a fellow student
I would definitely recommend this class - the content is extremely interesting, and Katherine is very knowledgeable. You won't regret it.
Yes! Very interesting and engaging class!
It's interesting and not a lot of work, but I didn't learn very much.
Yes! Great class for students interested in international business

Yes, I think that there is a lot of valuable learning to be had from the Professor's professional experiences. Yes, I would recommend this class - we get a chance to learn from Katherine and from our peers. It is also low lift and the cases are pretty interesting.
If you have no experience in marketing and have interest in how MNC marketing works, I recommend. If you already have a background, not much but it can be still interesting to listen to.
Yes. If you really want to understand how to enter a new market from a strategic perspective then this is your course. 100% to recommend
Yes - she is a real practitioner with great insights!
This is a crucial course if you are interested in an international career or international marketing. Also the only course heavy on international content. Other courses can be very US-centric.
Absolutely! One of the best classes I have taken at Haas, and learnt so much about how businesses work
internationally. Must take for anyone interested in understanding international businesses
Yes, the instructor has very valuable real life experience and like the board meeting style presentation. Come to class with open mind and you will love it.
Yes!
Yes. It is an interesting way to learn from an industry expert
Yes! Marketing within an international context is such a fascinating concept and Katherine does an excellent job of explaining this subject.

YES! I am not planning to go into marketing as a full-time job, but this class is honestly fun, informative, and feels really interesting. I love the aspects of getting to learn from international classmates and Katherine is a lovely professor with an incredible background in international business. Keep in mind - it's easy to loaf around on the group projects or to not fully read the case studies before showing up - but you will only get out what you put in. If you show up having read the case studies, the class will be a lot more engaging and meaningful. The guest speakers are also super qualified and incredible:D
Yes I would recommend this class. I looked forward to it every week

Overall yes, it's a good introduction to international marketing without a crazy workload. I do wish the cases are more creative/recent and the content could go beyond just Asia and North America. But Katherine is a great professor and she genuinely cares about students. I enjoyed the class overall!

I would highly recommend this course. It's shaped and enhanced my perspective on global international marketing in a new way, so much so I would like to really consider a long term career in this space. Also, I really like the diverse perspectives of my classmates. I think this type of course attracts people from all of the world. That added a lot of value for me.
50%. I think the cases are interesting to learn and I enjoy the conversation/discussions in the first few classes. But it got messy and made me tired soon.

I would recommend this course to someone who is very interested in learning about global companies and their international expansion strategies. This class is very case-heavy, so keep in mind there is a fair amount of reading before each class. However the topics are usually very engaging and provide a great opportunity to learn from our classmates' and professor's real world experiences living outside of the US.

rows.title: Data Analytics
rows.ghostNote: Ten-week data analytics course aimed at general managers rather than analysts. No history under this number; the instructor's career record (6.03, 31st percentile) is the only signal.

rows.title: Special Selected Topics for MBA Students

sections.goodFor: Students with little or no prior exposure to entrepreneurship or VC, especially those newer to the Bay Area, who want a condensed experiential introduction to both worlds and connections with MBA students from around the globe.
sections.notFor: Anyone with real entrepreneurship or VC experience or prior coursework; several commenters said it will not move the needle for them. Remote takers should expect painful cross-time-zone group logistics.
sections.workloadNote: An intense one-week immersion: roughly 48 hours deep as an entrepreneur, then another 48 as a VC, with short-turnaround group assignments; be prepared to work very hard.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (3 comments): the compressed one-week format made group assignments across time zones very difficult on short turnarounds. One student found the VC-side instruction disjointed and hard to follow, and another flagged misaligned incentives because some students were not taking the course for credit.
sections.quote: The style of the class is to sort of throw you in to the deep end and let you figure it out. It can get a little intense, but it works.
comments: Yes, if you have zero exposure to the world of investment/entrepreneurship

It is a bit of an intense week. A roughly 48 hour deep dive as an entrepreneur and then another roughly 48 deep dive as a VC. The style of the class is to sort of throw you in to the deep end and let you figure it out. It can get a little intense, but it works. I learned a ton about both worlds and their connection.

Definitely recommend it to students looking for 1) connection with fellow MBA students from different parts of the world 2) condensed introduction to entrepreneurship and VC and their connection, and 3) experimental learning by building business model as entrepreneur and building investment thesis as VC partner. However, if you already have experience with entrepreneurship and/or VC or have taken some classes with either subject, this may not be the right level of class for you. [Only for remote learning] Since a lot of students are taking this remotely from different time zones, you have classmates that are taking this class 3am in the morning. Prepare for different energy
level/availability/etc. when doing group project after class.

I would recommend the instructor and course if the student was newer to entrepreneurship and the Bay Area, the topic is definitely well covered. While I thought the course itself was valuable, I found the group assignments via Zoom and all constricted to a week very difficult. It was hard for me to coordinate with my team in different time zones and often times we were tasked to submit assignments on very short turnaround. I understand it's only a week long course and so it's not possible to have much depth in the assignments but I would almost prefer less assignments spread out over time. In addition, some students apparently were not going to receive grades or credits for the course and I feel that definitely makes the incentives less aligned for group project work.

If you could split this course into two different courses, I might take the first one with Sara (entrepreneur-side), but I would definitely not take the one with David (VC-side). The entrepreneur-side portion of the class was much more "real-life impact" as you got to work and talk with actual founders of companies, and fit those discussions into well- defined and taught aspects of entrepreneurship management. The VC-side was nearly impossible to follow, as David's approach to teaching material was entirely disjointed and followed logical progression, leaving most students without any kind of substantial learning. The guest speakers, as wonderful as they were, began to just start feeling like time- fillers, as the discussion with them were often unguided and rehashed comments made by other speakers. Their contributions would be much more impactful if they were tied to specific parts of the teaching and had their discussion based around that module. All in all, not a good course for Haas to be showing externally to the GNAM world.
It is a good overview of the entrepreneurship and VC ecosystem in Silicon Valley, but the class did not move the needle much for me.
Great course. Be prepared to work very hard. But it is only one week so you can do it.

Yes I absolutely would - If you are interested in data, algorithms, bias, data science - this is the course for you. Professor Doug does a great job in bringing in real world practical examples to supplement his theoretical sections. I would recommend this course for any leader or manager in the data analytics/AI space. It really opens your mind to potential issues and flaws. This is not a technical course at all and is more concept based. The content is NOT hard (AT ALL) to understand and is very practical in nature. That being said, if you are not in the analytics field then this course is probably not for you.
ABSOLUTELY. This class changed my career path, helped me see disruptive opportunities on the horizon for
businesses. Transformative course, should be in the core. Also, Professor G is ideal — engaging, caring, thorough and detailed in his planning, sets up expectations up front. Awesome course.

Would absolutely recommend. The course made AI/ML feel less intimidating, and helped me understand how to work with these tools, even as a non-technical leader. Prof. Guilbeault is clearly passionate about the topic and committed to helping students learn about this field and improve how organizations use AI/ML tools.
Yes. So many of the topics covered are relevant and applicable to a workplace.

I think this class would be great for anyone who is in or plan to pursue data-related careers. For me, it's still a great introductory class on some of the latest analytics methodology and trends, but it's hard to digest beyond certain level of complexity
I recommend this instructor for People Analytics given how well versed he is on the matter.
Yes

yes 100% very substantial deep learning, quite technical in the right way that was always accessible, yet challenging for classmates who wanted to dive deeper. He is also a fantastic listener and goes above and beyond in his timely, detailed responses to students. Supports us in and outside of the classroom. Rigorous in the right way. Very fulfilling class.

No. People Analytics is s valuable subject, but the course as structured felt inaccessible to novices. Additionally, almost all of the course is focused on AI/ML without any mention of more simple methods like surveys. This often felt more theoretical than discussing practical uses.

Yes. It's a great course for students interested in machine learning and people analytics. The course is really well done and there's plenty of room for students to debate and discuss. I felt like the course could benefit from slightly more structured cases but it's on an emerging field so that's to be expected.
Yes, great introduction for managers concerned with people analytics and management analytics. Prof was excited and knowledgeable to teach - great at connecting.
Yes, Doug is great. Excellent knowledge on the topics, great use of speakers, and great use of class participation techniques.

I would recommend this course if it is taught in person (not virtually). Erica's experience in interpersonal skills is second to none. She is an incredible listener, wonderfully organized, and truly passionate about the course's subject matter. She also isn't afraid to switch things up on the fly, which improves the classroom learning experience. The class dives deep into interpersonal relationships, which aren't covered in most classes at Haas. The applied nature of the course means that we get to practice Erica's techniques with other students in a psychologically safe environment. The learning is very applicable to personal and professional relationships. However, the virtual environment is not conducive to this type of class. This class relies on human connection, which is significantly more present in real life than on a computer screen. Zoom creates additional fatigue and also enables more distraction.

This class was hands down the most meaningful and transformational class of my entire MBA experience. I almost didn't take it because I had heard mixed reviews, especially regarding the virtual format of the class (even after other classes were back in person), but I can't imagine my time at Haas having been nearly as fulfilling and rewarding without this class. The course itself is beautifully designed, with a slow ramp-up with pre-readings and reflections, and then the sessions themselves do a wonderful job of tying together all of these concepts and putting them to practice. I will admit that the course would not have been as rewarding if the other students in my T-group hadn't been so committed to the experience, so it's important to only take this class if you will be willing and able to fully lean into it. I already feel like a much more confident person and that my ability to communicate and make connections with others has improved considerably. I can't wait to start applying these lessons in the real world, in both my personal and professional relationships.

I'd recommend the course, but be wary that it is a very large commitment, and the time invested vs. learnings may not be worth it for all. I think it's helped me practice and consciously think about how to better connect with others and build empathy

Yes, absolutely. I would go so far as to say this should be (or at least some version of this) should be part of the core curriculum. Even if students find the content challenging or uncomfortable the long-term benefits are significant. Yes, I would recommend this course to a fellow student. The written exercises were amazing reflective pieces and I have a ton of amazing tools for giving feedback and connection with family, friends and colleagues.
Absolutely. The skills taught a life-changing. I now have more confident to live a happy life. Best class ever taken in Haas.

Yes. At a structural level, this was one of the best run courses I have seen where all 4 of the instructors were in synch with one another. It was clear that they had either worked closely with one another before and/or they rehearsed before class.

At a content level, I would dare say this was unequivocally better than the similar core class of Leadership Communications -an-easy-to-understand progression of the curriculum, more practice for students within a similar amount of time, and most importantly, an emphasis on listening and internalization (a critical skill that I am struggling to think is present in other MBA courses).
As for Erica and her co-instructors, it is clear they are deeply invested in teaching the material and in the development of the students.
In brief, I came in as a sceptic, and came out a believer.
I am not very sure. I think the class content is good but there are some moments I feel awkward. For example, the discussion about rank and DEI...

I would recommend this course to students that are seeking to (re)connect with their inner-self and their presence. This course uses unconventional learning methods that may require a major stretch to some students.
Yes highly recommend, but I would be sure to set the expectation that it will probably be challenging in a way that's very different from what they are used to.
Absolutely. This course has been very valuable. It stretches you in essential areas and these aren't stretched in other MBA classes.

Yes, this class is WAY different than any other class you'll likely take at Haas and I genuinely feel the practices and awareness I've built throughout will be carried with me for the rest of my life. The impact is both personal and professional and usability is immediate.
Yes, this is a fantastic course and is extremely valuable. This is different than all other MBA classes, but it should be required for Haas graduates.
I would definitely recommend this course for students that are thinking to become a coach or explore other leadership styles other than advisor/mentor/dictator
Yes; the course is well managed and well-balanced by the co-facilitators. It is a long couple days but worth the experiential (and theoretical) learning.

Yes I would recommend this course to a fellow student because it is a rare opportunity to really hone in on communication and listening skills in a way that is highly applicable to our careers but also to all other aspects of our lives and relationships we will have in our lives.
Not but class. But I would suggest that you should check a syllabus in advance because this class was 9-6pm instead of 9-5pm unlike other classes.

You learn ways to coach and are given time to practice coaching. Its worthwhile if you have 2 Sunday's you can give up. Definitely more learning than in some 15-week Haas courses. Need to show up prepared to engage and be

present. Not too invasive, but its better if you choose to be vulnerable. In terms of people skills, its worthwhile. Highly recommend this course! It is fun and interactive, all of the instructors are amazing and it resulted in substantial learning on how to coach and lead through coaching. Lots of hands on experience that you can use immediately after class.
This is an Extremely worthwhile class. Haas soft skills classes are truly life transforming in a way that these skills go a long way in both personal and professional lives.
Yes, it is such a practical skill to learn and apply in life and work
Yes - great class as it teaches skills that you will use far beyond your career.

Yes if you are interested in managing people at some point in your career (everyone) this have really tangible skills for coaching and when and how to apply them. It gets you to actually do it which resonates more

Absolutely. Instructors were awesome and in tune with our needs. They respectful met us where we struggled and helped us identify ways of being better. This has been my favorite class at Haas to date. Full day long classes seem long but in this class, time flies by with the activities. The activities also allowed us to connect with one another and the instructors on a more personal level which made this class more meaningful than others.

Yes I would! I think this class and discussion is an amazing step into being a Leader especially with people who are smarter than you in other ways or even when it comes to managing other managers. Leading as a coach will be a skill for all of us as we grow in our careers past managing jobs in which we have direct experience in.
Yes was a practical class to learn from doing, and was good to have frameworks and skills to take away
Yes. This is a great course for someone who wants to be a manager or a leader. The course is particularly helpful when you can be fully present and can bring your heart into each of the exercises.
Coaching is a skill which will serve you for a long time not just in a professional setting but also in a personal setting.
I would definitely recommend this course

Yes, as a biopharma professional, this is definitely one of the best class I have ever taken at Haas during the whole program. Highly recommend this to my fellow students who are pursuing the career in this field.
Definitely. If you want to understand what is happening to the industry and have contact with people that have distinguished career in Healthcare, this class is a must

Interesting course covering the macro picture of the healthcare industry, with focus on pharmaceuticals. Very helpful to get a well-rounded view of the industry and the pros and cons to the current structure. Good guest speakers and interesting discussions held in class. One team presentation, one individual paper and one case study. Overall, not terribly difficult and learned more about the industry as a whole. Obviously, I recommend enrolling only if you plan to go into the healthcare industry.

I definitely will recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student because the topics are really interesting. I learn so much from the contents of material in this course. Guest speakers and the instructors are very experienced and knowledgable. The instructors are very nice and the students in this course are working in this field which adds on lots of input to this topic.
Yes, great guest lectures and lot of interesting practical insights into the industry shared
Instructors are passionate and bring a lot of energy to their presentation

Yes. The experience was definitely drastically better than normal due to what was clearly a one-time special visit by Novartis's head of US, but it was still an excellent experience overall. Highly topical and has us thinking about the right things. Kim and Scott are great.

Yes. For students interested in biotech, this class is wonderful. The concepts covered may be a bit difficult to follow for students who're exploring this area of interest but don't have a biotech/healthcare background. It may be helpful to hold a short session to review different players in the biotech ecosystem and their role (e.g. what a PBM is, etc.) The content shared by Scott and the amazing candor from Victor on Day 1 were amazing, one of the top five classes for me at Haas so far. It's really rare to get an in depth look at how a major company tackles significant challenges in their industry in real time, it was definitely special. The group case assignment provided a good opportunity to ideate and explore important challenges in the industry, which I found valuable. There were challenges operating in the group format since this was an elective where most of the students had no prior relationship. Dedicated effort to create students groups by the faculty and opportunities to do some team building before the start of the class would have helped a lot. The groups generated some interesting ideas, but the presentation format could have been better. During WeInnovate the groups develop their own ideas to address a specific industry challenge and they are provided feedback and guidance from the other participants. Incorporating a formal mechanism for the groups to evaluate all the other presentations would have been interesting. Overall, if someone is interested in a career in pharma/biotech this class is a must!

rows.title: Haas@Work
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2022 Spring;2023 Spring;2024 Spring;2025 Spring;2026 Spring

comments: For better or worse, it's an unique experience. It take time to get use to it at the start but the process is fun and lighthearted. Focus on the team project aspects of the class. lectures are usually hit or miss.
Yes, applies the design thinking framework in a very practical setting. I really enjoyed working on a real problem that a real company faced.

I would recommend as long as you have a strong interest in the industry/company that your project is focusing on. Recommend. Heavy workload, but being client facing and very project focused keeps your work ethic somewhat active while you slack off and atrophy as a student
Yes, because it teaches you how to work amidst ambiguity, adjust to different working styles, and solve complex problems.

No. This course has more work than 2 other electives combined. Unless you truly love design thinking, hard pass. You waste a lot of time in weekly plenaries that aren't all that informative and this course drags on way longer than most other classes.

Yes, but be aware the level of effort that this class requires. It is NOT a class you can BS or hide in, you should be prepared to work a good amount outside of this class. It is an AI course afterall so I understand why the LOE is high, but this class felt like a lot of work. I think it was worth it overall, but I do have some reservations. It was good client facing experience, and I learned a lot about my client, but there were definitely a few lates nights spent on assignments.
Definitely yes! It's not easy to get through the whole course, but it's worth to take and push yourself to think more and do more to the real business world.
Extremely practical and applicable to the real world

Good for getting consulting experience. Will have a really hard time if you are not bought into the Chaos of Design Thinking. I feel its like rolling the dice, if you get a good project and a good team, you can learn a lot. But, be prepared to be frustrated a lot. But, if you are into Design Thinking or Consulting, definitely an opportunity to get real world experience. Also, as with any course, you will really get what you put into it. Being a team lead is a great opportunity to practice your managerial skills.
yes
The course experience may be a hit or a miss.

In my experience. 2/3rd of the problem statement we received was completely out of the scope of the kind of work that's best-done by design thinking. Hence, we spent a lot of time sifting through the problems, and the teaching staff, instead of revising the problem statement, was intent on "fitting" the non-applicable solutions to those 2/3 of problems. That resulted in a lot of wasted time and effort.

The class organization is also VERY hierarchical under the project leader. So, contrary to the class description of the project leader being first among equals, the project leader is treated as more than equal when there are critical client conversations, such as the problem statement example above. The project leader is also the only one with a line of communication to the client. It was left to the project leader to include or not include other team members in client discussions, so there was a lot of monopolization of these client communications even though this is phrased as a project where "students work with clients," most of the team (except the project leader), close to zero client interaction outside of the presentations at various checkpoints.

This course is great at providing experience and exposure to innovation consulting. It is both an innovation project and a client engagement. There is a lot of work, but in the end students gain valuable experience on the process and how it applies in a consulting context.

I would recommend Hass@work for anyone interested in getting a client-facing experience. There isn't substantially more content to learn beyond the fundamentals of design thinking class, but the learnings from applying the theory to a real-world business problem are substantial.

Yes, Haas@Work is an amazing experience, especially if you're looking for a deep dive into design thinking or if you're looking to go into product management! I really enjoyed how we worked with real clients and were able to form full- fledged solutions for their very real business problems. Would 100% recommend.

I would recommend this class for people who are interested in applying design thinking process and are passionate about learning about one of the particular clients as you get to work immersively on a client's project which entails a real business challenge they're solving. There's some overlap in this class and fundamentals of design thinking, but I enjoyed taking them in the same semester so I can reinforce my understanding of the course.

The course was extremely effective in providing a taste of how consulting in the real-world would look like. I loved the frameworks the class provides around the design thinking process. I loved the open-ended vagueness of the class as well. As with any other experential class - the class will give you in return all that you put in. It has also helped me become a more effective leader leading a large diverse team. Definitely recommend the class to anyone interested in consulting and/or product management.
I would recommend this course if you're interested in diving into Design Consulting with real clients, real problems, coming up with real solutions.

I would highly recommend Haas@Work to anyone who has a hard problem to solve at work or in your personal life. This is a wonderful framework and combined with real world clients, it is a valuable experience. It is a great tool in your arsenal. Be ready to be uncomfortable and brace ambiguity as your friend
Yes - it's a rare opportunity to challenge yourself and dive into a design thinking framework with a real-world client while still having the support of experienced coaches and faculty.
I somewhat recommend this course to anyone without any consulting experience.

No, unless you want to practice Design Thinking without taking on an internship. Not all clients are a good fit for design thinking solutions, and this makes the course challenging. My client was not a good fit for design thinking because it is a very conservative organization. A quantitative approach would have been more effective in building business cases for them.

Yes I think it was great experience getting to work with a client and employ design thinking in an ambiguous space Although most of the Haas@Work instructors are kind people, this class yielded very little technical learning. Instead, it resulted mostly in the frustrations and headaches that come with doing one giant, semester-long group project. Yes
Yes, the course was very useful in learning to turn innovation and ambiguity into something understandable using a process based approach. 10/10 would recommend
Yes
I would recommend the course if individuals are interested in design thinking as a career. Otherwise I likely would not recommend it.

I believe that the class needs some improvements. One is that the class needs to be configure to be a learning hub, we take this class to learn, not to work for a company. I believe the incentives are not really align between the class creators and the student's needs.
Other than that, if you come with an open mentality, you will find it very interesting and you will get to work with an amazing team of peers that will surprise you.

I do not recommend this class unless: (1) you really want to work for one of the clients, (2) you absolutely need something like it for your resume, or (3) you already have lost faith in your classmates and Haas as a whole. This class singlehanded made me go from optimistic about my time at Haas after my first semester to souring on my classmates and the whole Haas system at the end of my second semester during this program. I learned very little in this class, the workload was hugely disproportionate, and the process of "learning innovation" was disappointing. My classmates abandoned me. They will abandon you. If you care, don't take this class. The clients were OK though.
I would only recommend Haas@Work to students who are very interested in design thinking and are prepared for a lot of work with unclear payoffs.
Yes. The course is a great opportunity to practice business skills, and it is highly applicable to future work experience Yea for sure.

This class is very much group and client dependent, which makes it hard to recommend overall. If you are set on going into innovation and design consulting, than you may want to consider this class, but you may be able to explore other ways to get this experience. I think this class is a great concept, but the execution needs help at this time. I wanted to like this class more than I did.
Yes. Good way to turn theory to practice.
100%. This course is great for those who are engineers and think they lack creativity
Yes, direct experience in client and project management
Would recommend, as have the opportunity to work with a leading company in the industry and gain real life practical experience.

Haas@Work is an excellent course to learn client management, design organization, and project management in a real environment. While it can be frustrating at times, it all makes sense in the end. If you get Jeff as your team mentor, you won.
Yes! All instructors are amazing!

Course gives a good overview of design thinking and innovation concepts. The client project are of mixed levels of interest. So you could get lucky or end up with a dry project. However, either way the learnings are solid and there is often food provided.

Absolutely loved my team and this class as a way for me to learn how to solve difficult client problems and work with my team to clearly define the problem. We were glad to have the GSIs and the instructors guide some of the way but this the strength of this course is working in a small team and understanding team dynamics with a challenging problem.
Yes, even though the class loading is relatively high and requires students to spend more time and efforts, the payoff and feedback from the client during the presentation is super rewarding.
This is a must take course. You get real world experience in a very collaborative environment.
I would recommend. It?s a great opportunity to learn and practice design thinking to real world problems. I just wished I had a wide variety of projects to choose from.
Yes, very insightful hands on work experience working with people from different backgrounds on real problems companies are facing

Yes! This course is a crash course on how you can come up with innovative solutions to any problem and thrive in ambiguity. It was one of my favourite courses this year and is full of really incredible people. The course staff are so insightful and supportive.
Yes: no pain no gain. Hard work pays off in this course
Yes if the student has an interest in digital transformation/innovation

I would recommend this course to anyone that?s interested in the innovation and creative process in general. This could be design work, but also could be any job that has a design component. Through the diverging and converging experience, I had any learning opportunities and have become more confident even when faced with a question that?s unconventional or doesn?t have an obvious answer. High recommend.
Yes
Yes, I think it is a good way to dip your toes into consulting and design thinking. Engaging and fun
Yes - this was a super valuable experience that's you can't find from most HAAS classes.
Yes; interesting experience working with a client. Great team building. Good opportunity to learn design thinking frameworks and learn tools to approach problems from a different perspective.
Yes, if you're looking for a practical application course. It really depends on what client you get. But I appreciated the opportunity to practice design thinking in a low stakes environment.
David is absolutely a wonderful instructor to have and learn from. Just expect the course to be more of a consulting style project and have appropriate expectations.

One of three projects in my year was great- the other two had client issues. I think that the learnings offered by the course are mostly derived from intuition and common sense. The real value is in the team and having fun, eating dinner, seeing your client excited about their work again.
100% recommend Jeff. You will be lucky to have him as a coach. Jeff made this innovative framework easy for someone like me with zero experience

Yes i would recommend this class. Its a low stake way to get experience with a new method for real clients I would recommend this instructor and course to fellow students, particularly those who have not had a consulting background and are looking to gain experience in that area. The course provides ample opportunities to work in large groups, which can be highly beneficial for developing teamwork and collaborative skills. However, prospective students should be aware that with large group sizes, sometimes reaching up to 9 members per team, individual contributions can feel somewhat diluted. This large team size can also lead to a competitive atmosphere, which might impact personal development time. If you are comfortable navigating these dynamics and are eager to engage in extensive group work, this course can offer valuable experience.

I would recommend if they are wanting to learn more about a new industry or topic and work in a team. This class is not for folks to want specific consulting experience because it is not really about that. But it's a great way to dive into a topic and learn fun things!

This has been my favorite class at Haas so far. I made friends through it, expanded my network, got great resume points/interview story, and was just a lot of fun. This is the best applied innovation class because you really get something substantive from it, but it's not as much work/stress as the other applied innovation courses. Yes, though I would emphasize that this course is pretty dependent on the project you get. Of course, there are many components that are shared across any team, but I think that the project really impacts your experience. No, not really because they are ample of other AI course that can be a better use of your time. In terms of learning, these concepts can be learned in other classes as well.

sections.goodFor: Students exploring consulting or design thinking with no prior client experience; strong practice at client interaction, insight generation and storytelling, and it stays local.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a true consulting class (it is framework/design-thinking focused), or anyone on a team that isn't bought in - several say a disengaged team makes it a slog. Team leads carry more.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified and contested: one calls it a relatively chill Applied Innovation class, others say it requires substantial outside work. Load depends on the client project and is worst for team leads.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; team client project and presentations are the visible deliverables
sections.redFlags: Experience varies a lot by project and team buy-in (3 students); team leads shoulder much more work (1); it is not a direct consulting class despite expectations (1).
sections.quote: But caveat, if people are not bought into the project, it can be hard work. I'd encourage team buy in from the beginning
comments: This was the most meaningful course of my first year. I absolutely loved being able to test and learn design thinking and consulting in such a growth-minded and fun environment. You will truly get as much out of this course as you put into it. The course's mantra of "trust the process, do the work", is something that I can't wait to apply for the rest of my life!
Yes
Yes, especially if you want a (relatively) chill Applied Innovation class that keeps you local
Yes - hugely applicable, great frameworks, repeatable process
Yes
Yes, absolutely! Both Haas and Ischool/ MIMS students should learn this method, how to work in diverse teams, the power of feedback, and would enhance their product design and management skills.
Great for someone that is looking to gain experience in engaging with clients

Great course. Highly practical. Good learning experience if you want to know how to present or interact to clients. It is not a direct consulting class, but if u have 0 prior experience this will give a good introduction. More a framework class to understand design thinking.

I would recommend the course. It's a great process to go through and understand. But caveat, if people are not bought into the project, it can be hard work. I'd encourage team buy in from the beginning

I would recommend this course as it helps get some relevant experience in design thinking and client work. However, some projects are more difficult than others, so it may require far more work. Be prepared to invest energy into this, especially if you are one of the team leads.

[REDACTED IN THE PUBLIC BUILD] A student described finding the team-lead role considerably harder and more emotionally draining than expected, and said they would not recommend it to others in their position. — Why: The original names the writer's race and gender. In a section this size that is potentially identifying, and it was written for a CalNet-gated audience.

This is a great course for any students exploring the consulting or design thinking spaces. It will give you plenty of practical experience and provide a boost to your resume when applying to jobs. This course does require a substantial amount of work outside the classroom, but it's worth it in the end!
Yes, helpful for navigating team and client dynamics.

Yes, it was great because you learn a ton about how to generate insights and communicate them, storytelling is a big part of this course and you get to practice it in real-time. It was also a great bonding experience with our team.

sections.goodFor: Students targeting consulting or wanting real client work, human-centered design/innovation methods, and practice leading through ambiguity.
sections.notFor: Anyone who can't absorb team-lottery risk or needs structured teaching - it is learning by doing, class time is unstructured, and instructors/TAs are reported not to intervene when teams break down.
sections.workloadNote: Semester-long team consulting engagement with a real client dominates the work; evening sessions are short lectures plus team working time. 'A fair amount of hands-on work.'
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: Experience hinges on your team/client (3+); one reports 'carrying a LOT of dead weight'; 2 call class time inefficient with instructors/TAs not stepping in; oneone student reported the team-lead role was unexpectedly draining.
sections.quote: Ultimately, your experience is far, far, far too at the mercy of who you get grouped up with on your team.
comments: The frameworks and thought process that I learned from this class were something I immediately started applying at my job, and I'm sure I will continue using them. It forces you to think in unconventional ways, to explore alternatives and to validate ideas. Working so closely with a team for a semester is also one of the best experiences I've had at Haas. I would definitely recommend the course.
I got a lot out of this course. I had fun, I learned a lot.

8 times out of 10, I would absolutely NOT recommend this course to a fellow student, unless they indicated to me that they would benefit from going through the type of consulting project that this course offers. Ultimately, your experience is far, far, far too at the mercy of who you get grouped up with on your team. While I had some great team members, I'm exhausted from carrying a LOT of dead weight.
Yes
Yes. This course is helpful in case you're looking for an internship and/or looking to work with a client without fear of failure

Haas@Work is a signature course at Haas for a reason and brings human-centered design and innovation principles into practice with real clients. The class combines consulting, product management, AI, strategy, and client work together in a hands on class. Even though it meets in the evenings, I found every class to be valuable time to work with my team and learn consulting and innovation skills that apply in any job context. I loved this class and highly recommend it, although it is a fair amount of hands on work with the internal team and client!

I highly recommend this course to anyone looking to work in the consulting industry. It involves real client needs and helps solve their actual pain points. The entire process closely reflects what real consulting work is actually like. Yes, absolutely; it was very hands on and helped me develop tools for dealing with ambiguous problems and helped in understanding how to " trust the process "
I probably wouldn't recommend the course. With the rise of AI tools today, I feel like part of the course's value proposition has become less compelling

Yes, this class is great if you're looking for hands-on client experience, experience with design thinking methodology, or growth in leadership (internal or client-facing). The experience can be mixed based on the client project you are assigned to, however. It's also less about structured learning and skill sets and more about learning through doing and getting comfortable with navigating ambiguous, complex problem spaces.

Yes, I would recommend both the course and professor. I appreciated the open creative space that was created for us to work in, the lectures were relevant and helpful, but short enough to leave time for group work. I enjoyed working on a real project with real clients and appreciate the structure of this course for making that possible.
No. The class time felt wildly inefficient and I didn't feel like the instructors or TAs stepped in to help or push us along when needed
