Yes, you will remember the experience
Yes! This class will provide you with a strong foundation to solve ambiguous challenges and allow you to build confidence in tackling challenges in areas you may not be familiar with.
no

This class resulted in incredible learning for only one unit. I highly recommend this class. You learn about financing, tax management and hedging, all in a "risk free" environment, and you have multiple opportunities to learn from your mistakes. This was an excellent class all around, and for only one unit, that makes it even better. Only comment is to not make your team more than 4 people. We had 6 and it was too many.

I would (and have already) recommended this class 100x over for any business student. Veselina is a great instructor and I felt that I learned worlds about corporate finance from this game that I otherwise would not have experienced (or paid attention to) without actually working in a corporate treasury function. I am by no means in finance myself, but the game is complex and extremely interesting. It shows you in a controlled fashion how operational, investing, and financial decisions will impact a company realtime, in everything from assets, liabilities, and debt expense to hedging, forex exposure, and credit ratings. I think this is the most worthwhile 1-credit course I have taken or will take at Haas.
Yes! It's a great course which allows you to actually manage forex and currency markets
Yes. Well worth the 1 credit.
Yes, I would recommend both. The class, while a lot of work for a 1 credit class, it was a good "cap stone" for business school.

FORAD is a lot of work but you will learn a lot if you put time into it. Make sure you have a group you'd want to work with before you fully enroll in the course since it's all group work. Veselina is a really caring professor and puts a lot of time into this course. Good luck!

100%. You will get out what you put in. So, don't take the class if you want to burn 1 credit because you'll be doing yourself and classmates a disservice. This was a great wrap up to my MBA experience.

This is a wonderful class to take for those who are looking to expand their understanding of corporate finance, in a fun and hands-on environment, especially for those who want to do so without reading an assigned textbook, studying material for a final or having to build a complex excel model.

Yes! The course is a great opportunity to understand the many different decisions and trade-offs that one has to think about in running a company. This is an opportunity to experiment and learn. The more you put into this class, the more you will get out of it. Also Veselina is just awesome as a teacher and highly recommend taking a class with her! I would be skeptical. I have heard wonderful things about this professor in other contexts/for other classes. However, in this class, I was very frustrated with her frustration when students didn't miraculously "get" or understand something that to her was apparently obvious. She sometimes used a condescending tone.
I recommend this course and I believe most MBAs, especially those in Management Rotation Programs will find the course conversations around interrelationships between business units very useful.
Yes but your group makes all the difference

yes for students who are interested in how to make a good financial decision in a multinational corporation. Unless you have a strong finance background, this course will be very difficult to get through.
YES! Take this course- it's a great capstone to the courses you've taken.

Yes, I recommend this course because the professor's relaxing teaching style and the strong engagement from the class. Also, learning through a simulation game helps you gain the knowledge deeply as if you are running a company in real-world. I really enjoyed the learning experience and class vibes.

This was a really fun course that resulted in substantial learning about operations, financing, investing, hedging, tax management, and more when it comes to running a multi-national corporation. It was a great opportunity to integrate materials from other Haas courses as well. I would highly recommend the course to Haasies interested in corporate management and understanding how to trade-off / balance various aspects of a corporation.

Yes! This class was very unique in covering exchange rates, commodity hedging, tax management and a number of additional concepts that I did not get exposure to in other courses. The semester long simulation was a fun and engaging way to learn about these concepts.

Yes I would recommend the class. It's a fun game to play through while learing about practical trade-offs. I especially like the last session when the professor and the class sat down together to discuss our choises and looking through the practical lens. It's reasonable (or someone might say light) amount of workload.
At the same time the professor allows auditor students to form a team and participate together too. If you feel confident about your level of participation, auditing the class is also a good choice.

A lot of learning for a single unit class, and it pulls together a lot of financial concepts and gives perspective into how companies approach strategy for dividend disbursement, commodity pricing and foreign exchange rate, managing interest rates on the Company's debt, overall tax management, etc. Fun simulation.

You get out what you put in in this class. If you like the simulation, you will meet with Veselina during Office hours and learn a lot. If you coast by or let your teammates do the work, it's going to be a very low-lift class
Veselina is one of the best professors I've had at Haas!

I recommend this class for those interested in financial management of a large company. It is a firsthand opportunity to practice skills for financial management. At first the amount of information is a bit overwhelming but it gets better and is a fun competition.
Absolutely! This class is very unique in being a full-semester simulation. It combines learning and applying finance, operations and other corporate management skills in a very thorough and fun way!

Possibly. I felt I learned a moderate amount from having to make "real" (simulated) decisions. For example, while I had a high-level understanding of what currency exposure was and how a company might deal with it before this class, this class really enforced how it actually works and how to think it through. (I didn't get that from FIA or Corporate Finance, so even if you've taken those, you'll learn things or have concepts reinforced in a helpful way here.) I say "possibly" because I feel I could have learned more, but all in all it was a useful 1-unit course.

Yes. I think that if you want to understand a little about international finance, it is a great experience Yes - good way to check yourself on what you've learned thus far and what is worth reviewing as you graduate.
Absolutely! It's a great way to familiarise with all the concepts seen during the core and understanding how they all interact with each other in the real world

Definitely take this course, especially if you have people who you can take it with to form a good team. It's a fun experience to learn the simulation (which is very complicated). Helped me get a lot smarter about things like FX, oil hedging, inventory, and tax management.
Yes I would, Veselina is a wonderful instructor and does a great job of explaining real world applications of the theory she reviews in class

I would absolutely recommend both. I think the class is very rewarding in terms of practical skills for the relatively low amount of time you have to put into it. Definitely a great opportunity for anyone who wants to apply (with a practical game) all the theoretical learnings of Operations, Finance, Accounting, Strategy,...
Yes I plan to recommend this course to first years next year
Yes - great practice and valuable feedback

Yes! Having a pitch (anything - job search, or your company or an event) and refining it over two sessions really helps. I feel like my pitch is way clearer than what it was before I started this class and I have been practicing this job search pitch for an entire year!!

Yes, if you want a relatively light 1-unit course and some practice on speech. It was pretty helpful to practice on a Zoom setting. The session's only for two weeks, so it can be a bit hard to achieve dramatic and lasting improvement in your speech skills

Yes, this class teaches you technicals to structure your thinking when preparing for a pitch, how to select the right materials to pitch, what kind of techniques can strengthen your pitch. Adam is approachable and knowledgeable about communication. Should take it if you want to build your communication to the next level.
Yes! Adam is great, and the content is useful. I think this is a great class especially for folks who are looking for jobs or who have businesses.

I would recommend this course to anyone looking to strengthen their public speaking skills. Adam is really great and an excellent public speaker who provides a lot of great feedback. It is important to know that you will be working on a pitch (can be yourself for a job, a product release, really anything you want) throughout the class so just keep that in mind before signing up!

I'd definitely recommend AFC. This class worked well in a virtual format, and Adam did a really great job structuring the class so that there wasn't too much work and we didn't get Zoom fatigue. I imagine the course would be at least as good were it held in person. Seems like most students in the class really did improve their speech-giving abilities in just one week, and there are definitely learnings from this class that I'll carry with me moving forward. This class is a great option for anyone who might be in a position of needing to pitch an idea in the future (so, essentially all MBAs), and it's also a great class to practice giving great feedback to others. Overall, quite pleasant experience! Yes! It's a light class that helps you with your communication skills. The technique is useful and truly make a change to people who are lack of skills like me
Highly recommend this class with Adam!!
Absolutely. Tangible addition to skill set
Absolutely great class, one of my favorites so far at Haas. It was amazing to see the improvement that the short time together can have.
It's a very interesting course as an introduction to public speaking. But if you have already been in a public speaking club like Toastmasters or done something similar, it feels a bit basic.
No, the course load is too heavy, the instructor's expectations are unreal and you get poor grades
Yes, I thought it was a very important piece of my overall MBA experience. If you are planning to take this course, be prepared for a decent amount of work in the three days after class 1.

Low-lift course - thought it was adapted well to COVID, but resulted in far fewer substantial learnings as compared to Storytelling for Leadership. Can definitely make the most of the class without a specific pitch in mind at enrollment (I came up with mine about 2 weeks ahead of the class). Adam is a good lecturer/facilitator. Heard lots of complaints from classmates about fairly arbitrary feedback on assignments. Overall recommend, but wouldn't allocate a large number of bid points towards it.
Yes, I would recommend it. It's a great space to learn by doing. And get coached by Adam and your peers.
Yes-- most helpful if you have a pitch in mind already
Yes. Take the course! Especially if you are currently working on pitching yourself (TMAY) or an idea.

This class was amongst my least favorite at Haas. It's squishy, soft, and not particularly helpful (I knew it was a soft skill class, but hoped it might've been helpful). Parts of the class are revisits to Leadership Communication, but there is not enough time for a student to really drill down on their pitch - and you will be working on "one pitch" throughout BOTH sessions. There a few practical take-aways regarding camera etiquette, room lighting (and light source placement, which the teacher will not hold back on scorching you for [as if you're going to rearrange your room and fix it]), the importance of a reliable internet connection for video conferencing (again, the teacher will call you out if yours stinks, as if you're going to get a comcast rep over to fix it), camera placement, and then a "ladder system" that advocates moving from highly detailed --> 30K foot view during a pitch. Adam is an incredible speaker and storyteller, however, so I wonder how much different this class might've been had it been held in-person.

Would recommend. The class is very light in terms of work and you get some nice techniques / frameworks to practice which can be really useful. Also - it is not a "touchy-feely" type of class, it's purely about techniques and presentation Yep! Extremely valuable class and I think I can take its teachings with me wherever I end up.

Yes! Great course. Touches on the technical aspects, business aspects, and ethical aspects of modern AI applications. A good course covering the technical and business aspects of AI in the world today. There was a lot of self-directed video watching to do before the sessions which can get a bit monotonous and confusing at times, as these videos provide the foundation for all other discussion and learning.
Cases were very relevant, recent, and applicable to the topics at hand, and all of the professors are extremely knowledgable in their field.

Yes, it was very interesting to understand what the different companies are doing in terms of AI, and also understand some technical terms I've often heard from my AI Data scientists and engineers at work but wasn't aware of what they meant
Yes. This course is a good introduction to the applications of AI. I would've preferred to attend this class in person since taking this on Zoom does impact the level of engagement.

Whether or not you want to pursue a career related to AI, This course is a must in order to become a more educated being who can understand the future world better (no matter which industry or sector or role you are or want to be in). Definitely. For anyone interested in AI, this class is gives just enough technical detail to understand the technology but also digs into the business applications, limitations, and areas for continued improvement (e.g., where you can invest for your next big idea!)
Maybe. This was worth it in terms of time commitment for a 1 credit class. However, content was very boring and lots of lecture.

Absolutely, this was a great class that showcased topics on emerging business and technology trends. I also liked how there was a little match but most of the subject matter was in regular every day language more appropriate to a manager who needs to be able to communicate and understand key AI concepts.
My favorite Zoom class this year!! Topics were super engaging, professors are fascinating, and class was very well structured.
yes
Yes! This is a comprehensive overview of AI in industry for a non-expert, with many opportunities for further reading and study, and connections with visiting speakers / VCs.
I would strongly recommend this course to other students. It is very well organized and taught, and the material is very relevant for pretty much any function or industry.

Great introduction to core AI concepts in a way that is relevant to business leaders. Videos were a great asset to absorbing material at one's own pace, especially for non-technical folks. There's a great opportunity to make this a more extensive course that gives students more time to learn about and apply these concepts — hoping that happens in later iterations!
This is a great class on the high level technical and business landscape of AI - highly recommend!
Yes, Very good introduction to AI and ML. If you don't know anything and want to immerse in the topic, the course it's a great way to do it.
Getting to learn from Pieter Abbeel is a treat. The rest of the class is average MBA fare.
I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.

As a first introduction or primer to the area of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, the pure content was informative. The deep problem was in how the content was presented. The instructors lectured off of slides for the large majority of both classes. I mean — straight up reading off of slides. Most of the lectures could have been pre- recorded videos, or presented in a custom course-pack to be read ahead of time. Of the 4 cases to read, only 1 was actually pertinent to business practices. The case discussions were extremely light — too light. The deep learning homework assignment was good for someone who never worked in python (like myself).

Yes, I would recommend these instructor and this course to other students. The course did a great job of giving students a peek under the hood of how many complex AI applications work, and it did a good job of highlighting the capabilities, complexities, and limitations of the technology in the field. The course had a good mix of technical explanations, business case studies, and thought exercises around strategy or investment scenarios that will be helpful for anybody working with or managing AI applications in the future.

Good course to get an intro to how AI works and recent developments in the industry. Nothing too technical and assignments were applicable and conducive to learning - for ex, there's a small assignment to get exposure to machine learning code.
Yes, great use of bringing in real-world companies to reinforce course concepts.

If you're interested in AI, applications, and future outlook, this class will give you a very engaging taste of all relevant topics. Good way to "wet the beak" and mapping out where to deep dive next!
I highly recommend this course, particularly for non-technical busniess people. AI and ML is extremely important to the future of all business types. Ignore at your own peril.

Yes - this is a very interactive class for students who want to have a quick download of the industry and trends Absolutely must take class even if you have prior computer science background. I came from an engineering

background, and have taken various online courses in AI, and still find this to be extremely worthwhile. The class is heavily integrated with the industry. VCs are invited, to share their insights on the AI industry. One of the instructors is one of the most recognized AI experts in the industry. What he shares is what you usually can't find from textbooks or online classes. This class is like having Gordon Ramsey teaching you all about cooking.
This class was okay. If you're new to AI/ML this could be a good opener, but overall the class sessions felt extremely long as professors mostly just presented from slides for 7 hours each day.
yes, interesting class

As it is today, I would not recommend this course. I was really excited about the potential of the content but was really disappointed in the delivery. All three professors spoke only to slides for 7.5 hours straight over 2 days. I was interested in the content for my career but this was way too In the weeds for me... was more like a data class than business. While some of the content was interesting on the surface, the teaching format was extremely dry and made it hard to stay alert, especially on a weekend. Also there was wayyy too much work for a one unit class. I hope the professors can make some improvements because I think there IS potential here!
Great for understanding the basics of tech and application of machine learning to date
Great Experience! The class was delivered very well. A lot of insights into the topic.

I would recommend this class overall. It was full of engaging material that was well worth the time. Meaningful grading is a challenge here though. Despite how hard one works, grades may come down to ability to decipher quiz questions that do not necessarily look like class material (or have the similar phrasing). There's room for improvement there. But I loved the material and would make the choice to take the class again. If you have a change to audit, this would have been a GREAT candidate for doing so.
I would strongly recommend this course

Yes, especially if the student is interested in learning about AI, they do a great job covering it in detail. However, yes only if adjustments are made to the workload to make it appropriate for a 1 unit course. This course should be worth 2 units given the amount of work we did.

Are you ready to take your brain to the next level of innovation? Then look no further than this cutting-edge, trailblazing, forward-thinking, and most of all, innovative graduate course about AI! Prepare to be blown away by the innovative methods and innovative tools used to innovate in the field of AI. You'll explore innovative techniques like deep learning, innovative algorithms that use innovative data structures, and innovative models that are pushing the boundaries of what we thought was possible. Don't be left behind in the dust of old-fashioned thinking! Join us in this innovative course and unleash your inner innovator! So come on and sign up today for an innovative and mind- blowing experience that will leave you innovatively innovating for years to come!
Tagline: "Innovate to dominate, or innovate to detonate!"

I'm uncertain if I would recommend this course. It has very intense technical content, which most MBAs are not aware of (and not interested in learning lots of equations) of. Having three professors is a good thing as they alternate and make the Sunday class seem like many different classes. The cases are interesting and applicable to real life and great for discussion, but I often missed a "so what" to the discussions.

This course can get pretty technical at some points and the course work seemed pretty heavy for a 1 unit course. That being said, the material was very interesting and fascinating. The professors were all very accomplished and brought great insights to class. Hearing about their real-world experiences at the forefront of AI was super valuable. I would recommend this course if you are just looking to learn some basic concepts and some of the applications. Absolutely recommend this course!

This course covers a broad range of topics within the field of AI. We reviewed everything from cases to a coding assignment (with guidance) and looked at startups doing AI work. However, given that we only had two days, we didn't dive too far into one particular topic in AI. It was good as a primer for students who don't have a background in AI. I thought it was worthwhile in that regard.

Would recommend if interested in topic and enjoyed classes such as data analytics. Class felt more like just pure AI and was lighter on talking about the actual business of AI (how to make money using AI, how much it costs, etc.) Yes, highly recommend this class!
this was very interesting as an intro course. I liked the VC panel, the computer vision session especially. Strongly recommend
Definite yes. Great 101 and 2 day base on business of AI. Can be fast and overwhelming at times, but overall feel I learnt a lot.

I would recommend having a 2 credit course with more detail. I think 1 credit is less and does not cover everything. Recommend this class to anyone who has little or no background in the subject of AI. Matthew Strepka brought his industry experience to the classroom. He was candid with his investment philosophy and brought his industry contacts to bear by inviting guest speakers deeply experienced in the field. Pieter is a leading figure in the field. He did a phenomenal job ensuring that the technical details of AI were covered well without losing the class in the weeds. I had no knowledge of AI and wanted to get a good overview as a future manager which I feel I got from this class. The morning of the second day definitely covered too much of the technical aspects, though. I wish we had spent more time hearing about businesses and covering case studies.

Yes, This class is well organized, and taught with a genuine passion. The exposure to the VC panel was awesome, the numerous cases and guest speakers were truly informative. Understanding AI is so essential for any future business professional. I think this course is invaluable. One of my best courses so far at Haas
very long course with no discussion or group work. too much lecturing.

comments: I would recommend this class. It's an interesting class with a focused topic, and lots of practical topics and speakers. It is relatively new in its current format, so I think it will get better through time.
Yes great course to learn about sustainable investment and apply it in practice
No. Talking about sustainable and impact investing in secondary market is just a joke.

I would recommend this course to another student if they are passionate about learning the topic. It's a great way to experience hands-on investing and learning about sustainability. I think despite the sustainability lens it is also a great way to gain exposure to the asset management / stock investing world in a hands - on manner.
Yes! Excellent learnings from world-class professors!
the class needs clearer structure and learning perspective from the beginning and the expected engagement with the students
you will learn a lot but the knowledge is kinda scattered around throughout the course, not knowing what's coming at you week-by-week
Yes!Anne & Peter are great to learn from as professionals doing the work in the space. Panos passion on subject matter and research is a great compliment to them both. Great class!

Great experiential learning experience with professors with both deep academic and professional backgrounds Yes! Have already recommended it to friends. This course gives a phenomenal look at both asset management and sustainability - for anyone interested in either, I'd highly recommend taking this course.
Yes I would recommend this class. It was a brand new topic for me and although I felt intimidated at first, by the end I felt like I was up to speed and had learned a lot!

rows.title: Sustainable, Impact, and Climate Investing Landscape

comments: Highly recommend. Great introduction into the impact investing landscape, understanding the foundational concepts, tools as well as the industry landscape. The concise class format balanced lecture, group work, class discussion, and industry expert guest speakers to provide holistic coverage of a complex space within the investment management landscape. Wish I had been able to take it in the first semester!

Definitely. Both Adair and Julia have great ideas about the impact investing industry and cast many insights from investors perspectives. It may be a little hard if you don't have the investment background but still relevant to take the class.

Highly recommend this brief, focused, and very well-run course to anyone even slightly interested in impact investing. Definitely worth your time and the weekend is well-structured and uses the time effectively.

Absolutely would recommend this course for the strong introductory overview on impact investing and how to get involved in this sector. We had multiple guest speakers of interest, as well as two dynamic and experienced professors (Adair & Julia). If you can, I'd recommend taking the class early in your time at Haas as the material will be useful and connected to other areas you're studying.
Not recommend for students who do not have a finance/ investment background.

I would recommend this instructor; I thought that she did a great job of explaining complex topics and exposing me to new information. I don't think I'd recommend this course on a Saturday-Sunday...very easy to burnout and stop retaining material.
Good overview financial/investment products for impact investing and frankly finance overall. Group projects kept class active.
It's a great introductory course to impact investing.
Absolutely! Necessary for anyone interested in sustainable finance.
100% recommend
Yes, this course provided a helpful landscape, and the panel discussions with individuals working in the field provided practical insights.

Yes, overall the course was highly informative and interesting. My only caveat is that some of the objectives are vague so it may take more time than one would anticipate based solely on the volume of work.

I would HIGHLY recommend this course to a fellow student, even though it's on a weekend. I learned so much, and a lot that I was confused about within the impact investing realm was clarified for me. Profs Morse and Sze are absolute powerhouses. The guest speakers they arranged, the group presentations we did, the knowledge they conveyed and the perspective they provided on a space that can be very intimidating because it is so amorphous was absolutely pivotal as I continue my search for an impact investing internship. They are both extraordinarily knowledgeable, very well connected, and quick to share any connections or knowledge they can. Anyone remotely interested in impact investing and how finance can be used to do good should take this class, unequivocally.
I would recommend the instructor but I think that the course feels too rushed. A semester long course where you can assess different asset classes would be preferable.

YES! I you want a primer/intro to all that is Impact Investing, this is it. Adair Morse is excellent and I wish she still tuaght New Venture Finance because I would take it with her. There was some good group work and helpful resources were given, and some interesting guest speakers as well.

Would absolutely recommend. This was one of my favorite Haas classes thus far, likely because the 1st in line with my interests and because it was so well structured. I will also note here that Eileen was an incredible GSI - so prepared. Impact Investing Landscape is a very fast tour through a large and particularly important topic. The scenery will go by quick, and you'll find yourself wishing for more time to dive in deeper - you'll have to follow up on your own or through additional classes to go deeper. Professor Adair Morse is crisp and well-organized - an excellent and expert tour-guide.

sections.goodFor: Students wanting a fast, well-networked overview of the sustainable and impact investing landscape: commenters consistently praise the energetic teaching team and the guest speakers, and recommend it as a crash-course primer, ideally with some finance vocabulary in hand.
sections.notFor: Students with no finance background repeatedly said fundamentals were assumed or glossed over, and those already working in impact investing found little new. Not a mechanism to break into the field, and depth-seekers found coverage superficial given the format.
sections.workloadNote: A compressed 1-unit weekend intensive that several found fatiguing, plus a group research project multiple students said took more time than the unit count suggests.
sections.gradingBasis: Work centers on a group research paper and presentation on a topic within the impact investing landscape.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (6+ comments): the group project was vague and poorly scoped; recurring (5+ comments): assumes finance/investing background and newcomers felt lost; several (3+): compressed format kept the material high-level and hard to digest; a couple felt too much learning came from student presentations rather than the professors.
sections.quote: Highly recommend this brief, focused, and very well-run course to anyone even slightly interested in impact investing.
comments: I would highly recommend the instructors and the course to fellow students. The class is energetic, fast-paced, and gives a very high-level overview of the impact investment landscape. The class project is interesting, engaging, and great for networking.
ABSOLUTELY! I have no background in finance and impact investing at all and simply took it out of curiosity, but I truly enjoyed it.
Yes, this course is accelerated, but trust me, this a very good (and practical) primer within the space. The course title truly meant what they say, and these 3 faculties delivered. Bravo!
If they are interested in impact investing, I would recommend it

I would still recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student but I do believe that there is room for improvement. I think many students (myself included) came in without much (or any) experience in the

finance/investment space so a bit more content on the fundamentals would have been helpful. If there isn't time in class, maybe readings/primers/pre-recorded videos could help fill this gap. I can also appreciate the value in just throwing students into an ambiguous problem, but the team activity in the first class felt a little fast and the group project felt a little nebulous - not a total miss but maybe a better balance could be struck here. That said, the entire teaching team and all of the speakers were great and very engaging presenters (I also appreciated the fact that there were a lot of POCs and women involved, very cool to see).

I would not. But this is not because of the instructors, per say. This is because the teams were extremely unequal and some topics were very easy and some difficult. It resulted in some teams having 1-2 people do work for everyone else on the team. The professors should review that for next class or survey students about share of work. Also the professors need to provide office hours because the assignment lacked definition besides "do the assignment." This is a great course and I highly recommend it for people interested in learning more about the impact investing space. Would definitely prime yourself (if you don't have a finance background) beforehand in terms of the terms used (e.g., the different asset classes), but I felt like I learned a lot and enjoyed diving deeper via the group project. The professors had incredible knowledge between the three of them, and they also brought in really great speakers that added a lot.

I strongly recommend this course for anyone who has even a slight or potential interest in working in or interacting with the sustainable, impact, and climate investing landscape? or even if, like myself, those descriptors sound interesting but you don't actually know what working in those sectors looks like. Great course!!

rows.title: Climate Solutions Fund
rows.disagree: Modest rating, but comments are uniformly enthusiastic

comments: I would highly recommend it as it is a great course with a lot of learning.

If you're interested in a career in climate finance this class is a must. Direct, tangible experience learning from industry professionals via a live deal. This class is a unique opportunity to experience life in this career path. However, there aren't many lectures and most learning comes from your own work, so this class is what you make of it. It demands lots of out-of-class time and collaboration with your project team, but the experiential rewards are worthwhile especially if you're trying to pivot into or explore climate investing careers.

This course is great to meet real CEOs and startups with the possibility of investing. Its pretty challenging given the small window of time and funding constraints like Series B and later. The course needs a few more semesters to be smoothed out, it felt a bit bumpy. For those with an existing big network and willingness to explore the network to find deals.
Yes, this is a course where you can get real-world investing experience.

I would. I really enjoyed the class and thought it was super productive in reaching out and strengthening networks. Its an unbelievable opportunity, but thought it could have used a bit of structure after the main classes ended. I felt like there were things I didn't know that I didn't know, which made it hard to ask questions during the advisor meetings. I loved the experience though and think there are a lot a area to improve.

Yes and no, there were things I liked about the course, but overall it was a bit chaotic in its organization and execution. It felt like we given an impossible task (to find later stage deals as a student, without any exposure to investing before) and wished there would have been a bit more direction as to what we needed to focus on. I think the sectors that each team was given either needed to be more defined, or removed entirely. I think the teacher office hours were hard to manage given they changed times every week, and it would have been easier / better to have the office hours during the class time that students already had planned in their schedules. I would have also been nice to have more in person classes / office hours because it was hard to connect with other teams / other students after we stopped having class. Overall, I felt like the class was rushed, and even though I learned through doing (not as much as others because I already came from investing / VC space) I wish there had been more opportunity to learn.

I would recommend this course and teaching team but with some caveats. I think it would be helpful for there to be more layers of accountability for teams and more up front team facilitation-- it requires teams of people who don't know each other to learn to work together immediately and there's not a lot of space to agree on team norms and expectations.
I also wish there was more information about the pitch structure and requirements earlier in the course

I would recommend this course. It's giving me great expertise that I can talk about in interviews. However, I wish I was not in the inaugural class. It seems like there are lots of details that need ironing out. For example, expectations around mentors (from the student side and the mentor side) were not clear leading to our team under-utilizing our mentor. Additionally, I wish we'd spent greater time in office hours, both in length of session and in frequency of sessions. I did not feel like I could go into as much depth around deals as I would have liked to during office hours. Yes, overall the class is helpful to get a feel for what it's like to be a venture capitalist. It is a lot of work and they are still figuring out the course format, but the professors are great people and are willing to help and the class had a lot of good learnings as a whole.

Yes, I would. I know it is a new class and there is progress to be made, but the overall purpose of the class is great. Very cool class concept but needs structural changes to be a worthwhile / effective course. Adair, Todd, and Jeep are really amazing in their fields but didn't feel effective coming together in this structure. There is a lot more learning and impact that could have been realized if there were structural changes and more formal class time. I hope this class continues and iterates and improves - it's really important but would not recommend if there are not changes. I would recommend this class to some students who have a strong interest in originating deals, and investing in potential projects and companies. I wouldn't say this class is made for everyone. Having some sort of a background in finance would also be helpful to any prospective students. All that to say, I would recommend this class to only ~50% of students I interact with. I believe this class needs a little more structure.

In general, I think this class is excellent and must take for anyone in climate. I would recommend that the teaching team is more direct on deliverables and has a bit more guidance along the way. It felt at times that the weekly office hours didn't have any subject - I would recommend to be prepared for each session and with your mentors for maximum impact. Given that this is a 3 unit course, we could benefit from some virtual learning sessions if not all in person. I just felt like class time was too limited and I really would have loved to interface and learn from Adair and the teaching team more. At times this class felt a bit too open ended, and some structured sessions through the semester (on pitch decks, term sheets, DD, etc) would help. However, this class is EXTREMELY practical and I highly recommend it.

Yes. I learned a lot by doing, enjoying talking to so many different companies. BUT it was a lot of work and as someone with no climate or no finance and no consulting background I often didn't feel like I had the skills or tools to contribute to a team. Make sure you have taken other courses to help prepare for the course.

The objectives of this course, though incredibly interesting and useful in application, are hard to accomplish in practice. It is a difficult investment model to pull off. I think it still remains to be seen how successful the course will be in sourcing the type of deals we were taught comprise "growth stage climate finance" but if we are able to invest in them will be really worthwhile. No matter what I learned a lot about investment as a whole, but might need additional teaching support to ensure that the actual DD of the companies is authentic & quality. The other issue is that most of the mentors that were sourced didn't have the bandwidth to help in the way it was likely envisioned, which led to other lack of quality/expertise in the DD process.
Yes only if the following changes are implemented:
- clear deliverables and timelines
- actual ways to learn how to do due diligence
- upfront communication

Its a really cool class and an amazing opportunity. I recommend it for students who are good at self-teaching in a chaotic environment. If you prefer a more traditional learning environment, this class is not for you.

sections.notFor: Anyone wanting structure or an easy class - 'don't expect structure or a clear pathway.' Teams cannot carry passive members, and one student warns the fast pace is hard with a learning disability.

sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the work product is deal sourcing, diligence and a pitch culminating in a real investment.

I took this course to learn more about Climate solution and do something totally different from Finance and I find the class to be interesting.
Yes would recommend - great course well delivered and good guest speakers.

A great place to learn more about growth stage climate investing and go through a proxy of sourcing and working through a deal thesis. (To that end, if you want an easy class where you don't have to try too much, please take a non- group class as this one is really hard for 1-2 people to carry and many of the folks taking this class care to try it on for a career and take it seriously)
Yes I would, it is a great way to get an idea of the job of a VC in a very impactful way.

Yes! Great way to get a taste of a true berkeley experience/plug into SF VC community/try something new.

I think it's helped me practice and consciously think about how to better connect with others and build empathy

This class was hands down the most meaningful and transformational class of my entire MBA experience. I almost didn't take it because I had heard mixed reviews, especially regarding the virtual format of the class (even after other classes were back in person), but I can't imagine my time at Haas having been nearly as fulfilling and rewarding without this class. The course itself is beautifully designed, with a slow ramp-up with pre-readings and reflections, and then the sessions themselves do a wonderful job of tying together all of these concepts and putting them to practice. I will admit that the course would not have been as rewarding if the other students in my T-group hadn't been so committed to the experience, so it's important to only take this class if you will be willing and able to fully lean into it. I already feel like a much more confident person and that my ability to communicate and make connections with others has improved considerably. I can't wait to start applying these lessons in the real world, in both my personal and professional relationships.

I would recommend this course if it is taught in person (not virtually). Erica's experience in interpersonal skills is second to none. She is an incredible listener, wonderfully organized, and truly passionate about the course's subject matter. She also isn't afraid to switch things up on the fly, which improves the classroom learning experience. The class dives deep into interpersonal relationships, which aren't covered in most classes at Haas. The applied nature of the course means that we get to practice Erica's techniques with other students in a psychologically safe environment. The learning is very applicable to personal and professional relationships. However, the virtual environment is not conducive to this type of class. This class relies on human connection, which is significantly more present in real life than on a computer screen. Zoom creates additional fatigue and also enables more distraction.

Yes, this class is WAY different than any other class you'll likely take at Haas and I genuinely feel the practices and awareness I've built throughout will be carried with me for the rest of my life. The impact is both personal and professional and usability is immediate.
Absolutely. This course has been very valuable. It stretches you in essential areas and these aren't stretched in other MBA classes.
Yes highly recommend, but I would be sure to set the expectation that it will probably be challenging in a way that's very different from what they are used to.

I would recommend this course to students that are seeking to (re)connect with their inner-self and their presence. This course uses unconventional learning methods that may require a major stretch to some students.

Yes. At a structural level, this was one of the best run courses I have seen where all 4 of the instructors were in synch with one another. It was clear that they had either worked closely with one another before and/or they rehearsed before class.

At a content level, I would dare say this was unequivocally better than the similar core class of Leadership Communications -an-easy-to-understand progression of the curriculum, more practice for students within a similar amount of time, and most importantly, an emphasis on listening and internalization (a critical skill that I am struggling to think is present in other MBA courses).
As for Erica and her co-instructors, it is clear they are deeply invested in teaching the material and in the development of the students.
In brief, I came in as a sceptic, and came out a believer.
I am not very sure. I think the class content is good but there are some moments I feel awkward. For example, the discussion about rank and DEI...

I really enjoyed this course. The student-driven nature of it is very different from many Haas classes but it was a really unique opportunity to learn how technologically innovative companies successfully deployed (or failed to deploy) their technologies. The cases are timely, and the concepts build across classes.

Yes, if you are interested in technology case studies. The class looks at companies including Airbnb, Tesla, and Google, among many others. The project is very dependent on your team, your technology/product, and your client, so do your due diligence in the first couple of weeks of class on the people and technology.
As a person new to the energy industry, I so appreciated how open the material was to individuals seeking additional context.
My favorite speaker series! I would happily recommend it!

I thought there could be more case discussions to facilitate learning but panel speakers were interesting (could be more diverse).
Yes! Great learnings, effective use of time.
Yes -- this professor is well prepared and easy to learn from.

Professor Heinrich did an excellent job of distilling down the core of what nonprofit boards are responsible for doing and hammering home the points with a huge wealth of knowledge from her own experience as a board member and as a consultant for nonprofit boards. She also brought two amazing groups of nonprofit board members and executive directors in to serve on panels so we could ask our questions and learn more about putting theory into practice. I think everyone who might want to have anything to do with any nonprofit at any point should take this class whether that be as a board member, member of staff, or person who wants to donate to nonprofits.

I would definitely recommend this course! It had the right amount of work for a 1 unit course and resulted in substantial learning. I particularly appreciated the professors knowledge of the topic and that she sets up panels with experts in the non-profit field.
If you are interested in learning the basics of sitting on an established nonprofit orgs board then yes. If you're looking to start or run a nonprofit board then this class is not as helpful.

Highly recommended; Professor Heinrich has one of the best networks of nonprofit board and executives I've seen. I would recommend this course to anyone interested in nonprofit boards or currently serving on one. It provided a great overview of the space and covered some key topics.

Yes!
