sections.workloadNote: Compressed into two very long days with readings; described as not too heavy a workload. One student breaks the sessions down as roughly 80% discussion, 20% lecture.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - readings and discussion are described, but no student mentions exams, papers or grading.
sections.redFlags: One detailed comment flags major time-management problems and letting students ramble across two very long days. One says the material could be learned self-paced; a couple appear to take it mainly for credit.
sections.quote: She did let a lot of people ramble which was a bit frustrating and had major issues with time management / watching the clock
comments: NA

Yes, it's a good high-level introduction to the nonprofit board operations and effectiveness. As an incoming Berkeley Board Fellow who has never been on a nonprofit board, I really appreciated the perspective I gained from this course. Yes. The class is good. Not too heavy workload.
Yes! If you are interested in learning more about nonprofit boards generally and the responsibilities of board members.
yes get your credit
I would recommend it! It was a great primer into nonprofit boards!
Yes, it is important to be exposed to the social sector
Maybe. I think the course is interesting, but how much you get out of it depends on your previous experience. Yes, really helpful course to learn about boards!
yes, i would highly recommend the course for folks who are interested in the sector. it's fascinating and Lynne's an excellent instructor.
YES
not only for these in non-profit business or board or any related
Yes I would recommend if you are interested in learning more about non profit boards
Highly recommend for anyone interested in being at a nonprofit or on a nonprofit board!
Yes recommended! I love how the sessions provide practical insights to the world of nonprofits

The professor was super well prepared and had very detailed slides, plus discussed not just our readings but real life relevant news stories at the start of both sessions as well. The class was 80% discussion and 20% lecture, which was super super helpful for both active learning and staying engaged during two very long days. She did let a lot of people ramble which was a bit frustrating and had major issues with time management / watching the clock, but the class was still very valuable if you're interested at all in the nonprofit space, not even necessarily just with being on a board. Yes - This was an amazing course that I would highly recommend to anyone interested in board governance or supporting an organization they're passionate about. I think this course reminded me that passion can fuel productive conversation and participation and encouraged me to spend more of my time in organizations that align with my personal values!
Yes
Yes, because it is straightforward and you learn a lot in a short period of time. It is valuable to anyone seeking an introduction to board governance and wants to serve on a nonprofit board someday
I would not, I feel most of the material could be learned self paced
Yes
You should take this course if you're interested in non-profit boards now or in the future.
Anyone wanting to serve on non profit boards will get immense value from this course.

rows.title: Mergers and Acquisitions: A Focus on Creating Value

comments: I would and would not. I thought the subject matter and assignments were great material to cover. However, the lack of guidance on formatting, structure of assignments, and grading rubrik for participation (50% of grade) would give me pause from recommending this course as too ambiguous, even if ambiguity is intentional.

I recommend it to anyone considering a transactional role. You get a good taste of the different parts of the deal process and you can dive in on the cases as deeply as you wish. This class relies on tried-and-true formulas with quick turnarounds on assignments, so if you are looking for open-ended cases or a light workload, you should probably look elsewhere.

The class is unique at Haas and if you are interested in a finance-related career a must. Be prepared that this class requires major time commitments and has tight deadlines for time-intensive cases. The tone of the class is a bit rougher compared to others, especially when you come unprepared to class. Professor G. shares amazing experiences from life, brings in great guest speakers, and keeps his class up to date. The class definitely is type 2 fun - I am glad to have taken it.
No. The only exception is if you KNOW you're going to work in M&A and have A LOT of time on your hands, but even then I recommend looking elsewhere.

The bad: The professor is snarky, everything in this class is pre-scripted preventing real dialogue / debate, the workload is so far over the top, and the class has no respect for your time (I had to show up to a webinar on Easter Sunday, and another during winter break). They tell you it's the hardest class at Haas but they don't tell you there's literally 1.5x the class time of a 2-credit course, plus hours and hours of outside work. Grading criteria is non-existent. Also, the obsession with grades and arcane grading scheme in this class is way too much, and they constantly threaten you with the sacred participation points. Everything is just taken so seriously but it creates so much busywork outside of what you're doing in class. It feels distasteful given how much else MBA students have going on.

The good: Goodson is a good guy and cares about students deep down. Some of the complaints I mention come out of what are in my opinion misguided attempts to make the class better, so I don't fault them for trying. I did learn a lot too, and Goodson's stories can be pretty interesting. Solid guest speakers though some are not as good as others. I wish I could recommend this class since I did learn some cool things, but it's just not worth it, trust me. The ROI for amount learned vs. time spent is just not as high as it is for many other classes. Wish I took FIA or Corp Finance instead.

Highly recommended class and instructor. Not as much work as the rumors might have it, and the instruction team goes out of their way to make sure they are available to help you learn. Assignments are engaging and useful. I would recommend this course if you are serious about a career in finance, but I would avoid if you don't want to pursue that as a career. This isn't your typical comfortable and chill Haas class, which is refreshing. This course is intense, fast-paced, and upfront (i.e., you will get cold called no matter what so you better prepare). If you can afford to take this Pass/Fail grading, I would encourage you to do so to ease some pressure while also learn a lot. I would recommend the course and would caution recommending the teacher. There were many occasions when
students were referred to as "dumb" or lacking intellect. Specifically for the last project, there were about 5 additional webinars that were hosted over the weekends and not on the syllabus.

Yes - its been the hardest but more rewarding class. I was challenged both in academically but also in my comfort level in discussing topics/subject matter. You can probably coast by, but don't. Its a short class and worth it if you but the time into it. The final project is a beast, and they try to simulate a real deal with information thrown at you at the last minute (aka Sunday @ 3pm when you have something due at 6pm). They should just block off this weekend in the syllabus. For non- finance backgrounds, you will have to accept that you may get some things wrong but even if they Professor acknowledge it, if you can see as a learning experience you'll get alot out of it. Teaching style is definitely not for everyone but I really enjoyed it. The only class I consistently did the readings for a came to class prepared for each week. Three hours flys by, even online

Yes because it is very interesting and the structure forces you to actively play a part in your learning experience. This is not a class where you have little incentive to pay attention and end up learning nothing.
Definitely recommend to students who are interested in M&A
Yes, but not on a remote setting (or with many distractions going around)

Absolutely not. Mr. Goodson is a great guy. Intelligent and clearly on top of his field but this class will be all stick and no carrot. You are bombarded by assignments, projects, and cases which have no guidance, explanation, or course correction. You will have to do an agonizing group project every week that will require 2-3 days of meeting for hours on end only to be graded exceptionally harshly. During the 3-hour 8am to 11am class, you will be aggressively cold called about a completely separate 5-15 page case you had to read individually every single week (on top of the group projects) and if you don't get this off-the-top-of the head cold call question 100% right, you will be made to look like an a**hole in front of your peers. In addition to the course load, which will be more than all other classes put together, you will also have to closely monitor additional social media nonsense that was formulated for this class on a regular basis. This also does not count as an Applied Innovation course. It is supposed to be to learn something but you will have far too much work to learn anything new about M&A and will have to do the part of the project which you did for your prior job in the past (ie; economics, PowerPoint, analytics, etc.). For a class which is 1-DAY-A-WEEK expect to have to constantly monitor your emails and work 4-5 days a week; one thankless project after another.
This has been the most challenging but at the same time most rewarding class at Haas. The knowledge gain
throughout these weeks has been nothing short of mind-blowing. Highly recommend it to anyone wanting to pursue a finance career.
it's a wonderful class where i have learned a lot. however, it is a lot of work and there are lots of times when i felt overwhelmed by the sheer volume of work required

Yes, absolutely, if you are willing to log in the hours. If you plan to work in PE, IB or related fields, or want a lesson in boardroom leadership, don't leave Haas without taking at least one of Prof. Gs courses. Here's why:

- Extremely engaging learning experience: the classes are 3 hours, but they feel like 1h - they go by so fast because they are fun, with world-class speakers and techniques to keep everyone on the edge of their seats, like warm- and cold-calling, extensive case readings

- Great training to be an executive: You are expected to behave like a Director of the Board from day one, and you'll get feedback if you don't act like one. At the end of the semester you can expect to be experienced in understanding what makes a merger succeed or fail, making to-the-point, sharp comments and in asking the right questions to a senior audience. It's a lesson in leadership as much as it is in M&A. It's also refreshing given that Haas sometimes will not always treat us like adults

- Exposure to real-world experience: Prof. G is himself an extremely accomplished PE executive. Being able to learn from his experience is invaluable. Don't miss opportunities to ask him about his war stories.

Absolutely -- if you have the opportunity to take a course with Peter Goodson, you will get your money's worth and then some. He expects a lot, so don't expect to coast by, but if you put in the time, read the cases, and come prepared, you will leave with valuable skills and knowledge. If you already had a background in M&A this course might be somewhat repetitive, but between the breadth and depth of topics covered over 10 weeks, you will almost certainly get something new out of this class.
No. Terrible course. Loads of work but also the least I've ever learned from a class. Teaching staff are horrible people and should be ashamed of how they conducted this class

[REDACTED IN THE PUBLIC BUILD] A student strongly advised against the instructor's classes, describing rambling Wall Street stories, aggressive graded cold calling, and assignments they found hard in the wrong ways: little context from class and unclear grading policies. — Why: The original makes personal character claims about a named instructor; the teaching criticism is preserved, the personal characterization is not republished.

Only if you want to a job working in M&A. With this class you could create a good network: the speakers and maybe the professor. But, the content is very high level and specific. This means that if you don't have an investment background it will be very difficult to follow class and even if you have some background it wouldn't dig much into details. The workload is very high and the teaching team will make you work as you were working for an Investment Bank.

YES. This was the most time-intensive class in my 2 years at Haas but afforded the most learning. Prof G has a ton of experience and translates it into lessons learned for the students. This rounded out my business school experience. Thank you!

Definitely, personally this course made Haas worthwhile in my first year. I learned substantially and really got to work closely with my peers in group projects that were simulations of the real world. I feel much more prepared to tackle investment banking as opposed to other core and elective classes that have been disappointing so far.
No.

I honestly can't think of anything I learned in this class. Other financial classes are much more worth it. Lectures are not good, professor is very methodical, but does not have a structured thinking. Class has no space for insightful student participation. There are a lot of cold and warm calls, but not for interesting comments. Example of question he opens for class participation: "What items would you prioritize in a due diligence?" Student A says "Financials", Student B says "Leadership", Student C says "Competition" and that's it, participation time is over - no discussion or comment about the answers. We heard absolutely zero student comments about previous professional experience, because professor does not allow time for it. Any attempt of comment was blocked by professor. Assignments are repetitive and don't add much to the learning objective. You're gonna do pretty much the same thing 10-12 times. Readings aren't good either.

I feel professor tries to hide his lack of teaching skills by adding a heavy workload, so students who do not do put enough effort think their learning was compromised by their own choices. That was not my case: I did the readings every week, read all cases, worked on all group assignments and I still feel I didn't learn anything. This was a huge waste of my time. Don't waste your time.

My take is that the professor goal is not to teach anything, he just wants to show off and say all investors are stupid and he is brilliant - but unwilling to share knowledge he got from his years of working. He refuses to answer students questions when he finds it to basic - and makes joke about the doubts.
If you want to learn about the PE market and mindset, there are certainly better classes to do so.

Absolutely take this course. Unless you're allergic to working. This was one of the most interesting and fulfilling courses at Haas. You'll work, but you'll walk away with an incredible amount of learnings. And not just as it pertains to M&A - you'll walk away with skills on creating slide decks, presenting in board meetings, and how to navigate multiple stakeholders in deals. I wish I could re-enroll to take another Goodson class but unfortunately I have to graduate. I would recommend this to any student that is highly driven and wants to challenge themselves. To those who want to learn about how to create value and truly think strategically and is ready to be uncomfortable.
I'd recommend - it is an engaging class and a great way to learn about M&A. Be prepared for a heavy workload, and one that sometimes requires specific blocks of time outside of class/on weekends.

I would, but only to people who are willing to really learn a lot about M&A, value creation, PEs, and also to people who can and are willing to put the most effort into this course than any other in that semester.

I highly recommend! Professor Goodson's knowledge and extensive industry experience make the course a highly practical experience. It's so clear that he deeply cares about his students and wants them to learn as much as possible. As a result, the students are really pushed to think differently, which results in significant growth in terms of presentation and analytical skills. Professor Goodson is also a natural at providing coaching; in each presentation, he provides "teachable moments" that truly improve presentation skills and 30,000-foot-view insights. He is a tremendous asset to Haas and business school students.

I would recommend the course to a fellow student if one wants to learn about M&A. The reading and cases are interesting and can give one a good idea what is typically involved/expected in an M&A process (valuation, legal, negotiation, etc). The workload is relatively high, but still manageable. It provides opportunities to practice valuation, but not a focus of the course. Most of the learning comes from pre-class preparation. The class itself is more like running a show and sometimes focus is given more to format. Hope there can be more deep content discussion during class time.

I would recommend this instructor and course to students who want to prioritize this class and their time towards it. I would not have been able to manage this workload during my first year when I had other responsibilities. This class is harder in terms of rigor than the core is, but it is not harder in terms of learning content, rather it's through quick turnarounds of reading and understanding cases to then apply learnings in class. It should definitely not be a 2 credit course, but I am grateful that I took this during my MBA and would not do it differently. Class prep and cold calls are rigorous, but if you put the time in you can get a lot out of it. I feel more prepared for board presentations from this class than in any other I've taken.

Yes, the class is extensive and really should be a 3 credit course. But you do get a lot out of it and various details about M&A are no longer confusing to me. Professor Goodsons usage of warm calls, cold calls, guests, zoom backgrounds, and cases make this class more interactive than many of my in-person classes.
Yes - this should be a core class in business school as it walks you through how to evaluate companies and what you need to consider when acquiring a company.
YES! So much real-world experience, I actually enjoyed working under the pressure on big assignments with tight turn arounds - this is how it will be in corporate America.
Absolutely! This is one of the best course at Haas. Be prepared to work really hard though. I would recommend taking some financial modeling class before too.

I would highly recommend this course to anyone who is interested in learning about this sector. Goodson is a fantastic instructor and he truly cares about his students. There are high standards for this class, so it isn't 'easy', but it's worth it. Yes. great learning experience and similar to a real world M&A working experience

Yes and No, it depends. For those interested in pursuing careers in corporate development and investment banking, this class is pretty essential. The material felt relevant enough. However, the way the course was taught was disappointing. Peter belittled students and created a biased and savage learning environment.

I would 100% recommend this course and instructor to other students so long as they are prepared to put in the work for the class. The experience was outstanding, the feedback from the professor was incredibly valuable, and the overall learning in the course was very high. That being said, students who are unprepared to put in the work may have a very negative experience as the value of this course is truly dependent on what students are willing to put in.

I am torn, I think the first 9 cases are great and result in substantial learning. However, they are all building up to the last case (TCRM) which lasts multiple weeks and requires many meetings with the teaching team outside of normal class hours. The case instructions are not clear and neither are the deliverables, I think the case plan needs to be re worked because it is not effective. The frustrating part is that when these issues were brought up to prof. G we were told that the deliverables are crystal clear, which we felt they were not. I just think there is a large disconnect between the teaching team and the students with respect to the end of the class.

The learning is great but your work team is crucial. the TCRM case at the end of the course will consume your life (lots of requirements in the last 2-3 weeks of the course so make sure you have some extra time in your calendar for ad hoc requests/group project requirements. In comparison to the PE class in the fall, the workload is slightly more in this class than the PE class. You have a lot of reading due to cold calls, so be sure to read the cases each week. Great course. High workload to read the cases, and do the work, but well worth it due to learning real world skills. I would recommend this course to anyone that wants to be pushed. You get out of this course exactly what you put in, but if you commit fully to the course it will result in substantial learning, especially in how to present financial topics to "real" audiences.

There was significant insight into the PE/M&A process in this course. That being said, the auction process in the last ~5 weeks of the course, while a good opportunity for learning, is also incredibly time consuming and can be frustrating if you do not have the schedule flexibility required to accommodate frequent short-notice, odd hours Zoom sessions. Overall class delivery via Zoom is well managed.
Highly recommend this course if you want to learn and be challenged. This course is not for the light of heart but its one of the best courses I've taken at Haas.
Yes: Difficult class, but you will learn a lot.

If you are looking for an MBA course that will challenge you and help you grow, I highly recommend Professor Goodson's M&A course. While it does require a significant amount of effort, the rewards are well worth it. By dedicating yourself to the course material and engaging in real-life case studies, you will gain a deep understanding of the M&A process and the key players involved. The group work is challenging, but it is also incredibly rewarding, allowing you to develop important skills such as collaboration and communication.

This is the best course I have ever taken at Haas, and it should be the standard for all MBA courses. Professor Goodson's expertise in the field is unparalleled. If you are looking for a course that will push you to your limits and help you reach your full potential, then this is the course for you. I highly recommend it!

I would recommend this class to any student with an interest in M&A, PE, or improving business operations. The class is more work than average and Prof G. is a demanding professor. The entire class is on Zoom and Prof G. will cold call you throughout the lecture. However, the learning is unparalleled and don't worry about your grade, while the lectures are intense the grading is easy.

This is an excellent class, but it is quite intensive and requires individuals who are accustomed to working under time and mental pressure. Those who thrive in fast-paced and challenging environments will find this course highly rewarding.

Yes, I would recommend this class but it will also make it clear that it requires a lot of work and 150% participation. This course resulted in a wealth of learning from start to finish. It is a ton of work for a 2 credit course so I recommend that students pair this course with 1-2 qualitative courses or speaker series that do not have the same workload. Pairing this course with managerial accounting or corporate finance will result in a very busy semester unless other courses have a much lighter workload

I would highly recommend Professor Goodson and the M&A course. This is by far one of the best courses at Haas for anyone even remotely interested in learning more about M&A. For students aspiring to enter Investment Banking or Corporate Development, this class is the best preparation you can get. Despite being taught in a remote setting, Professor Goodson does an incredible job at making M&A a highly engaging / interactive course. The cases and simulations are very interesting / relevant, and result in substantial learning. I also really appreciated the high degree of investment that Professor Goodson puts into seeing his students grow and succeed - he will make himself available to not only help with course content, but also to help guide / assist you with realizing your professional goals. Professor Goodson also emphasizes coaching throughout the course, and gives highly valuable (but honest) feedback to help you develop both hard and soft skills. Overall, the class is one of the most demanding at Haas, but if you are willing to put in the work, this will be one of the most valuable classes you take in business school.
Yes. The course is very useful for almost everyone, as many businesses have or will involve in M&A activities. Although the workload is heavier than average, the outcomes are worth it.

Highly recommend this to anyone who is keen to learn more about the qualitative aspects of M&A (how to structure, negotiate, integrate) and is fine with dedicating at least 7 hours per week on projects. Lots of work! Lots! Learning is immense, but only if you put in the time. The practical takeaways from this class will be a game changer for those stepping into the world of transaction activity.
Yes would definitely recommend this class. Very happy I took it and honestly would take it again if I could. Yes 100% if you want to do a course that involves deep learning and life-like simulations.
Yes, with the caveat that you must be interested in banking and finance

Brilliant professor. Coming to business school, I expected this level of learning, professionalism and pressure. Professor G is the best professor you'll ever come accross and I cannot recommend any of his classes more highly. You'll walk away with a clear understanding of real life application on the subject, more confident in your ability to pursue careers in this field and plenty of opportunities to practice your skills. You'll do yourself a disservice if you don't take at least one course from Prof G.

I recommend this class and not just if you want to pursue a career in finance. It is a great class to think about M&A and strategy that can be applied in every business. A great class to apply presentation and pitching skills. Even though it was an online class, I was more focused than in most other classes I have taken.

Wealth of knowledge, sharp witted and straight to the point. He is a breath of fresh air in Haas! Take the class. Very worth it. The professor is putting in a lot of work and also is a stellar practitioner of what he teaches. What more can you ask?

Yes! I have already started promoting this course through word of mouth to the 2025 FTMBA class. M&A is very relevant in all industries, especially in today's tech & entertainment + media. Personally, that's why I took this course. Yes. Apart from the M&A knowledge gained, you'll learn other soft skills. Peter never holds back his feedback which are all useful and helpful for one's professional journey.

I would definitely recommend this course. Despite the heavy workload, it offers substantial learning opportunities! The case studies are very hands-on and feel authentic. Peter challenged us not only to develop valuation models but also to create a credible narrative behind every assumption. I truly appreciate this approach.
Yes, extremely helpful for students going into the VC field.

100% Recommend Peter G to any and all students. Peter G IS the course so I can't imagine what it would be without him. For those hesitant to take a class that is 100% virtual, I can attest that I am more dialed into this class than any of my in-person classes. Peter is relentless and a monster on zoom. He will engage you, challenge you, and catch you if you're slacking. This course is not for the faint of heart.
Yes if you have a very light term (no other demanding classes). If you have a couple demanding classes together with this one, you are going to be overwhelmed.
This class requires a significant amount of work and with a group, so plan your schedule accordingly if you want to take this class.

Yes! The class is a lot of work, but Prof. Goodson is really entertaining and knowledgeable. I appreciated the wide range of interactive and hands-on opportunities to learn and engage with the material.
While the teaching is great and you will have ample opportunity to engage in the classroom, be prepared for a heavy courseload!

I would definitely recommend this class if it is run by Peter, because he understands what actually happens, not just theories. I think for classes like M&A we need professors who lived and breathed the subject that he teaches! I highly recommend this course. The course teaches you everything you need to know about M&A. It is great for those who are interested in pursuing careers in Finance but also for those who will not but want to know more about the topic.
Although the class in online, Peter and GSI does a great work to keep you engage through, surveys, cold and warm calls, interesting topics guest etc...
The professor is very engaged and loves to teach. He is rigorous and expects high from students, as professor should be with graduate students.
The topics are clear defined and cases are interesting and match the content taught.
This is a class where you come to learn, not just spend time and get credits.

Coursework is really intense - you will have a hard time if you don't have any finance/modeling/M&A experience. The portion of PERFORMATIVE tasks is way too high. Probably only 10% of those heavy work really lead to meaningful learning to me. Other Haas classes usually offer me a much higher work-to-leaning ratio.

Most of the class time, students are generating immature performative answers to satisfy some performative course designs. I wish the speaker portion or case debrief is given more time to substantiate the takeaways.

The online design seemed chill but it took away a lot of the relationship-building value of an elective class. Professor is stubborn and needs pampering. You should be prepared to be thick-skinned and pleasing a senior guy. I already recommended the class to more than 5 people including incoming class and exchange students
Yes - one of the better courses at Haas. Actually learned useful skills for the business world.
Recommended if you are looking to pursue PE or M&A and are willing to sacrifice for it - however the "lots of work" that is asked of you will include random 30 minute calls on sunday afternoon
Yes

I highly recommend this course if you are interested in M&A. I personally did not know much when I decided to take this course. 10 weeks later I don't think I am equipped to go sign an M&A deal but I can say I know more on it with depth now. 2 unit course but it feels like 4-5 units. Do not take it if you are not ready to spend a considerable amount of time and effort. Steep learning curve but worth it if you really want to learn.
Great class, very intense but worthwhile if you are interesting in investing, banking, or working at a company that will one day get acquired (so basically anywhere!)
Yes! Peter G is a great professor, you should definitely take this class!
Yes
I would recommend this course to anyone interested in M&A generally as it is good exposure to the factors to consider, challenges, and approaches to an M&A deal.

Yes, I would recommend this class only if you are willing to put in the time and effort. The course was excellently structured, including engaging and pertinent case studies. It was definitely interesting to have a SME's join to discuss similar viewpoints. Peter is exceptionally knowledgeable, and listening to his insights is intriguing. Although he is tough, the class discussions he leads are significant and thought-provoking. He encourages students to think critically, reflect, and actively participate.
Yes! Definitely one of the most time-consuming and challenging courses but super engaging and Peter is a legend!

sections.goodFor: Students already committed to M&A/IB/PE careers who want to feel the real process, or who want Peter Goodson as a personal connection. Best if teammates know IB mechanics.
sections.notFor: Anyone merely curious about M&A, or expecting to build finance/modeling skills - models are built but never debriefed. Ex-consultants with DD experience learn less. Effort far exceeds 2 units.
sections.workloadNote: One student reports 10-15 hrs/wk for a 2-unit online course. Three pitch exercises plus a final case simulation spiking in March/April; ad-hoc Fri/Sun evening meetings, 12-hour turnarounds.
sections.gradingBasis: weekly writeups/decks that reportedly count for almost nothing; team pitch exercises and a final case simulation
sections.redFlags: Weekend and 12-hr-turnaround demands aren't in the syllabus (3+); no feedback or grades on weekly work (2); models never explained (2); dated cases/videos (1); 1 says Goodson mutes students mid-question.
sections.quote: The majority of the homework comes down to preparing weekly writeups or decks - which can take significant time - but count for almost none of the grade.
comments: Definitely, but be prepared for the work!

If you are interested in M&A and willing to take on a very heavy workload, I highly recommend this course. The workload is substantial, and I spent about 10 to 15 hours per week outside of class. As someone with no prior M&A experience, I feel that the lectures and three pitch exercises prepared me well for the world of M&A.

This course is ideal if you have a foundational knowledge of PE, M&A, or Finance and are looking to deepen it in a highly practical, real-world setting. The pace is fast, but the quality, uniqueness, and applicability of the content is unlike anything else in the program. It has been the highest-value course in my experience so far.

That said, come prepared to work. The workload is intense and keeping up with instruction sessions is essential. The final case simulation demands significant dedication, particularly toward March and April. Given the heavy team component, it helps to have at least a few teammates with a solid grasp of IB concepts and processes.
Yes very good class. Will toughen you up.
Yes, for those interested in M&A this is surely the best course at Haas with the most hands on activities. Take it. Hectic work schedule, but the growth and learning are unmatched.
Yes- I think it offers a great contrast to other modelling / theoretical classes.

I would recommend with a grain of salt. It's a lot of work, and towards the end quite a few meetings with the instruction team on weekends. If you are interested in this class, definitely try out the first class and decide before the add/drop deadline. Don't commit to this class without knowing what you are getting into.
Yes,I would recommend. Course is really relevant for most career paths. I think it is one of the most relevant courses I took in the MBA

If you want a course that gives you a real idea of how world works, this is the one. Prof G gives another meaning to doing cases, using his own vast experience and pushing you to get involved and improve in every session. It's a tough course, with a heavier load than others, but if you're interested on the matter and want to be challenged, this is a good opportunity.

I strongly recommend the class with huge BUTS. I would encourage people to go during add/drop period and see how they feel about Peter's instruction style. You should really be interested in the topic cause it is a lot of work, so no just for people who are curious about the topic.

rows.title: The Neuroscience of Communication and Embodied Leadership
rows.disagree: Modest rating, but comments are uniformly enthusiastic

comments: This is a class you need to be ready for. Mentally and physically exhausting but good insight. Translation into being a good leader will take a lot of time. not an immediate win

Yes, I would highly recommend this course to everyone. It offers a powerful journey in learning how to manage emotions, communicate effectively, and integrate these skills into leadership. One of the most significant takeaways was building self-worth, which I hadn't realized so many of us struggle with — feeling " not enough. " This course gives you the tools to feel confident in who you are, fostering a supportive and thriving community. The class exercises, like receiving and returning bids, opened my eyes to how easily trust can be built or broken, making it a transformative experience.
100% recommed, major growth engine for leaders. Why - This course show us how to flex our whole living muscles to be a leader to ourselves so we can be to our community and surroundings.

I would recommend this course and instructor if you want to dig further into learning interpersonal skills and how it will apply to leadership and your own life. Even for those who "know" how to empathize and work with others, the whole class is worth taking.

No. It's like a group therapy session for some people, but they should go to actual therapy, not a class that teaches you how to breathe, dance, and watch clips of BTS. There wasn't any interpersonal skill training whatsoever. I understand that the instructor wants to follow a structure but the constant interruption, especially when people are bonding and building connections, is very distracting.

Yes, I'd recommend. The instructor brings a high level of expertise and creates a learning environment that is both engaging and thought-provoking. The course covers critical, real-world issues that many other courses tend to overlook, offering unique insights and fostering deep reflection. The structure encourages a strong leadership perspective, which I found particularly valuable and different from other courses at UC Berkeley. The resources provided — whether readings, videos, or articles — are of excellent quality, and the opportunity to explore challenging topics makes it a truly enriching experience.
I would highly recommend this course to people from Caucasian and Asian backgrounds so it becomes a learning experience for everyone.

Overall, I don't think this course is very worthwhile. I went in with the intention of really learning about interpersonal skills but I don't think this class helped me to accomplish any of the goals outlined in the syllabus. I took a similar class in undergrad and it felt a lot more genuine. By design, three full days packed into one weekend was extremely draining and made it hard for me to focus. The course content mostly revolved around Erica's own personal life and some activities, including an over-emphasis on BTS, that I didn't find useful. Although she came in with good intentions, the way this class is run felt quite inefficient (e.g. we spent a long time doing physical exercise/chitchatting; for a class that I expected to get deep and connect with fellow classmates, we were forced to mechanically stick to a structure that felt like we were just reading off a canned template of answers. And because of this focus on "structure", she would interrupt A LOT when anyone talked in class, which made me feel very uncomfortable and forced. Also, be warned that this class has LOTS of homework that didn't substantiate my learning at all - it was mostly reviews of her blogs, articles, dance videos etc. Think twice before you sign up just because it's virtual!
Yes! A brilliant class that makes me feel like I've transformed as a person. If you are willing to put in the work and dedicate yourself to this learning, you will reap the rewards.

Yes, because the small class size allows you to really learn. You can't find this sort of vulnerability and connection practice outside of this class because it was learning through doing. The learnings from this class can be immediately implemented in day to day life at home and at work.
If you are extemely low on self awareness, self worth and vulnerability, this class will give you a structure. If not, I don't think this class is for you.

Yes-- really interesting tools and a great opportunity to stretch as a leader
YEs definitely. The course is truly transforative.

I would not recommend this course as it is structured right now. I feel there are other courses in Haas that touch on the same ideas and concepts and are much more applicable to your real life and your work life (e.g., Conflict Lab). I learned more from the assigments and the readings Erica maked us read than from the class itself.

sections.goodFor: People who genuinely want to practice leadership - nervous system regulation, boundaries, hard feedback - and will invest real time and personal vulnerability outside class.
sections.notFor: Anyone looking for an easy 2-unit elective, or who struggles with virtual/weekend formats - one says the Zoom weekend format is ineffective and an added strain.
sections.workloadNote: Substantial pre-class assignments plus daily embodiment practices; several stress it is 'A LOT of work' for a 2-unit course. In-class time is interactive partner and small-group work on Zoom.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the graded artifacts appear to be pre-class work and participation in experiential exercises, but no one states weightings.
sections.redFlags: Heavy pre-class workload flagged by 4+ of 13 ('don't take this if you just want an easy 2-unit course'); 2 say the Zoom + weekend format is ineffective or draining; requires real emotional investment.
sections.quote: I would recommend this course if it is a subject you are keenly interested in and willing to put in the work for! Do not take this if you just want an easy 2-unit course.
comments: yes, the class was slow to start but at the last day I really started to understand why it was important. Yes. The experiential format made the learning stick in a way that lectures alone never could. I am already applying what I learned to how I communicate at work and at home.

Absolutely, without reservation. This is one of the most practically impactful courses I have taken at Haas. Unlike many leadership courses that stay at the conceptual level, this one gives you a rigorous scientific framework, grounded in neuroscience and somatic practice, and then immediately puts it to work through structured partner exercises, group T-sessions, and daily embodiment practices. By the end, you are not just thinking differently about leadership; you are physically experiencing it differently.

Erica is an exceptional instructor. She models every principle she teaches in real time. When unexpected moments of vulnerability arose in class, she met them with warmth and adaptability rather than redirecting to the agenda. That consistency between what she teaches and how she shows up created a level of psychological safety that made genuine risk-taking possible for the whole group. Her 10 years of experience mean she anticipates where students get stuck and intervenes with exactly the right nudge.

The one honest caveat: the pre-class assignments are substantial, so come prepared to invest real time outside of sessions. That said, the in-class experience is worth every hour of preparation. If you are serious about developing as a leader, not just learning about leadership, take this course.

Yes, I would strongly recommend this course and Erica to other students.. This is one of the few classes that meaningfully changes how you show up in relationships and leadership: you actually practice regulating your nervous system, setting boundaries, and giving/receiving hard feedback. Erica models what she teaches with a rare mix of clarity, vulnerability, and rigor, and creates a level of psychological safety that lets you do real inner work, not just learn concepts.

yes i would recommend. This course offers personal insight that you do not find in other courses which will help understand how and why you personally react to certain threats. This will help you regulate how you react in stressful situation, and to connect with people in a deeper more meaningful way which can help your career tremendously. Absolutely yes. I highly recommend this instructor. I loved her teaching style, which allowed me to embody the skills I desired. I didn't even realize I was missing these essential tools until this class helped me develop them. I highly recommend Erica if you would like professional guidance on self reflection and reflecting on your interactions with others. The pre-class work is a lot but the in-class work is very interactive.

This course is a must for anyone who is or wants to become a manager or leader. This course should be a mandatory elective at Haas. I would recommend this course if it is a subject you are keenly interested in and willing to put in the work for! Do not take this if you just want an easy 2-unit course. Just know what you are getting yourself into and it will be a great experience. rows.title: Human Rights and Responsible Business Strategy

comments: It is an interesting and different take than you would usually see in Haas; focused on supply chain human rights violations.
I would recommend this course! It felt like a practical version of ethics. I actually used a lot of what I learned in the course to chat with a manufacturing partner of mine!
Yes! I would like to recommend this course. It provides detailed explanation of human rights issue in various industries. The presentations of guest speakers in this course are wonderful.

This class should be a mandatory class - every business leader should understand the importance of upholding human rights commitments! This class allows you to work with a client on human rights risks they are currently facing, which provided a hands-on experience to the class. Faris and Roger are subject matter experts in human rights, and leverage their network of human rights experts to host presentations on risks they are facing in their respective industries as well. Great class!
I would definitely recommend. This class provided a really important and thoughtful framework for thinking about ethics and practice in business.
Yes HIGHLY recommend. Relatively easy course which results in a fair bit of learning that makes up for all that core ethics lacks.
Absolutely! I learned a ton about the field of human rights in business and I recommend this class to anyone who is interested in business, human rights, sustainability, or responsible innovation.

I would definitely recommend the Human Rights class! Roger and Faris are a fantastic duo and complement each other very well. At times the material got a bit heavy and the class does have an opportunity to be more interactive. That being said, the content is wonderful and both the professors and guest speakers are great. Finally, I worked in an interesting group project where the client was very invested and grateful for our work.

I believe this class should be a part of core maybe under the Ethics umbrella as I cannot imagine going back to business as a leader and not knowing about the UNDP human rights. The class imparts a framework to look at different human right violations and has personally helped me read and understand the news better. I felt comfortable to bring up any topic in class like what Elon is doing to Twitter employees and hear the professors' comments on the topic. I always left the class knowing more about what's happening in the world. The lineup of speakers is amazing, and as someone going to tech as a PM, I had huge takeaways on building responsible technology thanks to speakers from TikTok, Cisco, Amazon, etc.

The professors are very friendly and helpful and bring in lots of great guest speakers! Its an interesting class with good discussion but some of the topics can be a bit dry. The group project is also interesting to be paired with a company client but is a reasonable lift.
yes, very insightful content and lively discussions around

For anyone interested in ESG, human rights, CSR, YES! Learned a lot, super interesting topic.

These are very real situations that we could face, and I think learning the information in this class is super important for navigating these.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in real estate development or land use who want a qualitative, conceptual survey plus CA policy/law context and cross-school interdisciplinary exposure.
sections.notFor: Students taking several other development courses (overlap risk), or anyone wanting quantitative depth - coverage is uneven, deep on some topics and skimmed on others.

If you want to learn about real estate development this class is a must take.
It's an interesting course. Not requiring a lot of assignements, no final project, so you can easily loose track. Overall worth it.

I would suggest this course to fellow students if they are seeking to learn more about land development and the reality of developing. This course introduces the fundamental components of developing property, which is usually not too easy. This course ties together policies and law quite well, especially in California.

I would recommend this course as a qualitative and conceptual approach to land development. There are great speakers across various land development practices that complement lectures from Linda and Evan, who have a wealth of knowledge.

This was a very unique and interesting class for me, and I generally recommend it if students are looking for a high- level introduction to land development process and an interdisciplinary experience. Getting different perspectives on a subject matter and getting to meet/engage with students from different schools was valuable. I generally liked the course content and felt we covered a wide range of interesting topics. I found the course content to be interesting, but sometimes we went a little too deep on certain topics while others we skimmed over too quickly. However, this may just be the downside of the interdisciplinary nature of the course, which I otherwise quite enjoyed. There was a guest speaker in almost every class, who generally were quite interesting, engaging, and informative, but it was a bit much. Perhaps could have been a 2-credit class?

Yes I recommend this course, but I would caution against taking this and more than 1 other development focused class for fear of too much overlap. However, both teachers bring a practitioner's mindset to the teaching which helps blend real world perspectives with the course material.
Would recommend the class

I would HIGHLY recommend this course IF you are interested in working in real estate after school. I have taken every real estate class offered by Haas and this class in particular has the most material that was not also covered in other classes. VERY helpful

rows.title: International Business Development for MBAs, IP course

sections.goodFor: Students who want international consulting experience with a real client and travel; described as a once-in-a-lifetime, friendship-building MBA highlight.
sections.notFor: Students who need certainty or predictable load: you don't know your country, team or client when you sign up, and team leads do far more work with little recognition.
sections.workloadNote: Very heavy and back-loaded: spring class plus 80+ hour weeks for two weeks of in-country client work, and additional assignments/presentation in the following fall semester.
sections.gradingBasis: Team consulting deliverables, a blog post, a final presentation, plus a fall presentation for the last credit; guidelines unevenly enforced.
sections.redFlags: Recurring: credits do not match workload (fall assignments for spring credit), assignment instructions confusing and constantly changing, guidelines unevenly enforced, class time not relevant to all projects.
sections.quote: Project, team, and country dependent. Super MBA experience and would recommend doing it. Team leads should expect to do a lot more work with little recognition.
comments: Absolutely. Amazing opportunity to get consulting experience while traveling the world.
This is a truly transformative experience. A lot of work, a lot of hard work!! But you get to learn so much, experience so much, and explore so much! I highly recommend this course????
I would. This was a GREAT course!!

This course, as many people know, carries a lot of uncertainty. When you sign up for the course, you have no knowledge about what experience you are doing to get (country, team, client), so it is definitely a risk. But that said, I think the whole experience was worth it once you are able to go to your country, experience a new culture, and meet your client in person.

There were a few issues with this course throughout the semester that I hope are addressed: 1. The class time was not always relevant to all projects and it seemed not the best use of time for all teams. I think sharing a variety of resources that might or might not be applicable to projects would be rather, rather than providing only one framework or way to do things and assume that all teams can use this in their project. 2. Especially at the end, guidelines provided for some assignments were not followed by all teams. For example, we were told to keep the blog post at certain length, or the final presentation at 3 slides and these guidelines seemed almost "optional" and not really enforced by all teams, creating an unfair advantage for those teams who did follow the guidelines. 3. This class should be 4 credits if they still make us do assignments in the fall semester. I think it is ridiculous that we only get 2 credits in the spring for the amount of work we put in, including traveling in country and working 80+ hours for two weeks while in- country. All other applied innovation classes that have client-facing work are 3 credits. The fact that we also need to do a presentation in the fall to get the final 1 credit out of the 3 does not make sense at all, and this should be 1 credit IN ADDITION to the 3 credits we should already be earning for all our work from January to May. I hope this changes for future classes.
