expect to do a lot more work with little recognition.

It's a great course with plenty of opportunity. Well-organized but not all projects are Go To Market strategy, and that is all the course focuses on. Instructors are very helpful, but instructions for assignments are confusing and change constantly
Yes, this was my all time favorite experience at Haas. The in country travel was a once in a lifetime experience, and I made lifelong friendships with my teammates.
Yes for the travel and consulting case experience!! Bang for your buck

rows.title: Pricing
rows.disagree: Modest rating, but comments are uniformly enthusiastic

comments: Highly recommend this course- I believe this course builds on core Strategy a lot
Yes, highly recommend the course to those who have interests in pricing.
Must-take class at Haas. If you want practical knowledge of pricing and strategy, take this class. Everything you learn in the class is very applicable to your work.

Wasim's teaching style takes a few classes to get used to, but he is incredibly funny and approachable. His lectures are focused on learning and takeaways. He doesn't dwell on unnecessary details and calculations that you'll forget after the class. Great experience!
Absolutely! Great class and great professor.
Great class, I absolutely recommend it

Absolutely recommend, if you are interested in pricing or strategy. Wasim is old school but not stuck in old ways; you will be as engaged as you want to be in this very interactive, often intense, journey through the world of pricing. Yes, lots to learn from Wasim. Pricing may not be the most interesting sounding material, but there is a lot of strategic elements to the material as well. I wish I'd taken this course earlier, as a lot of the learnings would have helped me in interviews (consulting). Wasim also has lots of anecdotes about berkeley and business that are fun to hear, she brings in notable guest speakers. Additionally, the course is a relatively low lift despite being case heavy.

I would recommend this class because it does a great job of looking at pricing strategically (i.e., as the center of ops, sales, marketing, finance, the industry, and competitive environment) and includes some phenomenal guest speakers. Wasim is also a great professor. However, be aware that this is a case-heavy class (12 throughout the semester), and although the cases are helpful from a learning perspective they are almost all extremely outdated and tend to be on industrial and highly-technical industries that I feel don't really reflect the industries Haasies are most interested in. No. I would not recommend this course and I'm pretty disappointed with the course and instructor as a whole. I was excited for a course that felt practical! Especially going into a career where I know pricing will play an important role. But I don't know anything more about pricing than when I started the class.
Yes! Wonderful course VERY applicable to any area of business.
Highly highly recommend this class, especially if you are going into product management.

Great class. Be warned that the first quarter of the class is a bit slow where you go over elasticity and microeconomic concepts. However, the last 75% of the class is probably the best strategy class I've taken at Haas. The first quarter is necessary to build knowledge. The cases were truly interesting and complex, which made class discussions amazing!! Wasim was great at facilitating discussion and super funny.

This is an old-school mix of marketing and strategy-focused Pricing. I would recommend it if you are slightly strategy- leaning and you think you will be in a role at any point in the future that has to consider pricing in any manner. There's a lot of material but Wasim is a solid professor and if you pay attention, he is very witty and engaging. He probably could have managed class discussion a bit better (I admit that about 8 of us did the majority of talking) but it was a very laid-back, interesting, conversational class that you can really get out of it as much as you want and by how much work you put in. It's not an insane workload and it's pretty back-loaded throughout.

I would highly recommend this course. It was one of the most worthwhile courses that I have taken at Haas. Pricing is a fantastic capstone course--it synthesizes concepts from strategy, finance, marketing, and operations classes in teaching students about different pricing mechanisms. The course is almost entirely taught in the case method, which forces students to make decisions without perfect information, often needing to defend your position in the same fashion as the real world. Each case builds off the previous case, so students become well-versed in pricing strategy and leadership by the end of the semester. Wasim is an incredible professor with tremendous professional experiences that match the cases that are taught. He also makes himself very available outside of class, connecting students with industry professionals.
Absolutely 1000%! This is a must take class if you want to go into marketing or consulting! It really taught me how to case unlike any other class I have ever taken

Wasim is a witty professor who brings in decades of experience teaching pricing. He brings you along a broad range of cases to help you understand many aspects of pricing, both strategic and analytical. A must-take course if you are interested in the consumer behavior, psychology, and strategy side of pricing.

Pricing is an incredibly valuable skill and Wasim does a solid job of teaching it. Be aware that this is taught in the case method which means you do need to do some preparation to get the most out of the class (Maybe 1 case for every 3/4 classes).
This is a decent course. That subject material is rich but the organization and professor are below average. That being said, their isn't too much work and your grade will be fine.

Good course – a lot of quantitative theory but not necessary to do all the quantitative work in the class. A lot of qualitative strategy to merge with other ideas of product market fit and competitiveness. Wasim is a very thoughtful lecturer, and does a good job of trying to keep it lively and integrating literature while navigating the class. Yes! Great course and great professor. You'll learn a lot of concepts about pricing but the cases really make it memorable to take forward. He always follows up with what happened after an action in a case was taken so you know the aftermath of their pricing decisions. Some good speakers come and provide firsthand account of how pricing plays a crucial role in industry. Definitely take!
If Wasim tightened up his slides and frameworks a little, I would recommend this class. It's a nice build on the strategy core class.

Yes. This a class the goes beyond the math maximizing profit price and focus on business and market aspects instead. This seems more like a strategy and marketing class than an actual pricing class. If you want to learn about the specific tactics and economic theories utilized by companies to price products, this is not the class. But if you want to learn more about general strategy and apply some game theories, this is the class!

I would highly recommend this course to a fellow student. I wish I could take all courses offered by Professor Wasim. He is very knowledgeable and one of the best instructors I have taken here at Haas. I would say that this course was one of the best I've taken at Haas and has made me very interested in pursuing this as a future career. I only wish I took this class earlier than my last semester.
Interesting topics and class discussions, but not "groundbreaking". A good, fun, light course to take if that's what you're after. It had some useful insights but not enough rigor IMHO

Yes, it was one of the better electives I took at Haas. Good faculty and content. Really good guest lectures Absolutely. Pricing is essential in modern business, whether at a startup or large enterprise.

Yes, I would recommend this instructor and course? I think pricing is an interesting topic that is relevant in Finance, Marketing, Operations, Sales, basically all business units, and so can benefit anyone to have a good understanding of the many considerations one must make while pricing. It covers a wide array of types of products and revenue models and has a good balance of quantitative and qualitative pricing methods.
Yes – very informative and great revision of many core concepts from marketing, strategy etc.
Yes

This class feels like the summarization of everything I've learned during my MBA. It includes aspects of strategy, operations, micro, macro, finance, accounting, human resources, and even leadership communication. it incorporates all these perspectives into a single class, taught through the case method. The instructor is great, and made class fun and engaging.
Absolutely. Wassim is very effective instructor who introduces academically rigorous concepts into real–world practical situations

One of my favorite classes at Haas. This class goes far beyond pricing and is more of a strategy class looked at through a pricing lens. Course is mostly taught through case studies. Wasim is a great teacher and teaches cases in a very interesting and engaging way.
One of the best classes I have taken at Haas

I would recommend this course and instructor to a fellow student, because pricing is such an important topic for MBAs. I do, however, think that the course should be updated with some degree of demand curve estimation, some degree of value estimation, and more modern research on Pricing (potentially including behavioral econ, a dive into deep analytic pricing, modern models, such as three–part tariff, and their theory). The course, as it exists, does not include much, if any, on those topics, and instead feels like an extension of Core Strategy (which is helpful, but not as much as I was hoping).
Yes. This is one of the best courses I have taken here.

Wasim is, without a doubt, a pricing expert. However, the course can be repetitive and dry, as he uses many older cases. It would be much better if he could bring in newer cases, especially in technology (or guest speakers, like the one we had on pricing carbon credits). Alternatively, this course could be better if it was just a 1 or 2 credit class. I would highly recommend this course as one of my favorite classes at Haas. Wasim is such an entertaining, experienced and interesting speaker. It is a pleasure to learn Pricing Strategy from him.
Definitely recommended
Yes. Expert and kind professor.

Yes, absolutely necessary course for anyone interested in business strategy. This class is foundational to an MBA and should be required. It brings together all that we learned in the core and applies it in several interesting cases. Additionally, Wasim is a great resource I look forward to being in contact with after I graduate.
Big yes!
Highly recommend! Wasim is engaging, fun, humorous. He is also very receptive to student concerns/

preferences and adjusts his course regularly to meet student needs. Also brought in knowledgeable speakers. Learnt a lot on the topic of pricing. Course isn't too heavy in workload, with some group case writeups.

Strongly advise skipping this course. It is extremely repetitive and the teaching style is a little out of touch and needs to be refreshed. This course could easily be half a semester long, but it is stretched out to an entire semester despite not having the content to support it. Wassim is a kind Professor, but fails to give the course a throughline and direction. He often teaches 2–3 "chunks" of material, which just ends up feeling disjointed and odd. One of the lowest quality electives I have taken at Haas.

This class is trying to bridge the quantitative and qualitative aspects of pricing and doesn't do either as well as other classes. If you want deep dives on different pricing techniques, it is good. But I've learned almost 75% of the course material by taking Marketing Strategy, just not as much time dedicated to explaining the intricacies. The course work is a little light, but the cases are painfully boring. You'll be an expert at pricing heavy industrial machinery and obscure utility components at the end of the semester.

Pricing is an important topic for MBAs to know upon graduation. Sadly, this course feels like it was executed at ~50% of its potential. Wasim clearly cares about this topic, but was disorganized, brusque with students in class, and his lectures were very dry. Course workload was far too high for the low amount of value I got, but would have been totally fine if the delivery of key concepts was more polished/accessible. I would advise future students to take pricing, but heavily prioritize enrolling in a section with a different professor. If you take with Wasim, you'll get through the class, but you won't be impressed.
Good in the first few weeks. You will learn a lot of strategy and marketing but far too long!

I would not recommend this class, though it?s great in theory, the cases we had were limited across industries and the professor didn?t do a great job contextualizing the material in a relevant manner.

Pricing is one of the most important subjects an MBA student can learn about. Wasim is incredibly knowledgeable and well-connected in this field, and you can truly believe he is speaking to the experiences of pricing he and his (many) students have faced. This class does not have a particularly high work load, but it is easy to let it fall to the wayside - like many other courses, you get what you put in, so try to make as many efforts as possible to do the write ups and participate. Wasim can be hard to follow sometimes, so also come in and be ready to pay attention, because you will otherwise miss out on great material and that wealth of knowledge.
Yes, I would recommend this course. It is a great way to think about business broadly.

I would recommend you only take this course if you do not know anything about Pricing. Be ready to find a lot of overlapping content with marketing and negotiation courses if you are also taking those courses. The cases used in Pricing are old and B2B focused - which is the main factor why the class wasn't amazing for me.

I would recommend this course! The content is really useful and Wasim is incredibly knowleadgeable about it. It does require some personal organization to place what you are learning that week in the broader class context, and to not get distracted by some of the digressions.

Instructor - not at all. I have dealt with many strong personalities, but I would not take this instructor again, even for a course I was incredibly excited about. I really I enjoyed the course material, but I can't imagine myself recommending this course to another person because the professor makes the experience so painful!
Class is a bit outdated but you do learn some key principles
One of the must-take classes at Haas!

Highly recommend this class for all interested in product / marketing / sales as pricing is a crucial topic. This class covers a wide variety of topics and factors to consider in pricing and will set you up well for your professional futuer Content is very important and valuable - I'd recommend the course.
Not this instructor, but this class would be a good one otherwise.

I would recommend this course as an extremely valuable learning opportunity; that being said it the workload is intense and the class moves quickly. Brush up on your algebra before you take this class as there's a lot of manipulation of equations that is essential to understanding, but may not be shown step-by-step every time. Yes, good course, good professor, good husband
Yes, useful and interesting class
I think that topic is really important and everyone can learn something from this class. He definitely tried to cover as much as possible and provide guidelines for future use.
Yes! Wasim is very knowledgable, funny, and truly cares about his students
I would recommend this class for someone who has no idea about pricing because this class does. Told that foundation.
Yes but I found it very hard to be engaged during classes.

yes absolutely one of the only classes focused on both GTM strategy and product management at the same time No - I wish I could have learned more from this class but I think I would learn more by reading books on pricing by myself instead of taking this class
this is probably the worse class in haas for me

If the course is listed with Wasim, don't take the course. Wasim speaks too quickly and is hard to understand for native english speakers nevermind internatonals. He cuts people off, calls on men a lot, does a lot of mental math and calculus, and generally has lost the teaching abilities he had in the past, which is sad because he used to be a great professor.

sections.goodFor: Students headed into consulting, strategy, product marketing or pricing roles; several argue it should be core because it ties micro, marketing and strategy together.
sections.notFor: Students who bounce off a dry, insistent lecture style (one detailed pan says he cuts people off), or who dislike case-and-group-work formats and dated cases.
sections.workloadNote: One student states about 2 hours outside class per week; case prep plus group assignments each session. Class runs ~1.5 hrs case discussion + 30 min takeaways. Take-home final.
sections.gradingBasis: Case discussion and participation, recurring group written assignments, and a take-home final.
sections.redFlags: One long detailed pan of the teaching/communication style: dry content, poor transitions, cutting students off, syllabus hard to parse. 2-3 others note some cases are antiquated.
sections.quote: Be prepared for around 2 hours of work outside class each week.
comments: The course was a fascinating combination of pricing insight, business insight, and life insight. It was a true pleasure to attend and I felt I learnt a huge amount. Wasim was able to draw a vast wealth of stories from students, and encouraged everyone to get involved and share their opinions. A huge bonus to the class was the incredible speakers that Wasim was able to get in as well, they really made a massive positive impact!

This class is the cornerstone of the MBA, as likely, in one form or another, an MBA graduate will have to interface with Pricing. This course will provide you with a comprehensive view of pricing from the perspective of different products, pricing mechanisms and markets. The course was also well executed with engaging discussions and great speakers (we had a BCG senior partner, a Simon Kucher Pricing consultant, and a SaaS sales leader). Case workload was very manageable. Wasim himself is also a great guy.

Yes. 100%. In fact, I STRONGLY urge the program office to make this class part of the core. It blends microeconomics, marketing, and strategy in a way that is actually useful, practical, and real. All those classes in the core are very subpar. You could give students more opportunities to take electives by making pricing a rich, full core requirement, mandatory for all students.
Yes, i recommend this class to fellow students. This class gives you real life examples of pricing strategies that will be useful for anyone

Rethink at least three times before you bid for this class: 1) read the syllabus and imagine all the content and communication in the semester are presented similarly. Would you be ok with having to parse through information always like this by yourself? 2) Would you be okay with content being extremely dry and lacking good transitions from topic to topic? 3) Would you be ok with the professor always insisting on the point he's trying to make, and sometimes even cutting people off once he hears what he was trying to get?
TL, DR: I don't like his teaching and communication style strongly. Even given the rich content and its potential usefulness in my future work, I would have told my old self to take another class.

Yes! This course is the ultimate course if you are looking for relevant and useful content. It links and expands upon work done in ethics, strategy, micro, macro, and finance. It is among the few classes that I feel I will actually use in my career.
Yes its a must do for mbas

This is one of the BEST classes I've ever taken at Berkeley Haas for two years so far. Ton of insights and learnings. If you are considering your career at consulting or strategy ops at big tech companies, you should take this course as there are so much insights not only about pricing but competitive strategy in general.

To be honest, I first hesitated taking this course as folks left a review about "old-fashioned case" and "too much focused on SaaS pricing" - both being the main reason. However, those were NOT TRUE at all, at least in my personal experience. The cases were balanced between traditional business and SaaS, for some of them, you can hear what had happened actually from the professor. Cases are a bit old thou, you can still learn a timeless learnings, like pure "classics" in every field of expertise. During the semester, I really enjoyed this course with Prof. Azhar this semester. I wish we had more of this kind of practical classes during my two years.
I would recommend! It's different and very very important way to think about strategy
Yes, he explain the class concept well in and engaging way

Wasim is one of the most genuine professors I've come across at Haas. He truly cares not just about students' learning but their approaches and curiosity to think differently. His class has so many tiny anecdotes that add more to the MBA experience and makes it more human.
I highly recommend this course to those who enjoy not just pricing but comprehensive business strategies. A very worthwhile learning experience.

Pretty good class, would say that it is a bit more about overall strategy than solely pricing, which was a strength of the class in my opinion. Wasim is a great professor if a bit quirky - just takes some getting used to. The workload is really not that bad if you don't mind group work, plus the final is take-home. Overall, I would take this class again. I would definitely recommend this course. It touches on core business fundamentals that are relevant across roles like product development, marketing, and strategy. The case-based format (similar to consulting interviews) really sharpens your structured thinking, which is invaluable in corporate settings. Prof. Wasim keeps the class engaging by connecting business strategies to real-life decision-making, making the concepts easy and relatable.

Be prepared for around 2 hours of work outside class each week. The class typically runs 1.5 hours of case discussion and 30 minutes of key takeaways; personally, I found the concepts section could be a bit shorter, but it doesn't take away from the overall experience.

10000% yes. This has not only been the most relevant class I have taken at Haas, but it has remained so because Prof. Azhar keeps it relevant through his masterful lectures, cases and guest speakers. He imparts wisdom by the minute, is humble, kind, and strikes the perfect balance for an MBA course. Prof. Azhar was by far the best Prof. I have taken at Haas. He is not only incredibly gifted, but can convey that knowledge and wisdom through humor, in his assignments, lectures, and outside of class. The first speakers he brought in were the best guest lecturers and the most relevant ones to the context of the class and the current economy. He masterfully keeps the class engaged and interested throughout. Finally, he has been the kindest person overall in my entire Haas experience and the most understanding of my particular situation as a mother in her postpartum. I could not recommend him more.

I think this class is great if you're looking to get more knowledgeable on pricing methodology, some of the cases were a bit antiquated and made it difficult to connect to. but If you can get over that, Wassim is a great professor. I would 100% recommend this course. Core Strategy does not have a lot of frameworks to develop business intuition. Pricing helps you see many strategic situations through frameworks, so it serves as a great complement. The case work and guest speakers help you see how those frameworks work in the real world. Professor is funny and remembers a lot about students. He has many great experiences to share.
For sure. The way Wasim teaches the courses, he will ingrain concepts into your mind - making sure you are able to recall ideas well after you've left Haas.
I will say to get maximum value out of the class you need to put the work into cases - its of no use showing up for class if you arent doing the readings and contributing to the group assignments

Absolutely! I believe Pricing should be in the MBA core or advertised more by the academics offices. There are so many relevant frameworks and learning that I will leverage in my Product Marketing role in tech.

Yes - this course is extremely useful for anyone who wants to work in strategy/marketing/product or want to learn about pricing in different industries. This is not a low lift class but it isn't too heavy either - it is the perfect level or course load that pushes you to engage and come prepared. Also, Prof.Azhar lets everyone participate and is open to different perspectives which is great.

As long as Wasim teaches it, this class is a must-take. It's far better than managerial accounting, brand management, or any litany of similar courses that touch upon its topics. Take it as a capstone.

I highly recommend this class. Wasim is both highly knowledgeable and facilitates class in an engaging way; you'll both be interested in the material and also learn insights that you can apply in future real world scenarios. Absolutely! It's an extremely practical course with widespread applications across industries and roles. The various nuances of pricing along with examples of how companies are using them is helpful in approaching problems that we face in the real business world.

I would highly recommend this course to anyone who plans to go into a pricing or strategy-based role in the future. The cases spanned a wide variety of industries, with learnings and principles that are highly practical to anyone that will be in a senior management position in the future.

This was one my favorite classes at Haas. I felt like I learned so much that will be applicable in my career and just my day-to-day life. The professor facilitated engaging discussion, and there were so many valuable lessons we gained experientially and through case review. Cannot recommend more.
Great class with a decent amount of workload. You get as much as you put in as work on each case and each assignment.

Wasim clearly stated objectives and expectations right from the start and stuck by it. He is extremely proficient at understanding the class pulse and moving us through tricky concepts. He listens without judgement but has very strong opinions which he voices with utmost confidence and conviction. His course taught me the rigour of constantly learning and how to mould quantitative and qualitative information. I now feel I understand the moving parts of all functions in a business much better just through the lens of pricing!

The cases and course design was on-point. Fabulous mix of cases, lectures and guest speakers. We moved through content not only efficiently but also with key reinforcements from time to time. I only got better writing each assignment and I could see my thought process evolve.

sections.goodFor: Any function or industry - students frame it as a full strategy and market-research course, not just pricing; especially useful for founders and strategy roles.
sections.notFor: Non-quantitative students, who one commenter warns may struggle; anyone wanting AI-era content, since some frameworks and material felt dated.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified. Case-based with guest speakers; students call it content- and math-heavy on the surface but well-structured and digestible as taught.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: One student says some material and frameworks felt outdated and wants more current cases and AI tools; one bare 'No.' with no explanation.
sections.quote: Maybe - if you are already a quantitative person, this class will be a breeze. If not, this class might be a struggle.
comments: Yes, the class is very helpful for likely any position post-Haas, Professor Azhar is incredible overall, and I think I was the most intellectually challenged in this class.
Yes! This class was one of my favorite advanced topics and will be a strong value add regardless of function or industry you are going into. Highly recommend!
Yes, Absolutely.
Yes! Professor is one of the most caring professors I have met at Haas!
Absolutely 11/10 would recommend
Yes, I would definitely recommend this course. It's pretty essential in your toolkit irrespective of your post MBA industry.

Yes, absolutely. Professor Wasim is a highly effective and engaging instructor who brings strong clarity and structure to complex pricing concepts. He does an excellent job connecting frameworks to real-world applications, making the material both practical and memorable. The course is well-designed, with thoughtful case selection that reinforces key ideas, and the guest speakers add valuable industry perspective. Overall, it's a rigorous yet rewarding class that I would strongly recommend to anyone interested in pricing or strategy.

Yes I would. If you want to learn about differentiation, pricing strategies and go to market this is a great class. He is very experienced but stays on top of industry news. I really appreciated being able to discuss pricing strategies for OpenAI or Anthropic's products rather than the usual Coke or Airline cases that we cover on other courses

The class is extremely worthwhile. Beyond pricing you lose learn about strategy and market research. It is a very good aggregation of everything I have learned in the MBA so far. As a founder there were many insights I will take with me to my own company.

Yes, very much! A must-course in your MBA degree, seems content and math heavy but is really easy to digest and understand the way Prof Ashar teaches. In fact, he brings down complex concepts to intuition that you build through this course. He is a gem of a teacher, well-connected with a bajillion star alumni, and genuinely caring/helpful. Maybe - if you are already a quantitative person, this class will be a breeze. If not, this class might be a struggle. I also wish that this class leveraged AI tools and more current cases to stay at the cutting edge. Some material and frameworks felt outdated.
Yes, would definitely recommend
No.
Yes on course, yes on the professor. Thoroughly enjoyed the class and how Prof. Azhar managed class conversations with us.
Yes. He is well prepared and I learned a lot from his frameworks and way of analyzing industries and companies. Pricing is not just related to product elasticity, it's a full on strategy course,

I absolutely recommend this course to anyone considering working in business. Even if you won't be working in pricing directly, learning pricing strategy will make you a better business leader. Great class regardless of function or industry you are going into.
yesss

sections.goodFor: Students who want a current, well-connected overview of the impact investing landscape beyond just impact VC; the instructor is consistently praised as engaging and generous with office hours, and the guest speakers as high caliber. Best suited to those with basic finance under their belt.
sections.notFor: Students without finance fundamentals, despite the course being billed as entry level; several say it gets technically heavy and one had to run separate sessions to help classmates keep up. Also not for anyone wanting practical fund-building skills rather than a survey, or who dislikes cramming a broad topic into two Sundays.
sections.workloadNote: Repeatedly called a lot of work for a one-credit class, with substantial pre-reading and an intense group project squeezed between the two full-day Sunday sessions.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (10+ comments): the two-Sunday compressed format is too short for the breadth of material and should be a multi-week elective. Recurring (8 comments): assumes real finance background despite being marketed as entry level. Recurring (4 comments): workload is out of proportion to one credit.
sections.quote: It was a really useful, practical, and interesting overview of the impact investing landscape and trends.
comments: Absolutely, particularly from Dave Chen. This course opened my eyes to the different asset classes in impact investing, beyond Venture Capital that everyone thinks about. It has influenced what I want to do here at Haas, and what kinds of career options I assess. It was an extremely high-leverage experience.

Would not recommend. Course content was too focused on the US and was not useful for international students I would absolutely recommend this course. In fact, I would recommend this course for every business and STEM student. This covers the entire collective of global industries and how the world can use capital to collaborate and build the impact needed for today and tomorrow.
Yes, without hesitation. Important knowledge base, case studies, insights if you want to do work in social impact. Yes and yes. Watch out for the finance specific content.
Yes - great overview of the field.

yes but on the condition that the class can take place in four weeks so that we can prepare more and less exhausted I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking to learn foundational concepts in Impact Investment. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a peek into the Impact Investment world, a peek into the minds of people, the culture and the kind of conversations taking place.
I would recommend this course and instructor to a fellow student. For a student new to impact investing, the course will help to clarify potential pathways for entry into the space.
I would definitely recommend this class and instructor, however not with the given course structure (i.e. over two Sundays). This course should definitely be taken over the court of a semester.
Yes due to the substantial learning, but might give them a side note that as long as the time spent compared to the unit is not a concern, this is a good class.

I would definitely recommend this instructor and course. It was a really useful, practical, and interesting overview of the impact investing landscape and trends. Even as someone relatively familiar with the sector I felt like I learnt a lot. The guest speakers were great and David himself was a very engaging lecturer.

However, the course was quite a lot of work for a 1-credit class (lots of pre-reading and a pretty intense group project between the two classes) so be aware if you also have a lot of other things on!
Yes. It's a great starter for those who want to understand and get into the field.
Highly recommend it, Dave is an excellent professor and is invested in your learning. He is well connected and able to bring incredible speakers into the course.
Great class for understanding the landscape. You will be bombarded with concepts, terms, and ideas and not everything will make sense. Make notes and go back to do more digging to get the full worth.

I would recommend it to people who has a previous finance background in finance and is interested in continuing this journey, but probably not for people who perhaps don't want to get too deep in finance.
Neutral. It really depends on how interested the students are in this topic. But it was a good introduction course in general.
Love the class! Impact investing is very interesting and David is the one person who know it all. He loves teaching the subject and always try to help students.
Not in its current form
200% not only to students but also to core course professors
Absolutely worth every penny. One of the most enlightening courses I've taken at Haas and a huge value-add for anyone (regardless of background) looking to get involved in impact investing.

100% if you are interested in any form of investment field this class is a must whether or not you are interested in impact investment - this field is a need to know. For non finance background students, brush up on finance terminology as it can get a bit technically heavy, but the fundamentals and insights gained are going to be very helpful.

David Chen was a wonderful instructor for this Impact Investing Landscape course; however, I wish we were given practical skills on how to design products or funds in these space. This course provided a general overview of what people are doing in this space, but it is not enough information or skill building that would allow me to do this myself or even know where to start.
Yes!
Yes
Yes. Incredibly knowledgeable and friendly. Held multiple office hours to meet with our team and discuss our project. Well-connected to industry and able to bring in multiple high-level speakers.
Yes, but only if it's expanded to a 2 unit course. Two sessions was barely enough to scratch the surface Yes, this class was a great crash course in impact investing.

Yes, class is a refreshing break from company-centric classes in the MBA by considering the mix of business, policy, and economics in making cities/regions successful. Useful for entrepreneurs or policy-interested students looking to figure out where to locate, especially for international students looking to take learnings from the US back to their home countries (e.g, starting an AI startup in their home country). Not every region is equal in determining success. Yes! Great professor, cares a lot and takes a real interest in students.

Not sure. You can learn a lot from the cases but it is TOO MUCH pre-reading material and the class discussions always tended to deviate from readings to things half the class didn't know about or couldn't follow
Yes
It depends. If a student is interested in this topic and has enough time to commit to after/before-class assignments, I'd recommend this class.
The anxiety of job search and the limited time we could dive in each cluster per time distracts me from fully enjoying this course.

rows.title: Systems Change for a Small Planet

comments: This class is a MUST take. If you want to practice critical thinking, question what you're learning in other business classes, have a moment to step outside your own ambitions and goals and think about your place in society and our planet this is the class to take. Kris and Will guide the class with the deepest empathy, practice (and thus teach us) active listening, and let us sit with our discomfort, realizations, fears, and, longings. If you want to truly grow personally and professionally, take this class.
Yes, 100%. Especially if they care about social impact. It's an interesting class and the probably the closest class in Haas to getting whoo-whoo and hippie dippie (if you like that kind of stuff)

This was the most worthwhile class I have taken throughout my entire schooling history. You learn about the role of metaphors in life, the body as a system, modernity as a system, how to analyze systems, how to change systems...how to sit with the complexity of it all. The classroom is such a nourishing environment for vulnerability, expression, and expansion. The "homework" assignments are multi-modal, sometimes videos, podcasts, meditations, articles, etc. This class expanded my brain and my soul.

This course is singlehandedly making me not regret getting an MBA. It is what I envisioned getting my MBA at Haas would be like, and is one of the only courses that has lived up to my expectations. It pushed us to re-imagine how we might move through the world in more generative not extractive, ways, as business leaders, as friends, as family members, and as human beings period. We used a lot of metaphors in the class so I will use one here. It was like a cup full of fresh, spring water that hasn't yet been spoiled yet by any chemicals, climate change effects, or disease - offered up to us in the middle of a 100-mile journey through a hostile, harsh, and dry desert. It has helped me not only in my life as a business student/leader, but in my broader life. The lessons I learned here I will take with me for the rest of my life!

Will and Kris provided the most warm, supportive, and generative class environment I've experienced in graduate school. The readings, ideas, and experiences they offered were so meaningful and developed our thinking as well as our hearts. I'm so grateful to them, my classmates, and this class, and would take this class again in a heartbeat. Absolutely yes! This course triggered a lot of personal growth and helped me get more comfortable with complexity. It was like doing therapy for a semester:) This course is very different from traditional Haas courses focused on business skills, this one is about a lot of self-reflection and multi-layered interaction with the world. It definitely inspired me to try and live my values with less fear and bias.

This is a new course that could use some ironing. The syllabus states that "students will use systems thinking to explore the power dynamics and feedback loops that keep the current system in place" and "students will analyze real-world examples of emerging models (including regenerative and ecological economics, `doughnut economics,? and the circular economy) that fundamentally reframe the system?s goals to support a flourishing population and planet." The readings for this class do related to those topics, but classtime is not managed effectively. I often found myself leaving class wondering, "what did we even do today? Did I learn anything?" Instead, this class served as an opportunity to slow down and find serenity, an uncommon opportunity at Haas.

If you are looking for a platform to challenge what you know and think about what you need to unlearn, this is the class for you. If you are looking to explore systems change and the 'how,' this class may not be for you.
I would recommend the INSTRUCTOR to all. I would recommend the COURSE *if* a student is interested in how to
change the systems in which we exist; in other words, if "Questioning the Status Quo" isn't your favorite HDLP, this course may not be for you. Personally, I adored this class.
This is a feel good class, relatively low lift- very soft skill. Good if you want to learn about how to help the world with your specific skills

This was definitely one of the most impactful courses I've taken. Don't go into it expecting to learn a specific tool, process, or skill. Go into it with an open mind and find comfort in the ambiguity. This course is definitely just part of a larger process we go though. 10/10 would take again

This is the most inspiring class at Haas by far! It was a breath of fresh air in the midst of every other traditionally academic classes. The professors helped me rethink my purpose and meaning and redirect my efforts to my next big life step. My favorite Haas class by far.

I would recommend this class because it's unique in the Haas MBA architecture. There aren't any other classes that allow you to zoom out and think in this way. However, if you're looking to build more technical skills this isn't the right class.

Yes, this course is what I hoped grad school would be. It gives you space and material for reflecting on your values and worldview. It has helped me explore a theory of change and outlook for how I want to impact the world post-Haas. I overall really liked the class and how different it was compared to all other classes I've taken here. I think I expected more concrete examples, more lecturing from the professors at first, and something to just make the class "stick" more. Maybe concrete strategies for how to become a more effective beyond capitalism leader? I also think more concrete lecturing from the professors were helpful to bring it back to a framework. The most impactful things I learned were the two loops theory and the concept of donut economics, so the more tangible things we can leave with students, the better.

Yes, but I don't think it's for everyone. If you are self-aware and open to checking your limiting beliefs and assumptions, I think you'll get a lot out of this! But fair warning: it's more of a playground or sandbox to grapple with how we live our lives individually and collectively rather than a lecture based class that will impact lessons upon you Not in this current format for most students. If you want unstructured reflections and a place to build connections and explore big systems, this is the class for you - but I think most people wouldn't leave with any new tools or concepts. The professors are incredible and kind, but they are lacking real concepts and cases to help ground the class. I truly believe this class can have a big improvement!

definitely, this is such a unique course in the MBA, and I think it resonates so well with the type of leaders Haas is trying to build. So much of our life is structured and linear, and it is so special to have the space and opportunity to think non-linearly and think about how we can exist within the system, yet change the system at the same time. I really hope that the theories and frameworks make their way into the rest of the Haas courses so that its not just the students in this class who are exposed to these ideas.

Taking this class will likely change you. It made me learn things about myself, how I think and how I interact with the world, and gave me new ideas to reflect on whenever I think about societal change. It is not a very applied class, I'd call it more philosophical, but I'd recommend everyone taking at least one class in this style during your time at Haas. The only thing is that I wish more people from "traditional MBA career interests" were taking this class too, to get more different opinions during the discussions.

I would recommend the course, with some warnings: the course does not teach an actual application, it does not teach you how to change the systems. It is mostly self-reflection on how you want to show up in the world and what you want to do. It gives space to research anything you are passionate about and learn about anything that you are passionate about. I loved my 3 hours in the class every week, but I am not sure I learned anything applicable. Yes! This class brings forth why I came to business school in the first place. It gives the structures if how to be a better, more community driven leader and gives space for reflection and introspection in a way that I hadn't explore before I would recommend this course! Professors really care about the topic and the students, is super dynamic and makes you reflect a lot on the current system and how could it be better. Sometimes it felt a bit messy with not very clear objectives but that was part of what the professors wanted to teach, not always follow the same structure.

I would recommend taking the course in conjunction with courses that have more links to research and practical applications. It's nice to provoke thought but if it's your only course in the area you may feel dissatisfied with the lack of utility.

I was very excited to take this course after it being highly recommended, but was very disappointed in how this class was structured and taught. It wasn't clear how the readings translated into actionable ideas/steps, and we often spent time critique other's work without any tangible ideas on how WE would do it differently. I wish there were more forums for students to express dissenting opinions from the status quo of the class. It felt like an echo chamber with no actionable takeaways and structure. I would not recommend taking this course unless it is more well-thought out and applicable.
Transformative class, so inspiring and thought-provoking
The class had great potential but I'm ending it feeling I have nothing to show from the course besides selfishly enjoying my own time. No takeaways to improve the world
Absolutely yes!! The most important class at haas

sections.goodFor: Students wanting a reflective, values-oriented break from the MBA bubble - questioning capitalist assumptions, personal growth, and frameworks for dominant versus emergent systems.
sections.notFor: Anyone after practical systems-change knowledge (crash course, cases, implementation, pitfalls) - one points to the 1-credit Systems Change course instead - or averse to touchy-feely reflection.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (6 comments). Reflective, discussion-driven work; one student says instruction was unclear and assignment expectations ill-defined. No hours or assignment cadence given.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - one student says assignment expectations were ill-defined, but nobody describes how the grade is determined.
sections.redFlags: One of six says the course was under-thought and poorly delivered, with unclear instruction and ill-defined assignment expectations. One would condense it to 2 credits with more actual systems-change content.
sections.quote: If you are just looking for system changes knowledge (i.e., crash course, case examples, how to implement, pitfalls, etc.), then this class is not for you
comments: I'm so glad I took this class - it was such a breath of fresh air in business school. This class really challenged my worldview and self-view and truly nourished my soul.

Yes - I absolutely loved this class. It was so different from every other class I've taken, and was a much needed breath of fresh air to reflect on my values and how they are aligned or misaligned with how I am living, and how we are all encouraged to live in modernity. The class gave me some really useful frameworks to think about systems change and my role in dominant and emergent systems, and how to promote systems change. I really really loved this class. I would not. The course was a good place to reflect on bigger systemic issues and provided meaningful opportunity to reflect on my place and role within those systems, but the course overall was under thought and poorly delivered. I do think the course has potential, but instruction was generally unclear and expectations around assignments, expectations, etc. were generally ill-defined and again, poorly delivered.

Yes. As a business school student, this could be the most important course you take during your time at Haas, especially if you open yourself up to the questions and discomfort that will arise from it.

It depends what you want out of the class. If you are just looking for system changes knowledge (i.e., crash course, case examples, how to implement, pitfalls, etc.), then this class is not for you and would recommend looking at the Systems Change 1-credit course that's offered. Now if you are looking for that + a touchy-feely course that is different than anything else you've taken at Haas, let's you spend time to reflect (vs go-go-go that bschool is), and grow as a person (vs student, corp ladder climber, etc.), then this course if for you. It was a breath of fresh air and a safe heaven. I'm glad I took it, but also would have been glad if it was condensed to a 2-credit course and focused more on systems change knowledge, implementation, etc.
Yes! Even if it isn't being offered again, this class really helped me step outside of the MBA bubble and question a lot of the business / capitalist oriented thinking that Haas embodies.
Yes 100% recommend - this was one of the most intellectually expansive and introspective classes I have ever taken and would recommend it to everyone.
Yes, applies the design thinking framework in a very practical setting. I really enjoyed working on a real problem that a real company faced.
Recommend. Heavy workload, but being client facing and very project focused keeps your work ethic somewhat active while you slack off and atrophy as a student

I would recommend this class for people who are interested in applying design thinking process and are passionate about learning about one of the particular clients as you get to work immersively on a client's project which entails a real business challenge they're solving. There's some overlap in this class and fundamentals of design thinking, but I enjoyed taking them in the same semester so I can reinforce my understanding of the course.

Yes, Haas@Work is an amazing experience, especially if you're looking for a deep dive into design thinking or if you're looking to go into product management! I really enjoyed how we worked with real clients and were able to form full- fledged solutions for their very real business problems. Would 100% recommend.

I would recommend Hass@work for anyone interested in getting a client-facing experience. There isn't substantially more content to learn beyond the fundamentals of design thinking class, but the learnings from applying the theory to a real-world business problem are substantial.
Definitely yes! It's not easy to get through the whole course, but it's worth to take and push yourself to think more and do more to the real business world.

The course was extremely effective in providing a taste of how consulting in the real-world would look like. I loved the frameworks the class provides around the design thinking process. I loved the open-ended vagueness of the class as well. As with any other experential class - the class will give you in return all that you put in. It has also helped me become a more effective leader leading a large diverse team. Definitely recommend the class to anyone interested in consulting and/or product management.

I would highly recommend Haas@Work to anyone who has a hard problem to solve at work or in your personal life. This is a wonderful framework and combined with real world clients, it is a valuable experience. It is a great tool in your arsenal. Be ready to be uncomfortable and brace ambiguity as your friend
Extremely practical and applicable to the real world

This course is great at providing experience and exposure to innovation consulting. It is both an innovation project and a client engagement. There is a lot of work, but in the end students gain valuable experience on the process and how it applies in a consulting context.

Yes, but be aware the level of effort that this class requires. It is NOT a class you can BS or hide in, you should be prepared to work a good amount outside of this class. It is an AI course afterall so I understand why the LOE is high, but this class felt like a lot of work. I think it was worth it overall, but I do have some reservations. It was good client facing experience, and I learned a lot about my client, but there were definitely a few lates nights spent on assignments.

I would recommend as long as you have a strong interest in the industry/company that your project is focusing on. For better or worse, it's an unique experience. It take time to get use to it at the start but the process is fun and lighthearted. Focus on the team project aspects of the class. lectures are usually hit or miss.

No. This course has more work than 2 other electives combined. Unless you truly love design thinking, hard pass. You waste a lot of time in weekly plenaries that aren't all that informative and this course drags on way longer than most other classes.
Yes, because it teaches you how to work amidst ambiguity, adjust to different working styles, and solve complex problems.
I would recommend this course if you're interested in diving into Design Consulting with real clients, real problems, coming up with real solutions.
yes
The course experience may be a hit or a miss.

In my experience. 2/3rd of the problem statement we received was completely out of the scope of the kind of work that's best-done by design thinking. Hence, we spent a lot of time sifting through the problems, and the teaching staff, instead of revising the problem statement, was intent on "fitting" the non-applicable solutions to those 2/3 of problems. That resulted in a lot of wasted time and effort.

The class organization is also VERY hierarchical under the project leader. So, contrary to the class description of the project leader being first among equals, the project leader is treated as more than equal when there are critical client conversations, such as the problem statement example above. The project leader is also the only one with a line of communication to the client. It was left to the project leader to include or not include other team members in client discussions, so there was a lot of monopolization of these client communications even though this is phrased as a project where "students work with clients," most of the team (except the project leader), close to zero client interaction outside of the presentations at various checkpoints.

Good for getting consulting experience. Will have a really hard time if you are not bought into the Chaos of Design Thinking. I feel its like rolling the dice, if you get a good project and a good team, you can learn a lot. But, be prepared to be frustrated a lot. But, if you are into Design Thinking or Consulting, definitely an opportunity to get real world experience. Also, as with any course, you will really get what you put into it. Being a team lead is a great opportunity to practice your managerial skills.
Great course! Highly recommend if you are interested in becoming a more effective coach or manager.

This is a great class. It is almost entirely practice with lots of feedback. I highly recommend taking it! Yes, if in-person and deeply patient. The instructors don't know much more than you/ aren't more skilled/ aren't exceptional in this arena, but it's the practice and observation that you'll benefit from.

I would recommend this course I think is very good.

What is a shame (and a constant across Berkeley) is that there is no coordination between the other courses that deal with interpersonal development skills. I wish there were, because would be more effective for students

NO ABSOLUTELY NOT!!! This is probably the worst class I ever attended at Haas, it felt like mental and physical torture. The teachers have no idea about human biology. A bio break every 2 hours and a 55 minute lunch in a 9 hour zoom session, ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!

This class was challenging on Zoom, but it's a valuable and useful class otherwise. The scope is focused so substantial learning could occur on the frameworks they teach. I wish the days weren't quite so long (9am - 6pm is tough, and there weren't enough breaks). Great teaching team though.

Yes, would recommend it. It's a little less on the "touchy feely" side and more about the practice. I would say the class gives good groundwork for you to be a better leader and coach on the job and gives some very practical tools for that This class is a great opportunity to practice coaching (and learn what coaching is... aka asking open-ended questions to help coaches arrive at their own next steps, without any opinions/advising by the coach). Great opportunity to practice active listening, gain empathy for other students, and maybe even get some good guidance on a problem you're currently struggling with! In all seriousness, I thought we covered a lot of material and learned useful frameworks in this class, and would recommend it to anyone who's serious about going into the business of managing people (and would consider it mandatory for any future executive coaches/HR folks).

The course content itself is probably better off as a 20 min TED talk. There is an extreme burden of outside work for a one-credit class (4 interviews, a 8 page paper, a outside of class hours practicum.)
This course may be valuable if you've had minimal work experience, leading teams/managing people, and want to practice with BECI coaches in breakouts.

Yes! The skills are useful for personal and professional situations. Jenny, Susan, and Thomas are great. Would expect only base level coaching, only helpful to take if you have not taken other soft skill courses at Haas I would recommend this course. It really helps on some of the softer skills which so many people overlook but are vital to career progress.
Yes! Very practical application to life outside Haas. Will be immediately useful in my life and career.
YES!! Coaching is a skills we could use in every area of our lives. This was the right amount of time, homework and plenty of practice. Thank yoU!

Skills of coaching very valuable as a "tool in your toolkit". Not for all situations of communication, but where relevant, is incredibly useful and can certainly define the success/failure of your situation.

I wish this course was longer. I loved our external coach Shawn! She was so amazing and the practice sessions really resulted in substantial learning. Yes. I will recommend. I didnt know the difference between coach and mentor before the class and now I think I am a better coach.

This is a great course that everyone who wants be a leader should take. Especially if you want to empower & set your team up for success.
Great learning in 16 hours of time.

I felt there could be more frameworks/tools taught/real life examples of what works well vs. not (as opposed to those being brought up after a question was asked).

I would highly recommend the Leader as Coach course to fellow students. The coach/coachee practice sessions were all extremely impactful, and really delivered meaning and valuable practice for everyone involved. I'm definitely going to take away the practices from this course and apply them in my relationships, both personally and professionally.

rows.title: Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Leadership

comments: Definitely recommend. After taking the course, I felt I have taken the first step on the journey to love myself before I can love others. This course will ask you to look inside, stretch and be vulnerable so only attend the course if you are ready to do that. The home assignments are huge so be ready for that too.

I DO NOT recommend the course. It could be fit for a psychology program but definitely not an MBA. I signed up for it to build "interpersonal skills" but I have gotten none of that. While the instructor was immersed in the methods and was dedicated to giving students a good learning experience, the content seemed very light and the

exercises/practices felt like a waste of time. I found it very hard connecting what I did during the course to any helpful skill or competence relevant to my journey as a business leader or career person.
The course seems to be overly focused on neurobiology, feelings and emotions, which I personally did not find helpful for my journey in becoming a business leader.
Also, if it has to be taught, then it may be best taught in-person.
Yes. The experiential portion of the class (almost 95% of it) really got me rethink about the way I approach people and life.

I would definitely recommend this course to other students with the caveat that they have to be genuinely curious about the material and content. The course is truly transformative for those that make the commitment to immerse themselves in the course content.

Depending on what stage you are in your leadership or professional development, this class might resonate with you. I went through many practices that were useful and explored concepts I had not done before.
Having said that, I felt we could have package more grounded, concrete learnings in this 2 unit course compared to other similar courses.

Not at all! This course had very little to no substance and was a sheer waste of time. The course description was so different from the content that was taught. this can be described as a breathing, dancing, distressing spiritual class. If you are on the verge of an emotional breakdown, perhaps this class can serve as a therapy session for you. Most folks in the class were surprised by the content. The professor shares some of her childhood memories, her love for dancing and a rock band (BTS) that she adores over and over. I am beyond flabbergasted how Haas even approved this class. It is a total waste for time and money. The only useless class I have ever taken at Haas. It was like being held hostage for 4 days for no reason. Please do yourself a favor by not enrolling for this class.

Yes...she reverse engineers connections. Makes you think of negatives cycles, and defines emotions and how to deal with them. As someone who never took a course like this, and was from a quantitative background, probably the coolest course at Haas I've ever met. Businesses, politics are all about managing relationships and this teaches you about the very human fundamentals of connection from neuroscience and psychology.

This class is a must take. Its short and intense but unconventional and a breath of fresh air among normal MBA classes. Its awesome if you like to stretch yourself socially and develop as well as making friendships and being vulnerable. If there is any part of you that wishes that you felt more connected to people at Haas, please take this course. The stories you hear from others and the stories that you share will create such a powerful experience that cannot be replicated by any other Haas course. I specifically encourage my fellow men at Haas to challenge themselves with a course that tests their emotional intelligence and boundaries. If you identify as a man and struggle with
vulnerability/emotional expression, please take this course and allow yourself to grow.
Trust Erica and her process, and it will pay dividends.

Yes definitely take this class. This is a powerful class that allows you to tap into your deepest emotions in a safe space. I have noted some points which I would like Erica to include in the course. With those included, I would recommend this course
Course materials have included quite a few video clips selections that reflect personal preference but might be difficult to arouse resonance among students
I would aslo like to see more structures of how the concepts and theory relate to the practice.

I would highly recommend it. It is a lot of work, but I have learnt practical frameworks that challenge unhelpful inner chatters/old patterns and regulate my nervous system, which I think is not only useful for leadership but also for personal fulfillment and happiness.
This course is a really concentrated time commitment - you are essentially sacrificing 3 weeks in a row (pre-work, class sessions and post-work)

This class was not really what I expected, I wish we had more practical application to real life scenarios. If you want more practice on being vulnerable and in touch with your emotions, then this class might be beneficial for you. But if you are looking to apply these learnings to your professional or personal life, I do not see much of a benefit. This class is heavily focused on group sessions in which we open up and are vulnerable with each other, but it doesn't go too deep into how we would apply this in real life. For that reason, when it comes to recommending this class, I would say that it depends on what you are looking for.

I highly recommend this course to others. It is a difficult course, yes, but it is the most practical course I?ve ever been a part of and will no doubt help drive the positive change in you and your relationships.

Yes! Absolutely yes! This course has been the true highlight of my Haas experience. It was really nice to see how to improve interpersonal skills, build truly meaningful relationships, be vulnerable, have heart to heart conversations. It has a lot of work, a lot of work, but in my opinion, it was necessary and worth it. I got to know 18 beautiful human beings through this course, and I will never forget this experience.

As it stands today, I would not recommend. However, if the class is increased from 2 credits to 3 credits and is spread out over the course of 10 weeks or a full semester (currently it is over two weekends), I would consider it. The workload is extremely heavy and it is difficult to accomplish everything in three weeks, especially on top of everyone's busy schedules. Not only is this taxing, but it also detracts from the value of what you are learning. If you are located in the Bay Area, I would also require that the course be in-person. The current Zoom medium leaves something to be desired. i think this needs to be a required class.. it probably be shortened and doesn't need to be as long.. perhaps havfe class times start at 10am always?

These studies are given to the students to reflect on and make a impact on how we present ourselves as leaders, and as people, in difficult situations.

I would not. I think that this class would be a great one-day, 3-hour session. But I do not see value in it being as long and intensive as it is. The workload has exceeded a majority of the core classes at Haas, filled with videos of BTS interviews and music videos and ted talks. I think that Erica is a very passionate and knowledgable professor, but I do not think that I gained much value from this course. The forced intimacy led to numerous triggering moments, including Erica showing screenshots of messages between her and her mother with whom she has a tumultuous
relationship with to the class and crying. Overall, this class is an extremely heavy lift, with little to no value, and will expose you to high levels of emotional distress. Do not recommend.

yes for someone who would love to know themselves better. but it's too many workloads.

This is a truly unique course in the Haas curriculum. There are plenty of leadership and communications courses offered, many of which are very good. This one has the reputation it has though because it really forces introspection and understanding yourself. Where you come from, your environment, your interactions, and how all of that comes together for who you are and how you lead.
Erica also embodies all that is Berkeley Haas. She has a true passion and connection to what she teaches - its in her core.

With that said, you absolutely get out of it what you put into it. If you do not show up, put in the work in the assignments, and actively engage, you'll probably waste a lot of time and your tuition dollars. If you're looking for a very deterministic outcome or result, you may be disappointed. If you think this will be some version of 'How to win friends and influence people,' you're also off track. As such, this class isn't for everyone.

I would recommend Professor Zhang as he provides a structured and clear way to learn accounting that is based on practice rather than only theory, which in my opinion is the only way to really understand accounting.
I would certainly recommend fellow students take this class.
Learning accounting might be very tedious, but it's a crucial subject for future business leaders. XJ made this class more dynamic and did a great job facilitating our learning.
I feel more prepared to discuss accounting topics after this class and decided to continue learning finance and accounting in Corporate Finance.

I would not recommend this course/ instructor - the course is not engaging, there are very few take aways and the instructional materials are not efficient in providing a strong education in accounting. Using the textbook and other professors materials were more effective than following the course and the instructor's given materials. Yes! Loved the class

Yes, I would. It was a very challenging course for me, but it taught me a lot about accounting given I didn't have any prior knowledge. XJ cares about his students and is a good instructor - I just wish that we went at a slower pace to cover so much material and that I had grasped the fundamentals of accounting (how the three statements relate, for example) before rushing onto the next material
Yes. I recommend. Professor teaches accounting effortlessly and effectively. It does not feel like pulling teeth, as opposed to the accounting stereotype.
I would recommend an accounting class to learn how to read corporate financial statements.
If you have a choice of professors, I recommend you take it with Omri, as I hear he makes class more engaging. Useful like skill!

I would, but really wish that we were able to experience this in NL, especially since it should make up such a large portion of the course fees. Or, have the opportunity to visit THNK in the future when the pandemic is over! Yes, the virtual experience was pretty good and I would imagine the experience would have been great if it was in Netherlands Experiencing the problem and culture first hand in Netherlands would have made it the perfect class. I would highly recommend it. The learning is substantial, but also depends upon your team a little bit. I was fortunate to have a good time which really put in the time and used the resources. You can apply the skills learnt from this course to any kind of work, but it has huge application for entrepreneurship and consulting.

Great instructors. Course is super valuable if someone wants to learn and experience design thinking first hand. I would have preferred in person Netherlands though, because there is lot of collaboration work and the experience of seeing/feeling problems we are trying to solve in real is super critical. I do not recommend this course if it is online only version, otherwise definitely worth taking this class.

I would only recommend taking this course if you can do it in person. It is difficult to get what you want out of work like this when you're distributing it via all-day virtual sessions a month apart.
Yes, but only if it's in-person.
Yes the class resulted in learnings

Rajiv and Sam were great instructors. It is a shame that this class was virtual because I feel like you miss out a lot on the excitement of the subject matter by being tied to a screen. Obviously no ones fault and the entire teaching team did their best to bring the subject to life. Definitely recommend this as an in person experience.
We didn't get to go to the netherlands this year, but I thought this was an interesting and fast way to get exposure to the design thinking process.
Yes and I am sure the course will be even more engaging in person in Amsterdam than virtually
Yes, this is an effective course to learn and apply Design Thinking principles with an optimal workload. There were no unnecessary exercises or assignments.

Yes! Take this class if you are looking into developing a faster framework to view insights and business problems and have an iterative process on hand at your next job or internship. It helped me think as a future business leader how to approach problems in a multi-disciplinary approach and it could be seen in what other groups presented, from CPG to experiential in-store experiences, and technology solutions, a lot of these aspects could be implemented to push the "healthy-eating habits" that the brief asked. Lots of room to get creative!

rows.title: Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Leadership
rows.terms: 2022 Spring;2022 Fall;2023 Spring;2023 Fall;2024 Spring;2025 Spring;2025 Fall

comments: There is no other class like this at Haas. Take it if you want to spend 30+ hours thinking about yourself and how you interact with the rest of the world. Erica has woven together disparate practices into a cohesive whole. I found it useful and enlightening.
I would absolutely recommend this class for anyone looking to deepen their interpersonal skills and learn the tools for being a more empathetic and emotionally intelligent leader.
Yes I would, this class was really powerful in helping me develop my active listening and be aware of the emotions and physical sensations I am experiencing in the moment.
Absolutely. One of the best courses I've taken at Haas

No. I would not recommend this course AT ALL. This class was bizarre with numerous references to BTS as an example of embodied leadership. That did NOT resonate with the class. Part of the course curriculum was to watch a video of the instructor performing a BTS dance cover. The BTS fan base is teenage kids so for the instructor to be this into it did not feel appropriate. The use of emotion from the instructor felt manufactured and disingenuous. The exercises in class were not effective on Zoom and dragged on and on.

I personally would recommend it to anyone who is open to actually examining and putting in the time to explore their own real identity, stress, anxiety, and goals in life. I am not exaggerating when I say that this course helped me rediscover what I believe to be my purpose and the meaning in life. I didn't come in thinking that would happen, but near the end session, I felt a wall inside me just fall down and realized how implicitly self-centered I had been throughout my whole life and what events informed that, and I realized I could make a conscious change to not let myself be defined by comparison & productivity. However I think this class comes down to how much you are able to put in (time commitment wise) and how open you let yourself be to evolving and changing. Every single person had different insights and takeaways and changes I think. So while I know this class is extremely polarizing, I found it valuable and perhaps the most memorable class I took at Haas because it caused me to re-conceptualize my own identity, self, priorities, anxieties, and how I see the world. For me, that's more valuable than a power & politics class that tells you how to win in the world / manipulate people in a nutshell haha. Because I feel like in my own happiness I have a framework to transcend a mentality where " i will only be happy if I have material success. " And that is freeing. On the other hand, this class is a lot of what can feel like busywork and journaling/writing, as well as reading, so it's not a commitment that can be made lightly. There's a lot of pre-work and post-work, and so it's not a 3-day seminar you can just show up, get insights, and leave. It requires substantial work on your own side, but setting aside that time for reflection helped me mostly (though I think it's maybe still a bit on the heavy side).
Absolutely, this is one of the few classes where you learn an applicable skill.

This was the most transformative class I've taken at Haas. There is very distinctly a pre-ISEL period in my life as well as a post-ISEL period in my life. If you are open to the process and want to better self-regulate your emotions (as well as handle and take care of the emotions of people around you) I recommend this class. There is so much to be said about effective leadership coming from leaders that know how to self-regulate AND recognize the emotional experience of the people around them.
Course is probably one of the best at Haas in terms of a course that will actually teach you something and lead to professional growth.
Yes, I recommend ISEL to all fellow Haasies.

ISEL teaches a holistic system of how to relate internally to oneself and externally to others (and vice versa). I believe it's crucial (absolutely critical) to learn such skills especially since as top MBAs we are ascending into managerial roles at elite firms in our capitalistic society.

Now, many students have not had positive experiences in ISEL. I respect that, and I went into the class knowing those experiences are real, legitimate, and exist. Ultimately, in order to benefit from ISEL, it's important to go into it with an open mind, earnestly doing all the assignments, all the practices, and all the readings.

ISEL is not perfect.
