It has some minor flaws; particularly in how it presents itself as being tied to the GSB "touchy feely" class, which sets up an unmet expectation; a minority few of the methods Erica employ feel too unrelated to the course content; the all virtual format my cohort experienced can be difficult for some — but some prefer it, but its also unrealistic given that we don't conduct our lives entirely virtually (for now...); many of the assignments deal with intersectional identity, but we didn't cover enough of that in fishbowl T-groups; I think the "crash-course weekend" might be too tiring to have lasting learnings for some people.
yes! i am glad i chose to spend some time at haas working on softer skills and feel honored to have done so with Erica, who clearly cares about this subject and her students an extraordinary amount.

Yes; The course is a good new perspective on other courses around leadership in the Haas curriculum. This is one of the only ones I know that talks about regulating your emotions (not controlling or avoiding them) and how that might benefit you and your connections to others. Erica and the co-learners are so passionate and they really seem to enjoy this work. It is a long class and lot of commitment but it is worth the investment.
highly recommended if you are sensitive to other people's comments on you. you will be able to build up your capacity to deal with interpersonal issues and better connections with people around you

This course is a great capstone of interpersonal leadership courses at Haas. The professors are incredibly nice and supportive. The three days of solid class on the weekend was long, but nicely broken up with breaks, stretching, and meditation. There is quite a lot of written work to do both before and after (6 total assignments that may take most of a day each), but maybe that is expected given it is a two unit class.

I would highly recommend the instructor and course to fellow students, as I truly believe this is one of the most transformative classes at Haas. Through this class, I reflected and reexamined my past experiences interacting with people in my personal life or at the workplace, and now have a better strategy in place to handle conflicts, and surging emotions. This class has given me the tools to be in touch with my true self and express myself in the world with authenticity and humility.

I would NOT recommend this course in its current design and fashion. The workload is IMMENSE, with very LITTLE learnings, and a very rigid instructor who created distance with students. There is a HUGE potential for this course in the curriculum and the team and instructor put a lot of work in building its content. But its force is becoming its weakness - it is too rigid, too structured, too dictated, and is the only course that Haas still offers online fully (which is a shame for the focus is on building connection and students do value in-person teaching). This online model may be more adapted for EMBA and EWMBA students.
No.
The class pre-work is insane...and so the workload during the class
I feel that this class could have been done in two Fridays maximum

No. It is a horribly executed class that taught me nothing. When thing started to get intersting, Erica would interrupt to add her two cents. The continous references to the k-pop boy band were completely unecessary and irrelevant. This class should also not be done in three days but a few hours a week for 5 to 6 weeks.

I would recommend this course, but I would caution student that this course is more about learning about oneself and one's subconscious reactions (and self regulation strategies) and less on application of how to apply the learnings in a business or professional environment.
I highly recommend this class. I learnt more than I expected to learn and grew so much with this class.
Definitely yes, wholeheartedly!
No other course will empower you with the same level of awareness and "tools" you need for a happier relationship with others and yourself, and a sense of freedom.

If you, like me, came to business school to develop soft skills, learn how to connect with others, and understand yourself, then this class is for you. Erica formerly taught Touchy Feely at the GSB and has adapted it to account for one's social background and to create deeper connection with students from all backgrounds. However, be warned that the course readings and engagement requirements far surpass that of an average Haas class (core included). Even though English is my first language, I struggled to understand the readings and assignments. The zoom nature of the course was also emotionally draining. However, I am leaving the course feeling empowered to become a better person, friend, sibling, and coworker.

Those who aren't sure they can handle the intense course workload should look at Jennifer and Rajiv's two-day Building Trust Based Relationships Course. The courses overlap with each other, although Trust Based Relationships doesn't go as deep due to the course's brevity.

I think I would not recommend this class, as is, to fellow students. The material is important: real connection and conversations, dignity, conflict, etc., are all critical pieces of developing as people and leaders, but this class was more work than learning and could be more impactful in a different format.
This is a good course to get better at communicating with people you care about under stress

This class is about self-reflection and building connections with people in different scenarios. Overall, the content is quite engaging, and I can see it being useful. However, the significant amount of pre-assignments and post- assignments and the time commitment of the whole weekend make me doubt my decision to choose this class. I think the content could be condensed into a one-credit course with substantial learning and much less workload. On the other hand, the instructor showed a lot of BTS content as examples of embodied leadership. But, I personally found it really hard to relate.

Do not take this class to take workload off the rest of your semester. The pre-work and post-work is ridiculously long. I came in interested to learn, but due to the length of the assignments, I ended up not being able to go deep in order to get it done within my schedule. The class was about as Berkeley as it could be. There were some good learnings but it felt like an hour of learning was extended into 4.

would highly prefer this class to be in person....zoom makes it hard to engage fully in the class. There are a lot of useful frameworks and exercises but hindered by the online format. Hopefully this changes.

To be honest, this ISEL cohort / class was a challenge (so many micro-aggressions and overall poor DEI competency from the teaching staff) however, they were genuinely open to feedback, I learned a lot of frameworks to talk through my own feelings, and according to my partner I'm already a better listener. I have asked that this be in-person again, but in the absence of that definitely take this at an Air BnB with friends.
I would because I learned a lot and I also feel a lot closer to my classmates and this was an opportunity for me to realize how amazing my classmates are.

I would not take the class if it is operated remotely. The format simply doesn't translate well to the virtual environment and 24 hours of virtual class over a 3 day period is a very tall order, despite instructor efforts to incorporate breaks. It is a good class to push yourself emotionally, but requires a ton of investment both from an emotional perspective as well as an time/effort perspective.

If you are super new to building interpersonal skills and embodied leadership, you might get something out of this course. The assignments are long and tedious, the class is long and not a super great use of time. I would want to see major shifts/changes in the course before being able to enthusiastically recommend the course, especially related to DEI.

This class has too much homework compared to the number of credits it is. The facilitation framework of the class needs to be updates to reflect more up-to-date best practices for DEI work. The class is significant emotional labor, especially for students from under-represented backgrounds.

I can not recommend this course in its current form. I had very high hopes but am very disappointed with what I experienced. The amount of pre- and post- work for this class is overwhelming, repetitive, and emotionally exhausting. The current format on Zoom is not conducive to such a heavy topic that is complex, emotionally intense, and has a great deal of nuance that you don't get through the screen. Most of my learning in this class was from classmates and unfortunately came at the expense of other students who were put in very uncomfortable situations. The teaching team is not as well-trained as they should be in DEI-related topics, including power, privilege, oppression, and marginalization.
Yes. I believe the future of work (in an AI world) would be about connecting more deeply with what makes me human. The course helped me discover that.
I would absolutely recommend this course and Erica. She is an incredible instructor and was willing to share and connect with us all.
yes, if your focus is on interpersonal skills building and having difficult conversation. This is not a typical leadership class.

Absolutely, this is the best soft skills class at Haas and broke down my negative associations with touchy/feely classes. Erica is one of the best, most aware professors at Haas and this course is essential for all future business leaders who want to elevate their ability to communicate clearly and even impacted my life well beyond my career into my family life and friendships. This course has had one of the biggest impacts on me out of all the courses I have taken in two years at Haas.
Yes
I highly recommend this class to my fellow classmates who needs some self discovery and struggle with inperson relationships.

Yes! This course made me much more aware of my personal biases, social context, and privilege and how these factors may leave an imprint on others. I have learned how to listen with greater empathy and connect to others amidst differences.

Excellent learning experience in a safe and encouraging environment setting. You will be able to learn different communication and interpersonal skills in first three days and then apply them to the real life scenario. Bluntly, I would not. However, I do think Erica and the co-learners have a wealth of untapped knowledge. Had this class been offered in person or include an office hour component, it would be EXTREMELY worthwhile as the topic is very real-world applicable and something that almost everyone struggles with in various ways.
Less structure will spur greater room for discovery, improvisation, Q&A, and as a result, learning.

highly recommend this class if you're interested in knowing how to self-regulate your behavior when you feel threatened and/or anxious, and how to recognize/describe/share your feelings to others. Human connects via emotions. It will teach you practices on how to address feelings like perfectionism, fear, comparison, self-doubt, and how to connect with other people deeply via feeling words.
Yes!

The readings for pre-HW 1 and 2 were very useful and interesting, definitely eye-opening and enriched my experience, thought very long (each took at least 6hrs). As for the class, the 1st day was extremely cringy and mechanical, it did not feel natural at all, but as time passed by, we kinda got used to each other and started becoming more comfortable with speaking to each other and sharing handles. The classes were too long and intensive, I think such a course would be better if taken over longer periods of time and not all in 1 weekend. On another note, the type of people in this class are the best, all of them are intentionally trying to work on interpersonal connections and emotions, they are emotionally available to be open and vulnerable.

Yes - this was one of my most amazing classes I've taken at Haas. I think that it provides such a depth of personal and interpersonal learning outside of any class. This is not a business class but more so a life class. I think that I learned more about being a leader and being a strong human than any other class at Haas. This class does require you to take it very seriously to get the most benefit out of it plus honoring the effort your fellow students put into it. I would not take this class if you are not committed to showing up. I would take this class if you are looking to learn more about how you can connect more deeply with other people.

I highly highly highly recommend this course. I think it should be mandatory. The amount of connection built among the group in such a short time is incredible, I've struggled with connection and belonging my whole life and this course created a safe place to feel "buoyed" and held by others. This is such an emotionally driven course and some precaution should be taken as there are likely things under the surface that will come up. This course is really counter- culture and goes against the social conditioning we've had our whole lives. We talk about deeply personal things, we focus on deep listening and ensuring everyone feels heard. I can't think of a better example of what Haas stands for than this course, because this is the course that most exemplifies "confidence without attitude". Before taking it, I was interested to get someone else's feedback and shocked to learn that "they couldn't recommend it" because of some things that came up in their course. I feel sad knowing that valuable lessons were not taken away from that experience, because I know Erica would have done her best to encourage connection instead of disconnection. I can't recommend this course enough, it really was a powerful experience. The downside is that it's a lot of effort, these things take a lot of work. The homework is challenging and reflective and you will feel tired throughout the days of the workshop. But it is so worth it.

Yes - this course requires significant energy, but the material is very interesting and fulfilling. I would recommend this course for anyone who wants to have a positive impact on their team (and anyone around them, really), and wants to learn how to advocate for themselves and resolve conflicts for the long-term with mutual understanding and appreciation.

I learned a lot from group practicing where I would never have had the opportunity to practice otherwise. But there're just too many assignments -- before, during, and after classes. Sometimes, I feel overwhelmed by the mental energy put in this class, especially the 2nd week where we had day-long classes for 3 days.

I would highly recommend this instructor and course because to be quite frank, I feel now that I have the tools to improve the relationships I have and to form strong connections with the people I have yet to meet! Erica really allows you to explore and examine the factors that have shaped your identity, and she provides data-driven research related to the emotions that we feel. It's a wonderful class to take, and I truly have learned so many things that I'll keep with me for the rest of my life.

I would 100% recommend this class. This class can really change how to interact with families, friends, and colleagues. I would recommend this course, but I think it could be slightly better in person. Zoom gives way to not paying attention.
Wonderful course and instructor, Erica is great!
Came into this class dealing with some past trauma and some recent trauma, thought this course was just about communication, that's it.

But this course ended up being a powerful experience in which I was granted the rare opportunity to interact with strangers and classmates in a highly structured setting, and also ask tough questions of others. Ended up learning a great deal about myself!

Definitely recommend. After taking the course, I felt I have taken the first step on the journey to love myself before I can love others. This course will ask you to look inside, stretch and be vulnerable so only attend the course if you are ready to do that. The home assignments are huge so be ready for that too.

I DO NOT recommend the course. It could be fit for a psychology program but definitely not an MBA. I signed up for it to build "interpersonal skills" but I have gotten none of that. While the instructor was immersed in the methods and was dedicated to giving students a good learning experience, the content seemed very light and the

exercises/practices felt like a waste of time. I found it very hard connecting what I did during the course to any helpful skill or competence relevant to my journey as a business leader or career person.
The course seems to be overly focused on neurobiology, feelings and emotions, which I personally did not find helpful for my journey in becoming a business leader.
Also, if it has to be taught, then it may be best taught in-person.
Yes. The experiential portion of the class (almost 95% of it) really got me rethink about the way I approach people and life.

I would definitely recommend this course to other students with the caveat that they have to be genuinely curious about the material and content. The course is truly transformative for those that make the commitment to immerse themselves in the course content.

Depending on what stage you are in your leadership or professional development, this class might resonate with you. I went through many practices that were useful and explored concepts I had not done before.
Having said that, I felt we could have package more grounded, concrete learnings in this 2 unit course compared to other similar courses.

Not at all! This course had very little to no substance and was a sheer waste of time. The course description was so different from the content that was taught. this can be described as a breathing, dancing, distressing spiritual class. If you are on the verge of an emotional breakdown, perhaps this class can serve as a therapy session for you. Most folks in the class were surprised by the content. The professor shares some of her childhood memories, her love for dancing and a rock band (BTS) that she adores over and over. I am beyond flabbergasted how Haas even approved this class. It is a total waste for time and money. The only useless class I have ever taken at Haas. It was like being held hostage for 4 days for no reason. Please do yourself a favor by not enrolling for this class.

Yes...she reverse engineers connections. Makes you think of negatives cycles, and defines emotions and how to deal with them. As someone who never took a course like this, and was from a quantitative background, probably the coolest course at Haas I've ever met. Businesses, politics are all about managing relationships and this teaches you about the very human fundamentals of connection from neuroscience and psychology.

This class is a must take. Its short and intense but unconventional and a breath of fresh air among normal MBA classes. Its awesome if you like to stretch yourself socially and develop as well as making friendships and being vulnerable. If there is any part of you that wishes that you felt more connected to people at Haas, please take this course. The stories you hear from others and the stories that you share will create such a powerful experience that cannot be replicated by any other Haas course. I specifically encourage my fellow men at Haas to challenge themselves with a course that tests their emotional intelligence and boundaries. If you identify as a man and struggle with
vulnerability/emotional expression, please take this course and allow yourself to grow.
Trust Erica and her process, and it will pay dividends.

Yes definitely take this class. This is a powerful class that allows you to tap into your deepest emotions in a safe space. I have noted some points which I would like Erica to include in the course. With those included, I would recommend this course
Course materials have included quite a few video clips selections that reflect personal preference but might be difficult to arouse resonance among students
I would aslo like to see more structures of how the concepts and theory relate to the practice.

I would highly recommend it. It is a lot of work, but I have learnt practical frameworks that challenge unhelpful inner chatters/old patterns and regulate my nervous system, which I think is not only useful for leadership but also for personal fulfillment and happiness.
This course is a really concentrated time commitment - you are essentially sacrificing 3 weeks in a row (pre-work, class sessions and post-work)

This class was not really what I expected, I wish we had more practical application to real life scenarios. If you want more practice on being vulnerable and in touch with your emotions, then this class might be beneficial for you. But if you are looking to apply these learnings to your professional or personal life, I do not see much of a benefit. This class is heavily focused on group sessions in which we open up and are vulnerable with each other, but it doesn't go too deep into how we would apply this in real life. For that reason, when it comes to recommending this class, I would say that it depends on what you are looking for.

I highly recommend this course to others. It is a difficult course, yes, but it is the most practical course I?ve ever been a part of and will no doubt help drive the positive change in you and your relationships.

Stanford touchy feely style class. I think this class is very interesting and teaches many interpersonal concepts and practice it, which is very great experience you cannot have anywhere else. But if you take, you need to spend whole week and a tons of reading and writing. This is a demanding class. Also, I feel the class is better in the format of in- person.

Yes! Absolutely yes! This course has been the true highlight of my Haas experience. It was really nice to see how to improve interpersonal skills, build truly meaningful relationships, be vulnerable, have heart to heart conversations. It has a lot of work, a lot of work, but in my opinion, it was necessary and worth it. I got to know 18 beautiful human beings through this course, and I will never forget this experience.

As it stands today, I would not recommend. However, if the class is increased from 2 credits to 3 credits and is spread out over the course of 10 weeks or a full semester (currently it is over two weekends), I would consider it. The workload is extremely heavy and it is difficult to accomplish everything in three weeks, especially on top of everyone's busy schedules. Not only is this taxing, but it also detracts from the value of what you are learning. If you are located in the Bay Area, I would also require that the course be in-person. The current Zoom medium leaves something to be desired. i think this needs to be a required class.. it probably be shortened and doesn't need to be as long.. perhaps havfe class times start at 10am always?

I would whole-heartedly recommend this course to anyone who wants a more scientific approach to leadership communication than the core course. It ranges through a lot of techniques that are backed up with studies and data. These studies are given to the students to reflect on and make a impact on how we present ourselves as leaders, and as people, in difficult situations.

I would not. I think that this class would be a great one-day, 3-hour session. But I do not see value in it being as long and intensive as it is. The workload has exceeded a majority of the core classes at Haas, filled with videos of BTS interviews and music videos and ted talks. I think that Erica is a very passionate and knowledgable professor, but I do not think that I gained much value from this course. The forced intimacy led to numerous triggering moments, including Erica showing screenshots of messages between her and her mother with whom she has a tumultuous
relationship with to the class and crying. Overall, this class is an extremely heavy lift, with little to no value, and will expose you to high levels of emotional distress. Do not recommend.
No I would not.

I would recommend this course to a student looking to get more in touch with their feelings. This course will certainly not be a fit for everyone (both given the time and the course content) but if someone is willing to engage fully, it can be a rewarding course.
yes for someone who would love to know themselves better. but it's too many workloads.

This is a truly unique course in the Haas curriculum. There are plenty of leadership and communications courses offered, many of which are very good. This one has the reputation it has though because it really forces introspection and understanding yourself. Where you come from, your environment, your interactions, and how all of that comes together for who you are and how you lead.
Erica also embodies all that is Berkeley Haas. She has a true passion and connection to what she teaches - its in her core.

With that said, you absolutely get out of it what you put into it. If you do not show up, put in the work in the assignments, and actively engage, you'll probably waste a lot of time and your tuition dollars. If you're looking for a very deterministic outcome or result, you may be disappointed. If you think this will be some version of 'How to win friends and influence people,' you're also off track. As such, this class isn't for everyone.

If you are interested in learning about your social context, how you think and react to fight/flight triggers, discussing core feelings with others using vocabulary and building capacity to handle that, then you'll love this course and you'll love learning it from Erica.

I would recommend this course to students who want to gain more depth in self-reflection, connecting with others, and ready to put what you learned in class practices. It's not just about how to connect or social with others, but about understand ourselves and others in fundamental ways. Overall, I really liked Erica and what she offered in this class, a truly rewarding journey.
Yes, if you want to learn how to be a better listener.

Highly recommended if you want to build better self-awareness and build a strong connection with a small group of classmates and you're willing to spend a good amount of time to it. It's definitely a special type of class, kind of like a group therapy and an awakening journey.
I would recommend the course if Erica makes the tweak on not viewing her work as a fight for freedom.

I would not recommend this class to the average person who isn't open minded and on a journey for personal growth. This is the type of class that you have to give a lot to get anything out of it. Thus, if you are just trying to click the box and get the credits to fulfill your course load, then this is not the class for you. I also found the amount of work was daunting. I was stressed due to the short deadlines and the amount of detail that was requested in a limiting format of being able to express ones self in less than a few hundred words per question. I experienced a lot of anxiety doing the homework. I will honestly say due to these two things I was extremely stressed with this course more than any course I've ever taken in college period. If you are working and have a lot going on this class would be very difficult to balance as far as life / work balance goes.
No! I feel like Conflict Lab is a better course to experience the same concepts in person and with a much lesser workload.

Highly recommend this class. It should be part of the core curriculum. Good leaders are vulnerable and understanding, especially in difficult and sensitive situations, and this class teaches you just that. Of course, knowledge alone is not enough, so practice makes it achievable.
yes and I hope Erica takes some of the feedback and makes adjustments in examples and biases she shares...seems highly skewed and negative on america

Yes, I'd recommend taking this class. This class is the most useful class I've taken in my MBA journey and is one that I will have takeaways that I can apply to all aspects of my life. You'll need to be comfortable with stretching a little bit out of your comfort zone, but it does pay off in the end. I learned a lot about myself through the class because of all the different practices taught and there is a lot of deep reflection about what shaped you. As an FYI, there are times that the purpose of the practices are a bit unclear, but you'll need to trust the process and see where it leads. The class is not very focused on theory or concept, but more on practical skill building so you will be doing a lot of practice sessions with classmates.
Yes I would recommend it to all my classmates

Yes. I would recommend this course. I feel like a toddler learning how to walk first time, guided by Erica. I felt a different mental muscle being practiced the whole time. But people taking this class need to be aware that this is not a therapy session and is not a magic stick to solve any mental problem and issues happening in your life.
Yes absolutely

Yes! Highly recommended. This class helps you better understand who you are and what is your desire. It helps you to learn how to connect to yourself, be authentic about yourself, care for yourself. Through different practices and techniques, you are introduced with a new approach to manage your relationship with yourself and with others. These practices give you idea how to build stronger connections with people in personal and professional settings. Last but not least, this course helps you understand how to be a system leader and co-create the world with others. I would not recommend it if you want to learn anything meaningful. Even the instructor herself could not explain how her class would be relevant in real-world interactions.

I think the course has a lot of value especially for kids coming from cultures or backgrounds in which they don't get to express themselves. Erica is a good facilitator and her course will provide value to them. Thank you for your efforts over the years, especially the last few days.
Yes. This course is worth it for personal growth and introspectiveness.

If you have never taken or engaged with an "interpersonal skills" class before (or reading, workshop, etc.), then this may be helpful for you. However, the online format of the class limits how deeply you can go into practicing the skills you read about in the class.

I would recommend and I recommend anyone planning to take this course to take this with intentionality. It is easy to get lost when taking such a fluffy course and it can be easy credit if you just want to passively participate or can be inspiring if you really want to improve the way you encounter others. The more you put into this course, the more you get out of it. Erica is very nice and helpful!
Absolutely.

Yes. If you are looking for a 2 unit credit load with the right amount of work (not too much and not too little) that is also therapeutic, then this is the course for you. I enjoyed this course and saw it as the right balance to just let go.

I recommend this course to a fellow student. Communication is a very important skillset both in personal and professional life and this is the course you can learn a lot about how to be a better listener and communicator. Communication skill sounds very intangible and something very difficult to develop, but this class is so organized and gives you detailed tips about how we can develop.
yes surely.

Sure. I think there are things every Haas student can learn from this course. If you're interested in understanding that even though we may all have biases or privileges we are all humans and can share emotions and struggles with one another, then this class is for you. The online nature of the course is hard though, so be prepared to be mentally drained by the end.
One of the most overhyped and downright mediocre classes here at Haas.

- If you're coming here because of the " touchy-feely " hype, PLEASE don't. It's a zoom class with only some concepts used from the Stanford class. It's hard to debunk this notion because there is no counterfactual - nobody can attend both Haas and GSB at the same time. Nonetheless, there moments that actually made me think this class is worth it are far and between. Erica uses her Stanford dropout brand very effectively but it creates unrealistic expectations. If you come in, come in with a realistic mindset on what this would be.

- Assignments take 4-6hrs each and there are five of them. On top of that, there are almost no discussions of your responses and the pieces you read in class. I spent 12 hours in the pre-assignments and stopped putting in the effort for the last three assignments as it's simply not worth it if the assignments are so seldomly mentioned in the curriculum. It's like doing a case write-up thoroughly yet have no meaningful discourse of it in class

- Erica keeps everything a secret. She doesn't share slides and actively warn you to NOT practice this or impart what you learn to other people as it is " dangerous " to practice without supervision since it's such a delicate framework. Hint: it's really not. This lack of openness and cult-like secrecy just goes against what I expected. It points to a lack of confidence and substance in the class material itself

- Prepare to watch a lot of BTS (yes the Korean band) videos. People are literally falling asleep at these videos and there are in both the assignments and during class. I personally don't see the merits in watching these, but we're forced to. I just don't think any level of personal infatuation with a band justifies this amount of mandated exposure for the entire class
- Like many other weekend classes, the class starts after the add/drop period, which means by the time you realize you want to drop it after the first session, it will be too late

The verdict: I'm at best neutral/slightly negative on this class because of the above and the fact that it's 4 days (should really be 2 days like the other EW classes). Instead, I recommend " storytelling for leadership " and " leader as coach " which would be much better learning experiences

This is a course that REALLY shows how to embody being an authentic leader. It's novel, funky and deep. You will use your breath, body and emotions to understand much better your leadership style and beyond.
I wish it was part of the core or something. Honestly, this is the type of courses I was looking forward to have in Berkeley.
Can't recommend it enough.
Vulnerability is contagious, go for it!

I think if you are an individual who struggles communicating/connecting this class can be beneficial. The course focuses on your internal self and how to regulate that in a work environment. It was almost like a 4 day therapy session which could be applied to your job. If you feel comfortable with communicating/connecting, you may find the class redundant and long winded.

Yes, definitely. I think these are skills that we don't emphasize enough. More than that, this course has real frameworks that I can practice and takeaway. I don't feel like that's the case in a lot of similar "leadership development" courses at Haas. Truly, one of the most impactful courses I've taken in my MBA.

I recommend this course if you have 4 full days to burn on the zoom class + many hours to spend on the assignment and nothing better to do. This course can benefit from being shortened to one or two days max with concurrent breakout rooms. It would be helpful to have real peer-reviewed research to back up the teachings. Conversation structures taught are mechanical. Students are asked to write down in class and present live (,when under pressure of the spotlight, made up) learnings. When negative feedback was given (by previous students I presume), the instructor chalks it up to 'people don't understand'. I agree in this case that I didn't understand the need for the collective watching of so many BTS videos. On a positive note, here's what I learned to save you the time 1. be intentional and say "xyz, I want to connect with you" 2. acknowledge by saying 'thank you for connecting, abc' 3. remember to ask what's the level of vulnerability was that? 4. check with the quesioner 'what's your intention for asking that question?' (to defuse a situation or understand the true intention. 5. when appropriate, repeat what you heard and try to cover as much as possible and ask ''did I miss anything that's important to you" 6. regulate your breathing and practice Pranayama/Alternate Nostril breathing 7. take breathing pauses and shake it off

I recommend this instructor and course to those who want to further explore concepts around vulnerability, empathy, and authentic leadership through experiential practice. This course delves deep and takes great mental and emotional focus.

Absolutely recommend. This courses touches on "touchy feely" subjects, and is something I think every MBA student should take before going back out into the real world so that difficult but necessary convos on emotions and feelings are had.

Yes. However, I hope that changes are made to the structure. This course is very important for future leaders. Yes, but they should know that it is a lot of sitting and talking, but overall a good course if you lean in What you get out of the class totally depends on whether you want to believe in this and how much effort you put in It's a weird class with mixed reviews. Some people hate the class and didn't get much out of it, but some people (mainly EW and EMBA) found it to be helpful
Talk to other students before taking the class, otherwise it might be a waste of time for you. it's also not a easy 2 unit class. A TON of homework and draining 4 days on zoom.

sections.goodFor: Students who want deep listening, EQ and hard-conversation practice as a counterweight to quant leadership classes, and who are comfortable with vulnerable, embodied exercises.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting practical, applicable leadership tools or a light 2-unit. Detractors call the prep useless, the exercises cringe-worthy, and say Conflict Lab is the better choice.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy for 2 units per critics: 7 assignments, the first 5 taking 4-5 hours each and reportedly never debriefed in class. Pre/post work called excessive; delivered over weekends on Zoom.
sections.gradingBasis: 7 written pre/post assignments plus in-class participation, which the instructor tracked and categorized
sections.redFlags: 2 students: excessive pre/post work never debriefed. 1 detailed complaint that she publicly bucketed students as high/average/low participators and had peers call on the low ones, and was pedantic about cameras.
sections.quote: it's a tough two credits for a soft skill class. The pre/post work was excessive, but the actual class time was valuable... class unfolds more like a remote wellness retreat than a leadership course.
comments: I would recommend this class. It was a really nice complement to so many of the quant-heavy types of leadership classes that tend to focus on content rather than connections. I think what Erica is teaching is resilience and adaptability that is helpful in any sort of work environment and often missing from many management style courses. I would not recommend this course as it is set up now. I feel it would have been a better course done in person because it is a bit touchy feely, which is a nice counter to the business space. it felt like there was a lot lost because of the Zoom dynamic, which reduced the high level of intention that Erica has put into such a beautiful program. Doing this online does not do it justice and doesn't feel like it was worth the investment, unfortunately.
Yes! Erica is wonderful. Great leader, excited to have met her along my leadership and life journey

Erica Peng is not only incredibly empathetic, but also a complete master of her domain and beyond. She brings amazing expertise in her field, and also ties her field into many others that enrich our learning outcomes. She's open, she's kind, she cares for us, and she makes that known. She's a fantastic instructor.
No constructive feedback - this was perfect.

Every leader should take this course, I truly believe that. It helps develop deep listening skills, emotional intelligence, and the ability to navigate tough conversations with empathy. The course challenges you to reflect on your leadership style, understand team dynamics better, and build stronger relationships. The personal stories and discussions create a unique learning experience that fosters both self-awareness and connection with others. Highly recommended. Yes. I learned a lot from the course and left the class with new bonds.
Yes, I would recommend this instructor. She knows how to bring out deeper responses from the students which leads to a better learning experience.
NA

While Erica fosters a supportive and inclusive environment, the workload felt excessive, with repetitive assignments and breakout exercises that didn't always add value. Some embodied practices lacked clear connections to the course material, and key moments of vulnerability came too late to fully shape the class dynamic. With a more streamlined approach and clearer structure, the course could be more effective.

Hell no. Please don't waste your time. You might make the same mistake like me and think this is a good opportunity to complete a 2 unit course virtually over the weekend. But the prep work is not just painful but nearly ABSOLUTELY USELESS. I gained nothing from this class other than a better understanding of what BTS is (which I don't give a crap about and actually semi-dislike after this course). Nothing in this class is applicable in the near world - the professor is caught up in a fantasy of how humans operate and communicate with each other. Most of the things you do in the class is also highly cringe-worthy - you "stand in your dignity" rotating between breakout rooms with other classmates everyday. No one has a clue what to do and what they are actually gaining out of it. The professor is also very pedantic about how you setup your camera. She would continuously pick on students to adjust their camera even when

everyone could clearly see them. She also makes it EXTREMELY uncomfortable for students to participate in class. She decided to show up to class on day 2 and categorize students into three buckets - high participators, average participators, and low participators - and encouraged on the high participators to raise their hands and call on the average and low participators to participate during the session. It was very uncomfortable and I've never seen something like this from a course at Haas. She also showed us a video of her dancing to an entire BTS song and salsa- dancing - again how is this conducive to learning??? I don't need to see this nor do I want to. I'll leave you with this - seriously step back and consider before signing up for this class. Talk to some folks who did this class the previous semester before you do. It's incredibly painful with little to no return.
Yes. Absolutely.
Worthwhile course to increase your influence at work.

This is an efficient course that students can miss, while only focusing on hard skills. If you don't know yourself or have difficulty dealing with daily encounters, I would suggest that everyone join this class. Sometimes we don't realize what we don't know.

Yes with a caveat; it's a tough two credits for a soft skill class. The pre/post work was excessive, but the actual class time was valuable. Good practice with EQ issues that you may not want to bring up elsewhere (how to address a boss/coworker that you're having issues with, how to reconnect with a family member, etc), and you will get closer with everyone in the class. I think Prof. Peng is a good contact to have in general, but class unfolds more like a remote wellness retreat than a leadership course. "Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Communications" would probably be a more appropriate title. Still learned a bunch though, so no regrets.

No, this was the most disappointing class I have taken at Haas. I should have taken "Conflict Lab" instead which was far more practical. The workload is also very intense for a 2 credit course (we have 7 assignments. The first 5 assignments each took 4-5 hours to complete and they are not even discussed or debriefed in class)
Yes, I'd highly recommend this course and instructor to anyone looking for a deeper connection to systems leadership and build a greater understanding of self and limitations.

sections.goodFor: Students with the emotional bandwidth to be vulnerable and reflect deeply, who want real practice at feedback, conflict, reading the room and building trust.
sections.notFor: Anyone closed to discomfort or self-disclosure - students say flatly it will waste your time and degrade the experience for classmates. Also those who dislike long remote sessions.
sections.workloadNote: Pre-work and assignments plus long hours of self-reflection; called a lot of work where you get out what you put in. Sessions mix short frameworks, live exercises, peer coaching and reflection.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; pre-work, assignments and in-class exercises are described, but grading itself is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: One student would only recommend the in-person version, saying 10 hours on Zoom is hard to stay focused for. No other recurring complaints across 15 comments.
sections.quote: Expect to embarass yourself a little bit, step out of your comfort zone and have really deep conversations. If you are not open to these types of experiences, don't take the class.
comments: Absolutely. Erica creates one of the most meaningful learning environments at Haas. Grounded, human, and deeply reflective. This course helps you slow down, reconnect with your values, and lead with more presence and authenticity. It's not just another class; it's an experience that stays with you long after the class/session ends. You notice immediately in your interactions with others, you remember concepts and practices from class, and your practice with the people around you.
This is a life changing course if you are willing to put in the work. It pushes you to self reflect on a very deep level and gives you real practice in interacting in various situations.

I've been working for eight years, and I think taking this class now has a very different impact on me compared to if I had taken it eight years ago. Back then, I had just graduated, full of dreams and ideals, and my way of thinking was very straightforward. But over the years, I've encountered many complex and indirect challenges — especially in interpersonal relationships, whether with colleagues, leaders, or family.

Although this class was short, every simple metaphor in it suddenly helped me understand things that once confused me. For example, the metaphor of the rubber band reminded me of the times when I was under a lot of pressure at work and felt unsatisfied with my own performance. Now, I understand that I need to forgive myself, because I am human, not perfect. I need to accept both the good and the imperfect parts of myself — they're all part of who I am. I want to embrace that imperfect self, give myself space to breathe, adjust my mindset, and then move forward bravely toward the next destination.

Transformational course, if you come in with an open mind, the right level of curiosity, and a desire for personal change. Erica is an amazing instructor and manages the course really well. A bit of research into what touchy-feely looks like for me before I signed up was important.

You should take this class if you 1) are willing to devote long hours reflecting on yourselves and practicing interpersonal skills, 2) are willing to practice vulnerabilities by putting yourself out there and sharing them with your classmates (who you might not know), 3) want to be more conscious about your senses, deeply rooted assumptions / preconceived notions, and how to lead with intuition. If all the above conditions satisfy, this class would be a gratifying experience and has a long-term positive impact.
100000%. This is the type of class that adds true value on an MBA.
Yes! Absolutely. I learned about making deep connections through this course, which is a life skill.

I absolutely recommend this class. It has been the most impactful class at Haas and probably has changed the way I relate with myself and others forever in a very positive way. I truly think it it unique, and I am so so grateful for Erica to put herself out there and guide us through this journey of embodied leadership.
Not unless it was in-person, as even though Zoom is flexible it's hard to to stay focused for 10 hours
I would absolutely recommend this instructor. Erica creates an environment fostering openness and connection that fosters deep insights and growth.

This course is very useful and impactful, specially for those who are open to really different experiences. I got really reflexive while engaging on the practices and also got to know so many amazing people from my class.

Expect to embarass yourself a little bit, step out of your comfort zone and have really deep conversations. If you are not open to these types of experiences, don't take the class. It will be a waste of time for you and will make the learning experiences worse for your classmates.

Recommend in the highest terms! Erica is a highly valued resource of the university and I wish her course could be offered to all students. This course is perhaps the most introspective at Haas and the learnings truly come from your own internal work. It is a lot of work, and you get out what you put in, so don't take it unless you really want to stretch yourself and grow and you have the time and emotional bandwidth to do that.
I would absolutely recommend taking this course - I benefitted from it immensely and think it should be required for everyone. This class will change your life!

1000% yes! This course is transformative if you commit to the work. It's not a passive class; it challenges you to slow down, reflect, and engage deeply with yourself and others. Erica creates a space where you can safely explore discomfort, vulnerability, and growth with peers in ways that connect directly to real-world leadership. The pre-work and assignments are meaningful and build toward a powerful in-class experience. If you're willing to show up fully, this class will change how you lead, listen, and connect.

Every Haas student should take this class. You practice real-world people skills that show up daily like giving/receiving feedback, navigating conflict, reading the conversation dynamics, and building trust. The format mixes short frameworks with live exercises, peer coaching, and structured reflection, so you're not just learning concepts, but you're applying them in the room. It's a course where trusting the process matters. You'll be asked to lean into discomfort, try new behaviors, and debrief what worked. I walked away with practical tools that I now use in everyday life.

100000% YES recommend. These are the skills that will truly impact our career and our lives, as it has everything to do with interpersonal relationships, connection, and how to navigate oneself and others.
Yes, highly recommend. The safest I've ever felt in my whole time at Berkeley to ask questions and voice my true opinions

Yes, I would recommend this course to any student at Haas because I think it will bring to light certain qualities and characteristics about yourself you may not be aware of. The process of being in T-group will warm up muscles that desperately need to be worked in order to develop more effective relationships

I was afraid that ISEL had been too "over-hyped" but I am so grateful I went with my gut and took the course. It is the course that made me feel most connected with classmates, even ones I thought I knew pretty well, and especially those I hadn't known at all. I feel honored to get to know them on a deeper level and I look forward to establishing similar connections with others in the future. I felt safe being vulnerable and taking personal risks in this space. Yes! It takes a few days for the "a-ha" moments to come, but they do!
Yes, definitely recommend. It's an amazing learning about interpersonal communications. Very touchy, very feely. One in a lifetime experience.

The course itself is a worthwhile experience. The in-class learnings and T-group sessions are valuable practical experiences. However, the workload can be much. One one hand the assignments feel like busy work that checks that we did the readings. On the other, most of the readings are valuable and required to get the most out of the class. It's a lot for a 2 unit course so I would only take it if you're committed to putting in the work.

This is a course with an extremely heavy workload. Unless you intentionally want to focus on your personal communication skills, this course might hurt more than help. It can be a transformative experience but one must truly commit 100% and enjoy working on themselves.
Additionally it is very centric on US centric culture norms and so might not be beneficial to those looking to work internationally.

I would recommend this course to other students, especially for those who are struggling with expressing with their own feelings or listen with empathy. There are lots of practice in the class that could help you practice your red brain. And it's a change in the mindset, could have a lasting impact in life.
Yes, I had some good personal learnings and insights in particular from the full-day Saturday. I also enjoyed the readings and found them very relevant to relationship building.

Depends on where the student is in their educational journey. Not for everyone but probably great for some No. This course, as is, does not provide the personal or holistic benefit that the time within it demands. Yes, the course gives amazing tools and opportunities to build relationships with classmates

Yes, I would. We never receive this kind of training on interpersonal skills and self-awareness. I feel like these learnings can be applied in our professional lives and personal relationships. This is an extremely valuable course. Yes, if you are interested in learning more about yourself and how you relate to others.

Yes! This is a must-take course. The skills you learn in this class will help you be a better leader and improve your relationships in all facets of your life. The learnings from this course are invaluable and have the potential to really impact our understanding of ourselves, our leadership, the systems we live in and also shape the impact that we as Haasies will have on the world.
It depends. If someone really has an interest in improving or enhancing his/her soft skills, it would be a good class for them.

ISEL is a good course option for those who want to learn more about how to process one's own feelings. You get out what you put into the course. Engage with all the readings / videos and do all the assignments with a genuine mindset...then you'll feel like you are learning more about yourself. If the course is still given as a weekend intensive, make sure you can dedicate your weekend and mindset to the course. Your experience will largely depend on your preparation and the buy-in of those in your specific T-group. Good luck!
It's a lot of work for the week the class is on but it's 10000% worth it if you want to learn more about yourself and how to interact with others
Yes, however come with an open mind, and a practice mentality first.... you'll get to practice making connection, but you'll keep having to practice that well beyond the end of the course.

Yes, if you are ok with a more unstructured approach. The class taught me some important lessons of life, such as how to share handles, what's the true meaning of empathetic listening, and how to build connections.
Yes, would definitely recommend it. It's the "touchyfeely" class and it really makes you
1) Understand a lot about interpersonal communications
2) Get to know some of your classmates on a deeper level which is great

Just beware, there is a ton of homework before and after the class. Like really a ton. Hope they do something with it It depends. I think the learnings are much diminished in a virtual environment. This must be an in-person workshop. Know that it is a lot of work and plan your schedule around this. If you put the effort and come with an open mind, then yes, you will be able to get some important learning out of this - depends on where you are on your journey. I felt that I knew and practiced much of it before, hence I did not gain a lot, other than being able to forge some better relationship with some of my classmates (which is a worthy goal on its own).

Yes, definitely. This has been the most impactful course I've taken at Haas and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to have done so with this group of my peers. I will immediately take-away significant learnings from this class that I can use to improve my relationships and therefore my life. It has helped me to feel more secure in myself and deepened my sense of belonging in this community. The caveat that I will offer is that you need to be willing to open yourself up to vulnerability in order to get a lot out of this course.

I would highly recommend this course to a fellow student. I feel like I took a lot away from this class, and it was one of the only classes where I think it is 100% worth giving up your weekends. I do think the course would be far better in person and would recommend making sure it is in person in the fall it is if you are debating between fall/spring. I absolutely recommend this course. It is impossible to describe the scope and depth of the learnings I have taken away from this experience. Actually, that word is a much better descriptor for what this course is. It is an experience. Not a course, not a class - an experience. This is the rare case where I stopped caring at all about what might impact my grade. I wanted to lean into the group sessions with my full attention because of the level of personal learning I would get from it. I plan to stay in at least monthly communication with Erica over the course of my career and marriage to make sure I am continuing to practice the communication learned from this class. DO NOT MISS OUT ON THIS OPPORTUNITY! You will not only further your personal growth but also make connections with your fellow classmates in a deeper way than any other course. This is why I came to this program, and I'm glad I stretched myself to be here!

It's like Erica was made for this. She leans on her own identity and the learnings she's experienced in her life as a teacher for us. She distills the class learnings in our conversations so well. The academic learning and practice are integrated in a way that I've never experienced before - this has truly been life-changing. There are stories that I tell myself about my own experience and what I believe others are experiencing. This class has taught me not only to recognize those but to rewrite the narrative of difficult conversations to move towards not only a shared understanding but a more connected and compassionate world.

Ling is so honest, authentic, effective, and astute. Ling shared his own personal stories with us (as handles) and as a participant, that helped me build trust in him. He very gracefully interrupted participants when a learning opportunity had been missed. I felt so safe and supported by Ling. Even more, the coaching comments in the pre-assignments assuaged some unease and fears I had coming in and I felt very seen, heard, and encouraged.

If you want practice in tough, interpersonal situations in a low-stakes environment, and you have the time and determination to really commit to it, then I would recommend the course. If you are not ready to really jump in, or if you want a very data-driven approach, then it might not be for you.

I recommend that every student takes this course--it was life-changing for me as a person and as a leader. Systems thinking and connection are the tools that we have to tackle big challenges like climate change--this course gave me a foundational understanding of those core concepts and how to use them in my interpersonal relationships.

This course was an absolute waste of time. The course is 65% filler material that does not have any substantial impact on your personal growth. The "practice" is stilted and awkward to the point where it is a chore rather than an opportunity for development. Whatever lightning in a bottle this course captured at Stanford did not translate to Haas. Most importantly, this class was not fun. You would leave with almost the same amount of knowledge from reading whatever books are available on the topic and would save yourself almost 40 hours of busywork.

I would definitely recommend this class taught by Erica. Even though our class has met only a handful of times, I am already applying some of my learnings to my current relationships and seeing them improve.
I think everyone should take this course. The skills taught have the opportunity to be life changing, personally and professionally
Yes. It is a transformational course.

Yes, I would because the friendships that come out of it are invaluable. Some of the frameworks and roleplaying are really helpful for future relationships both personal and professional. Be prepared that it is a lot of work and energy investment, and it is not a class that speaks to everyone's personality type, but is a unique Haas experience that I am glad I could participate in.
Yes, depending on the other courses that the student is doing and their personal circumstances (i.e. do they have a current issue connecting with people).
Yes, I developed a lot as an individual, communicator, and leader. The class was hands-on and we used all the readings and theory in practice.
Yes, I would recommend this class.

This is a really excellent course but it really requires you to have an open mind and buy into the teachings in order to get something out of it. I would recommend it to any student who is serious about improving their interpersonal skills. This has been the most productive and purposeful class I have enrolled in at Haas. I have grown tremendously over the course of the class and only just started to more fully understand and implement the tools and learnings I gathered from ISEL. A must take before graduation!
100%! Amazing course! A must-take course for all students.
I would recommend this to students who wants to lean in on their emotions and are ready to open up

Yes I would recommend it. The course is personally and emotionally challenging and can bring you to your limits. I do not "buy" all of the concepts in the course, but definitely had 2-3 fundamental learnings that I can apply in my future personal and professional life. Students taking it should be aware of the high degree of "touchy feeliness" of the class and be willing to engage with that. Overall, it's definitely one of the most interesting and unique courses I have taken in my life.

This class is very important. I learned a lot from it. It also was quite exhausting to go through three 8 hr workshop settings over zoom. However, I believe it was worth it at the end of the day. So I'd recommend. I also have faith in the teaching team's abilities to continue to improve it as we transition back to in person from zoom.

Yes. At a structural level, this was one of the best run courses I have seen where all 4 of the instructors were in synch with one another. It was clear that they had either worked closely with one another before and/or they rehearsed before class.

At a content level, I would dare say this was unequivocally better than the similar core class of Leadership Communications -an-easy-to-understand progression of the curriculum, more practice for students within a similar amount of time, and most importantly, an emphasis on listening and internalization (a critical skill that I am struggling to think is present in other MBA courses).
As for Erica and her co-instructors, it is clear they are deeply invested in teaching the material and in the development of the students.
In brief, I came in as a sceptic, and came out a believer.
I am not very sure. I think the class content is good but there are some moments I feel awkward. For example, the discussion about rank and DEI...

I would recommend this course to students that are seeking to (re)connect with their inner-self and their presence. This course uses unconventional learning methods that may require a major stretch to some students.
Absolutely. This course has been very valuable. It stretches you in essential areas and these aren't stretched in other MBA classes.

Yes, this class is WAY different than any other class you'll likely take at Haas and I genuinely feel the practices and awareness I've built throughout will be carried with me for the rest of my life. The impact is both personal and professional and usability is immediate.
Yes highly recommend, but I would be sure to set the expectation that it will probably be challenging in a way that's very different from what they are used to.

I would recommend this course if it is taught in person (not virtually). Erica's experience in interpersonal skills is second to none. She is an incredible listener, wonderfully organized, and truly passionate about the course's subject matter. She also isn't afraid to switch things up on the fly, which improves the classroom learning experience. The class dives deep into interpersonal relationships, which aren't covered in most classes at Haas. The applied nature of the course means that we get to practice Erica's techniques with other students in a psychologically safe environment. The learning is very applicable to personal and professional relationships. However, the virtual environment is not conducive to this type of class. This class relies on human connection, which is significantly more present in real life than on a computer screen. Zoom creates additional fatigue and also enables more distraction.

I'd recommend the course, but be wary that it is a very large commitment, and the time invested vs. learnings may not be worth it for all. I think it's helped me practice and consciously think about how to better connect with others and build empathy

Yes, absolutely. I would go so far as to say this should be (or at least some version of this) should be part of the core curriculum. Even if students find the content challenging or uncomfortable the long-term benefits are significant. This class was hands down the most meaningful and transformational class of my entire MBA experience. I almost didn't take it because I had heard mixed reviews, especially regarding the virtual format of the class (even after other classes were back in person), but I can't imagine my time at Haas having been nearly as fulfilling and rewarding without this class. The course itself is beautifully designed, with a slow ramp-up with pre-readings and reflections, and then the sessions themselves do a wonderful job of tying together all of these concepts and putting them to practice. I will admit that the course would not have been as rewarding if the other students in my T-group hadn't been so committed to the experience, so it's important to only take this class if you will be willing and able to fully lean into it. I already feel like a much more confident person and that my ability to communicate and make connections with others has improved considerably. I can't wait to start applying these lessons in the real world, in both my personal and professional relationships.
Absolutely. The skills taught a life-changing. I now have more confident to live a happy life. Best class ever taken in Haas.

Yes, I would recommend this course to a fellow student. The written exercises were amazing reflective pieces and I have a ton of amazing tools for giving feedback and connection with family, friends and colleagues.
Yes, this is a fantastic course and is extremely valuable. This is different than all other MBA classes, but it should be required for Haas graduates.

Yes of course, If anybody want to understand real impact investment philosophy, how can create sustainable investment and how practically do all this staff in the class this course definitely suited for that person. Maybe, it really depends on the participation of the fellow peers as well as how much financial background and comfort they have. This class is a hidden treasure but I wish it had an additional lab component to master some of the technical skills and the tools/databases we have been introduced to. This should be a 3 hour course!

sections.goodFor: Only one comment to go on: students who want hands-on portfolio management and impact-investing exposure and can tolerate a course that is still rough around the edges.
sections.notFor: Anyone expecting polished execution or structured training on Bloomberg, FactSet or CapIQ - the sole commenter got no lab practice and says enrollment collapsed to about six students.
sections.workloadNote: Very thin evidence - only one comment. Managing a real portfolio is said to take a lot of work and time; the student wanted an added lab component and more hands-on practice.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - the single comment mentions lectures, speakers and portfolio management, but nothing about grading.
sections.redFlags: Single comment (n=2), treat with caution: severely under-enrolled (~6 students by year end), no lab component, little hands-on practice with Bloomberg/FactSet/CapIQ, speakers not paired with practical tasks.
sections.quote: The class in theory is so great, but the execution was short of my expecations given my classmates were only 5 others by the end of the year.
comments: Yes and No. The class in theory is so great, but the execution was short of my expecations given my classmates were only 5 others by the end of the year. It takes a lot of work to manage a portfolio and learning to do so takes time. I would add a lab component and make sure the class is well enrolled. I would have found it useful to have more lab practice on using resources like Bloomberg terminals, Facset, CapIQ, and the myriad of other resources available to us for this course. But learning is best done by doing, so more hands on experience would have been useful. Highly recommend, but I believe there are much more to improve, like how to apply our skills early on, how each lecture and speaker could be paired with more practical tasks. Despited these, I still learned so much that it changed my way of thinking about how to create impact.
Would expect only base level coaching, only helpful to take if you have not taken other soft skill courses at Haas I would recommend this course I think is very good.

What is a shame (and a constant across Berkeley) is that there is no coordination between the other courses that deal with interpersonal development skills. I wish there were, because would be more effective for students
Yes, you get a lot of practice.

Yes, would recommend it. It's a little less on the "touchy feely" side and more about the practice. I would say the class gives good groundwork for you to be a better leader and coach on the job and gives some very practical tools for that This class was challenging on Zoom, but it's a valuable and useful class otherwise. The scope is focused so substantial learning could occur on the frameworks they teach. I wish the days weren't quite so long (9am - 6pm is tough, and there weren't enough breaks). Great teaching team though.
Great course! Highly recommend if you are interested in becoming a more effective coach or manager.

This class is a great opportunity to practice coaching (and learn what coaching is... aka asking open-ended questions to help coaches arrive at their own next steps, without any opinions/advising by the coach). Great opportunity to practice active listening, gain empathy for other students, and maybe even get some good guidance on a problem you're currently struggling with! In all seriousness, I thought we covered a lot of material and learned useful frameworks in this class, and would recommend it to anyone who's serious about going into the business of managing people (and would consider it mandatory for any future executive coaches/HR folks).
Yes.

NO ABSOLUTELY NOT!!! This is probably the worst class I ever attended at Haas, it felt like mental and physical torture. The teachers have no idea about human biology. A bio break every 2 hours and a 55 minute lunch in a 9 hour zoom session, ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!

I did not find this course valuable - there is only one framework given for coaching, without any backing scientific studies, and no room for alternative methods. The course content itself is probably better off as a 20 min TED talk. There is an extreme burden of outside work for a one-credit class (4 interviews, a 8 page paper, a outside of class hours practicum.)
This course may be valuable if you've had minimal work experience, leading teams/managing people, and want to practice with BECI coaches in breakouts.

Yes, if in-person and deeply patient. The instructors don't know much more than you/ aren't more skilled/ aren't exceptional in this arena, but it's the practice and observation that you'll benefit from.

This is a great class. It is almost entirely practice with lots of feedback. I highly recommend taking it! Yes! The skills are useful for personal and professional situations. Jenny, Susan, and Thomas are great. Yes, I would recommend this course to fellow students who would like to develop their coaching skills or are people managers.
Great for those who want to learn standard coaching techniques.

Depends - it seems to be more of a learning to ask questions course. I had thought it would be more on mentorship and didnt know the difference before I joined. I felt there could be more frameworks/tools taught/real life examples of what works well vs. not (as opposed to those being brought up after a question was asked).
Yes, to be a good leader it is imperative to learn how to be a coach (and not an advisor/mentor). This class sets you on the path to that goal.
This is a great course that everyone who wants be a leader should take. Especially if you want to empower & set your team up for success.
Great learning in 16 hours of time.
YES!! Coaching is a skills we could use in every area of our lives. This was the right amount of time, homework and plenty of practice. Thank yoU!

I would highly recommend the Leader as Coach course to fellow students. The coaching frameworks were really helpful in approaching coaching sessions with a new mindset, helping us focus on practicing active listening instead of the more natural advice giving. The coach/coachee practice sessions were all extremely impactful, and really delivered meaning and valuable practice for everyone involved. I'm definitely going to take away the practices from this course and apply them in my relationships, both personally and professionally.
I would recommend this course. It really helps on some of the softer skills which so many people overlook but are vital to career progress.
Yes. I will recommend. I didnt know the difference between coach and mentor before the class and now I think I am a better coach.
none
Yes, the course is practical and something I can apply both at work and personal settings.

I wish this course was longer. I loved our external coach Shawn! She was so amazing and the practice sessions really resulted in substantial learning. Will keep referring back to this course in my professional and personal life. Skills of coaching very valuable as a "tool in your toolkit". Not for all situations of communication, but where relevant, is incredibly useful and can certainly define the success/failure of your situation.
Yes, this course provided extremely value skills that are applicable no matter what career you are in.
Yes! Very practical application to life outside Haas. Will be immediately useful in my life and career.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in impact investing, sustainability or asset management, with or without an investing background - the hands-on manager selection is called invaluable.
sections.notFor: Students who need a clearly structured syllabus, or who are not genuinely interested in sustainability; one rejects the premise of impact investing in secondary markets outright.
sections.workloadNote: A fair amount of work built around hands-on investing, selecting asset managers, and practitioner speakers; 2-3 say the week-to-week structure and expectations are not laid out clearly.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: Structure and expected engagement unclear from the start, knowledge feels scattered week to week (2-3 comments); format is relatively new; 1 flat 'no' calling secondary-market impact investing 'a joke'.
sections.quote: the class needs clearer structure and learning perspective from the beginning and the expected engagement with the students
comments: I would recommend this class. It's an interesting class with a focused topic, and lots of practical topics and speakers. It is relatively new in its current format, so I think it will get better through time.
Yes great course to learn about sustainable investment and apply it in practice
No. Talking about sustainable and impact investing in secondary market is just a joke.

I would recommend this course to another student if they are passionate about learning the topic. It's a great way to experience hands-on investing and learning about sustainability. The opportunity to select asset managers and hear about what they prioritize is invaluable. The course is a fair amount of work, and you have to be keenly interested in sustainability. I think despite the sustainability lens it is also a great way to gain exposure to the asset management / stock investing world in a hands - on manner.
Yes! Excellent learnings from world-class professors!
the class needs clearer structure and learning perspective from the beginning and the expected engagement with the students
you will learn a lot but the knowledge is kinda scattered around throughout the course, not knowing what's coming at you week-by-week
Yes!Anne & Peter are great to learn from as professionals doing the work in the space. Panos passion on subject matter and research is a great compliment to them both. Great class!

Great experiential learning experience with professors with both deep academic and professional backgrounds Yes! Have already recommended it to friends. It is a great class for folks both with and without an investing background, and especially for those who want to pursue a career in impact investing or related fields.
This course gives a phenomenal look at both asset management and sustainability - for anyone interested in either, I'd highly recommend taking this course.
Yes I would recommend this class. It was a brand new topic for me and although I felt intimidated at first, by the end I felt like I was up to speed and had learned a lot!
If you already have a real estate and/or finance background, YES absolutely. Nancy is a genius and you will learn a lot from her.
