If you don't have any real estate or finance background, I would highly recommend you to take a basic finance class and also Dennis' real estate development class first. These courses will give you a solid foundation to understand the content taught in real estate finance.

I thoroughly enjoyed this course, but it's not for everyone. If you're interested in understanding the mechanics behind real estate investments, how securitization works, and what a REIT is, then absolutely take this course. The profesor is a wealth of knowledge and is easy to learn from. But if you hate finance and never see yourself going into any finance or real estate related field, then this course is Likely too detailed for you. Keep in mind that this course is finance heavy. Yes if you're interested in very deep knowledge of real estate finances - not as much for intro to real estate or personal/home application
Yes. The course is very challenging but you'll learn a lot and Nancy is a great instructor.

Overall, yes. I came into this class intimidated as someone who didn't know much about real estate. But this class, while challenging, helped cement my understanding of some of the concepts we learned in core finance (particularly related to bonds) in a really useful way. The first part of the class is heavy on loan structures and bond math. We spent a lot of time in Excel. For me it really paid to actually read the textbook and skim through the slide deck before class. The second half of the course moved into alternative funding structures and trends in the real estate industry. That was much more of a survey and I was somewhat disappointed to find it less engaging and accessible as someone without experience in the RE space. Many of the guest speakers weren't able to speak to their work in an accessible way. But Nancy is so passionate about this work, and is actively making strides to incorporate more ESG components into this class. I'd recommend it for someone who feels reasonable confident in finance and who is interested in learning more about the real estate space

I would definitely recommend this class for those interested in real estate finance. As someone who did not have a background in that area and who was less interested in real estate specifically, I did find that this class provided helpful and practical examples of how to calculate mortgages, get comfortable with securitization, and know how a REIT is created. Nancy has added in lots of sustainability information, which was super interesting. She encouraged us to do our group project on an asset-backed solar model, right at the forefront of the industry. That said, this class is a significant amount of work, as it has a midterm, final, two homeworks, and 3 cases. I felt like this was one of the most challenging, but also rewarding classes I took while at Haas--one that pushed me outside of my comfort zone! highly recommend for people interested in real estate finance. Nancy is well-versed in this topic and can answer most any question you have. the class will challenge you but is worth it if the topic is of interest/importance to you. Definitely! It is applicable to real estate generally speaking, but also infrastructure finance more broadly. Absolutely would recommend to anyone who would like to enter into real estate. Nancy is very knowledgeable, brings in great guest speakers and applies fundamental concepts to innovations in the real estate industry that will give you an upper hand in interviews.
Absolutely would recommend this course. Great for those with a finance background who want to delve into
securitization of real estate.

Partially. Nancy is wonderful and exceptionally intelligent in regards to the subject matter. But the homework and assignments require an overload of financial modeling knowledge which is not actually taught in class so you end up having to learn most of the information on your own. Great class, but it is difficult and this should be kept in mind Yes, I definitely will. I learnt so much about the fundamentals of real estate securitisation, from bond maths to the structure of an MBS or a REIT. I feel like I will definitely be able to apply the knowledge I learnt from this class to my future work.
Not really. There is knowledge to be had, but the class is a slog.

sections.goodFor: Students serious about real estate or finance careers who want deep technical grounding in mortgages, securitization, MBS, and REITs from an instructor commenters consider a top authority in the field; best taken with bond fundamentals and core finance already solid.
sections.notFor: Those without a finance or real-estate foundation, or with only casual interest in real estate, who will be playing catch-up all semester; the traditional lecture-heavy style and dense material were dull or a slog for some.
sections.workloadNote: Significant and technical, with heavy Excel and bond-math work, a fast pace, and material that requires self-teaching modeling skills if you lack a finance background.
sections.gradingBasis: Assessment included a midterm, a final, two homework sets, three cases, and a group project, with homework and exams described as fairly tough.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (6+ comments): very hard to follow without prior finance/real-estate background. Several (3): lectures are dense and dull despite strong content. One noted assignments demand financial-modeling knowledge not taught in class.
sections.quote: When the Fed, Fannie, or state regulators have a hard question, they call Nancy. She is absolutely cutting edge.
comments: 100% would recommend for any students who are interested in a career in the real estate industry. Some of the course material is difficult, so I'm not certain I would recommend to all students who are not interested in careers in real estate or finance.

Yes, this is an incredible course, no matter your prior knowledge level of real estate finance. I had zero knowledge of real estate and only cursory familiarity with mortgage backed securities. After this class I can have an intelligent conversation about real estate finance.

I'd recommend this course to another student but with a word of warning. If you do not have a finance or real estate background, you will be playing catchup the entire semester as the material becomes very technical and challenging! Yes. It was not an easy class for me, but I think I've learned a lot

Wallace is extremely knowledgeable and thus a great resource. I wouldn't say the class is for everyone though - it is dense and very targeted to the subject matter. It makes it much easier if you're good at math and especially excel. Yes.
I learned a lot in this class. One part to note is that bond fundamentals are essential to this class you should come in with prior knowledge of bond fundamentals or be prepared to learn about it
Yes, similar
Yes. It's valuable if you are interested in pursuing a real estate career.

When the Fed, Fannie, or state regulators have a hard question, they call Nancy. She is absolutely cutting edge. Her teaching style is traditional: lecture lecture lecture, then "any questions." This works for many, not all. The sharpest students tend to find her classes career-changing.

If you are interested in Real Estate it is an interesting class, Nancy is an extraordinary professor, not the most entertaining but she is an expert in the topic. If you are not interested in Real Estate of Finance, the class could be hard to follow.
The lectures are full of useful information but tend to be pretty dull. The HW and exams are also fairly tough. I would only take if genuinely interested in real estate.
Yes I would.
Yes.

Yes I would recommend Professor Wallace and this course. I only have 5 credits left for graduation and if I took Professor Wallace earlier on in the program I would take her other courses. I just think Professor Wallace is a super smart and super nice person that is passionate about helping her students.
Yes

If you are interested in real estate as a career then yes its very applicable. If you are just interested in real estate as a side passion or hobby, then I would recommend real estate development or real estate investments.

Yes. Despite the incredibly long learning curve and very high expectations of each given student (frankly, nigh insurmountable without prior real estate and/or finance background), this has been the second-most worthwhile class I have taken at Haas by a mile. You will learn lots. The pacing is too fast and still manages to go too in-depth, but the content is too good to miss out on. Just know what you're getting yourself into.
If you want a teacher who is an expert, she is the one!

sections.goodFor: Students who want an accelerator-style, learn-by-doing experience pitching an idea, doing customer discovery, and leading a team, and who are comfortable with low structure.
sections.notFor: Students wanting organized instruction; most of this cohort described the course as disorganized, with the two co-instructors visibly misaligned, content crammed into half the term after a mid-semester disruption to the teaching team, and several saying they would not recommend it in its current form.
sections.workloadNote: Workload is uneven; students whose ideas are selected as founders do a lot of the customer-discovery and leadership work for their team.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (4 of 7 comments): disorganization and misalignment between the co-instructors; unclear expectations; poor pacing with material compressed into the back half; team assignment can make or break the experience.
sections.quote: In its current form, I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.
comments: I think this course is very practical and can personally participate in the works of startup, so I highly recommend it. No

Great class to take if you want to experience what a startup accelerator feels like. But know that that comes with less structure and it will challenge you to be a presenter and " sell " your idea. You will also do a LOT of work if you end up being selected as a founder (because your idea got picked as 1 of 10 among 50 or so pitches). You know your product best so you will have to really pull through the weight to do customer discovery interviews and provide real leadership to your team who just joins you mid class. Your group can be make or break for your experience in the class. This class had a lot of potential and failed to deliver to my expectations. Some of it was likely due to the unforeseen circumstances surrounding Kurt's health, but Dave and Shiva never seemed to recover their footing over the remaining 10 weeks, even with Kurt's template. It was hard to believe that this is a course that has been taught for many years, and that both instructors have been involved in previous iterations.

I found the level of disorganization in this course extremely disconcerting. Dave and Shiva seemed to talk regularly but not align. When asked about the difference in their responses, they said it was a learning opportunity for us to learn and evaluate different frameworks, which I would have found more believable if they had shared this upfront. The timing of this course was also off, with a lot of material crammed into half of the course. It would have been far more useful to do Darwin Day in week 2 (like the weekend version with Sharat, which has much more glowing feedback), and then spend the rest of the course working on our projects and evaluating different business models, while having lectures that mimicked the stage of our projects.

As a lecturer, Shiva clearly knows his material, but he always seems to defer to the other instructor in the room, until he's by himself. Dave was very encouraging and also facilitated some great class discussion. I think either of them might have been good as standalone instructors, but the combination just didn't work well.
In its current form, I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.
No
why not? definitely.

comments: I would recommend as long as you have a strong interest in the industry/company that your project is focusing on. Yes, applies the design thinking framework in a very practical setting. I really enjoyed working on a real problem that a real company faced.

No. This course has more work than 2 other electives combined. Unless you truly love design thinking, hard pass. You waste a lot of time in weekly plenaries that aren't all that informative and this course drags on way longer than most other classes.
I would recommend this course if you're interested in diving into Design Consulting with real clients, real problems, coming up with real solutions.

I would recommend this class for people who are interested in applying design thinking process and are passionate about learning about one of the particular clients as you get to work immersively on a client's project which entails a real business challenge they're solving. There's some overlap in this class and fundamentals of design thinking, but I enjoyed taking them in the same semester so I can reinforce my understanding of the course.

For better or worse, it's an unique experience. It take time to get use to it at the start but the process is fun and lighthearted. Focus on the team project aspects of the class. lectures are usually hit or miss.

Yes, Haas@Work is an amazing experience, especially if you're looking for a deep dive into design thinking or if you're looking to go into product management! I really enjoyed how we worked with real clients and were able to form full- fledged solutions for their very real business problems. Would 100% recommend.

Yes, but be aware the level of effort that this class requires. It is NOT a class you can BS or hide in, you should be prepared to work a good amount outside of this class. It is an AI course afterall so I understand why the LOE is high, but this class felt like a lot of work. I think it was worth it overall, but I do have some reservations. It was good client facing experience, and I learned a lot about my client, but there were definitely a few lates nights spent on assignments.
Recommend. Heavy workload, but being client facing and very project focused keeps your work ethic somewhat active while you slack off and atrophy as a student
Yes, because it teaches you how to work amidst ambiguity, adjust to different working styles, and solve complex problems.
The course experience may be a hit or a miss.

In my experience. 2/3rd of the problem statement we received was completely out of the scope of the kind of work that's best-done by design thinking. Hence, we spent a lot of time sifting through the problems, and the teaching staff, instead of revising the problem statement, was intent on "fitting" the non-applicable solutions to those 2/3 of problems. That resulted in a lot of wasted time and effort.

The class organization is also VERY hierarchical under the project leader. So, contrary to the class description of the project leader being first among equals, the project leader is treated as more than equal when there are critical client conversations, such as the problem statement example above. The project leader is also the only one with a line of communication to the client. It was left to the project leader to include or not include other team members in client discussions, so there was a lot of monopolization of these client communications even though this is phrased as a project where "students work with clients," most of the team (except the project leader), close to zero client interaction outside of the presentations at various checkpoints.
Definitely yes! It's not easy to get through the whole course, but it's worth to take and push yourself to think more and do more to the real business world.
yes

I would highly recommend Haas@Work to anyone who has a hard problem to solve at work or in your personal life. This is a wonderful framework and combined with real world clients, it is a valuable experience. It is a great tool in your arsenal. Be ready to be uncomfortable and brace ambiguity as your friend

Good for getting consulting experience. Will have a really hard time if you are not bought into the Chaos of Design Thinking. I feel its like rolling the dice, if you get a good project and a good team, you can learn a lot. But, be prepared to be frustrated a lot. But, if you are into Design Thinking or Consulting, definitely an opportunity to get real world experience. Also, as with any course, you will really get what you put into it. Being a team lead is a great opportunity to practice your managerial skills.

I would recommend Hass@work for anyone interested in getting a client-facing experience. There isn't substantially more content to learn beyond the fundamentals of design thinking class, but the learnings from applying the theory to a real-world business problem are substantial.

The course was extremely effective in providing a taste of how consulting in the real-world would look like. I loved the frameworks the class provides around the design thinking process. I loved the open-ended vagueness of the class as well. As with any other experential class - the class will give you in return all that you put in. It has also helped me become a more effective leader leading a large diverse team. Definitely recommend the class to anyone interested in consulting and/or product management.

This course is great at providing experience and exposure to innovation consulting. It is both an innovation project and a client engagement. There is a lot of work, but in the end students gain valuable experience on the process and how it applies in a consulting context.
Extremely practical and applicable to the real world

Yes. The course is a great opportunity to practice business skills, and it is highly applicable to future work experience I do not recommend this class unless: (1) you really want to work for one of the clients, (2) you absolutely need something like it for your resume, or (3) you already have lost faith in your classmates and Haas as a whole. This class singlehanded made me go from optimistic about my time at Haas after my first semester to souring on my classmates and the whole Haas system at the end of my second semester during this program. I learned very little in this class, the workload was hugely disproportionate, and the process of "learning innovation" was disappointing. My classmates abandoned me. They will abandon you. If you care, don't take this class. The clients were OK though.
I would only recommend Haas@Work to students who are very interested in design thinking and are prepared for a lot of work with unclear payoffs.

I believe that the class needs some improvements. One is that the class needs to be configure to be a learning hub, we take this class to learn, not to work for a company. I believe the incentives are not really align between the class creators and the student's needs.
Other than that, if you come with an open mentality, you will find it very interesting and you will get to work with an amazing team of peers that will surprise you.
I would recommend the course if individuals are interested in design thinking as a career. Otherwise I likely would not recommend it.
Yes
Yes
Yes, the course was very useful in learning to turn innovation and ambiguity into something understandable using a process based approach. 10/10 would recommend

Yes I think it was great experience getting to work with a client and employ design thinking in an ambiguous space Although most of the Haas@Work instructors are kind people, this class yielded very little technical learning. Instead, it resulted mostly in the frustrations and headaches that come with doing one giant, semester-long group project. No, unless you want to practice Design Thinking without taking on an internship. Not all clients are a good fit for design thinking solutions, and this makes the course challenging. My client was not a good fit for design thinking because it is a very conservative organization. A quantitative approach would have been more effective in building business cases for them.
Yes - it's a rare opportunity to challenge yourself and dive into a design thinking framework with a real-world client while still having the support of experienced coaches and faculty.
I somewhat recommend this course to anyone without any consulting experience.
Yes. Good way to turn theory to practice.
Yea for sure.

This class is very much group and client dependent, which makes it hard to recommend overall. If you are set on going into innovation and design consulting, than you may want to consider this class, but you may be able to explore other ways to get this experience. I think this class is a great concept, but the execution needs help at this time. I wanted to like this class more than I did.
100%. This course is great for those who are engineers and think they lack creativity
Yes, direct experience in client and project management
Would recommend, as have the opportunity to work with a leading company in the industry and gain real life practical experience.

Haas@Work is an excellent course to learn client management, design organization, and project management in a real environment. While it can be frustrating at times, it all makes sense in the end. If you get Jeff as your team mentor, you won.
Yes! All instructors are amazing!

Course gives a good overview of design thinking and innovation concepts. The client project are of mixed levels of interest. So you could get lucky or end up with a dry project. However, either way the learnings are solid and there is often food provided.

Absolutely loved my team and this class as a way for me to learn how to solve difficult client problems and work with my team to clearly define the problem. We were glad to have the GSIs and the instructors guide some of the way but this the strength of this course is working in a small team and understanding team dynamics with a challenging problem.
Yes, even though the class loading is relatively high and requires students to spend more time and efforts, the payoff and feedback from the client during the presentation is super rewarding.
This is a must take course. You get real world experience in a very collaborative environment.
I would recommend. It?s a great opportunity to learn and practice design thinking to real world problems. I just wished I had a wide variety of projects to choose from.
Yes, very insightful hands on work experience working with people from different backgrounds on real problems companies are facing

Yes! This course is a crash course on how you can come up with innovative solutions to any problem and thrive in ambiguity. It was one of my favourite courses this year and is full of really incredible people. The course staff are so insightful and supportive.
Yes: no pain no gain. Hard work pays off in this course

High recommend.

Yes - this was a super valuable experience that's you can't find from most HAAS classes.
Yes; interesting experience working with a client. Great team building. Good opportunity to learn design thinking frameworks and learn tools to approach problems from a different perspective.

David is absolutely a wonderful instructor to have and learn from. Just expect the course to be more of a consulting style project and have appropriate expectations.

One of three projects in my year was great- the other two had client issues. I think that the learnings offered by the course are mostly derived from intuition and common sense. The real value is in the team and having fun, eating dinner, seeing your client excited about their work again.
100% recommend Jeff. You will be lucky to have him as a coach. Jeff made this innovative framework easy for someone like me with zero experience

Yes i would recommend this class. I would recommend if they are wanting to learn more about a new industry or topic and work in a team. This class is not for folks to want specific consulting experience because it is not really about that. But it's a great way to dive into a topic and learn fun things!

This has been my favorite class at Haas so far. I made friends through it, expanded my network, got great resume points/interview story, and was just a lot of fun. This is the best applied innovation class because you really get something substantive from it, but it's not as much work/stress as the other applied innovation courses. Yes, though I would emphasize that this course is pretty dependent on the project you get. No, not really because they are ample of other AI course that can be a better use of your time. In terms of learning, these concepts can be learned in other classes as well.

Yes

Yes - hugely applicable, great frameworks, repeatable process
Yes

Great for someone that is looking to gain experience in engaging with clients

Great course. Highly practical. Good learning experience if you want to know how to present or interact to clients. It is not a direct consulting class, but if u have 0 prior experience this will give a good introduction. More a framework class to understand design thinking.

I would recommend the course. It's a great process to go through and understand. But caveat, if people are not bought into the project, it can be hard work. I'd encourage team buy in from the beginning

I would definitely recommend the course.
I got a lot out of this course. I had fun, I learned a lot.

8 times out of 10, I would absolutely NOT recommend this course to a fellow student, unless they indicated to me that they would benefit from going through the type of consulting project that this course offers. Haas@Work is a signature course at Haas for a reason and brings human-centered design and innovation principles into practice with real clients. The class combines consulting, product management, AI, strategy, and client work together in a hands on class. Even though it meets in the evenings, I found every class to be valuable time to work with my team and learn consulting and innovation skills that apply in any job context. I loved this class and highly recommend it, although it is a fair amount of hands on work with the internal team and client!

I highly recommend this course to anyone looking to work in the consulting industry. It involves real client needs and helps solve their actual pain points. The entire process closely reflects what real consulting work is actually like. Yes, absolutely; it was very hands on and helped me develop tools for dealing with ambiguous problems and helped in understanding how to " trust the process "
I probably wouldn't recommend the course. With the rise of AI tools today, I feel like part of the course's value proposition has become less compelling

Yes, I would recommend both the course and professor. rows.title: Systems Change for a Small Planet

comments: This is a feel good class, relatively low lift- very soft skill. Good if you want to learn about how to help the world with your specific skills

This was definitely one of the most impactful courses I've taken. Don't go into it expecting to learn a specific tool, process, or skill. Go into it with an open mind and find comfort in the ambiguity. This course is definitely just part of a larger process we go though. 10/10 would take again

This is the most inspiring class at Haas by far! It was a breath of fresh air in the midst of every other traditionally academic classes. The professors helped me rethink my purpose and meaning and redirect my efforts to my next big life step. My favorite Haas class by far.

I would recommend this class because it's unique in the Haas MBA architecture. There aren't any other classes that allow you to zoom out and think in this way. However, if you're looking to build more technical skills this isn't the right class.

Yes, this course is what I hoped grad school would be. It gives you space and material for reflecting on your values and worldview. It has helped me explore a theory of change and outlook for how I want to impact the world post-Haas. I overall really liked the class and how different it was compared to all other classes I've taken here. I think I expected more concrete examples, more lecturing from the professors at first, and something to just make the class "stick" more. Maybe concrete strategies for how to become a more effective beyond capitalism leader? I also think more concrete lecturing from the professors were helpful to bring it back to a framework. The most impactful things I learned were the two loops theory and the concept of donut economics, so the more tangible things we can leave with students, the better.

Yes, but I don't think it's for everyone. If you are self-aware and open to checking your limiting beliefs and assumptions, I think you'll get a lot out of this! But fair warning: it's more of a playground or sandbox to grapple with how we live our lives individually and collectively rather than a lecture based class that will impact lessons upon you Not in this current format for most students. If you want unstructured reflections and a place to build connections and explore big systems, this is the class for you - but I think most people wouldn't leave with any new tools or concepts. The professors are incredible and kind, but they are lacking real concepts and cases to help ground the class. I truly believe this class can have a big improvement!

definitely, this is such a unique course in the MBA, and I think it resonates so well with the type of leaders Haas is trying to build. So much of our life is structured and linear, and it is so special to have the space and opportunity to think non-linearly and think about how we can exist within the system, yet change the system at the same time. I really hope that the theories and frameworks make their way into the rest of the Haas courses so that its not just the students in this class who are exposed to these ideas.

Taking this class will likely change you. It made me learn things about myself, how I think and how I interact with the world, and gave me new ideas to reflect on whenever I think about societal change. It is not a very applied class, I'd call it more philosophical, but I'd recommend everyone taking at least one class in this style during your time at Haas. The only thing is that I wish more people from "traditional MBA career interests" were taking this class too, to get more different opinions during the discussions.

I would recommend the course, with some warnings: the course does not teach an actual application, it does not teach you how to change the systems. It is mostly self-reflection on how you want to show up in the world and what you want to do. It gives space to research anything you are passionate about and learn about anything that you are passionate about. I loved my 3 hours in the class every week, but I am not sure I learned anything applicable. Yes! This class brings forth why I came to business school in the first place. It gives the structures if how to be a better, more community driven leader and gives space for reflection and introspection in a way that I hadn't explore before I would recommend this course! Professors really care about the topic and the students, is super dynamic and makes you reflect a lot on the current system and how could it be better. Sometimes it felt a bit messy with not very clear objectives but that was part of what the professors wanted to teach, not always follow the same structure.

I would recommend taking the course in conjunction with courses that have more links to research and practical applications. It's nice to provoke thought but if it's your only course in the area you may feel dissatisfied with the lack of utility.

I was very excited to take this course after it being highly recommended, but was very disappointed in how this class was structured and taught. It wasn't clear how the readings translated into actionable ideas/steps, and we often spent time critique other's work without any tangible ideas on how WE would do it differently. I wish there were more forums for students to express dissenting opinions from the status quo of the class. It felt like an echo chamber with no actionable takeaways and structure. I would not recommend taking this course unless it is more well-thought out and applicable.
Transformative class, so inspiring and thought-provoking
The class had great potential but I'm ending it feeling I have nothing to show from the course besides selfishly enjoying my own time. No takeaways to improve the world
Absolutely yes!! The most important class at haas

sections.goodFor: Students wanting a reflective, values-oriented break from the MBA bubble - questioning capitalist assumptions, personal growth, and frameworks for dominant versus emergent systems.
sections.notFor: Anyone after practical systems-change knowledge (crash course, cases, implementation, pitfalls) - one points to the 1-credit Systems Change course instead - or averse to touchy-feely reflection.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (6 comments). Reflective, discussion-driven work; one student says instruction was unclear and assignment expectations ill-defined. No hours or assignment cadence given.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - one student says assignment expectations were ill-defined, but nobody describes how the grade is determined.
sections.redFlags: One of six says the course was under-thought and poorly delivered, with unclear instruction and ill-defined assignment expectations. One would condense it to 2 credits with more actual systems-change content.
sections.quote: If you are just looking for system changes knowledge (i.e., crash course, case examples, how to implement, pitfalls, etc.), then this class is not for you
comments: I'm so glad I took this class - it was such a breath of fresh air in business school. This class really challenged my worldview and self-view and truly nourished my soul.

Yes - I absolutely loved this class. It was so different from every other class I've taken, and was a much needed breath of fresh air to reflect on my values and how they are aligned or misaligned with how I am living, and how we are all encouraged to live in modernity. The class gave me some really useful frameworks to think about systems change and my role in dominant and emergent systems, and how to promote systems change. I really really loved this class. I would not. The course was a good place to reflect on bigger systemic issues and provided meaningful opportunity to reflect on my place and role within those systems, but the course overall was under thought and poorly delivered. I do think the course has potential, but instruction was generally unclear and expectations around assignments, expectations, etc. were generally ill-defined and again, poorly delivered.

Yes. As a business school student, this could be the most important course you take during your time at Haas, especially if you open yourself up to the questions and discomfort that will arise from it.

It depends what you want out of the class. If you are just looking for system changes knowledge (i.e., crash course, case examples, how to implement, pitfalls, etc.), then this class is not for you and would recommend looking at the Systems Change 1-credit course that's offered. Now if you are looking for that + a touchy-feely course that is different than anything else you've taken at Haas, let's you spend time to reflect (vs go-go-go that bschool is), and grow as a person (vs student, corp ladder climber, etc.), then this course if for you. It was a breath of fresh air and a safe heaven. I'm glad I took it, but also would have been glad if it was condensed to a 2-credit course and focused more on systems change knowledge, implementation, etc.
Yes! Even if it isn't being offered again, this class really helped me step outside of the MBA bubble and question a lot of the business / capitalist oriented thinking that Haas embodies.
Yes 100% recommend - this was one of the most intellectually expansive and introspective classes I have ever taken and would recommend it to everyone.
100% the best class and best professor I've had at Haas so far in my MBA journey. Got my tuititon's worth after this course!

Yes, it is a great class especially for the students who have interests in new venture capital. If the student invested more time into the class, definitely, the student will learn more from the class. The guest speakers part are super great and there are tons of speakers invited for the class.
Yes, good content
Please refer to my previous comment. I would truly take any future class of hers.
This is a great introductory course on how to finance new ventures through a variety of vehicles (VC, Angels, Search Funds, etc.). Really a fantastic and manageable class.

This class doesn't jump too deep into theory, but is great for first-time founders or entrepreneurs. A lot of the items covered are the "soft" aspects of entrepreneurship and seeking VC funding - like how to negotiate term sheets and how to raise money. There isn't really a "finance" element to this class as the only math is centered on constructing cap tables and payouts. The examples are rather simple to introduce concepts.
Yes, It gives an overview of what you should do to finance your venture.

I would recommend Maura as an instructor because she is engaging, experienced and her passion for teaching others comes through in every aspect of the NVF class. The information she teaches is so relevant and deep and it is provided in a way that is incredibly helpful for someone like me who wants to start a company and raise venture funds in the next few years. She focuses on key information (like, you should plan to raise 2x the amount of capital and assume it will take you 2x longer than you anticipate) and also shares incredibly engaging stories from her real world experience during each class.

I would totally recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. The class resulted in substantial learning not only through traditional methods (readings, slides), but also through great speakers that shared their insights. Absolutely - one of the most informative and relevant courses in entrepreneurship and finance at Haas
Yes. Maura is fantastic. Don't take the other New Venture Finance or you'll regret it, no doubt. This one is a good amount of work, but worth it.

If you are an entrepreneur trying to understand how to sustain your business, this is a valuable course. Likewise, if you're an investor (or an aspiring one), this course provides exposure to the broader financing environment outside of your specialty. If you're pretty experienced in either of these, though, this may not be the class to get the latest techniques — it definitely hits the highlights. This course can also serve as an intro to venture funding as well for the uninitiated. At times, I felt like the course could be shorter — but the bulk of the benefit comes from hearing from the guest speakers.
Yes - but caveat that the group project was a lot of work / tough to pull together
Yes. The course is extremely applicable to future entrepreneurs.
Yes! If you're interested in entrepreneurship of venture capital it is a must.

Yes, because finance is one thing. How to negotiate a term and a solution with another party is a different thing. This class can give you the knowledge of what common terms people use nowadays and what you should think about as an entrepreneur.
Yes, I highly recommend this class

Yes, 100%. I learned a lot in a short amount of time through the course and felt like the workload was enough to emphasis the key concepts that Maura felt were most important to take away from the class without being
overburdened with work. I enjoyed going to class each week.

Absolutely. This course is great if you want to work or be involved in some way with the startup world. The class helps you learn how to setup a term sheet and understand all aspects of a deal with a VC

Yes!!! Most definitely! It was probably one of the best classes I've taken. The content was extremely engaging with a strong mix of activities, cases, speakers. I highly recommend if you are even remotely interested. Despite the final project being daunting, it is an amazing way to network with potential VCs and other funders!
Yes, I would recommend this course to anyone excited about entrepreneurship or VC

Without question!! This was one of my all time favorite courses, and I was shocked to learn that it's relatively new. It makes me feel sorry for any founder who attended Haas before this class was offered!
Would definitely recommend Maura. Maura brings her five-decade experience in this field and presents it with great style and clarity.

Absolutely, this is one of the capstone classes and a must-take for founders and non-founders alike. Super high- quality guest speakers, one of the best professors at Haas teaching you essential knowledge for any bay area workers. I highly recommend this course to students regardless if they have plans to fundraise for their company in the future. It helps to just understand the different stages, methods, and how early choices you may can impact your relationship with investors later on etc. The course leverages a mix of forums from cases, guest speakers to group projects that reinforce the learnings. Super interesting!
Great course if you want to start your own venture! Very valuable lessons in Venture financing which will be super useful in real life.
Absolutely, best course I have taken so far.
YES

No I would not recommend this class to others. It tends to assume that students have a significant interest in entrepreneurship (I took it hoping to get more content on the perspective of VCs, like how they evaluate companies). And while we did get some of this through the final project, I found it to be a waste of time that we had to interview 12 investors - after about 8 I feel like we were hearing the same thing over again. Having to then edit it into a video and watch everyone's video in class was also a waste of time - it should be that each group puts together a deck with the insights and shares how they approached the conversations and how the conversations evolved as more interviews were completed. I had also heard good things about Maura, but I honestly don't think she was one of the top professors I've had. A lot of the insights seemed based in her own personal experience as opposed to broader theory/insight gathering and the teaching felt kind of chaotic/not clear on what the topic of each session was going to be and what the takeaway was.
A journey through the world of new venture financing. Extremely engaging lectures and guest speakers. One of the most practical learning experience at Haas that's relevant and current.
Yes. It is a practical course for whoever is interested in venture capital and startups.
Yes

Maybe - if you're really new to entrepreneurship and the fundamentals of fundraising. I came into the course thinking I'd learn more about the quantitative stuff and takeaway hands-on tools that VCs/founders need for fundraising. Instead, it turned out to be mostly a series of theoretical and qualitative lectures around 'how to do entrepreneurship and fundraising right'. I learned more from doing the final take-home exam than I did in all of the lectures! Maura is one of those amazing people that teach many contributing topics that support the primary topic. She is the most compelling instructor I have ever had, and I would recommend any class she teaches on any subject. She stretches us to grow in terms of ambition (what can we hope to solve for the world), ethically, and in terms of output. When we might tire, her example pulls us forward. Her generosity of spirit and generosity giving her time, opening her network to us, and sharing her insights is greatly appreciated and inspires us to want to give back in turn. Yes. Absolutely must take if you are working on a venture or planning to start one in the future
Yes. It serves the objective of the course well, and the readings, cases, components, projects, and assignments do a good job giving us the required know-how of venture financing

Yes, I would recommend this class to a fellow student. The class is inspiring and relevant. The project assignment was also beneficial to investigate your interested segment. The class is also focusing on the every day entrepreneur and see entrepreneurship as a learning process.
Must take if you want to understand VC space and listen to Great Speakers
100% if you are looking to learn about raissing capital as an investor

This is almost my favorite class which provides me with deep substantial learning! You cannot miss this class if you would like to pivot your career as an entrepreneur or at least learn something about how entrepreneurs raise money. I will 200% recommend Maura O'neal as a professor that you should take during your Haas experience. She brings you along every single minute of class and has a humble and human demeanor that is impressive.

This class in incredible. As a full-time MBA, it was absolutely worth giving up 8 Saturday mornings to take the course with Maura and Paul. They are both incredibly accomplished and well-connected on top of being engaging and effective teachers. I highly recommend this course for any student who aspires to be a startup founder. You will build a cap table and exit waterfall, practice negotiating term sheets with VCs, learn how to protect yourself when you sell your company, discuss how to split equity and responsibilities with your co-founder, consider when to pursue non- dilutive capital instead of equity, and absorb many words of wisdom from seasoned entrepreneurs. The main course project is to interview 12+ investors in your industry of interest, which is an amazing excuse to proactively build your network.
This is the best class I've taken at Haas. I learned substantially about the VC industry from a founders perspective. Protect your board seats!
Yes! Super informative!
No, lots of unnecessary of work that doesn't result in substantial learning.

Yes, but the learning will not be substantial... some basic terms on a term sheet like liquidation preference and types of shares... she rambles alot, limited structure in the class and inserts her politics into class.

On a number of occasions she went on mini discussions on how privileged white men are. On one occasion she went to a white male student (Spanish exchange student) and said in front of the class, whats the first thing you think when you see a female interview applicant? Then answered her own question by saying "its that she's a women and less capable isn't it... isn't is?". He responded with "no it is not" and she laughed it off and kept going. On other occasions she brought a guest in who was Indian and began his career in the 1970's and kept going on how white men discriminate in hiring... on another occasion went on about how much of modern medicine is racist because many of the studies are based on white samples and do not match medications to the biologies of minorities.
After the first few weeks I came to expect a politics more than skills - I felt if she focused on teaching contracts, valuations, and term negotiations more, we would have benefited as a class more.
I would recommend for anyone looking to work in startup environments, tons of valuable info on early stage finance. Yes

Maybe. If you are doing the VC PE course, all of the material is covered there (and arguably goes into more detail). The main difference between the classes and what makes it worthwhile is that this class is from the POV of the founder, whereas VC PE is from the POV of the VC. Speakers are generally great. Classroom experience is generally a bit chaotic and the VC project gives you a lot of exposure to the industry.
Great class! Sometimes the speakers didn?t show up or there ere some technical issues that were distracting but overall loved the class, worth my Saturday mornings

It would be a better fit for students who is working on a startup or expected to start a new company. The course was thorough, rigorous and well structured. There was a good balance of theory and practice, which was extremely helpful. If you're looking to start a business at any point in your life, take this class. The course assignments were particularly useful, even though they were quite time intensive. Maura brought in wonderful guest speakers who were also a great value-add to the learning.
Absolutely recommend taking this course for anyone interested in understanding what are your options for funding when you re starting new venture
Yes!

NVF is probably one of the best courses to take early on in your Haas journey. It's a great cross of all things entrepreneurship, while providing critical insights into the financial & governance aspects regarding investors. Maura as a professor is passionate and knowledgeable, and taking this course will certainly inform future Haas elective selections whether its Search Funds, VC & PE, or any other entrepreneurial or finance courses. With that said, do not underestimate the investment of time that is required to succeed in the group project of cold-calling VCs. It will take a lot of time and energy, absolutely start early.
Yes! Highly recommended for anyone who is interested in becoming an entrepreneur & going into VC.

Great course to understand fund raising from founder and investor's perspectives. Each class had case study and guest speaker, which gave insights into real-world challenges and negotiations that are part of fund raising.

This is a must take course if you think you'll want to finance your venture at some point in life. I loved the team project which involved interviewing many investors (really acts as cement for all the learnings), loved the guest speakers. Amazing instructor, very useful course.

Yes. This was a great course for those that do not have experience in VC and new venture finance. It would be great to spend more time on the math and spreadsheet modeling so this can be reinforced as we glossed over it.
Highly recommend.
Yes!

I do recommend this course to a fellow student. However it is important to consider that the class is very interesting- engaging-useful if you don't have any background on Venture Finance (VC, Search Funds, Angel Investment) because you will have the opportunity to learn broadly what they are about. I really loved that the class was
Founder/entrepreneur focused, but I can understand that for those folks that are more interested in the VC dynamics might felt that the class content was not comprehensive or very detailed.
I took the class with Maura O'Neill and she is great!, Very well connected, a lot of experience in the industry (both sideds investor and entrepreneur) and great teacher.
Yes, I would recommend this course due to its extreme usefulness on anyone planning to take a venture from concept to an exit

If you are a founder or going to eventually be responsible for interactions with VCs in any manner, this class is a great way to do a high-value (2credits) with lots of context. The VC math (shares and pricing, etc.) is covered, but not extensively -- so if you're looking for a hardcore VC math class, you might want to add on another finance oriented class.
Overall, I found Maura wonderful to learn from and would recommend this class for anyone doing anything early stage.
Good instructor, but needs to improve slide content and class materials.

Yes! This was one of the best courses I've ever taken in terms of learning and real world application. I was really pushed out of my comfort zone in a great way. I understand the art of negotiation between founders and VCs as well as within the startup environment much better now. The guest speakers and final project were awesome.

sections.goodFor: Current or aspiring founders who want fundraising from the founder's side: term sheets, cap tables, negotiations, guest speakers, and direct VC access through the interview project. Repeatedly called a must-take for entrepreneurs, powered by Maura's practitioner experience.
sections.notFor: Students with prior VC experience or who have taken the VC/PE course will find substantial overlap, and those wanting rigorous VC math or a tightly structured classroom should look elsewhere.
sections.workloadNote: Widely called heavy for a 2-unit class, arriving in waves, driven by case prep and a time-intensive final project interviewing 12 or more investors.
sections.gradingBasis: Casework, term-sheet negotiation exercises, readings, and a final group project built on 12+ investor interviews; several students said assignment weights and due dates were poorly communicated.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (8+ comments): chaotic or disorganized structure, unclear assignment logistics, and weak slides. Recurring (5+ comments): workload too heavy for 2 units, with the 12-investor interview project hitting diminishing returns. Several (4+) said it adds little if you already know venture finance. A couple of comments objected to political commentary in class.
sections.quote: Be aware, the class is chaotic but embrace it and you will enjoy this class. If you must have structure, this isn't the place for you.
comments: I would recommend it if you're interested in learning how to think from a founder's perspective. The workload is heavy at times, and comes in waves. The class time isn't as interesting though Maura is great.

Maura is an experienced practitioner with deep expertise in the industry. She came up with very creative exercises in class, such as mock negotiations between VCs and startups, that I found very comprehensive and great learning. Venture financing and capital continues to be an evolving industry, and it was very fun taking the class during a rate cutting cycle and Presidential election. With all the uncertainty in the following months/years, students came up with very complex and niche questions. Maura welcomed these, was very patient even if some questions derailed her lesson plan, and most importantly, had a fantastic, in-depth answer to each. Oftentimes questions were simply, 'where do you think this is going', and Maura absolutely knocked those out of the park. The class was far less 'fluffy' than I expected, which I greatly appreciated. I would highly recommend this class to any student interested in the startup industry, whether that be as a founder, funder, operator or engineer.

Although the lecture and simulation is not related, and the course is a little bit un-organized, I recommend the class to students who want to go deeper into marketing strategy, both theoretical and in reality.

yes. it touches a lot of stuffs around the PEBLO. Great class to take if you are interested about what happens behind the door.

This was Nils first time teaching this class so I cut him some slack, but I felt the class was ineffective and did not utilize the time we had well. The class's approach of learning by jumping straight into the deep end was not effective since we only had two Sundays together. Some of the concepts needed to be fleshed out more and learned through more practice examples. We really only model twice in the class, and both are graded (the first one is during the first class, just minutes after learning basic concepts). This class will improve as Nils incorporates feedback from the first class but right now it's hard to recommend this over the 2-unit LBO class.

Nils Hellmer has done a great job to keep the class engaged, however, I would like to see Nils show more details around how to run EV, ARR, valuation, return analysis etc. The lecture seems easy, but the homework is a bit too difficult. would recommend to show more steps and materials step by step.

In addition, recommend Nils provides more reading articles and highlights notes. Lecture 1 does not has any speaker, recommend to add one more speaker in Lecture 1. the 2nd class guest speaker is great from Liftoff. Overall is a good class, and have learn how PE works and optimize efficiency.
There were some flaws but this is his first-time teaching. I think he'll get better.
Yes, he knows what he is talking about. If you want to learn about Private Equity and LBOs, take this class! Yes but maybe a more time to pace the course learnings instead of two weekends

I don't recommend this course unless you have good amount of exposure to financial modeling skills as you have to do the LBO modeling on the day one. It was a quite frustrating experience without any bankers in the team. I just don't think PE/LBO course is suitable for two Sunday class - it should be at least two credit, a semester-long class.

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting exposure to PE/LBO dealmaking and applied model-building reps, including people not going into PE/IB but in industries that interact with them.
sections.notFor: Students wanting PE-level depth - it stays introductory; and those with no finance/modeling background, who will need self-study to keep up with the compressed format.
sections.workloadNote: Two Sunday sessions with one case/LBO model assigned in between; heavy at-home work for whoever builds the model. No follow-up class after the final presentation.
sections.gradingBasis: Group case and LBO model with a final presentation; one student states the group work is 40% of the grade.

comments: Absolutely yes

I definitely would recommend this class to other Haas students. I didn't have any real PE experience and I feel like I'm leaving with academic interest and knowledge. I'm not sure I see myself working in PE or IB, but I feel better prepared when I do encounter these entities in my career.
Yes, great primer and wished I took it my first semester honestly

I would definitely recommend this course for anyone interested in understanding PE more, even if they are not considering going into IB or PE themselves. The coursework provides important context and information about PE dealmaking that is useful for most everyone in industries that have interactions with PE.

I believe this is a good course for gaining a basic understanding of the private equity world, especially for someone working in a late-stage startup that might be acquired. However, it lacks the depth needed to be truly useful in professional settings for someone wanting to work in private equity.

I have taken two other one credit classes so far and this was the best one yet. The struggle in these short classes is trying to find true value in such a short period of time. I think the class did a great job of introducing Private Equity Leveraged Buyouts and building a model. However, I wish it could be longer, so we could run through more cases and more modeling practice. It is a great introductory class into PE LBOs for any students interested in the topic, but not sure if they want to commit to the longer class. Overall I really enjoyed the class and would like to take more PE classes.

Absolutely! Nils is a strong industry expert and great at making the key concepts in PE approachable. Course covers theory and then directly applies it to building an LBO model (beginner-friendly, do not be intimidated if you don't have a finance background). One of the rare courses at Haas that provides applied finance reps — very worth it! Yes, 100%. So much of the world we live is in impacted by not only private equity but general mergers and acquisitions. This course while focused on PE / LBO, still gives a really good insight of just how events like these could impact companies and therefore every day life. Nils is great! highly recommend
I would highly recommend this course because it teaches you from start to finish how to create an LBO model and get exposure to LBOs.
Yes

I definitely would. It's instructive and engaging and fun and you would learn a lot especially if you don't have a strong finance background

I would recommend both the instructor and the course, but with some context for prospective students. Nils brings a wealth of real-world experience and does an excellent job illustrating the complexity of LBO transactions through concrete examples, which makes the material engaging and grounded in practice.

That said, the course is compressed into two Sundays, which makes it challenging for students without prior finance or LBO experience to fully absorb the material. One case is assigned between the two sessions, but with no follow-up class after the final presentation, there is limited opportunity to receive feedback on your modeling approach or validate your thinking.

The course would be even more effective as a half-semester offering, with more time dedicated to hands-on modeling practice and iterative feedback. If you come in with some prior exposure to financial modeling or LBO concepts, you will get a lot out of it. If you are coming in with no background, be prepared to do additional self-study alongside the coursework.
Nils is very knowledgeable. He created an engaging, inclusive environment and seemed genuinely interested in helping us understand the course materials.
Yes, it's a great introductory course to The world of PE and LBO modeling.

Very useful insights about the PE LBO industry even for people that's not in the field or don't intend to go into the field. Good to have some basic knowledge.

yes, this class is a great asset to business students especially those going into finance. we don't have enough finance / hard skill classes like this and within just 2 classes I felt more comfortable with modeling

comments: I would recommend this course for students who are interested in learning about situational contexts of developing countries and working on solutions to prominent problems in varying areas.

Not really. Not without significant work to adapt the course better, especially as it works towards MBAs. There are cool projects it would be fun to get involved with, but all of the busywork and assignments and lectures were repetitive with things we already know from our core, and made it too difficult to even invest in the projects. Fun to meet M. Dev Eng folks at least.

Maybe. I have mixed feelings about the course. I have a prior interest in international development, so a lot of the "intro to development" (plus stats and study design) material felt like repetition. I would have liked the class to be focused almost entirely on the project work. (The profs are new [this year?] to teaching the course and are very interested in feedback on the course, so it may see some changes in the future.) As to the project work, it was messy and imperfect like all consulting project courses are, and which project you end up on (and your team) will determine a lot. Weekly reading responses felt like busy work, even if the readings were sometimes interesting case studies. On the plus side, I did feel that my project was a useful glimpse into a development context, and given my interest in that, that may have made the course worthwhile. I also met a non-Haas student with whom I'm now working on a Big Ideas application, so that was great. (The class was about 15 Haasies, 40 Master's in Development Engineering students [a mix of really interesting/cool people and young inexperienced people who BS a lot], and a few randos.)

comments: This is a really great class to learn real consulting skills and learn about the social sector. I bet it is even better experience in person. One thing for EWMBA students to know, it can be difficult to be the only EW student on a team of full time students. Setting expectations of work commitments up front is key.
Yes - incredibly immersive learning experience, even over Zoom
Yes - great on the ground experience. Lots of autonomy, opportunities to connect with different people, learn new skills, apply knowledge learned through Haas

Yes, as a non Haas student, I gained so much from this course in understanding the "business-side" of non-profits and how to be effective and responsible non-profit consultants. Going through the process of taking our client's problem and going through the process of research, converging on key insights, and finally delivering tangible products to them was invaluable. And I had a lot of fun!

I would definitely not recommend this class to another person without first priming them on the fact that this class is an incredibly large time commitment. I didn't know that information before signing up and then when I gained an understanding of the workload at the first class, it was too late to back out. It is A LOT of work regularly throughout the semester, including some very late nights and weekend work. I really enjoyed working with my team and made great friends, but it was definitely a point of stress during my semester.
Definitely! It's a very hands on class and it has been my favorite class thus far!

Yes, I would recommend this course to a fellow student, especially for those who want to pivot to consulting or non profit organizations, as you will get to learn a lot of hands on experiences with various of tools.
Students are left to their own devices. Can be good or bad.
Yes, able to practice to an extent what was taught at core.

Yes, the applied innovation and hands-on work with the client resulted in substantial learning. Being able to solve real- world problems with real-world clients that students are also passionate about also was great!

Excellent course for those uninitiated in consulting. As it is a real-world project, very relevant and impact-driven. Yes. A fantastic course with a great mix of theory and practice. A ton of work but ultimately I found it very rewarding. I think your team lead can really determine your experience. Would recommend those interested in a project connect with the team lead before the semester to check fit and vibes.

Yes if they are looking to get real world consulting experience. The combination of working with a client, the instructors, and the McKinsey coach made this very beneficial in that regard. The biggest warning would be that this has much more workload then your typical 3 unit class.

yes 100%

YES. I had an absolutely wonderful experience in this class, especially as a non-Haas student. I learned a lot and felt both supported while also being treated like a real professional. I dreaded every week of this class.

I would think twice about committing to this course given those circumstances. I didn't find the course as valuable as I would have hoped in terms of frameworks or nonprofit sector insights. yes - it was really valuable for me and was one of my favorite courses because it offered an opportunity to work with my teammates

Yes! I think any opportunity for experiential learning and actually serving a client gives you something to leverage in future job interviews.
Yes! Such an incredible learning opportunity.

I learned a lot in this class, specifically from my peers who were not in the business school or had different backgrounds. If you have not worked in consulting before, I would recommend this course. It gives you hands-on and real-world / accurate experience of what a consulting project is actually like. It is quite a lot of work, so I would be prepared for that. If you have worked in consulting, I might consider a different applied innovation elective to get broader set of experience.
Yes, I would highly recommend this class. There are a number of valuable skills to be learned.

Yes - even if one does not pursue a career in management consulting, the structure and the frameworks are largely applicable to any given field. Also, it's a great way of meeting people in the non-profit sector if that's the line of work you want to do.
This course gives you the chance to connect with non profit organization.
You can use your consulting skills for them, but the course is heavily project-based, which means each weeks " class " is mostly working time in a team.
If you have some social impact consulting I'd say no.

Heavy course load. Made the entire semester way too much to handle. Demanding, time consuming with a ssteep learning curve.

There seems to be potential for misalignment of objectives / outcomes in this course. We are expected to adhere to a fairly cookie cutter set of frameworks / principles taught in the course, no matter what the client is asking. I often felt what the client wanted / needed to be in direct conflict with what we were expected to produce for our deliverables. I think there needs to be better communication of exactly how we are evaluated in this course and how much time we are expected to put in. Otherwise, it's very difficult to draw the line with the client + team about how much work is "too much" for a given week or how much effort we should put into our deliverables. This is a class after all, and we are not being paid.

Yes I would recommend. It was a lot of effort, but I feel it was super helpful to learn about nonprofit consulting as a MSW student. I enjoyed working with non-MSW students and seeing how they ticked.

I would recommend this course, as long as students know that it is a lot of work going in and a lot of confusion and revisiting the scope multiple times over the course of the project. You learn a lot and you grow as a team, at the end I really felt like we had an impact.

I think this course is fairly dependent on the project and the team you get. It is a lot of work compared to other classes. Of course. The course is helpful in developing organizational, analytical, and team collaboration skills. There is no busy work, the concise and useful content is put to direct use in the client program. The work completed for clients is high impact and has real world application. It is was a great experience taking this course.
Yes! The course was a wonderful learning experience! It was a ton of work but well worth it for the learning and hands on opportunity to work with a real nonprofit client.
Yes, I would recommend if students are interested in consulting or NGO. I would tell them the hours required for this class as well.
If you want to explore your interest in non-profit or consulting, this course is a good start to test that hypothesis. But do expect a lot of extra work outside of the class time.

It is very important to understand how unique this course is. The entire experience depends on your client and assigned team lead, neither of which you'll know much, if anything, about prior to enrolling in the course. It is also a true consulting project. So unless you want to go into consulting I would take another class.

I would recommend this course if students are interested in going through the full life cycle of a consulting project and are interested in the social sector. Keep in my this class is a ton of work, especially given the Tuesday time slot. It did not always feel like a good use of time as conversations can feel circular. This is definitely for someone who likes group work and is fully committed to putting in the work weekly.

This course requires a minimum of 15+ hours per week. As a result, if one has the time absolutely take the course. Be sure to be selective of who your team lead is because this can make or break the experience.

It is hard to say because I think this class depends so much on your team lead, teammates, and the client you are working with. I personally had a positive experience because I had a great team lead and grew to really like the client, but there were definitely times throughout the semester that were frustrating given the mix of working styles and varying contributions from team members. Before registering for this course, I would highly recommend looking at the different clients, projects, and meet up with team leads that own projects you may want to work on. Ending up on a project you don't care about with a team lead you don't like could result in a miserable semester. That being said, this class can be extremely worthwhile if you proactively find a team and project that you are excited about. Yes! This is a great applied innovation class getting to work on real projects for mission based organizations, and getting to work with classmates beyond just your own program. I learned a lot and while it was challenging, I felt like there was enough structure and support to the class to help all teams find success

Definitely! I learned a ton about consulting and the philanthropic landscape and I was able to network with amazing professionals in the social sector. That said, I know that people's experiences are heavily influenced by their team, and I happened to have an absolutely amazing team, we all got along super well and were really supportive of each other.

Yes – the real world experience of working with a client was extremely valuable, particularly in an industry I was interested in. I left with more knowledge on the topic, working with clients, and running a strategic consulting project. Highly recommended course especially if you want to understand what consulting for non profits entails.
Excellent class but the experience is really made by your team and client. Would really suggest taking this class if you are ready to put in a lot of effort into a project you are passionate about.

Social Sector Solutions is an interesting opportunity to gain consulting experience in a classroom setting with real–world clients. I appreciated being able to build some of my core consulting skills and practice for my future role while receiving feedback from instructors along the way. Even if you aren't going into consulting, the skills that you practice in this class will definitely benefit you in your future workplace.

In a real consulting role, you might not get this level of attention or this kind of freedom to try something new or pursue a reach work stream, so this course is a good opportunity for aspiring consultants. You also won't get this level of client exposure again until you reach a higher level in your consulting career, so this is helpful in understanding the client–consultant relationship even if you won't practice it for some time.

The overall experience is definitely dependent on your project team and how you're able to work together. While my team experience was probably below average, I'm broadly glad that I took this class and had the chance to work for an awesome client. I learned a lot about myself, team work, and how to function in a
long–term group project.

Will recommend the instructors to others who are intreseted in. The teaching team is great and helpful. However, the course experience heavily depends on your team and the project you are assigned to. The peak of the happiness curve also varies. In my team, we went through a challenging period where everyone was burnt out and the project felt like a burden. Effective expression skills and interpersonal social skills are crucial here, and those who are new to consulting teamwork may feel stressed and experience culture shock.

This course is extremely time consuming. It's a real life consulting project for a nonprofit company, and the nonprofit will definitely try to squeeze as much work out of you as possible. I enjoyed the class but thought that it took too much of my time throughout each week. Take the course if interested in consulting or nonprofit work. The instructors are great – Paul is ex–McKinsey and was a founding member of the nonprofit practice at the firm.

This is a great course! Very engaging and hands on projects with clients who are working towards important and inspiring missions. Great way to get a sense of what working in social impact consulting is like. It?s definitely time consuming but we?ll worth it.

This course has undoubtedly been one of the most beneficial experiences during my graduate studies, significantly enhancing my skillset and broadening my perspective.
The course was the best I've taken at Haas!

Yes I would recommend. It's a great hands on learning experience and a real project that you'll be able to point to when taking about what you did at Haas. It is a bit of a heavier load compared to other classes, but manageable. Good class if you have never consulted before! Warning that the course load can be very heavy.
Yes! I would strongly recommend this class as a way to build a strong skillset in consulting, social sector and project management. Besides, it is a nice opportunity to meet students across campus.
As a first year MBA student the opportunities in this course were amazing. The exposure to consulting and. My client ended up being a job reference!
However there is a risk in taking this class as it's a lot of work. The learning is get your hands dirty messy and the hours are long and late.

It depends. I don't think I learned as much as I thought it would
