Yes, this is a great class to get real-life experience that you can't get from a traditional class setting.

Interesting AI course. This was my third AI course total so I feel I have a good position to judge them from. This one was the most real world since we were out working with real companies. It was also by far the most work intensive in terms of the time the projects demanded. The other AI courses were three credits, this one was only 2 credits. So for that reason I cannot strongly recommend it compared to the others. If the course was increased to 3cr and included some lecture type sessions that supplemented the Impact investing weekend 1cr course, then I would highly
recommend it.
Yes, but highly dependent on the client you are matched with, how reasonable they are with scope creep (or
shrinkage), as well as the mentor you have for your project. It took much longer than expected to nail down scope and get to work on our deliverable, and that discrepancy led to a lot of stress.

I would recommend this course if you want to go into an impact investing or ESG role so that you can get hand-on client experience. There is very little class content, so this is really just a 12 week mini-internship with a real company. Good course overall with a variety of topics. It is crucial to choose your project wisely and define the scope as this will have a high impact on your experience.

It's a project-based class so it really depends on what project you end up with and what client you work with. There is a lot of client expectation management involved and definitely feels more like a consulting project rather than an investment project. The course organization is a little messy in the beginning because the 3 instructors were also new in teaching it, but hopefully it'll get better next year.

Take this class if you want to get to know the awesome faculty better (Amon, Liz, Etter) and work on a concrete project for an external party. Similar to any AI class, your experience in the practicum will largely depend on who your client is and the nature of the project. The course will give you hands on experience with a real-life, real-time problem faced by an impact investor. Your experience here will be incredibly helpful if you want to go into impact consulting or impact investing.
Totally worth it! Dive deep into an impact project and learn as you go. Your mentor is important to help you bridge your knowledge gaps and they are very committed to help through working sessions.
Yes! The projects were super interesting and my project helped me getting a lot closer to my summer internship since I was very interested in this field.
Do not expect a lot of structure though. It's all about working with an interesting client on an interesting project and figuring it out with your group.

Yes, this was one of the most practical courses I've ever had. It was a well structured consulting project where I could get true hands on experience in a field I am looking to work in after work (impact investing). I'd recommend this as a must do class for anyone who wants to work at the intersection of impact and finance. Amon, Liz, and Steve bring their real world knowledge, experience, and networks into the classroom to help us have impactful projects, learn new things, and help position us for jobs and internships after school.

I would not recommend this course unless changes are made to ensure that projects are within the scope of what can reasonably be asked of students taking a 2 unit course over the length of one semester, and the faculty take a more active role in managing the clients' expectations.

Overall, yes. I thought the professors did an excellent job finding quality speakers and trying to be supportive as teams managed the client relationships. The projects were well-sourced and generally interesting. It is "project work" class -- there's very little aside from that. So if you're not wanting to deal with team dynamics and a client, and are looking for more instruction, then I'd reconsider.

Yes, I would recommend this course to another student interested in social impact VC. This is a hands-on course. Impact Investing Practicum is a good opportunity to gain hands on experience with an impact investing firm within the context of a Haas class. With the volatility and time commitment of in-semester internships, it's a good way to guarantee that you'll get this experience. Ultimately, you get out what you put in, and the projects vary substantially, but it's a great opportunity. There are some kinks to work out on the organizational side, but those should hopefully be fixed going forward.
Would recommend for students interested in impact investing bc of the practical experience.

rows.title: Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Leadership

comments: yes and I hope Erica takes some of the feedback and makes adjustments in examples and biases she shares...seems highly skewed and negative on america

Yes, I'd recommend taking this class. This class is the most useful class I've taken in my MBA journey and is one that I will have takeaways that I can apply to all aspects of my life. You'll need to be comfortable with stretching a little bit out of your comfort zone, but it does pay off in the end. I learned a lot about myself through the class because of all the different practices taught and there is a lot of deep reflection about what shaped you. As an FYI, there are times that the purpose of the practices are a bit unclear, but you'll need to trust the process and see where it leads. The class is not very focused on theory or concept, but more on practical skill building so you will be doing a lot of practice sessions with classmates.
Yes I would recommend it to all my classmates

Yes. I would recommend this course. I feel like a toddler learning how to walk first time, guided by Erica. I felt a different mental muscle being practiced the whole time. But people taking this class need to be aware that this is not a therapy session and is not a magic stick to solve any mental problem and issues happening in your life.
Yes absolutely

Yes! Highly recommended. This class helps you better understand who you are and what is your desire. It helps you to learn how to connect to yourself, be authentic about yourself, care for yourself. Through different practices and techniques, you are introduced with a new approach to manage your relationship with yourself and with others. These practices give you idea how to build stronger connections with people in personal and professional settings. Last but not least, this course helps you understand how to be a system leader and co-create the world with others. I would not recommend it if you want to learn anything meaningful. Even the instructor herself could not explain how her class would be relevant in real-world interactions.

I think the course has a lot of value especially for kids coming from cultures or backgrounds in which they don't get to express themselves. Erica is a good facilitator and her course will provide value to them. Thank you for your efforts over the years, especially the last few days.
Yes. This course is worth it for personal growth and introspectiveness.

If you have never taken or engaged with an "interpersonal skills" class before (or reading, workshop, etc.), then this may be helpful for you. However, the online format of the class limits how deeply you can go into practicing the skills you read about in the class.

I would recommend and I recommend anyone planning to take this course to take this with intentionality. It is easy to get lost when taking such a fluffy course and it can be easy credit if you just want to passively participate or can be inspiring if you really want to improve the way you encounter others. The more you put into this course, the more you get out of it. Erica is very nice and helpful!
Absolutely.

Yes. If you are looking for a 2 unit credit load with the right amount of work (not too much and not too little) that is also therapeutic, then this is the course for you. I enjoyed this course and saw it as the right balance to just let go.

It is hard to say because I think this class depends so much on your team lead, teammates, and the client you are working with. I personally had a positive experience because I had a great team lead and grew to really like the client, but there were definitely times throughout the semester that were frustrating given the mix of working styles and varying contributions from team members. Before registering for this course, I would highly recommend looking at the different clients, projects, and meet up with team leads that own projects you may want to work on. Ending up on a project you don't care about with a team lead you don't like could result in a miserable semester. That being said, this class can be extremely worthwhile if you proactively find a team and project that you are excited about. Yes! This is a great applied innovation class getting to work on real projects for mission based organizations, and getting to work with classmates beyond just your own program. I learned a lot and while it was challenging, I felt like there was enough structure and support to the class to help all teams find success

Definitely! I learned a ton about consulting and the philanthropic landscape and I was able to network with amazing professionals in the social sector. That said, I know that people's experiences are heavily influenced by their team, and I happened to have an absolutely amazing team, we all got along super well and were really supportive of each other.

Yes – the real world experience of working with a client was extremely valuable, particularly in an industry I was interested in. I left with more knowledge on the topic, working with clients, and running a strategic consulting project. Highly recommended course especially if you want to understand what consulting for non profits entails.
Excellent class but the experience is really made by your team and client. Would really suggest taking this class if you are ready to put in a lot of effort into a project you are passionate about.

Social Sector Solutions is an interesting opportunity to gain consulting experience in a classroom setting with real–world clients. I appreciated being able to build some of my core consulting skills and practice for my future role while receiving feedback from instructors along the way. Even if you aren't going into consulting, the skills that you practice in this class will definitely benefit you in your future workplace.

In a real consulting role, you might not get this level of attention or this kind of freedom to try something new or pursue a reach work stream, so this course is a good opportunity for aspiring consultants. You also won't get this level of client exposure again until you reach a higher level in your consulting career, so this is helpful in understanding the client–consultant relationship even if you won't practice it for some time.

The overall experience is definitely dependent on your project team and how you're able to work together. While my team experience was probably below average, I'm broadly glad that I took this class and had the chance to work for an awesome client. I learned a lot about myself, team work, and how to function in a
long–term group project.

Will recommend the instructors to others who are intreseted in. The teaching team is great and helpful. However, the course experience heavily depends on your team and the project you are assigned to. The peak of the happiness curve also varies. In my team, we went through a challenging period where everyone was burnt out and the project felt like a burden. Effective expression skills and interpersonal social skills are crucial here, and those who are new to consulting teamwork may feel stressed and experience culture shock.

This course is extremely time consuming. It's a real life consulting project for a nonprofit company, and the nonprofit will definitely try to squeeze as much work out of you as possible. I enjoyed the class but thought that it took too much of my time throughout each week. Take the course if interested in consulting or nonprofit work. The instructors are great – Paul is ex–McKinsey and was a founding member of the nonprofit practice at the firm.

This is a great course! Very engaging and hands on projects with clients who are working towards important and inspiring missions. Great way to get a sense of what working in social impact consulting is like. It?s definitely time consuming but we?ll worth it.

I highly recommend taking this class, especially if you aspire to work in a team with members from diverse backgrounds. As a public policy student, I found immense value in collaborating with my Haas teammates, who provided me with fascinating insights, including tips on creating visually appealing slides – their slides are STUNNING. This course has undoubtedly been one of the most beneficial experiences during my graduate studies, significantly enhancing my skillset and broadening my perspective.
The course was the best I've taken at Haas!

Yes I would recommend. It's a great hands on learning experience and a real project that you'll be able to point to when taking about what you did at Haas. It is a bit of a heavier load compared to other classes, but manageable. Good class if you have never consulted before! Warning that the course load can be very heavy.
Yes! I would strongly recommend this class as a way to build a strong skillset in consulting, social sector and project management. Besides, it is a nice opportunity to meet students across campus.
As a first year MBA student the opportunities in this course were amazing. The exposure to consulting and. My client ended up being a job reference!
However there is a risk in taking this class as it's a lot of work. The learning is get your hands dirty messy and the hours are long and late.
Your team can be great or a nightmare. My team lead had no experiencing leading a team which was challenging for getting the work done.
No.
I would. Best course at Haas and you get pushed.

MBA/EWMBA students - really consider what you're wanting to get out of this course before you enroll. Your experience and workload is highly dependent on your team, client, and team lead. For a three credit, sometimes heavy workload course, I wouldn't recommend this course unless you're deadset on getting nonprofit consulting experience as it's a pretty big gamble.

I would not recommend this course. This course is setup poorly with weird team structure. Lot of variables - team, client and professor relationship - need to align to derive the expected learning outcomes. There is little support from Professors and there is completely no transparency. One has no control over the learning experience, class environment, the team collaboration and grades. Overall it was the most toxic 15 weeks that one gets to experience at Haas!
It depends. I don't think I learned as much as I thought it would

sections.notFor: Both ends of the spectrum: students without a technical or analytics background report getting lost by the third lecture, while those with operations research or Solver experience say it adds little. comments: This course was a really great way to marry together the data core for the FTMBA with operations and micro Econ. That said, the software used for these projects (solver) is not native to excel and requires a virtual machine, and the learning curve was steep. I'd say take this class if you want to understand how data can integrate effectively in management settings and the boardroom, but don't expect all of the content to come easily.
I would recommend this course and instructor enthusiastically. It built my understanding of a new topic immensely overtime along with making me feel safe to take risks.
The professor is in the top 3 I have had at Haas and would appreciate taking any course I could.
Yes! Great professor!
Yes
Yes, very worthwhile course

This class could be worthwhile for students who have limited knowledge of Solver in Excel, although if you have some experience with sensitivity models this class won't add much to your knowledge base. The class also relies heavily on an Excel plug-in that I have never seen used in practice.

TLDR: take this class if you already have some qualitative background in data/analytics. Skip if it if you don't as a large amount of the class is spent on technical aspects of the problems, and very little time is spent on actually discussing the insights and shaping business recommendations around them.

Tom seems like a really great person who genuinely cares about his students and their learning. Despite this, I found the lectures often very difficult to follow, and a wasn't able to keep up. It would be helpful if Tom kept in mind that there is a range in abilities and backgrounds in the class, As someone who doesn't have a technical or data analytics background, I would say by lecture #3, I was pretty lost and relied on other students to explain the concepts to me in layman terms. I really wanted to like this class, and was excited to learn about this but the technical aspect really put a damper on things. I also think that it would be great if we could focus more on generating insights, and how to use that to shape your recommendation vs. figuring out all the intricacies of analytical solver- this would make it much more applicable to the MBA.

Yes, i would definitely recommend this course. If you have an interest in analytics, data and decisions then this course successfully builds on these topics while showcasing a practical application. I think it makes a lot of sense in the business analytics curriculum
One of the few classes that maintains a perfect balance of concepts and practicality. Case studies clearly demonstrate the course material and provide relevant practice for practical skills.
Highly recommend to anyone interested in how to approach decision making under uncertainty.
If you are in consulting, or in a PM sort of role, this subject is likely very useful to your career.

If you know you are going to be using this in your work then go for it. I'm not sure I will actually use many of the tactical concepts and approaches (I don't even have access to the software after I graduate). It would have been more helpful to learn and build models that were a bit more practical to the average corporate job, versus something using a software I won't have access to.

Its a great class if you want to understand decision models such as use of solver in excel, how to do sensitivity analysis, or create decision trees. However, if you come from an analytical background or have taken operations research courses before, then this class may not be super valuable.
Professor Thomas is great and emphasizes how the models should be used and what you should be thinking about when creating these models, rather than the nitty gritty of how the models work!

I'd recommend this course but you really need to go into the course with 100% attention span. The lectures build on top of each other and missing one leads to a snowball effect where you could be perpetually confused at the end. But the concepts learned in this class are valuable, if nothing else.
Absolutely. very relevant to any field
I would recommend this class to other students at Haas. This was one of the more difficult classes I've taken at Haas, but was also extremely applicable to a wide range of business applications.
I would recommend this course to those interested in optimization and decision models. It was a helpful overview of how these models are built.

No. The course was way too difficult and the concepts were often too abstract to be effectively taught. The useful part of the class was the actual analysis of the models/decisions/results but those nuggets were hidden behind tedious excel workshops.

Yes, I would recommend this course. If you are in a capacity of making decisions of any kind, the techniques you will learn in this class will help frame those decisions in a technical way that gives weight to a better decision beyond intuition.

sections.notFor: Students without a quantitative background - one says prior knowledge seemed required to follow lectures; another would skip it unless you want data analytics as a career.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (8 comments). In-class workshops plus modeling/analysis exercises over 10 weeks; one says there is too much content for the time so some topics get rushed. Hours never stated.

comments: Yes - super interesting course, a lot of the analysis / modeling mimic real world applications and/or are based on actual problems that were done in industry. Professor Lee is super engaging. Would highly recommend the class (although the Thursday evening time slot was rough)
Yes absolutely, I would take another class with Prof Lee if given the opportunity. He has a lot of knowledge to share and this course is very useful.
If you want to go into consulting or PM, this might be a must take class.
Yes, I would recommend this course to a fellow student. The content can be very applicable to real-world challenges no matter the domain.

Yes, I would recommend this course to students who are interested in learning how decisions models are built and applied in real world scenarios. It is challenging, but you learn a lot in a short amount of time.

I really enjoyed this course. It was a useful overview of tools and methods that are helpful and I felt like it was high- level enough to cover good ground but detailed enough such that I feel like I learned enough to be a more educated consumer of models needed in decision-making. The thought, enthusiasm, and preparation that the professor puts into the class is evident, and I really appreciated his skill at tying everything back to real world examples. I also really liked the in-class workshops as I learn best by trying something myself. The only critique I have is that there is a bit too much content for the 10 weeks of class, so we had to fly through some stuff I wish we'd had more time to spend on. May be not- unless they want to really get into data analytics as a career

This class was very informative and the professor is very engaged! However, the material was very difficult and it felt like previous knowledge / background info was required to understand the lectures.

My brain hurt after lecture, but it was a workout that my brain needed. This is not an easy course, but it's given me a new toolset that I'm excited to apply in my career. I would 100% recommend this course, it'll give you a new way to analyze complex issues and solve them
