The class evolves as AI technology evolves, and is designed to give you a good grasp of the latest AI systems, their use cases and hands on practice on a couple of them. In my class we had a hand-on practice with replit, bland and make.com

Yes, it was one of the more effective AI classes that I've taken and synthesized the technical topics of AI with the quantitative and qualitative topics very well. Honestly, this should be a two credit hour course taught during the week instead of some of the other AI classes in the certificate.
Yes, Isaiah's sharing was excellent.

Yes. Roopesh was a great professor who was incredibly engaging and knowledgable and I am walking away with real useful tools which is more than I can say for many other classes. He is a great speaker and engager.
I think this is a decent 1-credit course, low lift, and laid back. Instructor is really chill and nice, workload was not over the top, and the class was just low key and relaxed. recommend.
Yes this class helped me learn a lot about social impact and be part of the social impact community.

I wish this course was longer. I loved our external coach Shawn! She was so amazing and the practice sessions really resulted in substantial learning. Will keep referring back to this course in my professional and personal life. I would highly recommend the Leader as Coach course to fellow students. The coaching frameworks were really helpful in approaching coaching sessions with a new mindset, helping us focus on practicing active listening instead of the more natural advice giving. The coach/coachee practice sessions were all extremely impactful, and really delivered meaning and valuable practice for everyone involved. I'm definitely going to take away the practices from this course and apply them in my relationships, both personally and professionally.
Yes! Very practical application to life outside Haas. Will be immediately useful in my life and career.

Depends - it seems to be more of a learning to ask questions course. I had thought it would be more on mentorship and didnt know the difference before I joined. I felt there could be more frameworks/tools taught/real life examples of what works well vs. not (as opposed to those being brought up after a question was asked).
Yes. I will recommend. I didnt know the difference between coach and mentor before the class and now I think I am a better coach.
Great for those who want to learn standard coaching techniques.
none
Yes, the course is practical and something I can apply both at work and personal settings.
Yes, this course provided extremely value skills that are applicable no matter what career you are in.

Skills of coaching very valuable as a "tool in your toolkit". Not for all situations of communication, but where relevant, is incredibly useful and can certainly define the success/failure of your situation.
YES!! Coaching is a skills we could use in every area of our lives. This was the right amount of time, homework and plenty of practice. Thank yoU!
This is a great course that everyone who wants be a leader should take. Especially if you want to empower & set your team up for success.
Great learning in 16 hours of time.
Yes, to be a good leader it is imperative to learn how to be a coach (and not an advisor/mentor). This class sets you on the path to that goal.
Yes, I would recommend this course to fellow students who would like to develop their coaching skills or are people managers.
I would recommend this course. It really helps on some of the softer skills which so many people overlook but are vital to career progress.
Yes! The skills are useful for personal and professional situations. Jenny, Susan, and Thomas are great. I would recommend this course I think is very good.

What is a shame (and a constant across Berkeley) is that there is no coordination between the other courses that deal with interpersonal development skills. I wish there were, because would be more effective for students
Yes.

Yes, if in-person and deeply patient. The instructors don't know much more than you/ aren't more skilled/ aren't exceptional in this arena, but it's the practice and observation that you'll benefit from.

Yes, would recommend it. It's a little less on the "touchy feely" side and more about the practice. I would say the class gives good groundwork for you to be a better leader and coach on the job and gives some very practical tools for that This class was challenging on Zoom, but it's a valuable and useful class otherwise. The scope is focused so substantial learning could occur on the frameworks they teach. I wish the days weren't quite so long (9am - 6pm is tough, and there weren't enough breaks). Great teaching team though.

NO ABSOLUTELY NOT!!! This is probably the worst class I ever attended at Haas, it felt like mental and physical torture. The teachers have no idea about human biology. A bio break every 2 hours and a 55 minute lunch in a 9 hour zoom session, ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!
Great course! Highly recommend if you are interested in becoming a more effective coach or manager.
Yes, you get a lot of practice.

I did not find this course valuable - there is only one framework given for coaching, without any backing scientific studies, and no room for alternative methods. The course content itself is probably better off as a 20 min TED talk. There is an extreme burden of outside work for a one-credit class (4 interviews, a 8 page paper, a outside of class hours practicum.)
This course may be valuable if you've had minimal work experience, leading teams/managing people, and want to practice with BECI coaches in breakouts.

Would expect only base level coaching, only helpful to take if you have not taken other soft skill courses at Haas This is a great class. It is almost entirely practice with lots of feedback. I highly recommend taking it! This class is a great opportunity to practice coaching (and learn what coaching is... aka asking open-ended questions to help coaches arrive at their own next steps, without any opinions/advising by the coach). Great opportunity to practice active listening, gain empathy for other students, and maybe even get some good guidance on a problem you're currently struggling with! In all seriousness, I thought we covered a lot of material and learned useful frameworks in this class, and would recommend it to anyone who's serious about going into the business of managing people (and would consider it mandatory for any future executive coaches/HR folks).

I really like the experience this class provided and would recommend it. I wish there were more technical components. If the technologies were broken down into categories and there was technical instruction tailored to those categories, I would have learned much more. Technical learning was limited to personal research and interviews.

If you are interested in the climate tech space as an investor/entrepreneur/operator/strategy role, you must take this course. This course helped gain a great understanding of this space through personal and team research - learn by doing rather than in class. Also, working with cross industrial and cross functional teams on an unsolved challenge that is not easy to solve led to a lot of personal growth.
Yes. 100%. Because of the unique nature of C2M, working with real companies with real stakes, the instructors were especially dedicated to our success throughout this course.
Yes
I would absolutely recommend this class. It's an amazing springboard for anyone looking to break into cleantech! Two pieces of feedback on the course:
1) Six students is too many for one group. I think five is a better mix -- six just caused too much spinning and resulted in too many cooks in the kitchen.

2) I'd also highly recommend segmenting the course by early stage/ low TRL companies vs. more established. I think it's too difficult in 15 weeks to evaluate an early stage company with a low TRL with the same level of fidelity and detail as teams with more established companies. I'd recommend not including low TRL companies in C2M because to successfully tackle a project like that you need such a high level of industry expertise. You spend most of the time on 'how would you even sell this' vs. quantifying future markets, forecasting revenue etc. I'd also say that because early stage/ low TRL companies require such industry expertise to figure out 'what is this', the team dynamics become heavily skewed towards engineers who simultaneously lack business acumen. There is less of role for business folks, and the team dynamics really suffer.

Yes, as it justifies its reputation as more than a 3.0 credit course, both in terms of time needing to be put in and learnings taken out, and value from the overall experience of being put into a cleantech startup's shoes and seeing the market discovery and go to market strategies get crafted from the ground up. Could have used more material and focus on that G2M backend, but overall the class gave a great experiential opportunity to practice the key life cycle steps for scaling up pre/seed-size cleantech startups. The Investor/VC roundtable, presentation atmosphere and networking, and other non-instructional elements were just icing on the cake.

I would recommend this course even if it is a lot of work. There are several instances where we are pushed out of our comfort zones and that was incredibly beneficial to my growth. This is truly a once in a lifetime experience. Yes most definitely, this class is extremely useful and provides a lot of useful experiences for future opportunities. It will be stressful, and will require a not so insignificant amount of work to get the full benefits of the course. Yes, I would recommend this class. It was really helpful to see how startups operate and navigate the early, difficult decisions. It is also underscored just how much work is required to do the research necessary to make those decisions. I would definitely recommend this course to students. I think it was a fairly unstructured course my year and so there might not be a lot of additional learning done, but I learn by doing, and as a non-Haas student, I learned a lot about how to approach market discovery, value-based pricing, business models, and the role of presentations in different contexts by working with my classmates. It also felt good to work with real clients. Again, though, I wouldn't come in expecting to learn a whole lot in this class but rather see this class as an opportunity to put project management, communication, and market research skills to the test.

I would recommend this course to another student. However, I think the focus is a bit different than what is listed on the class description. Roughly a month is spent on developing a pitch for the company for the symposium, with dozens of practices sessions and coaching on storytelling. I think being able to give a really well rehearsed pitch is useful, but students should go into this course understanding that that is roughly ~1/3 of the time of the course. This class has the potential to be really great, however it currently isn't. The instructors seem to be holding onto the past and haven't adapted the class to the boom that the cleantech industry has experienced in the last few years. The course is disorganized (their bcourses needs a big update) and the technologies selected are not similar enough to have one set of content for the course (software vs deeptech & hardware at very different TRLs). There needs to be more cases, possibly bringing in entrepreneurs that have actually commercialized hardware/deeptech

cleantechnologies because there are quite a few now and that would help us structure our learning. The focus on "beachhead" markets seems difficult when some technologies are still at the lab-scale and others are already being sold to consumers. They might consider hiring a GSI to help them with this. There is too much focus on the presentation vs the market report because the presentation is public facing and helps fundraising, which feels a little misaligned.

This class is very much focused on group work and whether your experience is good or bad is highly contingent on your team (including your ability to work together) and the company you've been assigned. The instructors are helpful for high-level discussions and guidance on business models, thinking about applications of tech, preparing for the symposium, etc.
Maybe. Your experience depends on a lot of factors: the startup you work with, your team, your ability to plan and organize in advance.

The course is A LOT of work. I was putting at least 10 hours every week into it, and sometimes it feels like it's just not worth it. This is also not a class where you will learn something--there are no lectures or cases and there are barely any reading--but it's more learning by doing. You learn a lot about the markets of your startup, and some of it might be replicable for a very early stage startup. I think you can have a good experience if everything aligns and you have luck, but you still have to be aware that this course is really a lot of work.

Maybe. I really enjoyed the class and found I learned a lot. That said, it's challenging (which could be good or bad depending on who you are), requires a decent amount of work, and can be hit-or-miss depending on the

company/founders you match with (and not everyone gets their first choice). I came into this class without any energy/cleantech background, more interested in the entrepreneurship aspect of the class (namely, finding a good beachhead market), and it ended up being a great fit for me. I don't think "I'm interested in cleantech" equals "I must take Cleantech to Market"; it's more about if you're interested in early-stage startups and finding a market for a new technology.

You should not if you are not interested in the topics. You need to expect to manage team dynamics properly since there are both students who have strong interests (and commitment for the time) and less interests.

This is a good course, but it could be better. It is focused too much on the pitching/symposium aspect, and not enough effort is spent on the market research side of things. If you are interested In becoming an entrepreneur or working at a smaller company, this is great! However, if you want to work at a larger company, this may not be the best use of your time.

Yes, but with caution. It is an interesting class but be fully aware that your experience will completely depend on two things 1. Your entrepreneur and the technology that you are working with and 2. Your team. If either one is not aligned with your learning objectives from this class you are going to have a bad time. That being said, it is an interesting class and worth the experience especially if you have an entrepreneurial sprit.

The experience of this class is highly dependent on your team and your company. If you're interested in clean tech and would find the projects alone intellectually stimulating, I recommend taking the class. However, don't bother if you aren't 100% in. Starting off with the technology in this course makes it extremely difficult for people with a non- technical background to get caught up to speed and engage in the project. There are intentionally individuals that are supposed to serve as a bridge between technical and business people, but if those individuals aren't a good bridge and are too technical, the experience is brutal.

I would recommend the course with the caveat that it is highly catered toward pitching and showman ship and less so toward detailed tech review, market entry strategy, and many of the fundamentals necessary to equip the next generation of climate tech founders and funders. Pitching is super important, but this style is much more "big room/TED Talk" style, which is rare, so it's good to get that rep, but maybe not worth 80%+ of the course work going into perfecting. I think the course could also benefit tremendously from bringing in a third professor, or part-time advisor, preferably someone younger and from a different background in the climate tech space (female, under represented demographic group, etc.). This person would ideally be actively involved in the climate tech VC world (as an investor) or as an entrepreneur and could bring current perspectives to class. That would make a HUGE difference and help adapt what is a great, but at times dated, course into the critical new world of climate tech.

Yes I would definitely recommend, with the caveat that there are no guarantees of which team you will get but there's a substantial amount of growth and learning that takes place depending on what you make of the program.
Absolutely would recommend to non- Haas students. So much learned this semester and one of the most rewarding classes taken at Berkeley

I would recommend it if you are interested in the climate tech space. It was a ton of work and stressful, but I am definitely glad I did it. The middle of the class was a grind when you didn't know what market you could present, but looking back, it was all worth it. It was great to have people outside of Haas on my team to get to know them and get their insights on the technology.
I do not take class again. This class should be 5 units class in stead of 3. Just too much and learned almost none for a person who was in cleantech industry like me.

I would not recommend this class at all. Despite having 3 faculty members leading the class, they did not actually instruct much and I find this a pity as I'm sure we could have learnt a lot from them. The class meets twice a week but the time is not well used: there is little time for team work, but also no real content that is being taught. Most of the classes require each team to give an update, one by one, about where they are in the process and what type of tools they are using (eg, are you tracking interviews on Excel vs. Word?), which becomes extremely repetitive and is not helpful. In addition, it felt like the entire class was designed for the final summit where the audience is a mix of investors and thought leaders in cleantech. I found it a pity that very little emphasis was being put on actually delivering something valuable for the entrepreneurs and startups we are actually working with and on making sure that students learnt, and instead it just felt like it was important to the faculty to save face in front of whoever was invited to the summit. Therefore, I felt that from beginning to end there was a huge misalignments in goals between the students, the entrepreneurs, and the faculty. From a project perspective, the class was way more "technical" than I expected (but unfortunately with nobody really teaching us any technical content), and there was surprisingly very little emphasis on go-to-market strategies and commercialization! That being said, I really liked that the teams were mixed, with students from many different programs, including PhD students. In addition, Bill and Sheeraz were always available, approachable and happy to help out, and I really appreciated their commitment to the class, their deep care for students and their receptivity to feedback!
this sucked - too much work, no guidance, lots of busy work type assignments, huge time committment and 0 payoff. only cool part is the startups themselves, and the other students in the class

Rewarding, especially if you haven't done consulting style before (less valuable if you have). The courseload is very heavy, so plan for this if you decide to take the class. Also, spend a lot of time selecting your company. Summit presentations were very rewarding
This class was a significant learning for my career and an engaging way to work with startups in delivering significant content. A class that you make your own!
Absolutely! By far, one of the best classes I have taken. An awesome learning experience and a fun community to engage with.
Yes. This is a great class. Really helped me develop, especially within the cleantech sphere.
Yes, this course taught me a lot about market research, interviewing, and giving effective presentations.

I would -- as a PhD student, this is one of a few opportunities to take a business class and diverge from the many technical courses we take. I think it was a good experience overall but is highly dependent on your team and the startup you'll eventually work with. I've had the good fortune of working with some incredible business students from whom I've learned a lot. The startup we worked with this year is also really responsive to our feedback and concerns. The instructors do a great job encouraging us to ask them for feedback or help whenever we need it, though I feel like I got more out of working with my team than the instructors' lectures.
I would highly recommend this course to fellow engineering students because it teaches engineers very different knowledge and motivates them to have their own startups.

Yes, if you could truly put the time in that this class deserves. This class is most valuable if everyone in the team in engaging and participating. There were different levels of dedication in the team and I think that dragged us down quite a bit.

I would definitely recommend this instructor and course to another student. I had a great time in this class and it was so useful to my education to have the real-life experience of consulting with a start-up and learning about how products are brought to market.

I have told students that if you have a passion for working in Cleantech you can get a lot of this class if you are willing to put a lot of work into it, however, if you are only casually interested then I would not take this course. Yes. It was a great opportunity to work with passionate entrepreneurs. High degree of freedom is the beauty of the class. You may set your own goal in this class and leverage the activities to achieve your goal. You can broaden your energy network in a very effective way with this class.
The final symposium presentation is a honorable chance to speak in front of energy professionals in the bay area and get your foot in to the community.

This is a LOT of work - but there is substantial value in deeply getting into a problem, working through it, building external connections, and potentially even finding jobs. Don't go in half-heartedly but if you're committed to cleantech it is the class to take.

If you are interested in clean or climate tech or energy, take this course. Your enjoyment of the class will highly depend on the technology you get and your team. I got an OK tech and an excellent team and the course was one of the best I've taken at Haas. If you end up on a team full of typical "haas apathy" (you know what I mean) then this class has the potential to be rough. Overall, this is an excellent learning experience and, for some of you, why you came to Haas, so take the class. It is a lot of work, but if you keep on top of it all semester, it's perfectly manageable. For all of those interested in how startups find their ideal market and design their go-to-market strategy this is a great course. It is a lot of work, so starting early by defining team dynamics and planning the semester with your team in the first week of class is ideal if you want to get the most out of this class.
Yes I would. I learned quite a lot from hands on research, which is the most impactful way of learning for me. The things I learned and connections I made are directly impactful to my future career.
Yes! I learned so much about early-stage climate tech start ups and the climate tech space in general. I am so happy that I took this course!
YES!

Students should have a very clear reason for what they intend to get out of the class, whether that is presentation skill development, deep exposure to a technology, GTM strategy experience, etc. and make sure it is worth the high workload required to do well in the course

Absolutely not. I was so excited about this class, and it was one of the main reasons that brought me to Haas in the first class. I'm very sad to say that this course was the single biggest regret of my Haas experience. It was poorly designed from the start.

This class hinges on having strong client partnerships. Several of the clients did not set their teams up for the success. They came in with different understandings of what they would get out of the course, indicating that the instructors did not prep or debrief them well. It's also very hard to teach uniformly to a class that is working with very different clients at very different stages. If you don't see a client you're SUPER excited about, please don't even think about this course.

The lecture materials were disjointed, and topics didn't flow well from one to another. The instructors attempted to give us group work time during class, but it was usually only in 20 minute blocks amidst other content. This was disruptive and we were unable to get much done in this time. Most of the content ends two thirds into the course, and the end is dedicated to the symposium presentation and report.

The instructors are just okay. Bill and Bill have been doing this forever, but it seems like their hearts just aren't in it anymore. Sheeraz was truly a fantastic instructor and is a great leader in this space.

Much of the course is spent conducting stakeholder interviews and doing market research. I believe that these concepts are better taught and better utilized in other courses and experiences at Haas. Due to the forced deliverables (symposium presentation and 75+ page report) and needlessly uniform teaching style, this class ate up more time than all of my other courses combined. It was a frustrating experience in which I look back and reflect that I have learned very little from it. I wish so badly that I could reset this semester and not take C2M. Please don't make the same mistake I did.

C2M is an incredible experience. Probably life changing. It gave me the opportunity to apply the learnings from my MBA to a real-life scenario. I would highly recommend this for anyone who wants to work in clean tech but I do agree with comments from previous years that it requires A LOT of work. I spent easily 5-6 credits worth of of time on it

No one should take this course until it is completely overhauled. Working with cleantech startups feels like the quintessential Haas project, and in many ways it is, however, there is little to no education being provided in this class. At their worst, AI courses are unpaid internships, and that's what this course is in its current form. Almost 2/3rds of total class time was dedicated to unstructured teamwork, which is unacceptable. If we could be properly taught about how to go about performing the final deliverables before they were due, this would be a decent class, but with so many years to get things right, it's hard to believe there will be any significant change.
Ultimately most of the course is experiential and I learned a lot through the process of the projects assigned and would recommend the course.
Yes, this course is one of the best classes I have taken at UC Berkeley. I learned a lot about the technology commercialization process through this course.

Overall if you are interested in the Cleantech startup space I think that this is a good primer for what it looks like. It puts you in a place where there is a lot of ambiguity and you need to just grind a lot to get to your ultimate goal. I think that most of that work has to happen at an individual and team level, and it is not easy, which can make it easy to complain about the instructors even if it does not necessarily have to do with them. Ultimately I think this is very valuable course and would recommend it.

C2M was a challenging but ultimately rewarding course to enroll in. I got to learn about a very interesting technology, dive into new markets and areas of knowledge, while working with a good team who were all bought in in their own ways. I think if you get the short end of the stick on the team perspective it can be a pretty miserable experience given the volume of work and relative lack of structure in the class.

I would highly recommend taking this class as it's a capstone class where we can practice aspects of finance, marketing, econ, data, sale and last but certainly not least, public speaking. I wish more Executive MBA (EMBA) would be aware of this class as it's a great opportunity to work directly with founders. EMBA also bring a different perspective as well as access to a more robust network that will come hand during the industry interviews.
If you want to learn about clean tech in an immersive experiential way, AND have plenty of time (i.e. few other time commitments) then it's a great experience
It depends. Your experience will depend heavely on the team you are assigned to and the entrepreneur you are assigned to.

Besides this, the class itself in terms of content was not particularly attractive to me. The content was not well structured and the feedback you get during the process of preparing the final presentation and paper are not necesarrily appropiate or helpfull.

On the other hand, you get a real consulting kind-off experience and learn a bit about how startups work. But for the most part, your are on your own with your team and the entrepreneur without too much detailed guidance.

This course is challenging not just because of the subject matter, the workload, or the deliverables, but because of the scattered instruction, poorly designed class meetings, and irrelevant interim deliverables.

Yes - beware that while this is 3 credits, expect to put in work akin to a 5 credit class. It really feels like a badge of honor to have for anyone looking to make their career in climate tech but certainly not a walk in the park and there are certainly easier applied innovation courses to take if you're not all in on climate tech.

For a fellow science-focused student I don't know if I would recommend it. This was a good overall experience, but the summit made me feel like most presentations could have been written a few weeks ago with minimal research. It becomes a game of giving the best "show" and not showcasing research. The final presentation that called TEM tea and had a planted question from a friend to start off the discussion made me feel sick to my stomach.

I cannot recommend this course in its current form. It is an ungodly amount of work which may or may not have any influence for the companies we work with. The professors do not maximize our class time or really teach us much valuable content. They do not provide enough guidance throughout the semester or add much value to the projects at all. This class has added a tremendous amount of stress to my life. I was warned that it would be stressful, but thought that if I approached the course proactively and diligently, I would be able to avoid the horror stories I had heard from past students. I was wrong. Given the current format, the stress is unavoidable.

I would only say that I hope this course changes. It has so much potential, but unfortunately falls short. A hard maybe. The course is well run and an intense learning experience. Students need to understand that this is at its core a marketing course. If students are going into other fields outside cleantech or marketing, this course may be less relevant. Weigh this against C2Ms significant time commitment. However, if going into cleantech, I feel like this course is a must take if for the network of C2M alum and sponsors alone. Learnings are largely based on the specific team and technology you will be working on so choose wisely!

Without significant upgrades, I would have a difficult time recommending this course to a fellow student. With that being said, it is an awesome opportunity to dive deep into a clean tech-focused market. I learned A TON about the market my team was focused on (critical minerals), but wish there had been far more teachings on Go-To-Market strategy, project scoping, and other project management skills.

I would absolutely recommend this course to a fellow student. I feel that I gained a lot of really valuable experience, and that it was very much worth the effort. I feel that I am a better-rounded student now.
If you are interested in Climate Tech, this is a course that you have to take.

Mixed feelings.... depends a lot on the expectations students have. Hopefully students get a very real understanding of the class before enrolling. Maybe having panels with alumni could be helpful before round 1 bidding.
Not sure; I have mixed feelings about the course. We worked very hard, but there was little guidance or class lectures that made me learn from them.

I would not. I think there are easier and more educational ways to fulfill this learning and the applied innovation requirement. I think that there was just not a lot of learnings in class and that the experiences vary so widely by the project that I would pick a different course for a sure thing. If you need a project, there are other classes. If you want to learn this stuff, right now it is better to chat with faculty rather than sit through this whole class and project. I would absolutely not recommend this course unless one of the startups is exactly the type of company you are interested in. You will learn very little from the instructors about cleantech, start ups, business strategy, etc. The priority of the course is not student learning but putting on a summit that connects the instructors and the broader cleantech community. The most direct learning you'll do is I guess around how to present a powerpoint at a summit - not exactly what I signed up for.
The course is very poorly organized. The uses of BCourses was so confusing and the expectations around assignments and final deliverables was constantly shifting at the last minute.

I was also pretty unimpressed by the quality of the startups. Furthermore, because the priority of this course is not actually student learning but the final summit which is basically a pitch competition you don't actually get authentic engagement from the startups. Instead the startups are more or less pitching to you the whole time because they want to win the money more than they are interested in your learning. Remember that the financial awards presented at the summit go to the start ups not to to you so they want your free labor to make them look is as good as possible! On top of that, it is a ton of work. The market report and summit presentation is a huge lift but you will not be learning new tools to execute on it. Instead, you are asked to bring whatever skills you already have to perform free labor. Yes, if the student is a non-Business School student and if is particularly interested in getting a sense of how climate technology and business intersects. I would definitely mention that even the class connects you and your team with a startup, there will be a lot of business knowledge that students are supposed to know beforehand. Probably not really hard to get those knowledge over the semester, but definitely something to keep in mind.
Yes if they're really interested in diving deeper into climate tech companies and working with start-up for commercialization. It is a lot of work so it depends on the students willingness to commit!

Definitely recommend IF you are interested in Cleantech. But it requires a lot of work outside of the class Working on this course absolutely destroyed my fall semester, and as much as I'd like to say I learned a lot about clean tech and go to market, I didn't really learn about either of those things. The course is basically one giant consulting interview with an added bonuses of working with 4-5 other people (at least 2 of whom probably don't actually care about this class) and a 70+ page paper on the end. Do market sizing on 20 markets, select some of them, interview random people so that there's an air of legitimacy to the whole thing, then send the final result over to a startup that might appreciate it or might literally never look at it.

No, I don't recommend it. Like many incoming students passionate about cleantech, I was really excited about this class but ultimately I regret taking it. Previous students tried to warn us but I chose not to heed their feedback and even bid all my points to take this class; after the first few weeks it became apparent I made the wrong decision. The class was not worthwhile at all, in fact it made my semester difficult. We did not get much lecture content or learn much and were expected to basically teach ourselves while at the same time do work for the clients on such short and immense time pressure. Essentially we were paying our tuition to do free consulting work, except it isn't free we're paying to work for these startups.

This is a great course! It teaches you a lot of things from working with startups to market discovery as well as exposes you to a lot of ideas in the climate tech space. Definitely one of the heavier lifts in terms of workload but was rewarding!

I would recommend this course to students if they want to understand the reality of startup market research. The course is quite scrappy and the research and conclusions are never developed in absolute confidence, but one of my key learning from the course is that it really is like that outside of the course too. Teams learn and grow and never stop learning and growing.

I'm not a Haas student, but I recommend C2M if you're interested in the cleantech space and have at least 5 hours/week to spend on this class for 15 weeks. You get how much you invest in the class. It was particularly rewarding to work with PhDs and grad students pursuing other fields of study, and a nice intro to network with folks in the space. Would absolutely recommend this course if you're interested in climate tech or deep tech / hard tech start-ups in general. The course was especially helpful for non-Haas students, as it included lots of business frameworks, practice building slides and presentations, working with clients, etc.

I would recommend this course to a fellow student if they are looking for a broad overview into connecting research/technology with business development. While the course content itself is not challenging, the workload and time commitment does become extensive especially as you approach the end of the semester. You will be able to learn a lot of new business concepts and understand what can make or break a technology, which as a someone from a research background don't necessarily get exposure to normally. The class structure can sometimes make it difficult to see how all the pieces fit together, but process ultimately gets the students to where they need to be. The class is very much designed to be "you get what you put into it".

I would but only if they're willing to put in the time. Overall, it was a lot of work with some assignments that felt silly or unnecessary but I do think I got a lot out of it as someone who has never worked in the hard sciences. If you're interested in commercialization work at all, this class is necessary.
Yes! Incredibly value learning opportunity. In addition to learning about startups, it also felt like a great presentation/public speaking skill buillder
I would recommend it cautiously, for several reasons.
1) The workload is heavy.
2) Lectures and class deliverables feel somewhat disconnected from the actual market research you end up doing, but the actual work is very interesting.

3) The climate tech curriculum is interesting, and could have more promise if the guest speakers come with a prepared presentation — I feel I got more value out of the guest lectures that had presentations this semester.
4) Rehearsals for summit and feedback from instructors during in-class working session is quite helpful.
Yes! I would definitely recommend this course to students. It was a lot of work but I learned so much about my start up and market and generally the process of climate tech commercialization.

It is a good class and a great way to learn more about a industry that you're interested in. I recommend being really thorough with the startup selection (before class starts), as that can make or break your experience (I got the one I wanted and really liked it). It is also a lot of work, be prepared to email (and cold email) many, many people that you're interested in talking to.

If you're interested in clean tech / climate tech, you must take this course for the learning, the network you build, and the credibility it gives you in the climate tech community (yes, really). Provides great hands-on introduction to a wide range of skill sets -- market research, techno-economic analysis, storytelling for business, customer research. It requires a ton of work, which you won't want to (or really be able to) put off until the end of the semester, but you'll have learned a lot by the end of it. Delivering this material in a compelling fashion as a classroom experience is a tall order for the instructors given the sheer breadth pf the course -- and the tension with the need to dive deep in your individual startup -- but the faculty puts a ton of effort into making it work and brings the very relevant experience and network to bear to do so.
Yes. Definitely recommended. Think of this class as Lean Launchpad 2.0 on steroids focusing on deep-tech and climate sectors. The most rigorous Applied Innovation class I have ever taken

It's a lot of work for little return. You must be *really really* into climate tech to enjoy this class. One nice thing about this class is the multi-disciplinary team you get to work on with PhD's, Law students, and Public Policy folks and you get to view problems from multiple angles.

Yes I will particularly because of the overall experience and impact. particularly for technical students I believe is a great opportunity to get to understand how startups work and even how exactly it may mean working in a founder of a a startup and the dynamics of the real world experience. I would however be very specific on the demands of the course and notify them of the extra requirements of time they may have to devote to the course in the beginning of the semester

Working alongside a real-world startup to understand their technology and find where it fits in the larger market was great, but the course did not really set you up for success. Class time was spent more on high-level theories and frameworks than actionable advice or insights, the group project dynamic of the deliverables made it more stressful and contentious than it needed to be, and at the end of the day I'm confident I would have learned more and worked less if I'd just done an internship at a climatetech start-up instead.

I'd highly recommend this course to students who are interested in or want to learn more about climate tech. The alumni and startup network, together with the industry expert guest speakers are valuable resources that brought this class to a next level. To me, this is more of a "program" than a "course", in the sense that there are amazing networking opportunities with guest speakers each class and happy hours to connect with past alumni. C2M is also a high profile program in the climate tech space and adds credentials to your experience if you want to work in the space in the future.
es, I would recommend it. For students with a technical background, it provides an excellent opportunity to explore potential business avenues.

I would recommend this class. I learned a lot about the business world that I would never have gotten a chance to engage with in other classes. I really appreciate how many people we got connected to and how many resources I was offered while taking this class. I am also extremely grateful for all the instructor's time and effort put into organizing multiple guest speakers, the MetLife Coaches, the Summit, etc... I have never taken a class with this much dedication put behind it. It is very energizing to see that much passion and energy behind a graduate class, not many classes in other departments are like this. This class was a great opportunity to put myself outside of my comfort zone and develop additional communication, analytical, and presentation skills. I have never spoken to a room that big before so the summit was a really knew and exciting experience. I also very much appreciate Berkeley offering a class with a values driven goal, if this was a class about a generic tech start up as opposed to a climate tech related one, I would not have been as engaged. The overall emphasis on supporting companies that are finding solutions to serious climate issues makes this class very motivating and the experience very rewarding. I am sure the skills I developed in this class will prove useful in the future. I found most assignments to be valuable and instructive, although I felt that some deadlines were arbitrary and unhelpful. The multiple business model canvas assignments did not really help our team. The assignment we struggled with the most was the TEA by far. I hade never made one before and I think we weren't properly prepared in this class to build a satisfactory TEA so I felt very unfulfilled by this assignment. To be clear, I think it is a great thing to learn how to do and excellent material for the class, but I would have appreciated more time spent on how to develop one and possibly multiple checkins and feedback sessions on this assignment as well. Without a complete TEA I felt that the some of the subsequent economic modeling we did on promising markets was inaccurate. The example TEAs provided were very helpful.

sections.goodFor: Students wanting climate/energy networking, deep-tech consulting experience, and hands-on go-to-market work with a real startup; non-business students get a strong intro.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a light lift or who can't invest heavy outside hours; experienced founders/product people (too basic); those who need to pick their own startup or teammates.
sections.workloadNote: Among the heaviest at Haas. Most work is outside class: stakeholder interviews, entrepreneur meetings, assignments, and the final C2M Summit. The 3-hour single session drew complaints.
sections.gradingBasis: Team project deliverables, stakeholder interviews and the final Summit presentation; specific weights not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Startup matching is 'a complete blackbox' (2); experience hostage to your team and assigned startup (5+); lectures long/redundant (3); startups not climate-focused enough (2); 1 calls it admin-heavy and 'fluffy.'
sections.quote: The whole course is dependent on how good your team and your startup is. It would have been nice to have some content that didn't depend on those two factors
comments: Yes, if you're interested in climate technology. In particular, building out a network in climate/energy and/or thinking through how tech can scale are the core strengths of the class. The guest speakers and networking opportunities in this class are fantastic. And the teaching team does a good job introducing how to interview stakeholders, how to approach techno-economic analysis, and preparing you to present. However, while I have some frameworks to think about how tech scales (TEA, Competitive Analysis, TAM), these concepts are introduced then left up to us to really apply them in-depth. Because of this (as well as all the stakeholder interviews we have to do), the class can feel like a lot of work.

Yes! This is a great course for anyone, even someone with no experience in clean tech. It'll give you exposure and there's tons of investment that the course makes in you as a professional regardless of your industry vertical Yes, depending on what you are looking to get out of it and how much time you have. This is a great class for consulting experiential learning, plus startup and deep tech real-world experience -- both of which are great things. If you're looking for a safe environment that's flexible in terms of workload and has team members to lean on, this class is a great fit. If you're looking to learn lots by doing, want to learn quickly, and want to learn broadly, then an in- semester internship is likely more effective from a time-effort perspective -- but this is a much larger commitment than a class.
Yes I would

This is an awesome class and clearly a lot of time and energy has gone into perfecting it for students. My main recommendation is to choose more climate-focused technologies and companies. All of our eggs are in one basket re the company we're paired with and I wish I was able to work with a company more focused on GHG emissions
reductions.
Yes. I learnt a lot about the operation and key factors impacting clean tech startups
Yes. These instructors are really helpful not only delivering the program but also navigating related issues and problems

I would recommend this course to anyone who is interested in learning the challenges early-stage deep-tech startups face. There is a considerable amount of work that takes place outside of class meetings in the form of interviews, meetings with entrepreneur, and assignments. You do NOT get to choose the startup you wish to work with; you are asked to distribute 100 points to your top 5 startups. I was not selected to work with my top choice, to whom I assigned 96 points. The matching process is a complete blackbox.

You will work with people outside of Haas, people who are a lot busier than your average MBA students. They, understandably, will not be as available to put in the work as you would and FT or EWMBA students will be responsible for carrying the team.
Yes. It's chaotic but gives valuable insight into what it might be like to work at a clean tech startup. Awesome networking opportunities within cleantech.
I thought the lectures were helpful but they were very long considering the value I got out of them.
The whole course is dependent on how good your team and your startup is. It would have been nice to have some content that didn't depend on those two factors
I recommend splitting the class back up into 2 different class sections
I think this class is helpful if you've never launched a product before but if you have, it doesn't help you delve much deeper into it.
I wish that the startups felt more like clean tech - more energy related startups or solutions that, if scaled, would address bigger climate problems.

I absolutely have and would recommend this course. It's easily my most well-organized, well-facilitated class. This inspired me in turn to be involved in this class above and beyond, and I used many of the lessons I learned in this class (especially in effective storytelling and presenting) even in other courses. I also feel grateful to now be connected with my amazing team, who I can now call my friends.
I am not an MBA, and do not come from a business background. This course has been a welcoming, intensive intro into Haas, where I will certainly try to take more courses.
Difficult but gratifying class. A lot of effort expended and the C2M Summit helps deliver a gratifying end. yes, helpful for understanding early stage cleantech

I would recommend to people who want to do a ton of work, who are really interested and doing this type of work, and don't have experience. The main thing is it is a ton of work, and takes a ton of time, not really all of it super useful - I was jealous of those who skipped class because so much of it was redundant

I would recommend this class to those who are interested in working in the clean tech space or working with startups and founders to shape their go-to-market strategy. However, I would also like to mention that the workload is probably one of the heaviest among all classes I've taken as a third year MBA student. Additionally, you don't get to choose your teammate - you kind of do by selecting the same company but not really know who will be on your team till the team is formed - and your teammates will have a huge impact on your experience with this class, positive or negative.
Maybe. I would prefer if the course is again split into two classes every week because 3 hours is too much with me (and I learnt that)

It depends on your desires/priorities. This is a heavy lift class and the type of class that you get out as much as you are willing to put in. Also, I feel like non-MBA people might have gotten more out of this than MBAs (except for those specifically looking for consulting experience in a deep tech/climate tech field) since the business portion is not extremely advanced (which makes sense considering the class has students from other schools with no prior business experience).

Yes, I would recommend this course. It offers a rare mix of real-world industry exposure, structured guidance, and hands-on teamwork that helps you build both technical and commercial skills in cleantech.
Absolutely recommend. This course gives you real exposure to cleantech startups, investor thinking, and
commercialization. The team is incredibly supportive, and the final summit is a unique, high-stakes experience that pushes you to grow.
For people who have limited startup or entrepreneurial experience absolutely for those with might be a little too basic It is a lot of work, and a lot depends on if your company is cool.

Yes, I would recommend this course if you have the time to really invest in and engage with it. The class is very time- consuming, and most of the learning happens outside of the classroom. If you don't have the capacity to give the course the attention it deserves, you likely won't learn as much and won't be able to contribute effectively to your team.

No. Way too much time spent on administrative matters, not practical enough. Not close enough to real world experiences and more geared towards a "fluffy" summit presentation than for actually providing useful inputs to startups. There are much better classes available (including on Coursera).
Yes, but only if you need the credit

I would recommend this class to students who want an interactive class that works with an external client. It is a great resume builder but it is A LOT of work. Also the experience is very dependent on the group you are placed with and the startup.
I would recommend this course though it is heavy workload, so be prepared when you enroll in this course. It is really worthy!!
The teaching team is solid, experienced, competent, helpful, responsive, interactive, and supportive. They help you get through a very difficult and intensive course/project.
Yes - but caveat that the group project was a lot of work / tough to pull together
Yes. Maura is fantastic. Don't take the other New Venture Finance or you'll regret it, no doubt. This one is a good amount of work, but worth it.
Yes. The course is extremely applicable to future entrepreneurs.

If you are an entrepreneur trying to understand how to sustain your business, this is a valuable course. Likewise, if you're an investor (or an aspiring one), this course provides exposure to the broader financing environment outside of your specialty. If you're pretty experienced in either of these, though, this may not be the class to get the latest techniques — it definitely hits the highlights. This course can also serve as an intro to venture funding as well for the uninitiated. At times, I felt like the course could be shorter — but the bulk of the benefit comes from hearing from the guest speakers.
Absolutely - one of the most informative and relevant courses in entrepreneurship and finance at Haas

This class doesn't jump too deep into theory, but is great for first-time founders or entrepreneurs. A lot of the items covered are the "soft" aspects of entrepreneurship and seeking VC funding - like how to negotiate term sheets and how to raise money. There isn't really a "finance" element to this class as the only math is centered on constructing cap tables and payouts. The examples are rather simple to introduce concepts.
Yes, good content
Yes, It gives an overview of what you should do to finance your venture.
Please refer to my previous comment. I would truly take any future class of hers.

I would recommend Maura as an instructor because she is engaging, experienced and her passion for teaching others comes through in every aspect of the NVF class. The information she teaches is so relevant and deep and it is provided in a way that is incredibly helpful for someone like me who wants to start a company and raise venture funds in the next few years. She focuses on key information (like, you should plan to raise 2x the amount of capital and assume it will take you 2x longer than you anticipate) and also shares incredibly engaging stories from her real world experience during each class.

Yes, it is a great class especially for the students who have interests in new venture capital. If the student invested more time into the class, definitely, the student will learn more from the class. The guest speakers part are super great and there are tons of speakers invited for the class.

I would totally recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. The class resulted in substantial learning not only through traditional methods (readings, slides), but also through great speakers that shared their insights. This is a great introductory course on how to finance new ventures through a variety of vehicles (VC, Angels, Search Funds, etc.). Really a fantastic and manageable class.
100% the best class and best professor I've had at Haas so far in my MBA journey. Got my tuititon's worth after this course!

Yes, 100%. I learned a lot in a short amount of time through the course and felt like the workload was enough to emphasis the key concepts that Maura felt were most important to take away from the class without being
overburdened with work. I enjoyed going to class each week.
Yes! If you're interested in entrepreneurship of venture capital it is a must.
Yes, I highly recommend this class

Yes, because finance is one thing. How to negotiate a term and a solution with another party is a different thing. This class can give you the knowledge of what common terms people use nowadays and what you should think about as an entrepreneur.
Yes, I would recommend this course to anyone excited about entrepreneurship or VC

Without question!! This was one of my all time favorite courses, and I was shocked to learn that it's relatively new. It makes me feel sorry for any founder who attended Haas before this class was offered!
Would definitely recommend Maura. Maura brings her five-decade experience in this field and presents it with great style and clarity.

I highly recommend this course to students regardless if they have plans to fundraise for their company in the future. It helps to just understand the different stages, methods, and how early choices you may can impact your relationship with investors later on etc. The course leverages a mix of forums from cases, guest speakers to group projects that reinforce the learnings. Super interesting!
Great course if you want to start your own venture! Very valuable lessons in Venture financing which will be super useful in real life.

Absolutely, this is one of the capstone classes and a must-take for founders and non-founders alike. Super high- quality guest speakers, one of the best professors at Haas teaching you essential knowledge for any bay area workers. Yes!!! Most definitely! It was probably one of the best classes I've taken. The content was extremely engaging with a strong mix of activities, cases, speakers. I highly recommend if you are even remotely interested. Despite the final project being daunting, it is an amazing way to network with potential VCs and other funders!

Absolutely. This course is great if you want to work or be involved in some way with the startup world. The class helps you learn how to setup a term sheet and understand all aspects of a deal with a VC

sections.goodFor: Aspiring founders and students new to venture financing: term sheets, cap tables, exit waterfalls, negotiation practice, and high-quality guest speakers, taught by practitioners many called among the best at Haas; the investor-interview project doubles as network building.
sections.notFor: Students wanting quantitative depth or the investor-side toolkit for evaluating companies, and those already experienced in venture finance; a cluster in one term found lectures unstructured and qualitative, wanted more time on contracts, valuations, and term negotiation, and felt class time drifted into off-topic personal commentary.
sections.workloadNote: Moderate overall; the main lift is a final group project interviewing 12+ investors, which some found a great networking excuse and others found repetitive and time-consuming.
sections.gradingBasis: Work included cases, a group project built on 12+ investor interviews, and a final take-home exam.
sections.redFlags: Several 2022 Fall comments (4): lectures felt unstructured and light on technical depth (contracts, valuations, term negotiation). A few (3): the 12-investor interview/video project grew repetitive with limited learning value. A couple felt class time strayed into off-topic commentary at the expense of skills content.
sections.quote: This is the best class I've taken at Haas. I learned substantially about the VC industry from a founders perspective.
comments: Absolutely, best course I have taken so far.
YES

No I would not recommend this class to others. It tends to assume that students have a significant interest in entrepreneurship (I took it hoping to get more content on the perspective of VCs, like how they evaluate companies). And while we did get some of this through the final project, I found it to be a waste of time that we had to interview 12 investors - after about 8 I feel like we were hearing the same thing over again. Having to then edit it into a video and watch everyone's video in class was also a waste of time - it should be that each group puts together a deck with the insights and shares how they approached the conversations and how the conversations evolved as more interviews were completed. I had also heard good things about Maura, but I honestly don't think she was one of the top professors I've had. A lot of the insights seemed based in her own personal experience as opposed to broader theory/insight gathering and the teaching felt kind of chaotic/not clear on what the topic of each session was going to be and what the takeaway was.
A journey through the world of new venture financing. Extremely engaging lectures and guest speakers. One of the most practical learning experience at Haas that's relevant and current.
Yes. It is a practical course for whoever is interested in venture capital and startups.
Yes

Maybe - if you're really new to entrepreneurship and the fundamentals of fundraising. I came into the course thinking I'd learn more about the quantitative stuff and takeaway hands-on tools that VCs/founders need for fundraising. Instead, it turned out to be mostly a series of theoretical and qualitative lectures around 'how to do entrepreneurship and fundraising right'. I learned more from doing the final take-home exam than I did in all of the lectures! Maura is one of those amazing people that teach many contributing topics that support the primary topic. She is the most compelling instructor I have ever had, and I would recommend any class she teaches on any subject. She stretches us to grow in terms of ambition (what can we hope to solve for the world), ethically, and in terms of output. When we might tire, her example pulls us forward. Her generosity of spirit and generosity giving her time, opening her network to us, and sharing her insights is greatly appreciated and inspires us to want to give back in turn. Yes. Absolutely must take if you are working on a venture or planning to start one in the future
Yes. It serves the objective of the course well, and the readings, cases, components, projects, and assignments do a good job giving us the required know-how of venture financing

Yes, I would recommend this class to a fellow student. The class is inspiring and relevant. The project assignment was also beneficial to investigate your interested segment. The class is also focusing on the every day entrepreneur and see entrepreneurship as a learning process.
Must take if you want to understand VC space and listen to Great Speakers
100% if you are looking to learn about raissing capital as an investor

This is almost my favorite class which provides me with deep substantial learning! You cannot miss this class if you would like to pivot your career as an entrepreneur or at least learn something about how entrepreneurs raise money. I will 200% recommend Maura O'neal as a professor that you should take during your Haas experience. She brings you along every single minute of class and has a humble and human demeanor that is impressive.

This class in incredible. As a full-time MBA, it was absolutely worth giving up 8 Saturday mornings to take the course with Maura and Paul. They are both incredibly accomplished and well-connected on top of being engaging and effective teachers. I highly recommend this course for any student who aspires to be a startup founder. You will build a cap table and exit waterfall, practice negotiating term sheets with VCs, learn how to protect yourself when you sell your company, discuss how to split equity and responsibilities with your co-founder, consider when to pursue non- dilutive capital instead of equity, and absorb many words of wisdom from seasoned entrepreneurs. The main course project is to interview 12+ investors in your industry of interest, which is an amazing excuse to proactively build your network.
This is the best class I've taken at Haas. I learned substantially about the VC industry from a founders perspective. Protect your board seats!
Yes! Super informative!
No, lots of unnecessary of work that doesn't result in substantial learning.

Yes, but the learning will not be substantial... some basic terms on a term sheet like liquidation preference and types of shares... she rambles alot, limited structure in the class and inserts her politics into class.

On a number of occasions she went on mini discussions on how privileged white men are. On one occasion she went to a white male student (Spanish exchange student) and said in front of the class, whats the first thing you think when you see a female interview applicant? Then answered her own question by saying "its that she's a women and less capable isn't it... isn't is?". He responded with "no it is not" and she laughed it off and kept going. On other occasions she brought a guest in who was Indian and began his career in the 1970's and kept going on how white men discriminate in hiring... on another occasion went on about how much of modern medicine is racist because many of the studies are based on white samples and do not match medications to the biologies of minorities.
After the first few weeks I came to expect a politics more than skills - I felt if she focused on teaching contracts, valuations, and term negotiations more, we would have benefited as a class more.
I would recommend for anyone looking to work in startup environments, tons of valuable info on early stage finance. Yes
Amazing class and Adam and Dave are just great professors. Relevant and super interesting topic.

It's a new course, but the client work is super interesting/rewarding - would recommend to fulfill AI requirement. Yes, with caveats. The class is great if you are interested in social impact from a corporate stand point, especially because you work for a really client, however I think that the class was still finding its sea legs when I took it ( spring 2021)

This course was really interesting; without a CSR class offered at Haas this class does a good job of scoping the landscape and detailing how tech for good fits. It's a unique class offering if you are curious about the social impact of technology, how business plays a role, and the interdisciplinary nature of this topic (was really additive to have Goldman students part of the class).

Yes, if the student is specifically interested in the subject matter. It was an interesting survey course for me and I learned useful things for my professional career - that's the goal right? I think some people may get into the course and realize how specific the subject matter is and not be as thrilled. I really appreciated the key take aways in the class and applicability to the real world

Instructors were fantastic! The course was interesting but I think it could use some refinement in terms of content. It felt at times like it was about everything under the sun related to corporate/tech for good. I enjoyed the speakers and would've liked more of those. I also think we should spend more time on critiquing the actual impact of tech for good. It feels hollow without talking about its shortfalls.
Yes! This was a great course to learn about tech for good initiative es and work on client projects that are corporate socially focused.
Yes if you're interested in the topic.

Yes! This was a great way to expose students interested in tech and social impact to work on a meaningful project. Dave and Adam really care about their students and their success in the future. Great AI class!

This was a fun class. It's low lift, and you get to be pretty creative. If you've taken Design Thinking, it can feel pretty repetitive. That said, this was just the first time they were teaching this class - and they have plans to make some improvements. So I think it will be a lot better next year. Both Adam and Dave are really passionate about this topic, and I think that got the students more engaged too.
Definitely recommend this course to people who are interested in CSR or tech for good in corporations. I came out of the course with lots of learning of useful frameworks and cases.
Yes! I loved it and learned a lot. It is so important to emphasize tech for good especially in a time where there is so much distrust of tech.
Yes. Great AI course, working with really interesting clients on projects you can feel good about. Dave and Adam are great teachers.

I'd say your experience in this class depends heavily on the client you're assigned. All in all, this class was unique compared to other classes at Haas and highly applicable if you want to work in the social impact space in tech. Yes, I enjoyed taking this class. It was engaging, productive, and resulted in substantial learning.

Really depends on your case whether this would be a worth a while class or not. The course materials sometimes feel like they are taking time away from the project and sometimes don't align. Very little time to work on the projects as well

Yes. Definitely. Working with a real client and learning more about how a foundation organizes their tech initiatives was valuable in creating a program for the company I work for. I also learned a lot from seeing the outcomes of the other projects and how they worked through their projects. Time is limited, however and it was difficult to do all the interviews and research in the time allotted.
I think the content is useful, and the client work is interesting.

Steve and Adam did a wonderful job being the instructors for this new course. The course at first seemed to lack structure because it's a new course, but as the semester went on there was more relevance and structure to the course. I thought the best part was working with the clients and proposing new ideas to them.
Yes, if they are interested in CSR and social impact (great way to also network with clients)

yes this is a good course. think the project timeline was a little rushed, but definitely a cool experience to work with clients on cool stuff. would have appreciated more informal meetings with client, everything felt like it was a presentation. would have been nice to jsut chat and learn more abt their capabilities and expectations.

I would definitely recommend this course to another student - both those who are interested in social impact and those who are not. Social impact is now a part of every business, and this class teaches you first hand the practical ways that any business can be enhanced by doing good.

No- I struggled with the short length of the consulting project timeline and found the content not as relevant/broadly applicable as I had hoped. It was very focused on philanthropic work at tech companies instead of designing technology/finding use cases for technology to be used for social good.
Yes - more applications of social impact are sorely needed and also very important to explore in becoming an impact- oriented leader.
Yes, they both worked well together, had great snacks, and are very knowledgeable about the subject
Yes. It's a good experience working with the client to solve real-life problems.

As of 2022, this is an easy Applied Innovation, but unfortunately there won't be major learnings gained from the class. The project only takes half of the course (~6 weeks). The beginning of the course is very little work and the project workload is somewhat heaver but you have the class time to work with your groups.

It feels more like "Tech Philanthropy" rather than "Tech For Good." If you're looking for a class that addresses how to solve the negative issues caused by tech (like racial ad profiling in social media or climate impact from crypto exchanges), then you will be sorely disappointed. But if you're looking for an AI course that helps align some tech companies' philanthropic initiatives, then you might like this course.
Yes I'd generally recommend this class because I think it fills a void in the Haas curriculum around CSR and social enterprise foundational learning and applied innovation.

This class does provide an opportunity for practical application with a real world tech for good team. If you would like to explore this space, then I would recommend this as an AI course. However, I did not feel the class resulted in substantial learning when it came to course concepts, so if you are looking for more concrete tools and frameworks, I would opt for another course.

Yes! This course is taught by two great experts in the field and does a great job bringing in outside perspectives to round out the experience, too. Dave and Adam teach very helpful concepts and tools that can be immediately and appropriately applied to the project work, and did a great job sourcing projects.

This course should be renamed as "Understanding different philanthropic models of tech companies". I came into the course thinking I'd understand the ethics of designing tech products and how one can design them for good. I came out of the course understanding how different companies invest their funds into social impact initiatives and the AI project is also based on that thinking. If you take this course, expect a lot of theory on philanthropic/social enterprise models of tech companies. This course did not result in substantial learning for me.
Yes! This course was a great mix of relevant in-class learning and hands-on experience working with a tech company. Adam and Dave are great professors as well!

Know what you're signing up for. This class is NOT about how to design technology for societal good. It is about teams within tech companies using existing commercial products for "good". Way more corporate philanthropy than I was expecting.
yes

Maybe. This class is very focused on the philanthropic work of large and/ or established tech companies, with little to no content on mission driven, purpose built, or even nonprofit companies. This was disappointing to me as it wasn't clear from the course description. The first 2/3 of the class is a conventional lecture. It was only okay. It was EXTREMELY high level, I found it to be far too broad to actually be useful. I will likely not use any of the information taught in the class, sadly. The final third of the class is a client project and can be super hit or miss. Many of the projects were vague and the clients were unengaged. It was challenging to divide work amongst 6 team members at times. Most of the class was devoted to group worktime, which was nice I guess.

Overall, I didn't really learn anything and I think that there are much better AI/ client facing projects at Haas. Consider taking this course if you specifically want to work in big tech philanthropy.

this is an easy AI class if you're looking for that but I wouldn't really recommend unless they substantially change the format of the course. the client projects were interesting and fun but only 6 weeks long and everything leading up to those client projects was brutally boring and a waste of time. nothing was learned.
