In its virtual format, I do not recommend the course. The ability to travel internationally is something that's truly missing from the Haas curriculum, so this class is no different than Haas@Work without the travel component. Putting that aside, the course is almost entirely practical, as it focuses on engaging in an consulting project with an international client. Whitney is an ideal instructor, due to her experiences as a consultant and history teaching the class. She's seen it all, so her comments and suggestions are particularly helpful to improving the quality of deliverables and managing the client relationship.

I would definitely recommend this course to a fellow student. The class is a great opportunity to sharpen and hone typical consulting skills that can be used in all careers - things like public speaking, structuring a problem, working with a team, and driving insights.

Yes, but only when you know what to expect and you're good with it. The professor holds a space for the project team to run, and that's about it. Very little hard-skill training; class contents are mainly about soft skills, e.g. how to handle stakeholders. Had to find my own way to most of the work -- how to conduct market research, how to build a good financial model, how to structure your project in a MECE way, how to draw solid conclusions, etc. Most deliverables are self-driven and don't have a lot of quality control.

I absolutely recommend this course to students. Even though project teams did not get to travel to give our final presentations to our clients in their home countries, we had enough interaction with them that made this whole experience very worthwhile. Whitney did a great job tying in concepts and helping us all along the way.
I'd recommend this class provided it's in person.

Yes, I would recommend the course if you want to get a real-life hands on project with an international client. You work on tough problems and really pick up some consulting skillset such as communication with clients, interviewing, deck building, brainstorming etc. I would not expect to a learn a lot from lectures though - it is more experiential. yes.nice learning journey and good opportunity to make friends.
Yes I would most definitely recommend this course but I think it is best taken in person and not as effective as a virtual course.
Yes, absolutely - this class has a lot of applicability outside of Japan
Highly recommend, we study relevant issues through the lens of Japan but these same issues can/will be found in any developed country

I would recommend this could for anyone interested in Japan specifically and how Japan fits in the whole business landscape in the Asian region. I took this course for the international business aspect and was pleasantly surprised at how involved Japan is. This was an enjoyable course, and I loved the occasional Japanese treats for the students. The course is relatively easy and if you have an interest in Japan may be worthwhile but don't expect to take away any concrete learnings.
I wouldn't recommend as a "must take" just because the topic is so niche, but I really enjoyed it and thought the workload was appropriate. Thanks Jon!!
Yes
Yes, I would recommend this class for sure!
Highly recommend, beyond the obvious if you're interested in Japan, there are a lot of lessons and examples from Japan's business, political, and societal culture that are applicable beyond Japan.

I would recommend this course to a student already familiar with Japan. It appeared beneficial to me for that reason. Yes if you are interested in Japanese business, culture, and history. It's a great course even if you are new to the material, which is applicable globally.

I would definitely recommend this course and instructors to a fellow student. It's a really great way to get real-world experience in the impact VC space and connect with many investors, startup founders and accelerators. Be prepared for a significant amount of time outside of class to juggle intro calls and due diligence work but it's definitely worth it! I would recommend this course to people who are interested in early stage VC investing, but this course is much more experiential (there's less structure/guidance on how to do valuations/due-diligences). I would only take it once you have taken a well-taught course on venture finance.
Maybe - it depends on the student. I would say that overall I learned a lot from working with my team but I don't feel like I learned specific strategies on how to be a better investor.

I would recommend, with the caveat "you get what you put in". How much or little time, effort, commitment and energy you put into the class is what you will get out of it. If you want to experience what is its like to source and pitch early stage impact oriented start ups, this class is for you. However, it is up to you and your team to really commit time and effort to make the most out of the opportunities the course provides. The real learning is in the experience of finding / sourcing the company.

This course gives you real experience of trying to source and invest in an attractive impact startup. It is very self directed, so you'll need to be comfortable in ambiguous and challenging situations. Only the basics are handed to you in this class, but its a great opportunity to learn and bring together learnings from many courses.

This course and the teaching staff is amazing! 10/10 recommend, however, EXPECT A TON OF WORK. Learnings are directly proportional to time put in, but you can't really do the appropriate amount of work to be successful and keep it to a reasonable 2 credit course load.

Yes, Overall the class went well. However, I think that this course needs to assume a much lower base knowledge of students and explain some fundamentals of investing and sourcing. 90% of time and effort was spent on sourcing which was a tiny part of instrcution and support.

Highly recommend! It's super time intensive and one of the hardest sprints I've ever done, so be ready for the time commitment, but it was such a great applied learning experience (hopefully it'll get the AI designation in the future). I loved talking to founders, VCs and deciding what company to pitch. It was super helpful and aligned with my internship search in climate tech VC, too, because it gave me a great reason to be in touch with all of the VCs and accelerators I wanted to get connected with!

Overall, the course was a good introduction to impact investing. I think if the course had a bit more structure and provided more direction, it would be an even better learning experience. The instructors in the course can be a bit harsh and direct, but I think they're just trying to help everyone succeed.
It was definitely a great learning opportunity
I would recommend as an experiential learning opportunity in sourcing early-stage deals, but not as a way to learn core tools of finance.

Yes overall. it was a rich (and very messy) learning experience but I did learn a lot. The course could use a lot more structure and re-working to make it a richer learning experience, but overall HIF is a great way to get hands dirty on the work of impact investing or even VC.

Personally, I got a lot of out HIF as it's directly related to my career goals. It allows you to begin to think like an impact VC and begin to build a solid VC/startup network. It's very important to get on a good team and one that's relevant for your future career as you will be spending a lot of time doing research on that sector. This class is a LOT of work (often more than all my other classes combined) in a very short time. I would only recommend this course if it aligns with your career interests, because so much of it is self taught and time consuming. This class did not provide the technical guidance I was looking for, so you have to find that yourself (e.g., how to value a company, how to create a pro-forma, how to conduct due diligence). Since it's a relatively new course, it may change considerably over the next year, so reach out to the professor/GSI to learn more about the expected time, course material, etc.

At least in its current format, HIF is a class that asks for a ton from you without necessarily promising much in return. SO much of your experience in this class depends on your teammates and mentor. I was one of two people on my team who were very engaged, and we ended up shouldering much of the work. Because there were so few classroom sessions in the beginning of the semester where we learned how to source, diligence, and pitch companies, teams get pushed out of the nest pretty quickly and have to figure things out for themselves. Luckily, our team had an amazing mentor who was an industry expert that we were able to meet with weekly. I heard other teams weren't as lucky with their mentors. This class does provide an amazing platform to get out of the classroom and talk to real founders and companies. In that way, you do learn a lot about how the real world of impact investing works. But it's very trial and error — although the professors made themselves available through weekly office hours, there was very little hand- holding. I think this class is a rewarding one, and is a must-take if you're considering a career in impact investing. But it could be structured better.

I would definitely recommend this class to anyone who is interested in VC. It was helpful to go out in the field and source and diligence investments. This class is a ton of work, especially toward the end, and it's only worthwhile if you put in the effort. It was a great opportunity to learn from experts in the field, however, most of the learning happens on your own and you will only get out what you put in. However, the professors are there to support you and provide a ton of their time through office hours to help you along the way.

HIF was pitched as an exciting "day in the life of an impact investor" where you could make an actual $50K investment if you win - the course has so much potential but ultimately fell flat this year. They tried expanding and grew too big, brought in new faculty to replace Adair who didn't properly structure and organize the class, and despite good intentions across the board, left most people feeling disillusioned. You'll get the following for sure: an interesting team of classmates to work with, an overview of what impact investing is, and an introduction to the VC deal sourcing process. You won't get: a thorough understanding of venture fundamentals, a structured course with real learning objectives, or too much of a relationship with the faculty. Experience probably varies pretty widely. They're trying but it seems like they just jumped into things and didn't thoughtfully plan for how things would unfold. That said, VC offerings are limited, especially for first-year FTMBAs. It's a worthwhile course, but they really have a ton of room for improvement before it becomes anything people would rave about as a "must take"

Take the class if you are interested in exploring early stage seed stage investing. Your mentor matters a lot and so does your sector area (assigned team). It's good practice in sourcing deals and due diligence. I did not like the structure of other students deciding if you present in front of judges (seems like there is some bias there).

Danner is a good professor but students should be aware of the subject matter and only take this course if they are interested in this type of topic. He is probably even more engaging and effective in person.
Not really... is just a class about personality tests. However, the professor is really competent. He should be used to teach a class that adds more value.
Yes I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. It's practical for team building and it keeps you engaged with your peers inside and outside class
Yes, it is in great to dive into a topic many companies are currently struggling with and work with classmates to create practical and repeatable solutions.
I would recommend it only to people who are interested in people ops.
Not the best use of 2 Sundays

Absolutely! He is an expert for his subject matter, his communication style is beyond what one would expect, he makes time to meet all of us one on one but also, holds sessions with each team for the project and gives constructive and specific feedback!!
No

If you've been a part of a group project before, or have struggled to build understand what makes a good team, I'd recommend this class. Just know going in that it can be a bit undefined/ambiguous, and you can take the

project/learnings in different directions based on the perspective you approach it with/your prior work experience. I would but I think it needs to be more consistent involved course to drive value. I also think in person will help if there is a lot of emphasis on course discussions.
No. The instructions were exceedingly vague for all assignments, the Professor doesn't respond to email even in an online class.

The Professor is unprofessional and writes with " bleeped curses " like "^*&!" in emails to the entire class. In what world does a professional in any field write to their entire group of stakeholders with an implied profanity like that? It wouldn't be appropriate for me to email my stakeholders with an implied profanity, it wouldn't be appropriate for high school teacher to write to their high school students with an implied profanity, so how is it appropriate for Haas Professor to write with an implied profanity to his entire class?

I have serious reservations about the class and do not think it provided structure, learning, or insight. Recommend that future students sign up for something else, and recommend the professor revise the syllabus to get substantially more specific. The content of this class would be fluffy even for an undergrad class.

This is a great class if you are actively involved with building teams. Also if you need a 1 unit relatively low lift course to supplement a heavy schedule. Otherwise, read his book and watch the youtube videos/audit this course when more relevant to your career.

It's ok. I would not recommend unless you needed a random 1 credit to fill a requirement. I think you can get the same out of this class as reading his built for growth book, which he essentially covers and assigns as reading for the class. Yes, interesting discussions and thinking points as future leaders
Interesting discussions on teaming, but I feel like there are other more valuable classes. Take if you want a fluff discussion course.
Yes! So worthwhile!
Yes - the course was very interesting and touch topics that are crucial for organizations.
Yes, it was a good class.
Recommend for anyone who wants to look into current challenges of how we work together.
Depends. If you want to learn various personality and work style assessment methods and tactics, then yes. For practical advice on how to structure a team for growth, no.

This is a course with a super light workload and an interesting twist on other people-centered courses you might take at Haas, with strong focus on leveraging personality insights in building better teams.
Most definitely. I think this was a great course to learn about different ways for individual and team growth. This can be applied at all different levels of your professional life.

Absolutely would recommend, this course is all about taking the next step. Appreciate how John took the time to provide builder type, but then follow up by implementing it, explaining it, then providing us multiple frameworks to consider thank you!

I would recommend this course for auditing. The first session had a powerful guest speaker and was filled with engaging content and activity. The 2nd class had a broad presentation for each team. I feel a more engaging 2nd session would make the class great
Not worth the time - too much work for a 1 credit class and didn't learn anything new that wasn't covered in Leading People. Vague and disorganized.

This course is fantastic if you are thinking to be in a position where you will be building teams or looking to put together the right dynamics for growth within an organization or from yourself. I see this as a great extension to Built for Growth the book, given tools and anecdotes to be used in the future. If you are currently a team manager - taking this class will give you instant tools you can use.

This is a class about leadership and tools to evaluate your own leadership and put together teams. It is an easy class and John Danner is engaging, smart and interesting. I did not enjoy the group assignment that was a large part of the course, nor did I find it a worthwhile use of time to spend half of the second class (2 of 2) listening to other groups? presentations.
Absolutely! Animated professor who embodies the defining leadership principles

I would recommend it to the extent that you learn new concepts, however, in terms of workload for a 1 unit course, this was much more work than anticipated. Possibly not have an individual assignment at the end, or make the individual assignment a shorter reflective piece.

I would recommend it. It was refreshing to have more tangible course topics and takeaways that could be readily applied. The prescriptive aspect was complemented with divergent thinking and creative problem-solving.

I would recommend this course as I learned how to work with different personalities in a professional context Yes, I would recommend this course. While there are some insights that could be accomplished by just taking the personality tests, I think being able to discuss it with others and contextualize the impact in an organization was really nice. Professor Danner is a kind and extremely wise lecturer that I think lots of students could benefit from. Overall, creative and engaging course!
It was a useful thought experiment on team dynamics, but there's a lot of ambiguity and open-endedness about the curriculum.
Yes because it was very helpful to me and I learned lessons that will stay with me for the rest of my life. Maybe. I'm not sure the course in practice was what I expected, but he is a fun professor.

I do not recommend. Just make the build for growth test online and ask chatGPT to summarize the book indicating how to compensate for your profile weaknesses. Unfortunately, the group assignment between the classes and the second day of class is time lost to students with any background.
Yes - I think the first class was very informative. I'm not as sure about the second class though (which was mostly presentations by classmates).
Yes

No. I think the course content was very surface level and did not seem worth the time commitment I provided. I would recommend this with reservations. I wasn't fully satisfied with the takeaways I could extract from the course in its current 1-credit form. It might be worthwhile to look at expanding this into a 2-credit class so that we can get deeper into some of the concepts discussed in the class!
Yes
Very high level concepts
This was a very informative, enjoyable, and useful course to take. I strongly recommend it!
Yes, would good course to get an idea about organization structure, framework, and approaches to form successful teams.
Yes
Yes. An engaging 1-unit course which is beneficial in team building
I would recommend this if you wanted a deep dive on building teams and being a leader overall. I think there were enough insights to justify the 1 credit class.

I would absolutely recommend the instructor, great person to learn from. This was my first weekend class (I am a full time student) and the course project was a challenge to coordinate and complete with part timers. I would recommend reviewing the syllabus and assignment before you sign up for the course.
Yes, this class is great for people who aspire to build and lead teams. The knowledge gained from this class is not something you will have learned in any other classes.

Absolutely! I think this class allows you to reflect on leadership principles in a much more meaningful way than other classes at Haas. It goes beyond theory to talk about how you can become a leader today.

Yes, I highly recommend this class. John is extremely knowledgeable in the subject of team building and organization structure. This makes for an informative class, and the ability to allow discussion to proceed in whatever direction it may. Furthermore, John is an extremely engaging speaker, which makes it much easier to endure an 8 hour Sunday class!
I recommend this course to those who are seeking to build highly effective teams that aim to achieve what most teams can only dream of.
Would recommend yes

sections.goodFor: Students who want a creative, hands-on chance to prototype a team-building tool and get feedback, and who value Danner's real-world experience and the guest speaker.
sections.notFor: Students expecting rigorous research or real instruction on high-performing teams - several say the content was thin and the value came from peers, not the class.
sections.workloadNote: ~14 lecture hours across two eight-hour sessions: personality assessments, a few framework lectures, a guest speaker, and team-built prototype tools presented on a demo day.
sections.gradingBasis: Team prototype/tool build plus presentation and slide decks critiqued at demo day; personality assessments assigned.
sections.redFlags: 3 detailed critiques: MBTI assigned though the syllabus admits it is flawed; 4 of 14 lecture hours went to a guest speaker duplicating an assigned documentary; hours of student presentations; disjointed.
sections.quote: Of the 14 lecture hours, 4 were used for a guest speaker to talk about his experiences after the class already watched the documentary of the experiences.
comments: Yes
Instructor is great. Course overall I would but I feel like half a day of presentations and a couple less different personality tests would make it better.

Probably not? I don't feel like I learned something new that I didn't or couldn't from reading/researching myself Yes. Very engaging and encourages you to build a full prototype. Good guest speaker brought in (Jason) and great feedbacks. Very worthwhile
No way. The course is advertised as a lesson on building high performing teams, but it entailed:

1. One eight-hour session wherein we first watch a rower talk about how his teammates all failed and he sacrificed the safety of others to achieve some record. We then took personality quizzes for a few hours.

2. Another eight-hour session where he did not engage in ANY instruction at all. We watched other student teams present AI tools they made that supposedly were meant to help people build and solidify champion teams. However, he critiqued people on how much he liked or disliked their slide decks and — I kid you not — the small talk people made as members of their teams connected to the projector.
AVOID. Unless you want to get some input on the investor deck of an ERM/project management tool you're building. Then maybe take it.
You will learn a lot during the demo day from your other students.

Absolutely! John teaches an excellent course that grounds leadership principles into theory and gives you a creative opportunity to put them into practice through the development of a working prototype tool
Yes. This course provides exposure to leadership and team building concepts.
Yes! Would recommend to students are interested in thinking deeply about how to create the conditions for high- performing teams.
Yes
Yes
100%! you can learn thoughtful leadership
Yes
Yes recommended especially for those who want to use the MBA to build upon self leadership potential and prepare for a strong future teamwork

I came into this course with genuine curiosity about leadership and high-performing teams. I left feeling like the material didn't respect either subject. Assigning MBTI while acknowledging it's flawed in the same syllabus is an uncomfortable position for a research institution. It signals the tool is being used for vocabulary rather than insight. That's a low bar.
What I'd want instead:

Harder questions. Research with more rigorous foundations. Case studies set inside the kind of organizational complexity we actually face. A format that demands more than creative application of a framework and ready to be pressure-tested.
The questions this course is trying to ask are genuinely worth asking. The delivery isn't worth it.
Yes. Otra her y interesting, taught well and overall fun class.
I would not recommend this class for the following reasons.
1. The actual course content as provided by the professor had very very little value.

2. Of the 14 lecture hours, 4 were used for a guest speaker to talk about his experiences after the class already watched the documentary of the experiences. Although inspiring, those experiences had no relevance to the course topic. 3 hours were used to briefly touch on four or five different team dynamic or leadership frameworks that we never touched again. The rest of the class was used to marathon present projects that had no direct relevance to the course description.
3. The class was disjointed and incoherent from a topic standpoint.
4. All value was provided by my peers.

Yes. The course offers valuable insights on how to build stronger, more resilient, and more successful teams. John brings strong real-world experience and research-backed perspectives, making the sessions engaging and practical. The inclusion of a great guest speaker also added meaningful depth. Overall, it is a solid course for developing soft skills that are highly relevant in professional settings.

sections.goodFor: Students targeting climate finance or VC who are self-motivated and comfortable teaching themselves in an ambiguous environment: commenters call the live-deal experience unique, interview-ready, and a rare chance to work closely with knowledgeable, supportive professors.
sections.notFor: Students who want a traditional, structured learning environment; multiple commenters in this inaugural run found it chaotic, with vague deliverables and little formal instruction. Those without any finance, climate, or consulting background often felt they lacked the tools to contribute.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy and largely self-directed: few lectures, lots of out-of-class time sourcing and diligencing live climate deals with your project team.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (8+ comments): inaugural-class growing pains, including vague deliverables, unclear mentor expectations, shifting office hours, and too little formal class time; several (4+): the core task (students sourcing later-stage climate deals) felt near-impossible as scoped; a few (3): newcomers lacked the finance foundation to contribute; isolated: uneven workload across teams.
sections.quote: Its a really cool class and an amazing opportunity. I recommend it for students who are good at self-teaching in a chaotic environment.
comments: I would highly recommend it as it is a great course with a lot of learning.

If you're interested in a career in climate finance this class is a must. Direct, tangible experience learning from industry professionals via a live deal. This class is a unique opportunity to experience life in this career path. However, there aren't many lectures and most learning comes from your own work, so this class is what you make of it. It demands lots of out-of-class time and collaboration with your project team, but the experiential rewards are worthwhile especially if you're trying to pivot into or explore climate investing careers.

This course is great to meet real CEOs and startups with the possibility of investing. Its pretty challenging given the small window of time and funding constraints like Series B and later. The course needs a few more semesters to be smoothed out, it felt a bit bumpy. For those with an existing big network and willingness to explore the network to find deals.
Yes, this is a course where you can get real-world investing experience.

I would. I really enjoyed the class and thought it was super productive in reaching out and strengthening networks. Its an unbelievable opportunity, but thought it could have used a bit of structure after the main classes ended. I felt like there were things I didn't know that I didn't know, which made it hard to ask questions during the advisor meetings. I loved the experience though and think there are a lot a area to improve.

Yes and no, there were things I liked about the course, but overall it was a bit chaotic in its organization and execution. It felt like we given an impossible task (to find later stage deals as a student, without any exposure to investing before) and wished there would have been a bit more direction as to what we needed to focus on. I think the sectors that each team was given either needed to be more defined, or removed entirely. I think the teacher office hours were hard to manage given they changed times every week, and it would have been easier / better to have the office hours during the class time that students already had planned in their schedules. I would have also been nice to have more in person classes / office hours because it was hard to connect with other teams / other students after we stopped having class. Overall, I felt like the class was rushed, and even though I learned through doing (not as much as others because I already came from investing / VC space) I wish there had been more opportunity to learn.

I would recommend this course and teaching team but with some caveats. I think it would be helpful for there to be more layers of accountability for teams and more up front team facilitation-- it requires teams of people who don't know each other to learn to work together immediately and there's not a lot of space to agree on team norms and expectations.
I also wish there was more information about the pitch structure and requirements earlier in the course

I would recommend this course. It's giving me great expertise that I can talk about in interviews. However, I wish I was not in the inaugural class. It seems like there are lots of details that need ironing out. For example, expectations around mentors (from the student side and the mentor side) were not clear leading to our team under-utilizing our mentor. Additionally, I wish we'd spent greater time in office hours, both in length of session and in frequency of sessions. I did not feel like I could go into as much depth around deals as I would have liked to during office hours. Yes, overall the class is helpful to get a feel for what it's like to be a venture capitalist. It is a lot of work and they are still figuring out the course format, but the professors are great people and are willing to help and the class had a lot of good learnings as a whole.

Yes, I would. I know it is a new class and there is progress to be made, but the overall purpose of the class is great. Very cool class concept but needs structural changes to be a worthwhile / effective course. Adair, Todd, and Jeep are really amazing in their fields but didn't feel effective coming together in this structure. There is a lot more learning and impact that could have been realized if there were structural changes and more formal class time. I hope this class continues and iterates and improves - it's really important but would not recommend if there are not changes. I would recommend this class to some students who have a strong interest in originating deals, and investing in potential projects and companies. I wouldn't say this class is made for everyone. Having some sort of a background in finance would also be helpful to any prospective students. All that to say, I would recommend this class to only ~50% of students I interact with. I believe this class needs a little more structure.

In general, I think this class is excellent and must take for anyone in climate. I would recommend that the teaching team is more direct on deliverables and has a bit more guidance along the way. It felt at times that the weekly office hours didn't have any subject - I would recommend to be prepared for each session and with your mentors for maximum impact. Given that this is a 3 unit course, we could benefit from some virtual learning sessions if not all in person. I just felt like class time was too limited and I really would have loved to interface and learn from Adair and the teaching team more. I believe this class will come in handy in my career and therefore recommend the class. I liked the presentations from classmates and guest speakers. Most of the content was relevant. In my career experience, product pricing is one of the most challenging decisions companies make so I consider this class to be table-stakes for anyone looking to go into Product Management (due to Product Pricing considerations & P&L ownership), Strategic Alliances (Partner product pricing and incentives), Business Development (Partner product pricing and incentives), Sales, Marketing. The first 10 weeks are practical and the last 5 are on Auctions/other pricing strategy that would come in handy when bidding contracts, but not so much for me.

One Caveat was that the course structure did not lend itself to the virtual format, in my opinion. As it currently stands, the format lended itself to slacking off then cramming; which ended up being a bad mix for my own learning. This is because the quizzes were relatively easy: the difficult class material was generally optional or re-explained during class; but we did not do a lot of applying forumlas until the exams. Including a GSI + GSI study/review sessions (or maybe it would be fixed by simply being in-person instead of online this year) would have been beneficial to ensure that we were on-track to do well on both the midterm and final exams. Sensei offered frequently to help via e-mail and always proved responsive, but I felt confident in the class material until receiving the practice exams, then it seemed too late to reach out. Make sure to have a study group that you rely on so that when the practice exams are distributed, you can review them together as those 1-2 weeks (midterm/final) proved extremely challenging. That being said, I learned a solid base-knowledge and have reference material for when I need to apply this in the future so the class is certainly worth taking.

I would definitely recommend Shawn Merani's course on new venture finance to students who are not yet familiar with startup ventures and the intricacies of financing in this context. This course offers valuable insights into the landscape of startups, including the different conversations and negotiations that occur within new ventures. However, I would caution students who have no interest in the startup ecosystem or do not envision themselves growing within a startup environment. The course often operates on the assumption that a startup will succeed, discussing how investments will play out in such scenarios. This perspective can sometimes feel distant from the immediate, hard work required to make a startup successful, focusing more on the 'what ifs' rather than the 'how-tos' of initial stages. If you're seeking a deep dive into startup financing and are eager to engage with the potential outcomes of successful ventures, this course is for you

PJ teaches highly relevant and applicable techniques that will help MBAs be literate and effective while working with analytics teams in any industry. Marketing Analytics allows you to get your hands dirty on very realistic problems, gain confidence and expertise on highly valuable skills.

I would highly recommend this course! It is one of the Haas classes that I feel like is most useful in the real world (as data is everywhere these days) and leaders need to be able to communicate with technical folks. Also, PJ is such a great teacher and kind person, and he clearly loves to interact with students! Definitely take Marketing Analytics if PJ is teaching – you won't regret it.

Yes! This is what Data Analytics should be. It's a good blend of working with data, running the models that people use in the real world, and making decisions using data as a person with real–training in management. You aren't going to leave this class as a data scientist, but you will leave understanding what data scientists do. The homework is challenging, but PJ rewards that effort throughout the course by not including a Final, which is a great feature of this class.

Highly recommend PJ and Marketing Analytics! Great way to expand on the high–level topics introduced in the core (Marketing, Data & Decisions, etc.). Very useful class for MBAs who are interested in learning more about data science, working with programmers, or just want to take their analytics skills up a level. The HWs are also very collaborative, so even if you?ve never seen Python before, you?ll be able to reason through the exercises (with the help of classmates).

One of the very best professors at Haas, this feels like somewhat of a hidden gem of a class. PJ is extremely thorough and thoughtful in his engagement with students who come to this class with varying levels of marketing background (including those like me who had never seen Python before). He thinks creatively about attacking a wide range of problems, was informed by countless real world examples, and constantly found ways to make this applicable for our careers going forward.

He is refreshingly honest about what we need to know and don't need to know to be successful in marketing (e.g., all the technical details of how a model runs... we just need to use it!), and could not only dive into the details but also discuss high level approaches to various marketing campaigns.

I think this could (should?) definitely be a core class, or at least the core should adopt his teaching philosophy. It's not as hard of a lift at all as it might look from the syllabus, assuming you show up and are interested, and PJ really walks through everything to make it accessible. Can't recommend enough!

This course is very well designed. Even though you are not going to work in marketing, the cases and python in the class can help you learn more about the data analytics. Don't be afraid of the coding part. Now you have ChatGPT!! It is worth taking.

PJ has set up the materials and structure of this course really well to make Python highly approachable for use in analytics. If you leave the homework projects til the last day or two you may find yourself scrambling badly when you run into issues with the code that cause you to have to invest a bunch of time in chasing down the solution. It is extremely easy to see how the content of this class directly applies into workplace/business scenarios. A super practical and worthwhile course!

I would recommend both the instructor and the course, but it definitely needs some introduction material to help understand what quantum computing is, specially for MBA/non-engineering students.

Would absolutely recommend. She is well connected, well prepared, and well informed about emerging trends in tech. Definitely recommended - Quantum computing felt like a black-box to me up until this class. I'm more familiar with the fundamentals now so it doesn't seem to be as intimidating of a concept anymore!
Yes
Yes
Yes! Great intro to quantum

There is a lot of ambiguity in the quantum world and that's what we all realized in the class as well. The class kind of gets you started and maybe increases your curiosity and gives you slight direction. But a one unit class cannot really clear your ambiguity when industry experts are themselves trying to navigate fairway trying to make sense of things. Come to the class with that in mind.
Yes. I love how Haas (and Rhonda) are trying to offer future-looking courses and making the effort to keep Haas students informed on what's coming, not just about what's already here!

I would recommend the instructor but at its current state, the course material could be much more complex and longer in duration, which would help the material be more effective. Thus, I would suggest the quantum computing to be a longer course than a 2 day weekend class.

I would not recommend this in its current state to a fellow MBA student. I would recommend this - in its current state, recognizing that this was the first time the course was offered! - to a more technical audience, such as SCET, MEng, and other more technical audiences.
Yes, I think the subject matter is fascinating and as a student at Berkeley, to be able to have thoughtful discussions around this bleeding edge technology it is very useful.
A
Rhonda is an Excellent Teacher. I took another class with her: Startup Disco and she was great.
Yes! It's a working process but the potential for this class is huge
No
No. Please don't waste your hard earned cash on this course. Just watch YouTube
Sure, she's inclusive and great
Yes
Yes highly recommend she is very responsive and friendly. Knowledgeable
Yes - Rhonda is great and the course while quite abstract is a great first step
Yes, in case that this is one of the course, which GSPP students can easily access and do not have to pass the lottery.

This is a really great class to learn real consulting skills and learn about the social sector. I bet it is even better experience in person. One thing for EWMBA students to know, it can be difficult to be the only EW student on a team of full time students. Setting expectations of work commitments up front is key.
Yes - incredibly immersive learning experience, even over Zoom
Yes - great on the ground experience. Lots of autonomy, opportunities to connect with different people, learn new skills, apply knowledge learned through Haas

Yes if they are looking to get real world consulting experience. The combination of working with a client, the instructors, and the McKinsey coach made this very beneficial in that regard. The biggest warning would be that this has much more workload then your typical 3 unit class.

YES. I had an absolutely wonderful experience in this class, especially as a non-Haas student. I learned a lot and felt both supported while also being treated like a real professional. It was my favorite class in grad school thus far. No, the class value is completely dependant on the client. We had a bad client and it made the semester a waking nightmare. I dreaded every week of this class.
yes - it was really valuable for me and was one of my favorite courses because it offered an opportunity to work with my teammates

Yes, I would recommend this course to a fellow student, especially for those who want to pivot to consulting or non profit organizations, as you will get to learn a lot of hands on experiences with various of tools.
Students are left to their own devices. Can be good or bad.

I took this class as a policy student, which made it very challenging to manage my time in the spring semester with IPA and Quant. I would think twice about committing to this course given those circumstances. I learned a lot of valuable lessons about working with a team and with a client, which was something I hoped to get out of the course. I didn't find the course as valuable as I would have hoped in terms of frameworks or nonprofit sector insights. Nora is an exceptional coach who pushed us to do our best, although she challenged us a lot along the way.
yes, if student is seeking hands-on consulting experience
yes 100%
Potentially. Having this class virtually was difficult, but the class is very client dependent. Our client was difficult, but others weren't.

Excellent course for those uninitiated in consulting. As it is a real-world project, very relevant and impact-driven. Yes, as a non Haas student, I gained so much from this course in understanding the "business-side" of non-profits and how to be effective and responsible non-profit consultants. Going through the process of taking our client's problem and going through the process of research, converging on key insights, and finally delivering tangible products to them was invaluable. And I had a lot of fun!
Definitely! It's a very hands on class and it has been my favorite class thus far!
Yes, able to practice to an extent what was taught at core.
Yes I would recommend it with a word of caution that this class is A LOT of work. Sometimes I would forget this was a class because it felt like a part-time internship.

Yes, the applied innovation and hands-on work with the client resulted in substantial learning. Being able to solve real- world problems with real-world clients that students are also passionate about also was great!

I would definitely not recommend this class to another person without first priming them on the fact that this class is an incredibly large time commitment. I didn't know that information before signing up and then when I gained an understanding of the workload at the first class, it was too late to back out. It is A LOT of work regularly throughout the semester, including some very late nights and weekend work. I really enjoyed working with my team and made great friends, but it was definitely a point of stress during my semester.

Yes. A fantastic course with a great mix of theory and practice. A ton of work but ultimately I found it very rewarding. I think your team lead can really determine your experience. Would recommend those interested in a project connect with the team lead before the semester to check fit and vibes.
Possibly. Given that I came from a discipline outside of Haas I was not ready for the aggressive amount of time this course required.

This course requires a minimum of 15+ hours per week. As a result, if one has the time absolutely take the course. Be sure to be selective of who your team lead is because this can make or break the experience.

I would recommend but only with the caveat that the experience is heavily impacted by the client, team lead, and McKinsey coach. Be clear on your expectations and that your team lead will make those available to you.
Great class - but be careful about what team you join and what client you have. A great client and team can lead to a phenomenal experience.
If you have some social impact consulting I'd say no.
If you haven't, I think it's valuable but know that there's significantly more work in this class than what we're used to doing at other haas courses.
This course gives you the chance to connect with non profit organization.
You can use your consulting skills for them, but the course is heavily project-based, which means each weeks " class " is mostly working time in a team.
Yes, I would highly recommend this class. There are a number of valuable skills to be learned.

Yes - even if one does not pursue a career in management consulting, the structure and the frameworks are largely applicable to any given field. Also, it's a great way of meeting people in the non-profit sector if that's the line of work you want to do.

If you have not worked in consulting before, I would recommend this course. It gives you hands-on and real-world / accurate experience of what a consulting project is actually like. It is quite a lot of work, so I would be prepared for that. If you have worked in consulting, I might consider a different applied innovation elective to get broader set of experience.
Yes! Such an incredible learning opportunity.

I learned a lot in this class, specifically from my peers who were not in the business school or had different backgrounds. I loved our client but did feel like a bit more support from Paul & Nora would have been helpful - for example, we did not understand how to work with our McKinsey coaches for the first few weeks of the class.
Yes! I think any opportunity for experiential learning and actually serving a client gives you something to leverage in future job interviews.

It is very important to understand how unique this course is. The entire experience depends on your client and assigned team lead, neither of which you'll know much, if anything, about prior to enrolling in the course. It is also a true consulting project. So unless you want to go into consulting I would take another class.

I would recommend this course if students are interested in going through the full life cycle of a consulting project and are interested in the social sector. Keep in my this class is a ton of work, especially given the Tuesday time slot. It did not always feel like a good use of time as conversations can feel circular. This is definitely for someone who likes group work and is fully committed to putting in the work weekly.
Yes, I would recommend if students are interested in consulting or NGO. I would tell them the hours required for this class as well.
If you want to explore your interest in non-profit or consulting, this course is a good start to test that hypothesis. But do expect a lot of extra work outside of the class time.
Yes! The course was a wonderful learning experience! It was a ton of work but well worth it for the learning and hands on opportunity to work with a real nonprofit client.

Of course. The course is helpful in developing organizational, analytical, and team collaboration skills. There is no busy work, the concise and useful content is put to direct use in the client program. The work completed for clients is high impact and has real world application. It is was a great experience taking this course.

I think this course is fairly dependent on the project and the team you get. It is a lot of work compared to other classes. I would recommend this course, as long as students know that it is a lot of work going in and a lot of confusion and revisiting the scope multiple times over the course of the project. You learn a lot and you grow as a team, at the end I really felt like we had an impact.

There seems to be potential for misalignment of objectives / outcomes in this course. We are expected to adhere to a fairly cookie cutter set of frameworks / principles taught in the course, no matter what the client is asking. I often felt what the client wanted / needed to be in direct conflict with what we were expected to produce for our deliverables. I think there needs to be better communication of exactly how we are evaluated in this course and how much time we are expected to put in. Otherwise, it's very difficult to draw the line with the client + team about how much work is "too much" for a given week or how much effort we should put into our deliverables. This is a class after all, and we are not being paid.

Yes I would recommend. It was a lot of effort, but I feel it was super helpful to learn about nonprofit consulting as a MSW student. I enjoyed working with non-MSW students and seeing how they ticked.
Heavy course load. Made the entire semester way too much to handle. Demanding, time consuming with a ssteep learning curve.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Agentic AI
rows.ghostNote: New seven-week course on agentic AI fundamentals, added to the schedule in May with 15 seats reserved for first-years. The most exciting title on the schedule sitting on the weakest, most variable instructor prior in the F26 set (18th percentile, SD 0.97). High ceiling, wide error bars.

sections.goodFor: Students serious about climate finance or investing careers who want live-deal experience they can talk about in interviews, and who are comfortable self-directing; the teaching team is consistently described as expert, committed, and generous with support.
sections.notFor: Students who prefer a structured, traditional classroom: this inaugural run was widely called chaotic, with unclear deliverables, shifting office hours, and underused mentors, and several say a finance background is needed to contribute. One estimated they would recommend it to only about half of students.
sections.workloadNote: Demands a lot of out-of-class time on team deal sourcing and diligence, with few lectures; most learning comes from your own work.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (8+ comments): first-run disorganization, with unclear deliverables, expectations, and timelines. Recurring (3 comments): mentor and office-hour structure was unclear or underused. Recurring (3 comments): little formal instruction, so students must teach themselves due diligence.
sections.quote: Its a really cool class and an amazing opportunity. I recommend it for students who are good at self-teaching in a chaotic environment.
comments: I would highly recommend it as it is a great course with a lot of learning.

If you're interested in a career in climate finance this class is a must. Direct, tangible experience learning from industry professionals via a live deal. This class is a unique opportunity to experience life in this career path. However, there aren't many lectures and most learning comes from your own work, so this class is what you make of it. It demands lots of out-of-class time and collaboration with your project team, but the experiential rewards are worthwhile especially if you're trying to pivot into or explore climate investing careers.

This course is great to meet real CEOs and startups with the possibility of investing. Its pretty challenging given the small window of time and funding constraints like Series B and later. The course needs a few more semesters to be smoothed out, it felt a bit bumpy. For those with an existing big network and willingness to explore the network to find deals.
Yes, this is a course where you can get real-world investing experience.

I would. I really enjoyed the class and thought it was super productive in reaching out and strengthening networks. Its an unbelievable opportunity, but thought it could have used a bit of structure after the main classes ended. I felt like there were things I didn't know that I didn't know, which made it hard to ask questions during the advisor meetings. I loved the experience though and think there are a lot a area to improve.

Yes and no, there were things I liked about the course, but overall it was a bit chaotic in its organization and execution. It felt like we given an impossible task (to find later stage deals as a student, without any exposure to investing before) and wished there would have been a bit more direction as to what we needed to focus on. I think the sectors that each team was given either needed to be more defined, or removed entirely. I think the teacher office hours were hard to manage given they changed times every week, and it would have been easier / better to have the office hours during the class time that students already had planned in their schedules. I would have also been nice to have more in person classes / office hours because it was hard to connect with other teams / other students after we stopped having class. Overall, I felt like the class was rushed, and even though I learned through doing (not as much as others because I already came from investing / VC space) I wish there had been more opportunity to learn.

I would recommend this course and teaching team but with some caveats. I think it would be helpful for there to be more layers of accountability for teams and more up front team facilitation-- it requires teams of people who don't know each other to learn to work together immediately and there's not a lot of space to agree on team norms and expectations.
I also wish there was more information about the pitch structure and requirements earlier in the course

I would recommend this course. It's giving me great expertise that I can talk about in interviews. However, I wish I was not in the inaugural class. It seems like there are lots of details that need ironing out. For example, expectations around mentors (from the student side and the mentor side) were not clear leading to our team under-utilizing our mentor. Additionally, I wish we'd spent greater time in office hours, both in length of session and in frequency of sessions. I did not feel like I could go into as much depth around deals as I would have liked to during office hours. Yes, overall the class is helpful to get a feel for what it's like to be a venture capitalist. It is a lot of work and they are still figuring out the course format, but the professors are great people and are willing to help and the class had a lot of good learnings as a whole.

Yes, I would. I know it is a new class and there is progress to be made, but the overall purpose of the class is great. Very cool class concept but needs structural changes to be a worthwhile / effective course. Adair, Todd, and Jeep are really amazing in their fields but didn't feel effective coming together in this structure. There is a lot more learning and impact that could have been realized if there were structural changes and more formal class time. I hope this class continues and iterates and improves - it's really important but would not recommend if there are not changes. I would recommend this class to some students who have a strong interest in originating deals, and investing in potential projects and companies. I wouldn't say this class is made for everyone. Having some sort of a background in finance would also be helpful to any prospective students. All that to say, I would recommend this class to only ~50% of students I interact with. I believe this class needs a little more structure.

In general, I think this class is excellent and must take for anyone in climate. I would recommend that the teaching team is more direct on deliverables and has a bit more guidance along the way. It felt at times that the weekly office hours didn't have any subject - I would recommend to be prepared for each session and with your mentors for maximum impact. Given that this is a 3 unit course, we could benefit from some virtual learning sessions if not all in person. I just felt like class time was too limited and I really would have loved to interface and learn from Adair and the teaching team more. At times this class felt a bit too open ended, and some structured sessions through the semester (on pitch decks, term sheets, DD, etc) would help. However, this class is EXTREMELY practical and I highly recommend it.

Yes. I learned a lot by doing, enjoying talking to so many different companies. BUT it was a lot of work and as someone with no climate or no finance and no consulting background I often didn't feel like I had the skills or tools to contribute to a team. Make sure you have taken other courses to help prepare for the course.

The objectives of this course, though incredibly interesting and useful in application, are hard to accomplish in practice. It is a difficult investment model to pull off. I think it still remains to be seen how successful the course will be in sourcing the type of deals we were taught comprise "growth stage climate finance" but if we are able to invest in them will be really worthwhile. No matter what I learned a lot about investment as a whole, but might need additional teaching support to ensure that the actual DD of the companies is authentic & quality. The other issue is that most of the mentors that were sourced didn't have the bandwidth to help in the way it was likely envisioned, which led to other lack of quality/expertise in the DD process.
Yes only if the following changes are implemented:
- clear deliverables and timelines
- actual ways to learn how to do due diligence
- upfront communication

Its a really cool class and an amazing opportunity. I recommend it for students who are good at self-teaching in a chaotic environment. If you prefer a more traditional learning environment, this class is not for you.
Top-3 courses at Haas
Yes! The professors are extremely knowledgeable and more than happy to meet and guide students
Yes, they are all expert and understand all cases. Should take this course with them
I would recommend.
I think there is more potential to be explored, but the course is nice, and I learned. I also think it will be better each time, because the professors are very committed.
Yes! Although intense the opportunity to meet and get to know Jeep and Todd and Adair is very worth it
Yes - great real-life skills and experience. Very applied course. The profs were super supportive and always available to workshop ideas or issues.
Yes. It was an interesting course. However, I would like the professors to help teach up the students more before sending them out.
not sure. there could be more improvement to ensure the fairness to all of the students to make sure they got heard before reporting something negative to the university program.
I would not recommend this course, because it doesn't lead to substantial learning. Many topics are covered in Power & Politics, Negotiations, Strategy, Product Management, etc.
This course may be insightful if your knowledge about PM working environment is very limited.

Yes! This course provides an excellent overview of the opportunities/challenges that Product Managers face, and methods for overcoming these barriers. Extremely practical course with real-world applications. Excellent! Yes, it was good.
It was the most practical class so far at Haas, it felt more linked to what we will actually do at work than the rest of the classes.

Yes. The courses taught by Vince are always well designed and structured and often leads to effective, useful and practical learning. The case Vince prepared for this course is very relevant and insightful for the learning objective of this course. Also, Vince prepare videos and readings that are very relevant and easy to digest. (So no 30-page academic research papers or 20-page HBS cases where you need to spend a long time to read in order to find the important information from). I can see that he truly values and respects the time of his students and want us to have a high ROI for the time we invest in the learning the course he teaches.

I would highly recommend this course to other students. This course is an engaging and fun way to understand some basics about the product management industry. I would not hesitate to take this course again.

My feelings are mixed on this class. Especially virtually, it was really hard for me to pay attention during the lecture part of the class. I thought the meta activities and stakeholder monopoly were great. Some of the speakers weren't great and I didn't get what the point. I had a hard time paying attention and think I would have to some degree in person too. I think this class could improve by being more hands on and less listening to other's experiences. If you don't have any previous PM experience and never facilitated meetings/projects before, this is a great course for you.

Vince Law and Sam Ham make a great team! I really enjoyed both of them as facilitators, and they were always very well prepared for class. They have great work experiences that can be applied to their teachings as well. I would recommend this course more for students who don't have any PM or related experience designing or implementing software/systems. My favorite part of the course were the Thursdays where we were able to hear from alumni from different companies and sometimes roles -- they were very relevant to us and widened our perspectives on the scope of PM.

I wouldn't recommend this course if you are trying to learn about how to be a PM. I found the subject matter too general to be helpful. It felt more like a class about soft skills needed to work in teams rather than a course to prepare you for PM.

It depends. Class is very light for the 2 units assigned (the easiest 2 unit class I have taken), but at the same time the value is somewhat limited. I would recommend this to someone who doesn't really know anything about PM and looking to understand the role better, but if you have some experience / knowledge in the field then I only would take it if you need 2 easy units
Yes, immensely valuable — great for understanding the world of PMs, Tech, and cross functional partnerships. Vince and Sam are fantastic teachers and having this time with them is precious.
Absolutely! This course is super helpful who anyone interested in the tech industry or looking to polishing their soft skills.
As someone with no prior PM experience, I thought this was an interesting elective and would recommend it as a relatively low-lift class.
Yes for those who are certain that they would like to go into PM. I wouldn't recommend it to those who are uncertain since it may not be as applicable.
Yes - good from workload perspective and very helpful for people preparing for interviews.

Professors are kind, and have a lot of experience. While I did learn some cool things, I don't think the learnings from lectures are anything super useful unless you have no background in the tech / PM space. Great class structure though, and lots of organic interactions take place. Also great to be a quarter class.

I would recommend this course someone looking for a relatively low-lift 2-unit course, or someone with absolutely no background/understanding of product management in the tech industry. You'll learn about PM/tech vocabulary and topics at a very high-level. If you've worked in tech or have PM experience, there's very little value add. this is really worth itif you want to learn how to influence and lead teams of people effectively
Sam and Vince are great instructors who have substantial knowledge of the material and have been successful in their industry roles.

Yes, this course provides a lot of relevant content for aspiring PMs, particularly on the interpersonal skills aspects of the job rather than just the technical product development. Guest speakers are very relevant, and the case we use each week is low reading while high value in illustrating concepts. Overall, the course is relatively lighter lift while being very engaging. Vince and Sam are very helpful in bringing their own experiences to the course.

This is a pretty fluffy organizational dynamics course that is not a substitute for taking Product Management. This is probably a good course for someone 100% planning on going into big tech/PM but as someone in a different space I didn't get much out of it.
If you plan/hope to be a PM, this class will give you some helpful tips and tricks to consider.
Definitely! Vince and Sam are wonderful teachers with an enormous amount of shared experience in product

management. The concepts and methods learned in this course are all based on real-life situations and I now feel much more prepared to face difficult work dynamics in the tech industry. I highly recommend this course!
Yes, overall this is a great introduction to the function
Yes! I thought the course was a really helpful one if you're interested in going into PM. Sam and Vince are great! Yes
For those interested in product management, this course would be worthwhile. For those who aren't, it isn't. Also the professor will email you if you miss class, its a little weird.

There might be more worthwhile courses for deeper learning but I do think this class had some real-world tips that will be more directly applicable to things I will be doing in the future than other classes at Haas so it's a good course to balance with more technical classes.

Vince and Sam are really nice. The class seems designed to be low-effort rather than to provide substantial learning. If that's for you go for it, but don't expect to improve your team facilitation skills.
For someone without tech industry experience who is going into a PM or adjacent role there is some value in learning more about the environments which PMs operate in.
10/10 would recommend this class. I learned so much in 7 weeks and feel a lot more confident heading into my summer PM internship!

I would definitely recommend this course to anyone who is interested in applying for a PM role. The course content reinforces PM best practices and introduces students to a cohort of peers seeking similar roles. The instructors are super knowledgeable and are a great resource for career advice.
Easy class with tangible takeaways - would recommend!
Yes, only if they are interested in product related roles and want to work on soft skills. This course has a very niche focus and may not be for everyone.

This is a light lift class and would recommend taking this for learnings on the soft skills of being a PM. Vince and Sam bring in guest speakers every week and the course load was effective but not very heavy. Class discussion was interesting and there was a lot to be learned from peers.
Highly recommend - great real life experience, approachable in career advices, amenable to student feedback and cares about our careers as PMs
Yes, if you are interested in product management with no experience, this is a great intro into the "soft skills" of being a PM.

I would recommend this to a first year spring student before their summer internship and if they are pivoting to PM. Its a really manageable lift and the professors are both extremely thoughtful, knowledgeable and kind.
Yes if they are interested in PM
Yes, pre-training for stepping into a real PM job.
Yes. The course is useful. However, I took New Product Development Process with Vince last semester and some content is overlapped.

Definitely not. In fact, I have talked to several of my peers from this class and I have heard the same response. This is probably the most useless class I have taken here at Haas so far (as someone who is trying to transition into PM). You don't learn anything more than you probably already know. Plus, this class is such a drag. You go to class on Monday, sit there for 2 hours just to have a class discussion that is close to pointless. And all your peers are working on something else on their laptops. The only somewhat benefit I have gained is from the Wednesday sessions when some guest speakers are invited. There are definitely better classes at Haas that would be more worthwhile for your time and money. However, if you want a VERY low-lift class that you can work on other things, this might be the class for you. I think this course has a lot of potential, but some aspects like the assignment pacing need to be rethought (the interview time turnaround for the first assignment was tough and it felt like it took a while for the other assignments to hit. It was also challenging to see the relevance of the non-interview assignments). However, I think that it's good exposure to 'PM-y' language and thought processes, so it could be a good intro for people new to PM.
Yes, lots of soft skills learned and I feel more prepared heading into my first PM internship. Every week there were guest lectures and they brought in really valuable insights and advice.

If you know nothing about PM, this might be a helpful class to take. However, given that this is a spring course, most students interested in PM will already have a good understanding of what it takes to be an effective PM through coffee chats, speaker panels, etc. in the fall. If that's you, I would not recommend this class - the content covered is quite broad and general, and I don't feel like I learned a ton. But if you have zero baseline knowledge of PM, this would be an interesting class to get that exposure. That being said, Sam and Vince are great instructors who are very helpful and kind.
I don't think I know more about facilitating a team after taking the course than I knew before.
Yes. This course provides practical experience for students to become a product manager.

I really wanted to like this course and was so excited that Sam and Vince were teaching it. They are phenomenal teachers and have a wide range of experience but when I got to the first few classes, I slowly realized this class was a huge waste of my time. The content for the course needs to be totally revamped. We had a whole class where we talked about if design thinking was dead and so many more classes like this is where we should have learned how to facilitate and lead discussions as a PM. Being a PM is difficult and most people don't have a technical background and are going to work on somewhat technical projects. This class should be geared more toward leading discussions when you need to get engineers to do something they might not necessarily want to do and then give them candid feedback on this. Unless they revamp the course, don't waste your time taking this and instead take power and politics. yes. for someone who wnats to be a pm, i would highly recommend taking all classes that vince teaches
would be nice if the class had a field trip option on a wednesday. i liked the guest speakers.

Not really. If you're expecting an actual PM class that goes over how to manage/develop products, you'll be disappointed. This class is more on how to manage teams that you would work with as a PM and focused on soft skills and political structure of a PM. Useful, but any student with work experience working with people would find it repetitive.
Yes! its a light class with lots to learn about how to navigate corporate/start work environments and how to convince management.

I would not recommend this course. I have been a big fan of Vince so enrolled this class but it was quite disappointing. Simply listening to each person's experience in every class made me easily bored. The cases we covered in class were also too fictionalized and didn't really resonate with me. I think it would have been better to have individual business cases from HBR or something.
Yes to both, with my only caveat being that I couldn't help at times feeling that I wanted a bit more of the things that I mentioned in the " areas of improvement " section
Depends

Donatella brought so much positive energy and enthusiasm to the class, encouraging us to want to learn even late in the evening. But overall, while I loved the intent of this class, the delivery felt disorganized and hard to follow. I describe it as a combination of finance 101, coding 101, and ESG 101. By doing so many little things in such a short class, it ended up feeling like we did not get enough time to go deep on the material and take up any new practical skills. Although not on the syllabus, we did end up having a group presentation and a short final. Guest speakers and student presentations were great!
This course was very..confusing.

Donatella is fantastic and her guest speakers were amazing! On the finance side I think it was really beginner level stuff — good if you want a refresher, not so much if you have a strong background in finance
If you're trying to create your own portfolios, this isn't the class for you. It's more of a good overview on how ESG focused portfolios are created.
Yes
No, the theory we learned is a summary of the finance core class. Not a lot of practice on python or sustainable funds, which could've been the novel parts of this class.
I would definitely recommend Donatella as an instructor. I think this course is valuable but should be extended to better cover all of the relevant material.
Yes! I feel like I have a better understanding of portfolio theory now and solidified what I learned in core finance course. I enjoyed our class speakers too, very interesting topics.

I would definitely recommend the professor, but the course title is misleading. Most of the course is geared toward traditional portfolio construction and material learned in core finance. It's disappointing for those who came in looking for an ESG investing class because it's barely addressed. Hopefully, they adjust this class to focus more on ESG. Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend this course to fellow students if it were to stay in its current format. The course attempted to accomplish too much, in the end accomplishing less than desired.
No, unless you need this as a pre-req - it felt repetitive to core finance and didn't get into new ESG-related material until the very end.
Yes for learning about portfolio construction and modern finance theory and applying those learnings

Would recommend if you already have a solid finance foundation and some experience in Python. Linking what we learned in class (Python basics and modern portfolio theory) to actually constructing a sustainable portfolio without a background on either (besides Core Finance) was difficult. It could be due to the short course or lack of experience in finance or coding. That being said, the guest speakers were very interesting and informative and Donatella is very passionate and well-informed on the topics.
I would absolutely recommend taking a class with Professor Donatella. She is very enthusiastic about the class material, is very knowledgeable, and listens well to student questions and concerns.
If you are curious to learn how python can be used for portfolio construction and engage with likeminded sustainability oriented students, this is a good course.
Excellent course to dig deeper into portfolio theory and an overview of ESG investing.
Please note that a lot of this class is on Modern Portfolio Theory and not on ESG investing.
Not really
It depends. I think Professor does a great job at breaking down portfolio theory as best as she can, but that's not necessarily what I wanted to take this class for.

This is a great course for anyone interested in managing their own investment portfolio, or pursuing a career in investment management. The course blends core finance theory, application of ESG criteria to investment choices, and powerful tools which enable the student investor to evaluate large amounts of data in order to design optimal portfolios for given objectives.

I would recommend this to students who are interested in impact investing/socially responsible finance. I took away new information from the class, and the guest speakers were really interesting. I do, however, think students should manage expectations about how much time is spent on the sustainability aspect, as the first two sessions were mostly a recap of teachings from core finance classes. Perhaps the class would be more impactful as a longer 2-3 credit course -- it went by too quickly!
Yes, as she has great experience and does well in teaching this crucial finance topic
Yes. Solid class if you don't have a finance background
I would like to see that the content is considered with the other courses in mind before recommending Yes. Great class and professor. Good workload for a 1 unit class

I would not recommend this course to a fellow student because the learnings were unclear. We went over some concepts from core finance and the sustainability aspect was dismissed. So I'm not quite sure what I was supposed to learn.

If you already understand basic portfolio management concepts, this course is not likely to be additive. The "sustainable" component of the course was minimal and was really just a refresher on concepts like the efficient frontier and Sharpe ratio.
Yes. The subject matter is interesting and I enjoyed her as an instructor.

Yes, I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. You'll be refreshed on some material that you already know, learn something about new topics, and engaged by new directions that you can take.
Yes!
Yes, you will learn a lot.
Yes highly recommended - A good class to get an understanding of ESG fundamentals & portfolio construction. Although the workload is a bit more than 1 unit.
Yes. Just good overall for portfolio construction, not just sustainable investing.
Yes. It is a nice overview of what sustainable portfolio means
With some minor changes (more instruction, less lectures, maaaybe in-class emphasis on Python and how it relates to building models) I would recommend this class.
