I would recommend this class to any student who wants to work in asset mgmt. or finance overall. The theory of this class serves as a basic principle of portfolio construction
Yes.
I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student because you will learn very specific industry knowledge necessary to be successful in finance.
YES!!!!
Yes. Super interesting course if you are interested in Finance.

It's a great intro/review for CAPM and MVO from core finance/asset management plus a in depth discussion on how it relates from an ESG lens. Donatella brings a lot of energy. The class went by quick and was fun. Bring questions!

Not if you work in finance. This course barely discusses sustainablity as it relates to portfolio construction at all. It is merely a "basic of investing" class geared towards non–investment professionals. If you actually have an interest in ESG investing principles, don't waste your time.
(the professor is super nice though)
Yes.

Donatella is extremely knowledgable and engaging as an instructor but the course content is less about the practical challenges with sustainable/impact investing and more about fundamental portfolio construction concepts. The guest speakers were thought–provoking but be warned that 50% of the course content is not specific to ESG or sustainability concepts.
I'd recommend this course over the 2–credit Asset Management course as it efficiently covers similar subject material but with a sustainability lens that's relevant to current market trends.
Yes – the professor is great and for the short class schedule it is highly valuable.
instructor yes, class no.
Yes – wholeheartedly
If you want a technical perspective on portfolio construction, take this course. It does not go into the sustainable part that much..

This class was a great way to solidify principles of portfolio construction and understand how the push for ESG/sustainability influences not only portfolios but companies and governments. I would definitely recommend if interested in the topic.

rows.title: Reinventing Capitalism for a Sustainable, Humane and Equitable World

comments: If you want to be in a highly interactive class where students participate a lot this is a good fit for you! The speakers are excellent. Gloria is really enjoyable! It is a place where all the 1st and 2nd years who are interested in impact are so its a good place to connect with classmates cross years and cross cohorts that are likeminded! I really enjoyed the cases she chose.

Yes! Gloria is personable, thoughtful about the curriculum she puts together for the course, brought incredible guest speakers from her network and was a pleasure to connect with outside of class in office hours.

Really good class! Gloria is an amazing teacher! For me personally, the course was a lot about being introduced to new discussions I never heard before (while other folks where much more versed on the topics and I got to learn a lot from them). The course is not a huge lift, but it's definetely more worthwile if you have the proper time to do all the readings and engage in the conversations. I would think twice before taking the course in a very busy semester. This class should become part of the Core, every MBA student in the US should take it and rethink a lot about what should be done for business

So excited this class is available! It is my favorite class I've taken at Haas by far. I would definitely recommend this class because it really creates space for important discussion around capitalism and the role we can play as members of civil society and the private sector in shifting capitalism in a way that makes it more sustainable for all of us. This course should replace the core ethics course. It effectively defines values to improve the common good, and explores how to adjust capitalist structures to benefit people while creating value. The course is well structured, and most of the guest speakers are fantastic. The biggest con is the people who sign up- everyone is great, but they self- select a very common viewpoint. We needed more people to challenge common opinions and create a more diverse discussion.
Yes, it's a great way to understand how as future leaders we can make progress towards a more equitable and sustainable society.

This class is a great complement to a business-focused curriculum. It provides a whole range of alternative approaches to capitalism and thinking about the purpose of business and our roles in it, and was very useful. Even people who already know exactly what they want out of their career would benefit from taking it!

Yes! I learned a lot from Gloria and the other students. The readings were interesting and class was typically fun to attend. I'll say that it's not as heavy on content as Systems Thinking or other courses I've heard about addressing similar topics, so that's something to keep in mind.

Gloria did a great job leading class and discussion probing us to think more deeply about the sessions each week. It was a great class to bring together students across disciplines to have a deeper discussion about what is possible to reimagine the system we are in. Reading and discussions were all very thoughtful and the speakers are all great. I would recommend this instructor and course to a fellow student. The class highlights many of the most important issues of the day, and gives a lens with which to look at them. As someone who came in with less experience thinking deeply about these issues, the class provided a platform to do so. It opened my eyes and allowed me to see the world in a different way. Isn't that was education is all about?
This class is a must take, simply put.

If you are being exposed to what's wrong with capitalism and the potential solutions for the first time, this is a great introductory course. If you've already done a lot of study in this area, however, I think you will be disappointed by what the course has to offer.

Yes! It's a great class to learn more about different ownership models, the pros and cons of different initiatives. However, it important to keep in mind that most of the discussions are still within a capitalist framework This is a class pushing actual critical thinking as a business class - it was so refreshing compared to my other classes. So glad I took it and loved the community of the peers who also chose to take it!

Great class to reflect on interesting and relevant topics, to hear your classmates opinions and experiences, and hear excellent speakers. Save some time to do the readings, cause a big part of the learning comes from there, and just attending classes is not enough.
Yes - this course addresses a gap in MBA curriculum which connects personal values to business levers. I appreciated the encouragement to turn learning into practical application.

Yes, I would recommend this. I would also encourage students to be more vocal about their opinions, irrespective of what side of the spectrum they are on. Discussion is the best way to get as much value as possible out of the class. This is overall a low/medium-effort course that allows for great guest speakers/interesting topics to be discussed. Truthfully not the most amazing class I have taken, but was a refreshing outlet for otherwise traditional business classes.

I think the course depends heavily on the makeup of your class as well as it's strongly weighted towards group/in-class participation-- so if you want to take this class, I recommend convincing all your friends to take it too. Yes - this should be a course in the core at Haas in my opinion.

I think the course structure would need to be improved considerably for me to be able to recommend the class. The topic and readings were great, but the format of the class not, so that made it feel like a burden each week. I would definitely recommend this class. The guests and the readings are very relevant and unique - and above all, it was a great way to create community with like-minded and values-aligned classmates - which is invaluable.

sections.goodFor: Students who want a small, discussion-heavy seminar on alternative capitalism and social impact business models, strong guest speakers, and a close-knit class community.
sections.notFor: Students wanting tangible implementation tools or a real critique/deconstruction of capitalism; examples are US-centric and skew to small companies, and value depends on engaged classmates.
sections.workloadNote: Reading- and discussion-driven: liberal-arts Socratic seminar style with readings, debate and guest speakers. 'Be ready to read and debate.' Hours not quantified.
sections.gradingBasis: Seminar discussion and participation; the class depends on everyone showing up engaged. Grading not otherwise discussed.
sections.redFlags: Two students note the material is US-centric, small-scale in its examples, and light on how to implement the ideas; discussion quality depends entirely on classmates being prepared and engaged.
sections.quote: I would with the caveat that the challenges and solutions that we discuss in class are 1) very US-centric, 2) somewhat small-scale
comments: I would recommend this class, it's a really unique opportunity to examine complicated issues that are very relevant in to business, government, society, and our futures. The class relies a lot upon everyone showing up and wanting to explore these topics, so it's important to be invested and engaged, otherwise the discussion can be lacking. I think this is the most enjoyable and interesting course I've taken at Haas so far - the course was very non-business school structured, more liberal arts socratic seminar stye with readings and debate and discussion, developing relationships with the people in the class, and listening to awesome guest speakers. The guest speakers in this class were the most interesting and inspiring people I've interacted with on campus.
Highly recommend, be ready to read and debate!
I really enjoyed this class
Yes, if you are willing to stir the pot and challenge the prevailing group sentiment. Also, if the class structure changes to have more debates between opposing perspectives.
Yes! Gloria is not only a great professor but also a great person, she was a really warm and nice person, perfect for this course!

I enjoyed the conversations, the classmates truly make the class- people were engaged and brought in different perspectives which I probably haven't thought about before. Gloria brought in AMAZING guest speakers too. All in all, I would recommend:)

This class is great! Didn't really think I would enjoy it that much but signed up for it cuz it worked for my schedule but I actually learned a lot in this class. Gloria is so supportive, compassionate and kind. It was a pleasure to spend a semester with her.

I would recommend this course as a great introduction to alternative forms of capitalism. There is much to learn, and this course provides great breadth for a student exploring where they may want to make an impact.

Yes - Gloria is a great facilitator, and the class has some amazing speakers that come in! I also think this class is small enough for you to really get to know your classmates better. It also helps you better articulate values that matter to you.
Yes - Gloria does a good job of creating community and introducing interesting ideas to the course. The speakers she brings in are also fantastic.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this course to other students who are interested in understanding now just how to support shaping and changing capitalism, but also for better understanding the philosophical underpinnings of corporations and how they are being adapted and innovated upon currently.

I would with the caveat that the challenges and solutions that we discuss in class are 1) very US-centric, 2) somewhat small-scale -- many of the companies reinventing capitalism are on the smaller side, 3) student-driven with lots of student discussion.

Yes, I definitely think this is an important class for all business school students and future leaders to take! We're at a point where we need to start prioritizing more than just profits, and I think this class provides different ways to do that while still running a successful business
I would! I met and learned from so many amazing people, not just Gloria and the speakers she brought in, but my fellow classmates. It was a really great community to be in!

It depends on what you're looking for. I expected to leave the class with more tangible ways to challenge capitalism, but in retrospect, the class is called "reinventing capitalism," which implies working within existing economic structures. I think a course more focused on challenging and deconstructing capitalism would have been more interesting. That said, I did learn a lot more about innovative social impact business models than I knew before, which is useful to know as I continue my career post-Haas.

I would recommend it - it did a good job of opening my mind. I wish we were able to dive even deeper into how to implement some of these concepts, but learning about them in the first place was a fantastic start.

sections.goodFor: Students who want an overview of alternative models of capitalism, enjoy reflective/experiential assignments and value the guest speaker roster.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting concrete business content, rigor or debate - critics call it surface-level, an echo chamber, with infantilizing activities; skip if you already agree with the premise.
sections.workloadNote: One student reports routinely 4-6+ hrs/week for a 2-credit course: dense readings, weekly experiential activities plus write-up reflections, and a semester-long project.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly reflections/activities and a semester-long project; 2 say deliverables and grading were unclear and changed mid-semester.
sections.redFlags: 3 detailed critiques: surface-level content and messy delivery, shifting assignment instructions, semester project first raised in March, an unannounced Easter-weekend simulation, unresponsive prof/GSI.
sections.quote: This course also had far too much work for a 2-credit course. I have routinely spent over 4-6 hours a week in preparation for this class.
comments: I would want this course to be redesigned for greater impact and a more challenging approach before recommending it. The material was sped through and was surface-level at best. I don't believe we redefined anything. Gloria is passionate and enjoyable to interact with, but the presentation of the material was messy, the grading and deliverables unclear, and the weekly reflections are infantilizing at best and offensive at worst.
No. Many of my classmates were very engaged with this class, but I really don't think anyone coming to Haas for tangible and concrete business would get a lot of use out of it.

This was the worst class I took at Haas. If you feel like you already understand that the current state of capitalism is bad for us, you're not going to get anything more out of this class, so stay far, far away. Gloria is a perfectly nice person and I took it because the title seemed interesting and because I heard from people who liked her other classes. But it feels like she has no idea what she wants this class to be yet. It had so much potential and started strong, but I don't feel like it ever got around to the actual "reinventing" part beyond the first two classes where we talked about alternate forms of capitalism. There were also just WAY too many activities that felt extremely middle school ("go spend time in nature!"). I ended up skipping a lot of the very dense readings because the reflections took too many hours between doing the activities and doing the write up every single week. The classes also sometimes seemed to have no aim and it felt like we were just killing time until the guest speakers came. A lot of class time pre-speaker would be us sharing our feelings from the reflections and very little conceptual lecture. When we did have conceptual lecture, it felt very elementary. In general, it felt like the course content was aimed at changing people's minds about capitalism = good when in reality most of us took this class because we were already there. This class shouldn't be offered again until she has a better idea of what she wants to do with it, besides making it a speaker symposium class. She and the GSI were also pretty unresponsive. All in all this class was a huge waste of my time and credits and I really regret taking it. Feels bad saying that because she's such a nice person, but it's true.
Yes, if you want to change the world, this is a must-have course! If you wish to change the world while keeping your core values as you navigate capitalism, this is a mandatory course!
Would recommend - thought provoking class that gives a helpful overview of the menu of options that exist to build a capitalist system.
Good learning if you're willing to invest in the readings / class discussions. Great speakers.

No I would not recommend this instructor or course to a fellow student. I had much higher expectations for this course. By nature of this class being an elective with a somewhat provocative course name, the students in the class already largely all had similar opinions despite coming from various different schools at Berkeley (ie- Haas, Goldman, etc) and having different backgrounds. During discussions, the class quickly became the same repetitive echo chamber praising and complaining about the same topics in very similar ways. At the beginning of the semester, multiple students suggested that the professor and GSI implement anonymous " devil's advocates ": 1-2 students assigned (via email before class) to pressure-test assumptions and opinions voiced in class by respectfully disagreeing or dissenting and bringing up alternative thought processes instead for discussion. Despite the professor and GSI nodding and taking this into consideration, it was never implemented.

Ironically, this class on reinventing capitalism for a sustainable, humane, and equitable world was one of, if not the most, economically dissonant courses I have taken at Haas. There were several weekly assignments that were significantly disconnected from the reality of people's everyday lives in a way that was derogatory towards others. The most notable one being to interview a service worker about essentially why does life suck for the average American worker. The assignment literally said " Bonus if you have the conversation over coffee or a meal, your treat " as if essential workers should be oh so thankful so as to accept the gracious charity from some super duper smart fancypants Cal grad student in exchange for a conversation where a random nerd gawks at their life situation. This course also had far too much work for a 2-credit course. I have routinely spent over 4-6 hours a week in preparation for this class. The instructions for weekly assignments and for the semester-long project would change in the middle of the semester which was confusing especially when the syllabus and bCourses announcements gave different instructions. There was not an introduction to the semester-long project back in January when the class began. Instead, the prof brought it up as an aside in March to remind us that our semester-long projects should be about halfway done. This blindsided many individuals in the class who were barely aware of the project or that was supposed to be treated and planned differently than a " final project ". For another weekly assignment, we were told on a Monday in class that we needed to clear our schedules at 12pm and 5pm the upcoming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday for a simulation that was not scheduled in the syllabus or mentioned at all previously. This caused multiple people in class to have to change pre-scheduled weekend plans on short notice, and the icing on the cake was that this was Easter weekend as well.

Between unclear assignments, barriers to completing assignments, an echo chamber of students without prof/GSI encouraging different perspectives, and lack of in-depth deep dives on any topic, I did not enjoy this course nor would I recommend it to others. To barely ever mention how wealth in the U.S. is currently distributed by race because of historic and present-day racist policies and to have never mentioned anti-consumerism was a shock to me. This course lacked diversity of thought, and because of the self-selection of students who choose this course, I had at least expected to learn more deeply about any topic at all instead of glossing over a topic for barely an hour to then have a random guest speaker there to promote their business.
YES HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Gloria is an amazing professor who is humble, genuine, and incredibly well connected:)

sections.goodFor: Students already in or entering biotech/pharma/healthcare who value direct access to big pharma, small biotech and VC leaders; better after an M&A class.
sections.notFor: Beginners with no pharma/biotech or pharma finance background - 2 say it is not taught as an intro; also those wanting quant depth or teaching rather than speakers.
sections.workloadNote: Two Sunday sessions only one week apart plus project work in between; 2 students say the load is too heavy for a 1-unit class and ask for the Sundays to be spaced further apart.
sections.gradingBasis: Project work and assignments between the two Sunday sessions; specifics not described.
sections.redFlags: Runs like a speaker series with little actual teaching and does not match the syllabus/course description (2 comments, one calls it 'a waste of time and money'); workload too heavy for 1 unit (2); light on quant.
sections.quote: It was more like a speaker series or a seminar where we heard from different speakers (all great) but there was not much teaching involved.
comments: Yes
Yes I would but with a caution about lack of hard/quant learning
Yes, the learning and insights you get from the instructors and guest speakers were truly inspiring, highly recommend if you are in biotech, or consider a career in this field.

Kim and Shalini were great. But the course format can be improved a lot. Loved that we got to hear from a lot of different prominent leaders in big pharma, small biotech, VC. But the course load was a lot. One recommendation is to split the two Sundays further apart so that there's enough time to do the project work. This is a heavy lift for 1 unit class with just one Sunday apart.

Yes, the most engaging classes I've been in. The wealth of experience provided by the guest lecturers was amazing. Having industry leaders in class made it very easy to understand the practical applications of theory. Their unique backgrounds provided excellent perspective on the biotech industry as a whole.
Yes - recommend any of Kim's classes - I always leave with a new perspective and resources that help me in my career. Yes but would recommend an M&A class before to get the most out of it

I would not recommend this class. The syllabus and course description was completely different from the actual class format. It was more like a speaker series or a seminar where we heard from different speakers (all great) but there was not much teaching involved. For someone who doesn't have a background in Pharma/Biotech or Pharma finance and is looking to learn as a beginner, this class is not it. The workload was also too heavy for a 1 unit class. No
10/10 if you are in bio/pharma/healthcare world
Yes!
Yes, if you are at all interested in the space, gives a great overview and practical application of it through the course work and assignments
Definitely. Bot Shalini and Kim are amazing professors with incredible experience and bring amazing speakers that bring great value to the class.
Not at all what a waste of time and money felt like a conference
Yes, but I would caution them against what I consider an undue amount of busy work
I would not recommend the course or the professor.
yes, i would. I think leading teams and management should be fundamental part of our learnings at Haas.

Maybe yes. I think this year was the first year of the course, so it was expectedly a bit bumpy, but I can tell that it will improve. I think Brandi has a lot of great teaming gems in this class, and if some of the unnecessary work gets shaved off then I would recommend. I just didn't like the fake teaming work that tried to apply the concepts in a fake simulation.
Yes. There is a lot of work with the readings and simulation, but also a lot of opportunity to learn more about operating a diverse team and the theories behind creating a more impactful team.
I'd be indifferent - it depends on the opportunity cost of the credits. It's certainly better and more useful than just sitting at home, but it's on the lower end of worthwhile courses at Haas.

Yes - I would recommend this class to another student. I would let them know that although I didn't necessarily enjoy the class each week, as a whole I feel it was very helpful in reflecting on my leadership style and managerial abilities. It also taught me the importance of various aspects about team design, which were useful.

Would recommend this class if you have lead or are leading a team. Many times we as managers got where we are because of our positive results to our organizations. During the career ladder movement, we may not all get the opportunity to really reflect and learn on how to create and develop High Impact Teams. This class provides the frameworks for achievement and I have found myself using these frameworks at my job and have already seen the positive impacts it has had.
Yes, Brandi Pearce is an excellent lecturer and incorporates interesting material, examples, and activities into the course. It was very engaging

I would recommend if you think you will be leading many teams and want to have some things to keep in mind doing so. I think there are other courses at Haas that would result in much more learning but there are some useful nuggets in the class to take forward in most jobs that you will do.

Yes; the course is a good experience because it simulates working in a team where there is some ambiguity about roles and you all have to work as a team to manage both the execution of tasks and the development of the individuals. Brandi is really passionate about the material and is willing to adapt and help students as the course progresses which makes the process easier for everyone.

I would recommend this course to anyone looking to develop skills to better manage and engage with teams. The tools you gain are effective in a variety of situations and can substantially improve overall performance. Definitely! I am taking away a wide set of tools that would be for sure very useful in the future
Yes absolutely!

I liked this class, but it is a higher lift than you think it will be. Especially at the end of the semester, there are a lot of assignments (both individual and group) due. Brandi is really an expert in the field, and she does give you a toolkit and a new vocabulary in leadership. The simulation is fun, but it really depends on what kind of team you get. Yes, it was a good experience outside of my department. I feel comfortable expressing my point of view.
yes because the class is fair with workload

Yes, only if the workload is reduced. You do learn some tangible tools and frameworks, and process steps to diagnosis in team collaboration and effectiveness. But there is almost too much to cognitively download and retain. Trim the focus on the content and try to reinforce it with repetition instead of trying to cram it all into the course. I would recommend this course only to a student who has high interest in team dynamics and about leadership. Otherwise, the course does have many small activities that you must follow and it could be easy to lose focus. Yes, strong domain expertise, especially for people who are looking to be direct managers
I highly recommend this class. It goes in depths in a ton of interesting subjects and Prof Pearce is an outstanding instructor.

I think this is an important topic, but if this class continues to be taught in seven weeks with the same number of assignments/workload, I'd advise against. However, if the course gets restructured a bit, it's a good topic to have at Haas.

Yes! Great course, a great instructor who is very passionate about the subject they teach. HIT is applicable to all parts of work and life and recognizing that there is a science behind making better performing teams can help anyone in their future careers and roles.
While this course was valuable, I would encourage a student who truly wants to improve their leadership qualities take part in some design competition or the like.

This is some relatively easy credits. There a fair volume of 'stuff' to take up your time. If you've background in management/leadership, you won't learn much. Brandi's reputation typically precedes her - ask around at Haas if you haven't heard; this is important.

This is a great course for second semester second years! It is supremely well organized and run – little things like how Brandi physically sets up the classroom were impactful in creating an inspiring environment for learning / trying new tools. Brandi also really cares about her students and took the time to give me 1–1 coaching outside of class.

I would recommend this course. If you are planning to work in or lead a team, it provides a strong foundation in best practices knowledge as well as lots of space to practice and apply learning. Dr Pearce is also a great lecturer and makes class engaging and fun!
Yes – this is an extremely helpful course to take as a second–year MBA finishing their time at Haas. You will learn effective teaming tools that you can take straight to the workplace.
Yes, it's pretty interesting
Yes. Very interesting dynamics, quite different from the classes I am used to.
TAKE THIS! Super practical tools and learnings. Not too much work, but genuinely useful especially right before graduating.
I would recommend this class because it really helps to get you thinking about leading a team that is effective and also enjoys working together.
Yes I would recommend this class. I think no matter what area or specialization someone may be in, all of these concepts can be applied to every one's lives
No
To prolix in giving the main learnings topics with a lot of assignments for this amount of credit
Yes, it's a must on how to engage with teams and deal with conflict and personalities within an organization. Definitely. Great class to practice high impact teams and leadership.

I would recommend this class and instructor to anyone interested in building leadership capacity! Great course! Yes. It is a lot of theory (which was hard to digest at first) but the practical experience and reflections make it a good class for those who want to increase self–awareness.
Yes
Very good class for anyone trying to go into a management or leadership position
Yes.
Yes. Great application for industry
Yes, the course is extremely relevant to the workplace and your future endeavors.
yes, but if the course can be made more practical

This is a great course! It teaches you a lot of things from working with startups to market discovery as well as exposes you to a lot of ideas in the climate tech space. Definitely one of the heavier lifts in terms of workload but was rewarding!

I would recommend this course to students if they want to understand the reality of startup market research. The course is quite scrappy and the research and conclusions are never developed in absolute confidence, but one of my key learning from the course is that it really is like that outside of the course too. Teams learn and grow and never stop learning and growing.

I'm not a Haas student, but I recommend C2M if you're interested in the cleantech space and have at least 5 hours/week to spend on this class for 15 weeks. You get how much you invest in the class. It was particularly rewarding to work with PhDs and grad students pursuing other fields of study, and a nice intro to network with folks in the space. Would absolutely recommend this course if you're interested in climate tech or deep tech / hard tech start-ups in general. The course was especially helpful for non-Haas students, as it included lots of business frameworks, practice building slides and presentations, working with clients, etc.

I would recommend this course to a fellow student if they are looking for a broad overview into connecting research/technology with business development. While the course content itself is not challenging, the workload and time commitment does become extensive especially as you approach the end of the semester. You will be able to learn a lot of new business concepts and understand what can make or break a technology, which as a someone from a research background don't necessarily get exposure to normally. The class structure can sometimes make it difficult to see how all the pieces fit together, but process ultimately gets the students to where they need to be. The class is very much designed to be "you get what you put into it".

I would but only if they're willing to put in the time. Overall, it was a lot of work with some assignments that felt silly or unnecessary but I do think I got a lot out of it as someone who has never worked in the hard sciences. If you're interested in commercialization work at all, this class is necessary.
Yes! Incredibly value learning opportunity. In addition to learning about startups, it also felt like a great presentation/public speaking skill buillder
I would recommend it cautiously, for several reasons.
1) The workload is heavy.
2) Lectures and class deliverables feel somewhat disconnected from the actual market research you end up doing, but the actual work is very interesting.

3) The climate tech curriculum is interesting, and could have more promise if the guest speakers come with a prepared presentation — I feel I got more value out of the guest lectures that had presentations this semester.
4) Rehearsals for summit and feedback from instructors during in-class working session is quite helpful.
Yes! I would definitely recommend this course to students. It was a lot of work but I learned so much about my start up and market and generally the process of climate tech commercialization.

It is a good class and a great way to learn more about a industry that you're interested in. I recommend being really thorough with the startup selection (before class starts), as that can make or break your experience (I got the one I wanted and really liked it). It is also a lot of work, be prepared to email (and cold email) many, many people that you're interested in talking to.

If you're interested in clean tech / climate tech, you must take this course for the learning, the network you build, and the credibility it gives you in the climate tech community (yes, really). Provides great hands-on introduction to a wide range of skill sets -- market research, techno-economic analysis, storytelling for business, customer research. It requires a ton of work, which you won't want to (or really be able to) put off until the end of the semester, but you'll have learned a lot by the end of it. Delivering this material in a compelling fashion as a classroom experience is a tall order for the instructors given the sheer breadth pf the course -- and the tension with the need to dive deep in your individual startup -- but the faculty puts a ton of effort into making it work and brings the very relevant experience and network to bear to do so.
Yes. Definitely recommended. Think of this class as Lean Launchpad 2.0 on steroids focusing on deep-tech and climate sectors. The most rigorous Applied Innovation class I have ever taken

It's a lot of work for little return. You must be *really really* into climate tech to enjoy this class. One nice thing about this class is the multi-disciplinary team you get to work on with PhD's, Law students, and Public Policy folks and you get to view problems from multiple angles.

Yes I will particularly because of the overall experience and impact. particularly for technical students I believe is a great opportunity to get to understand how startups work and even how exactly it may mean working in a founder of a a startup and the dynamics of the real world experience. I would however be very specific on the demands of the course and notify them of the extra requirements of time they may have to devote to the course in the beginning of the semester

Working alongside a real-world startup to understand their technology and find where it fits in the larger market was great, but the course did not really set you up for success. Class time was spent more on high-level theories and frameworks than actionable advice or insights, the group project dynamic of the deliverables made it more stressful and contentious than it needed to be, and at the end of the day I'm confident I would have learned more and worked less if I'd just done an internship at a climatetech start-up instead.

I'd highly recommend this course to students who are interested in or want to learn more about climate tech. The alumni and startup network, together with the industry expert guest speakers are valuable resources that brought this class to a next level. To me, this is more of a "program" than a "course", in the sense that there are amazing networking opportunities with guest speakers each class and happy hours to connect with past alumni. C2M is also a high profile program in the climate tech space and adds credentials to your experience if you want to work in the space in the future.
es, I would recommend it. For students with a technical background, it provides an excellent opportunity to explore potential business avenues.

I would recommend this class. I learned a lot about the business world that I would never have gotten a chance to engage with in other classes. I really appreciate how many people we got connected to and how many resources I was offered while taking this class. I am also extremely grateful for all the instructor's time and effort put into organizing multiple guest speakers, the MetLife Coaches, the Summit, etc... I have never taken a class with this much dedication put behind it. It is very energizing to see that much passion and energy behind a graduate class, not many classes in other departments are like this. This class was a great opportunity to put myself outside of my comfort zone and develop additional communication, analytical, and presentation skills. I have never spoken to a room that big before so the summit was a really knew and exciting experience. I also very much appreciate Berkeley offering a class with a values driven goal, if this was a class about a generic tech start up as opposed to a climate tech related one, I would not have been as engaged. The overall emphasis on supporting companies that are finding solutions to serious climate issues makes this class very motivating and the experience very rewarding. I am sure the skills I developed in this class will prove useful in the future. I found most assignments to be valuable and instructive, although I felt that some deadlines were arbitrary and unhelpful. The multiple business model canvas assignments did not really help our team. The assignment we struggled with the most was the TEA by far. I hade never made one before and I think we weren't properly prepared in this class to build a satisfactory TEA so I felt very unfulfilled by this assignment. To be clear, I think it is a great thing to learn how to do and excellent material for the class, but I would have appreciated more time spent on how to develop one and possibly multiple checkins and feedback sessions on this assignment as well. Without a complete TEA I felt that the some of the subsequent economic modeling we did on promising markets was inaccurate. The example TEAs provided were very helpful.

sections.goodFor: People new to startups or deep tech who want climate/energy networking, consulting-style experiential work and a resume project, and who genuinely have time to invest.
sections.notFor: Anyone who has already launched a product (too basic), or who is time-constrained. One student calls it impractical, admin-heavy and geared to a 'fluffy' summit, saying better options exist.
sections.workloadNote: Very heavy; most work happens outside class - stakeholder interviews, entrepreneur meetings, assignments, and a final C2M Summit presentation. 3-hour sessions several call long or redundant.
sections.gradingBasis: Team project with an assigned startup client plus presentations culminating in the C2M Summit; explicit grade weights not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Startup matching is a 'complete blackbox' (one gave 96 of 100 pts to a choice they didn't get); long/redundant 3-hour lectures; heavy admin time; startups often not climate-focused enough; team luck dominates.
sections.quote: The whole course is dependent on how good your team and your startup is. It would have been nice to have some content that didn't depend on those two factors
comments: Yes, if you're interested in climate technology. In particular, building out a network in climate/energy and/or thinking through how tech can scale are the core strengths of the class. The guest speakers and networking opportunities in this class are fantastic. And the teaching team does a good job introducing how to interview stakeholders, how to approach techno-economic analysis, and preparing you to present. However, while I have some frameworks to think about how tech scales (TEA, Competitive Analysis, TAM), these concepts are introduced then left up to us to really apply them in-depth. Because of this (as well as all the stakeholder interviews we have to do), the class can feel like a lot of work.

Yes! This is a great course for anyone, even someone with no experience in clean tech. It'll give you exposure and there's tons of investment that the course makes in you as a professional regardless of your industry vertical Yes, depending on what you are looking to get out of it and how much time you have. This is a great class for consulting experiential learning, plus startup and deep tech real-world experience -- both of which are great things. If you're looking for a safe environment that's flexible in terms of workload and has team members to lean on, this class is a great fit. If you're looking to learn lots by doing, want to learn quickly, and want to learn broadly, then an in- semester internship is likely more effective from a time-effort perspective -- but this is a much larger commitment than a class.
Yes I would

This is an awesome class and clearly a lot of time and energy has gone into perfecting it for students. My main recommendation is to choose more climate-focused technologies and companies. All of our eggs are in one basket re the company we're paired with and I wish I was able to work with a company more focused on GHG emissions
reductions.
Yes. I learnt a lot about the operation and key factors impacting clean tech startups
Yes. These instructors are really helpful not only delivering the program but also navigating related issues and problems

I would recommend this course to anyone who is interested in learning the challenges early-stage deep-tech startups face. There is a considerable amount of work that takes place outside of class meetings in the form of interviews, meetings with entrepreneur, and assignments. You do NOT get to choose the startup you wish to work with; you are asked to distribute 100 points to your top 5 startups. I was not selected to work with my top choice, to whom I assigned 96 points. The matching process is a complete blackbox.

You will work with people outside of Haas, people who are a lot busier than your average MBA students. They, understandably, will not be as available to put in the work as you would and FT or EWMBA students will be responsible for carrying the team.
Yes. It's chaotic but gives valuable insight into what it might be like to work at a clean tech startup. Awesome networking opportunities within cleantech.
I thought the lectures were helpful but they were very long considering the value I got out of them.
The whole course is dependent on how good your team and your startup is. It would have been nice to have some content that didn't depend on those two factors
I recommend splitting the class back up into 2 different class sections
I think this class is helpful if you've never launched a product before but if you have, it doesn't help you delve much deeper into it.
I wish that the startups felt more like clean tech - more energy related startups or solutions that, if scaled, would address bigger climate problems.

I absolutely have and would recommend this course. It's easily my most well-organized, well-facilitated class. This inspired me in turn to be involved in this class above and beyond, and I used many of the lessons I learned in this class (especially in effective storytelling and presenting) even in other courses. I also feel grateful to now be connected with my amazing team, who I can now call my friends.
I am not an MBA, and do not come from a business background. This course has been a welcoming, intensive intro into Haas, where I will certainly try to take more courses.
Difficult but gratifying class. A lot of effort expended and the C2M Summit helps deliver a gratifying end. yes, helpful for understanding early stage cleantech

I would recommend to people who want to do a ton of work, who are really interested and doing this type of work, and don't have experience. The main thing is it is a ton of work, and takes a ton of time, not really all of it super useful - I was jealous of those who skipped class because so much of it was redundant

I would recommend this class to those who are interested in working in the clean tech space or working with startups and founders to shape their go-to-market strategy. However, I would also like to mention that the workload is probably one of the heaviest among all classes I've taken as a third year MBA student. Additionally, you don't get to choose your teammate - you kind of do by selecting the same company but not really know who will be on your team till the team is formed - and your teammates will have a huge impact on your experience with this class, positive or negative.
Maybe. I would prefer if the course is again split into two classes every week because 3 hours is too much with me (and I learnt that)

It depends on your desires/priorities. This is a heavy lift class and the type of class that you get out as much as you are willing to put in. Also, I feel like non-MBA people might have gotten more out of this than MBAs (except for those specifically looking for consulting experience in a deep tech/climate tech field) since the business portion is not extremely advanced (which makes sense considering the class has students from other schools with no prior business experience).

Yes, I would recommend this course. It offers a rare mix of real-world industry exposure, structured guidance, and hands-on teamwork that helps you build both technical and commercial skills in cleantech.
Absolutely recommend. This course gives you real exposure to cleantech startups, investor thinking, and
commercialization. The team is incredibly supportive, and the final summit is a unique, high-stakes experience that pushes you to grow.
For people who have limited startup or entrepreneurial experience absolutely for those with might be a little too basic It is a lot of work, and a lot depends on if your company is cool.

Yes, I would recommend this course if you have the time to really invest in and engage with it. The class is very time- consuming, and most of the learning happens outside of the classroom. If you don't have the capacity to give the course the attention it deserves, you likely won't learn as much and won't be able to contribute effectively to your team.

No. Way too much time spent on administrative matters, not practical enough. Not close enough to real world experiences and more geared towards a "fluffy" summit presentation than for actually providing useful inputs to startups. There are much better classes available (including on Coursera).
Yes, but only if you need the credit

I would recommend this class to students who want an interactive class that works with an external client. It is a great resume builder but it is A LOT of work. Also the experience is very dependent on the group you are placed with and the startup.
I would recommend this course though it is heavy workload, so be prepared when you enroll in this course. It is really worthy!!
The teaching team is solid, experienced, competent, helpful, responsive, interactive, and supportive. They help you get through a very difficult and intensive course/project.
Yes
Yes, Elizabeth and this course gave me practical and real toolkits for improving my life design.

would not recommend this course, I enjoyed the DYL book more than the course. Save your money and time and take another course. Also the syllabus describes this as popular course at Stanford, may be it is taught by other people, almost sound baity. the program office should remove that language.. not apple to apple comparison

Yes - I have even recommended the book to min. 5 of my friends at ESADE already. It is the perfect way to complement your MBA with practical tools to design a meaningful life for you, apart from typical MBA business focus. I would recommend this course if you really enjoyed the Design Thinking course and/or WE Innovate. Otherwise, I would recommend going through the "Design Your Life" book with a group independently as you can get many of the same benefits that way. If you do sign up for the course, be aware that a lot of time is required outside of class. I took a 3 credit course the same semester and found that I was spending about 2x as much time each week on this class, even though it is 2 credits.
My course feedback:

1) Please upload specific written instructions for each assignment at the time it is assigned. More than once, we went a week between receiving an assignment and getting specific written instructions on what was expected. For students who are managing careers in the part time program, it feels disrespectful and like an unnecessary challenge in time management to have to write to the GSI and professor to ask for instructions on what is expected.

2) Group discussions were often on topics which felt irrelevant or better suited for undergrads. Specifically, the discussion about what startup idea would you pursue with $5 on a street outside campus felt like a poor use of time. 3) Instruction on assignments overall was vague and needs to be improved for future classes. As supporting evidence, the GSI and instructor both had to clarify what they expected from students in the Aristotle paper assignment after we had submitted it when clearly >50% of the class didn't understand what the expectations were.

4) I would recommend having the professor's GSI upload all written assignments (with clearer instructions) in the week before class starts so that the professor doesn't have to upload them to bCourses on a weekly basis, since she was often un-reachable by the GSI and students who were requesting specific written instruction. Upload everything once and then forget about it to make life easy.

A RESOUNDING NO. Please save 2 credits to be used elsewhere. The course was a mess with no learnings. If you want to DYL, please buy the book on DYL (Bill Burnett and Dave Evans), read it and do the exercises. That will do a much better job and better!/$.

The professor's teaching was way sub-par. There was no valuable classroom discussion. The breakout rooms ended prematurely. Each class's valuable 40 mins were spent in what I'd characterize as banter:
(a) introduce yourself to the class (for a full 4 classes after the sem started)
(b) what did you notice in the world
(c) what are you thankful for.
I agree these are good thoughts, but using up valuable class time to discuss these was an utter waste? It's not worth the money I spent for this course.
The professor asks students to read out the text on slides out loud. Last time I saw/did this was in elementary school. What value add is this?

Towards the end, the professor cut one class and split the final presentations from the last class to the last 2 classes. Half of us were asked to present our final papers 3 weeks before the deadline for the paper!!! How in the world do you expect us to come up with quality papers and content so early/ahead in the course when we've not even started with them?! To add to the unfairness, there was one more paper due during the same weeks. Half the class was asked to present on 3/17 and the other half on 3/31 (2 full additional weeks!)

The readings were insane. At times we had to read full books (2+) during one week. How can someone who is either a FT student with other full classes or an EW with a full time job and family to attend to possibly read so much for one class?
There were 2 quizzes which were duplicates of each other (class 2 and class 7). What's the point of those quizzes that asked the same question?
The professor added 0 value to the class other than reading out some slides. No real insights were given. The prototype designs were a joke.
Designing something in 10 mins?! We all take FDT in core, half of this class was a repeat of that.
Overall, one of the worst classes at Haas I've taken.
Yes but depends on whether or not this is something they are interested in

I will recommend the course as a soul searching exercise. You are enriched by doing it with a team of people that bring perspective into life. I am curious to know if the experienced may had been more enriching if it was in person. This class is very interesting and a continuation of Design Thinking but much more personal. The workload is high for sure, both with assignments that need to be turned in and readings, and sometimes a little vague on what it is you need to do. Would recommend if you are looking for a class that helps you around how to plan your life, look inward, develop more agency, etc but it is not an easy class and participation is forced and a lot of cold calling. This class was something of a pickle for me - there's so much incredible content and it can certainly feel overwhelming. It's a long class that's absolutely jam packed for 3 hours. All that being said - it's by far one of my favorite classes I've taken. I'm here for the ooey gooey touchy feely work and I love Elizabeth's method of historical, philosophical texts and modern poetry. Not exactly what I was expecting, but delighted. Assignment load is manageable, if you did all of the readings expect to commit 5+ or so hours/week to JUST reading. Elizabeth cares greatly for her students and I really felt that genuine care from her with every class.
I would recommend this course only to individuals that will do readings and assignments. What you get out is what you put in. This would not be a good class for someone who simply wants "credit".
Yes. The class is pretty good. Not too heavy of a lift and great introspection.
I think that if this class is taken alongside another class that works on emotional maturity and intelligence, that combination would be very strong and derive in a huge learning.

I would recommend this instructor and course. Taking this course has changed how I view the world and how I view myself in it. Elizabeth is the type of professor that could make anything interesting so taking a course about designing your life with her was truly fascinating.

I absolutely would recommend it. This is such a great course. A lot of students come to Haas not knowing what their paths should be. This class should be offered in the Core curriculum to help students define their career paths. Absolutely! I feel that I learned the most from this class. The content was very relevant for a first year MBA trying to pivot into a different stage of life. The readings, classmates, and instructors were great in providing support and shaping my experience.

This was a good class, but more work than I anticipated. Elizabeth is really fun and engaging, and assigns some interesting readings. You really need to want to make changes in your life to get the most out of this class. Otherwise you are sort of just going through the motions and it's not a good use of your time. I wish I had taken this in my 2nd year.
Yes - extremely valuable class.

It's a good class if you're looking to set aside time in the week to take a philosophical and somewhat design-oriented look at what comes next in life. It's definitely a class where the more you put into it the more you'll get out of it. Yes, this course is helpful for touching on topics that we don't talk about in other classes, such as figuring out how we see meaning in our work and in our lives, and learning mindsets for approaching life like thinking about
success/failure, attention, etc.
Yes, it's fun and not too difficult. It requires you to tap into your creative side.
If introspection and self-discovery are priorities of the student, I highly recommend this course.
If the student is looking for a low-lift, entertaining class then I would not recommend. -- you get as much as you put in.

It depends. The materials of this class are developed on top of two core classes – virtue ethics and design thinking. If you like those classes, you are at a great starting point to enjoy and do well in this class. Otherwise, be prepared to put in 110% of your effort to develop new way of thinking, vision, and approach to address different life issues. Up until class 7, all topics are elaborative without an absolutely answer. I kept on waiting for the professor to tell us the right way to approach life, purpose, career, success, failure, attention, etc. and ended up, we have to design prototype to answer our own questions. In the last three class, all of a sudden, professor shared so much useful insights about attention, growth, and relationship. They are so impactful that I could not hold back but share the knowledge with my spouse, my colleagues, and my friends and they all got amazed.

This class has a lot of reading and writing. You will get what you put in –– not necessarily a good grade but definitely a transformative mindset. Also, half of this class are students from the full time program and another half from the EW program. Being an EW student, being able to meet and develop connection with the full time students are great DEI experience.
This is a class where you get out what you put in. If you're willing to be vulnerable and share, it could be life changing. If not, just buy the book and do it yourself in private.
The professor adds somewhat to guiding you through the process, but is not a compelling enough reason on its own. This class wasn't what I expected –– it's more like a personal

development/philosophy class where you learn how to use a designer's mindset to develop your agency, become aware of your attention, etc. It felt a little stretched for two units but it was interesting course to take outside of the technical/quant course curriculum. The small class community is nice for building relationships. I recommend this course – this course gave me space and tools to think feely about my work, relationships and life. The course requires students to be open minded and do the work to learn tools that will help designing our life. This class requires a lot of lower level busy work that took many hours to design and complete. There is an assignment due prior to each class and the level of works seems more than average for a 2 unit course.
I would completely recommend this course to another student.

I would not recommend this class or instructor to fellow students. I found this class in particular to be among the worst that I have experienced not only at Haas but at Berkeley since I have taken many courses over the years at the University in several departments. The professor has offered another class and I have actively told students to avoid her class because I felt that her class was not value added for the time and financial cost associated. There was no real benefit to taking the class and I did not learn much other than having many side conversations with other students that also felt that the class was terrible. Many students took the class because it was literally the last class they intended to take before graduating and they heard that there was little substance to it. I wish I would have known this prior to taking the class thus, I now inform everyone I know to avoid this class and professor. Especially since she has also canceled class without much notice as well. I felt it was inconsiderate because I found out luckily from a student while I was on my way to Berkeley from San Francisco after working all day. I usually don't have access to my school email and I would've travelled to the campus for no reason and ended up still missing class which was rescheduled for zoom. This was literally one of the worst classes I've ever taken at UC Berkeley and I regret it strongly. I really did not get anything from the class but frustration since the class lacked substance and direction. I felt like we were floating through the semester just waiting to get through it. this is my first negative review for a course and I hope that there will be some changes to give the class a more structured feeling. More time for the Design Sprints, more guidance for the assignments, quicker feedback to let you know where you are succeeding and where you are not so you have the time to course correct. Less group discussions and better connecting the course materials with the subject matter and the in class lecture rather than using the time for personal stories that may or may not have anything to do with the course material.
I recommend this course to those students that are interested to develop innerly as personality as well and learn the consciousness and see things differently.
Definitely! I have already recommended this class to a few of my friends, as i have been able to see the impact of the lessons learned in my life and in my daily interactions

It is a great class to be part of. A small number of students enable everybody to make significant contributions to class discussions. It is a great class to focus more on ourselves, rather than business. Help you to think out of the box and also do great exercises throughout the course of 10 weeks. Definitely recommend it to everyone.
Yes she is amazing
This class was very critical to help create more agency over my mind and life
Yes. Take this class. Best I've had at Berkeley Haas.

The content of this course is incredibly interesting and useful, but the delivery falls short. It was a lot of busy work (weekly reflections, asynchronous team simulations, readings, papers), and the majority of class time in spent in breakout rooms rather than lecture. I wanted a lot more lecture because Brandi is clearly so knowledgeable, but instead we got very minimal lecture from her and most of the learnings came from readings. It seems non-Haas students got much more out of this course, while Haas students who have taken Leading People and had leadership experience at work got less. If you are new to managing people, it would be useful.

Yes definitely. As a course focusing on soft skills, the workshops and activities are well designed and effective to engage everyone in the class. I think the reflection assignments and group reflexivity activities are extremely helpful to understand the strength and shortcome of yourself and your team.

I feel that this course has really helped to prepare me to be successful in a leadership position. While the course content and readings are helpful, being able to put it into practice and get feedback from classmates was invaluable. I would highly recommend this class for any student who may be younger or has little experience in the business and team leadership world. For students with no experience, it provides an excellent introduction into this field. Definitely recommend. In this new era of remote work, the concepts in Dr. Pearce's course are more important than ever. Take this class if you're interested in learning how to get the very best out of a dispersed team.
Yes I would. Brandi really cares about her students and how teams interact, and you will learn valuable skills that are directly applicable to the workplace as it becomes more globalized.

It depends. The class is a deeper dive into your first Teams@Haas session for 1st years. The simulations are quite interesting but course lectures may be a bit dry. Ideas are interesting but since it's developed by the professor, are hard to find real world examples of. I believe this class is more interesting for non-Haas students.

Maybe. Brandi cares so much and is incredibly organized. Her energy was made me engaged and made me excited to learn. However, there was a lot of noise with different assignments, too many readings, different websites to go to, simulations, cases, etc. The course should be simplified things got lost in this noise. The course was generally pretty academic too. Brandi did tie in some practical skills, such as practicing conversations (which was great), the simulation (which was pretty good), and a couple of case studies. But the rest of the material was too wordy and academic with too many frameworks that made it hard to apply the concepts from class.

Yes! This class helps me feel more prepared to lead teams when I join the corporate world. Not only am I well equipped as a leader, but I know how to better resolve and identify when things go wrong in teams. The class flew by in 7 weeks, but it's one of my favorite classes at Berkeley. There was a mix of teaching methods (cases, simulations, and traditional lecture) so that you never get bored. The team I had in this class are my friends now!

Great class, learned a lot!! Super interesting content. It was a lot of work when I took it as a two credit hour class over seven weeks- more work than I expected and more work than I am accustomed to from other MBA courses.
Yes
Yes, really great teacher and I'm sure when the class is in person, would be a great way to get to know other students on a more personal level.

Yes, I would absolutely recommend this course for students who will work in field with high levels of teamwork. The course offers very practical tools that can be utilized post-graduation as well as the opportunity to work with a team and exercise the skills learned in class.

I would recommend this course to a student that planned to work on a team with various countries / cultures represented, and most importantly if they struggled with teamwork in general. A lot of the learnings from this course probably come naturally to students that have already high EQ and / or teamwork capabilities.
Honestly, it repeated many of the same learnings of Teams@Haas. I was hoping for more of a deep dive into the international aspect of teamwork.
Yes, but mainly for the interactive team element. The lectures were a bit too lingo-heavy and I was unable to follow the concepts.
Yes, super helpful if you want to start your own company.
Would highly recommend even if you aren't planning to build a start-up currently
Absolutely it was so engaging

Hell yes. For one, every veteran must take a course with Professor Beyer because he will have your back and is a strong advocate for our community. Moreover, this class was an eye-opening experience for me as a military and finance professional. I was skeptical about the MBA until I found immense value in staying put at Berkeley and in the Bay Area because of Professor Beyer and my learnings in the Entrepreneurship class. I unequivocally recommend this class to my peers.
Yes!
Yes- especially if your pitch ends up being chosen. Even if not, it's a safe environment to see how you would function in a start-up environment.

I would strongly encourage this class. I feel prepared with a basic understanding of how a founder goes from identifying an opportunity through raising an initial round. I fundamentally have a different idea of what it means to be a founder/co-founder and feel much more confident in my ability to start a winning company. Also, I think this is a lighter lift than similar courses at Haas such as Lean Launch Pad.
Yes. A fun course, especially if you seriously want to build a business.
Yes definitely, great course for someone wanting to start their entrepreneurial journey, or for someone who wants to work for startups or for someone who wants to work in VC/PE.
Yes definitely a must course to take

Its a good introductory course but I wish we spent more time actually building things like financial models in class. I would only recommend it early on in your academic career - its not as valuable when you're about to graduate and you bring other people in the class down with your lack of motivation.
I would definitely recommend this course and the instructors to other students!
Yes
Yes, super knowledgeable and well prepared and answer any and all questions.

Yes. Great at the real-world application. You learn so much and it's fun, every single class was enjoyable. Yes - great class whether you see entrepreneurship in your future or not. Excellent content for what it takes to build a business.

Absolutely. You might think that the best way to start a business is to go start a business and not take a class on starting a business. You will learn so much from this class which are mistakes you want to avoid and things you need to do well. Kurt is a super star professor and has many valuable insights from his time as an Entrepreneur and is an excellent resource through out the course.

Yes, especially if they want to understand how to be an entrepreneur as well as understand the world of selling. yes! It helps anyone who has an idea to materialize achieve it step by step. The most amazing part is you probably find your partner in the class!
yes if you ever wondered if you had what it takes to create a start up, this class if for you. The next step is then figuring out if you want to

I would 100% recommend other students to take this course - You will not find a better way to simulate the process of starting a company. Kurt has extensive experience and through interesting guest speakers + the group project you will be much more knowledgeable about the entire ecosystem
Ye

Yes, good high-level intro to Entrepreneurship! A bit high workload for the actual learnings in the course. I already recommended it to some engineering friend because engineer we do not know a lot about business and having the point of view of founder it great teaching
Yes! I highly recommend both instructors and the course to fellow students.

Great class to take if you want to experience what a startup accelerator feels like. But know that that comes with less structure and it will challenge you to be a presenter and " sell " your idea. You will also do a LOT of work if you end up being selected as a founder (because your idea got picked as 1 of 10 among 50 or so pitches). You know your product best so you will have to really pull through the weight to do customer discovery interviews and provide real leadership to your team who just joins you mid class. Your group can be make or break for your experience in the class. This class had a lot of potential and failed to deliver to my expectations. Some of it was likely due to the unforeseen circumstances surrounding Kurt's health, but Dave and Shiva never seemed to recover their footing over the remaining 10 weeks, even with Kurt's template. It was hard to believe that this is a course that has been taught for many years, and that both instructors have been involved in previous iterations.

I found the level of disorganization in this course extremely disconcerting. Dave and Shiva seemed to talk regularly but not align. When asked about the difference in their responses, they said it was a learning opportunity for us to learn and evaluate different frameworks, which I would have found more believable if they had shared this upfront. The timing of this course was also off, with a lot of material crammed into half of the course. It would have been far more useful to do Darwin Day in week 2 (like the weekend version with Sharat, which has much more glowing feedback), and then spend the rest of the course working on our projects and evaluating different business models, while having lectures that mimicked the stage of our projects.

As a lecturer, Shiva clearly knows his material, but he always seems to defer to the other instructor in the room, until he's by himself. Dave was very encouraging and also facilitated some great class discussion. I think either of them might have been good as standalone instructors, but the combination just didn't work well.
In its current form, I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.

Yes, I would highly recommend this course to any MBA student, or those considering entrepreneurship. Its extremely hands on, so only take it if you are ready to engage and put the work in, especially at the end of the semester. The learnings are invaluable and whether or not you have an idea or business you want to work on now, this will help you learn how to think about problem spaces, validate ideas and progress through bringing a product/service to life. If you do have an idea or business now, this will be an opportunity for guided strategic development.

The course began on a strong note, with the first 3 – 4 weeks offering well-structured and valuable content. However, the quality and coherence of the course declined significantly afterward. The structure appeared to unintentionally encourage groupthink and popularity-driven decisions, often at the expense of better ideas. Strong projects were sometimes overlooked, while weaker or duplicate ideas advanced. While the professors aim to stay neutral in team formation and idea selection, some degree of intervention — especially when multiple teams are proposing near- identical or clearly underdeveloped concepts — might improve the overall experience and outcomes.

A more flexible team formation process would also be beneficial. Forcing students to join groups they may not be genuinely interested in, rather than allowing them to pursue topics they are passionate about, can limit engagement and stifle creativity.

Also I really want to emphasize how the GSI was unnecessarily strict and annoying about random things when they themselves were so disorganized. Many students, including myself, found the GSI to be overly rigid and

unapproachable. For instance, I was incorrectly marked absent from a session I clearly attended and signed in for. When I raised the issue, the GSI dismissed it without considering a correction. This kind of inflexibility and lack of responsiveness undermines trust and adds unnecessary frustration to the student experience. Given that most graduate students are working professionals, a more respectful and collaborative approach would have been more appropriate.

I would 100% recommend this course. It's fantastic from a learning perspective, I loved how the course was structured layer by layer to build up a business plan. I've already taken an entrepreneurship course, but this landed in a much bigger way.

Absolutely. These two professors went above and beyond to create an environment that prompted thought and beyond the surface level. They also paired with each other really well
Not enough practical examples. A lot of repetition from core classes or orientation lectures.
I learned a lot from this course, especially from my fellow students. Haas does a great job in ensuring we are equipped to navigate difficult conversations and topics.
I don't see the point of this class. I prefer more practical DEI classes

I think there was a lot that the instructors wanted to cover, but we never were able to dive deep into topics. The abbreviated learnings were tough to turn into tangible changes in our lives and I'm not sure how much I will be able to retain from this class that I didn't hear in other classes

No. The course itself is very much theoretical and I'm not sure how much of it would actually be useful in the workplace. Some of the activities seemed pretty unnecessary and I don't think I'm taking away too much other than some high-level observations.
Yes, although I think that it could be longer and deeper
Yes! Loved Drew and Keira
No I would not. These instructors did not add to my knowledge of DEI or my readiness to carry out these very important issues in the workplace.
Absolutely! Loved this class - such a difficult subject to approach and thought the professors were incredibly thoughtful!

No, I would not. This class has an absurd amount of busy work, writing multiple paragraphs to make sure we did the readings and surveys for us to tattle on our fellow teammates. It has generally useful content and has potential to be useful, but is not in it's current iteration.
No. I didnt reallyyyyy learn anything new
Absolutely! I hope they could bring guest speakers from other ethnic groups working on DEI initiatives. Would have loved seeing a brown person or other demographic.

I would discourage a fellow student from taking this class. I felt that the time spent in class, and the time spent preparing for class was a general waste of time. The curriculum could be distilled into a two hour block of instruction taken virtually or sent in an e-mail.
Absolutely! I wish that we took this earlier in our MBA first-year. This was by far the most engaging leadership/DEI course and gave very practical advice to future leaders.

Yes, I would recommend this class to students because I believe that all business professionals should understand DEIJB and its importance in the workplace. Especially for international students or those who have not been as exposed to these concepts in an American setting, I think it is critical to ensure that all Haas graduates have a base level understanding of equity and diversity.

l would not recommend this class. The contents and cases/exercises are superficial and repetitive. We mostly focus on understanding the problem (which we are all aware of), instead on effective solutions and practical steps that the companies are successfully implementing. I also don't think that different opinions are appreciated in the class and feedback is not always well received.
I think the material double-taps a lot of what leading people did. By and large, the material felt academic, not practical. Jarvis was the ray of applicability that I absolutely loved.

I would recommend these instructors. Presentations were top notch. I will say, however, that the environment does not necessarily promote open discussion and opinions from both sides on controversial issues.
Would not recommend as it is today
No. This class does an extremely poor job bringing DEI dialogue to life and instead spoon feeds concepts through repetitive and shallow assignments and class presentations.

I would recommend the instructors but not the class. As stated previously, I would have preferred this class focused more on the applicability of DEI in the workplace, rather than society at large.
