I understand learning about DEI challenges in the workplace necessitates understanding the larger, systemic picture-- however, I think a disproportionate amount of time is spent talking about society and not applicability in work. For example, I am glad my classmates have learned about the history of race relations and redlining in Chicago... but I also fear they might not be equipped to confront discriminatory coworkers or policies in their day-to-day employment.

I would not recommend this class to a friend or fellow student. It was far too broad, the course actively wanted you to have one perspective and discouraged other perspectives, and contributed very little to my learning. The exercises felt half-baked and did not allow much actual discussion, just coming to the conclusion they CLEARLY wanted you to come to.
No, no real learnings, many essays and readings without a take-away
Yes! I enjoyed this course and hope it stays part of the core.

The in class exercises felt performative and often times we didn't have realistic situations. It was not useful to act out saying racist comments and then seeing how we would handle it, would have preferred to here more student perspectives about these situations and how they handled them in the real world vs hypothetical. The class at its core could be useful but it's more about DEI versus business communications
Yes, I would definitely recommend this course! I learned a lot on how to be a more equitable leader and better ally. This course was very valuable and important as I enter the business world.
Would recommend for students interested in impact investing bc of the practical experience.

Overall, yes. I thought the professors did an excellent job finding quality speakers and trying to be supportive as teams managed the client relationships. The projects were well-sourced and generally interesting. It is "project work" class -- there's very little aside from that. So if you're not wanting to deal with team dynamics and a client, and are looking for more instruction, then I'd reconsider.

Yes, I would recommend this course to another student interested in social impact VC. This is a hands-on course. Impact Investing Practicum is a good opportunity to gain hands on experience with an impact investing firm within the context of a Haas class. With the volatility and time commitment of in-semester internships, it's a good way to guarantee that you'll get this experience. Ultimately, you get out what you put in, and the projects vary substantially, but it's a great opportunity. There are some kinks to work out on the organizational side, but those should hopefully be fixed going forward.

I would not recommend this course unless changes are made to ensure that projects are within the scope of what can reasonably be asked of students taking a 2 unit course over the length of one semester, and the faculty take a more active role in managing the clients' expectations.

Yes, this was one of the most practical courses I've ever had. It was a well structured consulting project where I could get true hands on experience in a field I am looking to work in after work (impact investing). I'd recommend this as a must do class for anyone who wants to work at the intersection of impact and finance. Amon, Liz, and Steve bring their real world knowledge, experience, and networks into the classroom to help us have impactful projects, learn new things, and help position us for jobs and internships after school.
Yes! The projects were super interesting and my project helped me getting a lot closer to my summer internship since I was very interested in this field.
Do not expect a lot of structure though. It's all about working with an interesting client on an interesting project and figuring it out with your group.

Interesting AI course. This was my third AI course total so I feel I have a good position to judge them from. This one was the most real world since we were out working with real companies. It was also by far the most work intensive in terms of the time the projects demanded. The other AI courses were three credits, this one was only 2 credits. So for that reason I cannot strongly recommend it compared to the others. If the course was increased to 3cr and included some lecture type sessions that supplemented the Impact investing weekend 1cr course, then I would highly
recommend it.

It's a project-based class so it really depends on what project you end up with and what client you work with. There is a lot of client expectation management involved and definitely feels more like a consulting project rather than an investment project. The course organization is a little messy in the beginning because the 3 instructors were also new in teaching it, but hopefully it'll get better next year.
Totally worth it! Dive deep into an impact project and learn as you go. Your mentor is important to help you bridge your knowledge gaps and they are very committed to help through working sessions.

Take this class if you want to get to know the awesome faculty better (Amon, Liz, Etter) and work on a concrete project for an external party. Similar to any AI class, your experience in the practicum will largely depend on who your client is and the nature of the project. The course will give you hands on experience with a real-life, real-time problem faced by an impact investor. Your experience here will be incredibly helpful if you want to go into impact consulting or impact investing.
Good course overall with a variety of topics. It is crucial to choose your project wisely and define the scope as this will have a high impact on your experience.

I would recommend this course if you want to go into an impact investing or ESG role so that you can get hand-on client experience. There is very little class content, so this is really just a 12 week mini-internship with a real company. Yes, but highly dependent on the client you are matched with, how reasonable they are with scope creep (or
shrinkage), as well as the mentor you have for your project. It took much longer than expected to nail down scope and get to work on our deliverable, and that discrepancy led to a lot of stress.
Decent class – it's a bit too much like a consulting project. More of a focus on vc or growth investing would be nice
This course is worthwhile only if you want a very independent consulting project for an impact fund, without learning anything from instructors about the industry as a whole.
Yes but is very dependent on the project

No. If student wants to learn about impact investing this is not the class to do so. I dont think the professors took into account that students came from varying experiences and some have limited background in impact investing. It is very disappointing that professors just threw the students into the client work without any assistance. This course also heavily dependent on getting good team members that can equitable do the work but it is not the case for some team!

No – we did not feel supported and empowered by peer advisors to do effective work on the project. One of the professors communicated to our team in a patronizing and condescending way. Many of the clients had
interesting work and this class does have potential, but it was not met.
Would definitely recommend this course if you're interested in VC because it's great hands–on experience with a real fund!
Yes great on the job experience – pick your client well. access to impact investors

I would not recommend to get any class from Stephen Etter, if you would like to be respected as an individual and not be treated as 5th grade students. Liz Rockett on the other hand is a kind person and overall, I am thankful that Impact Investing Practicum class exists. It gives students a unique opportunity to work with real world projects with noteworthy funds.

This is a great class if you want to not only learn about impact investing, but get involved with a client on a real project where you can make a contribution. I had heard complaints about the course in previous versions, but I think the instructors really took those to heart and reformatted the source a bit and I thought it was great. It was a good combination of self-paced learning, real life projects, and instruction.
Its a great class to get hands on experience working with impact investing funds. The course brings a lot of great impact investors and funds students can connect with.

I would! This class is great hands on experience into Impact Investing. Treat it like a part-time internship (set agreed timelines and stick to them, communicate with the client like a true consultant) during the semester if you really want to get the most out of it.

This class is a mixed bag. There may be very inconsistent experiences. It is very heavy group work for your client project which can be valuable as a resume builder. If you don't have an impact investing or climate and sustainability background you will have to invest in supplementary learning because the client project topics are much deeper in scope than the 3-4 classes the cover high level topics.

Additionally you don't get to select your team and that significantly impacted the experience given that different members will have different levels of expertise, skills, and motivation (i.e. first year vs. second years vs. non-Haas students). There are no checks and balances if work is being distributed equally and if the client scope is still in alignment. Recommend that you flag any issues with team or client early to professors.

A great course to get your hands dirty if you're interested in impact investing. Highly recommend taking a prep course for this e.g., Impact Investing Landscape, PE/VC class to get a better understanding of the types of work, players, asks, etc. This is best for a 2nd year spring.
Yes, definitely, the project gave me an opportunity to work an impact investing firm
I would recommend it as a great opportunity for learning outside of the classroom. Great for anyone with an interest in impact investing.

I would recommend this to students looking for a project centric class that helps you learn about investing and wants to start a network in the investing field. If you are like me and were not looking to get into investing but wanted to learn more about it (specifically impact or climate investing) this is a good but not great fit. The class really lends itself well to people who want to test the hypothesis of working in impact investing, and consequently there is very little theory. There are other classes like corporate finance (strong recommend) or PE or Fixed income (strong recommend) or LBOs for people who want to feel they have a strong fundamental understanding and large knowledge base about investing.

The projects in this class are useful work for the client, but it isn't day to day work. You will not be able to say you have experience working as an investor exactly or have confidence that you could do investing, but you will through work learn what it is like to work in the industry.

I would recommend this class to students who want to work with specific funds. It is hard for me to take the project I have done and apply it to my future work given its so specific for the fund itself.
Absolutely, yes.

Yes, for anyone looking to enter the impact investing space, the set of clients Liz / Etta was able to bring onboard is really impressive. We learnt a lot working directly with the client on their project. That said, the class is somewhat unstructured (like many AI classes) and requires a fair amount of team coordination and discipline.

I definitely recommend this course because you get real world experience in the field. The professors have a wealth of industry experience that they openly share and they are very excited to help students navigate the field. Yes, absolutely. This is such a great way to get experience working with real clients. In semester internships can be difficult to get without having any background in impact investing, so to have the opportunity to work directly with funds as a part of class (and with the support of industry vets aka professors) is tremendously valuable. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to gain experience in impact investing. It is great exposure and a great opportunity to learn more about different impact investors and get experience and build a network in an impact investing firm.

The instructors are still figuring out how to structure course and class time, and so that could be improved. But if you get a good client project, then it's very worth it. You get out what you put in.
Yes I would - it was a great learning experience and I have a lot of course material that I can now link back to things I see and hear about in the real world.

sections.goodFor: Students pivoting into climate/impact VC who want real client work, investor network access and interview material; one landed an in-semester internship through their client.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a structured introduction to impact investing - learning is self-driven and peer-to-peer. If your client is unfocused, the project drifts and you learn less than peers.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified. Almost all work is the semester-long client project; a lot for 2 units if scope isn't set with the client. Class sessions sometimes cancelled to give project work time.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the client project and its deliverables dominate
sections.redFlags: Experience varies heavily by client and team (5+ students); 2 say there is little real lecture or teaching from the instructors; 1 reports classes cancelled at the last minute for 'project work time'.
sections.quote: This class is entirely based on your client project, with little to no lecture or deep learning coming from the professors. In fact, class is often cancelled (at the last minute)
comments: Absolutely - specially if you're interested in getting real life experience more about impact and climate investing and/or working with it.

I learned a lot with this course, but I think part of it was because of the client we were assigned to. Potentially this is a class that the more you give the more you get, and part of it depends on the clients engagement and organization to support the project.

Amazing opportunity to connect with the impact and climate investing space - we got to know a lot of the clients and part of them (not only ours) joined the final happy hour and we were able to network more.
Yes, this was a fantastic class for anyone that wants hands-on experience in impact investing

Yes if you're interested in hands-on experience in impact investing. Like most experiential classes, your group and project idea will have a big impact on your actual experience, but I found the ROI on project time very high and would have invested more time in this class if I could do it over. Both instructors are very willing to share their expertise and time with you, the lectures themselves are very informative, and I highly recommend this class.
Yes
Definitely would recommend the course! I thought this was a great experience working with a client and learning real world applications of what we learn in the classroom.
Yes, especially for future investors! It's fun and meaningful to work with real VCs/investors.
Yes if you already have experience in this industry. If you are new it is how much you put into this class.

I would recommend this course with the caveat that what you get out of it really depends on the client and project you get. If you get a client who doesn't really know what they want or how to utilize your skills, the project may end up being very unfocused, and you may not learn as much as your peers. A lot of our project felt self-driven, and we kind of lost the benefit of working with someone who works in the industry- we didn't really get to know what he does on a day-to-day basis. That said it was useful to speak to my experience in interviews and gave us credibility to have conversations with some really influential people in the industry.

Yes! Your experience will be somewhat colored by the client youre paired with but regardless, the class is an incredible value add. You'll also have a lot of opportunities to learn from your classmates' projects.

This class is entirely based on your client project, with little to no lecture or deep learning coming from the professors. In fact, class is often cancelled (at the last minute) to give us more "project work time." Honestly, I was hoping to learn more about impact investing from the professors who are such seasoned professionals in this space, but they seem to believe that it's only worthwhile to learn by doing through our client projects, which are highly variable depending on the assigned client and topic.

This was a fantastic class! We had the chance to work with real-world clients and could select them during the first week. I really appreciated how dedicated Etter and Liz were to our growth and supporting us throughout the process. Coming in with no understanding of impact investing (or investing, in general), I felt like it helped to provide me with a deeper understanding and real-world skills.

If you want to work in VC, TAKE THIS CLASS! As someone who is looking to pivot into Climate VC, this may have been the single most impactful class I took in my first year at Haas. Landing a first role in venture is hard, but this class gives you the practical experience to make it easier. The connections with your client are also very helpful, and mine led to an in-semester internship with a fund my client connected me with.
I would recommend this class as it does a great job of tying in the real world into Haas. It was also extremely interesting to see all the other projects other teams were covering.

Good class, very hands-on, but like any applied innovation, the workload and overall class experience depends heavily on the group and client you are assigned. I feel like the class can end up being a lot of work for only 2 units if you don't set a clear scope with your client or get a hard to tackle problem. A lot of the class is self-driven and learning is meant to be peer-to-peer, so this might not be the best class if you are looking for an introductory overview of the impact investing space.
Absolutely, fantastic instructors that bring deep industry knowledge and a great network
Yes fun class and engaging

I would definitely recommend this course if you are interested in climate investing. The projects themselves vary, but Liz and Etter are great resources if you are willing to engage with the class and put in the time.
Yes I would especially if you have never thought about impact investing (applications, capital structures etc.)

rows.title: Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Leadership

comments: Yes, I recommend ISEL to all fellow Haasies.

ISEL teaches a holistic system of how to relate internally to oneself and externally to others (and vice versa). I believe it's crucial (absolutely critical) to learn such skills especially since as top MBAs we are ascending into managerial roles at elite firms in our capitalistic society.

Now, many students have not had positive experiences in ISEL. I respect that, and I went into the class knowing those experiences are real, legitimate, and exist. Ultimately, in order to benefit from ISEL, it's important to go into it with an open mind, earnestly doing all the assignments, all the practices, and all the readings.

ISEL is not perfect. It has some minor flaws; particularly in how it presents itself as being tied to the GSB "touchy feely" class, which sets up an unmet expectation; a minority few of the methods Erica employ feel too unrelated to the course content; the all virtual format my cohort experienced can be difficult for some — but some prefer it, but its also unrealistic given that we don't conduct our lives entirely virtually (for now...); many of the assignments deal with intersectional identity, but we didn't cover enough of that in fishbowl T-groups; I think the "crash-course weekend" might be too tiring to have lasting learnings for some people.
Yes I would, this class was really powerful in helping me develop my active listening and be aware of the emotions and physical sensations I am experiencing in the moment.

No. I would not recommend this course AT ALL. This class was bizarre with numerous references to BTS as an example of embodied leadership. That did NOT resonate with the class. Part of the course curriculum was to watch a video of the instructor performing a BTS dance cover. The BTS fan base is teenage kids so for the instructor to be this into it did not feel appropriate. The use of emotion from the instructor felt manufactured and disingenuous. The exercises in class were not effective on Zoom and dragged on and on.
Absolutely. One of the best courses I've taken at Haas

I personally would recommend it to anyone who is open to actually examining and putting in the time to explore their own real identity, stress, anxiety, and goals in life. I am not exaggerating when I say that this course helped me rediscover what I believe to be my purpose and the meaning in life. I didn't come in thinking that would happen, but near the end session, I felt a wall inside me just fall down and realized how implicitly self-centered I had been throughout my whole life and what events informed that, and I realized I could make a conscious change to not let myself be defined by comparison & productivity. However I think this class comes down to how much you are able to put in (time commitment wise) and how open you let yourself be to evolving and changing. Every single person had different insights and takeaways and changes I think. So while I know this class is extremely polarizing, I found it valuable and perhaps the most memorable class I took at Haas because it caused me to re-conceptualize my own identity, self, priorities, anxieties, and how I see the world. For me, that's more valuable than a power & politics class that tells you how to win in the world / manipulate people in a nutshell haha. Because I feel like in my own happiness I have a framework to transcend a mentality where " i will only be happy if I have material success. " And that is freeing. On the other hand, this class is a lot of what can feel like busywork and journaling/writing, as well as reading, so it's not a commitment that can be made lightly. There's a lot of pre-work and post-work, and so it's not a 3-day seminar you can just show up, get insights, and leave. It requires substantial work on your own side, but setting aside that time for reflection helped me mostly (though I think it's maybe still a bit on the heavy side).
Absolutely, this is one of the few classes where you learn an applicable skill.

This was the most transformative class I've taken at Haas. There is very distinctly a pre-ISEL period in my life as well as a post-ISEL period in my life. If you are open to the process and want to better self-regulate your emotions (as well as handle and take care of the emotions of people around you) I recommend this class. There is so much to be said about effective leadership coming from leaders that know how to self-regulate AND recognize the emotional experience of the people around them.

There is no other class like this at Haas. Take it if you want to spend 30+ hours thinking about yourself and how you interact with the rest of the world. Erica has woven together disparate practices into a cohesive whole. I found it useful and enlightening.
Course is probably one of the best at Haas in terms of a course that will actually teach you something and lead to professional growth.
I would absolutely recommend this class for anyone looking to deepen their interpersonal skills and learn the tools for being a more empathetic and emotionally intelligent leader.
yes! i am glad i chose to spend some time at haas working on softer skills and feel honored to have done so with Erica, who clearly cares about this subject and her students an extraordinary amount.

Yes; The course is a good new perspective on other courses around leadership in the Haas curriculum. This is one of the only ones I know that talks about regulating your emotions (not controlling or avoiding them) and how that might benefit you and your connections to others. Erica and the co-learners are so passionate and they really seem to enjoy this work. It is a long class and lot of commitment but it is worth the investment.
highly recommended if you are sensitive to other people's comments on you. you will be able to build up your capacity to deal with interpersonal issues and better connections with people around you

This course is a great capstone of interpersonal leadership courses at Haas. The professors are incredibly nice and supportive. The three days of solid class on the weekend was long, but nicely broken up with breaks, stretching, and meditation. There is quite a lot of written work to do both before and after (6 total assignments that may take most of a day each), but maybe that is expected given it is a two unit class.

I would highly recommend the instructor and course to fellow students, as I truly believe this is one of the most transformative classes at Haas. Through this class, I reflected and reexamined my past experiences interacting with people in my personal life or at the workplace, and now have a better strategy in place to handle conflicts, and surging emotions. This class has given me the tools to be in touch with my true self and express myself in the world with authenticity and humility.

I would NOT recommend this course in its current design and fashion. The workload is IMMENSE, with very LITTLE learnings, and a very rigid instructor who created distance with students. There is a HUGE potential for this course in the curriculum and the team and instructor put a lot of work in building its content. But its force is becoming its weakness - it is too rigid, too structured, too dictated, and is the only course that Haas still offers online fully (which is a shame for the focus is on building connection and students do value in-person teaching). This online model may be more adapted for EMBA and EWMBA students.
No.
The class pre-work is insane...and so the workload during the class
I feel that this class could have been done in two Fridays maximum

No. It is a horribly executed class that taught me nothing. When thing started to get intersting, Erica would interrupt to add her two cents. The continous references to the k-pop boy band were completely unecessary and irrelevant. This class should also not be done in three days but a few hours a week for 5 to 6 weeks.

I would recommend this course, but I would caution student that this course is more about learning about oneself and one's subconscious reactions (and self regulation strategies) and less on application of how to apply the learnings in a business or professional environment.
I highly recommend this class. I learnt more than I expected to learn and grew so much with this class.
Definitely yes, wholeheartedly!
No other course will empower you with the same level of awareness and "tools" you need for a happier relationship with others and yourself, and a sense of freedom.

If you, like me, came to business school to develop soft skills, learn how to connect with others, and understand yourself, then this class is for you. Erica formerly taught Touchy Feely at the GSB and has adapted it to account for one's social background and to create deeper connection with students from all backgrounds. However, be warned that the course readings and engagement requirements far surpass that of an average Haas class (core included). Even though English is my first language, I struggled to understand the readings and assignments. The zoom nature of the course was also emotionally draining. However, I am leaving the course feeling empowered to become a better person, friend, sibling, and coworker.

Those who aren't sure they can handle the intense course workload should look at Jennifer and Rajiv's two-day Building Trust Based Relationships Course. The courses overlap with each other, although Trust Based Relationships doesn't go as deep due to the course's brevity.

I think I would not recommend this class, as is, to fellow students. The material is important: real connection and conversations, dignity, conflict, etc., are all critical pieces of developing as people and leaders, but this class was more work than learning and could be more impactful in a different format.
This is a good course to get better at communicating with people you care about under stress

This class is about self-reflection and building connections with people in different scenarios. Overall, the content is quite engaging, and I can see it being useful. However, the significant amount of pre-assignments and post- assignments and the time commitment of the whole weekend make me doubt my decision to choose this class. I think the content could be condensed into a one-credit course with substantial learning and much less workload. On the other hand, the instructor showed a lot of BTS content as examples of embodied leadership. But, I personally found it really hard to relate.

Do not take this class to take workload off the rest of your semester. The pre-work and post-work is ridiculously long. I came in interested to learn, but due to the length of the assignments, I ended up not being able to go deep in order to get it done within my schedule. The class was about as Berkeley as it could be. There were some good learnings but it felt like an hour of learning was extended into 4.

would highly prefer this class to be in person....zoom makes it hard to engage fully in the class. There are a lot of useful frameworks and exercises but hindered by the online format. Hopefully this changes.

To be honest, this ISEL cohort / class was a challenge (so many micro-aggressions and overall poor DEI competency from the teaching staff) however, they were genuinely open to feedback, I learned a lot of frameworks to talk through my own feelings, and according to my partner I'm already a better listener. I have asked that this be in-person again, but in the absence of that definitely take this at an Air BnB with friends.
I would because I learned a lot and I also feel a lot closer to my classmates and this was an opportunity for me to realize how amazing my classmates are.

I would not take the class if it is operated remotely. The format simply doesn't translate well to the virtual environment and 24 hours of virtual class over a 3 day period is a very tall order, despite instructor efforts to incorporate breaks. It is a good class to push yourself emotionally, but requires a ton of investment both from an emotional perspective as well as an time/effort perspective.

If you are super new to building interpersonal skills and embodied leadership, you might get something out of this course. The assignments are long and tedious, the class is long and not a super great use of time. I would want to see major shifts/changes in the course before being able to enthusiastically recommend the course, especially related to DEI.

This class has too much homework compared to the number of credits it is. The facilitation framework of the class needs to be updates to reflect more up-to-date best practices for DEI work. The class is significant emotional labor, especially for students from under-represented backgrounds.

I can not recommend this course in its current form. I had very high hopes but am very disappointed with what I experienced. The amount of pre- and post- work for this class is overwhelming, repetitive, and emotionally exhausting. The current format on Zoom is not conducive to such a heavy topic that is complex, emotionally intense, and has a great deal of nuance that you don't get through the screen. Most of my learning in this class was from classmates and unfortunately came at the expense of other students who were put in very uncomfortable situations. The teaching team is not as well-trained as they should be in DEI-related topics, including power, privilege, oppression, and marginalization.

Yes - this was one of my most amazing classes I've taken at Haas. I think that it provides such a depth of personal and interpersonal learning outside of any class. This is not a business class but more so a life class. I think that I learned more about being a leader and being a strong human than any other class at Haas. This class does require you to take it very seriously to get the most benefit out of it plus honoring the effort your fellow students put into it. I would not take this class if you are not committed to showing up. I would take this class if you are looking to learn more about how you can connect more deeply with other people.

I highly highly highly recommend this course. I think it should be mandatory. The amount of connection built among the group in such a short time is incredible, I've struggled with connection and belonging my whole life and this course created a safe place to feel "buoyed" and held by others. This is such an emotionally driven course and some precaution should be taken as there are likely things under the surface that will come up. This course is really counter- culture and goes against the social conditioning we've had our whole lives. We talk about deeply personal things, we focus on deep listening and ensuring everyone feels heard. I can't think of a better example of what Haas stands for than this course, because this is the course that most exemplifies "confidence without attitude". Before taking it, I was interested to get someone else's feedback and shocked to learn that "they couldn't recommend it" because of some things that came up in their course. I feel sad knowing that valuable lessons were not taken away from that experience, because I know Erica would have done her best to encourage connection instead of disconnection. I can't recommend this course enough, it really was a powerful experience. The downside is that it's a lot of effort, these things take a lot of work. The homework is challenging and reflective and you will feel tired throughout the days of the workshop. But it is so worth it.

Yes - this course requires significant energy, but the material is very interesting and fulfilling. I would recommend this course for anyone who wants to have a positive impact on their team (and anyone around them, really), and wants to learn how to advocate for themselves and resolve conflicts for the long-term with mutual understanding and appreciation.

I learned a lot from group practicing where I would never have had the opportunity to practice otherwise. But there're just too many assignments -- before, during, and after classes. Sometimes, I feel overwhelmed by the mental energy put in this class, especially the 2nd week where we had day-long classes for 3 days.

I would highly recommend this instructor and course because to be quite frank, I feel now that I have the tools to improve the relationships I have and to form strong connections with the people I have yet to meet! Erica really allows you to explore and examine the factors that have shaped your identity, and she provides data-driven research related to the emotions that we feel. It's a wonderful class to take, and I truly have learned so many things that I'll keep with me for the rest of my life.

I would 100% recommend this class. This class can really change how to interact with families, friends, and colleagues. I would recommend this course, but I think it could be slightly better in person. Zoom gives way to not paying attention.
Wonderful course and instructor, Erica is great!
Came into this class dealing with some past trauma and some recent trauma, thought this course was just about communication, that's it.

But this course ended up being a powerful experience in which I was granted the rare opportunity to interact with strangers and classmates in a highly structured setting, and also ask tough questions of others. Ended up learning a great deal about myself!

Definitely recommend. After taking the course, I felt I have taken the first step on the journey to love myself before I can love others. This course will ask you to look inside, stretch and be vulnerable so only attend the course if you are ready to do that. The home assignments are huge so be ready for that too.

I DO NOT recommend the course. It could be fit for a psychology program but definitely not an MBA. I signed up for it to build "interpersonal skills" but I have gotten none of that. While the instructor was immersed in the methods and was dedicated to giving students a good learning experience, the content seemed very light and the

exercises/practices felt like a waste of time. I found it very hard connecting what I did during the course to any helpful skill or competence relevant to my journey as a business leader or career person.
The course seems to be overly focused on neurobiology, feelings and emotions, which I personally did not find helpful for my journey in becoming a business leader.
Also, if it has to be taught, then it may be best taught in-person.
Yes. The experiential portion of the class (almost 95% of it) really got me rethink about the way I approach people and life.

I would definitely recommend this course to other students with the caveat that they have to be genuinely curious about the material and content. The course is truly transformative for those that make the commitment to immerse themselves in the course content.

Depending on what stage you are in your leadership or professional development, this class might resonate with you. I went through many practices that were useful and explored concepts I had not done before.
Having said that, I felt we could have package more grounded, concrete learnings in this 2 unit course compared to other similar courses.

Not at all! This course had very little to no substance and was a sheer waste of time. The course description was so different from the content that was taught. this can be described as a breathing, dancing, distressing spiritual class. If you are on the verge of an emotional breakdown, perhaps this class can serve as a therapy session for you. Most folks in the class were surprised by the content. The professor shares some of her childhood memories, her love for dancing and a rock band (BTS) that she adores over and over. I am beyond flabbergasted how Haas even approved this class. It is a total waste for time and money. The only useless class I have ever taken at Haas. It was like being held hostage for 4 days for no reason. Please do yourself a favor by not enrolling for this class.

Yes...she reverse engineers connections. Makes you think of negatives cycles, and defines emotions and how to deal with them. As someone who never took a course like this, and was from a quantitative background, probably the coolest course at Haas I've ever met. Businesses, politics are all about managing relationships and this teaches you about the very human fundamentals of connection from neuroscience and psychology.

This class is a must take. Its short and intense but unconventional and a breath of fresh air among normal MBA classes. Its awesome if you like to stretch yourself socially and develop as well as making friendships and being vulnerable. If there is any part of you that wishes that you felt more connected to people at Haas, please take this course. The stories you hear from others and the stories that you share will create such a powerful experience that cannot be replicated by any other Haas course. I specifically encourage my fellow men at Haas to challenge themselves with a course that tests their emotional intelligence and boundaries. If you identify as a man and struggle with
vulnerability/emotional expression, please take this course and allow yourself to grow.
Trust Erica and her process, and it will pay dividends.

Yes definitely take this class. This is a powerful class that allows you to tap into your deepest emotions in a safe space. I have noted some points which I would like Erica to include in the course. With those included, I would recommend this course
Course materials have included quite a few video clips selections that reflect personal preference but might be difficult to arouse resonance among students
I would aslo like to see more structures of how the concepts and theory relate to the practice.

I would highly recommend it. It is a lot of work, but I have learnt practical frameworks that challenge unhelpful inner chatters/old patterns and regulate my nervous system, which I think is not only useful for leadership but also for personal fulfillment and happiness.
This course is a really concentrated time commitment - you are essentially sacrificing 3 weeks in a row (pre-work, class sessions and post-work)

This class was not really what I expected, I wish we had more practical application to real life scenarios. If you want more practice on being vulnerable and in touch with your emotions, then this class might be beneficial for you. But if you are looking to apply these learnings to your professional or personal life, I do not see much of a benefit. This class is heavily focused on group sessions in which we open up and are vulnerable with each other, but it doesn't go too deep into how we would apply this in real life. For that reason, when it comes to recommending this class, I would say that it depends on what you are looking for.

I highly recommend this course to others. It is a difficult course, yes, but it is the most practical course I?ve ever been a part of and will no doubt help drive the positive change in you and your relationships.

Stanford touchy feely style class. I think this class is very interesting and teaches many interpersonal concepts and practice it, which is very great experience you cannot have anywhere else. But if you take, you need to spend whole week and a tons of reading and writing. This is a demanding class. Also, I feel the class is better in the format of in- person.

Yes! Absolutely yes! This course has been the true highlight of my Haas experience. It was really nice to see how to improve interpersonal skills, build truly meaningful relationships, be vulnerable, have heart to heart conversations. It has a lot of work, a lot of work, but in my opinion, it was necessary and worth it. I got to know 18 beautiful human beings through this course, and I will never forget this experience.

As it stands today, I would not recommend. However, if the class is increased from 2 credits to 3 credits and is spread out over the course of 10 weeks or a full semester (currently it is over two weekends), I would consider it. The workload is extremely heavy and it is difficult to accomplish everything in three weeks, especially on top of everyone's busy schedules. Not only is this taxing, but it also detracts from the value of what you are learning. If you are located in the Bay Area, I would also require that the course be in-person. The current Zoom medium leaves something to be desired. i think this needs to be a required class.. it probably be shortened and doesn't need to be as long.. perhaps havfe class times start at 10am always?

I would whole-heartedly recommend this course to anyone who wants a more scientific approach to leadership communication than the core course. It ranges through a lot of techniques that are backed up with studies and data. These studies are given to the students to reflect on and make a impact on how we present ourselves as leaders, and as people, in difficult situations.

I would not. I think that this class would be a great one-day, 3-hour session. But I do not see value in it being as long and intensive as it is. The workload has exceeded a majority of the core classes at Haas, filled with videos of BTS interviews and music videos and ted talks. I think that Erica is a very passionate and knowledgable professor, but I do not think that I gained much value from this course. The forced intimacy led to numerous triggering moments, including Erica showing screenshots of messages between her and her mother with whom she has a tumultuous
relationship with to the class and crying. Overall, this class is an extremely heavy lift, with little to no value, and will expose you to high levels of emotional distress. Do not recommend.
No I would not.

rows.title: Interpersonal Skills and Embodied Systems Leadership

comments: yes and I hope Erica takes some of the feedback and makes adjustments in examples and biases she shares...seems highly skewed and negative on america

Yes, I'd recommend taking this class. This class is the most useful class I've taken in my MBA journey and is one that I will have takeaways that I can apply to all aspects of my life. You'll need to be comfortable with stretching a little bit out of your comfort zone, but it does pay off in the end. I learned a lot about myself through the class because of all the different practices taught and there is a lot of deep reflection about what shaped you. As an FYI, there are times that the purpose of the practices are a bit unclear, but you'll need to trust the process and see where it leads. The class is not very focused on theory or concept, but more on practical skill building so you will be doing a lot of practice sessions with classmates.
Yes I would recommend it to all my classmates

Yes. I would recommend this course. I feel like a toddler learning how to walk first time, guided by Erica. I felt a different mental muscle being practiced the whole time. But people taking this class need to be aware that this is not a therapy session and is not a magic stick to solve any mental problem and issues happening in your life.
Yes absolutely

Yes! Highly recommended. This class helps you better understand who you are and what is your desire. It helps you to learn how to connect to yourself, be authentic about yourself, care for yourself. Through different practices and techniques, you are introduced with a new approach to manage your relationship with yourself and with others. These practices give you idea how to build stronger connections with people in personal and professional settings. Last but not least, this course helps you understand how to be a system leader and co-create the world with others. I would not recommend it if you want to learn anything meaningful. Even the instructor herself could not explain how her class would be relevant in real-world interactions.

I think the course has a lot of value especially for kids coming from cultures or backgrounds in which they don't get to express themselves. Erica is a good facilitator and her course will provide value to them. Thank you for your efforts over the years, especially the last few days.
Yes. This course is worth it for personal growth and introspectiveness.

If you have never taken or engaged with an "interpersonal skills" class before (or reading, workshop, etc.), then this may be helpful for you. However, the online format of the class limits how deeply you can go into practicing the skills you read about in the class.

I would recommend and I recommend anyone planning to take this course to take this with intentionality. It is easy to get lost when taking such a fluffy course and it can be easy credit if you just want to passively participate or can be inspiring if you really want to improve the way you encounter others. The more you put into this course, the more you get out of it. Erica is very nice and helpful!
Absolutely.

Yes. If you are looking for a 2 unit credit load with the right amount of work (not too much and not too little) that is also therapeutic, then this is the course for you. I enjoyed this course and saw it as the right balance to just let go.

I recommend this course to a fellow student. Communication is a very important skillset both in personal and professional life and this is the course you can learn a lot about how to be a better listener and communicator. Communication skill sounds very intangible and something very difficult to develop, but this class is so organized and gives you detailed tips about how we can develop.
yes surely.

Sure. I think there are things every Haas student can learn from this course. If you're interested in understanding that even though we may all have biases or privileges we are all humans and can share emotions and struggles with one another, then this class is for you. The online nature of the course is hard though, so be prepared to be mentally drained by the end.
One of the most overhyped and downright mediocre classes here at Haas.

- If you're coming here because of the " touchy-feely " hype, PLEASE don't. It's a zoom class with only some concepts used from the Stanford class. It's hard to debunk this notion because there is no counterfactual - nobody can attend both Haas and GSB at the same time. Nonetheless, there moments that actually made me think this class is worth it are far and between. Erica uses her Stanford dropout brand very effectively but it creates unrealistic expectations. If you come in, come in with a realistic mindset on what this would be.

- Assignments take 4-6hrs each and there are five of them. On top of that, there are almost no discussions of your responses and the pieces you read in class. I spent 12 hours in the pre-assignments and stopped putting in the effort for the last three assignments as it's simply not worth it if the assignments are so seldomly mentioned in the curriculum. It's like doing a case write-up thoroughly yet have no meaningful discourse of it in class

- Erica keeps everything a secret. She doesn't share slides and actively warn you to NOT practice this or impart what you learn to other people as it is " dangerous " to practice without supervision since it's such a delicate framework. Hint: it's really not. This lack of openness and cult-like secrecy just goes against what I expected. It points to a lack of confidence and substance in the class material itself

- Prepare to watch a lot of BTS (yes the Korean band) videos. People are literally falling asleep at these videos and there are in both the assignments and during class. I personally don't see the merits in watching these, but we're forced to. I just don't think any level of personal infatuation with a band justifies this amount of mandated exposure for the entire class
- Like many other weekend classes, the class starts after the add/drop period, which means by the time you realize you want to drop it after the first session, it will be too late

The verdict: I'm at best neutral/slightly negative on this class because of the above and the fact that it's 4 days (should really be 2 days like the other EW classes). Instead, I recommend " storytelling for leadership " and " leader as coach " which would be much better learning experiences

This is a course that REALLY shows how to embody being an authentic leader. It's novel, funky and deep. You will use your breath, body and emotions to understand much better your leadership style and beyond.
I wish it was part of the core or something. Honestly, this is the type of courses I was looking forward to have in Berkeley.
Can't recommend it enough.
Vulnerability is contagious, go for it!

I think if you are an individual who struggles communicating/connecting this class can be beneficial. The course focuses on your internal self and how to regulate that in a work environment. It was almost like a 4 day therapy session which could be applied to your job. If you feel comfortable with communicating/connecting, you may find the class redundant and long winded.

Yes, definitely. I think these are skills that we don't emphasize enough. More than that, this course has real frameworks that I can practice and takeaway. I don't feel like that's the case in a lot of similar "leadership development" courses at Haas. Truly, one of the most impactful courses I've taken in my MBA.

I recommend this course if you have 4 full days to burn on the zoom class + many hours to spend on the assignment and nothing better to do. This course can benefit from being shortened to one or two days max with concurrent breakout rooms. It would be helpful to have real peer-reviewed research to back up the teachings. Conversation structures taught are mechanical. Students are asked to write down in class and present live (,when under pressure of the spotlight, made up) learnings. When negative feedback was given (by previous students I presume), the instructor chalks it up to 'people don't understand'. I agree in this case that I didn't understand the need for the collective watching of so many BTS videos. On a positive note, here's what I learned to save you the time 1. be intentional and say "xyz, I want to connect with you" 2. acknowledge by saying 'thank you for connecting, abc' 3. remember to ask what's the level of vulnerability was that? 4. check with the quesioner 'what's your intention for asking that question?' (to defuse a situation or understand the true intention. 5. when appropriate, repeat what you heard and try to cover as much as possible and ask ''did I miss anything that's important to you" 6. regulate your breathing and practice Pranayama/Alternate Nostril breathing 7. take breathing pauses and shake it off

I recommend this instructor and course to those who want to further explore concepts around vulnerability, empathy, and authentic leadership through experiential practice. This course delves deep and takes great mental and emotional focus.

Absolutely recommend. This courses touches on "touchy feely" subjects, and is something I think every MBA student should take before going back out into the real world so that difficult but necessary convos on emotions and feelings are had.

Yes. However, I hope that changes are made to the structure. This course is very important for future leaders. Yes, but they should know that it is a lot of sitting and talking, but overall a good course if you lean in What you get out of the class totally depends on whether you want to believe in this and how much effort you put in It's a weird class with mixed reviews. Some people hate the class and didn't get much out of it, but some people (mainly EW and EMBA) found it to be helpful
Talk to other students before taking the class, otherwise it might be a waste of time for you. it's also not a easy 2 unit class. A TON of homework and draining 4 days on zoom.

sections.goodFor: Students who want deep-tech commercialization exposure with real early-stage clients, plus unusually high-quality networking nights with VCs, serial entrepreneurs and operators (~3 per term).
sections.notFor: MBAs seeking consulting or entrepreneurship practice: one warns business students hard-carry teams of masters students with 0-2 years' experience, plus an age gap and heavy unpaid labor.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (5 comments) but consistent: extremely heavy - one says ~3x the time the unit count suggests, covering interviews, weekly assignments, deliverables and several rounds of presentations.
sections.gradingBasis: Team client project with mid-term presentation, alumni night and final demo day; grading not otherwise discussed.
sections.redFlags: Team composition: the MBA is often the only business student and ends up carrying and coaching much younger masters students (2 of 5). Workload far exceeds the unit count. Experience hinges on client and team.
sections.quote: That said, be ready for an extremely heavy workload. The class easily takes 3x the time suggested by the unit count
comments: Not if you're a business student, unless you are making a hard pivot and are seriously in need of a hands-on client project on your resume, and you're willing to put in the time and unpaid labour for it. It's a good project to talk about during interviews, but that can easily be achieved through other Haas Experiential Learning courses or an in-semester internship. The workload is much higher than you think, because the teams are usually Masters students who are fresh out of undergrad with <2 years of work experience (often 0 or 1 year), so it's much more work than you'd think to coordinate with them and work with them to get the material up to a standard that you're willing to present and put your name on. The projects are usually a business question at its core (market entry, commercialisation, pricing, etc) and most groups this year had max 1 business school student, so as a business student you'll be hard-carrying most of the analysis and being a pseudo-coach for the rest of your team trying to grapple with business content that they might be learning for the first time.

Also be aware that there is usually an age gap, so if you're above the median age for business school students, be prepared to have sufficient patience to work with other students in the 22 to 25 year old range.

One advantage of this course is that the networking nights are truly impressive. Lots of VCs, serial entrepreneurs, and folks from all backgrounds (e.g. ex-military, someone who used to work at a large insurer and now is a GTM specialist for healthtech startups). The quality of contacts here is higher than the average business school networking event, so it does have value if you're interested in continuing in the deep tech space. Networking nights happen ~3 times per term (mid-term presentation, alumni night, and final demo day, though along the way you sometimes get connected with one-time "mentors" that you can speak to about your project too).

The course is a great opportunity to leaarn about the path to commercializing frontier "deep tech" innovations (frontier technologies). Profs Rappaport and Bowman are great and have experience, especially on the patent and regulation side of things. The course is a great opportunity to connect with industry professionals and experts that may open up future opportunities. That said, be ready for an extremely heavy workload. The class easily takes 3x the time suggested by the unit count and requires managing interviews, project deliverables, weekly assignments, and several rounds of presentations. The experience is also heavily team-dependent and teams are formed based on interest and past experience (plus availability)

I think this course has a lot to offer. It gives you exposure and experience to working at an early stage startup. Prof Rappaport and the GSIs offer a reasonably laidback class, and I think any complaints of the course are probably centered on their teams or startups. I enjoyed the course and would recommend it whole heartedly.

From a business student perspective, if you are eager to support early stage startups in whatever challenge they might have, this class is for you. If you are interested in practicing consulting skills or entrepreneurship, there are probaly better options out there.

Startups come in various development stages and industries, so you should come prepared to work in industries you did not want/expect to work with and with founders with differing levels of engagement.

If you want to work on the commercialization of deep tech with real clients, this is a very good class. However, be prepared for a heavy workload. Also, as you might expect, the experience can vary significantly depending on the client and your teammates.

If you are looking for a speaker series that covers basic asset management topics, this is a helpful course. I would not recommend this class to other students. I think you really need to be fully engaged and willing to do 100% of the reading to have real learnings by the end of the semester.
Sam is very nice. If you're a finance person, you'll probably enjoy this class. To get something out of this class you have to read the books, which are very dry.
If core finance didn't do it for you and you want to expand your financial knowledge, this class is not for you. Yes, but likely not the course.

I would not recommend this class. I was excited going into it but did not learn much. Classes weren't particularly engaging and the content covered I mainly could have learned reading through wikipedia. Many people stopped going to class as the semester went on.
Yes, I thought the class was very valuable in terms of thinking about asset allocation. The textbooks were very useful and relevant as well.

Definitely - I took this class to become a better personal investor, and though it's approached through a more institutional lens (speakers from CALPERS, venture capital, who work in bonds, etc) I still learned a ton. I spent years pretending to know what the different was between private equity and venture capital, or not knowing what it meant to be on the sell-side or buy-side of investment banking, and now I can explain it comfortably. Sam is a genuinely very kind teacher who clearly knows the field very well and makes himself very approachable and available to students. I would recommend this instructor and course as long as you do the readings prior to class and come prepared. Otherwise, the midterm and final project will be challenging since there are not other assignments or exercises in between to check on learning of topics.

I think the class can be really valuable in the right setting, but I'm not I would take this class in retrospect Yes: the instructor is helpful and just wants his students to learn. The course gave me confidence in building and managing my own portfolio and at least understanding what someone else managing a portfolio is doing well or poorly which was my goal.
Absolutely! Was a really valuable class with low lift
I think the class was helpful, but it isn't a must-take class.
Yes - perhaps highest financial ROI class I'll have taken at Haas

No - there are other ways, and possibly other Haas classes to learn this topic in a more engaging manner. No, it was low energy and I don't think it even remotely met my expectations coming into the class.
Recommended if the students would like to know more about asset management in general.
Yes
If you don't have a good foundational knowledge in different asset classes, this is a very helpful course. If you're already familiar with them, I don't see how this class would be of great help.

Without some serious re-tooling, I would not recommend this class if you really want to learn asset management. This is a very low lift class that resulted in some learning, but class usually felt like a burden instead of exciting. Yes, this is a good overview of asset management for those interested in the field or looking to manage their personal finances

Yes I would! It is a very useful class to have even if you do not wish to pursue a career in finance. From a personal investor view point, this class has been extremely useful in helping me to crystallize my thoughts and thesis on which asset class to choose and invest in.
Yes because it touches on all types of investments and analysis methods.

I wouldn't recommend this unless you feel totally lost and have no idea at all when thinking about how to invest personally--it's not going to help prepare you for a buy side role. I think a little more structure and practical focus on portfolio construction would go a long way. The final project was really good for that, but thinking through the content of a few actual investment vehicles (i.e. what are the components of an ETF that is designed to cover the global market? Why is it set up like that?). I think we could scrap the section on technical analysis and the individual presentations. Also, the students were often disengaged and on their computers.

I would recommend both this class and the professor. I feel confident in my ability to become my own investor and allocate my assets. The class is a light lift, but I would HIGHLY recommend doing all of the readings because they were actually great! The books, podcasts, and articles Sam assigned added to my learning.
yes, substantial learning

Sam is a great professor and great person and this is a good survey course to gain familiarity with portfolio construction and multiple asset classes. It may not go into as much detail as you'd like if you have a background in asset management, but it's still been a good experience overall.
This course gives a great overview of asset management and the basics of investing your money. This is an
introductory class that is a very light lift. It is valuable for people who do not understand investing, but it is not meant for people who already understand asset management.
I would recommend Asset Management with Sam Olesky to my fellow students. It was a great overview of the

different types of assets we can invest in and the considerations associated with each one. I think it's a great primer for those who may want to start investing their own money / building their own wealth. Sam makes the topic very approachable and he has great real-world knowledge that he brings to the classroom.

If you are new to the world of finance then yes, if not then no. Before this class, I didn't understand how hedge, mutual, or index funds worked not I do right not in great detail, still not an expert. Great entry-level course - if you have any finance experience might not be worth your while
Yes
yes, Sam is good at this subject, and goes through the material at a good pace

Definitely! Especially for students thinking of pursuing a career in finance as Sam gives a great overview of the industry This course is a great way to learn a broad perspective of all the investable asset classes and how each one can be valuable in an investment portfolio. If you want to learn how to invest your savings or retirement, this course is a great way to teach you how to do that.
Yes.
No.
I would absolutely recommend Sam Olesky and the Asset Management course to other students. I'm honestly

surprised that this class isn't part of the core curriculum - the content is incredibly practical (and interesting) even for students who do not plan to go into finance professionally. There is a mix of the professor's lectures, guest lectures, and student mini-presentations, which keeps the course fresh, and the workload outside of class is very manageable. Sam is well-organized, thoughtful, engaging, and always patient with questions (and willing to stay after class to chat about any topic whatsoever). If you have the opportunity to take this class with Sam - do it!
Good course - general perspective on asset allocation and investing.
Yes, I think this is an important course for everyone given everyone will be managing either their own money or others for the remainder of their life.
Yes, its a good class but only scratches the basics of asset management.

YES! This was probably the most beneficial class for me at Haas. Because I started from almost 0 in terms of knowledge level. Prioritize classes based on the learning goals you have and take on classes that will complement your current skillset. I learned practical skills that will be useful for my personal investing strategy.
yes. if not directly relevant to goals, knowing how to manage money is a life long skill.

Yes, it is a very great class for students who want to learn investment, not only professionally, but also personally. Yes I would, this is a great class to understand the market and asset management. Definitely worthwhile taking a class with Sam also
Yes!

Yes! Professor Olesky is a great professor and expert in asset management. I would recommend this course to any student interested in asset management as a career (there are great guest speakers from top asset management firms most weeks) and/or students interested in personal asset management and learning about different investment strategies and asset classes.
Highly recommend this course and Professor Olesky to gain a broad overview to different investment opportunities in a digestable way.

The course is very basic and theoretical. It tries to cover a lot of content, staying on the surface and citing a lot of literature. It has a bias towards liquid investments/public markets. I think it was rather scattered, not very useful for someone who already has experience in investing. If you want to go "beyond yourself" in the class projects, you will probably be punished more than rewarded. I would recommend the course for someone with no prior investment knowledge, who wants a broad overview of the subject.

I highly recommend this course. I learned a great deal about asset management after knowing very little prior, and feel like the lessons learned are applicable across contexts (e.g., for strategic decision-making generally). The professor is also really good listener and creates space for student questions and perspectives.
I think this course is great and helpful if you want to learn about the markets and different approaches. Helpful for personal and professional learnings.

First set your expectations right - this course teaches you about the various asset classes and factors to consider when investing in each asset. The class does NOT deal with personal investments. There are a lot of speakers in the course, so if you are looking for making more connections in the industry this class is useful.
The slides and class discussion can feel a bit dry to people who come from non-finance backgrounds.
Yes, I would. Extremely insightful and important as a MBA student to take this course.

Sure Its helpful for students who are willing to pursue a career in asset management and build a strong portfolio! I would recommend this course to someone who is not well versed on asset management and wants to know how to manage their personal portfolio. The class is also relatively little work, so go for it if that is your priority. I personally would have preferred a more intensive course where I could have learned more.
More than anything, I would HIGHLY recommend reading both books assigned for the course (Unconventional
Success and A Random Walk Down Wall Street). I read both before the class started and got most of what I needed to know from them, rather than the class.

I would recommend this class to anyone going into asset management, private wealth management, etc. However, the level of the class is quite basic so if you already come from that sort of background you would likely not benefit as much from the actual lectures (you may still benefit from the guest speakers however).
of course! I like the guest speaker sessions a lot. The speakers provided a bunch of practical insights.
I would recommend. It is a great foundational course.

I believe that every MBA student should leave the program with an understanding of how to manage their assets and investment portfolios. Some of the content does overlap with the core finance course, but there are many discussions around alternative investments and asset classes which our intro finance did not cover. If you are an experienced finance professional already, a more intensive course such as corporate finance may be a better fit.
Not sure if I would recommend. Depends on the background of the student. Student with previous knowledge in finance might find this class too basic.

I would recommend this course. It gives a great overview of investment management and the universe of (common) asset classes. Sam's lectures are informative and interesting, as are his guest speakers.
I would recommend this course.

Yes. The course provides valuable insights into investment strategies, portfolio management, and the psychology of markets. Prof. Olesky is an engaging and knowledgeable instructor who effectively connected theoretical concepts with real-world applications. The class discussions and case studies are particularly enriching, fostering both analytical thinking and practical understanding. However, students should be prepared for a significant amount of reading outside of class and come ready to actively discuss the material to fully benefit from the course.
I probably wouldn't. I don't feel I got my money's worth this time around.

Yes, I would definitely recommend Sam and this class! It's been one of the most useful courses I've taken at Haas since you learn a lot about investing. Therefore, it's really helpful for how you should think about allocating your personal portfolio. Sam is a really caring and knowledgeable professor who wants to make sure we learn!

sections.goodFor: Students without a finance background who want a 30,000-foot survey of asset management and a map of the career options in it; guest speakers are a draw.
sections.notFor: Anyone who has worked in the industry, or who wants specific financial concepts applicable in a role - coverage is broad and stays shallow.
sections.workloadNote: Not discussed. Very thin evidence - 8 short comments, several one-liners, no mention of assignments or readings.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: 2 of 8 say the breadth of asset classes keeps everything at a high level; 1 of those also calls the classes not particularly engaging. Small sample, so treat as directional.
sections.quote: Covering such a broad range of asset classes is an ambitious goal, and as a result each asset type was explored only at a high level.
comments: 100% SAM OLESKY IS AN INCREDIBLY EFFECTIVE TEACHER AND THE MATERIAL IS INTEGRAL FOR ANY STUDENT
INTERESTED IN FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT WHETHER PERSONAL OR PROFESSIONAL.

Yes, great for a general overview of asset management, especially if you don't have a background in finance. I would recommend this course to any students who want an overview of the different career options that exist in asset management as Sam does a good job providing a 30,000 foot view. For anyone that has worked in the industry, I wouldn't say it's necessary to take the class.
Yes. He is the best
Yes

I would not recommend the course. Covering such a broad range of asset classes is an ambitious goal, and as a result each asset type was explored only at a high level. Combined with classes that were not particularly engaging, it was difficult to gain a deeper understanding of the material.

I would recommend it if you're interested in learning about different parts of asset management from a professor and guest speakers who have had very successful careers in the industry. Professor Olesky has a wealth of knowledge and passion for asset management, which makes the course more interesting. However, if you're trying to learn specific financial concepts that you can apply in a future role, I would probably recommend a different course.

rows.title: Design, Evaluate, and Scale Development Technologies

comments: The class is truly unique in giving MBAs a chance to work in real development issues (I worked on water and electricity access in rural sub Saharan Africa) also great chance to work with engineers and other disciplines as an MBA. It could definitely be better structured but I would take it again if I could go back a semester.
Definitely wouldn't recommend it. Very high level, we didn't learn much theory.

sections.goodFor: Students with a food-system idea they genuinely plan to pursue after graduation, who value community, reciprocity, and diverse speakers from across the food system.
sections.notFor: Anyone without an idea they are excited about - both commenters say the value depends on bringing one you intend to deeply pursue outside class.
sections.workloadNote: The class is what you make it; teams matter but some students worked alone and still produced strong final projects. Only 2 comments - no workload detail at all.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; a final project/business idea is the visible output.
sections.quote: Yes, but only if you have an idea for a business that you are planning on deeply pursuing outside of class/after graduating.
comments: Yes, but only if you have an idea for a business that you are planning on deeply pursuing outside of class/after graduating.

I would recommend this class to folks who are really interested in improving the food system. The class is what you make it, and it definitely helps if there's an idea you're super stoked about pursuing. Your team is important, but folks also worked alone and so many people ended up with amazing final projects and business ideas. Will is a phenomenal connector and community builder, and puts a lot of care into creating a positive, systems-change focused

environment within the class. He brings in diverse speakers from all nodes of the food system. I value the space and community this class provided, and the opportunity to reach out to and learn from so many talented people. I love Will's focus on reciprocity and am carrying that into my future work and projects.

rows.title: Haas Sustainable Investment Fund
rows.terms: 2021 Fall;2022 Spring;2022 Fall;2023 Spring;2023 Fall;2024 Fall;2025 Spring

comments: Yes! Great opportunity to practice making investments in a supportive setting. Super interesting guest speakers too! I would say it depends on what your interests are. For me, this is new topics for me so it was hard for me to participate and feel engaged. Student's knowledge in this space is very broad so I think it's hard to tailor the course based on background.

The Instructor's are truly legends in the field and are very generous with their knowledge. However this course is quite unstructured and the learning outcomes were unclear. I became frustrated with the lack of process around decisions and clarity on how we were being graded.

I would recommend this course to anyone with an interest in sustainable finance who is willing to be a self starter and to throw away all of their pre-conceptions about the investment industry. Its a great opportunity to challenge the status quo and explore innovative and exciting ideas, but does require a high amount of initiative from the students. SIF is a great class! Unparalleled access to industry leaders. You really get what you put in!

I have learned so much from John and Anne. They are at the forefront of sustainable investing and bring the nuance and complexity of the industry to life while also bringing an intense optimism for the possibilities within the space. They bring in fantastic guest speakers and make themselves available to us as resources often. It is a relatively unstructured course thus far, which is great if you have a lot of ideas or areas you want to explore. Future iterations of the class will likely be more structured in some ways, as this is the first time they are teaching it, but they are committed to helping us learn about what we want to learn about, which is great.
Yes, especially people without any investment or ESG background.

The course is not a good option for students with little / no experience in the investment industry, even though allegedly it's not a pre-requisite. This greatly undermines the ability of students with different backgrounds to succeed in the course, creating an unfair environment.

This is an incredibly interactive class that will challenge your assumptions on what sustainable investing looks like. While it's challenging managing group work among 10-15 principals, I find this class very worthwhile.

Absolutely--if you're interested in any aspect of ESG investing, public or private, there is no better source for the latest industry movements, dynamics, happenings, and strategies than in John and Anne. The course is being rebuilt, which comes with growing pains, but after this year it should be smooth in addition to being incredible.

I was really excited to take this course based on who was teaching it, but I honestly would not recommend the course.
