The course was very student run which was a little frustrating given the amount we pay for tuition. There were questions asked in class and the professors would often say, "why don't you research that and get back to the class." Yes, the professors are very well connected but it's clear that they have never taught a course before, which becomes frustrating when you're unsure of learning objectives and target deliverables. There are also a lot of varying levels of understanding in the class which made things difficult because overviews were never really provided to get people on the same page. There were a lot of guest speakers but I would have preferred more learning and less guest speakers. No. I learned more in this clas in the little hour I spent working with a partner than I did the entire semester. I do not come fromthe ESG impact investing space and this course only allowed those who do to shine and elevate their opinions

Highly recommend this class if you are enthusiastic about the idea of being launched into the day-to-day of investment management. The coursework and decisions are very applied, but as a result some of the focus of the class might be less interesting to people who are not interested in the tactical elements of sustainable investing. The instructors (Anne Simpson & John Goldstein) are so knowledgeable and leaders in the field - it has been very fun to learn under their guidance.

Cool practice of ESG public equity investing with really cool professors. You'll get to hear from very high profile guest speakers. It is public equities though, so make sure you are interested in that topic (versus other forms of sustainable investing).

Yes I would. It's a self-driven class, so the first few months of the class are really dedicated to building the class structure, so be aware of this. If you don't like ambiguity, then you may find yourself confused or lost at times - something to be aware of.

If you are passionate about investment management and want to explore the intersection of sustainability and investing, than this is the class for you! If this is not your career path, I would stay away. This class is why I came to haas so I enjoyed it, but it was solely due to personal interest. The class did nothing to amplify this interest, and in fact made it hard to learn and enjoy.

This class has a lot of potential and likely changes year to year depending on the instructor and how they would like to manage the curriculum. This year, with two new professional faculty members, there was little learning to be had. It was entirely self-guided. I did learn about the specific stocks I pitched and it was nice to be part of a community focused on sustainable investing, but I would not recommend it in its current format.
DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. I have never in my life experienced a course that did not have a syllabus and was

completely student run (when there were two paid professionals supposed to be running it). The fact that people in our class had to create a " syllabus " so we had any direction on what to do in the class was absolutely insane. Also, these students never got paid despite doing the job of a GSI. Furthermore, I've never been apart of the course where the professors showed up less frequently than the students, which is saying a lot considering I missed 3 classes this semester. The worst part about the professors not being in class was that we would never have a heads up, so we would show up to class and no one would be there to teach. There was never any teaching in the class. If you didn't know how to do something and emailed the professor they would never respond, so you were kind of out of luck. People who came from the finance background did all of the work for projects because I truly didn't even know how to. Professors did not respond to emails, even after many follow ups. Professors were also often times doing other work on their computer during class. I can't even believe they were being paid. Again, an insane course to even be offered. Don't take it.
Absolutely. Fantastic intersection of theory and practice and the instructors are a real value-add
Yes. Great class. Lots of great speakers. Applied knowledge.
Yes, very practical and hands on experience. It's real money.

Yes, as the experiential learnings achieved from adjusting the Investment Policy Statement and allocation ranges, making and acting upon pitches, and pursuing adjacent learning opportunities (advocacy case competitions etc.) gave a well–rounded learning experience more than worth the 4 credits required. Ideal class for applying prior learnings from FIA, Portfolio Construction and other prerequisites and FIN/SUST courses.
Definitely yes!! This class is a must for students interested in sustainable finance. It's a great way to have real life learning and practice of managing a portfolio and learning about ESG
You get out what you put in – this can be a great opportunity if you're willing to take the lead as a student
Excellent course to learn how to manage a portfolio of assets with a focus on both financial and impact metrics. In short, there is nothing like managing an actual $4+ MM fund as an MBA student!
100%. Incredible course and instructor team
I'd recommend this course to anyone that is interested in learning more about impact investing! The hands–on approach makes it so that you learn an incredible amount about how a fund is managed.

Yes of course, If anybody want to understand real impact investment philosophy, how can create sustainable investment and how practically do all this staff in the class this course definitely suited for that person. Maybe, it really depends on the participation of the fellow peers as well as how much financial background and comfort they have. This class is a hidden treasure but I wish it had an additional lab component to master some of the technical skills and the tools/databases we have been introduced to. This should be a 3 hour course!

sections.goodFor: Self-directed students who want real portfolio and impact-investing experience and can tolerate a very small, loosely structured cohort.
sections.notFor: Students who need structured hands-on practice with Bloomberg, FactSet or CapIQ, or a properly enrolled class - the section dwindled to about six people.
sections.workloadNote: Managing a real portfolio is described as a lot of work, but nothing is quantified. Only 2 comments - very thin evidence. Students want a lab component added.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; lectures, speakers and portfolio management work are described, but grading is not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Both comments raise execution gaps: enrollment collapsed to about 6 students, there is no lab component for Bloomberg/FactSet/CapIQ practice, and lectures and speakers are not paired with practical tasks.
sections.quote: The class in theory is so great, but the execution was short of my expecations given my classmates were only 5 others by the end of the year.
comments: Yes and No. The class in theory is so great, but the execution was short of my expecations given my classmates were only 5 others by the end of the year. It takes a lot of work to manage a portfolio and learning to do so takes time. I would add a lab component and make sure the class is well enrolled. I would have found it useful to have more lab practice on using resources like Bloomberg terminals, Facset, CapIQ, and the myriad of other resources available to us for this course. But learning is best done by doing, so more hands on experience would have been useful. Highly recommend, but I believe there are much more to improve, like how to apply our skills early on, how each lecture and speaker could be paired with more practical tasks. Despited these, I still learned so much that it changed my way of thinking about how to create impact.

No, because while the breadth was wide and interesting in terms of range of topics/cases studied, the depth was far too shallow, and left me wondering what I was supposed to takeaway for each topic. Professors kept it lively and engaging, such that students unfamiliar with most aspects of sustainability probably took away alot from the topic intro discussions. But for those of us who live and breathe this daily, this did not result in substantial learning. Better to use the valuable 3 credits on denser courses, such as C2M (also a final pre-req for Sust. Certificate). It depends - the best parts of the class for me were most of the readings and the consulting project. I would recommend the course as is to someone who can be self-directed.

Yes, if changes are made to the course. The client project is the most significant part of the course and learning opportunity, so it would be useful to know who those clients are (and, of possible, what the projects are) in advance. Supplemental readings weren't as useful as hearing from the amazing guest speakers who came in and presented and from the professors themselves, who have extremely relevant work experience in CSR work.
yes, great way to do sustainability work for a major client and get hands on experience. some of the readings are pretty lengthy but otherwise really good reads and great speakers

Yes, it is helpful to do sustainability strategy consulting projects to get to know what is happening in the industry I would, the consulting aspect of the course was the only part I did not enjoy. Overall the course is interesting and engaging. If they ever offer this course as a non applied innovation course I would recommend without equivocation. I found this class underwhelming and disappointing. I entered the class hoping to learn generalizable strategies on how to sustainably operate in a business setting and frankly all I learned with respect to that was a few facts about the bleak state of the environment. The vast majority of the class was focused on consulting practices and presentation practices, which was absolutely not what I signed up for and I frankly felt misled by the class description. I also felt the lecture practices left a lot to be desired. The three main types of classes were: group time to work on our consulting projects, guest lecturers, and case studies. For one, the group time felt redundant and unnecessary for our group (and I can imagine most groups, who were already encouraged to meet multiple times a week), and really just felt like a time for the professors to catch up on the projects; not a great use of one out of every 5 classes in my opinion. I also found almost all of the speakers esoteric and not engaging. After almost every one of the presentations I left feeling uninspired and unable to extrapolate almost anything I had heard to general concepts that I could leverage in the future. Finally, the case studies seemed like exercises to fill the class period rather than exercises to learn from. There was almost never a comprehensive debrief from the professors. All of the discussions occurred in groups of my peers, who are equally as unknowledgeable as I am, and as such resulted in almost zero learning on my end, and I can imagine limited learning for my peers. What I was most disappointed by in the class was the dogmatic focus on the consulting framework and the lack of lectures that actually revolved around sustainable strategies. I really don't feel like I learned much except how handwavy consulting can be. I hope this class takes on a different tone in the future if it is offered.

I would recommend the course. There is a lot to learn, especially about consulting and dealing with clients. But I would really warn you about how important teams are. Do not take this class if you are not going to do any work. You are just hurting your teammates who have to carry you. Pick your teams wisely, and hope that your client is a good one. They are vetted by the professors, but sometimes clients can still be really MIA and it makes the semester very stressful. Yes I would! Clients are great and projects super interesting
If you aren't super passionate about sustainability this class can feel like an echo chamber which can sometimes be frustrating.
Aleksandra and Debbie are a great teaching duo. Their class, Strategic and Sustainable Business Solutions, was one of the top 3 I took during my time at Haas.
I would recommend this course if you are planning on working on sustainability consulting or have some real life experience in the sustainability field.
Yes fun class

As an applied innovation course, a student's experience change vary depending upon which project they are placed on. This class is helpful in understanding how sustainability decisions are made within organizations, but does not deeply cover sustainability field learnings.

This course is a great Applied Innovation for anyone looking to go into consulting who is interested in ESG based work. It was a heavy lift due to the client project, but Sasha and Debbie are two of the coolest professors and just professional contacts and it's worth taking just to have them in your corner!
Yes! Great experience working with an outside company and see what it's like to work as a consultant.

The course gives great overview to corporate sustainability practices and covers diverse topics (environment, human rights, ecosystems, etc). I found the concept of systems thinking extremely useful. Practicing consultancy was new to me, so the course gave me an insightful experience in general. Very organized, workload is not heavy, although depends on the client project. Also guest speakers were amazing!

Yes, I would recommend this course with these instructors to a fellow student since it is a course that prepares you very well to go into the sustainability industry. This course has a wide variety of guest speakers and includes a consulting project that gives you real-life experience.

think twice. Would love to see more engaged with clients before class starts as I feel there was miscommunication between clients and the instructor team. This leads to a much heavier workload for the consulting projects due to lack of guidance and client's over-ambitious asks

I have already been recommending this class to my peers. My project was extremely interesting and helped solidify my interest in consulting, energy, and sustainability. This class is a lot of work, but I had an amazing group and got through it while learning a ton.

sections.goodFor: Students targeting sustainability/ESG or consulting careers who want real client experience with big-name companies, exposure to strong guest speakers, and instructors commenters describe as experienced and well worth knowing; best for the self-directed who can handle a variable, team-heavy workload.
sections.notFor: Anyone expecting to be taught consulting skills or deep sustainability content in class; the experience hinges heavily on your assigned client and team, remote and mixed-program teams frustrated many, and several 2024 Fall commenters flatly called the current format a waste of time.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy and unpredictable: the client project can balloon when clients give little direction, and several found it unmanageable stacked on a full-time job or other demanding courses.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (7+ comments): outcome depends on client and team luck, with vague or absent clients and disjointed mixed-cohort teams derailing projects. Recurring (5+): class sessions and speakers do not teach consulting skills or connect to the project. A few (3): class content felt shallow for people already in the sustainability field.
sections.quote: I would recommend it to someone, but the quality of the course is very dependant on the group and the project you get
comments: Yes for FT/EW/EMBA. Not for flex MBA as this should be an in person class not Zoom. Hard to build team in such short time frame remotely. Students not from around the campus tended to be disconnected

I would recommend this to classmates interested in consulting careers, and sustainability. It's a fantastic opportunity to network with companies leading sustainability work, and gain real experience managing clients and large teams. I would NOT recommend fellow EWMBA classmates to take this course in the spring of their second year. Between this course, the additional Leadership communications course, and capstone Strategy course, the workload was very unmanageable for me on top of a full time job.

I would not, I had a hard time working with my group. We all had different schedules (a mix of part time, full time and other schools) there were too many of us on calls to be effective, and the client didn't even know what he wanted. Calls often went on long tangents (internal team calls), people couldn't chime in, and trying to figure out what all 7 people had to say was an issue. While real-life consulting projects are better equipped for this, learning other people's working style in tandem to trying to unpack what your clients want, all over the course of a few months was ineffective. Often times it was the same few people contributing, communication was disjointed and every week we were
scrambling to find something to deliver to our client who provided almost no direction on what he wanted.

Yes. The course is very relevant to today's sustainability challenges. Guest speaker are excellent. Instructors have real hands on experience about the sustainability issues and their experience is very enriching. The projects are also a great opportunity to work on an actual problem. Great class overall!

I would recommend being taught by Debbie and Sasha; they are amazing. The thing I am disappointed with the class is just how we don't learn consulting skills. Some people are unfamiliar with consulting schemes, and given some teammates have more skills, and this course is online, it's really hard to learn from one another. It is siloed, and we can't learn that much. I especially wish the teaching team could make a prior agreement with the client and a clear timeline for them so we can really get through the project without any obstacles.
Yes I would strongly recommend

I would not recommend this course until you are insanely passionate about hearing about social causes. Since this class has a project element, I found the course content and speakers were useless to the project. I would have enjoyed it more if it had been a class without a heavy project. However, having to sit through class and then find hours to work on the project outside of the classroom was very time-consuming, especially since each team consisted of FTMBA and EWMBA. In addition, the content taught in class was not useful to the project at all. I was spending double the time and effort for this class.

The clients that this class gives access to are great (big name brands), but the content of the class itself could have been made more difficult engaging. The cases were great, but we had too many guest speakers, and too little time to discuss the cases as a whole, which could be fixed
Absolutely not - a total waste of time. You won't learn anything about consulting.
It's a glorified speaker series but with an external client.
I would recommend it to someone, but the quality of the course is very dependant on the group and the project you get
I would not recommend this class in its current state.
Yes!
You can always learn something. However, this class could be better thought out to have a richer learning experience.

comments: I would recommend this class. It's an interesting class with a focused topic, and lots of practical topics and speakers. It is relatively new in its current format, so I think it will get better through time.
Yes great course to learn about sustainable investment and apply it in practice

I think despite the sustainability lens it is also a great way to gain exposure to the asset management / stock investing world in a hands - on manner.
Yes! Excellent learnings from world-class professors!
the class needs clearer structure and learning perspective from the beginning and the expected engagement with the students
you will learn a lot but the knowledge is kinda scattered around throughout the course, not knowing what's coming at you week-by-week
Yes!Anne & Peter are great to learn from as professionals doing the work in the space. Panos passion on subject matter and research is a great compliment to them both. Great class!

Great experiential learning experience with professors with both deep academic and professional backgrounds Yes! Have already recommended it to friends. Yes I would recommend this class. It was a brand new topic for me and although I felt intimidated at first, by the end I felt like I was up to speed and had learned a lot!

Yes for FT/EW/EMBA. Not for flex MBA as this should be an in person class not Zoom. Hard to build team in such short time frame remotely. Students not from around the campus tended to be disconnected

I would recommend this to classmates interested in consulting careers, and sustainability. It's a fantastic opportunity to network with companies leading sustainability work, and gain real experience managing clients and large teams. I would NOT recommend fellow EWMBA classmates to take this course in the spring of their second year. Between this course, the additional Leadership communications course, and capstone Strategy course, the workload was very unmanageable for me on top of a full time job.

I would not, I had a hard time working with my group. We all had different schedules (a mix of part time, full time and other schools) there were too many of us on calls to be effective, and the client didn't even know what he wanted. Calls often went on long tangents (internal team calls), people couldn't chime in, and trying to figure out what all 7 people had to say was an issue. While real-life consulting projects are better equipped for this, learning other people's working style in tandem to trying to unpack what your clients want, all over the course of a few months was ineffective. Often times it was the same few people contributing, communication was disjointed and every week we were
scrambling to find something to deliver to our client who provided almost no direction on what he wanted.

Yes. The course is very relevant to today's sustainability challenges. Guest speaker are excellent. Instructors have real hands on experience about the sustainability issues and their experience is very enriching. The projects are also a great opportunity to work on an actual problem. Great class overall!

I would recommend being taught by Debbie and Sasha; they are amazing. The thing I am disappointed with the class is just how we don't learn consulting skills. Some people are unfamiliar with consulting schemes, and given some teammates have more skills, and this course is online, it's really hard to learn from one another. It is siloed, and we can't learn that much. I especially wish the teaching team could make a prior agreement with the client and a clear timeline for them so we can really get through the project without any obstacles.
Yes I would strongly recommend

I would not recommend this course until you are insanely passionate about hearing about social causes. Since this class has a project element, I found the course content and speakers were useless to the project. I would have enjoyed it more if it had been a class without a heavy project. However, having to sit through class and then find hours to work on the project outside of the classroom was very time-consuming, especially since each team consisted of FTMBA and EWMBA. In addition, the content taught in class was not useful to the project at all. I was spending double the time and effort for this class.

The clients that this class gives access to are great (big name brands), but the content of the class itself could have been made more difficult engaging. The cases were great, but we had too many guest speakers, and too little time to discuss the cases as a whole, which could be fixed
Absolutely not - a total waste of time. You won't learn anything about consulting.
It's a glorified speaker series but with an external client.
I would recommend it to someone, but the quality of the course is very dependant on the group and the project you get
I would not recommend this class in its current state.
Yes!
You can always learn something. However, this class could be better thought out to have a richer learning experience.

sections.goodFor: Students who want a live client consulting project and a sustainability speaker series, can self-manage without guidance, or need the applied innovation credit.
sections.notFor: Anyone needing structure or instructor intervention: multiple students report disorganization, no consulting framework guidance, no way to fix a bad group, and basic lectures with little depth.
sections.workloadNote: Semester-long team consulting project with a real client plus a guest speaker series; little teacher-led content and few check-ins, so workload depends almost entirely on your group.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; the graded work is the client consulting project and deliverables, with a framework given but not enforced.
sections.redFlags: Disorganization and no guidance on the consulting framework recur (5 of 16); instructors don't step in when groups break down; lectures called basic; one alleges the instructor used material students criticised as unoriginal to teach.
sections.quote: The course experience is highly dependent on the group project. There's a lack of guidance on the consulting framework and implementation of the framework from professors
comments: yes
I would recommend this course - the opportunity to work with a client on a real business challenge is really great. There is also a good mix of guest lecturers and class-voted discussion topics.
Absolutely... YES! I learned a lot and the experiential part of it was invaluable.
Yes, recommend this class for those looking to get into a consulting career. It provides solid foundation and familiarizes you with real work in the consulting realm.
The experience to work with a real company is really valuable.
yes- both are very personable and I would recommend that students get to know them personally as well.
Honestly no, it's a bit unorganized. Your experience is very dependent on who is in your group, and instructors aren't able to step in to adjust if thinks are truly back

The course experience is highly dependent on the group project. There's a lack of guidance on the consulting framework and implementation of the framework from professors (while the framework is given, it does not seem like projects have to align to it/not enough check-ins to ensure that teams are on track using the framework). The other half of the course are really great guest speakers that gives an overview of various sustainabiltiy topics throughout the semester, however there's a lack of structure on teacher-led content.
I don't know. If the course materials continue to be so unorganized then i wouldn't recommand to anyone. Yes

Take this course! Great way to link theory and practice - completing the consulting project throughout the semester with a real company and real clients made it feel very hands-on and valuable learning experience where we actually made an impact. One of the best courses I've taken as someone with a sustainability background who had grown tired of redundant theoretical sustainability classes - this one was actually worth it and I learned new things. Fine class if you need the applied innovation credit, but don't take it for fun. Despite good topics, deep disorganization and over-indexing on consultant nonsense made this feel like a waste of time. Very disappointing.
Absolutely
Yes, very interesting course and the instructors were awesome!!

I would not recommend it. The class seems very spontaneous, without proper planning, and the consulting projects have no guidance, and no hierarchy so it it so hard to actually do them adequately. I think this should be a speaker series. That part was nice. But the consulting project felt like I was doomed to fail from the start. So bad. I would not recommend this course. Some of the guest speakers were interesting, but the teachings didn't build on top of each other well and depth of content was severely lacking. Lectures were very basic and I don't think the format took advantage of the instructors' wealth of experience. I walked away without any clear value-add to my education or professional toolkit.

Highly recommend. This Strategic Business course blends core strategy frameworks with a live consulting project, amplified by relevant guest speakers and candid, actionable feedback, you'll leave with sharper problem-structuring, stronger storytelling, and client-ready deliverables.
I would recommend this class to a student who would be interested in hearing lots of interesting guest speakers, but caution them on some of the concerns I raised in the previous section.

[REDACTED IN THE PUBLIC BUILD] A student said the course is not worth the tuition and that comparable material is freely available elsewhere, and criticised the quality and originality of the teaching material. — Why: The original makes a specific unverified factual claim about how a named instructor prepares their material.
yes
Yes! This is a comprehensive overview of AI in industry for a non-expert, with many opportunities for further reading and study, and connections with visiting speakers / VCs.
I would strongly recommend this course to other students. It is very well organized and taught, and the material is very relevant for pretty much any function or industry.

Great introduction to core AI concepts in a way that is relevant to business leaders. Videos were a great asset to absorbing material at one's own pace, especially for non-technical folks. There's a great opportunity to make this a more extensive course that gives students more time to learn about and apply these concepts — hoping that happens in later iterations!
This is a great class on the high level technical and business landscape of AI - highly recommend!
My favorite Zoom class this year!! Topics were super engaging, professors are fascinating, and class was very well structured.
Yes. This course is a good introduction to the applications of AI. I would've preferred to attend this class in person since taking this on Zoom does impact the level of engagement.

Whether or not you want to pursue a career related to AI, This course is a must in order to become a more educated being who can understand the future world better (no matter which industry or sector or role you are or want to be in). Maybe. This was worth it in terms of time commitment for a 1 credit class. However, content was very boring and lots of lecture.

Yes! Great course. Touches on the technical aspects, business aspects, and ethical aspects of modern AI applications. Definitely. For anyone interested in AI, this class is gives just enough technical detail to understand the technology but also digs into the business applications, limitations, and areas for continued improvement (e.g., where you can invest for your next big idea!)

Yes, it was very interesting to understand what the different companies are doing in terms of AI, and also understand some technical terms I've often heard from my AI Data scientists and engineers at work but wasn't aware of what they meant

Absolutely, this was a great class that showcased topics on emerging business and technology trends. I also liked how there was a little match but most of the subject matter was in regular every day language more appropriate to a manager who needs to be able to communicate and understand key AI concepts.

A good course covering the technical and business aspects of AI in the world today. There was a lot of self-directed video watching to do before the sessions which can get a bit monotonous and confusing at times, as these videos provide the foundation for all other discussion and learning.
Cases were very relevant, recent, and applicable to the topics at hand, and all of the professors are extremely knowledgable in their field.
Getting to learn from Pieter Abbeel is a treat. The rest of the class is average MBA fare.
Yes, Very good introduction to AI and ML. If you don't know anything and want to immerse in the topic, the course it's a great way to do it.

Yes, I would recommend these instructor and this course to other students. The course did a great job of giving students a peek under the hood of how many complex AI applications work, and it did a good job of highlighting the capabilities, complexities, and limitations of the technology in the field. The course had a good mix of technical explanations, business case studies, and thought exercises around strategy or investment scenarios that will be helpful for anybody working with or managing AI applications in the future.
I would not recommend this class to a fellow student.

As a first introduction or primer to the area of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, the pure content was informative. The deep problem was in how the content was presented. The instructors lectured off of slides for the large majority of both classes. I mean — straight up reading off of slides. Most of the lectures could have been pre- recorded videos, or presented in a custom course-pack to be read ahead of time. Of the 4 cases to read, only 1 was actually pertinent to business practices. The case discussions were extremely light — too light. The deep learning homework assignment was good for someone who never worked in python (like myself).
Yes, great use of bringing in real-world companies to reinforce course concepts.

Good course to get an intro to how AI works and recent developments in the industry. Nothing too technical and assignments were applicable and conducive to learning - for ex, there's a small assignment to get exposure to machine learning code.

I would recommend this class overall. It was full of engaging material that was well worth the time. Meaningful grading is a challenge here though. Despite how hard one works, grades may come down to ability to decipher quiz questions that do not necessarily look like class material (or have the similar phrasing). There's room for improvement there. But I loved the material and would make the choice to take the class again. If you have a change to audit, this would have been a GREAT candidate for doing so.
I would strongly recommend this course
Great Experience! The class was delivered very well. A lot of insights into the topic.
Great for understanding the basics of tech and application of machine learning to date

As it is today, I would not recommend this course. I was really excited about the potential of the content but was really disappointed in the delivery. All three professors spoke only to slides for 7.5 hours straight over 2 days. I was interested in the content for my career but this was way too In the weeds for me... was more like a data class than business. While some of the content was interesting on the surface, the teaching format was extremely dry and made it hard to stay alert, especially on a weekend. Also there was wayyy too much work for a one unit class. I hope the professors can make some improvements because I think there IS potential here!
yes, interesting class
This class was okay. If you're new to AI/ML this could be a good opener, but overall the class sessions felt extremely long as professors mostly just presented from slides for 7 hours each day.
Absolutely must take class even if you have prior computer science background. I came from an engineering

background, and have taken various online courses in AI, and still find this to be extremely worthwhile. The class is heavily integrated with the industry. VCs are invited, to share their insights on the AI industry. One of the instructors is one of the most recognized AI experts in the industry. What he shares is what you usually can't find from textbooks or online classes. This class is like having Gordon Ramsey teaching you all about cooking.
I highly recommend this course, particularly for non-technical busniess people. AI and ML is extremely important to the future of all business types. Ignore at your own peril.

Yes - this is a very interactive class for students who want to have a quick download of the industry and trends If you're interested in AI, applications, and future outlook, this class will give you a very engaging taste of all relevant topics. Good way to "wet the beak" and mapping out where to deep dive next!

Yes, especially if the student is interested in learning about AI, they do a great job covering it in detail. However, yes only if adjustments are made to the workload to make it appropriate for a 1 unit course. This course should be worth 2 units given the amount of work we did.

Are you ready to take your brain to the next level of innovation? Then look no further than this cutting-edge, trailblazing, forward-thinking, and most of all, innovative graduate course about AI! Prepare to be blown away by the innovative methods and innovative tools used to innovate in the field of AI. You'll explore innovative techniques like deep learning, innovative algorithms that use innovative data structures, and innovative models that are pushing the boundaries of what we thought was possible. Don't be left behind in the dust of old-fashioned thinking! Join us in this innovative course and unleash your inner innovator! So come on and sign up today for an innovative and mind- blowing experience that will leave you innovatively innovating for years to come!
Tagline: "Innovate to dominate, or innovate to detonate!"

I'm uncertain if I would recommend this course. It has very intense technical content, which most MBAs are not aware of (and not interested in learning lots of equations) of. Having three professors is a good thing as they alternate and make the Sunday class seem like many different classes. The cases are interesting and applicable to real life and great for discussion, but I often missed a "so what" to the discussions.

This course can get pretty technical at some points and the course work seemed pretty heavy for a 1 unit course. That being said, the material was very interesting and fascinating. The professors were all very accomplished and brought great insights to class. Hearing about their real-world experiences at the forefront of AI was super valuable. I would recommend this course if you are just looking to learn some basic concepts and some of the applications. Absolutely recommend this course!

This course covers a broad range of topics within the field of AI. We reviewed everything from cases to a coding assignment (with guidance) and looked at startups doing AI work. However, given that we only had two days, we didn't dive too far into one particular topic in AI. It was good as a primer for students who don't have a background in AI. I thought it was worthwhile in that regard.

Would recommend if interested in topic and enjoyed classes such as data analytics. Class felt more like just pure AI and was lighter on talking about the actual business of AI (how to make money using AI, how much it costs, etc.) Yes, highly recommend this class!
this was very interesting as an intro course. I liked the VC panel, the computer vision session especially. Strongly recommend
Definite yes. Great 101 and 2 day base on business of AI. Can be fast and overwhelming at times, but overall feel I learnt a lot.

I would recommend having a 2 credit course with more detail. I think 1 credit is less and does not cover everything. Recommend this class to anyone who has little or no background in the subject of AI. Matthew Strepka brought his industry experience to the classroom. He was candid with his investment philosophy and brought his industry contacts to bear by inviting guest speakers deeply experienced in the field. Pieter is a leading figure in the field. He did a phenomenal job ensuring that the technical details of AI were covered well without losing the class in the weeds. I had no knowledge of AI and wanted to get a good overview as a future manager which I feel I got from this class. The morning of the second day definitely covered too much of the technical aspects, though. I wish we had spent more time hearing about businesses and covering case studies.

Yes, This class is well organized, and taught with a genuine passion. The exposure to the VC panel was awesome, the numerous cases and guest speakers were truly informative. Understanding AI is so essential for any future business professional. I think this course is invaluable. One of my best courses so far at Haas
very long course with no discussion or group work. too much lecturing.

comments: yes i would recommend both instructors to a fellow student. i would recommend the class only for people that are really interested in learning about what goes in the pro forma of developments
I like Nancy. But the guest speaker series become very boring after a while.
Strongly recommended. Nancy is one of the best professors and she is so knowledgeable in real estate. Highly recommended and this is personally enriching class.

Nancy is one of the most actively anti-racist teachers I have had at Haas. She uses quantitative research to both evidence examples of systemic racism while working actively to remediate those structures moving forward through her research and policy recommendations.

Yes, with the caveat that the class is mostly guest presenters and that one should have either or both a strong interest in real estate or previous experience in real estate. Many topics were esoteric, and not suitable for those seeking a "101" style course.

Yes! Take this course, especially if Nancy Wallace is teaching it. You will learn a lot about real estate. Yes - Nancy is an amazing instructor and Ed is a great resource. That being said, to some extent, it's up to the student to be proactive and utilize these amazing resources effectively.

Absolutely recommend for anyone looking to continue (or start) working in real estate business. May be too detailed / specific for someone just curious about Real Estate and not really planning to work in the area.
90% spent on sustainability - 10% spent on investment analysis.
Yes, for any real estate focused MBA student this class is a must.

Yes but probably only if they're serious about real estate. This isn't a particularly low lift class and a lot of the onus for learning is on the student. The speakers are fantastic and the teachers are very knowledgeable.

This is an incredible course if you're looking to understand the intersection between real estate investing and sustainable development practices. Nancy and Ed are both experts in their field and bring a diverse array of speakers. Whether you've been in the industry for awhile or are new and looking to learn, this will be a rewarding class. Yes, I would. Great intro for 283.

This course will give you a good overview of the real estate industry but is a lot more development focused. You will need to supplement this with self study if you want to be prepared for real estate interviews.

Excellent class on global warming and how to radically re-imagine the real estate industry to deal with global warming. Yes, absolutely. Great class that gives a very comprehensive view on the real estate industry. Amazing guest speakers too.
I had never taken a real estate class before but with some finance and sustainability background, I was able to easily jump in given how the class is structured and learn a bunch.
I would. Nancy is just excellent. Her commitment to students, RE and ultimately making an impact to making this industry a little bit better is inspiring.

Don't let the name fool you. It should be called "Survey of Real Estate Development". Overweight guest lecturers, underweight practical real estate investing learnings. If you want a speaker series on real estate development, this is a great course! If you want to learn about how to value, analyze, and model real estate investments, look elsewhere.
Na
Yes, I found the course to a very informative and very enjoyable. I would highly recommend this course to anyone who is interested in real estate investments.

Overall I would recommend the class to other students. It helped spark a new interest in the real estate world and I am excited to take more real estate classes in my remaining time at Haas. However, the class would really benefit from better direction and communication on the group project. While the group project is brought up and explained in class 1, the format and methodology of how you should go about the project is lacking. Further, the class organization could be better. it is often not clear where assignments are posted or how they should be turned in.

One of the best courses I've taken anywhere. The lineup of guest speakers is nothing less than astonishing, and Nancy's deep industry knowledge is literally world class. If you are at all interested in development, urbanism, real estate, and finance, DO NOT MISS IT!

Not as a designed. I think the sustainability content was really valuable, but it wasn't effectively linked to the class projects. I think a richer set of smaller case studies, problem sets would have been more useful.
Course doesn't do a great job of teaching people about how to do a pro forma for real estate.
Yes, especially if you are going into the real estate world and are interested in development.

I would, but would recommend some changes - I think it would be appropriate to either slow down the instruction on pro forma work and investment analysis so everyone can get up to speed, or requiring some prerequisites/experience so that everyone can fully participate in the course.

If you want to understand how to develop and reach full operations for any type of real estate development this class is for you. There is definitely a nod to sustainability both in construction and in financing real estate developments.

Definitely recommend this course for anyone interested in real estate investment. It is a great primer on the major inputs to the process and the various stakeholders involved. The emphasis on guest panelists and in class presentations created a lot of opportunities for learning. I happened to be going through private RE fund interviews at the time of the course and it was incredibly valuable

As someone with no real estate background, this was me venturing to learn something new and boy do I wish I had taken more real estate courses sooner! Not only was the information very engaging, the course is systematically designed to take new students on a journey to understand key areas of real estate basics. Would recommend to anyone with any interest in Real Estate.

This class offers a nice easy entry into the world of real estate development and investment. You won't leave the course a master of real estate finance or investment principles. However, the more you invest the more you will get out since Nancy and Ed are so knowledgeable.
Yes. I learned a ton as a beginner about the fundamental elements of a real estate development deals and the current best practices in doing so.

I would recommend this course to anyone interested in learning about real estate and sustainability! There is a ton to learn about how real estate leverages new technologies to build sustainable developments.
Always take Nancy's class, she is the best in the game, you really want to go to her office hours too if you have time.

Yes. If you want a good overview of commercial real estate, this is the class to think. Prof Nancy Wallace is a giant in the field, and it is a privilege to hear her view and experiences. Prof Ed MacFarlane is also a wonderful resource to learn from, given his rich experience as an industry practitioner.
Yes, it would be good for an overview of development design and finance. If you have experience to have taken other development course it may be repetitive.
I would recommend taking a class with Nancy but I would not recommend taking a class with Ed.

Nancy does a great job teaching real estate courses and I wish she taught the entire class rather than split it 50/50. She is great at connecting the actual world of real estate with theory and cares about the students learning.
Definitely. While class content was interesting and worthwhile, Nancy as a professor would be the main motivator in recommending this class to others.
Yes I would. Nancy is a wealth of knowledge and inspires passion for innovative investment solutions to tackle social and environmental challenges.

I would highly recommend it. However some points for improvement– More about real estate investment vehicles, strategies and case examples. I would have also appreciated a little time every class dedicated to talk about current events or discuss a historical event related to the topic of discussion for that class.
Yes
Yes, but for MREDD there was a lot of crossover with previous classes, so the most relevant section for MREDD folks was Nancy's section.

Nancy Wallace is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. Her wealth of industry knowledge and experience made the class exciting, and her teaching style made the tricky course material easy to understand. The workload is just right, and I've learned a lot from the class. Coursework includes a very reasonable midterm to test your financial analysis knowledge to prepare you for a real–life current real estate development scenario in the second part of the course. You will not come across any outdated business school cases here. Weekly guest lecturers bring a very interesting and unique perspective to help students develop a well–rounded understanding of the subject matter. 10/10!
Absolutely, Nancy is wonderful and a really great teacher.
Neutral

Yes, this is a great course for any student that is not familiar with real estate to get first–hand experience. Absolutely. It was an incredible learning opportunity and forced me to think collaboratively and creatively. I am a CED student and the class was a great opportunity to work with other programs' students and share our perspectives.
yes if interested in real estate, it will be a great to get an overall sense
Yes - Nancy is extremely knowledgable and passionate about real estate development, there is no one in the world that would be more qualified to teach this class.
Keep doing what your are doing. the content is great!

The instructors are great! Super knowledgable and enthusiastic and keyed in. However, the class is very much you get what you put in. So if you're not genuinely interested and self motivated, you'll get very little from it as it's a low lift from the assignments point of view. Also you can get away with skipping a lot of the lectures. However if you're interested and curious and try out some new things, it's a great environment where you can get a lot of mentorship. And learn a lot from guest speakers who gave often frustratingly dense lectures. Very self guided learning, overall! Not as it currently is. In order to actually learn about real estate, you would need to teach yourself or go to office hours. Lectures are scattered and unhelpful.
yeah

Yes, however maybe not to an MRED student with a finance background. Lots of the materials covered are already covered in the MRED program, and some of the content was a repeat of what was covered in my undergrad real estate finance classes.

I recommend this course. Ed and Nancy have incredible industry knowledge and passion for the topic. The course is well designed to take you from a real estate novice to knowing just enough to be dangerous. Most of the guest speakers for this class are fascinating and relevant. The assignments are hefty but you work in a group so the workload is reasonable. However, the catch with this class is that you only get the most out of it if you invest time in working through the pro formas in the homework so I would recommend making time for that if you take this class. Yeah, and Nancy honestly is a delight. The sort of professor who inspires you to be like them.

This was a really worthwhile course - the instructors and guest speakers were so informative and gave very engaging real world examples of the challenges and opportunities in real estate development. The hands-on project was also really engaging. This course is a lot of work - so I wouldn't necessarily recommend for someone without a deep interest in real estate, or someone not wanting to pursue a career in real estate.
Absolutely. Exceptional overview of both commercial real estate development, asset analysis, and sustainability considerations in the real estate industry.
Yes, of course. I think it's a great survey of real estate, we have great speakers, the quality of the content is excellent and both Nancy and Ed do a great job and are very accessible and supportive

Good intro class to real estate investment, but need the student to take some initiatives to dig into the material. Nancy is very kind and make you feel very engaged and comfortable in class. She has a ton of experience in real estate! I definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in real estate.

sections.goodFor: People serious about commercial real estate - already working in it or recruiting for it - who know the terminology or will put in extra time to catch up on fundamentals.
sections.notFor: Casual learners, personal real-estate investors, and those expecting deep sustainability content: beginners get thrown into commercial jargon and one EWMBA student found little peer knowledge-sharing.
sections.workloadNote: Half of nearly every class goes to guest speakers, much of the rest to student presentations toward the final project; pro forma work sits outside class, assignments often posted 2-3 days before due.
sections.gradingBasis: Almost half the grade is the final project (pro forma model plus research) per one student, plus progress presentations.
sections.redFlags: Guest speakers consume ~half of most classes, crowding out teaching (4+). Disorganized: assignments posted to bCourses 2-3 days before deadlines with vague expectations (2). Little concrete pro forma guidance.
sections.quote: 90 minutes of almost every class was scattershot guest speakers talking about their various developments across the country that didn't add much to my learning.
comments: Highly recommend this course to those who look to learn fundamental and systematic real estate investment and development
Nancy has a lot to teach, but i think half of the time was spent on guest speakers which ate up the time to learn some really practical skills in real estate investment/finance

I would recommend this to folks who are serious or seriously curious about going into commercial real estate, but not for anybody else. I came in thinking this would be a nice foundation for future personal real estate investments, giving me the ability to evaluate the profitability of, say, buying a house or a small set of apartments. I also was hoping for in depth evaluation of the state of the real estate industry in the climate transition and where / how it needed to move faster. Unfortunately, neither of these were the case. We quickly dove into jargon and nuances of commercial real estate, which was good for the half of the class who had taken real estate classes already, but which made it difficult for me to engage. I do think the lineup of speakers were quite cool (e.g., the developers of Hudson Yards in NYC), but again, very focused on larger scale commercial real estate.

There's a slight disconnect among real estate classes. We learn how to build a proforma multiple times. There should be a foundational pro forma building course, giving other courses more time to go deeper into their specific real estate topic.

"Highly recommended! If you're a student interested in project development — whether from the business side or the engineering/architecture side — this class is extremely valuable. It equips you with the tools to plan, execute, and finance a project effectively."

Yes. It is definitely tailored for students already working in real estate or pursuing jobs in real estate, but it was well taught and the guest lecturers and panels were all incredibly additive to the course experience.
This class is worth what you put into it. I found immense value in the guest speakers, and as a gateway to the real estate industry.

I recommend taking this class for anybody interested in commercial real estate development. Professor Wallace is a great professor and has her pulse on the market, able to convey difficult concepts simply. Ed McFarlane supplements Nancy's lectures well, as an Architect he adds a practical element to classes and between the both of them can answer any question you may have. Each class starts with guest speakers, who are industry practitioners. This alone is great exposure and worth attending the class. What you get out of this class is very reliant on what you put in. As someone working in Real Estate, I can firmly say I learned some new things and got some great ideas.

Yes I would recommend this course to fellow students as think the insights from professionals were great to have in class and the exercises in the class helped develop real estate analysis skills I didn't have before.
Yes, good class to learn how real estate development numbers work
Would definitely recommend for anybody interested in real estate finance and how to view it from a sustainability lense!
Yes, I would, if the person was interested in pursuing a career in real estate. The material can be a bit overwhelming if a students does not know about the fundamentals of real estate investments.

This is good class to take if you are interested in learning more about real estate - the professors are both experts in this field - and are willing to look towards the future of where it should be going. However, the first few weeks will feel like getting thrown into the deep end - but it's actually quite manageable! I'd recommend. Real estate is something you should have given a bit of thought before graduating from business school (it is the biggest asset class in the US after all).

I loved Nancy Wallace as a knowledgeable professional but I would not recommend this course. I had hoped to get more practical financial skills in this course, but felt that ultimately very little teaching happened. 90 minutes of almost every class was scattershot guest speakers talking about their various developments across the country that didn't add much to my learning. And the other 90 min was often student presentations advancing towards the final project...but that left little time to do any real teaching/skill-building.

Also the course felt disorganized. The curriculum felt haphazard with topics not often progressing logically from one to the next, and assignments (and their accompanying details) wouldn't be created on BCourses until often 2-3 days before they were due. We would often have to remind the teaching team to post assignments (things that were vaguely labeled in the Syllabus like "Progress Report 2") and to give us details about what to submit, and then scramble to get those materials together on time. This is especially surprising in a 30-person course with two Readers that could have been supporting.

I would recommend as a very introductory class for real estate. It goes through most of the topics, but if someone wants something more technical or specific about the financials, this is not the class. Overall, speakers were great. Would liked to have more concrete learnings about applying sustainable features into real estate.

Yes. This class is a must for whoever used to, wants, or is about to work in the Real Estate industry. Professors are super professional and knowledgeable in this area. This class provides a hands on experience in Real Estate and cover almost every aspect of the industry from financial pro-forma to sustainability. If you don't have any finance or real estate background like me, this class might be a bit challenging but still manageable.

I would recommend this class as a great intro to real estate development and understanding the high level levers that could be utilized. Covers key topics and familiarizes you with different projects and companies within the ecosystem. I would recommend this course if you are interested in the built environment. That said, if you are only casually interested then this may be too technical/heavy on the finance side of things. The course has some heavy hitters as guest speakers who have implemented projects all over the country.

I would recommend this course for students who already have a good understanding of real estate or who are willing to put in extra time and effort outside of class to get up to speed on the concepts and fundamentals. Instructors were not the most organized and often were delayed in communicating expectations for class assignments. Half of the lecture time for almost each class was reserved for guest speakers, which was sometimes useful and interesting but not always. Almost half the grade is based on the final project and there is very little guidance on how to actually work through the pro forma model, complete the research, etc. (guidance is very high level).
I would recommend this course to students who want to dive deeper into the financial side of sustainable

development. This introductory course would require someone to have heard certain terminology from real estate to make this course more worthwhile. Other than terminology, coming from an engineering background, I was able to share sustainable strategies and was able to correlate how efficiency affects financial results.

I wouldn't recommend this to an EWMBA student. I didn't enjoy the low opportunity to share experiences and knowledge that other students had. This course is great prep for some one seeking a career in commercial real estate. However, as a someone with no background in real estate this course lacks breadth. I still don't understand how to develop a commercial real estate project. I get a few concepts like pro-forma and pitching projects to LPs.

sections.goodFor: Students targeting real estate or curious about the built environment and sustainability; strong networking via well-connected professors and industry guests.
sections.notFor: Students with no modeling/finance background (called VERY difficult), and anyone wanting professor-led lectures - one says most class time is guest speakers and advises auditing instead.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy for 3 units: pro forma case studies plus a final team project, with 'A LOT to absorb very quickly' including industry lingo; guest speakers fill much of class time.
sections.gradingBasis: Case studies and a final team real-estate project/pro forma; heavy guest-speaker component.
sections.redFlags: One student says the two professors hardly lecture and it is mostly guest speakers, recommending auditing rather than paying; steep unforgiving ramp for those without pro forma experience.
sections.quote: If you don't have much modeling experience or finance background, this course could be VERY difficult for you. There is A LOT to absorb very quickly
comments: I would highly recommend this instructor and course, especially for students interested in real estate. Regardless of whether you have a prior background in the field, the instructor is very supportive and makes a strong effort to help students understand the material. The course includes a project based on real-world scenarios, which provides a valuable and comprehensive experience of the real estate process. It allows students to engage with the challenges, opportunities, and complexities of real estate development in a meaningful way. Overall, it is a very rewarding and insightful course.
Yes, highly recommend this course. This course helps student to understand the real estate principle a lot if you are interested.

Whether you're interested in a career in real estate or just want to understand what defines a good real estate investment, you should take MBA280. This is a foundational course for anyone curious about the built environment. Nancy Wallace and Ed McFarlan are Berkeley's best and are complemented by an excellent roster of guest speakers. This is an experiential course so students should come prepared to work hard because they'll only get as much out of the class as they're willing to put in.
Yes, if they are interested in GP/LP real estate side of the business. it is very useful to understand the incentives for the built environment.
Yes, for the connections and networking opportunities the class affords.

Terrific course, the professors (especially Professor Wallace) add so much insight and context atop the great guest speakers. If you're interested in sustainability in the built environment and/or real estate development I highly recommend this class
Yes, if you're interested in real estate. this is one that should be taken.
Yes I would. The professors and guest speakers were wonderful and really deepened my understanding of the real estate industry.

I would not recommend paying for this class. If you are able to audit it, that would be much better. Most of the class is listening to guest lectures and the two professors hardly do any lectures themselves.

Yes, I would recommend this class if you are interested in a career in real estate. It provides a solid introduction to pro formas and financial modeling, taught by two stellar professors who are genuinely passionate about teaching and eager to help students learn. They emphasize gaining hands-on development experience while incorporating

sustainability principles. I learned a lot despite having very little pro forma experience when I entered the class, and my knowledge of pro formas grew significantly during the course through practice with case studies and the final team project (the Professors provided a lot of support). Both professors are very approachable and make themselves available. office hours, responding promptly over email. They are thoughtful in bringing a stellar lineup of industry guests, developers, investors, and other professionals, who share their experiences. This greatly enhances the classroom experience and offers a valuable opportunity to connect with industry leaders. You will leave with useful tools, industry terminology, and connections, as both professors are well-connected and encourage students to reach out to speakers and contacts. This was my favorite class during Haas, and I only regret not being able to take more classes with Professors Wallace and Ed.

I definitely recommend this course to folks, especially if you are looking to develop or hone your real estate skills. If you don't have muc h modeling experience or finance background, this course could be VERY difficult for you. There is A LOT to absorb very quickly, including industry lingo but also concepts. This is definitely a 3 unit and requires a lot of time and effort. Make sure you have a good, collaborative, communicative group because you will need to lean on them a lot with the case studies and projects. I'm not kidding. But it is worth it and you will feel prepared to talk shop about real estate after this class. I took away a lot, even if I don't plan to go into a real estate job after my MBA.

This course is helpful to anyone who wants to live and work in America. International students who plan to live and work outside of the U.S. after graduation may do better electing another class: the course materials have less bearing on their lives and the individual assignment may be difficult because many of the elements (social security, state taxes, etc.) may not be applicable to them.
Yes, I already have! Definitely the most applicable course I've taken in grad school. Who knew planning for retirement could be so fun:)

I thought it was great and would recommend. The course covers many useful topics (retirement, investing, buying a house, seeking financial advice, taxes, etc.) and gave solid advice on all of them -- I even learned some things during the topics that felt more basic like saving/spending and insurance. I also thought the final project was quite useful -- you put together a personal financial plan using a handy template that they provide.
Absolutely. Extremely valuable course for those who haven't taken a lot of time to dig into personal finance. Even for those who have it is a good refresher and covers a wide variety of topics.
Absolutely! This was such a worthwhile class and should be required for everyone throughout the campus to gain financial literacy.
Yes. learned a lot which can be greatly useful in life
I would definitely recommend this course. The contents of the course are extremely useful. It's critical to know how to manage personal finance and retirement.
yes!

Yes because it gives everyone the basic structure they need to meet their short-term and long-term financial goals. This should be taught to every student in this University so they don't end up in debt.
highly recommend

I would recommend the course to those interested in learning about personal finance but would suggest taking it pass/fail. I certainty would recommend this course. Is a course that focuses on life's financial decisions but adjusts to each student's background. As an international student, it is also great to learn about US tax system, retirement, healthcare, etc.

Yes! I think this course is a must for anyone interested in personal finance. Terry goes over almost every personal finance topic and gives you the opportunity to do further research into an area of interest you choose.
Useful class especially at the end of an MBA program to help you plan for the road ahead. The final individual project was particularly helpful.

I would recommend this course to any student looking for an easy 2 units who is interested in learning more about personal finance (and who is coming from a low level of knowledge and/or doesn't think they would put forth the effort to learn the material outside of being forced to learn it through a course). Terry & Donatella are great, and I think in person this class would be better. I found that class time often wasn't engaging, but the pre-class videos were helpful, and the group presentations at the end of the semester were the highlight of the class! I did take away a lot of practical knowledge and have a strong baseline to build from, which I didn't have before. Especially useful if you'll soon be making important financial decisions (buying a house, getting married, making other investments, paying off debt).

Yes! I would definitely recommend this course. This is a very well-structured class that walks you through some of the major financial decisions you will have in life. I don't think I've ever taken the time and thought about these until the class so definitely worthwhile. Terry and Donatella were great at making the content interactive and fun. I also really enjoyed the individual final project, made me realize how much more I'm spending than I should've.
Yes

While I knew some the material covered, there were instances where I learned a new application for my day to day. Also, there were some topics that I had zero understanding of. I was able to make decisions in my personal life in real time because of this course!

However, I honestly think that a class structure was messy and you can just watch videos (a basic class structure; 30min~1.5h video before class + class lecture) to get the knowledge, and the video is enough unless he changes a class structure. This class is a great overview of personal finance if you haven't had that before.
This is a low lift course. If you need structure and deadlines to get your finances in order, then I would recommend taking the course.

I would recommend the course. Need an instructor who can attend every class. Having a teacher on zoom and making the students attend in-person makes you feel like the instructor does not care (whether it's for a medical reason or not). If the teacher can't attend. class should be virtual.

As it currently stands, I would not recommend this course. The videos and course content were repetitive, I felt that the lectures lacked structure/direction. The final project was helpful, but should have been broken into pieces instead of the midterm. I found the midterm to be oddly hard seeing the lack of rigor in other aspects of the class.
Yes - very relevant for international students. Relatively low lift for a 2-unit course

Yes, it's useful content, especially as we leave business school. But hopefully the course is not just videos! Kind of. The content is helpful at times, but this could be an entirely online course where you just watch the hours of recorded videos that Terry has made and get all of the learning you need. Terry seems to put little effort into delivering a high-quality educational experience. In one of the first classes, he essentially taught exactly what was already taught to us in his videos. Not only was this a waste of everyone's time, it also was very indicative of the level of effort he puts into teaching his course. To me this suggests he puts very minimal effort into teaching and planning. Additionally, the last 5 classes were taught entirely by the students (group presentations). Seems like another way to let Terry coast through this course. Finally, we had to do an individual project where we put together our financial plan. The pre-populated Excel doc we received was filled with formatting errors, and was so simplistic that it is useless for me moving forward in my life. If you're going to make all of us do this, at least improve the quality of the Excel, and add some complexity so that it is actually useful. Looking at what professors are paid at Berkeley, I think Terry is grossly overpaid. He is one of the highest paid professors at all of Berkeley, but I would confidently say he is below average for the professors I have had at Haas.
Good contents, way of instruction can be improved.

I'd recommend it if the student was completely oblivious to personal finance.
I thought that the instructors could have been better prepared and make a class more dynamic.

Sure, you can find this knowledge on youtube...but will you actually sit down and do it? Probably not. If youre interested in your own personal finance, take this class. Its dedicated time to help you learn to improve your financial situation.
Yes, this class has a lot of great information and was the most universally applicable course at Haas. It honestly should be part of the core.

I really liked the class and content. I think it was really important and information everyone should get before leaving the MBA program. Terry was an okay professor. I was very excited for this class but sadly learned next to nothing. the videos are not useful, class time was extremely disorganized, all over the place, and taught no actual skills or knowledge. terry and donatella were both very nice, but the class needs to be revamped. it seems like they've just been doing the same thing for years and haven't updated their material. they need to have concrete, structured lessons. the final project had the potential to be useful, but they gave us no instruction on what we should do or how we should do it. I didn't learn anything in the course that helped me complete the project and didn't know if what I was doing was even correct. there was no guidance. I came into the class as a non–MBA student with no experience or even exposure to things like retirement planning, investments, etc. This class didn't teach me everything I would need to know for finance obviously, but it forced me to examine my own finances, consider various factors I hadn't even thought of, and overall just made me a lot more aware of my current and future financial situations and what steps I need to take in order to reach my desired financial goals. Highly recommend this class! One of the most practical classes you can take and the final project is building a personal financial plan, which is a complete win–win!

No I would definitely NOT recommend this class to anyone. I suppose it could be a little helpful for someone who is not an MBA student or is completely new to the U.S. financial system, but for anyone who grew up here and has paid attention at all to personal finance, it was useless. The content is way too broad and not nearly deep enough – we spent a whole week talking about saving, and that should have only been 20 minutes max. The class has potential, but it needs to go a lot deeper and be way more quantitative than what it is. Additionally, it should be split into two levels – one more introductory version for new US citizens and non–MBA students, and one for people who have experience on these topics but want to learn more. There should be more financial modeling and more info on things like stock options and less info on basic topics like saving. It is also WAY too much work for a two credit class. It should not have a midterm, or it should at least be an open book midterm since in the real world, you would always consult the internet when making these kinds of decisions.

I would recommend this course to international students who doesn't know much about how things work in the US. Yes, the class is fairly basic in terms of personal finance, however, even for those who are or think they are more financially savvy, you will likely come away with at least some helpful takeaways. I would not recommend this course for the following reasons:
- This is not a low-lift class; for a 1-unit course, the workload is way too heavy - multiple assignments per class, plus a complex final project for which clear instructions were not provided
- Instructions and expectations for the final project were never provided or clearly stated

- This was supposed to be a "safe space" for discussing DEI-related topics and other pressing issues surrounding that; however, instead of allowing for open discussions and healthy debates among students while acting as
guides/moderators, professors took on the task of monologuing, providing somewhat relevant but not a lot of value- adding insights and the rationale behind them
- Issues discussed were over-indexed on the black community, leaving aside other minorities

Bottom line, I would remove this course from the core MBA curriculum altogether, take maybe 10-15% of the topics reviewed in it and merge them onto "Leading People". And instead, I would provide an actual communications/public speaking class for students to be able to practice presentation and other soft skills.

I think so. My experience is that the EWMBA's are on their career path.
